metadata.title: National Building Code of Canada 2020
metadata.subtitle: Volume 1
metadata.authority: Issued by the Canadian Commission on Building and Fire Codes National Research Council of Canada

content.text: This Code applies to any one or more of the following:

clauses.text: the design and construction of a new [REF:term:bldng]building,
the [REF:term:ccpnc]occupancy of any [REF:term:bldng]building,
a change in [REF:term:ccpnc]occupancy of any [REF:term:bldng]building,
an [REF:term:ltrtn]alteration of any [REF:term:bldng]building,
an addition to any [REF:term:bldng]building,
the demolition of any [REF:term:bldng]building,
the reconstruction of any [REF:term:bldng]building that has been damaged by fire, earthquake or other cause,
the correction of an [REF:term:nsf-cndtn]unsafe condition in or about any [REF:term:bldng]building,
all parts of any [REF:term:bldng]building that are affected by a change in [REF:term:ccpnc]occupancy,
the work necessary to ensure safety in parts of a [REF:term:bldng]building

subclauses.text: that remain after a demolition,
that are affected by but that are not directly involved in [REF:term:ltrtn]alterations, or
that are affected by but not directly involved in additions,

clauses.text: except as permitted by the British Columbia Fire Code, the installation, replacement, or [REF:term:ltrtn]alteration of materials or equipment regulated by this Code,
the work necessary to ensure safety in a relocated [REF:term:bldng]building during and after relocation,
safety during construction of a [REF:term:bldng]building, including protection of the public,
the design, installation, extension, [REF:term:ltrtn]alteration, renewal or repair of [REF:term:plmbng-sstm]plumbing systems, and
the [REF:term:ltrtn]alteration, rehabilitation and change of occupancy of [REF:term:hrtg-bldng]heritage buildings.

content.text: This Code does not apply to the following:

clauses.text: utility towers and poles, and television, radio and other communication aerials and towers, except for loads resulting from their being located on or attached to [REF:term:bldng]buildings,
mechanical or other equipment and [REF:term:pplnc]appliances not specifically regulated in these regulations,
flood control and hydro electric dams and structures,

accessory [REF:term:bldng]buildings less than 10 m2
                               (metric) in [REF:term:bldng-r]building area that do not create a hazard,
with the permission of the [REF:term:thrt-hvng-jrsdctn]authority having jurisdiction, temporary [REF:term:bldng]buildings including

subclauses.text: construction site offices,
seasonal storage [REF:term:bldng]buildings,
special events facilities,
emergency facilities, and
similar structures,

clauses.text: factory built housing and components complying with CSA-Z240 MH Series standard, but this exemption does not extend to on site preparations (siting, foundations, mountings), connection to services and installation of [REF:term:pplnc]appliances, and
areas that are specifically exempted from provincial [REF:term:bldng]building regulations by provincial or federal enactments.

content.text: This Code applies to both site-built and factory-constructed [REF:term:bldng]buildings. (See [REF:internal:nbc.divA.part1.sect5.appnote2:short].)
[REF:term:frm-bldn]Farm buildings shall conform to the requirements in the National Farm Building Code of Canada 1995.

For [REF:term:hrtg-bldng]heritage buildings, the Alternate Compliance Methods for Heritage Buildings in [REF:internal:nbc.divA.part1.sect1.subsect1.art1.table1:long] may be substituted for requirements contained elsewhere in this Code. (See [REF:internal:nbc.divA.part1.sect5.appnote3:short].)

content.title:
Alternate Compliance Methods for Heritage Buildings
                            Forming Part of [REF:internal:nbc.divA.part1.sect1.subsect1.art1.sent5:long]

body_rows.content:
<italic>Fire Separations</italic>
                                    [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect1.subsect3.art1.sent1:long], [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect1.subsect3.art1.table1:long], [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part9.sect10.subsect9:long].
2 h [REF:term:fr-sprtn]fire separation required between some [REF:term:mjr-ccpn]major occupancies.
Except for F1 [REF:term:ccpnc]occupancies, 1 h [REF:term:fr-sprtn]fire separation is acceptable, provided the [REF:term:bldng]building is [REF:term:prnklrd]sprinklered.

<italic>Fire Separations</italic>
                                    [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect1.subsect3.art1.sent1:long], [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect1.subsect3.art1.table1:long], [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part9.sect10.subsect9:long].
1 h [REF:term:fr-sprtn]fire separation required between some [REF:term:mjr-ccpn]major occupancies.
30 min [REF:term:fr-sprtn]fire separation is acceptable if the [REF:term:bldng]building is [REF:term:prnklrd]sprinklered.

<italic>Noncombustible Construction</italic>
                                    [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect1.subsect5:long], [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect1.subsect5.art6.sent1:long].
All materials used in [REF:term:nncmbtbl-cnstrctn]noncombustible construction must be [REF:term:nncmbtbl]noncombustible unless otherwise permitted.

1. Roofs may be of [REF:term:cmbtbl-cnstrctn]combustible construction provided the [REF:term:bldng]building is [REF:term:prnklrd]sprinklered.
2. Up to 10% gross [REF:term:flr-r]floor area to a maximum of 10% of any one [REF:term:flr-r]floor area may be of [REF:term:cmbtbl-cnstrctn]combustible construction provided the [REF:term:bldng]building is [REF:term:prnklrd]sprinklered.

<italic>Fire-resistance Rating</italic>
                                    [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect1.subsect7.art1.sent1:long], [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part9.sect10.subsect3.art1:long].
Where a material, assembly of materials or structural member is required to have a [REF:term:fr-rtng]fire-resistance rating it shall be tested in accordance with CAN/ULC-S101, "Fire Endurance Tests of Building Construction Materials."

A [REF:term:fr-rtng]fire-resistance rating may also be used based on:
(a) HUD No. 8 Guideline on Fire Ratings of Archaic Materials and Assemblies.,
(b) Fire Endurance of Protected Steel Columns and Beams, DBR Technical Paper No. 194.,
(c) Fire Endurance of Unit Masonry Walls, DBR Technical Paper No. 207.,
(d) Fire Endurance of Light-Framed and Miscellaneous Assemblies, DBR Technical Paper No. 222.

Rating of Supporting Construction
[REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect1.subsect7.art5:long]., [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part9.sect10.subsect8.art3:long].
Supporting assemblies to have [REF:term:fr-rtng]fire-resistance rating at least equivalent to that of the supported floor.

<italic>Heavy timber construction</italic> is permitted to have a [REF:term:fr-rtng]fire-resistance rating less than would be required by the Code provided the [REF:term:bldng]building:
(a) is [REF:term:prnklrd]sprinklered, and
(b) does not exceed 6 [REF:term:str]storeys in [REF:term:bldng-hght]building height.

Continuity of <italic>Fire Separations</italic>
                                    [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect1.subsect8.art3.sent1:long], [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect1.subsect8.art3.sent2:long], [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part9.sect10.subsect9.art2:long].
<italic>Fire separations</italic> are required to be continuous above the ceiling space.

<italic>Fire separations</italic> are not required to be continuous above a ceiling space where
(a) the ceiling space is [REF:term:nncmbtbl-cnstrctn]noncombustible construction,
(b) both [REF:term:fr-cmprtmnt]fire compartments are [REF:term:prnklrd]sprinklered, or
(c) the ceiling has a minimum rating of 30 minutes.

Wired Glass
[REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect1.subsect8.art5.sent1:long], [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect1.subsect8.art14.sent2:long], [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part9.sect10.subsect13.art1:long]., [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part9.sect10.subsect13.art5:long].
6 mm wired glass in steel frame required in [REF:term:fr-sprtn]fire separations.
For fixed transoms or sidelights, 6 mm wired glass fixed to a wood frame of at least 50 mm thickness with steel stops is permitted in a required [REF:term:fr-sprtn]fire separation.

<italic>Mezzanines</italic>
                                    [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect2.subsect1.art1.sent4:long] and [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect2.subsect1.art1.sent7:long], [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part9.sect10.subsect4.art1:long].
<italic>Mezzanines</italic> enclosing more than 10% above the horizontal plane are considered as [REF:term:str]storey in [REF:term:bldng-hght]building height.

Enclosed [REF:term:mznn]mezzanines may be up to 40% of the [REF:term:str]storey in which they occur and not be considered a [REF:term:str]storey in [REF:term:bldng-hght]building height if the [REF:term:bldng]building is [REF:term:prnklrd]sprinklered.

<italic>Building Height</italic>
                                    [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect2.subsect2.art20:long]. to [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect2.subsect2.art90:long].
<italic>Noncombustible construction</italic> required for some [REF:term:bldng]buildings.

<italic>Buildings</italic> may be of [REF:term:cmbtbl-cnstrctn]combustible construction up to 6 [REF:term:str]storeys provided:
(a) the [REF:term:bldng]building is [REF:term:prnklrd]sprinklered,
(b) the [REF:term:bldng]building contains Group C, D, E, F, Division 2 or F, Division 3 [REF:term:ccpnc]occupancies, and
(c) floor assemblies not required to exceed 1 h [REF:term:fr-sprtn]fire separation requirements may be of <italic>heavy timber construction</italic>.

Spatial Separation
[REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect2.subsect3:long]., [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part9.sect10.subsect14:long].
The area of [REF:term:nprtctd-pnng]unprotected opening shall not exceed the limits in Tables 3.2.3.1.A to Table 3.2.3.1.E

The area of [REF:term:nprtctd-pnng]unprotected opening is not limited provided:
(a) the [REF:term:lmtng-dstnc]limiting distance is a minimum 1 m,
(b) the [REF:term:bldng]building has a supervised sprinkler system in conformance with [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect2.subsect4.art9.sent3:long], and
(c) the sprinkler system is connected to the fire department in conformance with [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect2.subsect4.art7.sent4:long].

Construction of <italic>Exposing Building Face</italic>
                                    [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect2.subsect3.art7:long], [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part9.sect10.subsect14.art5:long].
The [REF:term:xpsng-bldng-fc]exposing building face is required to have a [REF:term:fr-rtng]fire-resistance rating and/or be of [REF:term:nncmbtbl-cnstrctn]noncombustible construction.

<italic>Exposing building face</italic> is not required to have a [REF:term:fr-rtng]fire-resistance rating if the [REF:term:bldng]building is [REF:term:prnklrd]sprinklered. Also, the [REF:term:xpsng-bldng-fc]exposing building face is not required to be of [REF:term:nncmbtbl-cnstrctn]noncombustible construction if it is protected by an exterior sprinkler system conforming to NFPA 13, "Installation of Sprinkler Systems."

Roof Covering Rating
[REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect1.subsect15.art2.sent1:long]
Class A, B or C roof covering in conformance with CAN/ ULC-S107, "Fire Tests of Roof Coverings" required.
For existing roofs not covered by a Class A, B or C roofing a manually operated deluge system in accordance with NFPA 13, "Installation of Sprinkler Systems" is permitted.

<italic>Smoke Alarms</italic>
                                    [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect2.subsect4.art20.sent7:long], [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part9.sect10.subsect19.art4.sent1:long]
                                    <italic>Smoke alarms</italic> are required to be connected to an electric circuit.
<italic>Smoke alarms</italic> may be battery operated in single family homes only.

1. Open stairs in [REF:term:bldng]buildings of maximum 4 [REF:term:str]storeys in [REF:term:bldng-hght]building height need not comply with [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect2.subsect8:long]., provided
(a) the [REF:term:bldng]building contains a Group C or D [REF:term:ccpnc]occupancy,
(b) the [REF:term:bldng]building is [REF:term:prnklrd]sprinklered with fast-response sprinklers,
(c) corridors opening into the [REF:term:ntrconnctd-flr-spc]interconnected floor space are separated from the [REF:term:ntrconnctd-flr-spc]interconnected floor space by a [REF:term:fr-sprtn]fire separation with the rating required for the corridor, and
(d) [REF:term:mk-dtctr]smoke detectors are installed in the rooms opening into the [REF:term:ntrconnctd-flr-spc]interconnected floor space and the [REF:term:mk-dtctr]smoke detectors are connected to the fire alarm system.2. Open stairs in [REF:term:bldng]buildings of maximum 3 [REF:term:str]storeys in [REF:term:bldng-hght]building height, or first 2 [REF:term:str]storeys and [REF:term:bsmnt]basement, need not comply with [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect2.subsect8:long]. of Division B, provided:
(a) the [REF:term:bldng]building contains a Group C or D [REF:term:ccpnc]occupancy,
(b) the [REF:term:bldng]building is [REF:term:prnklrd]sprinklered with fast response sprinklers,
(c) [REF:term:mk-dtctr]smoke detectors are installed in the rooms opening into the [REF:term:ntrconnctd-flr-spc]interconnected floor space and the [REF:term:mk-dtctr]smoke detectors are connected to the fire alarm system, and
(d) at least one <italic>means of egress</italic> is not through the [REF:term:ntrconnctd-flr-spc]interconnected floor space.

Separation of <italic>Suites</italic>
                                    [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect3.subsect1.art1:long], [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part9.sect10.subsect9.art13:long]., [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part9.sect10.subsect9.art14:long].
<italic>Suites</italic> are required to be separated from adjoining [REF:term:t]suites by a [REF:term:fr-sprtn]fire separation having a fire resistance rating of 45 min or 1 hr.

Existing [REF:term:fr-sprtn]fire separations of 30 min, such as wood lath and plaster in good condition, are acceptable in [REF:term:prnklrd]sprinklered
                                    [REF:term:bldng]buildings not exceeding 6 [REF:term:str]storeys in [REF:term:bldng-hght]building height.

Corridor [REF:term:fr-sprtn]fire separation
                                    [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect3.subsect1.art4:long]., [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part9.sect10.subsect9.art15:long].
<italic>Public corridors</italic> are required to be separated from the remainder of the [REF:term:bldng]building by a [REF:term:fr-sprtn]fire separation having a [REF:term:fr-rtng]fire-resistance rating of at least 45 min.

Existing corridors with 30 min fire resistance ratings, such as wood lath and plaster in good condition, are acceptable in <italic>residential occupancies</italic> provided the [REF:term:bldng]building:
(a) does not exceed 6 [REF:term:str]storeys in [REF:term:bldng-hght]building height, and
(b) is fully [REF:term:prnklrd]sprinklered with fast response sprinklers.

Corridor Width
[REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect3.subsect1.art9:long]., [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect4.subsect3:long]., [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part9.sect9.subsect3.art3:long].
<italic>Public corridors</italic> and <italic>exit</italic> corridors are permitted to have a minimum width of 1 100 mm.

<italic>Public corridors</italic> and <italic>exit</italic> corridors are permitted with a minimum width of 800 mm provided:
(a) the [REF:term:ccpnt-ld]occupant load of the [REF:term:bldng]building is maximum 20 people, and
(b) the [REF:term:bldng]building does not exceed 3 [REF:term:str]storeys in [REF:term:bldng-hght]building height.

Door Swing
[REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect3.subsect1.art10:long]., [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect4.subsect6.art12:long]., [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part9.sect9.subsect6.art5:long].
Doors required to swing in the direction of <italic>exit</italic> travel.

2nd egress door from a room is not required to swing in the direction of <italic>exit</italic> travel provided:
(a) the [REF:term:bldng]building is [REF:term:prnklrd]sprinklered and the system is supervised in conformance with [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect2.subsect4.art9.sent3:long], and
(b) the [REF:term:ccpnt-ld]occupant load of the [REF:term:bldng]building is maximum 100 people.

Transparent Doors and Panels
[REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect3.subsect1.art19:long]., [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part9.sect6.subsect1.art4:long].
Safety glass required.
Existing glass or transparent panels that do not comply fully with the requirements are permitted if sufficiently discernible or [REF:term:grd]guards are provided in hazardous situations.

Dead-end Corridors
[REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect3.subsect1.art9.sent7:long], [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part9.sect9.subsect7.art3:long].
Dead-end corridors are permitted to a maximum length of 6 m.

1. Dead-end corridors are permitted to a maximum length of 10 m in Group C [REF:term:ccpnc]occupancies provided:
(a) the [REF:term:bldng]building is [REF:term:prnklrd]sprinklered with fast response sprinklers, and
(b) [REF:term:mk-dtctr]smoke detectors are installed in the corridor system.
2. Dead-end corridors are permitted to a maximum of 15 m in length in Group D, E, F, Division 2 and F, Division 3 [REF:term:ccpnc]occupancies provided:
(a) the [REF:term:bldng]building is [REF:term:prnklrd]sprinklered with fast response sprinklers, and
(b) [REF:term:mk-dtctr]smoke detectors are installed in the corridor system.

<italic>Exits</italic>
                                    [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect4.subsect2.art1:long], [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part9.sect9.subsect8.art2:long].
<italic>Floor areas</italic> shall be served by not fewer than 2 <italic>exits</italic> except as permitted by [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect4.subsect2.art1.sent2:long].

<italic>Floor areas</italic> may be served by a single <italic>exit</italic> within the limits of [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect4.subsect2.art1.sent2:long] provided:
(a) the [REF:term:bldng]building does not exceed 3 [REF:term:str]storeys in [REF:term:bldng-hght]building height,
(b) the [REF:term:bldng]building is [REF:term:prnklrd]sprinklered with fast response sprinklers, and
(c) all <italic>floor areas</italic> are protected by a system of [REF:term:mk-dtctr]smoke detectors connected to a fire alarm system.

Reduction of <italic>Exit</italic> Width
[REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect4.subsect3.art3.sent2:long], [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part9.sect9.subsect6.art1:long].
Swinging doors in their swing shall not reduce the effective width of <italic>exit</italic> stairs and landings to less than 750 mm.

Existing swinging doors in their swing are permitted to reduce the effective width of <italic>exit</italic> stairs and landings to a minimum of 550 mm provided:
(a) they serve Group C or D [REF:term:ccpnc]occupancies,
(b) the [REF:term:bldng]building does not exceed 4 [REF:term:str]storeys in [REF:term:bldng-hght]building height, and(c) the [REF:term:bldng]building is [REF:term:prnklrd]sprinklered.

<italic>Fire Separation</italic> of <italic>Exits</italic>
                                    [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect4.subsect4.art1:long]., [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part9.sect9.subsect4:long].
<italic>Exits</italic> are required to be separated from the remainder of the <italic>floor area</italic> by a [REF:term:fr-sprtn]fire separation having a [REF:term:fr-rtng]fire-resistance rating of not less than required by [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect2.subsect2:long]. , but not less than 45 min.

1. <italic>Buildings</italic> of 3 [REF:term:str]storeys or less may have <italic>exits</italic> that are separated by a [REF:term:fr-sprtn]fire separation that does not have a [REF:term:fr-rtng]fire-resistance rating provided:
(a) the [REF:term:bldng]building is [REF:term:prnklrd]sprinklered with fast response sprinklers, and
(b) the sprinkler system is supervised in accordance with [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect2.subsect4.art9.sent3:long].
2. <italic>Buildings</italic> not exceeding 6 [REF:term:str]storeys in [REF:term:bldng-hght]building height may have <italic>exits</italic> that are separated by a [REF:term:fr-sprtn]fire separation having a fire resistance rating of not less than 45 min provided the [REF:term:bldng]building is [REF:term:prnklrd]sprinklered.

<italic>Exits</italic> Through Lobbies
[REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect4.subsect4.art2:long]., [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part9.sect9.subsect8.art5:long].
Rooms adjacent to the lobby are required to be separated by a [REF:term:fr-sprtn]fire separation.

Rooms adjacent to the lobby are not required to be separated by a [REF:term:fr-sprtn]fire separation provided:
(a) the <italic>floor area</italic> is [REF:term:prnklrd]sprinklered with fast response sprinklers, and
(b) [REF:term:mk-dtctr]smoke detectors are installed in the adjacent rooms.

Rooms Opening into <italic>Exit</italic>
                                    [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect4.subsect4.art4.sent7:long], [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part9.sect9.subsect5.art9:long].
<italic>Service rooms</italic> and ancillary rooms are not permitted to open directly into an <italic>exit</italic>.

<italic>Service rooms</italic> and ancillary rooms may open directly into an <italic>exit</italic> provided:
(a) the room is [REF:term:prnklrd]sprinklered with fast response sprinklers, and
(b) weatherstripping is installed on the door to prevent the passage of smoke.

Illumination of <italic>Exit</italic> Signs
[REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect4.subsect5.art1.sent3:long] and [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect4.subsect5.art1.sent4:long] , [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part9.sect9.subsect11.art3.sent3:long] and [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part9.sect9.subsect11.art3.sent4:long]
                                    <italic>Exit</italic> signs are required to be illuminated continuously while the [REF:term:bldng]building is occupied.

Where <italic>exit</italic> signage may compromise historic appearances, or authenticity of displays, <italic>exit</italic> signs may be installed to light only on an emergency condition, such as by the fire alarm system or due to power failure.

Clearance from <italic>Exit</italic> Doors
[REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect4.subsect6.art11.sent1:long], [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part9.sect9.subsect6.art6:long].
Stair risers shall not be closer than 300 mm from an <italic>exit</italic> door.
Except as permitted in Sentences 3.4.6.11.(3) or 9.6.6.(2), existing <italic>exit</italic> doors shall not extend beyond the first riser.

Fire Escapes
[REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect4.subsect7:long]. , [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part9.sect9.subsect2.art1.sent2:long]
Fire escapes are required to conform to [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect4.subsect7:long].

Existing fire escapes that do not completely conform to [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect4.subsect7:long]. are acceptable provided:
(a) the fire escapes are acceptable and
(b) the [REF:term:bldng]building is [REF:term:prnklrd]sprinklered.

Existing [REF:term:cmbtbl]combustible fire escapes are permitted if the [REF:term:bldng]building is permitted to be of [REF:term:cmbtbl-cnstrctn]combustible construction by Part 3, Part 9 or by this Table.

Protection of Fire Escapes
[REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect4.subsect7.art4:long]., [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part9.sect9.subsect2.art1.sent2:long]
Openings in the exterior wall adjacent to the fire escape are required to be protected by <italic>closures</italic>.

Existing openings in the exterior wall adjacent to the fire escape are not required to be protected by <italic>closures</italic> provided:
(a) the [REF:term:bldng]building is [REF:term:prnklrd]sprinklered, and
(b) a sprinkler head is located within 1.5 m of the opening required to be protected by [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect4.subsect7.art4:long].

<italic>Vertical Service Space</italic>
                                    [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect6.subsect3.art1:long].
<italic>Vertical service spaces</italic> are required to be separated from the adjacent <italic>floor area</italic> by a rated [REF:term:fr-sprtn]fire separation.

Existing <italic>vertical service spaces</italic> that do not completely conform to the rated [REF:term:fr-sprtn]fire separation requirements are acceptable provided the <italic>vertical service spaces</italic> are [REF:term:prnklrd]sprinklered.

Height of Rooms
[REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect7.subsect1:long]., [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part9.sect5:long].
The height of rooms is required to comply to minimum dimension requirements.
Existing rooms are not required to comply to the minimum dimension requirements of [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect7.subsect1:long]. or [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part9.sect5.subsect3:long].

Washroom Requirements
[REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect7.subsect2:long]., [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part9.sect31:long].

Existing facilities are not required to completely comply to the requirements of [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect7.subsect2:long]. or [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part9.sect31:long]. provided it is acceptable to the [REF:term:thrt-hvng-jrsdctn]authority having jurisdiction.

<italic>Access for Persons with Disabilities</italic>
                                    [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect8:long]. of Division B

Existing exterior decorations are not required to fully comply to the anchorage requirements of [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect8:long]. provided:

(See [REF:internal:nbc.divA.part1.sect5.appnote4:short].)

content.title:
Alternate Compliance Methods for Alterations to Existing Buildings to Add a Secondary Suite
                            Forming Part of [REF:internal:nbc.divA.part1.sect1.subsect1.art1.sent6:long]

header_rows.content: Alternate Compliance Method (References to Division B)

body_rows.content:
Reinforcement for Grab Bars [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect8.subsect5.art1.sent2:long]
One bathroom in a <italic>secondary suite</italic> shall have walls adjacent the water closet and shower or bathtub location reinforced to accommodate the future installation of grab bars.
Reinforcement to accommodate the future installation of grab bars is not required in existing bathrooms serving a <italic>secondary suite</italic>.

Ceiling Heights of Rooms or Spaces
[REF:internal:nbc.divB.part9.sect5.subsect3.art1.sent1:long] and [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part9.sect5.subsect3.art1.table1:long].
Ceiling height shall be not less than 2.1 m over the minimum area required in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part9.sect5.subsect3.art1.table1:long].

Except as required by [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part9.sect9.subsect3.art4.sent3:long], the minimum ceiling heights in a <italic>secondary suite</italic> over the required area as indicated in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part9.sect5.subsect3.art1.table1:long]. shall be not less than 1.95 m. It shall be possible to travel from the required area of one room to the required areas of all other rooms within the <italic>secondary suite</italic> without reduction of the ceiling height to less than 1.95 m.Except as required by [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part9.sect9.subsect3.art4.sent3:long], the minimum clear height under beams and ducting, including where located over stairs, in a <italic>secondary suite</italic> shall be not less than 1.85 m.

Doorway Opening Sizes
[REF:internal:nbc.divB.part9.sect5.subsect5.art1.sent1:long] and [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part9.sect5.subsect5.art1.table1:long].
Doorway openings shall be designed to accommodate swing-type and folding doors not less than 1 980 mm high.

Except for <italic>exit</italic> doors and for doors serving <italic>public corridors</italic> and <italic>exit</italic> corridors that serve a house with a <italic>secondary suite</italic>, doorway openings within a <italic>secondary suite</italic> shall be designed to accommodate swing-type and folding doors not less than 1 890 mm high.

Height over Stairs
[REF:internal:nbc.divB.part9.sect8.subsect2.art2.sent3:long]
The clear height over stairs shall be not less than 1950 mm.

Except for stairs in a <italic>public corridor</italic> or <italic>exit</italic> corridor that serve a house with a <italic>secondary suite</italic>, the clear height over stairs that are located under existing beams and existing ducting in a house with a <italic>secondary suite</italic> shall be not less than 1 850 mm.

Openings Near <italic>Exit</italic> Doors
[REF:internal:nbc.divB.part9.sect9.subsect4.art6.sent1:long]
Where an exterior <italic>exit</italic> door in one [REF:term:fr-cmprtmnt]fire compartment iswithin 3 m horizontally of an [REF:term:nprtctd-pnng]unprotected opening inanother [REF:term:fr-cmprtmnt]fire compartment and the exterior walls of these [REF:term:fr-cmprtmnt]fire compartments intersect at an exterior angle of less than 135°, the opening shall be protected.

Protection of the [REF:term:nprtctd-pnng]unprotected openings as described in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part9.sect9.subsect4.art6.sent1:long] is not required when all [REF:term:mk-lrm]smoke alarms within a house with a <italic>secondary suite</italic> are of photo-electric type and interconnected as described in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part9.sect10.subsect19.art5.sent2.clause1:long].

<italic>Fire-Resistance Ratings</italic> for Walls, Columns and Arches [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part9.sect10.subsect8.art3.sent1:long]
                                    <italic>Loadbearing</italic> walls, columns and arches in the [REF:term:str]storey immediately below a floor or roof assembly shall have a [REF:term:fr-rtng]fire-resistance rating of not less than that required for the supported floor or roof assembly.

Except for heavy timber elements and those of masonry or concrete construction, light frame walls, columns, arches and beams as well as <italic>loadbearing</italic> steel elements that support floors between [REF:term:dwllng-nt]dwelling units in a house with a <italic>secondary suite</italic> including their common spaces shall be protected by not less than 12.7 mm thick gypsum board.

Sound Transmission
[REF:internal:nbc.divB.part9.sect11.subsect1.art1.sent2:long]
Each [REF:term:dwllng-nt]dwelling unit shall be separated from every other space in a house with a <italic>secondary suite</italic> in which noise may be transmitted by construction having joist and stud spaces <italic>filled</italic> with sound-absorbing material, resilient channel on one side of the separation, and 12.7 mm thick gypsum board on ceilings and on both sides of walls, or by either construction providing an STC rating of not less than 43, or by using a separating assembly and adjoining construction providing an ASTC rating of not less than 40.

The assemblies and adjoining constructions that separate the [REF:term:dwllng-nt]dwelling units in a house with a <italic>secondary suite</italic> including their common spaces need not comply with [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part9.sect11.subsect1.art1.sent2.clause1:long] where resilient metal channel spaced 400 or 600 mm o.c. and an additional layer of not less than 12.7 mm gypsum board is added to one side of an existing finished assembly.

articles.title: Book I (General) and Book II (Plumbing Systems) of the Code

content.text: This is the first of the two Books, Book I (General) and Book II (Plumbing Systems), that together form the British Columbia Building Code.
Unless a Book is specified, references to "the British Columbia Building Code," "the Code," "this Code" and the like shall be read as references to the Book in which they appear.

articles.title: Characteristics of Materials, Appliances, Systems and Equipment

content.text:
All materials, [REF:term:pplnc]appliances, systems
and equipment installed to meet the requirements of this Code shall
possess the necessary characteristics to perform their intended functions
when installed in a [REF:term:bldng]building.

All [REF:term:bldng]building materials, [REF:term:pplnc]appliances and equipment on the [REF:term:bldng]building site shall be stored in such a way as to prevent
the deterioration or impairment of their essential properties.

Unless otherwise specified, used materials, [REF:term:pplnc]appliances and equipment are permitted to be reused when they
meet the requirements of this Code for new materials and are satisfactory
for the intended use.
Personnel performing the installation, alteration, renewal or repair of a [REF:term:plmbng-sstm]plumbing system shall

be the registered owner and occupant or intended occupant of the single detached dwelling in which plumbing work will occur.

articles.title: Classification of Buildings Containing Agricultural Occupancies

content.text:
[REF:term:bldng]Buildings or parts of [REF:term:bldng]buildings containing an [REF:term:grc-ccp]agricultural occupancy that has an [REF:term:ccpnt-ld]occupant load of not more than one person per 40 m2
                            (metric) shall be classified according to their [REF:term:mjr-ccpn]major occupancy as belonging to Group G, Division
1, 2, 3 or 4.

[REF:term:bldng]Buildings or parts of [REF:term:bldng]buildings containing an [REF:term:grc-ccp]agricultural occupancy that has an [REF:term:ccpnt-ld]occupant load of more than one person per 40 m2
                            (metric) shall be classified according to their [REF:term:mjr-ccpn]major occupancy as belonging to one of the
Groups and Divisions listed in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect1.subsect2.art1.table1:long].

For the purposes of [REF:internal:nbc.divA.part1.sect3.subsect3.art6.sent1:short]
                           [REF:internal:nbc.divA.part1.sect3.subsect3.art6.sent2:short], the [REF:term:ccpnt-ld]occupant load shall be determined
based on the [REF:term:flr-r]floor area or the part of
the [REF:term:flr-r]floor area that contains the [REF:term:grc-ccp]agricultural occupancy.

A [REF:term:bldng]building intended for use by more
than one [REF:term:mjr-ccpn]major occupancy shall be classified
according to all the [REF:term:mjr-ccpn]major occupancies for which it is used or intended to be used.
Parts 1 and 2 of Division C apply to all [REF:term:bldng]buildings covered in this Code. (See [REF:internal:nbc.divA.part1.sect1.subsect1.art1:long])

Words and phrases used in this Code that are not included in
the list of definitions in [REF:internal:nbc.divA.part1.sect4.subsect1.art2:long] shall have
the meanings that are commonly assigned to them in the context in
which they are used, taking into account the specialized use of terms
by the various trades and professions to which the terminology applies.

Where objectives and functional statements are referred to in
this Code, they shall be the objectives and functional statements
described in Parts 2 and 3.

Where acceptable solutions are referred to in this Code, they
shall be the provisions stated in Parts 2 to 9 of Division B.

Where alternative solutions are referred to in this Code, they
shall be the alternative solutions mentioned in [REF:internal:nbc.divA.part1.sect2.subsect1.art1.sent1.clause2:long].

The words and terms in italics in this Code shall have the following
meanings:
                              
                                 Access or Accessible
                                 means an area and its facilities, or both, as required by this Code, which is easy to approach, enter, exit, operate, participate in, pass to and from, and use safely and independently by [REF:term:prsn-wth-dsblts]persons with disabilities.
                              
                              
                                 Access to exit
                                 means that part of a [REF:term:mn-f-gr]means of egress within a [REF:term:flr-r]floor area that provides access to an [REF:term:xt]exit serving the [REF:term:flr-r]floor area.
                              
                              
                                 Adaptable dwelling unit
                                 means a [REF:term:dwllng-nt]dwelling unit designed and constructed with some <italic>accessible</italic> features and which accommodates the future modification to provide more <italic>accessible</italic> features.
                              
                              
                                 Adfreezing
                                 means the adhesion of [REF:term:l]soil to a [REF:term:fndtn-nt]foundation unit resulting from the freezing of [REF:term:l]soil water.
(Also referred to as “frost grip.”)
                              
                              
                                 Agricultural occupancy
                                 (Group G) means the [REF:term:ccpnc]occupancy of a [REF:term:bldng]building or part thereof that is located on land that is associated with
and devoted to the practice of farming, and is used for the purpose
of producing crops, raising farm animals, or preparing, marketing,
storing or processing agricultural products. (See [REF:internal:nbc.divA.part1.sect5.appnote7.div1:short].)
                              
                              
                                 Agricultural occupancy with no human occupants (Group G, Division 4)
                                  means an [REF:term:grc-ccp]agricultural occupancy that is not intended
to be occupied by persons under normal use and is generally used for
the storage of agricultural materials and by-products. (See [REF:internal:nbc.divA.part1.sect5.appnote7.div2:short].)
                              
                              
                                 Air barrier system
                                 means the assembly
installed to provide a continuous barrier to the movement of air.
                              
                              
                                 Air-supported structure
                                 means a structure
consisting of a pliable membrane that achieves and maintains its shape
and support by internal air pressure.
                              
                              
                                 Alarm signal
                                 means an audible signal
transmitted throughout a zone or zones or throughout a [REF:term:bldng]building to advise occupants that a fire emergency
exists.
                              
                              
                                 Alert signal
                                 means an audible signal
to advise designated persons of a fire emergency.
                              
                              
                                 Alteration
                                 means a change or extension
to any matter or thing or to any [REF:term:ccpnc]occupancy regulated by this Code.
                              
                              
                                 Apparent sound transmission class (ASTC)
                                 means a single number rating of the airborne sound attenuation of [REF:term:bldng]building assemblies separating two adjoining
spaces, taking into account both the direct and flanking sound transmission
paths. (See [REF:internal:nbc.divA.part1.sect5.appnote7:short].) (See also [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.appnote79:long].)
                              
                              
                                 Appliance
                                 means a device to convert
fuel into energy and includes all components, controls, wiring and
piping required to be part of the device by the applicable standard
referred to in this Code.
                              
                              
                                 Artesian groundwater
                                 means a confined
body of water under pressure in the ground.
                              
                              
                                 Assembly occupancy
                                 (Group A) means the [REF:term:ccpnc]occupancy or the use of a [REF:term:bldng]building or part thereof by a gathering of persons for civic,
political, travel, religious, social, educational, recreational or
like purposes, or for the consumption of food or drink.
                              
                              
                                 Attic or roof space
                                 means the space
between the roof and the ceiling of the top [REF:term:tr]storey or between a dwarf wall and a sloping roof.
                              
                              
                                 Authority having jurisdiction
                                 means the governmental body responsible for the enforcement of any part of this Code or the official or agency designated by that body to exercise such a function.  Notwithstanding this definition, the Chief Inspector of Mines has the sole responsibility for administration and enforcement in respect to all [REF:term:bldng]buildings, structures and site services used at a mine, as defined in the Mines Act.
                              
                              
                                 Barrier-free
                                 means that a [REF:term:bldng]building and its facilities can be approached,
entered, and used by persons with physical or sensory disabilities.
                              
                              
                                 Basement
                                 means a [REF:term:tr]storey or [REF:term:tr]storeys of a [REF:term:bldng]building located below the [REF:term:frt-tr]first storey.
                              
                              
                                 Bearing surface
                                 means the contact surface
between a [REF:term:fndtn-nt]foundation unit and the [REF:term:l]soil  or [REF:term:rck]rock upon which
it bears.
                              
                              
                                 Boiler
                                 means an [REF:term:pplnc] appliance intended to supply hot water or steam for space
heating, processing or power purposes.
                              
                              
                                 Braced wall band
                                 means an imaginary
continuous straight band extending vertically and horizontally through
the [REF:term:bldng]building or part of the [REF:term:bldng]building, within which [REF:term:br-wl-pnl]braced wall panels are constructed.
                              
                              
                                 Braced wall panel
                                 means a portion of
a wood-frame wall where bracing, sheathing, cladding or interior finish
is designed and installed to provide the required resistance to lateral

to the entire [REF:term:tr]storey.

                                 means any person, firm or corporation controlling the property under consideration during that period of the application of [REF:internal:nbc.divA.part1.sect1.subsect1.art1.sent1:long] of this Code.
                              
                              
                                 Partition
                                 means an interior wall 1 [REF:term:tr]storey or part-[REF:term:tr]storey in
height that is not [REF:term:ldbrng]loadbearing.
                              
                              
                                 Party wall
                                 means a wall jointly owned
and jointly used by 2 parties under easement agreement or by right
in law, and erected at or upon a line separating 2 parcels of land
each of which is, or is capable of being, a separate real-estate entity.
                              
                              
                                 Perched groundwater
                                 means a free standing
body of water in the ground extending to a limited depth.
                              
                              
                                 Persons with disabilities
                                 means persons who have a permanent or temporary physical, mental, intellectual or sensory impairment which, in interaction with various barriers, may hinder their full and effective participation in society on an equal basis with others.
                              
                              
                                 Pile
                                 means a slender [REF:term:dp-fndtn]deep foundation unit made of materials such
as wood, steel or concrete or a combination thereof, that is either
premanufactured and placed by driving, jacking, jetting or screwing,
or cast-in-place in a hole formed by driving, excavating or boring.
(Cast-in-place bored [REF:term:pl]piles are often referred
to as [REF:term:cn]caissons in Canada.)
                              
                              
                                 Plenum
                                 means a chamber forming part
of an air duct system.
                              
                              
                                 Plumbing system
                                 means a drainage system,
a venting system and a water system or parts thereof.
                              
                              
                                 Post-disaster building
                                 means a building that the authority having jurisdiction has determined is necessary for the provision of essential services to the general public in the event of a disaster and includes buildings meeting these criteria but not limited to
                                       hospitals, emergency treatment facilities and blood banks,
                                       telephone exchanges,
                                       power generating stations and electrical substations,
                                       control centres for natural gas distribution,
                                       control centres for air, land and marine transportation,
                                       water treatment facilities,
                                       water storage facilities,
                                       water and sewage pumping stations,
                                       sewage treatment facilities,
                                       buildings having critical national defence functions, and
                                       buildings of the following types, unless exempted from this designation by the authority having jurisdiction:
                                             emergency response facilities,
                                             fire, rescue and police stations and housing for vehicles, aircraft or boats used for such purposes, and
                                             communications facilities, including radio and television stations.
                                          
                                       
                                    (See Note A-1.4.1.2.(1).)
                        
                              
                              
                                 Private sewage disposal system
                                 means
a privately owned plant for the treatment and disposal of sewage (such
as a septic tank with an absorption field).
                              
                              
                                 Process plant
                                 means an industrial occupancy where materials, including flammable liquids, combustible liquids or gases, are produced or used in a process. (See Table 3.2.7.1. of Division B of the British Columbia Fire Code.)
                              
                              
                                 Protected floor space
                                 means that part
of a [REF:term:flr-r]floor area protected from the effects
of fire and used as part of a [REF:term:mn-f-gr]means of egress from an [REF:term:ntrcnnct]interconnected floor space.
                              
                              
                                 Public corridor
                                 means a corridor that
provides [REF:term:cc-t-xt]access to exit from more than
one [REF:term:t]suite. (See [REF:internal:nbc.divA.part1.sect5.appnote7.div14:short].)
                              
                              
                                 Public way
                                 means a sidewalk, [REF:term:trt]street, highway, square or other open space to
which the public has access, as of right or by invitation, expressed
or implied.
                              
                              
                                 Ramp
                                 means a path of travel having a
slope steeper than 1 in 20.
                              
                              
                                 Registered professional
                                 means
                                       a person who is registered as an Architect with the Architectural Institute of British Columbia under the Professional Governance Act, or
                                       a person who is registered as a professional engineer or professional licensee engineering with the Association of Professional Engineers and Geoscientists of the Province of British Columbia under the Professional Governance Act.
                                    
                                 
                              
                              
                                 Registered professional of record
                                 means a <italic>registered professional</italic> retained to undertake design work and field review in accordance with [REF:internal:nbc.divC.part2.sect2.subsect7:long] of Division C.
                              
                              
                                 Repair garage
                                 means a [REF:term:bldng]building  or part thereof where facilities are provided for
the repair or servicing of motor vehicles.
                              
                              
                                 Residential occupancy
                                 (Group C) means
the [REF:term:ccpnc] occupancy or use of a [REF:term:bldng]building or part thereof by persons for whom
sleeping accommodation is provided but who are not harboured for the
purpose of receiving [REF:term:ca]care or [REF:term:trtm]treatment and are not involuntarily detained.
                              
                              
                                 Return duct
                                 means a duct for conveying
air from a space being heated, ventilated or air-conditioned back
to the heating, ventilating or air-conditioning [REF:term:pplnc]appliance.
                              
                              
                                 Rim joist
                                 means the outermost member
in floor framing, other than blocking, be it parallel, perpendicular
or on an angle to the floor joists. (See [REF:internal:nbc.divA.part1.sect5.appnote7.div15:short].)
                              
                              
                                 Rock
                                 means that portion of the earth's
crust that is consolidated, coherent and relatively hard and is a
naturally formed, solidly bonded, mass of mineral matter that cannot
readily be broken by hand.
                              
                              
                                 Run
                                 means the horizontal distance between
two adjacent tread nosings on a stair. (See [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.appnote29.figure2:long] in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.appnote29:long] of Division B.)
                              
                              
                                 Sanitary drainage system
                                 means a drainage
system that conducts sewage.
                              
                              
                                          Secondary suite
                                          means a self-contained [REF:term:dwllng-n]dwelling unit with a prescribed [REF:term:flr-r]floor area located in a [REF:term:bldng]building or portion of a [REF:term:bldng]building of only [REF:term:rdntl-cc]residential occupancy that contains only one other [REF:term:dwllng-n]dwelling unit and common spaces, and where both [REF:term:dwllng-n]dwelling units constitute a single real estate entity. (See [REF:internal:nbc.divA.part1.sect5.appnote7.div16:short] and [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect1.subsect2.art1:long].)
                                       
                              
                                 Service room

a [REF:term:bldng]building to contain equipment associated
with [REF:term:bldng]building services. (See [REF:internal:nbc.divA.part1.sect5.appnote7.div17:short].)
                              
                              
                                 Service space
                                 means space provided in
a [REF:term:bldng]building to facilitate or conceal the
installation of [REF:term:bldng]building service facilities
such as chutes, ducts, pipes, shafts or wires.
                              
                              
                                 Service water heater
                                 means a device
for heating water for plumbing services.
                              
                              
                                 Shallow foundation

it supports.

                                 means a combined [REF:term:mk-dtctr]smoke detector and audible alarm device designed
to sound an alarm within the room or [REF:term:t]suite in
which it is located upon the detection of smoke within that room or [REF:term:t]suite.
                              
                              
                                 Smoke detector
                                 means a [REF:term:fr-dtctr] fire detector designed to operate when the
concentration of airborne combustion products exceeds a predetermined
level.
                              
                              
                                 Soil
                                 means that portion of the earth's
crust that is fragmentary, or such that some individual particles

it includes boulders, cobbles, gravel, sand, silt, clay and organic
matter.

                                 means a single wythe or

collar joint or grout-filled space and the wythes may or may not be
constructed of the same masonry materials.

a [REF:term:rvc-wtr-]service water heater with an integral

square or other improved thoroughfare 9 m (metric) or more in
width, that has been dedicated or deeded for public use and is accessible
to fire department vehicles and equipment.

of the general subsurface conditions at a [REF:term:bldng]building site by analysis of information gained by such methods as geological
surveys, in situ testing, sampling, visual inspection, laboratory
testing of samples of the subsurface materials and [REF:term:grndwtr]groundwater observations and measurements.

of rooms of complementary use, operated under a single tenancy, and

guest rooms in motels, hotels, boarding houses, rooming houses and

air from a heating, ventilating or air-conditioning [REF:term:pplnc]appliance to a space to be heated, ventilated or air-conditioned.

intended for the production and viewing of the performing arts or

audience.

or other health-related intervention to persons, where the administration

person. (See [REF:internal:nbc.divA.part1.sect5.appnote7.div21:short].)

                                 (Group B, Division
2) means the [REF:term:ccpnc]occupancy or use of a [REF:term:bldng]building or part thereof for the provision of [REF:term:trtm]treatment, and where overnight accommodation is
available to facilitate the [REF:term:trtm]treatment. (See [REF:internal:nbc.divA.part1.sect5.appnote7.div22:short].)

appendix.introduction:
These Notes are included for explanatory
purposes only and do not form part of the requirements. The number
that introduces each Note corresponds to the applicable requirement
in this Part.

paragraphs.content:
This Code is most often applied to existing or relocated buildings
when an owner wishes to rehabilitate a building, change its use, or
build an addition, or when an enforcement authority decrees that a
building or class of buildings be altered for reasons of public safety.
It is not intended that the NBC be used to enforce the retrospective
application of new requirements to existing buildings or existing
portions of relocated buildings, unless specifically required by local
regulations or bylaws. For example, although the [REF:standard:nrcc-nfc] could be interpreted
to require the installation of fire alarm, standpipe and hose, and
automatic sprinkler systems in an existing building for which there
were no requirements at the time of construction, it is the intent
of the CCBFC that the NFC not be applied in this manner to these buildings
unless the authority having jurisdiction has determined that there
is an inherent threat to occupant safety and has issued an order to
eliminate the unsafe condition, or where substantial changes or additions
are being made to an existing building or the occupancy has been changed.
(See also [REF:external:nfc]Note A-1.1.1.1.(1) of Division A of
the NFC.)

Relocated buildings that have been in use in another location
for a number of years can be considered as existing buildings, in
part, and the same analytical process can be applied as for existing
buildings. It should be noted, however, that a change in occupancy
may affect some requirements (e.g. loads and fire separations) and
relocation to an area with different wind, snow or earthquake loads
will require the application of current code requirements. Depending
on the construction of the building and the changes in load, structural
modifications may be required. Similarly, parts of a relocated or
existing building that are reconstructed, such as foundations and
basements, or parts being modified are required to be built to current
codes.

Whatever the reason, Code application to existing or relocated
buildings requires careful consideration of the level of safety needed
for that building. This consideration involves an analytical process
similar to that required to assess alternative design proposals for
new construction. See [REF:internal:nbc.divA.part1.sect2.subsect1.art1.sent1.clause2:long] for information
on achieving compliance with the Code using alternative solutions.

In developing Code requirements for new buildings, consideration
has been given to the cost they impose on a design in relation to
the perceived benefits in terms of safety. The former is definable;
the latter difficult to establish on a quantitative basis. In applying
the Code requirements to an existing building, the benefits derived
are the same as in new buildings. On the other hand, the increased
cost of implementing in an existing building a design solution that
would normally be intended for a new building may be prohibitive.

The successful application of Code requirements to existing
construction becomes a matter of balancing the cost of implementing
a requirement with the relative importance of that requirement to
the overall Code objectives. The degree to which any particular requirement
can be relaxed without affecting the intended level of safety of the
Code requires considerable judgment on the part of both the designer
and the authority having jurisdiction.

Further information on the application of Code requirements
to existing or relocated buildings can be found in the following publications:
                        
                           [REF:standard:nrcc40383]
                        
                        
                           [REF:standard:nrcc35951]
                        
                        Commentary entitled “Application of NBC Part 4 of Division
B for the Structural Evaluation and Upgrading of Existing Buildings”
of the [REF:standard:nrcc-nbcug4]
                        
                        
                           [REF:standard:nrcc43963]
                        
                        
                           [REF:standard:cbd230]

These publications can be accessed through the NRC Publications
Archive at [REF:external:https://nrc-publications.canada.ca]https://nrc-publications.canada.ca.

The NBC applies the same requirements to site-built and factory-constructed
buildings. However, it can often be difficult to determine whether
a factory-constructed building complies with the Code once it has
been delivered to the construction site because many of the wall,
roof and floor assemblies are closed in and so their components cannot
be inspected. [REF:standard:csaa277] was developed
to address this problem with regard to residential, commercial and
industrial buildings. This standard describes a procedure whereby
an independent certification agency can review the quality control
procedures of a factory and make periodic unannounced inspections
of its products. The standard is not a building code, only a procedure
for certifying compliance of factory-constructed components with a
building code or other standard. If a factory-constructed building
bears the label of an accredited certification agency indicating that
compliance with the National Building Code has been certified using
the [REF:standard:csaa277] procedure,
the accepting authority will have some assurance that the concealed
components do not require re-inspection on site.

On the other hand, standards in the [REF:standard:csaz240mhseries] do resemble a building code.
Most of the individual standards in the series contain requirements
regarding many issues also covered in the NBC. Some of these [REF:standard:csaz240mhseries] provisions are performance
requirements with no quantitative criteria, some simply reference
the applicable NBC requirements, while others contain requirements
that differ from those in the NBC. Because it would be illogical to
have two different sets of requirements for buildings—one set that
applies to site-built buildings and one set that applies to factory-constructed
buildings—the NBC does not reference these [REF:standard:csaz240mhseries] standards. One of the individual
standards in the [REF:standard:csaz240mhseries] deals with special requirements for manufactured homes related
to the fact that these houses must be moved over roads, which is an
issue the NBC does not address. Therefore, labeling that indicates
that a factory-constructed house complies with the [REF:standard:csaz240mhseries] standards can NOT be taken
as an indication that the house necessarily complies with the building
code in effect for the location where the house will be sited.

The NBC does reference [REF:standard:csaz240.10.1] which
is not actually part of the [REF:standard:csaz240mhseries]. This standard contains requirements
for surface foundations where buildings—not just houses—comply with
the deformation resistance test provided in [REF:standard:csaz240.2.1]

If a building design (e.g. material, component,
assembly or system) can be shown to meet all provisions of the applicable
acceptable solutions in Division B (e.g. it complies with the applicable
provisions of a referenced standard), it is deemed to have satisfied
the objectives and functional statements linked to those provisions
and thus to have complied with that part of the Code. In fact, if
it can be determined that a design meets all the applicable acceptable
solutions in Division B, there is no need to consult the objectives
and functional statements in Division A to determine its compliance.

Where a design differs from the acceptable
solutions in Division B, then it should be treated as an “alternative
solution.” A proponent of an alternative solution must demonstrate
that the alternative solution addresses the same issues as the applicable
acceptable solutions in Division B and their attributed objectives
and functional statements. However, because the objectives and functional
statements are entirely qualitative, demonstrating compliance with
them in isolation is not possible. Therefore, [REF:internal:nbc.divA.part1.sect2.subsect1.art1.sent1.clause2:long] identifies the principle that Division B establishes the quantitative
performance targets that alternative solutions must meet. In many
cases, these targets are not defined very precisely by the acceptable
solutions—certainly far less precisely than would be the case with
a true performance code, which would have quantitative performance
targets and prescribed methods of performance measurement for all
aspects of building performance. Nevertheless, [REF:internal:nbc.divA.part1.sect2.subsect1.art1.sent1.clause2:long] makes it clear that an effort must be made to
demonstrate that an alternative solution will perform as well as a
design that would satisfy the applicable acceptable solutions in Division
B—not “well enough” but “as well as.”

In this sense, it is Division B that defines the boundaries
between acceptable risks and the “unacceptable” risks referred to
in the statements of the Code's objectives, i.e. the risk remaining
once the applicable acceptable solutions in Division B have been implemented
represents the residual level of risk deemed to be acceptable by the
broad base of Canadians who have taken part in the consensus process
used to develop the Code.

Where Division B offers a choice between several possible designs,
it is likely that these designs may not all provide exactly the same
level of performance. Among a number of possible designs satisfying
acceptable solutions in Division B, the design providing the lowest
level of performance should generally be considered to establish the
minimum acceptable level of performance to be used in evaluating alternative
solutions for compliance with the Code.

Sometimes a single design will be used as an alternative solution
to several sets of acceptable solutions in Division B. In this case,
the level of performance required of the alternative solution should
be at least equivalent to the overall level of performance established
by all the applicable sets of acceptable solutions taken as a whole.

Each provision in Division B has been analyzed to determine
what it is intended to achieve. The resultant intent statements clarify
what undesirable results each provision seeks to preclude. These statements
are not a legal component of the Code, but are advisory in nature,
and can help Code users establish performance targets for alternative
solutions. They are published as a separate electronic document entitled
“Supplement to the NBC 2020: Intent Statements,” which is available
on the NRC's website.

A subset of the acceptable solutions in Division B may establish
criteria for particular types of designs (e.g. certain types of materials,
components, assemblies, or systems). Often such subsets of acceptable
solutions are all attributed to the same objective: OS1, Fire Safety,
for example. In some cases, the designs that are normally used to
satisfy this subset of acceptable solutions might also provide some
benefits that could be related to some other objective: OP1, Fire
Protection of the Building, for example. However, if none of the applicable
acceptable solutions are linked to Objective OP1, it is not necessary
that alternative solutions proposed to replace these acceptable solutions
provide a similar benefit related to Fire Protection of the Building.
In other words, the acceptable solutions in Division B establish acceptable
levels of performance for compliance with the Code only in those areas
defined by the objectives and functional statements attributed to
the acceptable solutions.

In demonstrating that an alternative solution will perform as
well as a design that would satisfy the applicable acceptable solutions
in Division B, its evaluation should not be limited to comparison
with the acceptable solutions to which an alternative is proposed.
It is possible that acceptable solutions elsewhere in the Code also
apply. The proposed alternative solution may be shown to perform as
well as the most apparent acceptable solution which it is replacing
but may not perform as well as other relevant acceptable solutions.
For example, an innovative sheathing material may perform adequately
as sheathing in a wall system that is braced by other means but may
not perform adequately as sheathing in a wall system where the sheathing
must provide the structural bracing. All applicable acceptable solutions
should be taken into consideration in demonstrating the compliance
of an alternative solution.

This concept relates to the provisions directly regulated by
this Code and does not apply to electrical service entrance requirements,
which are regulated by other documents.

Application of the definition of grade to stepped buildings
on sloping sites often results in such buildings being designated
as being greater than 4 storeys in building height even though there
may be only 2, 3 or 4 storeys (metric) at any one location. [REF:internal:nbc.divA.part1.sect5.appnote6.figure1:long] illustrates this application compared to a similar
building on a flat site.

Under [REF:internal:nbc.divA.part1.sect3.subsect3.art4.sent2:long], Building A can be considered
as being 4 storeys (metric) in building height instead of 7 storeys
in building height. Both Building A and B are comparable with regard
to fire safety and egress.

This relaxation applies to the determination of building height
only. All other requirements continue to apply as appropriate.
