Where a doorway or stairway empties onto a [REF:term:rmp]ramp through a side wall, there shall be a level area extending
across the full width of the [REF:term:rmp]ramp, and for
a distance of 300 mm (metric) on either side of the wall opening,
except one side if it abuts on an end wall.

Where a doorway or stairway empties onto a [REF:term:rmp]ramp through an end wall, there shall be a level area extending
across the full width of the [REF:term:rmp]ramp and along
its length for not less than 900 mm (metric).
One handrail shall be provided on stairs that are less than 1 100 mm (metric) in width.
One handrail shall be provided on each side of

clauses.text: stairs that are 1 100 mm (metric) or more in width,
curved [REF:term:flght]flights of any width, and
[REF:term:rmp]ramps.

content.text:
In addition to [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect4.subsect6.art5.sent2:short], intermediate
handrails shall be provided so that

clauses.text:
a handrail is reachable within 750 mm (metric) of all portions
of the required [REF:term:xt]exit width,

at least one portion of the stair or [REF:term:rmp]ramp between two handrails is the minimum width required for stairways
or [REF:term:rmp]ramps (see [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect4.subsect3.art2.sent8:long]
                              [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect4.subsect3.art3.sent4:long]), and

all other portions of the stair or [REF:term:rmp]ramp between two handrails have a clear width of 510 mm (metric) or
more.

content.text:
Where a stair or [REF:term:rmp]ramp is wider than
its required [REF:term:xt]exit width, handrails shall be
located along the most direct path of travel. (See [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect9.appnote161:short].)

Handrails shall be continuously graspable along their entire
length, be free of any sharp or abrasive elements, and have

clauses.text: a circular cross-section with an outside diameter not less than 30 mm (metric) and not more than 50 mm (metric), or

a non-circular cross-section with a perimeter not less than 100 mm (metric) and not more than 160 mm (metric) and whose largest
cross-sectional dimension is not more than 57 mm (metric).

content.text:
The height of handrails on stairs, on aisles with steps and
on [REF:term:rmp]ramps shall be measured vertically from
the top of the handrail to

clauses.text:
a straight line drawn tangent to the tread nosings of the stair
or aisle step served by the handrail (see [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.appnote38:long]), or

the surface of the [REF:term:rmp]ramp, floor or landing
served by the handrail.

content.text:
Except as provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect4.subsect6.art5.sent8:short] and [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect8.subsect3.art5.sent1.clause5:long], the height of handrails on stairs,
on aisles with steps and on [REF:term:rmp]ramps shall be

clauses.text: not less than 865 mm (metric), and
not more than 1 070 mm (metric).

content.text:
Handrails installed in addition to required handrails need not
comply with [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect4.subsect6.art5.sent7:short].

Required handrails shall be continuously graspable throughout
the length of

clauses.text: a [REF:term:rmp]ramp, and

a [REF:term:flght]flight of stairs, from the bottom
riser to the top riser.

content.text:
Except where interrupted by doorways, at least one handrail
shall be continuous throughout the length of a stairway or [REF:term:rmp]ramp, including at landings.

Handrails shall be terminated in a manner that will not obstruct
pedestrian travel or create a hazard. (See [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect9.appnote162:short]).
At least one handrail at the side of a stairway or [REF:term:rmp]ramp shall extend horizontally not less than 300 mm (metric) beyond the top and bottom of the stairway or [REF:term:rmp]ramp.

The clearance between a handrail and any surface behind it shall
be not less than

clauses.text: 50 mm (metric), or

60 mm (metric) if the surface behind the handrail is rough
or abrasive.

content.text:
Handrails and their supports shall be designed and constructed
to withstand the loading values specified in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect5.art14.sent7:long].

A [REF:term:rmp]ramp shall have handrails on both
sides.
Every [REF:term:xt]exit shall have a wall or a well-secured [REF:term:guard]guard on each side, where

clauses.text: there is a difference in elevation of more than 600 mm (metric) between the walking surface and the adjacent surface, or

the adjacent surface within 1.2 m (metric) of the walking
surface has a slope of more than 1 in 2.

content.text:
Except as required by [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect4.subsect6.art6.sent4:short], the height of [REF:term:guard]guards for [REF:term:xt]exit stairs and [REF:term:xt]exit
                           [REF:term:rmp]ramps as well as their landings shall be not less than 1 070 mm (metric).

The height of [REF:term:guard]guards shall be measured
vertically to the top of the [REF:term:guard]guard from

clauses.text:
a line drawn through the outside edges of the stair nosings,
or
the surface of the [REF:term:rmp]ramp or landing.

content.text:
The height of [REF:term:guard]guards for exterior
stairs and landings more than 10 m (metric) above adjacent ground
level shall be not less than 1 500 mm (metric) measured vertically
to the top of the [REF:term:guard]guard from the surface
of the landing or from a line drawn through the outside edges of the
stair nosings.

Except as provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect3.subsect1.art18.sent3:long] and [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect3.subsect4.art7:long]
                           [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect3.subsect5.art10:short], [REF:term:guard]guards in [REF:term:xt]exits shall not have any openings that
permit the passage of a spherical object whose diameter is more than 100 mm (metric).

In a stairway, a window for which the distance measured vertically
between the bottom of the window and a line drawn through the outside
edges of the stair nosings is less than 900 mm (metric), or a
window that extends to less than 1 070 mm (metric) above the landing,
shall

clauses.text: be protected by a [REF:term:guard]guard that is

subclauses.text:
located approximately 900 mm (metric) above a line drawn
through the outside edges of the stair nosings, or

not less than 1 070 mm (metric) high measured to the top
of the [REF:term:guard]guard from the surface of the landing,
or

clauses.text:
be fixed in position and designed to resist the lateral design
loads specified for [REF:term:guard]guards and walls in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect5.art14:long]
                              [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect5.art16:long]

content.text:
Except for [REF:term:guard]guards conforming to [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect3.subsect5.art10:long], [REF:term:guard]guards that protect
a level located more than one [REF:term:tr]storey or 4.2 m (metric) above the adjacent level shall be designed so that no
member, attachment or opening located between 140 mm (metric) and 900 mm (metric) above the level being protected by the [REF:term:guard]guard facilitates climbing. (See [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.appnote47:long].)

Except as provided
in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect4.subsect6.art7.sent2:short] and as provided for aisles
in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect3.subsect2.art5:long], [REF:term:rmp]ramps shall
have a uniform slope along their length and a maximum slope of 1 in 12 (metric).

Except as provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect8:long], [REF:term:rmp]ramps in [REF:term:ndtrl-cc]industrial occupancies shall have a uniform slope along their length and a maximum slope
of

clauses.text: 1 in 6 (metric) for interior [REF:term:rmp]ramps, and
1 in 10 (metric) for exterior [REF:term:rmp]ramps.

content.text: Curb ramps shall be designed in accordance with [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect8.subsect3.art4.sent1.clause2:long].

Except as permitted for [REF:term:dwllng-n]dwelling units and by [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect4.subsect7.art5.sent1:long] for fire escapes, steps for stairs
shall have a [REF:term:run]run of not less than 280 mm (metric) between successive steps.
Steps for stairs referred to in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect4.subsect6.art8.sent1:short] shall have

clauses.text: a rise between successive treads not less than 125 mm (metric) and not more than 180 mm (metric), and
a riser with either no rakeback or a rakeback of not more than 38 mm (metric), or if nosing is provided, the underside of the nosing with an angle of not less than 60° from the horizontal.

content.text:
Except as provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect3.subsect4.art7:long] and except
for fire escape stairs, stairs that are principally used for maintenance
and service, and stairs that serve [REF:term:ndtrl-cc]industrial
occupancies other than [REF:term:trg-grg]storage garages, steps for stairs shall have no open risers.

Except in fire escape stairs and where an exterior stair adjoins
a [REF:term:wlkw]walkway as permitted in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect4.subsect6.art3.sent3:long], risers, measured as the vertical nosing-to-nosing
distance, shall be of uniform height in any one [REF:term:flght]flight, with a maximum tolerance of

clauses.text: 5 mm (metric) between adjacent treads or landings, and

10 mm (metric) between the tallest and shortest risers in
a [REF:term:flght]flight.

content.text: Except in fire escape stairs, treads shall have a uniform [REF:term:run]run with a maximum tolerance of

clauses.text: 5 mm (metric) between adjacent treads, and

10 mm (metric) between the deepest and shallowest treads
in a [REF:term:flght]flight.

content.text: Treads and risers shall not differ significantly in [REF:term:run]run and rise in successive [REF:term:flght]flights in any stair system.

The slope of treads or landings shall not exceed 1 in
50 (metric).

Except as permitted by [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect4.subsect6.art8.sent10:short], the top of the nosing of stair treads shall have a rounded or
beveled edge extending not less than 6 mm (metric) and not more
than 13 mm (metric) measured horizontally from the front of the
nosing.

The front edge of stair treads in [REF:term:xt]exits and public [REF:term:cc-t-xt]access to exits shall be
at right angles to the direction of [REF:term:xt]exit travel.

If resilient material is used to cover the nosing of a stair
tread, the minimum rounded or beveled edge required by [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect4.subsect6.art8.sent8:short] is permitted to be reduced to 3 mm (metric).
[REF:term:xt]Exit stair [REF:term:flght]flights shall consist solely of

clauses.text: straight [REF:term:flght]flights, or
curved [REF:term:flght]flights complying with [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect4.subsect6.art9.sent2:short].

content.text: A curved [REF:term:flght]flight used as an [REF:term:xt]exit shall have

clauses.text: a handrail on each side,
a minimum [REF:term:run]run of 240 mm (metric),

a [REF:term:run]run that conforms to [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect4.subsect6.art8:long] when measured at a point 300 mm (metric) from
the centre line of the handrail at the narrow end of the tread, and
an inside radius that is not less than twice the stair width.

content.text:
[REF:term:tpr-thr]Tapered treads shall have a consistent
angle and uniform [REF:term:run]run and rise dimensions
in accordance with the construction tolerances stipulated in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect4.subsect6.art8:long] when measured at a point 300 mm (metric) from
the centre line of the handrail at the narrow end of the tread.
All [REF:term:tpr-thr]tapered treads within a [REF:term:flght]flight shall turn in the same direction.

The [REF:term:flr-r]floor area on each side of a [REF:term:hrzntl-x]horizontal exit shall be sufficient to accommodate
the occupants of both [REF:term:flr-r]floor areas, allowing
not less than 0.5 m2
                            (metric) of clear floor space
per person, except that 1.5 m2
                            (metric) shall be
provided for each person in a wheelchair and 2.5 m2
                            (metric) for each bedridden patient.

If vestibules, enclosed balconies or bridges are used as parts
of a [REF:term:hrzntl-x]horizontal exit, their clear width
shall be not less than that of the [REF:term:xt]exit doorways
opening into them, except that handrails are not permitted to project
into this clear width more than 100 mm (metric).

In a [REF:term:hrzntl-x] horizontal exit where there
is a difference in level between the connected [REF:term:flr-r]floor areas, slopes not more than those specified for [REF:term:rmp]ramps in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect4.subsect6.art7:long] are permitted
to be used.
No stairs or steps shall be used in a [REF:term:hrzntl-x]horizontal exit.

If 2 doors are provided in a [REF:term:hrzntl-x]horizontal
exit that comprises a part of the required number of [REF:term:xt]exits from the [REF:term:flr-r] floor areas on both sides of the [REF:term:xt]exit

clauses.text:
the doors shall be mounted adjacent to each other with the door
on the right side in the direction of travel through the [REF:term:hrzntl-x] horizontal exit swinging in the direction
of travel through the [REF:term:hrzntl-x]horizontal exit, and

signs shall be provided on each side of the [REF:term:hrzntl-x] horizontal exit to indicate the door that swings in the direction
of travel from that side.

content.text:
If a [REF:term:hrzntl-x] horizontal exit utilizes
bridges between [REF:term:bldng]buildings  or outside balconies,
the bridges or balconies shall conform to [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect2.subsect3.art19:long]

The distance between a stair riser and the leading edge of a
door during its swing shall be not less than 300 mm (metric).

Except as provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect4.subsect6.art11.sent3:short] and where doorways are used to confine the spillage of [REF:term:flmmbl-l]flammable liquids within a [REF:term:rvc-rm]service room or within a room in an [REF:term:ndtrl-cc]industrial occupancy, a threshold for a doorway in an [REF:term:xt]exit shall be not more than 13 mm (metric) higher
than the surrounding finished floor surface.

Except for doors providing access to ground level as required
by [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect3.subsect1.art7.sent1.clause4:long]
                           [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect3.subsect1.art7.sent1.clause5:short], an [REF:term:xt]exit door
is permitted to open onto not more than one step which shall be not
more than 150 mm (metric) high where there is a risk of blockage
by ice or snow.

[REF:term:xt]Exit doors shall be clearly identifiable.
(See [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect9.appnote164:short].)

No door leaf in an [REF:term:xt]exit doorway with
more than one leaf shall be less than 610 mm (metric) wide.

Where an [REF:term:xt]exit door leading directly
to the outside is subject to being obstructed by parked vehicles or
storage because of its location, a visible sign or a physical barrier
prohibiting such obstructions shall be installed on the exterior side
of the door.

Except for doors serving a single [REF:term:dwllng-n]dwelling
unit and except as permitted by [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect4.subsect6.art12.sent2:short] and [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect4.subsect6.art14:long], every [REF:term:xt]exit door shall

clauses.text:
open in the direction of [REF:term:xt]exit travel,
and
swing on its vertical axis.

content.text: [REF:term:xt]Exit doors need not conform to [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect4.subsect6.art12.sent1:short], where

clauses.text:
they serve [REF:term:trg-grg]storage garages serving
not more than one [REF:term:dwllng-n]dwelling unit,

they serve accessory [REF:term:bldng]buildings serving
not more than one [REF:term:dwllng-n]dwelling unit,
they

subclauses.text:
serve storage [REF:term:t]suites not more than 28 m2
                                  (metric) in area that are on the [REF:term:frt-tr]first storey in warehousing [REF:term:bldng]buildings, and
open directly outdoors at ground level, or

clauses.text:
they serve individual self-service storage units referred to
in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect10:long]

content.text:
An [REF:term:xt]exit door that is normally required
to be kept closed

clauses.text: shall be provided with a self-closing mechanism, and

shall never be secured in an open position except as permitted
by [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect1.subsect8.art14.sent1:long].

content.text:
Except as permitted by [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect4.subsect6.art14.sent2:short]
                           [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect4.subsect6.art12.sent2:medium], an [REF:term:xt]exit door leading directly
to outdoors at ground level is permitted to be a sliding door provided
it conforms to [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect3.subsect1.art12.sent1:long].

An [REF:term:xt]exit door serving a Group B, Division
1 [REF:term:ccpnc]occupancy, or an [REF:term:mpdd-gr-]impeded egress zone in other [REF:term:ccpnc]occupancies, is permitted to be a sliding door that does not conform to [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect3.subsect1.art12.sent1:long] provided it is designed to be released in conformance
with [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect3.subsect1.art13:long]
Except as permitted by [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect4.subsect6.art15.sent3:short], a revolving door, if used, shall

clauses.text: be collapsible,

have hinged doors providing equivalent exiting capacity located
adjacent to it,

be used as an [REF:term:xt]exit from the ground floor
level only,
not be used at the foot of any stairway, and

have all glass in door leaves and enclosure panels conforming
to

subclauses.text: [REF:standard:cgsb-12.1] or
[REF:standard:cgsb-12.11]

content.text:
Except as permitted by [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect4.subsect6.art15.sent3:short], a revolving door shall not be considered to have an exiting capacity
for more than 45 persons.

An electrically powered revolving door is not required to conform
to [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect4.subsect6.art15.sent1:short]
                           [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect4.subsect6.art15.sent2:short] provided

clauses.text:
the door leaves will collapse and stop automatic rotation of
the door system and not obstruct the doorway if a force not more than
that specified in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect4.subsect6.art16.sent2:long] is applied at the centre
of a door leaf,

the door leaves are capable of being opened from inside the [REF:term:bldng]building without requiring keys, special devices,
or specialized knowledge of the door opening mechanism,

the allowable exiting capacity is based on the clear width of
passage through the door enclosure when the doors are fully collapsed,

a permanent sign, whose centre line is between 1 000 mm (metric) and 1 500 mm (metric) above the floor, is placed on each face
of each door leaf indicating the method for collapsing the door leaf
in an emergency, and
glass used for door leaves and enclosure panels is safety glazing conforming to

subclauses.text: [REF:standard:cgsb-12.1] or
[REF:standard:cgsb-12.11]

content.text:
Except for devices on doors serving a [REF:term:cntnd-r]contained use area or an [REF:term:mpdd-gr-]impeded egress
zone designed to be remotely released in conformance with [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect3.subsect1.art13:long], and except as permitted by [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect4.subsect6.art16.sent5:short]
                           [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect4.subsect6.art16.sent6:short] and [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect4.subsect6.art17:long], locking, latching and other fastening devices
on a principal entrance door to a [REF:term:bldng]building as well as those on every [REF:term:xt]exit door shall
include release hardware complying with [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect8.subsect3.art8.sent1.clause2:long] to permit the door to be readily opened from the inside with not
more than one releasing operation and without requiring keys, special
devices or specialized knowledge of the door-opening mechanism. (See [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect9.appnote165:short].)
If a door is equipped with a latching mechanism, a device complying with [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect4.subsect6.art16.sent3:short] shall be installed on

clauses.text:
every [REF:term:xt]exit door from a [REF:term:flr-r]floor area containing an [REF:term:mbl-ccpn]assembly occupancy having an [REF:term:ccpnt-ld]occupant load more than
100,

every door leading to an [REF:term:xt]exit lobby
from an [REF:term:xt]exit stair shaft, and every exterior
door leading from an [REF:term:xt]exit stair shaft in a [REF:term:bldng]building having an [REF:term:ccpnt-ld]occupant
load more than 100, and

every [REF:term:xt]exit door from a [REF:term:flr-r]floor area containing a [REF:term:hgh-hzrd]high-hazard
industrial occupancy.

content.text: The device required in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect4.subsect6.art16.sent2:short] shall

clauses.text: extend across not less than one half of the width of the door,
release the latch, and

allow the door to swing wide open when a force not more than
that specified in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect8.subsect3.art6.sent8:long] is applied to the device
in the direction of travel to the [REF:term:xt]exit.

content.text:
Except as required by [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect8.subsect3.art6.sent8:long], every [REF:term:xt]exit door shall be designed and installed so that,
when the latch is released, the door will open under a force of not
more than 90 N (metric), applied at the knob or other latch releasing
device.

Electromagnetic locks that do not incorporate latches, pins
or other similar devices to keep the door in the closed position are
permitted to be installed on doors, other than those leading directly
from a [REF:term:hgh-hzrd]high-hazard industrial occupancy, provided

clauses.text:
the [REF:term:bldng]building is equipped with a fire
alarm system,
the locking device releases upon actuation of the [REF:term:lrm-gnl]alarm signal from the [REF:term:bldng]building's fire alarm system,

the locking device releases immediately upon loss of power controlling
the electromagnetic locking mechanism and its associated auxiliary
controls,

except for locking devices installed in conformance with [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect4.subsect6.art16.sent6:short], the locking device releases immediately
upon actuation of a manually operated switch readily accessible only
to authorized personnel,

except as provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect4.subsect6.art16.sent5.clause12:short], a force of not more than 90 N (metric) applied to the door
opening hardware initiates an irreversible process that will release
the locking device within 15 s (metric) and not re-lock until
the door has been opened,

upon release, the locking device must be reset manually by the
actuation of the switch referred to in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect4.subsect6.art16.sent5.clause4:short],

a visual information
sign complying with [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect8.subsect3:long] is
permanently mounted on the door to indicate that the locking device
will release within 15 s (metric) of applying pressure to the
door-opening hardware,

a tactile information
sign complying with [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect8.subsect3:long] is permanently
mounted near the door to indicate that the locking device will release
within 15 s (metric) of applying pressure to the door-opening
hardware,

the total time delay for all electromagnetic locks in any path
of egress to release is not more than 15 s,

where a bypass switch is installed to allow testing of the fire
alarm system, actuation of the switch

subclauses.text:
can prevent the release of the locking device by the fire alarm
system, as stated in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect4.subsect6.art16.sent5.clause2:short], during
the test, and

causes an audible and visible signal to be indicated at the
fire alarm annunciator panel required by [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect2.subsect4.art9:long] and at the monitoring station specified in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect2.subsect4.art8.sent4:long],

clauses.text: emergency lighting complying with [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect2.subsect7.art3.sent1:long] is provided, and

where they are installed on doors providing emergency crossover
access to [REF:term:flr-r]floor areas from [REF:term:xt]exit stairs in accordance with [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect4.subsect6.art18:long],

subclauses.text:
the locking device releases immediately upon the operation of
a manual station for the fire alarm system located on the wall on
the [REF:term:xt]exit stair side not more than 600
mm (metric) from the door,

a visual information
sign displaying the words “Re-entry door unlocked by
fire alarm” that complies
with [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect8.subsect3:long] is permanently mounted
on the door on the [REF:term:xt]exit stair side, and

a tactile information
sign displaying the words “Re-entry door unlocked by fire alarm” that
complies with [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect8.subsect3:long] is permanently mounted
near the door on the exit stair side.

content.text:
Electromagnetic locks that do not incorporate latches, pins
or other similar devices to keep the door in the closed position are
permitted to be installed on doors in Group B, Division 2 and Division
3 [REF:term:ccpnc]occupancies, provided

clauses.text: the [REF:term:bldng]building is

subclauses.text: equipped with a fire alarm system, and
[REF:term:prnklrd]sprinklered,

clauses.text: the electromagnetic lock releases upon

subclauses.text:
actuation of the [REF:term:lrm-gnl]alarm signal from
the [REF:term:bldng]building's fire alarm system,
loss of its power supply and of power to its auxiliary controls,

actuation of a manually operated switch that is readily accessible
at a constantly attended location within the locked space, and

actuation of the manual station installed within 0.5 m (metric) of each door and equipped with an auxiliary contact, which directly
releases the electromagnetic lock,

clauses.text:
upon release, the electromagnetic lock requires manual resetting
by actuation of the switch referred to in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect4.subsect6.art16.sent6.clause2.subclause3:short],

a visual information
sign complying with [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect8.subsect3:long] that displays
the words “Emergency exit unlocked by fire alarm” is
permanently mounted on the door,

a tactile information
sign complying with [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect8.subsect3:long] that displays
the words “Emergency exit unlocked by fire alarm” is permanently mounted
near the door,

the operation of any by-pass switch, where provided for testing
of the fire alarm system, sets off an audible signal and a visible
signal at the fire alarm annunciator panel and at the monitoring station
referred to in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect2.subsect4.art7.sent4:long], and
emergency lighting complying with [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect2.subsect7.art3.sent1:long] is provided.

content.text:
Except as provided
in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect4.subsect6.art17.sent9:long], door release hardware for the operation
of the doors referred to in this Section shall be installed between 900 mm (metric) and 1 100 mm (metric) above the finished
floor.

articles.title: Security for Banks and Mercantile Floor Areas

content.text:
If a [REF:term:bldng]building is [REF:term:prnklrd]sprinklered throughout, the requirements of [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect4.subsect6.art16.sent1:long] are permitted to be waived for [REF:term:xt]exit and egress doors complying with [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect4.subsect6.art17.sent2:short]
                           [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect4.subsect6.art17.sent9:short] that serve a [REF:term:flr-r]floor area or part of a [REF:term:flr-r]floor
area used exclusively for

clauses.text: a bank, or
the sale of retail merchandise.

content.text:
[REF:term:xt] Exit and egress doors referred to in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect4.subsect6.art17.sent1:short] shall be designed to prevent locking
at any time that the part of the [REF:term:flr-r]floor area that they serve is open to the public.

A sign with the words “This door shall not be locked at any
time that the public is present” in letters not less than 50
mm (metric) high shall be permanently affixed to both sides of doors
referred to in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect4.subsect6.art17.sent1:short].

[REF:term:xt]Exit and egress facilities complying
with [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect4.subsect6.art17.sent5:short]
                           [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect4.subsect6.art17.sent9:short] shall be incorporated
for egress by persons other than the public from a [REF:term:flr-r]floor area or a part of a [REF:term:flr-r]floor area referred to in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect4.subsect6.art17.sent1:short] during times
when the public is neither present nor being admitted to the area
that they serve.

In [REF:term:xt]exit and egress facilities referred
to in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect4.subsect6.art17.sent4:short], at least one door
at each [REF:term:xt]exit and egress location shall

clauses.text:
be operable in conformance with [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect4.subsect6.art16.sent1:long],
or
be equipped with locks conforming to [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect4.subsect6.art16.sent5:long] that release immediately

subclauses.text:
if an [REF:term:lrt-gnl]alert signal or [REF:term:lrm-gnl]alarm signal is initiated in the fire alarm
system, or
the sprinkler system is actuated.

content.text:
A door referred to in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect4.subsect6.art17.sent5:short] shall be permanently and distinctly marked to indicate that it
is an emergency [REF:term:xt]exit.

[REF:term:xt]Exit and egress facilities required
for evacuation of persons other than the public from a [REF:term:flr-r]floor area or a part of a [REF:term:flr-r]floor area referred to in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect4.subsect6.art17.sent1:short] shall have an aggregate width based on the maximum number of persons
other than the public and determined in accordance with [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect4.subsect3.art1:long]
                           [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect4.subsect3.art3:long]

Travel distance to an [REF:term:xt]exit referred
to in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect4.subsect6.art17.sent7:short] shall not exceed the
travel distance determined in accordance with [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect4.subsect2:long]

[REF:term:xt]Exit and egress doors serving a [REF:term:flr-r]floor area or part of a [REF:term:flr-r]floor
area referred to in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect4.subsect6.art17.sent1:short] are permitted to be equipped with locks that require keys, special
devices or specialized knowledge of the door opening mechanism, provided

clauses.text: the doors do not lead into [REF:term:xt]exit stairs,

the doors do not lead from [REF:term:xt]exit stairs
to the exterior of the [REF:term:bldng]building,
the doors do not serve any other [REF:term:ccpnc]occupancy,
the area served contains at least one telephone

subclauses.text: that is accessible and in operation at all times,
that is not coin or card operated, and
marked to indicate that it is for emergency use,

clauses.text:
the area served is illuminated by normal power or by emergency
power when the doors are locked,

there are provisions that enable an announcement to be made
throughout the area served before the locks are fastened, and
the locks are designed for use during times that the [REF:term:bldng]building is not occupied.

articles.title: Emergency Crossover Access to Floor Areas

content.text:
Except as permitted in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect4.subsect6.art18.sent2:short], doors providing access to [REF:term:flr-r]floor areas from [REF:term:xt]exit stairs shall not have locking
devices to prevent entry into any [REF:term:flr-r]floor area from which the travel distance up or down to an unlocked door is
more than 2 [REF:term:tr]storeys.

Doors referred to in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect4.subsect6.art18.sent1:short] are permitted to be equipped with electromagnetic locks, provided
they comply with [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect4.subsect6.art16.sent5:long]
                           [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect4.subsect6.art16.sent6:short].

Doors referred to in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect4.subsect6.art18.sent1:short] shall be identified by visual and tactile information signs complying with [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect8.subsect3:long] mounted on the stairway side to
indicate that they are openable from that side.
Locked doors intended to prevent entry into a [REF:term:flr-r]floor area from an [REF:term:xt]exit stair shall

clauses.text:
be identified by visual and tactile information signs complying with [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect8.subsect3:long] mounted on the stairway side to
indicate the location of the nearest unlocked door in each direction
of travel, and

be openable with a master key that fits all locking devices
and is kept in a designated location accessible to firefighters or
be provided with a wired glass panel not less than 0.0645 m2
                               (metric) in area and located not more than 300 mm (metric) from the door opening hardware.

content.text:
Where access to [REF:term:flr-r]floor areas through
unlocked doors is required by [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect4.subsect6.art18.sent1:short], it shall be possible for a person entering the [REF:term:flr-r]floor area to have access through unlocked doors within the [REF:term:flr-r]floor area to at least one other [REF:term:xt]exit.

articles.title: Floor Numbering and Identification of Stair Shafts

content.text:
Arabic numerals indicating the assigned floor number in both visual and tactile forms in
accordance with [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect8.subsect3:long] shall
be mounted permanently on the wall on the stair side and on the floor side at
the latch side of doors to [REF:term:xt]exit stair shafts.

Upper case letters indicating the designation assigned to each [REF:term:xt]exit stair shaft in both
visual and tactile forms in accordance with [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect8.subsect3:long] shall be mounted permanently on the wall on
the stair side and on the floor side at the latch side of doors to [REF:term:xt]exit stair shafts.
Except as permitted by [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect4.subsect7.art1.sent2:short], fire escapes shall not be erected on a [REF:term:bldng]building.

If it is impracticable to provide one or more of the [REF:term:xt]exit facilities listed in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect4.subsect1.art4:long], fire escapes conforming to [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect4.subsect7.art2:long]
                           [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect4.subsect7.art7:long] are permitted
to serve [REF:term:flr-r]floor areas in an existing [REF:term:bldng]building provided the [REF:term:flr-r]floor
areas served are not more than

clauses.text: 2 [REF:term:tr]storeys above ground level in [REF:term:ca-cc]care, [REF:term:trtm]treatment or [REF:term:dtnt-cc]detention occupancies, and
5 [REF:term:tr]storeys above ground level in other [REF:term:ccpnc]occupancies.

content.text:
Fire escapes shall be of metal or concrete, of the stair type
extending to ground level, constructed throughout in a strong substantial
manner and securely fixed to the [REF:term:bldng]building, except that wooden fire escapes are permitted to be used on [REF:term:bldng]buildings of [REF:term:cmbtbl-c]combustible
construction if all posts and brackets are not less than 89 mm (metric) in their least dimension and all other woodwork is not
less than 38 mm (metric) in its least dimension.

Access to fire escapes shall be from corridors through doors
at floor level, except that access from a [REF:term:dwllng-n]dwelling
unit is permitted to be through a casement window having an
unobstructed opening not less than 1 100 mm (metric) high by 550 mm (metric) wide with a sill height of not more than 900 mm (metric) above the inside floor.

The clear area of a fire escape balcony onto which a door opens,
shall be not less than 1 m2
                            (metric).

If a fire escape serves any [REF:term:tr]storey above
the second, openings located in a zone described in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect4.subsect7.art4.sent2:short], including access doorways in the
exterior walls of the [REF:term:bldng]building to which
the fire escape is attached, shall be protected by [REF:term:clr]closures conforming to [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect1.subsect8:long]

The zone referred to in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect4.subsect7.art4.sent1:short] extends from any balcony, platform or stairway of a fire escape
to a distance

clauses.text: 3 m (metric) horizontally,
10 m (metric) below, or
1.8 m (metric) above.

content.text:
Stairs shall be inclined at an angle of not more than 45° (metric) with the horizontal, and their steps shall have risers
not more than 210 mm (metric) high and treads not less than 220 mm (metric) wide exclusive of nosing.

Stairway headroom shall be not less than 1 950 mm (metric) plus the height of one riser measured vertically above the nosing
of any tread or platform.

The width of a fire escape shall conform to [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect4.subsect3.art1:long]
                           [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect4.subsect3.art3:long], except that the width is permitted to be reduced
to 550 mm (metric) provided the fire escape serves

clauses.text: not more than 3 [REF:term:tr]storeys, and
not more than 15 persons.

content.text:
If a [REF:term:flght]flight of stairs leading to
the ground at the foot of a fire escape is not fixed in position,
it shall be held in the raised position without a latch or locking
device, and shall be fitted with a counterbalancing device that will
permit it to be easily and quickly brought into position for use.

The open sides of every platform, balcony and stairway forming
part of a fire escape shall be protected by [REF:term:guard]guards not less than 920 mm (metric) high measured vertically above
the nosing of any tread or platform.

The top rail of a [REF:term:guard]guard is permitted
to serve as a handrail if it is free from obstructions which could
break a handhold.

A wall handrail shall be installed if the fire escape is more
than 550 mm (metric) wide.

Unless it can be shown that the size of openings that exceed
this limit does not present a hazard, there shall be no opening that
permits the passage of a sphere whose diameter is more than 100 mm (metric) through a [REF:term:guard]guard for a fire
escape.

Unless it can be shown that the location and size of an opening
do not present a hazard, a [REF:term:guard]guard for a
fire escape shall be designed so that no member, attachment or opening
located between 140 mm (metric) and 900 mm (metric) above
a platform or the nosing of any tread will facilitate climbing.

Platforms for a fire escape shall be provided in conformance
with the requirements for stair landings in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect4.subsect6.art3:long]
                           [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect4.subsect6.art4:long]

This Section applies to vertical transportation facilities installed
in a [REF:term:bldng]building, including elevators, escalators
and dumbwaiters.

Elevators in a [REF:term:bldng]building within the
scope of [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect2.subsect6:long] shall conform to [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect2.subsect6.art4:long]
                           [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect2.subsect6.art5:long]
                           [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect2.subsect6.art6:long]

The design, construction, installation and [REF:term:ltrtn]alteration of every elevator, escalator and dumbwaiter shall conform to the Safety Standards Act and pursuant regulations. (See [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect9.appnote169:long].)

Before being placed in service, every elevator, escalator or dumbwaiter installation, including safety and control devices, shall be inspected and tested in accordance with the Safety Standards Act and pursuant regulations. (See [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect9.appnote169:long].)
Passenger elevators shall conform to Appendix E of [REF:standard:asmea17.1]

Except as permitted by [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect5.subsect3.art1.sent2:short], a [REF:term:vrtcl-rv]vertical service space used as
an elevator hoistway shall be separated from all other portions of
each adjacent [REF:term:tr]storey by a [REF:term:fr-prtn]fire separation having a [REF:term:fr-rtnc-]fire-resistance
rating conforming to [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect5.subsect3.art1.table1:long] for the [REF:term:fr-rtnc-]fire-resistance rating required by [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect2.subsect2:long] for

clauses.text:
the floor assembly above the [REF:term:tr]storey,
or

the floor assembly below the [REF:term:tr]storey,
if there is no floor assembly above.

content.title: Fire Separation for Vertical Transportation Space

header_rows.content:
[REF:term:fr-rtnc-]Fire-Resistance
Rating of [REF:term:fr-prtn]Fire Separation Required
for Floor Assembly

Minimum [REF:term:fr-rtnc-]Fire-Resistance Rating of [REF:term:vrtcl-rv]Vertical
Service Space for Elevator Hoistway

Minimum [REF:term:fr-rtnc-]Fire-Resistance Rating of [REF:term:vrtcl-rv]Vertical
Service Space for Dumbwaiters

content.text:
Passenger elevators, other than those provided for firefighters
in accordance with [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect2.subsect6.art5:long], are permitted to be
located within [REF:term:ntrcnnct]interconnected floor space without being enclosed in a hoistway separated from the remainder
of the [REF:term:bldng]building, provided the elevator
machinery is located in a room separated from the remainder of the [REF:term:bldng]building by a [REF:term:fr-prtn]fire separation having a [REF:term:fr-rtnc-]fire-resistance rating not
less than that required for hoistways by [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect5.subsect3.art1.sent1:short].

A [REF:term:vrtcl-rv]vertical service space containing
a dumbwaiter shall be separated from all other portions of each adjacent [REF:term:tr]storey by a [REF:term:fr-prtn]fire separation having a [REF:term:fr-rtnc-]fire-resistance rating conforming
to [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect5.subsect3.art1.table1:long] for the [REF:term:fr-rtnc-]fire-resistance
rating required by [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect2.subsect2:long] for

clauses.text: the floor assembly above the [REF:term:tr]storey or

the floor assembly below the [REF:term:tr]storey,
if there is no floor assembly above.

articles.title: Fire Separations for Elevator Machine Rooms

content.text:
Except as permitted by [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect5.subsect3.art3.sent2:short], a room containing elevator machinery shall be separated from all
other parts of the [REF:term:bldng]building by a [REF:term:fr-prtn]fire separation having a [REF:term:fr-rtnc-]fire-resistance rating not less than that required for the [REF:term:vrtcl-rv]vertical service space containing the elevator
hoistway.

A room containing elevator machinery need not be separated from
the elevator hoistway that it serves provided the room and the hoistway
are separated from all other parts of the [REF:term:bldng]building by a [REF:term:fr-prtn]fire separation having a [REF:term:fr-rtnc-]fire-resistance rating not less than that
required for the [REF:term:vrtcl-rv]vertical service space containing the elevator hoistway.

Except as provided
in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect5.subsect4.art1.sent2:short], if one or
more elevators are provided in a [REF:term:bldng]building, at least one elevator
on each [REF:term:tr]storey with access to an elevator
shall have inside dimensions that will accommodate and
provide adequate access for a patient stretcher 2 010 mm (metric) long and 610 mm (metric) wide in the prone position. (See [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect9.appnote170:short].)

The inside dimensions stipulated in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect5.subsect4.art1.sent1:short] do not apply to limited-use/limited-application elevators
designed and installed in accordance with [REF:standard:asmea17.1]

An elevator satisfying the requirements of [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect5.subsect4.art1.sent1:short] shall be clearly identified on the
main entrance level of the [REF:term:bldng]building.

Arabic numerals indicating the assigned floor number shall be
mounted permanently on both jambs of passenger elevator hoistway entrances
in conformance with Appendix E of [REF:standard:asmea17.1]

The provisions of this Section apply to [REF:term:hrzntl-r]horizontal service spaces, [REF:term:vrtcl-rv]vertical
service spaces, [REF:term:ttc-r-rf]attic or roof spaces, ducts, crawl spaces, shaft spaces, [REF:term:rvc-rm]service
rooms, and mechanical penthouses, and facilities contained
therein.
The installation of electrical wiring and electrical equipment shall conform to the requirements of the Safety Standards Act and pursuant regulations.

A lightning protection system, when provided, shall conform
to the requirements of the appropriate provincial or territorial legislation
or, in the absence of such legislation, to [REF:standard:csab72]

[REF:term:rvc-pc]Service spaces shall not be designed
to facilitate subsequent use as storage space.

A fuel-fired [REF:term:pplnc]appliance installed
on the roof of a [REF:term:bldng]building or in another
location outside the [REF:term:bldng]building shall be
installed not less than

clauses.text:
1.2 m (metric) from a property line, measured horizontally,
and

3 m (metric) from an adjacent wall of the same [REF:term:bldng]building if that wall contains any opening within
3 [REF:term:tr]storeys above and 5 m (metric) horizontally
from the [REF:term:pplnc]appliance, unless every opening
within these limits is protected by

subclauses.text:
a [REF:term:clr]closure having a [REF:term:fr-prtct]fire-protection rating not less than 45 min (metric) determined
in accordance with [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect1.subsect8.art4:long], or
a wired glass assembly permitted for use in a vertical [REF:term:fr-prtn]fire separation and described in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.appendixD.appsect2.subsect3.article15:medium] of Appendix D.

content.text:
Except as permitted by [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect6.subsect2.art1.sent2:short]
                           [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect6.subsect2.art1.sent8:short]
                           [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect6.subsect2.art1.sent9:short]
                           [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect6.subsect2.art1.sent10:short], fuel-fired [REF:term:pplnc]appliances shall be installed in [REF:term:rvc-rm]service rooms separated from the remainder of
the [REF:term:bldng]building by [REF:term:fr-prtn]fire
separations having a [REF:term:fr-rtnc-]fire-resistance
rating not less than 1 h (metric).

Except as required by [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect6.subsect2.art1.sent3:short], a fuel-fired [REF:term:pplnc]appliance that serves
only one room or [REF:term:t]suite is not required to be
installed in a [REF:term:rvc-rm]service room separated
from the remainder of the [REF:term:bldng]building.

A solid-fuel-burning [REF:term:pplnc]appliance shall
not be located in a [REF:term:rpr-grg]repair garage, a [REF:term:trg-grg]storage garage, or any other location where
it could be exposed to flammable vapours or gases, unless

clauses.text:
it is enclosed in a [REF:term:rvc-rm]service room that is separated from the remainder of the [REF:term:bldng]building by a [REF:term:fr-prtn]fire separation having a [REF:term:fr-rtnc-]fire-resistance rating not
less than 1 h (metric),
it is supplied with combustion air directly from outside the [REF:term:bldng]building, and

the heat that it generates is supplied indirectly to the space
served by means of ducts or piping.

content.text:
A [REF:term:rvc-rm]service room containing an incinerator
shall be separated from the remainder of the [REF:term:bldng]building by a [REF:term:fr-prtn]fire separation having a [REF:term:fr-rtnc-]fire-resistance rating not less than 2 h (metric).

Equipment that uses a liquid having a [REF:term:flh-pnt]flash point below 93.3°C shall be installed in a [REF:term:rvc-rm]service room separated from the remainder of
the [REF:term:bldng]building by a [REF:term:fr-prtn]fire separation having a [REF:term:fr-rtnc-]fire-resistance
rating not less than 1 h (metric).

Electrical equipment that is required to be located in a [REF:term:rvc-rm]service room according to [REF:standard:csac22.1] shall be installed in a [REF:term:rvc-rm]service room separated from the remainder of the [REF:term:bldng]building by a [REF:term:fr-prtn]fire separation having a [REF:term:fr-rtnc-]fire-resistance rating not
less than 1 h (metric).

Except as permitted by [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect6.subsect2.art1.sent8:short], in a [REF:term:tr]storey that is not [REF:term:prnklrd]sprinklered throughout, a [REF:term:rvc-rm]service room that contains service equipment other than that
addressed by [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect6.subsect2.art1.sent1:short]
                           [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect6.subsect2.art1.sent6:short] shall be
separated from the remainder of the [REF:term:bldng]building by a [REF:term:fr-prtn]fire separation having a [REF:term:fr-rtnc-]fire-resistance rating not less than 1 h (metric).

Where a [REF:term:rvc-rm]service room contains a
limited quantity of service equipment, and the service equipment neither
constitutes a fire hazard nor is essential to the operation of fire
safety systems in the [REF:term:bldng]building, the requirements
for a [REF:term:fr-prtn]fire separation shall not apply.

A [REF:term:fr-prtn]fire separation is not required
between a fireplace and the space it serves.

A [REF:term:fr-prtn]fire separation is not required
between a rooftop [REF:term:pplnc]appliance and the [REF:term:bldng]building it serves.

A [REF:term:rvc-rm]service room containing service
equipment subject to possible explosion, such as [REF:term:blr]boilers operating in excess of 100 kPa (metric) (gauge)
and some types of refrigerating machinery and transformers, shall
not be located directly under a required [REF:term:xt]exit.

A [REF:term:rvc-rm]service room containing space
heating, space cooling and service water heating [REF:term:pplnc]appliances is permitted to contain other service equipment
such as electrical service equipment.

A [REF:term:rvc-rm]service room containing an incinerator
shall not contain other fuel-fired [REF:term:pplnc]appliances.

articles.title: Storage of Combustible Refuse and Recycling

content.text:
Except as required by [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect6.subsect3.art3.sent9:long], a room for
the temporary storage
of [REF:term:cmbtbl]combustible refuse and materials for
recycling shall be

clauses.text:
separated from the remainder of the [REF:term:bldng]building by a [REF:term:fr-prtn]fire separation with a [REF:term:fr-rtnc-] fire-resistance rating not less than 1 h (metric), except that
a [REF:term:fr-prtn]fire separation with a [REF:term:fr-rtnc-]fire-resistance rating not less than 45 min (metric) is permitted where the [REF:term:fr-rtnc-]fire-resistance
rating of the floor assembly is not required to exceed 45 min (metric), and
[REF:term:prnklrd]sprinklered.

content.text:
An electrical equipment vault required by the Safety Standards Act and pursuant regulations shall conform to [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect6.subsect2.art7.sent2:short]
                           [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect6.subsect2.art7.sent8:short].

An electrical equipment vault referred to in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect6.subsect2.art7.sent1:short] shall be separated from the remainder
of the [REF:term:bldng]building by a [REF:term:fr-prtn]fire separation of [REF:term:sld-m]solid masonry or concrete construction having a [REF:term:fr-rtnc-]fire-resistance
rating not less than

clauses.text:
3 h (metric) if the vault is not protected by an automatic
fire extinguishing system, or

2 h (metric) if the vault is protected by an automatic fire
extinguishing system.

content.text:
If a [REF:term:bldng]building is [REF:term:prnklrd]sprinklered throughout, an electrical equipment vault referred
to in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect6.subsect2.art7.sent1:short] need not be [REF:term:prnklrd]sprinklered provided

clauses.text:
the vault is designed for no purpose other than to contain the
electrical equipment, and

the vault contains a [REF:term:mk-dtctr]smoke detector which will actuate the [REF:term:bldng]building fire
alarm system in the event of a fire in the vault.

content.text:
Only pipes or ducts necessary for fire protection or the proper
operation of the electrical installation shall penetrate the [REF:term:fr-prtn]fire separation referred to in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect6.subsect2.art7.sent2:short].

Explosion-relief devices and vents or other protective measures
conforming to [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect3.subsect1.art21.sent3:long] shall be provided for an
electrical equipment vault referred to in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect6.subsect2.art7.sent1:short] that contains dielectric-liquid-filled electrical equipment.
(See [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect9.appnote172:short].)

An electrical equipment vault referred to in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect6.subsect2.art7.sent1:short] shall be provided with a ventilation
system designed in conformance with [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part6:long] to
prevent the ambient temperature in the vault from exceeding 40°C (metric).

The ventilation system required by [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect6.subsect2.art7.sent6:short] shall be separate from the system for the remainder
of the [REF:term:bldng]building and shall be designed so
that it is automatically shut off in the event of a fire in the vault.

The floor of an electrical equipment vault referred to in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect6.subsect2.art7.sent1:short] shall be liquid tight and surrounded
by liquid tight walls and sills of sufficient height to confine within
the vault all of the liquid from the largest item of electrical equipment,
but to a height of not less than 100 mm (metric).

Electrical equipment vaults shall be secured against unauthorized
entry.

Where a generator intended to supply emergency power for lighting,
fire safety and life safety systems is located in a [REF:term:bldng]building, except where such [REF:term:bldng]building is used solely for the purpose of housing the generator and its
ancillary equipment, it shall be located in a room that

clauses.text: is separated from the remainder of the [REF:term:bldng]building by a [REF:term:fr-prtn]fire separation having a [REF:term:fr-rtnc-]fire-resistance rating not less than 2 h (metric), and

contains only the generating set and equipment related to the
emergency power supply system.

subsections.title: Vertical Service Spaces and Service Facilities

articles.title: Fire Separations for Vertical Service Spaces

content.text:
Except as provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect6.subsect3.art3:long]
                           [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect6.subsect3.art5:short] and [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect5:long], a [REF:term:vrtcl-rv]vertical service space shall be separated from all other portions of each adjacent [REF:term:tr]storey by a [REF:term:fr-prtn]fire separation having a [REF:term:fr-rtnc-]fire-resistance rating conforming
to [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect6.subsect3.art1.table1:long] for the [REF:term:fr-rtnc-]fire-resistance
rating required by [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect2.subsect2:long] for

clauses.text:
the floor assembly above the [REF:term:tr]storey,
or

the floor assembly below the [REF:term:tr]storey,
if there is no floor assembly above.

content.title: Fire Separations for Vertical Service Spaces

header_rows.content:
[REF:term:fr-rtnc-]Fire-Resistance
Rating of [REF:term:fr-prtn]Fire Separation Required
for Floor Assembly

content.text:
A [REF:term:vrtcl-rv]vertical service space that
does not extend through the roof of a [REF:term:bldng]building shall be enclosed at the top with construction having a [REF:term:fr-rtnc-]fire-resistance rating not less than that
required for the [REF:term:vrtcl-rv]vertical service space walls.

A [REF:term:vrtcl-rv]vertical service space that
does not extend to the bottom of a [REF:term:bldng]building shall be enclosed at the lowest level with construction having a [REF:term:fr-rtnc-]fire-resistance rating not less than that
required for the [REF:term:vrtcl-rv]vertical service space walls.

A vent from a [REF:term:vrtcl-rv]vertical service space not extending to the roof shall be enclosed within the [REF:term:bldng]building with construction having a [REF:term:fr-rtnc-]fire-resistance rating not less than that
required for the [REF:term:vrtcl-rv]vertical service space walls.

Only openings that are necessary for the use of the [REF:term:vrtcl-rv]vertical service space shall be permitted
through a [REF:term:vrtcl-rv]vertical service space enclosure.

Foamed plastic insulation in a [REF:term:vrtcl-rv]vertical
service space shall be protected in conformance with [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect1.subsect5.art15:long]
A linen chute or refuse chute shall

clauses.text: be impervious to moisture,
have a smooth internal surface,
be corrosion-resistant,
be constructed of [REF:term:ncmbtbl]noncombustible material, and

be located in a shaft in which there are no services other than [REF:term:ncmbtbl]noncombustible drain, waste and vent piping
or [REF:term:ncmbtbl]noncombustible water piping.

content.text:
A shaft containing a linen chute or refuse chute shall have
a [REF:term:fr-rtnc-]fire-resistance rating conforming
to [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect6.subsect3.art1.sent1:long], but not less than

clauses.text:
1 h (metric) if the chute outlet for the discharge room
is protected by an automatic, self-latching [REF:term:clr]closure held open by a fusible link, or

2 h (metric) if no [REF:term:clr]closure is provided
at the chute outlet into the discharge room.

content.text:
An interior linen chute or refuse chute shall extend not less
than 1 m (metric) above the roof and shall be vented above the
roof with a vent which

clauses.text:
has an unobstructed area not less than the cross-sectional area
of the chute, and

is equipped with a cover that will open automatically, or that
can be opened manually, in the event of a fire in the chute.

content.text: Intake openings for a linen chute or a refuse chute shall

clauses.text:
have an area not more than 60% of the cross-sectional area of
the chute, and

be fitted with [REF:term:clr]closures designed to
close automatically and latch after use.

content.text:
Intake openings for a linen chute or a refuse chute shall be
located in rooms or compartments that

clauses.text: have no dimension less than 750 mm (metric),

are separated from the remainder of the [REF:term:bldng]building by a [REF:term:fr-prtn]fire separation with a [REF:term:fr-rtnc-]fire-resistance rating not
less than 45 min (metric),
are designed for no other purpose, and
do not open directly into an [REF:term:xt]exit.

content.text:
Sprinklers shall be installed at the top of each linen chute
or refuse chute, at alternate floor levels and in the room or bin
into which the chute discharges.

The room into which a linen chute discharges shall be separated
from the remainder of the [REF:term:bldng]building by a [REF:term:fr-prtn]fire separation with a [REF:term:fr-rtnc-]fire-resistance rating not less than 1 h (metric).

A refuse chute shall be equipped at the top with spray equipment
for washing-down purposes.

A refuse chute shall discharge only into a room or bin separated
from the remainder of the [REF:term:bldng]building by a [REF:term:fr-prtn]fire separation with a [REF:term:fr-rtnc-]fire-resistance rating not less than 2 h (metric).

The room or bin into which a refuse chute discharges shall be
of sufficient size to contain the refuse between normal intervals
of emptying, be impervious to moisture and be equipped with a water
connection and floor drain for washing-down purposes.

A room into which a refuse chute discharges shall contain no
service equipment that is not related to refuse handling and disposal.

If a [REF:term:vrtcl-rv]vertical service space contains
an [REF:term:xht-dct]exhaust duct that serves more than
one [REF:term:fr-cmprt]fire compartment,

clauses.text:
the duct shall have a fan located at or near the exhaust outlet
to ensure that the duct is under negative pressure, and

the individual [REF:term:fr-cmprt]fire compartments shall not have individual fans that exhaust directly into the duct
in the [REF:term:vrtcl-rv]vertical service space.

content.text:
Except as provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect6.subsect3.art5.sent2:short], [REF:term:fr-prtn]fire separations enclosing grease
ducts for commercial cooking operations shall conform to [REF:standard:nfpa96]

The [REF:term:fr-rtnc-]fire-resistance rating of
field-applied and factory-built grease duct enclosure assemblies shall
be determined in conformance with [REF:standard:ulcs144]

subsections.title: Horizontal Service Spaces and Service Facilities

content.text:
This Subsection applies to [REF:term:hrzntl-r]horizontal
service spaces and service facilities, including ceiling spaces,
duct spaces, crawl spaces and [REF:term:ttc-r-rf]attic or roof
spaces.

articles.title: Fire Separations for Horizontal Service Spaces

content.text:
Except as provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect6.subsect3.art5:long], a [REF:term:hrzntl-r]horizontal service space that penetrates a
required vertical [REF:term:fr-prtn]fire separation shall
be separated from the remainder of the [REF:term:bldng]building it serves in conformance with [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect6.subsect4.art2.sent2:short].

If a [REF:term:hrzntl-r]horizontal service space or
other concealed space is located above a required vertical [REF:term:fr-prtn]fire separation other than a vertical shaft,
this space need not be divided at the [REF:term:fr-prtn]fire separation as required by [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect1.subsect8.art3:long] provided the construction
between this space and the space below is a [REF:term:fr-prtn]fire separation with a [REF:term:fr-rtnc-]fire-resistance
rating equivalent to that required for the vertical [REF:term:fr-prtn]fire separation, except that the [REF:term:fr-rtnc-]fire-resistance rating is permitted to be
not less than 30 min (metric) if the vertical [REF:term:fr-prtn]fire separation is not required to have a [REF:term:fr-rtnc-]fire-resistance rating more than 45 min (metric). (See [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect9.appnote175:short].)

A concealed space used as a [REF:term:plnm]plenum within a floor assembly or within a roof assembly need not conform
to [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect1.subsect5.art18.sent1:long] and [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect6.subsect5.art1:long], provided

clauses.text:
all materials within the concealed space have a [REF:term:flm-prd-]flame-spread rating not more than 25 and a
smoke developed classification not more than 50, except for

subclauses.text: tubing for pneumatic controls,

optical fibre cables and electrical wires and cables with [REF:term:cmbtbl]combustible insulation, jackets or sheathes
that are used for the transmission of voice, sound or data and conform
to [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect1.subsect4.art3.sent2:long]
                                 [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect1.subsect5.art21.sent2:long],

totally enclosed non-metallic raceways with an FT6 rating, when
tested in accordance with [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect1.subsect5.art23.sent1.clause1:long], in [REF:term:bldng]buildings required to be of [REF:term:ncmbtbl-]noncombustible construction or in [REF:term:bldng]buildings or parts
of [REF:term:bldng]buildings permitted to be of [REF:term:ncps-mt-nstr]encapsulated mass timber construction, and

totally enclosed non-metallic raceways with an FT4 rating, when
tested in accordance with [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect1.subsect5.art23.sent1.clause1:long], in [REF:term:bldng]buildings permitted to be of [REF:term:cmbtbl-c]combustible construction, and

clauses.text: the supports for the ceiling membrane are of [REF:term:ncmbtbl]noncombustible material having a melting point not below 760°C (metric).

content.text:
If a concealed space referred to in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect6.subsect4.art3.sent1:short] is used as a return-air [REF:term:plnm]plenum and incorporates a ceiling membrane that forms part of the required [REF:term:fr-rtnc-]fire-resistance rating of the assembly, every
opening through the membrane shall be protected by a [REF:term:fr-tp-fl]fire stop flap that

clauses.text:
stops the flow of air into the concealed space in the event
of a fire,

is supported in a manner that will maintain the integrity of
the ceiling membrane for the duration of time required to provide
the required [REF:term:fr-rtnc-]fire-resistance rating,
conforms to [REF:standard:ulcs1122] and

activates at a temperature approximately 30°C above the normal
maximum temperature that occurs in the return-air [REF:term:plnm]plenum, whether the air duct system is operating or shut down.

content.text:
An [REF:term:ttc-r-rf]attic or roof space more than 600 mm (metric) high shall be provided with access from the floor immediately
below by a hatchway not less than 550 mm (metric) by 900 mm (metric) or by a stairway.

A [REF:term:hrzntl-r]horizontal service space, consisting
of ceiling and duct spaces, which is more than 1 200 mm (metric) high and 600 mm (metric) wide shall have inspection doors not
less than 300 mm (metric) in both horizontal and vertical dimensions
placed so that the entire interior of the duct or space can be viewed.

A crawl space shall have at least one access opening not less
than 550 mm (metric) by 900 mm (metric).

Except as permitted by [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect6.subsect5.art1.sent2:short]
                           [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect6.subsect5.art1.sent5:short] and [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect6.subsect4.art3:long], all ducts, duct connectors,
associated fittings and [REF:term:plnm]plenums used in
air duct systems shall be constructed of steel, aluminum alloy, copper,
clay or other [REF:term:ncmbtbl]noncombustible material.

Except as permitted by [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect6.subsect5.art1.sent3:short], ducts, associated fittings and [REF:term:plnm]plenums are permitted to contain [REF:term:cmbtbl]combustible material provided they

clauses.text:
conform to the appropriate requirements for Class 1 duct materials
in [REF:standard:ulcs110]

conform to [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect1.subsect5.art18:long] in a [REF:term:bldng]building required to be of [REF:term:ncmbtbl-]noncombustible
construction or
in a [REF:term:bldng]building or part of a [REF:term:bldng]building permitted to be of [REF:term:ncps-mt-nstr]encapsulated mass timber construction,
conform to [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect1.subsect9:long],

are used only in horizontal runs in a [REF:term:bldng]building required to be of [REF:term:ncmbtbl-]noncombustible construction or in a [REF:term:bldng]building or part of a [REF:term:bldng]building permitted to be of [REF:term:ncps-mt-nstr]encapsulated mass
timber construction,

are not used in vertical runs serving more than 2 [REF:term:tr]storeys in a [REF:term:bldng]building permitted
to be of [REF:term:cmbtbl-c]combustible construction, and

are not used in air duct systems in which the air temperature
could be more than 120°C (metric).

content.text:
[REF:term:cmbtbl]Combustible ducts which are part
of a duct system conveying only ventilation air and are contained
entirely within a [REF:term:dwllng-n]dwelling unit need
not comply with the requirements of [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect6.subsect5.art1.sent1:short]
                           [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect6.subsect5.art1.sent2:short].

Duct sealants shall have a [REF:term:flm-prd-]flame-spread
rating not more than 25 and a smoke developed classification
not more than 50.
Duct connectors that contain [REF:term:cmbtbl]combustible materials and that are used between ducts and air outlet units shall

clauses.text:
conform to the appropriate requirements for Class 1 air duct
materials in [REF:standard:ulcs110]
be not more than 4 m (metric) long,
be used only in horizontal runs, and
not penetrate a required [REF:term:fr-prtn]fire separation.

content.text: Except as permitted by [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect6.subsect5.art2.sent2:short], vibration isolation connectors in air duct systems shall be [REF:term:ncmbtbl]noncombustible.

[REF:term:cmbtbl]Combustible fabric vibration isolation
connectors are permitted provided they

clauses.text: are not more than 250 mm (metric) long,
comply with the flame-resistance requirements of [REF:standard:ulcs109] and

content.text: This Section is concerned with the design and construction of [REF:term:bldng]buildings and occupancies to make them accessible.

[REF:term:bldng]Buildings and facilities required to be accessible in accordance with [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect8.subsect2:long] shall be designed in accordance with [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect8.subsect3:long]

detached houses, semi-detached houses, houses with a [REF:term:scnd-t]secondary suite, duplexes, triplexes, townhouses,
row houses and boarding houses (see [REF:internal:nbc.divA.part1.sect5.appnote7.div16:long], Secondary Suite),
[REF:term:bldng]buildings of Group F, Division 1 [REF:term:mjr-ccpn]major occupancy, and

[REF:term:bldng]buildings that are not intended to
be occupied on a daily or full-time basis, including automatic telephone
exchanges, pumphouses and substations.

number of spaces designated for wheelchair use within rooms or areas
with fixed seats shall conform to [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect8.subsect2.art3.table1:long] (See
also [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect8.subsect3.art22:long] for additional requirements.)

The number of spaces designated for wheelchair use within waiting
rooms or areas with fixed seats shall conform to [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect8.subsect2.art3.table1:long] (See [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect9.appnote186:short].)
(See also [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect8.subsect3.art22:long] for additional requirements.)

Except as provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect8.subsect2.art3.sent6:short], in an [REF:term:mbl-ccpn]assembly occupancy with more
than 25 fixed seats, each row of seats served by two aisles shall
have one adaptable seat conforming to [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect8.subsect3:long] located adjacent to one of the aisles. (See [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect9.appnote187:short].)

At least 5% of the adaptable seats required by [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect8.subsect2.art3.sent5:short] but no more than 20 adaptable seats
shall adjoin an [REF:term:brrr-fr]accessible path of travel.
(See [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect9.appnote187:short].)

articles.title: Access to Storeys Served by Escalators and Moving Walks

content.text: In a [REF:term:bldng]building in which a ramp, escalator or inclined moving walk provides access to any floor level, an interior [REF:term:brrr-fr]accessible path of travel shall also be provided to that floor level. (See [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect9.appnote188:short].)

The route from the ramp, escalator or inclined moving walk to the [REF:term:brrr-fr]accessible path of travel that leads from floor to floor as required by [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect8.subsect2.art4.sent1:short] shall be clearly indicated by appropriate signs.

articles.title: Paths of Travel to Building Entrances and Exterior Passenger-Loading Zones

content.text: A direct exterior [REF:term:brrr-fr]accessible path of travel that complies with [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect8.subsect3:long] shall be provided between an [REF:term:brrr-fr]accessible entrance referred to in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect8.subsect2.art2:long] and

clauses.text: a designated [REF:term:brrr-fr]accessible parking area, where provided,
an exterior passenger-loading zone, where provided,
common ancillary [REF:term:bldng]buildings on the lot, and
a public thoroughfare. (See [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect9.appnote189:short].)

content.text: In [REF:term:trg-grg]storage garages, an [REF:term:brrr-fr]accessible path of travel that complies with [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect8.subsect3:long] shall be provided between each parking level with parking spaces designated for [REF:term:brrr-fr]persons with disabilities and all other parts of the [REF:term:bldng]building required to be provided with [REF:term:brrr-fr]access in accordance with [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect8.subsect2:long] that are served by that [REF:term:trg-grg]storage garage. (See [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect9.appnote190:short].)
Exterior passenger-loading zones shall comply with [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect8.subsect3:long]

Except as provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect5.subsect2.art1.sent3:long], controls for the operation of [REF:term:bldng]building services or safety devices, including electrical switches, thermostats, faucets, door and window hardware and intercom systems and switches, that are intended to be operated generally by the occupant shall comply with [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect8.subsect3:short] (See [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect9.appnote191:short].)

Electrical outlets that are intended for general occupant use shall be located in conformance with [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect8.subsect3:short] (See [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect9.appnote195:short].)

Except as provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect8.subsect2.art7.sent2:short]
                           [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect8.subsect2.art7.sent3:short], and except for doors provided with hold-open devices, doors equipped with a self-closing device shall be equipped with power door operators complying with [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect8.subsect3:short] that allow persons to activate the opening of the doors in the intended direction of travel, where the doors are located

clauses.text: in an entrance referred to in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect8.subsect2.art2:long], including the interior doors of a vestibule where provided,

in an [REF:term:brrr-fr]accessible path of travel, between the entrance referred to in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect8.subsect2.art7.sent1.clause1:short] and the entrance doors to [REF:term:t]suites or rooms served by a [REF:term:pblc-crr]public corridor or a corridor used by the public (see [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect9.appnote192:short]), and
in an entrance to an [REF:term:brrr-fr]accessible washroom.

content.text: Only the active leaf in a multiple leaf door in an [REF:term:brrr-fr]accessible path of travel need conform to the requirements of this Article.

Where more than one doorway is provided at an [REF:term:brrr-fr]accessible entrance, only one of them is required to comply with this Article. (See [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect9.appnote193:short].)

Except as permitted by [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect8.subsect2.art8.sent3:short] and (16), at each location where washrooms are provided in a [REF:term:tr]storey to which an [REF:term:brrr-fr]accessible path of travel is required in accordance with [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect8.subsect2.art3:long], at least one universal washroom complying with [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect8.subsect3:long] shall be provided. (See [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect9.appnote194:short].)

Except as permitted by [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect8.subsect2.art8.sent3:short], where more than two water closets or a combination of more than one water closet and one urinal are provided in a washroom located in a [REF:term:tr]storey to which an [REF:term:brrr-fr]accessible path of travel is required in accordance with [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect8.subsect2.art3:long], at least one water-closet stall shall be [REF:term:brrr-fr]accessible in accordance with [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect8.subsect3:long] (See [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect9.appnote194:short].)

Except as required by [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect8.subsect2.art13:long], washrooms located within a [REF:term:t]suite of [REF:term:rdntl-cc]residential occupancy or a [REF:term:t]suite of [REF:term:ca-cc]care occupancy need not conform to the requirements of [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect8.subsect2.art8.sent1:short] or [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect8.subsect2.art8.sent2:short]. (See [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect9.appnote194:short].)

In a [REF:term:bldng]building in which water closets are required in accordance with [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect7.subsect2:long], at least one universal washroom shall be provided in the entrance [REF:term:tr]storey, unless

clauses.text: an [REF:term:brrr-fr]accessible path of travel is provided to a universal washroom elsewhere in the [REF:term:bldng]building, or
the water closets required by [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect7.subsect2:long] are for [REF:term:dwllng-n]dwelling units only.

content.text: At least one water-closet stall or enclosure in a washroom required to be [REF:term:brrr-fr]accessible shall comply with [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect8.subsect3:long]

Where urinals are provided in an [REF:term:brrr-fr]accessible washroom, at least one urinal for persons with limited mobility conforming to [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect8.subsect3:long] shall be provided for every 10 urinals.

Where water-closet stalls are provided in an [REF:term:brrr-fr]accessible washroom, at least one stall for persons with limited mobility conforming to [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect8.subsect3:long] shall be provided for every 10 stalls.
An [REF:term:brrr-fr]accessible washroom shall be provided with a lavatory that complies with [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect8.subsect3:long]
Where mirrors are provided in an [REF:term:brrr-fr]accessible washroom, at least one mirror shall comply with [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect8.subsect3:long]
At each location where one or more drinking fountains are provided, at least one of them shall comply with [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect8.subsect3:long]
At each location where one or more water-bottle filling stations are provided, at least one of them shall comply with [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect8.subsect3:long]

Except within a [REF:term:t]suite of [REF:term:ca-cc]care occupancy or a [REF:term:t]suite of [REF:term:rdntl-cc]residential occupancy, where showers are provided in a [REF:term:bldng]building, at least one shower stall in each group of showers shall comply with [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect8.subsect3:long]

At each location where a showering facility is provided for use by the general public or customers, or as part of a common-use area for employees, at least one universal dressing and shower room conforming to [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect8.subsect3:long] shall be provided. (See [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect9.appnote197:short].)

Where a bathtub is installed in a [REF:term:t]suite of [REF:term:rdntl-cc]residential occupancy required to be [REF:term:brrr-fr]accessible, it shall comply with [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect8.subsect3:long]
