notes.content: C_{w} = 1, as per [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect6.art2.sent3:long].
C_{s} = 1, as per [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect6.art2.sent7:long].

content.text:
For the purposes of calculating snow loads in drifts, the specific
weight of snow, γ, shall be taken as 4.0 kN/m3
                            (metric) or 0.43SS + 2.2 kN/m3
                            (metric), whichever is lesser.

Snow removal by mechanical, thermal, manual or other means shall
not be used as a rationale to reduce design snow loads.

For lattice structures connected to the [REF:term:bldng]building, and other [REF:term:bldng]building components
or appurtenances involving small width elements subject to significant
ice accretion, the weight of ice accretion and the effective area
presented to wind shall be as prescribed in [REF:standard:csas37]

Where solar panels are installed on a roof, the snow loads,
S, shall be determined in accordance with [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect6.art16.sent2:short]
                           [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect6.art16.sent6:short] or with the requirements for roofs without solar panels,
whichever produces the most critical effect.

For the purposes of this Article, solar panels shall be classified
as

clauses.text:
Parallel Flush, where the panels are installed parallel to the
roof surface with their upper surface less than or equal to C_{b}C_{w}S_{s}/γ above the roof surface,

Parallel Raised, where the panels are installed parallel to
the roof surface with their upper surface greater than C_{b}C_{w}S_{s}/γ above the roof surface, or

Tilted, where the panels are installed at an angle to the roof
surface with their highest edge greater than C_{b}C_{w}S_{s}/γ above the roof surface.

content.text:
For sloped roofs with solar panels, the snow loads, S, shall
be determined in accordance with the requirements for roofs without
solar panels, except that the slope factor, C_{s}, shall be

clauses.text:
taken as 1.0 for roof areas extending upslope from the downslope
edge of a panel or array of panels at an angle of 45° from each side
edge of the panel or array, and

as specified in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect6.art2.sent5:long]
                              [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect6.art2.sent7:short] for all other
roof areas.

content.text:
For sloped roofs with Parallel Flush solar panels, the snow
loads, S, shall be determined in accordance with the requirements
for roofs without solar panels, except that

clauses.text: C_{s} shall be determined in accordance with [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect6.art16.sent3:short],

where the gap width, w_{g}, between the panels along
the roof slope is greater than or equal to the panel width, w_{p}, along the roof slope, the accumulation factor, C_{a}, shall be taken as

subclauses.text: 0.0 for the panels,

2.0 for roof areas within a distance of w_{p} downslope
from a downslope panel edge, and
1.0 for all other roof areas

clauses.text:
where the gap width, w_{g}, between the panels along
the roof slope is less than the panel width, w_{p}, along
the roof slope, C_{a} shall be taken as

subclauses.text:
0.0 for panel areas within a distance of w_{g} downslope
from an upslope panel edge,
1.0 for other panel areas,
2.0 for roof areas in gaps between the panels, and
1.0 for all other roof areas

content.text:
For roofs with Parallel Raised solar panels, the snow loads,
S, shall be determined in accordance with the requirements for roofs
without solar panels, except that

clauses.text: where the roof is flat, C_{a} shall be taken as

subclauses.text: 1.0 for the panels,
1.0 for roof areas not under the panels,

1.0 for roof areas under the panels within a distance of min(2h_{g},2w_{g}) from a panel edge, where h_{g} is
the gap height between the lower surface of the panels and the roof
surface, and w_{g} is the gap width between the panels, and
0.0 for other roof areas under the panels

clauses.text: where the roof is sloped, the snow loads, S, derived from [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect6.art16.sent5.clause1:short] shall be used, except that

subclauses.text: C_{s} shall be determined in accordance with [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect6.art16.sent3:short],
S shall be taken as 0.0 on the panels, and

S for all roof areas shall be taken as the sum of S on the panels,
as derived from [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect6.art16.sent5.clause1.subclause1:short] and shifted
by a distance of w_{p} downslope onto the roof, where w_{p} is the panel width along the roof slope, and S on the roof
areas, as derived from [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect6.art16.sent5.clause1.subclause2:short]
                                 [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect6.art16.sent5.clause1.subclause4:short]

content.text:
For flat roofs with Tilted solar panels, the snow loads, S,
shall be determined in accordance with the requirements for roofs
without solar panels, except that

clauses.text: C_{a} shall be taken as 0.0 for the panels,

C_{a} shall be taken as 1.0 for roof areas beyond a
distance of 5(h – CbCwSs/γ) (metric) from the lowest edge of the panels, where h is the height of the
highest edge of the panels above the roof surface,

except as provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect6.art16.sent6.clause4:short]
                              [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect6.art16.sent6.clause5:short], for roof areas within a distance of 5(h – CbCwSs/γ) (metric) from the lowest edge of the panels,
C_{a} shall be taken as

subclauses.text:
1.25 for (hg – CbCwSs/γ) ≤ 0.3 m (metric), where h_{g} is the gap height
between the lowest edge of the panels and the roof surface,
1.294 – 0.1471(hg – CbCwSs/γ) (metric) for 0.3 < (hg – CbCwSs/γ) ≤ 2.0 m (metric), and
1.0 for (hg – CbCwSs/γ) > 2.0 m (metric)

clauses.text:
except as provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect6.art16.sent6.clause5:short], C_{a} shall be taken as 2.0 for roof areas within a distance
of w_{ph} beyond the lowest edge of the panels, where w_{ph} is the horizontal projection of the panel width, w_{p}, along the sloped panel edges, and

where the panels, panel supports or back plates obstruct snow
from sliding under the panels, the load of the increased volume of
snow in the gaps between the panels shall be considered to be uniformly
distributed.

content.text:
The specified wind loads for a [REF:term:bldng]building and its components shall be determined using the Static, Dynamic
or Wind Tunnel Procedure as stated in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect7.art1.sent2:short]
                           [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect7.art1.sent5:short].

For the design of [REF:term:bldng]buildings that
are not dynamically sensitive, as defined in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect7.art2.sent1:long], one of the following procedures shall be used to determine the
specified wind loads:

clauses.text: the Static Procedure described in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect7.art3:long],
the Dynamic Procedure described in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect7.art8:long], or
the Wind Tunnel Procedure described in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect7.art14:long]

content.text:
For the design of [REF:term:bldng]buildings that
are dynamically sensitive, as defined in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect7.art2.sent2:long], one of the following procedures shall be used to determine the
specified wind loads:

clauses.text: the Dynamic Procedure described in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect7.art8:long], or
the Wind Tunnel Procedure described in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect7.art14:long]

content.text:
For the design of [REF:term:bldng]buildings that
may be subject to wake buffeting or channelling effects from nearby [REF:term:bldng]buildings, or that are very dynamically sensitive,
as defined in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect7.art2.sent3:long], the Wind Tunnel Procedure
described in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect7.art14:long], shall be used to determine
the specified wind loads.

For the design of cladding and secondary structural members,
one of the following procedures shall be used to determine the specified
wind loads:

clauses.text: the Static Procedure described in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect7.art3:long], or
the Wind Tunnel Procedure described in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect7.art14:long]

content.text:
Computational fluid dynamics shall not be used to determine
the specified wind loads for a [REF:term:bldng]building and its components. (See [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect5.appnote51:short].)

Except as provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect7.art2.sent2:short]
                           [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect7.art2.sent3:short], a [REF:term:bldng]building is permitted
to be classified as not dynamically sensitive.

A [REF:term:bldng]building shall be classified as
dynamically sensitive if

clauses.text:
its lowest natural frequency is less than 1 Hz (metric) and
greater than 0.25 Hz (metric),
its height is greater than 60 m (metric), or

its height is greater than 4 times its minimum effective width,
where the effective width, w, of a [REF:term:bldng]building shall be taken as [EQ:display:]where the summations
are over the height of the [REF:term:bldng]building for
a given wind direction, h_{i} is the height above [REF:term:grade]grade to level i, and w_{i} is the width
normal to the wind direction at height h_{i}; the minimum
effective width is the lowest value of the effective width considering
all wind directions.

content.text:
A [REF:term:bldng]building shall be classified as
very dynamically sensitive if

clauses.text: its lowest natural frequency is less than or equal to 0.25 Hz (metric), or

it contains a human
occupancy, and its height is more than 6 times its minimum

content.text:
The net wind load for the [REF:term:bldng]building as a whole shall be the algebraic difference of the loads on the
windward and leeward surfaces, and in some cases, may be calculated
as the sum of the products of the external pressures or suctions and
the areas of the surfaces over which they are averaged as provided
in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect7.art3.sent1:short].

The net specified pressure due to wind on part or all of a surface
of a [REF:term:bldng]building shall be the algebraic difference,
such as to produce the most critical effect, of the external pressure
or suction calculated in accordance with [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect7.art3.sent1:short] and the specified internal pressure or suction due
to wind calculated as follows:[EQ:display:es007876q1]where

direction normal to the surface, either as a pressure directed towards
the surface or as a suction directed away from the surface,

                                 = as defined in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect7.art3.sent1:short],

content.text:
The reference velocity pressure, q, shall be the appropriate
value determined in conformance with [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part1.sect1.subsect3:long], based on a probability of being exceeded in any one year of 1
in 50.

The exposure factor, C_{e}, shall be based on the reference
height, h, determined in accordance with [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect7.art3.sent6:short], for the surface or part of the surface under consideration
and shall be

clauses.text:
(h/10)^{0.2} but not less than 0.9 for open terrain,
where open terrain is level terrain with only scattered [REF:term:bldng]buildings, trees or other obstructions, open
water or shorelines thereof,

0.7(h/12)^{0.3} but not less than 0.7 for rough
terrain, where rough terrain is suburban, urban or wooded terrain
extending upwind from the [REF:term:bldng]building uninterrupted
for at least 1 km (metric) or 20 times (metric) the height
of the [REF:term:bldng]building, whichever is greater,
or

an intermediate value between the two exposures defined in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect7.art3.sent5.clause1:short]
                              [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect7.art3.sent5.clause2:short] in cases where the
site is less than 1 km (metric) or 20 times (metric) the height
of the [REF:term:bldng]building from a change in terrain
conditions, whichever is greater, provided an appropriate interpolation
method is used (see [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect5.appnote53:short]).

content.text: The reference height, h, shall be determined as follows:

clauses.text:
for [REF:term:bldng]buildings whose height is less
than or equal to 20 m (metric) and less than the smaller plan
dimension, h shall be the mid-height of the roof above [REF:term:grade]grade, but not less than 6 m (metric),
for other [REF:term:bldng]buildings, h shall be

subclauses.text:
the actual height above [REF:term:grade]grade of
the point on the windward wall for which external pressures are being
calculated,

the mid-height of the roof for pressures on surfaces parallel
to the wind direction, and

the mid-height of the [REF:term:bldng]building for
pressures on the leeward wall, and

clauses.text:
for any structural element exposed to wind, h shall be the mid-height
of the element above the ground.

content.text:
The exposure factor for internal pressures, C_{ei},
shall be determined as follows:

clauses.text:
for [REF:term:bldng]buildings whose height is greater
than 20 m (metric) and that have a dominant opening, C_{ei} shall be equal to the exposure factor for external pressures, C_{e}, calculated at the mid-height of the dominant opening, and

content.text:
Except as provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect7.art3.sent9:short]
                           [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect7.art6.sent1:long], the gust effect factor, C_{g}, shall be one of the following
values:

clauses.text:
2.0 for the [REF:term:bldng]building as a whole and
main structural members, or

2.5 for external pressures and suctions on secondary structural
members, including cladding.

into a single product, C_{g}C_{p}, the values of C_{g} and C_{p} need not be independently specified. (See [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect7.art6:long])

For the design of the main structural system, the value of C_{p} shall be established as follows, where H is the height of
the [REF:term:bldng]building and D is the width of the [REF:term:bldng]building parallel to the wind direction:

For the design of roofs, the value of C_{p} shall be
established as follows, where x is the distance from the upwind edge
of the roof:

content.text:
For the design of the cladding and of secondary structural elements
supporting the cladding, the value of C_{p} shall be established
as follows, where W and D are the widths of the [REF:term:bldng]building:

clauses.text:
on walls, C_{p} shall be taken as ±0.9 (metric),
except that within a distance equal to the larger of 0.1D (metric) and 0.1W (metric) from a [REF:term:bldng]building corner, the negative value of C_{p} shall be taken as –1.2 (metric),

on walls where vertical ribs deeper than 1 m are placed on the
facade, C_{p} shall be taken as ±0.9, except that, within
a distance equal to the larger of 0.2D and 0.2W from a [REF:term:bldng]building corner, the negative value of C_{p} shall be taken as –1.4, and

on roofs, C_{p} shall be taken as –1.0 (metric),
except that

subclauses.text: within a distance equal to the larger of 0.1D (metric) and 0.1W (metric) from a roof edge, C_{p} shall be taken as –1.5 (metric),

in a zone that is within a distance equal to the larger of 0.2W (metric) and 0.2D (metric) from a roof corner, C_{p} shall be taken as –2.3 (metric) but is permitted to be taken
as –2.0 (metric) for roofs with perimeter parapets that are higher
than 1 m (metric), and

on lower levels of flat stepped roofs, positive pressure coefficients
established for the walls of the steps apply for a distance b (see [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect7.art6.figure4:long] for the definition of b).

content.text:
Except as provided
in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect7.art5.sent6:short], for the
design of balcony [REF:term:guard]guards, the internal
pressure coefficient, C_{pi}, shall be taken as zero and the
value of C_{p} shall be taken as ±0.9 (metric), except
that, within a distance equal to the larger of 0.1W (metric) and 0.1D (metric) from a [REF:term:bldng]building corner, C_{p} shall be taken as ±1.2 (metric).

Where the top of the balcony [REF:term:guard]guard is 2.0 m (metric) or less below the roof surface, the values
of C_{p} shall be taken as equal to those determined for parapets
in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect7.art5.sent7:short]
                           [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect7.art5.sent8:short].

To determine the contribution from parapets to the wind loads
on the main structural system, the values of C_{p} shall be
taken as

clauses.text: on the outer faces, equal to those on the walls below,

on the inner face of the windward parapet, equal to that on
the upwind edge of a roof surface at the level of the top of the parapet,
and
on the inner faces of the other parapets, zero.

content.text:
For the structural design of parapets themselves, the values
of C_{p} shall be taken as equal to those specified in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect7.art5.sent7:short], except that the value of C_{p} on the inner face of the leeward parapet shall be taken as equal
to that on the outer face of the windward parapet.
For the design of cladding on parapets, the values of C_{p} shall be taken as

clauses.text:
on the outer vertical surfaces, equal to those on the cladding
on the walls below, and

on the inner and top surfaces, equal to those on the cladding
of a roof surface at the level of the top of the parapet.

content.text:
For the design of [REF:term:bldng]buildings with
a height, H, that is both less than or equal to 20 m (metric) and
less than the smaller plan dimension, the values of the product of
the pressure coefficient and gust factor, C_{g}C_{p}, provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect7.art6.sent2:short]
                           [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect7.art6.sent9:short] are permitted to be used.

For the design of the main structural system of the [REF:term:bldng]building, which is affected by wind pressures
on more than one surface as shown in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect7.art6.figure1:long],
the values of C_{g}C_{p} are provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect7.art6.table1:long]

content.title:
Primary structural actions arising from wind load acting simultaneously
on all surfaces of low buildings (H ≤ 20 m)

graphic.alt_text: Primary structural actions arising from wind load acting simultaneously on all surfaces of low buildings (H ≤ 20 m)

notes.content:
The [REF:term:bldng]building must be designed
for all wind directions. Each corner must be considered in turn as
the windward corner shown in the sketches. For all roof slopes, Load
Case A and Load Case B are required as two separate loading conditions
to generate the wind actions, including torsion, to be resisted by
the structural system.

For the design of [REF:term:fndtn]foundations, exclusive of anchorages to the frame, only 70% of the effective
load is to be considered.

The reference height, h, for pressures is the mid-height
of the roof or 6 m, whichever is greater. The eave height, H, may
be substituted for the mid-height of the roof if the roof slope is
less than 7°.

End-zone width y should be the greater of 6 m or 2z, where
z is the width of the gable-wall end zone defined for Load Case B
below. Alternatively, for [REF:term:bldng]buildings with
frames, the end-zone width y may be the distance between the end and
the first interior frame.

End-zone width z is the lesser of 10% of the least horizontal
dimension and 40% of height, H, but not less than 4% of the least
horizontal dimension or 1 m.

For B/H > 5 in Load Case A, the negative coefficients
listed for surfaces 2 and 2E in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect7.art6.table1:long] should
only be applied on an area whose width is 2.5H measured from the windward
eave. The pressures on the remainder of the windward roof should be
reduced to the pressures for the leeward roof.

notes.content:
Coefficients for overhung roofs have the prefix “o” and
refer to the same roof areas as referred to by the corresponding symbol
without a prefix. They include contributions from both upper and lower
surfaces.

End-zone width z is the lesser of 10% of the least horizontal
dimension and 40% of height, H, but not less than 4% of the least
horizontal dimension or 1 m.

Combinations of external and internal pressures must be
evaluated to obtain the most severe loading.

Positive coefficients denote forces towards the surface,
whereas negative coefficients denote forces away from the surface.
Each structural element must be designed to withstand forces of both
signs.

For hipped roofs with 7° < α ≤ 27°, edge/ridge strips
and pressure-gust coefficients for ridges of gabled roofs apply along
each hip.

content.text:
Except where the wind loads are derived from the combined C_{g}C_{p} values determined in accordance with [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect7.art6:long], [REF:term:bldng]buildings and structural
members shall be capable of withstanding the effects of the following
loads:

clauses.text:
the full wind loads acting along each of the 2 principal horizontal
axes considered separately,

75% of the wind
loads described in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect7.art9.sent1.clause1:short] but offset
from the central geometric axis of the [REF:term:bldng]building by 15% of its width normal to the direction of the force to produce
the worst load effect,
75% of the wind loads described in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect7.art9.sent1.clause1:short] but with both axes considered simultaneously, and

56% of the wind
loads described in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect7.art9.sent1.clause1:short] but with
both axes considered simultaneously and offset from the central geometric
axis of the [REF:term:bldng]building by 15% of its width
normal to the direction of the force.

content.text:
In the design of interior walls and [REF:term:prttn]partitions, due consideration shall be given to differences in air pressure
on opposite sides of the wall or [REF:term:prttn]partition which may result from

clauses.text:
pressure differences between the windward and leeward sides
of a [REF:term:bldng]building,

stack effects due to a difference in air temperature between
the exterior and interior of the [REF:term:bldng]building, and
air pressurization by the mechanical services of the [REF:term:bldng]building.

content.text:
The effects of wind loads on exterior ornamentations, equipment
and appendages, including the  increase in exposed area as a result
of ice buildup as prescribed in [REF:standard:csas37] shall be considered in the structural design of
the connections and the [REF:term:bldng]building.

Where there are a number of similar components, the net increase
in force is permitted to be based on the total area for all similar
components as opposed to the summation of forces of individual elements.

articles.title: Attached Canopies on Low Buildings with a Height H ≤ 20 m

content.text:
For the purposes of this Article, “attached canopy” shall mean
a horizontal canopy with a maximum slope of 2% that is attached to
a [REF:term:bldng]building wall at any height, h_{c}, above ground level.

The specified external wind pressure, p, and the specified net
external wind pressure, p_{net}, for attached canopies on
exterior walls of low [REF:term:bldng]buildings with a
height H ≤ 20 m (metric) shall be determined as follows:[EQ:display:es013711q1]where
                              
                                 p
                                 = specified external wind pressure acting statically and
in a direction normal to the upper or lower surface of the canopy,
considered positive when acting towards the surface and negative when
acting away from the surface,
                              
                              
                                 p_{net}
                                 
                                 = specified net external wind pressure acting statically
on the canopy, considered positive when acting in a downward direction
and negative when acting in an upward direction,
                              
                              
                                 I_{W}, q, C_{e}, C_{t}
                                 
                                 = as defined in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect7.art3.sent1:long],
                              
                              
                                 C_{g}C_{p}
                                 
                                 = gust pressure coefficient on the upper or lower surface
of the canopy, as given in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect7.art12.figure1:long], and
                              
                              
                                 (C_{g}C_{p})_{net}
                                 
                                 = net gust pressure coefficient on the canopy, considering
simultaneous contributions from the upper and lower surfaces of the
canopy, as given in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect7.art12.figure2:long].

Gust pressure coefficients on the upper and lower surfaces
of attached canopies with no gap between the canopy and the building

graphic.alt_text: Gust pressure coefficients on the upper and lower surfaces of attached canopies with no gap between the canopy and the building

notes.content: The coefficients apply for any roof slope, α.

The reference height, h, is the mid-height of the roof
or 6 m (metric), whichever is greater.

Positive C_{g}C_{p} values denote forces
acting towards the upper or lower surface of the canopy, whereas negative
C_{g}C_{p} values denote forces acting away from the
surface. Each structural element must be designed to resist both the
positive and negative forces.

simultaneous contributions from the upper and lower surfaces of the
canopy

notes.content: The coefficients apply for any roof slope, α.

The reference height, h, is the mid-height of the roof
or 6 m, whichever is greater.

Positive (C_{g}C_{p})_{net} values
denote net forces acting in a downward direction on the canopy, whereas
negative (C_{g}C_{p})_{net} values denote
net forces acting in an upward direction on the canopy. The canopy
must be designed to resist both the positive and negative net forces.

articles.title: Roof-Mounted Solar Panels on Buildings of Any Height

content.text:
Where solar panels are installed on a roof, the roof wind loads
shall account for the wind loads on the solar panels, as determined
in accordance with [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect7.art13.sent2:short]
                           [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect7.art13.sent7:short], or shall be determined in the same way as for the roof without
solar panels, whichever approach results in the most critical effect.

For an array of solar panels where the panels are installed
close and parallel to the roof surface with their upper surface not
more than 250 mm (metric) above the roof surface and with gaps
around the panels of not less than 6 mm (metric), the net positive
or negative pressure difference between the upper and lower surfaces
of a panel or the array shall be calculated as follows:[EQ:display:es013704q1]where

the same manner as for the roof cladding,

                                 C_{p}
                                 
                                 = seismic coefficient for an element or component, as defined
in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect8.art18.sent1:long],
                              
                              
                                 D_{nx}
                                 
                                 = plan dimension of the [REF:term:bldng]building at level x perpendicular to the direction of seismic loading being
considered,
                              
                              
                                 e_{x}
                                 
                                 = distance measured perpendicular to the direction of earthquake
loading between centre of mass and centre of rigidity at the level
being considered (see [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect5.appnote64:short]),
                              
                              
                                 F_{a}
                                 
                                 = acceleration-based
site coefficient for application in standards referenced in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect8:long], as defined in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect8.art4.sent7:long],
                              
                              
                                 F_{s}
                                 
                                 = site coefficient as defined in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect8.art1.sent2:long] for application in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect8.art1:long],
                              
                              
                                 F_{t}
                                 
                                 = portion of V to be concentrated at the top of the structure,
as defined in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect8.art11.sent7:long],
                              
                              
                                 F_{v}
                                 
                                 = velocity-based
site coefficient for application in standards referenced in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect8:long], as defined in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect8.art4.sent7:long],
                              
                              
                                 F_{x}
                                 
                                 = lateral force applied to level x, as defined in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect8.art11.sent7:long],
                              
                              
                                 h_{i}, h_{n}, h_{x}
                                 
                                 = height, in m, above the base (i = 0) to level i, n, or
x respectively, where the base of the structure is the level at which
horizontal earthquake motions are considered to be imparted to the
structure,
                              
                              
                                 h_{s}
                                 
                                 = inter[REF:term:tr]storey height (h_{i} − h_{i−1}),
                              
                              
                                 I_{E}
                                 
                                 = earthquake importance factor of the structure, as described
in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect8.art5.sent1:long],
                              
                              
                                 J
                                 = numerical reduction coefficient for base overturning moment,
as defined in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect8.art11.sent6:long],
                              
                              
                                 J_{x}
                                 
                                 = numerical reduction coefficient for overturning moment
at level x, as defined in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect8.art11.sent8:long],
                              
                              
                                 Level i
                                 = any level in the [REF:term:bldng]building, i
= 1 for first level above the base,
                              
                              
                                 Level n
                                 = level that is uppermost in the main portion of the structure,
                              
                              
                                 Level x
                                 = level that is under design consideration,
                              
                              
                                 M_{v}
                                 
                                 = factor to account for higher mode effects on base shear,
as defined in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect8.art11.sent6:long],
                              
                              
                                 M_{x}
                                 
                                 = overturning moment at level x, as defined in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect8.art11.sent8:long],
                              
                              
                                 N
                                 = total number of [REF:term:tr]storeys above exterior [REF:term:grade]grade to level n,
                              
                              
                                 
                                    [EQ:inline:]
                                    _{60}
                                 
                                 = average standard penetration resistance, in blows per 0.3 m (metric), in
the top 30 m (metric) of [REF:term:l]soil, corrected to a rod energy efficiency of 60% of the theoretical
maximum,
                              
                              
                                 PGA(X)
                                 = peak ground acceleration, expressed as a ratio to gravitational
acceleration, for site
designation X, as defined in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect8.art4.sent1:long],
                              
                              
                                 PGV(X)
                                 = peak ground velocity, in m/s, for site designation X, as defined in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect8.art4.sent1:long],
                              
                              
                                 PI
                                 = plasticity index for [REF:term:l]soil,
                              
                              
                                 R_{d}
                                 
                                 = ductility-related force modification factor reflecting
the capability of a structure to dissipate energy through reversed
cyclic inelastic behaviour, as defined in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect8.art9:long],
                              
                              
                                 R_{o}
                                 
                                 = overstrength-related force modification factor accounting
for the dependable portion of reserve strength in a structure designed
according to these provisions, as defined in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect8.art9:long],
                              
                              
                                 R_{p}
                                 
                                 = element or component response modification factor, as defined
in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect8.art18.sent1:long],
                              
                              
                                 R_{s}
                                 
                                 = combined overstrength and ductility-related modification
factor, as defined in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect8.art1.sent7:long], for application
in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect8.art1:long],
                              
                              
                                 S_{a}(T,X)
                                 = 5%-damped spectral acceleration, expressed as a ratio to
gravitational acceleration, at period T for site designation X, as defined in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect8.art4.sent1:long],
                              
                              
                                 SC
                                 = Seismic Category assigned to a [REF:term:bldng]building based on its Importance Category and the design spectral acceleration
values at periods of 0.2 s (metric) and 1.0 s (metric), as
defined in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect8.art5:long],
                              
                              
                                 SFRS
                                 = seismic force resisting system, that part of the structural
system that has been considered in the design to provide the required
resistance to the earthquake forces and effects defined in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect8:long],
                              
                              
                                 S_{p}
                                 
                                 = horizontal force factor for part or portion of a [REF:term:bldng]building and its anchorage, as given in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect8.art18.sent1:long],
                              
                              
                                 S(T)
                                 = design spectral acceleration, expressed as a ratio to gravitational
acceleration, at period T, as defined in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect8.art4.sent6:long],
                              
                              
                                 
                                    [EQ:inline:]
                                 
                                 = average undrained shear strength, in kPa, in the top 30 m (metric) of [REF:term:l]soil,
                              
                              
                                 T
                                 = period, in s,
                              
                              
                                 T_{a}
                                 
                                 = fundamental lateral period of vibration of the [REF:term:bldng]building or structure, in s, in the direction
under consideration, as defined in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect8.art11.sent3:long],
                              
                              
                                 TDD
                                 = total design displacement of any point in a seismically
isolated structure, within or above the isolation system, obtained
by calculating the mean + (I_{E} × the standard deviation)
of the peak horizontal displacements from all sets of ground motion
time histories analyzed, but not less than √I_{E} × the mean,
where the peak horizontal displacement is based on the vector sum
of the two orthogonal horizontal displacements considered for each
time step,
                              
                              
                                 T_{s}
                                 
                                 = fundamental lateral period of vibration of the [REF:term:bldng]building or structure, in s, in the direction
under consideration, as defined in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect8.art1.sent7:long],
                              
                              
                                 T_{x}
                                 
                                 = floor torque at level x, as defined in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect8.art11.sent11:long],
                              
                              
                                 V
                                 = specified lateral earthquake force at the base of the structure,
as determined in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect8.art11:long],
                              
                              
                                 V_{d}
                                 
                                 = specified lateral earthquake force at the base of the structure,
as determined in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect8.art12:long],
                              
                              
                                 V_{e}
                                 
                                 = lateral earthquake elastic force at the base of the structure,
as determined in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect8.art12:long],
                              
                              
                                 V_{ed}
                                 
                                 = adjusted lateral earthquake elastic force at the base of
the structure, as determined in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect8.art12:long],
                              
                              
                                 V_{p}
                                 
                                 = specified lateral earthquake force on an element or component,
as determined in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect8.art18:long],
                              
                              
                                 V_{s}
                                 
                                 = specified lateral earthquake force at the base of the structure,
as determined in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect8.art1.sent7:long], for application in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect8.art1:long],
                              
                              
                                 V_{s30}
                                 
                                 = average shear wave velocity, in m/s, in the top 30
m (metric) of [REF:term:l]soil or [REF:term:rck]rock,
                                 
                              
                              
                                 W
                                 = specified [REF:term:dd-ld]dead load, as defined
in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect4.art1:long], except that the minimum [REF:term:prttn]partition weight as defined in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect4.art1.sent3:long] need not exceed 0.5 kPa (metric), plus 25%
of the specified snow load as defined in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect6:long], plus 60% of the storage load for areas used for storage, except
that [REF:term:trg-grg]storage garages need not be considered
storage areas, and the full contents of any tanks (see [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect5.appnote64:short]),
                              
                              
                                 W_{i}, W_{x}
                                 
                                 = portion of W that is located at or is assigned to level
i or x respectively,
                              
                              
                                 W_{p}
                                 
                                 = weight of a part or portion of a structure, e.g., cladding, [REF:term:prttn]partitions and appendages,
                              
                              
                                 X
                                 = site designation, either X_{V} or X_{S},
                              
                              
                                 X_{S}
                                 
                                 = site designation in terms of Site Class, where S is the
Site Class determined in accordance with [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect8.art4.sent3:long],
                              
                              
                                 X_{V}
                                 
                                 = site designation in terms of V_{s30}, where V is
the V_{s30} value calculated from in situ measurements of
shear wave velocity,
                              
                              
                                 X_{450}
                                 
                                 = site designation X_{V} with Vs30 = 450 m/s (metric),
                              
                              
                                 δ_{ave}
                                 
                                 = average displacement of the structure at level x, as defined
in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect8.art11.sent10:long], and
                              
                              
                                 δ_{max}
                                 
                                 = maximum displacement of the structure at level x, as defined
in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect8.art11.sent10:long].

content.text:
The [REF:term:bldng]building shall be designed to
meet the requirements of this Subsection and of the design standards
referenced in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect3:long]

Structures shall be designed with a clearly defined load path,
or paths, that will transfer the inertial forces generated in an earthquake
to the supporting ground.

The structure shall have a clearly defined SFRS, as defined
in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect8.art2:long]

The SFRS shall be designed to resist 100% of the earthquake
loads and their effects. (See [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect5.appnote65:short].)

All structural framing elements not considered to be part of
the SFRS must be investigated and shown to behave elastically or to
have sufficient non-linear capacity to support their gravity loads
while undergoing earthquake-induced deformations calculated from the
deflections determined in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect8.art13:long]

Stiff elements that are not considered part of the SFRS, such
as concrete, masonry, brick or precast walls or panels, shall be

clauses.text:
separated from all structural elements of the [REF:term:bldng]building such that no interaction takes place as the [REF:term:bldng]building undergoes deflections due to earthquake
effects as calculated in this Subsection, or
made part of the SFRS and satisfy the requirements of this Subsection.

content.text:
Stiffness imparted to the structure from elements not part of
the SFRS, other than those described in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect8.art3.sent6:short], shall not be used to resist earthquake deflections
but shall be accounted for

clauses.text:
in calculating the period of the structure for determining forces
if the added stiffness decreases the fundamental lateral period by
more than 15%,

in determining the irregularity of the structure, except the
additional stiffness shall not be used to make an irregular SFRS regular
or to reduce the effects of torsion (see [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect5.appnote67:short]), and

in designing the SFRS if inclusion of the elements not part
of the SFRS in the analysis has an adverse effect on the SFRS (see [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect5.appnote67:short]).

content.text:
Structural modeling shall be representative of the magnitude
and spatial distribution of the mass of the [REF:term:bldng]building and of the stiffness of all elements of the SFRS, including stiff
elements that are not separated in accordance with [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect8.art3.sent6:long], and shall account for

clauses.text:
the effect of cracked sections in reinforced concrete and reinforced
masonry elements,
the effect of the finite size of members and joints,

sway effects arising from the interaction of gravity loads with
the displaced configuration of the structure, and
other effects that influence the lateral stiffness of the [REF:term:bldng]building.

content.text:
For site designation
X, as determined in accordance with [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect8.art4.sent2:short]
                           [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect8.art4.sent3:short], the peak ground acceleration, PGA(X), the peak ground velocity,
PGV(X), and the 5%-damped spectral acceleration values, S_{a}(T,X), at periods T of 0.2 s (metric), 0.5
s (metric), 1.0 s (metric), 2.0 s (metric), 5.0 s (metric) and 10.0 s (metric) shall

clauses.text:
except as provided
in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect8.art4.sent4:short], be determined
in accordance with [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part1.sect1.subsect3:long], and

except as provided
in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect8.art23:long], correspond to a 2% probability
of exceedance in 50 years (metric).

content.text:
Except as provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect8.art4.sent3:short], the site designation referred to in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect8.art4.sent1:short] shall be determined using the average shear wave velocity,
V_{s30}, calculated from in situ measurements of shear wave
velocity, as follows:

clauses.text:
for the ground profiles described in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect8.art4.table1:long], the site designation shall be determined in accordance with the
Table, and

for all other ground profiles, the site designation shall be
X_{V}, where V is the value of V_{s30}.

body_rows.content:
Hard [REF:term:rck]rock
                                    Site designations
X_{A} and X_{B}, corresponding to Site Classes A and
B, are not to be used in cases where the ground profile
contains more than 3 m (metric) of softer materials between [REF:term:rck]rock and the underside of footing or mat [REF:term:fndtn]foundations. The appropriate site designation
for such cases is X_{760}.

Any ground profile other than Site Class F that contains more than
3 m of [REF:term:l]soil with all the following
characteristics:
                                       plasticity index, PI > 20,
                                       moisture content, w ≥ 40%, and
                                       undrained shear strength, s_{u} < 25 kPa (metric)

Other [REF:term:l]soils
                                    Site-specific geotechnical evaluation is required.

Any ground profile
that contains
                                        liquefiable [REF:term:l]soil, quick and highly
sensitive clay, collapsible weakly cemented [REF:term:l]soil, or other [REF:term:l]soil susceptible to failure or
collapse under seismic loading,
                                        more than 3 m (metric) of peat and/or highly organic
clay,
                                        more than 8 m (metric) of highly plastic [REF:term:l]soil (with PI > 75), or
                                        more than 30 m (metric) of soft to medium-stiff clay

content.text:
Site-specific geotechnical evaluation is required to determine the values of PGA(X_{F}), PGV(X_{F}) and S_{a}(T,X_{F}) for
site designation X_{F}.

Where structures
on liquefiable [REF:term:l]soils have a fundamental lateral
period, T_{a}, of 0.5 s (metric) or less, the site designation
X and the corresponding values of S_{a}(T,X) and PGA(X) are
permitted to be determined in accordance with [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect8.art4.sent1:short] by assuming that the [REF:term:l]soils are not liquefiable.

The design spectral acceleration, S(T), shall be determined in accordance with [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect8.art4.table3:long], using log–log or linear interpolation for intermediate
values of T. (See [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect5.appnote71:short].)

content.title: Design Spectral Acceleration

body_rows.content:
S_{a}(0.2,X) or S_{a}(0.5,X), whichever
is greater

content.text:
Where required for the application of a standard referenced
in this Subsection, the acceleration-based site coefficient, F_{a}, for site designation X shall be taken as S(0.2)/S_{a}(0.2,X_{450}) and the velocity-based site coefficient, F_{v}, for site designation X shall be taken as S(1.0)/S_{a}(1.0,X_{450}).

The earthquake importance factor, I_{E}, shall be determined
according to [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect8.art5.table1:long]

content.title: Importance Factor for Earthquake Loads and Effects, I_{E}

content.text:
[REF:term:bldng]Buildings shall be assigned a Seismic
Category in accordance with [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect8.art5.table2:long].

content.title: Seismic Categories for Buildings

header_rows.content:
Seismic CategoryThe Seismic Category of a [REF:term:bldng]building shall be taken as the more severe of the categories determined on
the basis of I_{E}S(0.2) and I_{E}S(1.0), irrespective
of the fundamental lateral period of the [REF:term:bldng]building, T_{a}.

content.text: Structures having any of the features listed in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect8.art6.table1:long] shall be designated irregular.
Structures not classified as irregular according to [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect8.art6.sent1:short] may be considered regular.

Except as required by [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect8.art10:long], where the Seismic Category is SC3
or SC4, structures designated as irregular must satisfy
the provisions referenced in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect8.art6.table1:long]

content.title:
Structural IrregularitiesOne-[REF:term:tr]storey penthouses with a weight of less
than 10% of the level below need not be considered in the application
of this Table.
                           See [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect5.appnote73:short]

body_rows.content:
<bold>Vertical
Stiffness Irregularity</bold>For concrete and masonry shear walls,
vertical stiffness irregularity shall be considered to exist where
the lateral stiffness of the SFRS in any [REF:term:tr]storey is less than 70% of the stiffness in an adjacent [REF:term:tr]storey, or less than 80% of the average stiffness in the three [REF:term:tr]storeys above or below. For all other types of SFRS,
vertical stiffness irregularity shall be considered to exist where
the inter[REF:term:tr]storey deflection under lateral earthquake
forces divided by the inter[REF:term:tr]storey height,
h_{s}, of any [REF:term:tr]storey is greater than
130% of that of an adjacent [REF:term:tr]storey.

See [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect8.art7:long]
                                    
                                    See [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect8.art10:long]
                                    
                                    Increased stiffness in [REF:term:tr]storeys below [REF:term:grade]grade need not be
considered in the determination of vertical stiffness irregularity.

<bold>Weight (mass) Irregularity</bold>Weight irregularity shall be considered to exist
where the weight, W_{i}, of any [REF:term:tr]storey is more than 150% of the weight of an adjacent [REF:term:tr]storey. A roof that is lighter than the floor below need not
be considered.

<bold>Vertical Geometric Irregularity</bold>Vertical geometric irregularity shall be considered
to exist where the horizontal dimension of the SFRS in any [REF:term:tr]storey is more than 130% of that in an adjacent [REF:term:tr]storey.

<bold>In-Plane Discontinuity
in Vertical Lateral-Force-Resisting Element</bold>Except for braced frames and moment-resisting frames, an in-plane
discontinuity shall be considered to exist where there is an offset
of a lateral-force-resisting element of the SFRS or a reduction in
lateral stiffness of the resisting element in the [REF:term:tr]storey below.

<bold>Out-of-Plane Offsets</bold>Discontinuities in a lateral force path, such as
out-of-plane offsets of the vertical elements of the SFRS.

<bold>Discontinuity in Capacity
– Weak Storey</bold>A weak [REF:term:tr]storey is one in which the [REF:term:tr]storey shear strength
is less than that in the [REF:term:tr]storey above. The [REF:term:tr]storey shear strength is the total strength of all
seismic-resisting elements of the SFRS sharing the [REF:term:tr]storey shear for the direction under consideration.

<bold>Torsional Sensitivity (to
be considered when diaphragms are not flexible)</bold>Torsional sensitivity shall be considered to exist when the ratio
B calculated according to [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect8.art11.sent10:long] exceeds 1.7.

<bold>Non-orthogonal Systems</bold>A non-orthogonal system irregularity shall be considered
to exist when the SFRS is not oriented along a set of orthogonal axes.

<bold>Gravity-Induced
Lateral Demand Irregularity</bold>Gravity-induced
lateral demand irregularity on the SFRS shall be considered to exist
where the ratio α calculated in accordance with [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect8.art10.sent7:long] exceeds 0.1 for an SFRS with self-centering characteristics
and 0.03 for other systems.

<bold>Sloped
Column Irregularity</bold>Sloped column irregularity
shall be considered to exist where a vertical member that is inclined
more than 2° from the vertical supports a portion of the weight of
the [REF:term:bldng]building in axial compression.

Earthquake forces shall be assumed to act in any horizontal
direction, except that the following shall be considered to provide
adequate design force levels in the structure:

clauses.text:
where components of the SFRS are oriented along a set of orthogonal
axes, independent analyses about each of the principal axes of the
structure shall be performed,

where the components of the SFRS are not oriented along a set
of orthogonal axes and the Seismic Category is SC1 or SC2, independent analyses
about any two orthogonal axes is permitted, or

where the components of the SFRS are not oriented along a set
of orthogonal axes and the Seismic Category is SC3 or SC4, analysis of the

of the specified earthquake loads applied in one direction plus 30%
of the specified earthquake loads in the perpendicular direction,
with the combination requiring the greater element strength being
used in the design.

the value of J obtained in accordance with Note (1). See [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect8.art11.sent2.clause1:long].

content.text:
Torsional effects that are concurrent with the effects of the
forces determined in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect8.art11.sent7:short] and
are caused by the simultaneous actions of the following torsional
moments shall be considered in the design of the structure according
to [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect8.art11.sent11:short]:

clauses.text:
torsional moments introduced by eccentricity between the centres
of mass and resistance and their dynamic amplification, and
torsional moments due to accidental eccentricities.

structure at level x produced by the forces determined in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect8.art11.sent7:short].

content.text: Torsional effects shall be accounted for as follows:

clauses.text:
for a [REF:term:bldng]building with B ≤ 1.7 or in Seismic Category SC1 or SC2, by applying torsional moments about a vertical axis at each level
throughout the [REF:term:bldng]building, derived for each
of the following load cases considered separately:where F_{x} is determined in accordance with [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect8.art11.sent7:short] and where each element of the [REF:term:bldng]building is designed for the most severe effect
of the above load cases, or
for a [REF:term:bldng]building with B > 1.7 in Seismic Category SC3 or SC4, by a Dynamic Analysis Procedure as specified in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect8.art12:long]

content.text:
Where the fundamental lateral period, T_{a}, is determined
in accordance with [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect8.art11.sent3.clause4:medium] and
the [REF:term:bldng]building is constructed with more than
4 [REF:term:tr]storeys of continuous wood construction
and has a timber SFRS consisting of shear walls with wood-based panels
or of braced or moment-resisting frames as defined in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect8.art9.table1:long], the specified lateral earthquake force, V, as
determined in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect8.art11.sent2:short] shall be multiplied
by 1.2 but need not exceed the value determined by using [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect8.art11.sent2.clause3:medium]. (See [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect5.appnote78:long].)

Except as provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect8.art19:long]
                           [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect8.art21:long], the Dynamic Analysis
Procedure shall be in accordance with one of the following methods:

clauses.text:
Linear Dynamic Analysis by either the Modal Response Spectrum
Method or the Numerical Integration Linear Time History Method using
a structural model that complies with the requirements of [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect8.art3.sent8:long] (see [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect5.appnote83:short]),
or

Non-linear Dynamic Analysis, in which case a special study shall
be performed (see [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect5.appnote84:short]).

content.text:
The spectral acceleration values used in the Modal Response
Spectrum Method shall be the design spectral acceleration values,
S(T), defined in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect8.art4.sent6:long].

The ground motion time histories used in the Numerical Integration
Linear Time History Method shall be compatible with a response spectrum
constructed from the design spectral acceleration values, S(T), defined
in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect8.art4.sent6:long]. (See [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect5.appnote85:short].)

clauses.text:
the static effects of torsional moments due to (±0.10Dnx)Fx
                               (metric) at each level x, where F_{x} is either determined from the elastic dynamic analysis or determined
from [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect8.art11.sent7:long] multiplied by R_{d}R_{o}/I_{E}, shall be combined with the effects determined
by dynamic analysis (see [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect5.appnote86:short]),
or

if B, as defined in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect8.art11.sent10:long], is less than
1.7, it is permitted to use a three-dimensional dynamic analysis with
the centres of mass shifted by a distance of −0.05D_{nx} and
+0.05D_{nx}.

content.text:
Except as provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect8.art12.sent6:short], the adjusted elastic base shear, V_{ed}, shall be equal
to the elastic base shear, V_{e}, obtained from a Linear Dynamic
Analysis.

For [REF:term:bldng]buildings located on a site designated as other than X_{F} that
have an SFRS with R_{d} equal to or greater than 1.5, the
elastic base shear, V_{e}, obtained from a Linear Dynamic
Analysis may be multiplied by the larger of the following factors
to obtain V_{ed}:[EQ:display:es016106q1]

content.text:
V_{ed} shall be multiplied by the earthquake importance
factor, I_{E}, as determined in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect8.art5:long], and shall be divided by R_{d}R_{o}, as determined
in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect8.art9:long], to obtain the specified lateral earthquake
force, V_{d}.

Except as required by [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect8.art12.sent9:short]
                           [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect8.art12.sent12:short], if V_{d}, as determined in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect8.art12.sent7:short], is less than 80% of V, as determined in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect8.art11:long], V_{d} shall be taken as 0.8V.

For irregular structures requiring dynamic analysis in accordance
with [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect8.art7:long], V_{d} shall be taken as
the larger of V_{d}, as determined in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect8.art12.sent7:short], and 100% of V, as determined in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect8.art11:long]

Except as required by [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect8.art12.sent11:short], the values of elastic [REF:term:tr]storey shears, [REF:term:tr]storey forces, member forces, and deflections obtained
from the Linear Dynamic Analysis, including the effect of accidental
torsion determined in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect8.art12.sent4:short], shall
be multiplied by V_{d}/V_{e} to determine their design
values.

For the purpose of calculating deflections, it is permitted
to use a value of V based on the value of T_{a} determined
in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect8.art11.sent3.clause4:long] to obtain V_{d} in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect8.art12.sent8:short]
                           [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect8.art12.sent9:short].

For [REF:term:bldng]buildings constructed with more
than 4 [REF:term:tr]storeys of continuous wood construction,
having a timber SFRS consisting of shear walls with wood-based panels
or braced or moment-resisting frames as defined in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect8.art9.table1:long], and whose fundamental lateral period, T_{a}, is determined in accordance with [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect8.art11.sent3.clause4:long],
V_{d} shall be taken as the larger of V_{d}, as determined
in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect8.art12.sent7:short], and 100% of V, as determined
in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect8.art11:long] (See [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect5.appnote78:long].)

Except as provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect8.art13.sent5:short]
                           [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect8.art13.sent6:short], lateral deflections of a structure shall be calculated
in accordance with the loads and requirements defined in this Subsection.

Lateral deflections obtained from a linear elastic analysis
using the methods given in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect8.art11:long]
                           [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect8.art12:long] and incorporating the
effects of torsion, including accidental torsional moments, shall
be multiplied by R_{d}R_{o}/I_{E} and increased
as required in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect8.art10.sent8:long] and [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect8.art16.sent1:number] to give realistic values of anticipated
deflections.

Based on the lateral deflections calculated in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect8.art13.sent2:short]
                           [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect8.art13.sent5:short]
                           [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect8.art13.sent6:short], the largest inter[REF:term:tr]storey deflection
at any level shall be limited to 0.01hs
                            (metric) for [REF:term:pt-dtr-b]post-disaster buildings, 0.02hs
                            (metric) for High Importance Category [REF:term:bldng]buildings, and 0.025hs
                            (metric) for all other [REF:term:bldng]buildings.

The deflections calculated in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect8.art13.sent2:short] shall be used to account for sway effects as required
by [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect3.art2.sent12:long]. (See [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect5.appnote87:short].)

The lateral deflections of a seismically isolated structure
shall be calculated in accordance with [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect8.art20:long]

The lateral deflections of a structure with supplemental energy
dissipation shall be calculated in accordance with [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect8.art22:long]
Adjacent structures shall be

clauses.text:
separated by a distance equal to at least the square root of
the sum of the squares of their individual deflections calculated
in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect8.art13.sent2:long], or
connected to each other.

content.text:
The method of connection required in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect8.art14.sent1:short] shall take into account the mass, stiffness, strength,
ductility and anticipated motion of the connected [REF:term:bldng]buildings and the character of the connection.

Rigidly connected [REF:term:bldng]buildings shall
be assumed to have the lowest R_{d}R_{o} value of
the [REF:term:bldng]buildings connected.

[REF:term:bldng]Buildings with non-rigid or energy-dissipating
connections require special studies.

Except as provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect8.art15.sent2:short]
                           [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect8.art15.sent3:short], diaphragms, collectors, chords, struts and connections
shall be designed so as not to yield, and the design shall account
for the shape of the diaphragm, including openings, and for the forces
generated in the diaphragm due to the following cases, whichever one
governs:

clauses.text:
forces determined in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect8.art11:long]
                              [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect8.art12:long] applied to the diaphragm are increased
to reflect the lateral load capacity of the SFRS, plus forces in the
diaphragm due to the transfer of forces between elements of the SFRS
associated with the lateral load capacity of such elements and accounting
for discontinuities and changes in stiffness in these elements, or

a minimum force corresponding to the specified lateral earthquake
force, V, divided by N for the diaphragm at level x.

content.text:
Steel deck roof diaphragms in [REF:term:bldng]buildings of less than 4 storeys
                            (metric) or wood
diaphragms that are designed and detailed according to the applicable
referenced design standards to exhibit ductile behaviour shall meet
the requirements of [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect8.art15.sent1:short], except
that they may yield and the forces shall be

clauses.text:
for wood diaphragms acting in combination with vertical wood
shear walls, equal to the specified lateral earthquake force, V,

for wood diaphragms acting in combination with other SFRSs,
not less than the force corresponding to R_{d}R_{o} = 2.0, and

for steel deck roof diaphragms, not less than the force corresponding
to R_{d}R_{o} = 2.0.

content.text:
Where diaphragms are designed in accordance with [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect8.art15.sent2:short], the struts shall be designed in accordance
with [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect8.art15.sent1.clause1:medium], and the collectors,
chords and connections between the diaphragms and the vertical elements
of the SFRS shall be designed for forces corresponding to the capacity
of the diaphragms in accordance with the applicable CSA standards.
(See [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect5.appnote89:short].)

For single-[REF:term:tr]storey
                           [REF:term:bldng]buildings with steel deck or wood roof diaphragms designed
with a value of R_{d} greater than 1.5 and where the calculated
maximum relative deflection, Δ_{D}, of the diaphragm under
lateral loads exceeds 50% of  the average [REF:term:tr]storey drift, Δ_{B}, of the adjoining vertical elements of the
SFRS, dynamic magnification of the inelastic response due to the in-plane
diaphragm deformations shall be accounted for in the design as follows:

clauses.text:
the vertical elements of the SFRS shall be designed and detailed
to any one of the following:

subclauses.text:
to accommodate the anticipated magnified lateral deformations
taken as R_{o}R_{d}(Δ_{B} + Δ_{D})
− R_{o}Δ_{D},
to resist the forces magnified by R_{d}(1 + Δ_{D}/Δ_{B})/(R_{d} + Δ_{D}/Δ_{B}), or
by a special study, and

clauses.text:
the roof diaphragm and chords shall be designed for in-plane
shears and moments determined while taking into consideration the
inelastic higher mode response of the structure.

content.text:
Where the Seismic
Category is SC3 or SC4, the elements supporting any discontinuous
wall, column or braced frame shall be designed for the lateral load
capacity of the components of the SFRS they support. (See [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect5.appnote91:short].)

Where structures have vertical variations of R_{d}R_{o} satisfying [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect8.art9.sent4:long], the elements of the
SFRS below the level where the change in R_{d}R_{o} occurs shall be designed for the forces associated with the lateral
load capacity of the SFRS above that level. (See [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect5.appnote92:short].)

Where earthquake effects can produce forces in a column or wall
due to lateral loading along both orthogonal axes, account shall be
taken of the effects of potential concurrent yielding of other elements
framing into the column or wall from all directions at the level under
consideration and as appropriate at other levels. (See [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect5.appnote93:short].)

The design forces associated with the lateral capacity of the
SFRS need not exceed the forces determined in accordance with [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect8.art7.sent1:long] with R_{d}R_{o} taken as 1.0, unless
otherwise provided by the applicable referenced design standards for
elements, in which case the design forces associated with the lateral
capacity of the SFRS need not exceed the forces determined in accordance
with [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect8.art7.sent1:long] with R_{d}R_{o} taken
as less than or equal to 1.3. (See [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect5.appnote94:short].)

[REF:term:fndtn]Foundations need not be designed
to resist the lateral load overturning capacity of the SFRS, provided
the design and the R_{d} and R_{o} for the type of
SFRS used conform to [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect8.art9.table1:long] and that the [REF:term:fndtn]foundation is designed in accordance with [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect8.art16.sent4:long].

[REF:term:fndtn]Foundation displacements and rotations
shall be considered as required by [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect8.art16.sent1:long].

The increased displacements of the structure resulting from [REF:term:fndtn]foundation movement shall be shown to be within
acceptable limits for both the SFRS and the structural framing elements
not considered to be part of the SFRS. (See [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect5.appnote95:short].)

Except as provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect8.art16.sent3:short]
                           [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect8.art16.sent4:short], [REF:term:fndtn]foundations shall be designed
to have factored shear and overturning resistances greater than the
lateral load capacity of the SFRS. (See [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect5.appnote96:short].)

The shear and overturning resistances of the [REF:term:fndtn]foundation determined using a bearing stress equal to 1.5
times the factored bearing strength of the [REF:term:l]soil or [REF:term:rck]rock and all other resistances equal
to 1.3 times the factored resistances need not exceed the forces determined
in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect8.art7.sent1:long] using R_{d}R_{o} =
1.0, except that the factor of 1.3 shall not apply to the portion
of the resistance to uplift or overturning resulting from gravity
loads.

A [REF:term:fndtn]foundation is permitted to have
a factored overturning resistance less than the lateral load overturning
capacity of the supported SFRS, provided the following requirements
are met:

clauses.text:
neither the [REF:term:fndtn]foundation nor the supported
SFRS are constrained against rotation, and
the design overturning moment of the [REF:term:fndtn]foundation is

subclauses.text:
not less than 75% of the overturning capacity of the supported
SFRS, and

not less than that determined in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect8.art7.sent1:long] using
R_{d}R_{o} = 2.0.

content.text:
The design of [REF:term:fndtn]foundations shall be
such that they are capable of transferring earthquake loads and effects
between the [REF:term:bldng]building and the ground without
exceeding the capacities of the [REF:term:l]soil and [REF:term:rck]rock.

Where the Seismic
Category is SC3 or SC4, the following requirements shall
be satisfied:

clauses.text:
[REF:term:pl]piles or [REF:term:pl]pile caps, drilled piers, and [REF:term:cn]caissons shall
be interconnected by continuous ties in not less than two directions
(see [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect5.appnote98:short]),
[REF:term:pl]piles, drilled piers, and [REF:term:cn]caissons shall be embedded a minimum of 100 mm (metric) into the [REF:term:pl]pile cap or structure, and

[REF:term:pl]piles, drilled piers, and [REF:term:cn]caissons, other than wood [REF:term:pl]piles, shall
be connected to the [REF:term:pl]pile cap or structure
for a minimum tension force equal to 0.15 times (metric) the factored
compression load on the [REF:term:pl]pile.

content.text:
Where the Seismic
Category is SC3 or SC4, [REF:term:bmnt]basement walls shall be designed to resist earthquake lateral pressures from
backfill or natural ground. (See [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect5.appnote99:short].)

Where the Seismic
Category is SC4, the following requirements shall be
satisfied:

clauses.text:
[REF:term:pl]piles, drilled piers, or [REF:term:cn]caissons shall be designed and detailed to accommodate cyclic
inelastic behaviour when the design moment in the element due to earthquake
effects is greater than 75% of its moment capacity (see [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect5.appnote100:short]), and

spread footings founded on [REF:term:l]soil designated as X_{V}, where V_{s30} is less than
or equal to 180 m/s, X_{E} or X_{F} shall
be interconnected by continuous ties in not less than two directions.

content.text:
Each segment of a tie between elements that is required by [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect8.art16.sent6.clause1:medium]
                           [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect8.art16.sent8.clause2:medium] shall be designed to carry by tension
or compression a horizontal force at least equal to the greatest factored [REF:term:pl]pile cap or column vertical load in the elements
it connects, multiplied by a factor of 0.1I_{E}S(0.2), unless
it can be demonstrated that equivalent restraints can be provided
by other means. (See [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect5.appnote101:short].)

The potential for liquefaction of the [REF:term:l]soil and its consequences, such as significant ground displacement and
loss of [REF:term:l]soil strength and stiffness, shall
be evaluated based on the ground motion parameters referenced in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part1.sect1.subsect3:long], as modified by [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect8.art4:long],
and shall be taken into account in the design of the structure and
its [REF:term:fndtn]foundations. (See [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect5.appnote102:short].)

The potential for slope instability and its consequences, such
as slope displacement, shall be evaluated based on site-specific material
properties and ground motion parameters referenced in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part1.sect1.subsect3:long], as modified by [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect8.art4:long],
and shall be taken into account in the design of the structure and
