content.text:
For [REF:term:bldng]buildings in Seismic Category SC1 or SC2, other than [REF:term:pt-dtr-b]post-disaster buildings, seismically isolated [REF:term:bldng]buildings, and [REF:term:bldng]buildings with supplemental energy dissipation
systems, the requirements of [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect8.art18.sent1:short] need not apply to Categories 6 through 22 of [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect8.art18.table1:long]

For the purpose of applying [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect8.art18.sent1:short] for Categories 11 and 12 of [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect8.art18.table1:long], elements
or components shall be assumed to be flexible or flexibly connected
unless it can be shown that the fundamental period of the element
or component and its connection is less than or equal to 0.06
s (metric), in which case the element or component is classified as
being rigid and rigidly connected.

The weight of access floors shall include the [REF:term:dd-ld]dead load of the access floor and the weight of permanent
equipment, which shall not be taken as less than 25% of the floor [REF:term:lv-ld]live load.

When the mass of a tank plus its contents or the mass of a flexible
or flexibly connected piece of machinery, fixture or equipment is
greater than 10% of the mass of the supporting floor, the lateral
forces shall be determined by rational analysis.

Forces shall be applied in the horizontal direction that results
in the most critical loading for design, except for Category 6 of [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect8.art18.table1:long], where the forces shall be applied up and down
vertically.

Connections to the structure of elements and components listed
in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect8.art18.table1:long] shall be designed to support the component
or element for gravity loads, shall conform to the requirements of [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect8.art18.sent1:short], and shall also satisfy these additional
requirements:

clauses.text:
except as provided
in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect8.art18.sent17:short], friction
due to gravity loads shall not be considered to provide resistance
to earthquake forces,

R_{p} for non-ductile connections, such as adhesives
or power-actuated fasteners, shall be taken as 1.0,

R_{p} for shallow post-installed mechanical, post-installed adhesive, and
cast-in-place anchors in concrete shall be 1.5, where
shallow anchors are those with a ratio of embedment length to diameter
of less than 8,

post-installed mechanical, drop-in and adhesive anchors in concrete
shall be pre-qualified for seismic applications by cyclic load testing
in accordance with

subclauses.text: [REF:standard:csaa23.3] and
[REF:standard:aci355.2] or [REF:standard:aci355.4] as applicable,

clauses.text: power-actuated fasteners shall not be used for cyclic tension loads,

connections for non-structural elements or components of Category
1, 2 or 3 of [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect8.art18.table1:long] attached to the side of a [REF:term:bldng]building and above the first level above [REF:term:grade]grade shall satisfy the following requirements:

subclauses.text:
for connections where the body of the connection is ductile,
the body shall be designed for values of C_{p}, A_{r} and R_{p} given in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect8.art18.table1:long], and all
of the other parts of the connection, such as anchors, welds, bolts
and inserts, shall be capable of developing 2.0 times the nominal
yield resistance of the body of the connection, and

connections where the body of the connection is not ductile
shall be designed for values of C_{p} = 2.0, R_{p} = 1.0 and A_{r} given in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect8.art18.table1:long], and

clauses.text:
a ductile connection is one where the body of the connection
is capable of dissipating energy through cyclic inelastic behaviour.

content.text:
Floors and roofs acting as diaphragms shall satisfy the requirements
for diaphragms stated in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect8.art15:long]

Lateral deflections of elements or components shall be based
on the loads defined in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect8.art18.sent1:short] and
lateral deflections obtained from an elastic analysis shall be multiplied
by R_{p}/I_{E} to give realistic values of the anticipated
deflections.

The elements or components shall be designed so as not to transfer
to the structure any forces unaccounted for in the design, and rigid
elements such as walls or panels shall satisfy the requirements of [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect8.art3.sent6:long].

Seismic restraint for suspended equipment, pipes, ducts, electrical
cable trays, etc. shall be designed to meet the force and displacement
requirements of this Article and be constructed in a manner that will
not subject hanger rods to bending.

Isolated suspended equipment and components, such as pendent
lights, may be designed as a pendulum system provided that adequate
chains or cables capable of supporting 2.0 times (metric) the
weight of the suspended component are provided and the deflection
requirements of [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect8.art18.sent10:short] are satisfied.

Free-standing steel pallet storage racks are permitted to be designed according to CSA A344.2, "Standard for design and construction of steel storage racks," and to resist earthquake effects using rational analysis, provided design achieves the minimum performance level required by [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect8:long] (See [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect5.appnote107:short].)
Except as provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect8.art18.sent15:short], the relative displacement of glass in glazing systems, D_{fallout}, shall be equal to the greater of

clauses.text:
D_{fallout} ≥ 1.25I_{E}D_{p}, where
                                 
                                    D_{fallout}
                                    
                                    = relative displacement at which glass fallout occurs, and
                                 
                                 
                                    D_{p}
                                    
                                    = relative earthquake displacement that the component must
be designed to accommodate, calculated in accordance with [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect8.art13:long] and applied over the height of the glass component,
or
13 mm (metric).

content.text: Glass need not comply with [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect8.art18.sent14:short], provided at least one of the following conditions is met:

clauses.text:
the Seismic Category
is SC1 or SC2,

the glass is fully tempered, monolithic, installed in a non-[REF:term:pt-dtr-b]post-disaster building, and no part of the
glass is located more than 3 m (metric) above a walking surface,
or

the glass is annealed or heat-strengthened laminated glass in
a single thickness with an interlayer no less than 0.76 mm (metric) and captured mechanically in a wall system glazing pocket with the
perimeter secured to the frame by a wet, glazed, gunable, curing,
elastomeric sealant perimeter bead of 13 mm (metric) minimum glass
contact width.

For structures with supplemental energy dissipation, elements and components of [REF:term:bldng]buildings described in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect8.art18.table1:long] and their connections to the structure shall be designed for a
specified lateral earthquake force, V_{p}, determined at each
floor level as follows:[EQ:display:]where
                              
                                 S_{sed}
                                 
                                 = peak spectral acceleration, S_{a}(T,X), in the
period range of T = 0 s (metric) to T = 0.5 s (metric) determined
from the mean 5%-damped floor spectral acceleration values by averaging
the individual 5%-damped floor response spectra at the centroid of
the floor area at that floor level determined using Non-linear Dynamic
Analysis, and
                              
                              
                                 I_{E}, C_{p}, A_{r}, R_{p}, W_{p}
                                 
                                 = as defined in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect8.art18.sent1:short].

content.text: For the purposes of this Article and [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect8.art20:long], the following terms shall have the meanings stated herein:

clauses.text:
“seismic isolation” is an alternative seismic design concept
that consists of installing an isolation system with low horizontal
stiffness, thereby substantially increasing the fundamental period
of the structure;

“isolation system” is a collection of structural elements at
the level of the isolation interface that includes all individual
isolator units, all structural elements that transfer force between
elements of the isolation system, all connections to other structural
elements, and may also include a wind-restraint system, energy-dissipation
devices, and a displacement restraint system;

“isolator unit” is a structural element of the isolation system
that permits large lateral deformations under lateral earthquake forces
and is characterized by vertical-load-carrying capability combined
with increased horizontal flexibility and high vertical stiffness,
energy dissipation (hysteretic or viscous), self-centering capability,
and lateral restraint (sufficient elastic stiffness) under non-seismic
service lateral loads;

“isolation interface” is the boundary between the isolated upper
portion of the structure above the isolation system and the lower
portion of the structure below the isolation system; and

“wind-restraint system” is the collection of structural elements
of the isolation system that provides restraint of the seismically
isolated structure for wind loads and is permitted to be either an
integral part of the isolator units or a separate device.

content.text:
Every seismically isolated structure and every portion thereof
shall be analyzed and designed in accordance with

clauses.text: this Article and [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect8.art20:long],
other applicable requirements of this Subsection, and
appropriate engineering principles and current engineering practice.

content.text:
For the analysis and modeling of the seismically isolated structure,
the following criteria shall apply:

clauses.text:
a three-dimensional Non-linear Dynamic Analysis of the structure
shall be performed in accordance with [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect8.art12:long] (see [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect5.appnote112:short]),

unless verified from rational analysis, the inherent equivalent
viscous damping—excluding the hysteretic damping provided by the isolation
system or supplemental energy dissipation devices—used in the analysis
shall not be taken as more than 2.5% of the critical damping at the
significant modes of vibration,

all individual isolator units shall be modeled with sufficient
detail to account for their non-linear force-deformation characteristics,
including effects of the relevant loads, and with consideration of
variations in material properties over the design life of the structure,
and

except for elements of the isolation system, other components
of the seismically isolated structure shall be modeled using elastic
material properties in accordance with [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect8.art3.sent8:long].

content.text: The ground motion time histories used in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect8.art19.sent3:short] shall be

clauses.text:
appropriately selected and scaled following good engineering
practice,
compatible with

subclauses.text:
a response spectrum derived from the design spectral acceleration
values, S(T), defined in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect8.art4.sent6:long] for site designations X_{V}, where V_{s30} is greater
than 360 m/s, X_{A}, X_{B} and X_{C}, and

a 5%-damped response spectrum based on a site-specific evaluation
for site designations X_{V}, where V_{s30} is less than or equal to 360 m/s, X_{D}, X_{E} and
X_{F}, and

clauses.text:
amplitude-scaled in an appropriate manner over the period range
of 0.2T1
                               (metric) to 1.5T1
                               (metric),
where T_{1} is the period of the isolated structure determined
using the post-yield stiffness of the isolation system in the horizontal
direction under consideration, or the period specified in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect8.art20.sent1:long] if the post-yield stiffness of the isolation system
is not well defined.

content.text:
The period of the isolated structure, determined using the post-yield
stiffness of the isolation system in the horizontal direction under
consideration, shall be greater than three times the period of the
structure above the isolation interface calculated as a fixed base.

The isolation system shall be configured to produce a restoring
force such that the lateral force at the TDD at the centre of mass
of the isolated structure above the isolation interface is at least
0.025W_{b} greater than the lateral force at 50% of the TDD
at the same location, in each horizontal direction, where W_{b} is the portion of W above the isolation interface.

The values of [REF:term:tr]storey shears, [REF:term:tr]storey forces, member forces, and deflections used
in the design of all structural framing elements and components of
the isolation system shall be obtained from analysis conforming to [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect8.art19.sent3:long] using one of the following values, whichever produces
the most critical effect:

clauses.text:
mean plus I_{E} times the standard deviation of results
of all Non-linear Dynamic Analyses, or

√I_{E} times the mean of the results of all Non-linear
Dynamic Analyses.

content.text:
The force-deformation and damping characteristics of the isolation
system used in the analysis and design of seismically isolated structures
shall be validated by testing at least two full-size specimens of
each predominant type and size of isolator unit of the isolation system,
which shall include

clauses.text: the individual isolator units,
separate supplemental damping devices, if used, and
separate sacrificial wind-restraint systems, if used.

content.text:
The force-deformation characteristics and damping value of a
representative sample of the isolator units installed in the [REF:term:bldng]building shall be validated by tests prior to
their installation.

A diaphragm or horizontal structural elements shall provide
continuity immediately above the isolation interface to transmit forces
due to non-uniform ground motions from one part of the structure to
another.

All structural framing elements shall be designed for the forces
described in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect8.art20.sent3:short] with RdRo = 1.0 (metric), except

clauses.text:
for structures with IE < 1.5 (metric), all
SFRSs shall be detailed in accordance with the requirements for Rd ≥ 1.5 (metric) and the applicable referenced design standards,
and

for structures with IE = 1.5 (metric), all SFRSs
shall be detailed in accordance with the requirements for Rd ≥ 2.0 (metric) and the applicable referenced design standards.

content.text:
The height restrictions noted in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect8.art9.table1:long] need
not apply to seismically isolated structures.
All isolator units shall be

clauses.text: designed for the forces described in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect8.art20.sent3:short], and

able to accommodate the TDD determined at the specific location
of each isolator unit.

content.text:
The isolation system, including a separate wind-restraint system
if used, shall limit lateral displacement due to wind loads across
the isolation interface to a value equal to that required for the
least [REF:term:tr]storey height in accordance with [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect3.art5.sent3:long].
For the purposes of this Article and [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect8.art22:long], the following terms shall have the meanings stated herein:

clauses.text:
“supplemental energy dissipation device” is a dedicated structural
element of the supplemental energy dissipation system that dissipates
energy due to relative motion of each of its ends or by alternative
means, and includes all pins, bolts, gusset plates, brace extensions
and other components required to connect it to the other elements
of the structure; a device may be classified as either displacement-dependent
or velocity-dependent, or a combination thereof, and may be configured
to act in either a linear or non-linear manner; and

“supplemental energy dissipation system” is a collection of
energy dissipation devices installed in a structure that supplement
the energy dissipation of the SFRS.

content.text:
Every structure with a supplemental energy dissipation system
and every portion thereof shall be designed and constructed in accordance
with

clauses.text: this Article and [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect8.art22:long],
other applicable requirements of this Subsection, and
appropriate engineering principles and current engineering practice.

content.text:
Where supplemental energy dissipation devices are used across
the isolation interface of a seismically isolated structure, displacements,
velocities, and accelerations shall be determined in accordance with [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect8.art20:long]

For the analysis and modeling of structures with supplemental
energy dissipation devices, the following criteria shall apply:

clauses.text:
a three-dimensional Non-linear Dynamic Analysis of the structure
shall be performed in accordance with [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect8.art12:long] (see [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect5.appnote115:short]),

for an SFRS with Rd > 1.0 (metric), the non-linear
hysteretic behaviour of the SFRS shall be explicitly—with sufficient
detail—accounted for in the modeling and analysis of the structure,

unless verified from rational analysis, the inherent equivalent
viscous damping—excluding the damping provided by the supplemental
energy dissipation devices—used in the analysis shall not be taken
as more than 2.5% of the critical damping at the significant modes
of vibration,

all supplemental energy dissipation devices shall be modeled
with sufficient detail to account for their non-linear force deformation
characteristics, including effects of the relevant loads, and with
consideration of variations in their properties over the design life
of the structure, and

except for the SFRS and elements of the supplemental energy
dissipation system, other components of the structure shall be modeled
using elastic material properties in accordance with [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect8.art3.sent8:long].

content.text: The ground motion time histories used in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect8.art21.sent4:short] shall be

clauses.text:
appropriately selected and scaled following good engineering
practice,

compatible with a 5%-damped response spectrum derived from the
design spectral acceleration values, S(T), defined in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect8.art4.sent6:long], and

amplitude-scaled in an appropriate manner over the period range
of 0.2T1
                               (metric) to 1.5T1
                               (metric),
where T_{1} is the fundamental lateral period of the structure
with the supplemental energy dissipation system.

content.text:
The values of [REF:term:tr]storey shears, [REF:term:tr]storey forces, member forces, and deflections for
the design of all structural framing elements and all supplemental
energy dissipation devices shall be obtained from analysis conforming
to [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect8.art21.sent4:long] using one of the following values,
whichever produces the most critical effect:

clauses.text:
mean plus I_{E} times the standard deviation of the
results of all Non-linear Dynamic Analyses, or

√I_{E} times the mean of the results of all Non-linear
Dynamic Analyses.

content.text:
The largest inter[REF:term:tr]storey deflection at
any level of the structure as determined in accordance with [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect8.art22.sent1:short] shall conform to the limits stated
in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect8.art13.sent3:long].

The force-deformation and force-velocity characteristics of
the supplemental energy dissipation  devices used in the analysis
and design of structures with supplemental energy dissipation systems
shall be validated by testing at least two full-size specimens of
each type of supplementary energy dissipation device.

The force-deformation and force-velocity characteristics and
damping values of a representative sample of the supplemental energy
dissipation devices installed in the [REF:term:bldng]building shall be validated by tests prior to their installation.

All components of a supplemental energy dissipation device,
except that portion of the device that dissipates energy, shall be
designed to remain elastic.
All structural framing elements shall be designed

clauses.text:
for an SFRS with R_{d} = 1.0, using the forces referred
to in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect8.art22.sent1:short] with R_{d}R_{o} = 1.0, except that the SFRS shall be detailed in accordance
with the requirements for R_{d} ≥ 1.5 and the applicable referenced
design standards, or

for an SFRS with R_{d} > 1.0, using the forces referred
to in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect8.art22.sent1:short] with R_{d}R_{o} = 1.0, except that the SFRS shall be detailed in accordance
with the requirements for the selected R_{d} and the applicable
referenced design standards.

content.text:
Supplemental energy dissipation devices and other components
of the supplemental energy dissipation system shall be designed in
accordance with [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect8.art22.sent1:short] with consideration
of the following:

clauses.text:
low-cycle, large-displacement degradation due to earthquake
loads,

high-cycle, small-displacement degradation due to wind, thermal,
or other cyclic loads,
forces or displacements due to gravity loads,

adhesion of device parts due to corrosion or abrasion, biodegradation,
moisture, or chemical exposure,

exposure to environmental conditions, including, but not limited
to, temperature, humidity, moisture, radiation (e.g., ultraviolet
light), and reactive or corrosive substances (e.g., salt water),

devices subject to failure due to low-cycle fatigue must resist
wind forces without slip, movement, or inelastic cycling,

the range of thermal conditions, device wear, manufacturing
tolerances, and other effects that cause device properties to vary
during the design life of the device, and

connection points of devices must provide sufficient articulation
to accommodate simultaneous longitudinal, lateral, and vertical displacements
of the supplemental energy dissipation system.

content.text:
Means of access for inspection and removal for replacement of
all supplemental energy dissipation devices shall be provided.

articles.title:
Additional Performance Requirements for Post-disaster Buildings,
High Importance Category Buildings, and a Subset of Normal Importance
Category Buildings

content.text:
[REF:term:bldng]Buildings designed in accordance
with [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect8.art19:long]
                           [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect8.art22:long] need not comply with this Article.

The design of [REF:term:pt-dtr-b]post-disaster buildings in Seismic Category SC2, SC3 or SC4 shall be verified using 5%-damped
spectral acceleration values based on a 5% probability of exceedance
in 50 years and shall satisfy the following requirements:

clauses.text:
the [REF:term:bldng]building shall be shown to behave
elastically for a specified lateral earthquake force, V, determined
in accordance with [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect8.art11.sent2:long] using IE = 1.0 (metric) and RdRo = 1. (metric)3,

the largest inter[REF:term:tr]storey deflection at
any level of the [REF:term:bldng]building, as determined
in accordance with [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect8.art13.sent2:long] using I_{E} = 1.0 and R_{d}R_{o} = 1.0, shall not exceed 0.005h_{s}, and

the connections of elements and components of the [REF:term:bldng]building described in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect8.art18.table1:long] with R_{p} > 1.5 shall be shown to behave elastically
for a specified lateral earthquake force, V_{p}, determined
in accordance with [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect8.art18.sent1:long] using R_{p} = 1.5.

content.text:
The design of High Importance Category [REF:term:bldng]buildings in Seismic Category SC3 or SC4 shall be verified using 5%-damped
spectral acceleration values based on a 10% probability of exceedance
in 50 years and shall satisfy the following requirements:

clauses.text:
the [REF:term:bldng]building shall be shown to behave
elastically for a specified lateral earthquake force, V, determined
in accordance with [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect8.art11.sent2:long] using IE = 1.0 (metric) and RdRo = 1.3 (metric),

the largest inter[REF:term:tr]storey deflection at
any level of the [REF:term:bldng]building, as determined
in accordance with [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect8.art13.sent2:long] using I_{E} = 1.0 and R_{d}R_{o} = 1.0, shall not exceed 0.005h_{s}, and

the connections of elements and components of the [REF:term:bldng]building described in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect8.art18.table1:long] with Rp > 1.3 (metric) shall be shown to behave
elastically for a specified lateral earthquake force, V_{p}, determined in accordance with [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect8.art18.sent1:long] using Rp = 1.3 (metric).

content.text:
For Normal Importance Category [REF:term:bldng]buildings in Seismic Category SC4 with a height above [REF:term:grade]grade of more than 30 m (metric), the structural framing
elements not considered to be part of the SFRS shall be designed to
behave elastically for a specified lateral earthquake force, V, determined
in accordance with [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect8.art11.sent2:long] using spectral acceleration
values based on a 10% probability of exceedance in 50 years and RdRo = 1.3 (metric).

For the purposes of applying [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect8.art23.sent2:short]
                           [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect8.art23.sent4:short], torsional moments due to accidental eccentricities
need not be considered if B, as determined in accordance with [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect8.art11.sent10:long], does not exceed 1.7.

For the purposes of applying [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect8.art23.sent2:short]
                           [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect8.art23.sent4:short], elements of the SFRS and structural framing elements
not considered to be part of the SFRS, when included in the analysis,
shall be modeled in accordance with [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect8.art3.sent8:long] using
elastic properties.

All other requirements of [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect8.art2:long]
                           [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect8.art18:long] shall
be satisfied in meeting the additional requirements of this Article.
This Section applies to [REF:term:xcvtn]excavations and [REF:term:fndtn]foundation systems for [REF:term:bldng]buildings.

A [REF:term:brfc-nvt]subsurface investigation, including [REF:term:grndwtr]groundwater  conditions, shall be carried out
by or under the direction of a professional engineer having knowledge
and experience in planning and executing such investigations to a
degree appropriate for the [REF:term:bldng]building and
its use, the ground and the surrounding site conditions. (See [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect5.appnote116:short].)

Drawings associated with [REF:term:fndtn]foundations and [REF:term:xcvtn]excavations shall conform to the
appropriate requirements of [REF:internal:nbc.divC.part2.sect2:long]. (See [REF:internal:nbc.divC.part2.sect2.subsect4.art6:long].)

A field review shall be carried out by the [REF:term:dgnr]designer or by another suitably qualified person to ascertain
that the subsurface conditions are consistent with the design and
that construction is carried out in accordance with the design and
good engineering practice. (See [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect5.appnote117:short].)
The review required by [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect2.subsect2.art3.sent1:short] shall be carried out

clauses.text: on a continuous basis

subclauses.text:
during the construction of all [REF:term:dp-fndtn]deep foundation
units with all pertinent information recorded for each [REF:term:fndtn-nt]foundation unit,

during the installation and removal of retaining structures
and related backfilling operations, and

during the placement of engineered [REF:term:fll]fills that are to be used to support the [REF:term:fndtn-nt]foundation
units, and

clauses.text: as required, unless otherwise directed by the [REF:term:thrt-hvn]authority having jurisdiction,

subclauses.text:
in the construction of all [REF:term:hllw-fnd]shallow foundation
units, and
in excavating, dewatering and other related works.

content.text:
If, during construction, the [REF:term:l]soil, [REF:term:rck]rock or [REF:term:grndwtr]groundwater is found not to be of the type or in the condition used in design
and as indicated on the drawings, the design shall be reassessed by
the [REF:term:dgnr]designer.

If, during construction, climatic or any other conditions change
the properties of the [REF:term:l]soil, [REF:term:rck]rock or [REF:term:grndwtr]groundwater, the design
shall be reassessed by the [REF:term:dgnr]designer.

Wood used in [REF:term:fndtn]foundations or in support
of [REF:term:l]soil or [REF:term:rck]rock shall
conform with the appropriate requirements of [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect3.subsect1:long]

Wood exposed to [REF:term:l] soil, [REF:term:rck]rock or air above the lowest anticipated [REF:term:grndwtr]groundwater  table shall be treated with preservative in conformance with [REF:standard:csao80series] and the requirements of
the appropriate standard as follows:

clauses.text: [REF:standard:csao80.1]
[REF:standard:csao80.2] or
[REF:standard:csao80.3]

content.text:
Wood treated as
required in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect2.subsect3.art2.sent1:short] shall be cared
for as provided in [REF:external:csao80.0]Clause 4 of 
                           [REF:standard:csao80.0]

Plain or reinforced masonry used in [REF:term:fndtn]foundations or in support of [REF:term:l]soil or [REF:term:rck]rock shall conform with the requirements of [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect3.subsect2:long]

Where plain or reinforced masonry in [REF:term:fndtn]foundations or in structures supporting [REF:term:l]soil or [REF:term:rck]rock may be subject to conditions conducive to
deterioration, protection shall be provided to prevent such deterioration.

Plain, reinforced or pre-stressed concrete used in [REF:term:fndtn]foundations or in support of [REF:term:l]soil or [REF:term:rck]rock shall conform with the
requirements of [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect3.subsect3:long]

Where concrete in [REF:term:fndtn]foundations may
be subject to chemical attack, it shall be treated in conformance
with the requirements in [REF:standard:csaa23.1]

Steel used in [REF:term:fndtn] foundations or in
support of [REF:term:l]soil or [REF:term:rck] rock shall conform with the appropriate requirements of [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect3.subsect3:long] or [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect3.subsect4:number], unless otherwise specified in this Section.

Where steel [REF:term:pl] piles are used in [REF:term:dp-fndtn]deep foundations and act as permanent load-carrying
members, the steel shall conform with one of the following standards:

clauses.text: [REF:standard:astma252]
[REF:standard:astma283m]
[REF:standard:astma1008m]
[REF:standard:astma1011m] or
[REF:standard:csag40.21]

content.text:
Where high strength steel is used for tendons in anchor systems
used for the permanent support of a [REF:term:fndtn]foundation or in the erection of temporary support of [REF:term:l]soil or [REF:term:rck]rock adjacent to an [REF:term:xcvtn]excavation, it shall conform with the requirements of [REF:standard:csaa23.1]

Where conditions are corrosive to steel, adequate protection
of exposed steel shall be provided. (See [REF:internal:nbc.divA.part1.sect2.subsect1.art1:long] for use of other materials.)

The design of [REF:term:fndtn]foundations, [REF:term:xcvtn]excavations and [REF:term:l]soil-
and [REF:term:rck]rock-retaining structures shall be based
on a [REF:term:brfc-nvt]subsurface investigation carried
out in conformance with the requirements of this Section, and on any
of the following, as appropriate:

clauses.text:
application of generally accepted geotechnical and civil engineering
principles by a professional engineer especially qualified in this
field of work, as provided in this Section and other Sections of Part
4,

established local practice, where such practice includes successful
experience both with [REF:term:l]soils and [REF:term:rck]rocks of similar type and condition and with a [REF:term:fndtn]foundation or [REF:term:xcvtn]excavation of similar type, construction method, size and depth, or

in situ testing of [REF:term:fndtn-nt]foundation units, such as the load testing of [REF:term:pl]piles, anchors
or footings, carried out by a person competent in this field of work.

content.text:
The [REF:term:fndtn]foundations of a [REF:term:bldng]building shall be capable of resisting all the
loads stipulated in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1:long], in accordance with
limit states design in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect3:long]

For the purpose of the application of the load combinations
given in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect3.art2.table1:long], the geotechnical components
of loads and the factored geotechnical resistances at ULS shall be
determined by a suitably qualified and experienced professional engineer.
(See [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect5.appnote119:short].)

Geotechnical components of service loads and geotechnical reactions
for SLS shall be determined by a suitably qualified and experienced
professional engineer.

The [REF:term:fndtn]foundation of a [REF:term:bldng]building shall be designed to satisfy SLS requirements within
the limits that the [REF:term:bldng]building is designed
to accommodate, including total settlement and differential settlement,
heave, lateral movement, tilt or rotation. (See [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect5.appnote120:short].)

Communication, interaction and coordination between the [REF:term:dgnr]designer and the professional engineer responsible
for the geotechnical aspects of the project shall take place to a
degree commensurate with the complexity and requirements of the project.

A [REF:term:brfc-nvt]subsurface investigation shall
be carried out to the depth and extent to which the [REF:term:bldng]building or [REF:term:xcvtn]excavation will significantly
change the stress in the [REF:term:l]soil or [REF:term:rck]rock, or to such a depth and extent as to provide
all the necessary information for the design and construction of the [REF:term:xcvtn]excavation or the [REF:term:fndtn]foundations.

The identification and classification of [REF:term:l]soil, [REF:term:rck]rock and [REF:term:grndwtr]groundwater and descriptions of their engineering and physical properties shall
be in accordance with a widely accepted system.

Except as permitted in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect2.subsect4.art4.sent2:short], the [REF:term:brng-rfc]bearing surface  of a [REF:term:fndtn]foundation shall be below the level of potential
damage, including damage resulting from [REF:term:frt-ctn] frost
action, and the [REF:term:fndtn]foundation shall
be designed to prevent damage resulting from [REF:term:dfrzng]adfreezing  and frost jacking. (See [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect5.appnote121:short].)

The [REF:term:brng-rfc]bearing surface of a [REF:term:fndtn]foundation need not be below the level of potential
damage from frost where the [REF:term:fndtn]foundation

clauses.text: is designed against [REF:term:frt-ctn]frost action, or

overlies material not susceptible to [REF:term:frt-ctn]frost
action.

content.text:
Where a [REF:term:fndtn]foundation is to rest on,
in or near sloping ground, this particular condition shall be provided
for in the design.

Where there is eccentricity or inclination of loading in [REF:term:fndtn-nt]foundation units, this effect shall be fully
investigated and provided for in the design.

Where dynamic loading conditions apply, the effects shall be
assessed by a special investigation of these conditions and provided
for in the design.

Where a [REF:term:fndtn]foundation or any part of
a [REF:term:bldng]building is subject to hydrostatic uplift,
the effects shall be provided for in the design.

Where proposed construction will result in a temporary or permanent
change in the [REF:term:grndwtr-]groundwater level, the
effects of this change on adjacent [REF:term:bldng]buildings shall be fully investigated and provided for in the design.

Where conditions of permafrost are encountered or proven to
exist, the design of the [REF:term:fndtn]foundation shall
be based upon analysis of these conditions by a person especially
qualified in that field of work.

Where swelling or shrinking [REF:term:l]soils, in
which movements resulting from moisture content changes may be sufficient
to cause damage to a structure, are encountered or known to exist,
such a condition shall be fully investigated and provided for in the
design.

Where [REF:term:rck]rock that expands or deteriorates
when subjected to unfavourable environmental conditions or to stress
release is known to exist, this condition shall be fully investigated
and provided for in the design.
[REF:term:bldng]Buildings may be placed on [REF:term:fll]fill if it can be shown by [REF:term:brfc-nvt]subsurface investigation that

clauses.text:
the [REF:term:fll]fill is or can be made capable
of safely supporting the [REF:term:bldng]building,
detrimental movement of the [REF:term:bldng]building or of services leading to the [REF:term:bldng]building will not occur, and
explosive gases can be controlled or do not exist.

content.text:
The structural design of the [REF:term:fndtn]foundation of a [REF:term:bldng]building, the procedures and construction
practices shall conform with the appropriate Sections of this Code
unless otherwise specified in this Section.

The design of [REF:term:xcvtn] excavations and of
supports for the sides of [REF:term:xcvtn]excavations  shall
conform with [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect2.subsect4:long] and with this Subsection.
(See [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect5.appnote122:short].)

Every [REF:term:xcvtn]excavation shall be undertaken
in such a manner as to

clauses.text: prevent movement that would cause damage to adjacent [REF:term:bldng]buildings at all phases of construction, and
comply with the appropriate requirements of Part 8.

content.text:
Material shall not be placed nor shall equipment be operated
or placed in or adjacent to an [REF:term:xcvtn]excavation in a manner that may endanger the integrity of the [REF:term:xcvtn]excavation or its supports.

The sides of an [REF:term:xcvtn] excavation in [REF:term:l]soil or [REF:term:rck]rock  shall be supported
by a retaining structure conforming with the requirements of [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect2.subsect5.art1:long] and [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect2.subsect5.art2:number], except as permitted in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect2.subsect5.art4:long]

The sides of an [REF:term:xcvtn] excavation in [REF:term:l]soil or [REF:term:rck]rock  may be unsupported
where a design is prepared in conformance with the requirements of [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect2.subsect5.art1:long] and [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect2.subsect5.art2:number]

Surface water, all [REF:term:grndwtr]groundwater, [REF:term:prchd-gr]perched groundwater and in particular [REF:term:rtn-grnd]artesian groundwater shall be kept under control
at all phases of [REF:term:xcvtn]excavation and construction.

At all phases of [REF:term:xcvtn]excavation and construction,
loss of ground due to water or any other cause shall be prevented.

All sides of an [REF:term:xcvtn]excavation, supported
and unsupported, shall be continuously maintained and protected from
possible deterioration by construction activity or by the action of
frost, rain and wind.

Where an [REF:term:xcvtn]excavation is backfilled,
the backfill shall be placed so as to

clauses.text:
provide lateral support to the [REF:term:l]soil adjacent
to the [REF:term:xcvtn]excavation, and
prevent detrimental movements.

content.text:
The material used as backfill or [REF:term:fll]fill supporting a footing, [REF:term:fndtn]foundation or a
floor on [REF:term:grade]grade shall be of a type that
is not subject to detrimental volume change with changes in moisture
content and temperature.

The design of [REF:term:hllw-fnd]shallow foundations shall be in conformance with [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect2.subsect4:long] and the requirements of this Subsection. (See [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect5.appnote123:short].)

Where a [REF:term:hllw-fnd]shallow foundation is
to be placed on [REF:term:l]soil or [REF:term:rck]rock, the [REF:term:l]soil or [REF:term:rck]rock shall be cleaned of loose and unsound material and shall be adequate
to support the design load taking into account temperature, precipitation,
construction activities and other factors that may lead to changes
in the properties of [REF:term:l]soil or [REF:term:rck]rock.
Where a [REF:term:hllw-fnd]shallow foundation unit has not been placed or located as indicated on the drawings,

clauses.text: the error shall be corrected, or

the design of the [REF:term:fndtn-nt]foundation unit shall be recalculated for the altered conditions by the [REF:term:dgnr]designer  and action taken as required in [REF:internal:nbc.divC.part2.sect2.subsect4.art7:long].

content.text:
If a [REF:term:hllw-fnd] shallow foundation unit is
damaged,

clauses.text: it shall be repaired, or

the design of the [REF:term:fndtn-nt]foundation unit shall be recalculated for the damaged condition by the [REF:term:dgnr]designer  and action taken as required in [REF:internal:nbc.divC.part2.sect2.subsect4.art7:long].

content.text:
A [REF:term:dp-fndtn] deep foundation shall provide
support for a [REF:term:bldng] building by transferring
loads by end-bearing to a competent stratum at considerable depth
below the structure, or by mobilizing resistance by adhesion or friction,
or both, in the [REF:term:l]soil or [REF:term:rck]rock in which it is placed. (See [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect5.appnote124:short].)

[REF:term:dp-fndtn]Deep foundations shall be designed
in conformance with [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect2.subsect4:long] and this Subsection.
(See [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect5.appnote125:short].)

Where [REF:term:dp-fndtn]deep foundation units are
load tested, as required in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect2.subsect4.art1.sent1.clause3:long], the determination
of the number and type of load test and the interpretation of the
results shall be carried out by a professional engineer especially
qualified in this field of work. (See [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect5.appnote126:short].)

The design of [REF:term:dp-fndtn]deep foundations shall be determined on the basis of geotechnical considerations
taking into account

clauses.text: the method of installation,
the degree of inspection,
the spacing of [REF:term:fndtn-nt]foundation units and group effects,
other requirements in this Subsection, and

the appropriate structural requirements in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1:long] and [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect3.subsect1:long], [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect3.subsect3:number] and [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect3.subsect4:number]

content.text:
The portion of a [REF:term:dp-fndtn]deep foundation unit permanently in contact with [REF:term:l]soil or [REF:term:rck]rock shall be structurally designed as a laterally
supported compression member.

The portion of a [REF:term:dp-fndtn]deep foundation unit that is not permanently in contact with [REF:term:l]soil or [REF:term:rck]rock shall be structurally designed
as a laterally unsupported compression member.

The structural design of prefabricated [REF:term:dp-fndtn]deep foundation units shall allow for all stresses resulting
from driving, handling and testing.

Permissible deviations from the design alignment and the location
of the top of [REF:term:dp-fndtn]deep foundation units shall
be determined by design analysis and shall be indicated on the drawings.

Where a [REF:term:dp-fndtn] deep foundation unit has
not been placed within the permissible deviations referred to in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect2.subsect7.art3:long], the condition of the [REF:term:fndtn]foundation shall be assessed by the [REF:term:dgnr]designer, any
necessary changes made and action taken as required in [REF:internal:nbc.divC.part2.sect2.subsect4.art7:long].

[REF:term:dp-fndtn]Deep foundation units shall be
installed in such a manner as not to impair

clauses.text:
the strength of the [REF:term:dp-fndtn]deep foundation units and the properties of the [REF:term:l]soil or [REF:term:rck]rock on or in which they are placed beyond the
calculated or anticipated limits,
the integrity of previously installed [REF:term:dp-fndtn]deep foundation units, or
the integrity of neighbouring [REF:term:bldng]buildings.

content.text:
Where inspection shows that a [REF:term:dp-fndtn]deep foundation
unit is damaged or not consistent with design or good engineering
practice,

clauses.text: such a unit shall be reassessed by the [REF:term:dgnr]designer,
any necessary changes shall be made, and
action shall be taken as required in [REF:internal:nbc.divC.part2.sect2.subsect4.art7:long].

content.text:
Where special [REF:term:fndtn]foundation systems
are used, such systems shall conform to [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect2.subsect4:long], [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect1.art5.sent2:long] and [REF:internal:nbc.divA.part1.sect2.subsect1.art1:long].

Existing [REF:term:fndtn]foundations may be used

appendix.introduction:
These Notes are included for explanatory
purposes only and do not form part of the requirements. The number
that introduces each Note corresponds to the applicable requirement
in this Part.

paragraphs.content:
The requirements of Part 4, including the CSA design standards, generally
provide a satisfactory level of structural integrity. Additional considerations
may, however, be required for building systems made of components
of different materials, whose interconnection is not covered by existing
CSA design standards, buildings outside the scope of existing CSA
design standards, and buildings exposed to severe accidental loads
such as vehicle impact or explosion. Further guidance can be found
in the Commentary entitled Structural Integrity in the [REF:standard:nrcc-nbcug4]

Information
on serviceability can be found in the Commentary entitled Deflection
and Vibration Criteria for Serviceability and Fatigue Limit States
in the [REF:standard:nrcc-nbcug4]

[REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect1.art5.sent2:long] provides for the use of design methods
not specified in Part 4, including full-scale testing and model analogues.
This provision is usually used to permit the acceptance of new and
innovative structures or to permit the acceptance of model tests such
as those used to determine structural behaviour, or snow or wind loads. [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect1.art5.sent2:long] specifically requires that the level of safety
and performance be at least equivalent to that provided by design
to Part 4 and requires that loads and designs conform to [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1:long]

[REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect1.art5.sent2:long] and the provision for alternative
solutions stated in [REF:internal:nbc.divA.part1.sect2.subsect1.art1.sent1.clause2:long] are
not intended to allow structural design using design standards other
than those listed in Part 4. The acceptance of structures that have
been designed to other design standards would require the designer
to prove to the appropriate authority that the structure provides
the level of safety and performance required by [REF:internal:nbc.divA.part1.sect2.subsect1.art1.sent1.clause2:long]. The equivalence of safety and performance can
only be established by analyzing the structure for the loads and load
factors set out in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1:long] and by demonstrating
that the structure at least meets the requirements of the design standards
listed in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect3:long]
                     [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect4:long]

Information
on the definitions can be found in the Commentary entitled Limit States
Design in the [REF:standard:nrcc-nbcug4]

Information on effects due to temperature changes can be found in
the Commentary entitled Effects of Deformations in Building Components
in the [REF:standard:nrcc-nbcug4]

In a building containing more than one major occupancy and classified
in more than one Importance Category, the classification of each independent
structural system shall be the same as for any part of the building
that is dependent on that structural system and for the highest usage
group according to [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect2.art1.table1:long]

A minor storage
building is an example of a Low Importance Category building.

Low-human-occupancy farm buildings with an occupant load of 1 person (metric) or less per 40 m2
                         (metric) of
floor area are also examples of Low Importance Category buildings.

Most buildings will
fall into the Normal Importance Category.

The following types of buildings may be classified in the Normal
Importance Category: buildings that are equipped with secondary containment
of dangerous goods, including, but not limited to, double-walled tanks, dikes of sufficient
size to contain a spill, and other means to contain a spill or a blast
within the property boundary of the facility and prevent the release
of harmful quantities of contaminants to the air, soil, groundwater,
surface water or atmosphere, as the case may be.

The following buildings
may contain sufficient quantities of dangerous goods to
be classified in the High Importance Category:
                           petrochemical facilities,
                           fuel storage facilities (other than those required for post-disaster
use), and
                           manufacturing or storage facilities containing dangerous goods.

Information on community
centres can be found in the Commentary entitled Limit States Design
in the [REF:standard:nrcc-nbcug4]

Before classifying a building as a post-disaster building, Code
users should consider the intent of the classification and look beyond
the name of the building. For example, a building that is named “ABC
Treatment” but is used for emergency care should be considered as
a hospital and, as such, classified as a post-disaster building. Conversely,
a building named “XYZ Hospital” that is only used for walk-in medical
services could be classified as a Normal Importance Category building.

The
intent of [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect2.art2.sent1:long] is to draw attention to the
fact that there are loads, forces and effects that need to be considered
in addition to those specified in the Code. These loads, forces and
effects will vary in need, application, and magnitude for each use
and location. Some may result from environmental considerations (e.g.,
ice accretion, wave and ice action, water flow) while others will
result from the use and occupancy of the facility (e.g., dangerous
goods storage, manufacturing and mining operations). The reasonable
determination of the probability, type and magnitude of project-specific
loads must be assessed by a knowledgeable project team that includes
the building owner/operator and experienced design professionals,
and incorporated into the design where deemed necessary to maintain
the safety and integrity of the facility.

In recent years, security issues have prompted the consideration
of loads and effects due to improvised explosive devices and other
methods of sabotage. Consideration of these loads is driven by operational
and public safety requirements, and their incorporation in the design
is not considered a mandatory provision of the Code.

Information
on limit states design can be found in the Commentary entitled Limit
States Design in the [REF:standard:nrcc-nbcug4]

The load combinations in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect3.art2.table1:long]
                        [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect3.art2.table2:long] apply
to most situations for loadbearing building structures. Guidance on
special situations such as load combinations for fire resistance and
building envelopes is given in the Commentary entitled Limit States
Design in the [REF:standard:nrcc-nbcug4]

divisions.title: Load Cases and Crane Load Effects

paragraphs.content:
The load combinations in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect3.art2.table1:long] are to
be evaluated for structures with crane load effects for the scenario
where the crane loads are zero, and for structures without crane loads.
 The load combinations in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect3.art2.table2:long] are to be evaluated
for structures with crane loads for the scenario where the crane load
effects are other than zero.

Crane-supporting structures that have cranes in multiple parallel
bays should be designed for the maximum vertical crane load with the
cranes positioned for the most critical effect in conjunction with
a lateral load with each crane in turn positioned for the most critical
effect. For load combinations that include crane loads, additional
guidance can be found in [REF:standard:cisc-csssdg]

application_notes.title:
Effects of Lateral Earth Pressure,
H, Pre-stress, P, and Imposed Deformation, T, in Design Calculations

divisions.title: Effects of Lateral Earth Pressure, H, in Design Calculations

paragraphs.content:
For common building structures below ground level, such as walls,
columns and frames, 1.5H is added to load combinations 2 to 4. For

Limit States Design in the [REF:standard:nrcc-nbcug4]

paragraphs.content:
For structures and building envelopes designed in accordance
with the requirements specified in the standards listed in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect3:long], with the exception of [REF:external:csaa23.3]Clauses 8 and 18 of 
                        [REF:standard:csaa23.3] P and T need not be included in the load
combinations of [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect3.art2.table1:long]. For structures not within
the scope of the standards listed in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect3:long],
including building envelopes, P and T must be taken into account in
the design calculations. For recommended load combinations including
T, see the Commentary entitled Limit States Design in the [REF:standard:nrcc-nbcug4]

Information on overturning, uplift and sliding can be found
in the Commentary entitled Limit States Design in the [REF:standard:nrcc-nbcug4]

Failure due to fatigue of building structures referred to in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect3:long] and designed for serviceability in accordance
with [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect3.art6:long] is, in general, unlikely except for
girders supporting heavily used cranes, on which [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect5.art11:long] provides guidance.

Guidance on vibration effects can be found in the Commentary entitled
Deflection and Vibration Criteria for Serviceability and Fatigue Limit
States in the [REF:standard:nrcc-nbcug4]

application_notes.title:
Loads and Load Combinations for
Serviceability

paragraphs.content:
The loads and load combinations for serviceability
depend on the serviceability limit states and on the properties of
the structural materials. Information on loads and load combinations
for the serviceability limit states, other than those controlled by
deflection, can be found in the Commentary entitled Deflection and
Vibration Criteria for Serviceability and Fatigue Limit States in
the [REF:standard:nrcc-nbcug4]

Information on the determination of acceleration due to vibrations
resulting from loads L and W can be found in the Commentary entitled
Wind Load and Effects in the [REF:standard:nrcc-nbcug4]

Serviceability
criteria for deflections that cause damage to non-structural building
components can be found in the standards listed in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect3:long] Information on deflections can be found in the
Commentary entitled Deflection and Vibration Criteria for Serviceability
and Fatigue Limit States in the [REF:standard:nrcc-nbcug4] Information on loads and load combinations
for calculating deflection can be found in the Commentary entitled
Limit States Design in the [REF:standard:nrcc-nbcug4]

The limitation of 1/500 drift per storey may be exceeded if
it can be established that the drift as calculated will not result
in damage to non-structural elements. Information on lateral deflection
can be found in the Commentary entitled Wind Load and Effects in the [REF:standard:nrcc-nbcug4]

Information
on floor vibration can be found in the Commentary entitled Deflection
and Vibration Criteria for Serviceability and Fatigue Limit States
in the [REF:standard:nrcc-nbcug4] Information on loads and load combinations for the calculation
of vibration can be found in the Commentary entitled Limit States
Design in the [REF:standard:nrcc-nbcug4]

Floor Vibrations Caused by Resonance
with Operating Machinery or Equipment

paragraphs.content:
Guidance on floor
vibration effects caused by operating machinery and equipment can
be found in the Commentary entitled Deflection and Vibration Criteria
for Serviceability and Fatigue Limit States in the [REF:standard:nrcc-nbcug4]

Information on a dynamic analysis of floor vibrations from rhythmic
activities can be found in the Commentary entitled Deflection and
Vibration Criteria for Serviceability and Fatigue Limit States in
the [REF:standard:nrcc-nbcug4]

Information on lateral vibrations and accelerations under dynamic
wind loads can be found in the Commentary entitled Wind Load and Effects
in the [REF:standard:nrcc-nbcug4]

application_notes.title:
Permanent Partitions Fixed to the
Structure

paragraphs.content:
Partitions in residential buildings, including
condominiums, apartments and hotels, are typically permanent and fixed
to the structure. In such cases, the weight of partitions referred
to in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect4.art1.sent1.clause3:long] is the actual weight of the partitions
that are shown on the drawings.

application_notes.title: Partitions Not Shown on the Drawings

paragraphs.content:
The potential locations of partitions in work areas, such as
offices, are not typically shown on the drawings. For such areas,
a partition weight allowance must be considered based on the anticipated
weight and location of partitions, but not less than 1 kPa (metric) over the area of floor being considered.

application_notes.title:
Counteracting Dead Load Due to
Soil

paragraphs.content:
Examples of structures that traditionally employ
the dead load of soil to resist loadings are pylon signs, tower structures,
retaining walls, and deadmen, which resist wind uplift and overturning
in light structures.

application_notes.title:
Loads Due to Use of Floors and
Roofs

paragraphs.content:
In many areas of buildings, such as equipment areas,
service rooms, factories, storage areas, warehouses, museums, and
office filing areas, live loads due to their intended use may exceed
the minimum specified loads listed in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect5.art3.table1:long] In
these instances, the probable live load shall be calculated and used
as the specified live load for the design of that particular area.

The designer should give special consideration to the effects
of vibration.

Attic live loading is not required when the ceiling below the
attic consists of removable panels that permit access to the ceiling
space without loading the ceiling supporting members. Attic live loading
is not required in any area of the attic where the least dimension
of the attic space is less than 500 mm (metric).

divisions.title: Corridors, Aisles and Rows of Seats

paragraphs.content:
The spaces between rows of seats are typically designed for
the loads of the occupancy they serve. Rows of seats typically discharge
into aisles that are designed for the loads used for the rows of seats.
 Corridors have a minimum width of 1 100 mm (metric) and may serve
as collectors for aisles; they are therefore part of the exit system
and are required to be designed for a minimum live load of 4.8
kPa (metric).

divisions.title: Floor Areas That Could Be Used As Viewing Areas

paragraphs.content:
Some interior balconies, mezzanines, corridors, lobbies and
aisles that are not intended to be used by an assembly of people as
viewing areas are sometimes used as such; consequently, they are subject
to loadings much higher than those for the occupancies they serve.
Floor areas that may be subject to such higher loads must, therefore,
be designed for a loading of 4.8 kPa (metric).

For the purposes of applying the requirements of [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect5.art3.table1:long], lecture halls with fixed seats are similar to
theatres in configuration (the seats may have a writing tablet affixed
to one arm). Classrooms are typically furnished with full-sized desks
having separate or integrated seats.

[REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect5.art3:long]
                        [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect5.art10:long] stipulate a minimum uniform roof
live load of 1.0 kPa (metric) and a minimum concentrated live
load of 1.3 kN (metric). These live loads are “use and occupancy
loads” intended to provide for maintenance loadings: they are not
reduced as a function of area or as a function of the roof slope due
to their variability in distribution and location.

The general minimum specified load for office areas, including
mezzanines, is 2.4 kPa (metric).

A minimum specified load of 4.8 kPa (metric) applies to
office areas in basements, which are normally slab-on-grade, and to
office areas in floor areas that may be subject to an increase in
loading for brief periods, for example, when tenants temporarily use
that floor area to store furniture, equipment and files while moving
in or out of the building.

Where an office building is situated on a level site, all floors
are uniform in elevation, and there are no mezzanines, allocating
the correct loads is straightforward. However, where the site is steeply
sloped, the situation is more complex—even more so where there are
also mezzanines.

The principle is that floor levels and mezzanines with access
to the exterior at ground level could be used as staging areas during
a move, and so, must be designed for a minimum of 4.8 kPa (metric). Also, there is usually an area adjacent to the exterior exit that
can accommodate trucks.

A special study should be undertaken to determine the distributed
loads to be used for the design of floors and areas used by vehicles
exceeding 9 000 kg (metric) gross weight and of driveways and
sidewalks over areaways and basements. Where appropriate, the designer
should refer to [REF:standard:csas6]

In [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect5.art5:long], “accessible” refers to the lack of
a physical barrier that prevents or restricts access by vehicles or
persons to the site in the context of the specific use.

Information on the design of roof parking decks and exterior areas
that are accessible to vehicular traffic can be found in the Commentary
entitled Live Loads in the [REF:standard:nrcc-nbcug4]

Information
on tributary area can be found in the Commentary entitled Live Loads
in the [REF:standard:nrcc-nbcug4]

Special study is required to determine concentrated loads for
the design of floors and areas used by vehicles exceeding 9 000
kg (metric) gross weight, and of driveways and sidewalks over areaways
and basements. Where appropriate the designer should refer to [REF:standard:csas6]
Guidance on crane-supporting structures can be found in [REF:standard:csas16]

In the design of guards, due consideration should be given to
the durability of the members and their connections.

Information
on loads on firewalls can be found in the Commentary entitled Structural
Integrity of Firewalls in the [REF:standard:nrcc-nbcug4]

application_notes.title:
Specified Load Due to Rain or to
Snow and Associated Rain

paragraphs.content:
The location of a new building
or obstruction may affect the snow loads on the roof of an adjacent
existing building—on the same property or on an adjacent one—that
is lower in height. In such cases, designers should consider [REF:internal:nbc.divC.part2.sect2.subsect2.art1.sent1:long].

Additional guidance can be found in the Commentary entitled
Snow Loads in the [REF:standard:nrcc-nbcug4]

The [REF:standard:nrcc-npc] (NPC)

The designer must ensure that the building complies with both the

Elevator,
air-conditioning and fan housings, small penthouses and wide chimneys

application_notes.title:
Roof-Mounted Solar Panels on Buildings
of Any Height

paragraphs.content:
[REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect7.art13:long] provides procedures
for calculating the wind loads on roof-mounted arrays of solar panels
that satisfy particular geometrical requirements.

The area of the roof that is covered by a solar array does not
need to be designed for the simultaneous application of the solar
array wind loads and the roof wind loads. However, the cumulative
load effect of all solar panels does need to be accounted for in accordance
with [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect7.art11:long] Furthermore, the roof needs to be
designed for the case where the solar array has been removed.

Solar arrays that are mechanically fastened to the underlying
roof structure can modify the load distribution on the roof. The loads
from such arrays must be applied to the structural components of the
roof as concentrated loads at the points of attachment.

The calculations in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect7.art13:long] assume that
the solar panels and their mounting system are rigid. Therefore, there
is no allowance for wind-induced vibration of these components. However,
if the panels and their mounting system have a natural frequency less
than about 10 Hz (metric), it is possible that loads will be magnified
as a result of wind-induced vibration. In such cases, it is recommended
that expert opinion be sought and that the dynamic effects be investigated
in more detail.

[REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect5.appnote63.figure1:long] shows an example of a roof-mounted
solar array with exposed and unexposed panels. For the purpose of
determining the edge factor, E, to be applied in the calculations
of [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect7.art13:long], a panel is defined as exposed if it
is located within a distance of 1.5 times the panel chord length,
L_{p}, from an exposed edge of the array. An exposed edge
of the array is considered to occur where the horizontal distance,
d_{1}, from the panel edge to the roof edge (ignoring any
rooftop equipment) is greater than 0.5h, h being the reference height
of the roof, and greater than max(4h2,1.2 m) (metric), h_{2} being the height of the panel's highest point
above the roof surface. An exposed edge is also considered to occur
where the horizontal distance, d_{2}, from the panel edge
to the nearest edge in the next panel row (or across a gap in the
same panel row) is greater than max(4h2,1.2 m) (metric).

A sample calculation of net design wind pressure for roof-mounted
solar panels is provided in the Commentary entitled Wind Load and
Effects in the [REF:standard:nrcc-nbcug4]

The installation of solar arrays on a roof can significantly
affect the distribution of snow loads on the roof. Designers should
be aware that the accumulation of snow and ice around solar panels
can influence the calculations described in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect7.art13:long] For example, accumulated snow may obstruct the ventilation areas
between the roof and the underside of the panels, thereby increasing
wind loads on the panels. For the design of the anchorage of a solar
array to the roof and of the array itself, the pressure equalization
factor, γ_{a}, in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect7.art13.sent2:long] should be taken
as 1.0, unless it can be shown that the accumulation of snow and ice
will not obstruct the gaps between the panels in the array.

more susceptible to amplified displacements due to gravity-induced

Structural systems that include
components such as inclined columns or horizontal floor cantilevers
can induce lateral force demands on the SFRS under gravity loads.
Buildings with such gravity-induced lateral demands on the SFRS are
more likely to experience severe damage during strong ground shaking
due to their tendency to drift only in one direction, leading to large
residual displacements or instability. To determine if a building
is susceptible to amplification of displacements due to gravity-induced
lateral demands, the lateral resistance of the yielding mechanism
to resist earthquake forces alone, Q_{y}, must be compared
with the gravity-induced lateral demand, Q_{G}, at the same
location. The force component selected for this comparison depends
on the yielding mechanism for the SFRS. For example, for a coupled
wall, the overturning moment resistance at the level of the expected
plastic hinges should be compared with the overturning moment demand
(at the same level) due to gravity loads alone, whereas for a steel-braced
frame, the storey shear at the critical level of the yielding system
should be compared with the storey shear demand (at the same level)
due to the gravity loads alone. If the gravity-induced lateral demands
exceed the limits prescribed in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect8.art10.sent9:long], amplifications
in seismic displacements due to gravity-induced lateral demands can
only be identified through non-linear dynamic analyses using models
that adequately represent the hysteretic behaviour of the SFRS. Further
information on the impacts of gravity-induced lateral demands on the
seismic response of buildings can be found in the Commentary entitled
Design for Seismic Effects in the [REF:standard:nrcc-nbcug4]

application_notes.title:
Gravity-Induced Lateral Demand
– Non-linear Dynamic Analysis

paragraphs.content:

Dynamic Analysis, including

for Seismic Effects in the [REF:standard:nrcc-nbcug4]

The presence of inclined vertical members in a building leads
to a coupling of its horizontal and vertical vibrational modes. As
a result of this coupling, horizontal accelerations of the building
cause vertical accelerations of the mass supported by the inclined
vertical members. Vertical ground motions cause additional vertical
accelerations of the mass.

The additional earthquake forces resulting from both the coupling
of horizontal and vertical vibrational modes and the vertical ground
motions can be determined using the Dynamic Analysis Procedure described
in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect8.art12:long] with RdRo = 1.0 (metric). The structural model used in the analysis must account
for the vertical accelerations of all mass supported by inclined vertical
members and must include the SFRS, the inclined vertical members,
and all structural framing elements that transfer inertial forces
generated by the vertical accelerations of the mass supported by the
inclined vertical members.

The additional earthquake forces are sensitive to the degree
of coupling between the vertical and horizontal vibrational modes
of the building. Thus, to determine the maximum additional earthquake
forces for design, the range of possible stiffness values for all
structural members must be considered.

Further information on the analysis of structures with a sloped
column irregularity, including a simple procedure for scaling the
analysis results to avoid having to perform multiple analyses with
a range of stiffness values and vertical ground motions, can be found
in the Commentary entitled Design for Seismic Effects in the [REF:standard:nrcc-nbcug4]

application_notes.title:
Influence of Dynamic Diaphragm
In-Plane Response

paragraphs.content:
In lieu of carrying out a special study as stated in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect8.art15.sent4.clause1.subclause3:long], the anticipated total deformation demand on
the vertical elements of the SFRS, including inelastic deformations,
may be taken as equal to RoRd(ΔB + ΔD) − RoΔD
                         (metric), i.e., the
difference between the total storey drift including inelastic deformation
effects and diaphragm deformations, R_{o}R_{d}(Δ_{B} + Δ_{D}), and the diaphragm deformation under R_{o} times the seismic load, where R_{o} may be replaced
by the actual overstrength of the SFRS vertical elements. The design
engineer must verify that the SFRS vertical elements have sufficient
deformation capacity to accommodate the computed deformation demand.
If the vertical elements of the SFRS do not have sufficient deformation
capacity, the design forces for the vertical elements of the SFRS
must be magnified by Rd(1 + ΔD/ΔB)/(Rd + ΔD/ΔB
                         (metric)). The calculation
of the magnified design forces is iterative as the Δ_{D}/Δ_{B} ratio may change when using higher design forces for the
vertical elements of the SFRS. Reducing the Δ_{D}/Δ_{B} ratio by increasing the stiffness of the roof diaphragm relative
to that of the vertical elements of the SFRS may be considered to
reduce the deformation demand on the vertical elements of the SFRS.
Additional information can be found in the Commentary entitled Design
for Seismic Effects in the [REF:standard:nrcc-nbcug4]

The dynamic response of the diaphragm with the vertical elements
of the SFRS under seismic excitation involves several modes of vibration
that affect both the amplitude and distribution of in-plane shears
and bending moments in the roof diaphragm. The shape of the fundamental
mode of vibration resembles the deflected shape of the diaphragm/vertical
SFRS elements under a distributed lateral load while higher modes
involve increasing numbers of zero crossings of the deflected shapes
along the length of the diaphragm, similar to the modes of a simply
supported beam with distributed mass. Shears and bending moments therefore
deviate from the values obtained from the equivalent static force
procedure essentially due to higher mode response. Modal contributions
to shears and bending moments in the diaphragms can be obtained from
a Linear Dynamic Analysis. The contribution from the higher modes
is generally more pronounced when the Δ_{D}/Δ_{B} ratio,
the period in the first mode, or the ratio S(0.2)/S(2.0) is increased. It also increases when the SFRS is designed with
a higher R_{d} factor as inelastic deformations of the vertical
elements of the SFRS attenuate the first mode response. Methods to
take into account the inelastic higher mode effects on in-plane diaphragm
shears and moments are discussed in the Commentary entitled Design
for Seismic Effects in the [REF:standard:nrcc-nbcug4]

The bearing stress distribution in soil or rock that is used to determine
the factored overturning resistance of the foundation influences the
rotation of the foundation, which occurs due to the forces applied
by the SFRS. Generally, all foundations will rotate on soil or rock.
In particular, footings (a type of foundation unit) often undergo
uplift at one end, and if the factored bearing stress at the other
end is only over a short length, then the uplift and rotation of the
footing can be significant. [REF:standard:csaa23.3] contains design requirements for footings that rotate and uplift;
see also the Commentary entitled Design for Seismic Effects in the [REF:standard:nrcc-nbcug4] for guidance and
methods to account for foundation movement.

application_notes.title:
Actual Lateral Load Capacity of
the SFRS

paragraphs.content:
The actual lateral load capacity of the SFRS
includes the effects of member overstrengths similar to those used
to determine the R_{o} factors. The applicable CSA design
standards include requirements on calculating the overstrengths and
capacities, which may be based on the members' nominal or probable
resistance. The actual capacities are larger than the factored loads
and factored resistances and, in many cases, can be significantly
larger. Note that the foundations designed to develop the capacity
of the SFRS will undergo movements and [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect8.art16.sent1:long] still
applies.

For the special case where the foundation
is a footing, and where it and the attached SFRS are not constrained
against rotation, it is  permitted, with certain limitations, to size
the footing to have a factored overturning resistance less than the
overturning capacity of the supported SFRS. This approach results
in a smaller footing, increased footing rotations, increased drifts
in the structure, and increased soil stresses, all of which are over
and above those associated with footings sized to have a factored
overturning resistance equal to or greater than the overturning capacity
of the SFRS. The footing itself must have a factored resistance capable
of developing the required soil or rock reactions. An example of a
footing and SFRS that are not constrained against rotation is an SFRS
on a footing near the ground surface such that it can rotate freely
and is attached to a gravity-load-resisting system (non-SFRS) that
is laterally flexible and provides little lateral resistance. For
this case, the SFRS is usually analyzed on its own and the resulting
displacements are imposed on the non-SFRS elements in order to assess
the effects on them. Cases where the footing and SFRS are attached
to a system that has significant lateral stiffness require careful
analysis and engineering judgement, or the footing can be capacity-designed.

Limiting the overturning moment on the foundation and the R_{d}R_{o} value provides some control on the increase
in lateral displacement, drift and stress in the soil or rock. Cases
that exceed these limits require special study.

For the common case where the SFRS and/or the footing are constrained
in some way against rotation, the footing's factored resistance
must be equal to or greater than the capacity of the supported SFRS.
An example of an SFRS constrained against freely rotating with the
footing is an SFRS attached to adjacent foundation walls by below-grade
diaphragms. Examples of footings constrained against free rotation
are footings that use soil anchors to resist overturning, footings
on piles, and raft foundations. Note that [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect8.art16.sent1:long] still applies.
