paragraphs.content:
Information on the requirements
of [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect8.art18:long] can be found in the Commentary entitled
Design for Seismic Effects in the [REF:standard:nrcc-nbcug4]

The failure or detachment of non-structural
components and equipment during an earthquake can present a major
threat to life safety. The design requirements presented in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect8.art18:long] are intended to ensure that such components and
their connections to the building will retain their integrity during
strong ground shaking. Guidelines for the seismic risk reduction of
such components are given in [REF:standard:csas832]

Information on the cyclic tension load testing of anchors referred
to in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect8.art18.sent7.clause5:long] can be found in International Code
Council Evaluation Service (ICC-ES) Evaluation Reports. Additional
information can be found in the Commentary entitled Design for Seismic
Effects in the [REF:standard:nrcc-nbcug4]

Free-standing storage racks contain materials typically loaded
by forklift. Some are designed to store loaded pallets; however, in some cases, the
stored material does not sit on a pallet. Information on storage racks can be found
in the Commentary entitled Design for Seismic Effects in the [REF:standard:nrcc-nbcug4]

Information on glass fallout and testing for glass fallout can
be found in [REF:standard:aama501.6] Every surface
other than inaccessible areas or areas where occupancy is prevented
or access is prevented should be considered a “walking surface.” Additional
information can be found in [REF:standard:asce7] in [REF:standard:femap750] and [REF:standard:fema450-1] and related commentaries, and in
the Commentary entitled Design for Seismic Effects in the [REF:standard:nrcc-nbcug4]

application_notes.title:
Elements of Structures, Non-structural
Components and Equipment in Structures with Supplemental Energy Dissipation

paragraphs.content:
Information on the requirements of [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect8.art18.sent16:long] can be found in the Commentary entitled Design for Seismic Effects
in the [REF:standard:nrcc-nbcug4]

Climatic conditions leading to wetness or frost at the interface
between the supporting base of the array and the roof surface may
adversely affect the resistance provided by friction due to gravity
loads.

It
is strongly recommended that a design review of the seismically isolated
structure and its isolation system be carried out by an independent
team of professional engineers and geoscientists experienced in seismic
analysis methods and the theory and application of seismic isolation.
The design review should include, but not be limited to, the following:
                        site-specific spectra,
                        ground motion time histories, 
                        modeling and analyses,
                        testing program and results, and 
                        final design of all structural framing elements and isolation
system components.

Three-dimensional Non-linear Dynamic Analysis is a complex process
requiring special expertise. Guidance on Non-linear Dynamic Analysis
can be found in the Commentary entitled Design for Seismic Effects
in the [REF:standard:nrcc-nbcug4]

Ground motion time histories and their
horizontal and vertical components must be appropriately selected
and scaled according to accepted practice. Further information on
ground motion time histories can be found in the Commentary entitled
Design for Seismic Effects in the [REF:standard:nrcc-nbcug4]

It
is strongly recommended that a design review of the structure and
the supplementary energy dissipation system be carried out by an independent
team of professional engineers and geoscientists experienced in seismic
analysis methods and the theory and application of supplementary energy
dissipation. The design review should include, but not be limited
to, the following:
                        ground motion time histories,
                        modeling and analyses,
                        testing program and results, and
                        final design of all structural framing elements and supplemental
energy dissipation system components.

Three-dimensional Non-linear Dynamic Analysis is a complex process
requiring special expertise. Guidance on Non-linear Dynamic Analysis
can be found in the Commentary entitled Design for Seismic Effects
in the [REF:standard:nrcc-nbcug4]

Where acceptable information on subsurface conditions already
exists, the investigation may not require further physical subsurface
exploration or testing.

application_notes.title:
Responsibilities of the Designer
as Defined in Part 4

paragraphs.content:
In certain situations, such as when
the design is highly technical, it may be necessary for the “other
suitably qualified person” to be someone responsible to the designer.
In such cases the authority having jurisdiction may wish to order
that the review be done by the designer.

It is important that innovative approaches to foundation design be
carried out by a person especially qualified in the specific method
applied and that the design provide a level of safety and performance
at least equivalent to that provided for or implicit in the design
carried out by the methods referred to in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4:long]. Provision must be made for monitoring the subsequent performance
of such structures so that the long-term sufficiency of the design
can be evaluated.

Information on ultimate limit states for foundations, including
terminology and resistance factors, can be found in the Commentary
entitled Foundations in the [REF:standard:nrcc-nbcug4]

application_notes.title:
Design of Foundations for Differential
Movements

paragraphs.content:
Information on the design of foundations for
differential movements can be found in the Commentary entitled Foundations
in the [REF:standard:nrcc-nbcug4]

When adfreezing has occurred and subsequent freezing results in soil
expansion beneath this area, the resulting uplift effect is sometimes
referred to as frost jacking.

A heated building that is insulated to prevent heat loss through
the foundation walls should be considered as an unheated structure
unless the effect of the insulation is taken into account in determining
the maximum depth of frost penetration.

Information
on excavations can be found in the Commentary entitled Foundations
in the [REF:standard:nrcc-nbcug4]

Information on shallow foundations can be found in the Commentary
entitled Foundations in the [REF:standard:nrcc-nbcug4]

Information
on deep foundations can be found in the Commentary entitled Foundations
in the [REF:standard:nrcc-nbcug4]

that have been extensively used.

members to conform to [REF:standard:csaa23.4]

Qualification for fabricators and erectors of welded construction

application_notes.title:
Design Basis for Storage Garages and Repair
Garages

paragraphs.content:
Although the scope of [REF:standard:csas413] is limited to structural steel and reinforced concrete
(including prestressed and post-tensioned), the intent of [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect4.subsect2.art1.sent1:long] is to require any type of material used in the
construction of storage garages and repair garages to conform to the
performance level outlined in the standard.
See the Commentary entitled Live Loads in the [REF:standard:nrcc-nbcug4]

content.text: This Part is concerned with

clauses.text: the control of condensation

subclauses.text:
in [REF:term:bldng]building components and assemblies,
and

on [REF:term:bldng]building materials, components
and assemblies, and

clauses.text: the transfer of heat, air, moisture and sound through

subclauses.text:
[REF:term:bldng]building materials, components and
assemblies, and

interfaces between [REF:term:bldng]building materials,
components and assemblies.

articles.title:
Exposure to Exterior Space or the Ground and Separation of
Dissimilar Environments

content.text: This Part applies, as described in [REF:internal:nbc.divA.part1.sect3.subsect3:long], to

clauses.text:
[REF:term:bldng]building materials, components and
assemblies exposed to exterior space or the ground, including those
separating interior space from exterior space or separating interior
space from the ground,

[REF:term:bldng]building materials, components and
assemblies separating environmentally dissimilar interior spaces (see [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part5.sect11.appnote37:long]), and

site materials, components, assemblies and grading that may
affect environmental loads on [REF:term:bldng]building materials,
components and assemblies exposed to exterior space or the ground.

content.text: Words that appear in italics are defined in [REF:internal:nbc.divA.part1.sect4.subsect1.art2:long].

[REF:term:bldng]Building materials, components and
assemblies that separate dissimilar environments or are exposed to
the exterior shall have sufficient capacity and integrity to resist
or accommodate

clauses.text:
all environmental loads, and effects of those loads, that may
reasonably be expected having regard to

subclauses.text:
the intended use of the [REF:term:bldng]building,
and

the environment to which the materials, components and assemblies
are subject, and

clauses.text:
all structural loads, and effects of those loads, that may reasonably
be expected.

content.text:
Where [REF:term:bldng]building materials, components
or assemblies perform more than one function, they shall satisfy the
requirements of all of those functions. (See [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part5.sect11.appnote5:short].)

Compliance with [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part5.sect1.subsect4.art1.sent1.clause1:medium] shall
be demonstrated by design complying with [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part5.sect2.subsect1:long] and construction conforming to that design.

Compliance with [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part5.sect1.subsect4.art1.sent1.clause2:medium] shall
be demonstrated by design complying with [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part5.sect2.subsect2:long], and construction conforming to that design, with regard to

clauses.text:
materials, components and assemblies, and associated loads,
that are identified in Part 4,

air pressure loads imposed on [REF:term:r-brrr]air barrier
systems,
wind up-lift imposed on roofing, and

hydrostatic pressure imposed on the means of protection from
moisture in the ground.

content.text: For materials, components, assemblies and loads to which [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part5.sect1.subsect4.art1.sent4:short] does not apply, compliance with [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part5.sect1.subsect4.art1.sent1.clause2:medium] shall be demonstrated

clauses.text:
by design complying with [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part5.sect2.subsect2:long] for
individual applicable loads and construction conforming to that design,
or

in the case of common materials, components and assemblies,
and their installation, by proven past performance over a period of
several years for individual applicable loads.

content.text:
Materials, components and assemblies separating dissimilar environments
and assemblies exposed to the exterior, including their connections,
that are subject to structural loads as defined in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part5.sect2.subsect2.art1:long] shall

clauses.text:
transfer such loads to the [REF:term:bldng]building structure without adverse effects on the performance of other materials,
components or assemblies,

not deflect to a degree that adversely affects the performance
of other materials, components or assemblies (see [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part5.sect11.appnote7:short]), and

be designed, and constructed according to that design, to accommodate
(see [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part5.sect11.appnote7:short])

subclauses.text:
the maximum relative structural movement that may reasonably
be expected, and
construction tolerances that may be reasonably expected.

see_also.content:
(See [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect3.art5:long], [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect3.art3.sent2:long] and [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect8:long] for information on different
types of structural movements.) (See [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part5.sect11.appnote4:long])

content.text:
Except as provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part5.sect1.subsect4.art2.sent2:short], materials used in [REF:term:bldng]building components
and assemblies that separate dissimilar environments, or in assemblies
exposed to the exterior, shall be

clauses.text: compatible with adjoining materials, and

resistant to any mechanisms of deterioration that may reasonably
be expected, given

subclauses.text: the nature and function of the materials, and

the exposure and climatic conditions  in which they will be
installed.

content.text:
Material compatibility and deterioration resistance are not
required where it can be shown that incompatibility or uncontrolled
deterioration will not adversely affect any of

clauses.text: the health or safety of [REF:term:bldng]building users,

the intended use of the [REF:term:bldng]building,
or
the operation of [REF:term:bldng]building services.

articles.title: Requirements in Other Parts of the Code

content.text:
Structural and fire safety requirements in other Parts of the
British Columbia Building Code shall apply.
Above ground climatic loads shall be determined according to [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part1.sect1.subsect3:long]

Except as provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part5.sect2.subsect1.art1.sent3:short], below ground exterior environmental loads not described in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part1.sect1.subsect3:long] shall be determined from existing geological
and hydrological data or from site tests.

Where local design and construction practice has shown [REF:term:l]soil temperature analysis to be unnecessary, [REF:term:l]soil temperatures need not be determined. (See [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part5.sect11.appnote9:short].)

Interior environmental loads shall be determined in accordance
with good practice as described in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part6.sect2.subsect1.art1.sent1:long] based
on the intended use of the space. (See [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part5.sect11.appnote10:short].)

Calculations related to the transfer of heat, air and moisture
and the transmission of sound shall conform to good practice such
as that described in the ASHRAE Handbooks.

For the purposes of any analysis conducted to indicate conformance
to the thermal resistance levels required in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part5.sect3.subsect1.art2:long], [REF:term:l]soil temperatures shall be determined based
on annual average [REF:term:l]soil temperature, seasonal
amplitude of variation and attenuation of variation with depth.
Wind load calculations shall conform to [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect7:long]

articles.title: Determination of Structural Loads and Effects

content.text:
Where materials, components or assemblies that separate dissimilar
environments or are exposed to the exterior, or their connections,
are required to be designed to withstand structural loads, these loads
shall be determined in accordance with Part 4. (See also [REF:internal:nbc.divC.part2.sect2.subsect5:long].)

Except as provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect8.art18:short], the structural loads referred to in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part5.sect2.subsect2.art1.sent1:short] and their related effects shall include

clauses.text:
[REF:term:dd-ld]dead loads transferred from structural
elements,
wind, snow, rain, hydrostatic and earth pressures,

earthquake effects for [REF:term:pt-dtr-b]post-disaster
buildings, depending on their intended function (see [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part5.sect11.appnote11:short]),
[REF:term:lv-ld]live loads due to use and [REF:term:ccpnc]occupancy, and

loads due to thermal or moisture-related expansion and contraction,
deflection, deformation, creep, shrinkage, settlement, and differential
movement.

content.text:
Where materials, components or assemblies that separate dissimilar
environments or are exposed to the exterior, or their connections,
can be expected to be subject to loads or other effects not described
in this Subsection or in Part 4, such loads or effects shall be taken
into account in the design based on the most current and applicable
information available.

This Article applies to the determination of wind load to be
used in the design of materials, components and assemblies, including
their connections, that separate dissimilar environments or are exposed
to the exterior, where these are

clauses.text: subject to wind load, and
required to be designed to resist wind load.

content.text:
Except as provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part5.sect2.subsect2.art2.sent3:short], the wind load referred to in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part5.sect2.subsect2.art2.sent1:short] shall be 100% of the specified wind load determined in accordance
with [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect7.art1:long]

Where it can be shown by test or analysis that a material, component,
assembly or connection referred to in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part5.sect2.subsect2.art2.sent1:short] will be subject to less than 100% of the specified
wind load, the wind load referred to in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part5.sect2.subsect2.art2.sent1:short] shall be not less than the load determined by test
or analysis.

Except as provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part5.sect2.subsect2.art2.sent5:short], the wind uplift resistance of membrane roofing assemblies shall
be determined in accordance with the requirements of [REF:standard:csaa123.21] (See [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part5.sect11.appnote13:short].)

Membrane roofing assemblies with proven past performance for
the anticipated wind loads need not comply with [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part5.sect2.subsect2.art2.sent4:short]. (See [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part5.sect11.appnote6:short].)
Structural design shall be carried out in accordance with [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect3:long] and other applicable requirements in Part 4.

Except as provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part5.sect3.subsect1.art1.sent2:short], where a [REF:term:bldng]building component or assembly
will be subjected to an intended temperature differential, the component
or assembly shall include materials to resist heat transfer or a means
to dissipate transferred heat in accordance with the remainder of
this Subsection.

The installation of materials to resist heat transfer in accordance
with the remainder of this Subsection is not required where it can
be shown that uncontrolled heat transfer will not adversely affect
any of

clauses.text: the health or safety of [REF:term:bldng]building users,

the intended use of the [REF:term:bldng]building,
or
the operation of [REF:term:bldng]building services.

articles.title: Properties to Resist Heat Transfer or Dissipate Heat

content.text:
Taking into account the conditions on either side of the environmental
separator, materials and components installed to provide the required
resistance to heat transfer or the means implemented to dissipate
heat shall provide sufficient resistance or dissipation,

clauses.text:
to minimize surface condensation on the warm side of the component
or assembly,

in conjunction with other materials and components in the assembly,
to minimize condensation within the component or assembly,

in conjunction with systems installed for space conditioning,
to meet the interior design thermal conditions for the intended [REF:term:ccpnc]occupancy, and
to minimize ice damming on sloped roofs.

articles.title: Location and Installation of Materials Providing Thermal Resistance

content.text:
Where a material required by [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part5.sect3.subsect1.art1:long] is
intersected by a [REF:term:bldng]building assembly, penetrated
by a high conductance component or interrupted by expansion, control
or construction joints, and where condensation is likely to occur
at these intersections, penetrations or interruptions, sufficient
thermal resistance shall be provided so as to minimize condensation
at these locations.

Materials providing required thermal resistance shall have sufficient
inherent resistance to airflow or be positioned in the assembly so
as to prevent convective airflow through and around the material.
(See [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part5.sect11.appnote18:short].)

Where a [REF:term:bldng]building component or assembly
separates interior [REF:term:cnd-sp]conditioned space from
exterior space, interior space from the ground, or environmentally
dissimilar interior spaces, the properties and position of the materials
and components in those components or assemblies shall be such that
they control air leakage or permit venting to the exterior so as to

clauses.text: provide acceptable conditions for the [REF:term:bldng]building occupants,
maintain appropriate conditions for the intended use of the [REF:term:bldng]building,

minimize the accumulation of condensation in and the penetration
of precipitation into the [REF:term:bldng]building component
or assembly,
control heat transfer to roofs where ice damming can occur,

minimize the ingress of airborne radon and other [REF:term:l]soil gases from the ground with an aim to controlling the indoor concentrations
of these gases to an acceptable level, and
not compromise the operation of [REF:term:bldng]building services.

content.text:
Except as provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part5.sect4.subsect1.art1.sent7:short], an [REF:term:r-brrr]air barrier system shall be designed and constructed to provide
the principal resistance to air leakage to meet the requirements of [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part5.sect4.subsect1.art1.sent1:short].

The [REF:term:r-brrr] air barrier system  shall incorporate
air barrier assemblies that meet the appropriate Performance Class
as defined in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part5.sect4.subsect1.art1.table1:long] (See [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part5.sect11.appnote21:short].)

content.title: Maximum Air Leakage Rates for Air Barrier Assemblies

header_rows.content: Maximum Air Leakage Rate, L/(s×m^{2}), at a Pressure Differential of 75 Pa (metric)

content.text:
The [REF:term:r-brrr]air barrier system shall be
designed and constructed to be continuous

clauses.text: across construction, control and expansion joints,
across junctions between different air barrier assemblies, and
around penetrations through air barrier assemblies.

content.text:
The structural design of air barrier assemblies, including junctions
between air barrier assemblies, subject to air pressure loads shall
comply with [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part5.sect1.subsect4.art1:long] and [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part5.sect2.subsect2:long]

The maximum air leakage rates specified in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part5.sect4.subsect1.art1.table1:long] are permitted to be increased where it can be shown
that the higher rate will not adversely affect any of

clauses.text: the health or safety of the [REF:term:bldng]building users,

the intended use of the [REF:term:bldng]building,
or
the operation of [REF:term:bldng]building services.

content.text:
An [REF:term:r-brrr]air barrier system is not required
where it can be shown that uncontrolled air leakage will not adversely
affect any of

clauses.text: the health or safety of [REF:term:bldng]building users,

the intended use of the [REF:term:bldng]building,
or
the operation of [REF:term:bldng]building services.

content.text:
Except as provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part5.sect4.subsect1.art2.sent2:short]
                           [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part5.sect4.subsect1.art2.sent3:short], air barrier assemblies not in contact with the ground shall

clauses.text: conform with [REF:standard:ulcs742] and
meet the selected Performance Class of [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part5.sect4.subsect1.art1.table1:long]

content.text:
Air barrier assemblies not evaluated in accordance with [REF:standard:ulcs742] shall be designed
and constructed

clauses.text: to meet or exceed the selected Performance Class of [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part5.sect4.subsect1.art1.table1:long], and

with at least one air barrier material intended to provide the
primary resistance to air leakage that meets the requirements of [REF:standard:ulcs741]

content.text:
Air barrier assemblies covered in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part5.sect10.subsect2:long]
                           [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part5.sect10.subsect3:long]
                           [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part5.sect10.subsect4:long] shall meet the air
barrier performance criteria defined in those Subsections.

Below-[REF:term:grade]grade air barrier assemblies in contact with
the ground shall minimize the ingress of airborne radon and other [REF:term:l]soil gases. (See [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part5.sect11.appnote26:short].)

Where a [REF:term:bldng]building component or assembly
is subjected to differentials in temperature and water vapour pressure,
the properties and position of the materials and components in those
components or assemblies shall be such that they control vapour diffusion
or permit venting to the exterior so as to minimize the accumulation
of condensation in the [REF:term:bldng]building component
or assembly.

Except as provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part5.sect5.subsect1.art1.sent3:short], a [REF:term:vpr-brrr]vapour barrier shall be installed
to provide the principal resistance to water vapour diffusion.

A [REF:term:vpr-brrr]vapour barrier is not required
where it can be shown that uncontrolled vapour diffusion will not
adversely affect any of

clauses.text: the health or safety of [REF:term:bldng]building users,

the intended use of the [REF:term:bldng]building,
or
the operation of [REF:term:bldng]building services.

content.text:
The [REF:term:vpr-brrr]vapour barrier shall have
sufficiently low permeance and shall be positioned in the [REF:term:bldng]building component or assembly so as to

clauses.text:
minimize moisture transfer by diffusion, to surfaces within
the assembly that would be cold enough to cause condensation at the
design temperature and humidity conditions, or

reduce moisture transfer by diffusion, to surfaces within the
assembly that would be cold enough to cause condensation at the design
temperature and humidity conditions, to a rate that will not allow
sufficient accumulation of moisture to cause deterioration or otherwise
adversely affect any of

subclauses.text: the health or safety of [REF:term:bldng]building users,

the intended use of the [REF:term:bldng]building,
or
the operation of [REF:term:bldng]building services.

content.text:
Coatings applied to gypsum board to provide required resistance
to vapour diffusion shall conform to the requirements of [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part5.sect5.subsect1.art2.sent1:short] when tested in accordance with [REF:standard:cgsb-1.501]

Coatings applied to materials other than gypsum board to provide
required resistance to vapour diffusion shall conform to the requirements
of [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part5.sect5.subsect1.art2.sent1:short] when tested in accordance
with [REF:standard:astme96m] by the desiccant method (dry
cup).

Except as provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part5.sect6.subsect1.art1.sent2:short], where a [REF:term:bldng]building component or assembly
is exposed to precipitation, the component or assembly shall

clauses.text:
minimize ingress of precipitation into the component or assembly,
and
prevent ingress of precipitation into interior space.

content.text:
Protection from ingress of precipitation is not required where
it can be shown that such ingress will not adversely affect any of

clauses.text: the health or safety of [REF:term:bldng]building users,

the intended use of the [REF:term:bldng]building,
or
the operation of [REF:term:bldng]building services.

content.text:
Where protective materials are applied to assemblies to provide
the required protection from precipitation, they shall be installed
so as to shed precipitation or otherwise minimize its entry into the
assembly and prevent its penetration through the assembly. (See [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part5.sect11.appnote30:short].) (See also [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part5.sect3.subsect1.art2.sent1.clause4:long].)

Where protective materials applied to assemblies to provide
the required protection from precipitation are part of a vegetated
roofing system, they shall be resistant to root and rhizome penetration
when tested in accordance with [REF:standard:sprivr1] (See [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part5.sect11.appnote31:short].)

Except as provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part5.sect6.subsect2.art1.sent2:short], materials, components, assemblies, joints in materials, junctions
between components and junctions between assemblies exposed to precipitation
shall be

clauses.text: sealed to prevent ingress of precipitation, or
drained to direct precipitation to the exterior.

content.text:
Sealing or drainage are not required where it can be shown that
the omission of sealing and drainage will not adversely affect any
of

clauses.text: the health or safety of [REF:term:bldng]building users,

the intended use of the [REF:term:bldng]building,
or
the operation of [REF:term:bldng]building services.

content.text:
Where water, snow or ice can accumulate on a [REF:term:bldng]building, provision shall be made to minimize the likelihood
of hazardous conditions arising from such accumulation.

Where precipitation can accumulate on sloped or horizontal assemblies,
provision shall be made for drainage conforming with Article 2.4.10.4. of Division B of Book II (Plumbing Systems) of this Code.

Where downspouts are provided and are not connected to a sewer,
provisions shall be made to

clauses.text: divert the water from the [REF:term:bldng]building, and
prevent [REF:term:l]soil erosion.

content.text:
Junctions between vertical assemblies, and sloped or horizontal
assemblies, shall be designed and constructed to minimize the flow
of water from the sloped or horizontal assembly onto the vertical
assembly.

This Subsection applies to the location of [REF:term:bldng]buildings, the grading of [REF:term:bldng]building sites, the directing of water away from [REF:term:bldng]building assemblies, and the provision of means for drainage.

The [REF:term:bldng]building shall be located, the [REF:term:bldng]building site shall be graded, or water shall
be directed away from [REF:term:bldng]building assemblies
so as to prevent or accommodate the accumulation of surface water
against the [REF:term:bldng]building or adjacent [REF:term:bldng]buildings.

Drainage shall be provided to direct water away from assemblies
separating interior space from the ground, except

clauses.text:
where the assembly is designed in accordance with [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part5.sect7.subsect2:long] to withstand continuous hydrostatic pressure,
or

where it can be shown that the lack of drainage will not adversely
affect

subclauses.text: the health or safety of [REF:term:bldng]building users,

the intended use of the [REF:term:bldng]building,
or
the operation of [REF:term:bldng]building services.

content.text:
This Subsection applies to waterproofing materials, components,
assemblies and systems applied to [REF:term:bldng]building assemblies that separate dissimilar environments and are subjected
to hydrostatic pressure.

articles.title: Design of Building Elements Under Hydrostatic Loads

content.text:
Waterproofing materials, components, assemblies and systems
described in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part5.sect7.subsect2.art1:long] shall be designed in accordance
with [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part5.sect1.subsect4:long]
Hydrostatic design loads shall be determined in accordance with [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part5.sect2.subsect2:long]

Waterproofing materials, components, assemblies and systems
described in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part5.sect7.subsect2.art1:long] shall comply with [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part5.sect7.subsect3.art2:long]

This Subsection applies to the protection of [REF:term:bldng]building assemblies that separate interior space from the
ground.

Except as provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part5.sect7.subsect3.art2.sent2:short] and [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part5.sect7.subsect3.art4:long], [REF:term:bldng]building assemblies described in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part5.sect7.subsect3.art1:long] shall be protected
by waterproofing in accordance with [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part5.sect7.subsect3.art3:long] so
as to prevent the ingress of water into the [REF:term:bldng]building or the accumulation of water against the [REF:term:bldng]building.
Waterproofing is not required where it can be shown that

clauses.text:
a [REF:term:bldng]building is designed to accommodate
the ingress or accumulation of water, or
the ingress or accumulation of water will not negatively affect

subclauses.text: the health or safety of [REF:term:bldng]building users,

the intended use of the [REF:term:bldng]building,
or
the operation of [REF:term:bldng]building services.

content.text:
Waterproofing materials, components, assemblies, or systems
installed to provide the required protection shall form a continuous
and impervious barrier to the ingress of water and be capable of accommodating

clauses.text:
imperfections, construction joints, control joints and expansion
joints (see [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part5.sect11.appnote35:short]),
junctions between different [REF:term:bldng]building assemblies, and
elements penetrating [REF:term:bldng]building assemblies.

content.text:
Vertical [REF:term:bldng]building assemblies that
separate interior space from the ground are permitted to be dampproofed
where

clauses.text: such assemblies are not subjected to hydrostatic pressure,
the substrate is cast-in-place concrete, and
a drainage layer is installed between the [REF:term:bldng]building assembly and the [REF:term:l]soil.

content.text:
Joints, junctions and penetrations shall be designed and constructed
to maintain the continuity of the dampproofing.

Except as provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part5.sect9.subsect1.art1.sent2:short], a [REF:term:dwllng-n]dwelling unit shall be separated
from every other space in a [REF:term:bldng]building in
which noise may be generated by

clauses.text:
a separating assembly and adjoining constructions, which, together,
provide an [REF:term:astc]apparent sound transmission class (ASTC) rating not less than 47, or

a separating assembly that provides a [REF:term:stc]sound
transmission class (STC) rating of not less than 50 and adjoining
constructions that conform to [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect11.subsect1.art4:long]

content.text: Construction separating a [REF:term:dwllng-n]dwelling unit from an elevator shaft or a refuse chute shall have an [REF:term:stc]STC rating not less than 55.

The [REF:term:stc]STC ratings of separating assemblies
shall be determined in accordance with [REF:standard:astme413] using the results from measurements carried out in accordance with [REF:standard:astme90]

The [REF:term:astc]ASTC ratings of separating assemblies
and adjoining constructions shall be

clauses.text: determined in accordance with [REF:standard:astme413] using the results from measurements carried out in accordance with [REF:standard:astme336] or
calculated in accordance with

subclauses.text:
the detailed method described in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part5.sect9.subsect1.art4:long],
or
the simplified method described in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part5.sect9.subsect1.art5:long]

content.text:
Compliance with the required [REF:term:stc]STC ratings
shall be demonstrated through

clauses.text: measurements carried out in accordance with [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part5.sect9.subsect1.art2.sent1:long], or

the construction of separating assemblies conforming to those
presented in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.spectables1.table1:long]
                              [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.spectables1.table2:long], as applicable.

content.text:
Compliance with the required [REF:term:astc]ASTC ratings
shall be demonstrated through

clauses.text: measurements or calculations carried out in accordance with [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part5.sect9.subsect1.art2.sent2:long], or

the construction of separating assemblies conforming to those
presented in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.spectables1.table1:long]
                              [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.spectables1.table2:long], as applicable, that have an [REF:term:stc]STC rating of not less than 50 in conjunction with flanking
assemblies constructed in accordance with [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect11.subsect1.art4:long]

content.text:
The sound transmission loss measured in accordance with [REF:standard:astme90] shall be used in lieu of the sound reduction index
required in [REF:standard:iso15712-1]

The vibration reduction index for the junctions between separating
assemblies shall be

clauses.text:
determined using the equations presented in [REF:external:iso10848-1]Annex E of 
                              [REF:standard:iso15712-1] or

measured in accordance with [REF:external:iso10848-1]Parts
1 to 4 of 
                              [REF:standard:iso10848-1]

content.text:
The normalized flanking level difference shall be measured in
accordance with [REF:external:iso10848-1]Parts 1 to 4 of 
                           [REF:standard:iso10848-1]

The direct sound reduction index for the separating assembly
in situ shall be determined using [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part5.sect9.subsect1.art4.sent4.clause1:short]
                           [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part5.sect9.subsect1.art4.sent4.clause2:short], depending on the type of construction:

clauses.text:
for a separating wall or floor assembly that behaves like a
homogeneous panel, the index shall be determined in accordance with
the detailed method for structure-borne transmission presented in [REF:standard:iso15712-1] (see [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part5.sect11.appnote40:short]).

content.text:
The flanking sound reduction index for each flanking path at
each edge of the separating assembly shall be determined using [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part5.sect9.subsect1.art4.sent5.clause1:short]
                           [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part5.sect9.subsect1.art4.sent5.clause2:short]
                           [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part5.sect9.subsect1.art4.sent5.clause3:short], depending on the type of construction:

clauses.text:
for a separating wall or floor assembly with lightweight wood
or steel framing and connected flanking assemblies with lightweight
wood or steel framing, the index shall be taken as equal to the normalized
flanking level difference re-normalized for the [REF:term:astc]ASTC field situation in accordance with [REF:external:iso15712-1]Annex F of 
                              [REF:standard:iso15712-1]

for a separating wall or floor assembly that behaves like a
homogeneous panel and connected flanking assemblies that behave like
a homogeneous panel, the index shall be determined in accordance with
the detailed method for structure-borne transmission presented in [REF:standard:iso15712-1] (see [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part5.sect11.appnote40:long]),

for a mixture of assemblies with lightweight wood or steel framing
and assemblies that behave like a homogeneous panel, the index shall
be determined in accordance with [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part5.sect9.subsect1.art4.sent5.clause1:short]
                              [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part5.sect9.subsect1.art4.sent5.clause2:short] (see [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part5.sect11.appnote40:long]).

content.text:
Once the pertinent indices and measurements referred to in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part5.sect9.subsect1.art4.sent1:short]
                           [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part5.sect9.subsect1.art4.sent5:short] have been determined
based on the type of construction, the apparent sound reduction index
shall then be determined in accordance with [REF:standard:iso15712-1]

The [REF:term:astc]ASTC shall be calculated in accordance
with [REF:standard:astme413] using the apparent sound reduction
index determined in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part5.sect9.subsect1.art4.sent6:short], which
shall be treated as equivalent to the values of apparent sound transmission
loss measured in accordance with [REF:standard:astme336]

The [REF:term:stc]STC rating shall be used in lieu
of the weighted sound reduction index required in [REF:standard:iso15712-1]

The vibration reduction index for the junctions between separating
assemblies shall be

clauses.text: determined using the equations presented in Annex E of [REF:standard:iso15712-1] or
measured in accordance with Parts 1 to 4 of [REF:standard:iso10848-1]

content.text:
The weighted normalized flanking level difference shall be determined
in accordance with [REF:standard:astme413] using the results
from measurements carried out in accordance with Parts 1 to 4 of [REF:standard:iso10848-1]

The direct weighted sound reduction index for the separating
assembly shall be taken as equal to the [REF:term:stc]STC, without correction.

The weighted flanking sound reduction index for each flanking
path at each edge of the separating assembly shall be determined using [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part5.sect9.subsect1.art5.sent5.clause1:short]
                           [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part5.sect9.subsect1.art5.sent5.clause2:short], depending on the type of construction:

clauses.text:
for a separating wall or floor assembly with lightweight wood
or steel framing and connected flanking assemblies with lightweight
wood or steel framing, the index shall be taken as equal to the weighted
normalized flanking level difference re-normalized for the [REF:term:astc]ASTC field situation in accordance with Annex
F of [REF:standard:iso15712-1];

for a separating wall or floor assembly that behaves like a
homogeneous panel and connected flanking assemblies that behave like
a homogeneous panel, the index shall be determined in accordance with
the simplified method for structure-borne transmission presented in [REF:standard:iso15712-1] (see [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part5.sect11.appnote40:long]).

content.text:
Once the pertinent indices and measurements referred to in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part5.sect9.subsect1.art5.sent1:short]
                           [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part5.sect9.subsect1.art5.sent5:short] have been determined
based on the type of construction, the [REF:term:astc]ASTC shall then be calculated in accordance with [REF:standard:iso15712-1]

Except as provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part5.sect10.subsect1.art1.sent2:short] and elsewhere in this Part, materials and components, and their
installation, shall conform to the requirements of the applicable
standards in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part5.sect10.subsect1.art1.table1:long] where those materials or
components are

clauses.text:
incorporated into environmental separators or assemblies exposed
to the exterior, and
installed to fulfill the requirements of this Part.

content.text:
The requirements for [REF:term:flm-prd-]flame-spread ratings contained in thermal insulation standards shall be applied only
as required in Part 3.

Exposed to the Exterior

rating of gypsum board shall be determined in accordance with [REF:standard:ulcs102] in lieu of ASTM E84 as indicated
in [REF:standard:astmc1396m].

[REF:standard:astmc1658m]

5, [REF:standard:astmd3019] shall
only apply to the non-fibered and non-asbestos-fibered types of asphalt
roll roofing.

content.text:
This Subsection applies to windows, doors and skylights, including
their components, that separate

clauses.text: interior space from exterior space, or
environmentally dissimilar interior spaces.

content.text:
For the purpose of this Subsection, the term “skylight” refers
to unit skylights, roof windows and tubular daylighting devices.

Windows, doors and skylights, including their components, that are required to have a [REF:term:fr-prtn-rtng]fire-protection rating need not conform to the requirements of this Subsection. (See [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part5.appnote43:short].)

Except as permitted in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part5.sect10.subsect2.art2.sent5:short] and [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part5.sect10.subsect2.art3.sent1:long], windows, doors, skylights, including their components, shall conform to the requirements
in

clauses.text: [REF:standard:csa101a440] (Harmonized Standard), and
except as permitted in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part5.sect10.subsect2.art2.sent4:short], [REF:standard:csaa440S1]

content.text:
Performance grades for windows, doors and skylights shall be
selected according to the Canadian Supplement referenced in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part5.sect10.subsect2.art2.sent1.clause2:medium] so as to be appropriate for the
conditions and geographic location in which the window, door or skylight
will be installed.

Windows, doors and skylights shall conform to the performance
grades selected in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part5.sect10.subsect2.art2.sent2:short] when tested
in accordance with the Harmonized Standard referenced in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part5.sect10.subsect2.art2.sent1.clause1:medium].

For the purposes of conformance with [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part5.sect10.subsect2.art2.sent1.clause2:medium], loads and procedures from [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part5.sect2:long] may be used instead of the loads and procedures set out in the standard. (See Note 5.9.2.2.(4).)
A door designated as a "Limited Water" door in accordance with the standard referenced in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part5.sect10.subsect2.art2.sent1.clause1:medium] shall not be used unless the door

clauses.text: separates a [REF:term:dwllng-nt]dwelling unit from an unconditioned [REF:term:trg-grg]storage garage or a carport,

is designed with a clear width, a clear and level space, a door-opening device and a door closer in conformance with [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect8.subsect3:long] (see [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect8.subsect3.art6:long].), or
meets the criteria in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part9.sect27.subsect3.art8.sent3:short] such that flashing would not be required.

articles.title: Structural and Environmental Loads, Air Leakage and Water Penetration

content.text: Windows, doors, skylights and their components that do not conform to [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part5.sect10.subsect2.art2:long] shall be designed and constructed in accordance with [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part5.sect1.subsect4.art1:long], [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part5.sect4:long] and [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part5.sect6:long] (See [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part5.appnote44:short].)

Windows, doors and skylights shall meet the heat transfer performance
requirements stated in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part5.sect3:long] (See [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part5.sect11.appnote16:long])

Except as provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part5.sect10.subsect2.art4.sent3:short], all metal-framed glazed assemblies separating interior [REF:term:cnd-sp]conditioned space from interior unconditioned
space or exterior space shall incorporate a thermal break to minimize
condensation.
Metal-framed glazed assemblies need not comply with [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part5.sect10.subsect2.art4.sent2:short] where these assemblies are

clauses.text: storm windows or doors, or
windows or doors that are required to have a [REF:term:fr-prtct]fire-protection rating.

content.text:
For the purpose of this Subsection, the term “other fenestration
assemblies” refers to curtain walls, window walls, storefronts and
glazed architectural structures. (See [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part5.sect11.appnote48:short].)

Other fenestration assemblies and their components that are required to have a [REF:term:fr-prtn-rtng]fire-protection rating need not conform to the requirements of this Subsection. (See [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part5.appnote43:short].)

Other fenestration assemblies and their components shall be
designed and constructed in accordance with [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part5.sect1.subsect4.art1:long] (See [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part5.sect11.appnote49:short].)

Other fenestration assemblies and their components shall meet
the heat transfer performance requirements stated in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part5.sect3:long] (See [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part5.sect11.appnote50:short].)

Other fenestration assemblies using metal framing that separate
interior [REF:term:cnd-sp]conditioned space from interior
unconditioned space or exterior space shall incorporate a thermal
break to minimize condensation.

Other fenestration assemblies and their components shall be
designed and constructed in accordance with [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part5.sect4:long]

Except as provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part5.sect10.subsect3.art4.sent3:short], other fenestration assemblies and their components shall have
an air leakage characteristic, measured at an air pressure difference
of 75 Pa (metric), when tested in accordance with [REF:standard:astme283] that is not greater than

clauses.text:
0.2 L/(s×m^{2}) for fixed portions, including any
opaque portions, and
1.5 L/(s×m^{2}) for operable portions.

content.text: The following systems need not comply with [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part5.sect10.subsect3.art4.sent2:short]:

clauses.text:
interior windows and interior doors that do not serve as environmental
separators,
vehicular access doors (garage doors),
storm windows and storm doors,
commercial entrance systems,
revolving doors,
smoke and relief air vents,
site-built door systems, and
commercial steel doors.

content.text:
Other fenestration assemblies and their components shall be
designed and constructed in accordance with [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part5.sect6:long]

Except as provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part5.sect10.subsect3.art5.sent4:short], other fenestration assemblies and their components not covered
in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part5.sect10.subsect2.art2:long] shall resist water penetration when
tested in accordance with

clauses.text: [REF:standard:astme331] or
[REF:standard:astme547]

content.text:
Tests referred to in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part5.sect10.subsect3.art5.sent2:short] shall be carried out at the driving rain wind pressure as calculated
in accordance with [REF:standard:csaa440S1] (See [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part5.sect11.appnote54:short].)
The following systems need not comply with [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part5.sect10.subsect3.art5.sent2:short]:

clauses.text: interior windows and interior doors,
vehicular access doors (garage doors),
storm windows and storm doors,
commercial entrance systems,
revolving doors,
smoke and relief air vents,
site-built door systems, and
commercial steel doors.
