articles.title: Crawl Spaces and Attic or Roof Spaces

content.text:
Unconditioned and unoccupied crawl spaces and [REF:term:ttc-r-rf]attic or roof spaces shall be ventilated by
natural or mechanical means as required by Part 5. (See [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part6.sect10.appnote6:short].)

Except as provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part6.sect3.subsect1.art3.sent4:short]
                           [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part6.sect3.subsect1.art3.sent6:short], an enclosed [REF:term:trg-grg]storage garage for five or more motor vehicles shall have a mechanical ventilation
system designed to

clauses.text: limit the concentration of carbon monoxide to not more than 100 parts (metric) per million parts of air,

limit the concentration of nitrogen dioxide to not more than 3 parts (metric) per million parts of air, where the majority of the
vehicles stored are powered by diesel-fuelled engines, or

provide, during operating hours, a continuous supply of outdoor
air at a rate of not less than 3.9 L/s (metric) for each square
metre of [REF:term:flr-r]floor area (see [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect3.subsect1.art21:long]).

content.text:
Mechanical ventilation systems provided in accordance with [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part6.sect3.subsect1.art3.sent1.clause1:medium] shall be controlled by carbon monoxide
monitoring devices, and systems provided in accordance with [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part6.sect3.subsect1.art3.sent1.clause2:medium] shall be controlled by nitrogen
dioxide or other acceptable monitoring devices. (See [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part6.sect10.appnote8:short].)

Mechanical ventilation systems provided in accordance with [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part6.sect3.subsect1.art3.sent1:short] shall be designed such that the pressure
in the [REF:term:trg-grg]storage garage is less than the
pressure in adjoining [REF:term:bldng]buildings  of other [REF:term:ccpnc]occupancy, or in adjacent portions of the same [REF:term:bldng]building having a different [REF:term:ccpnc] occupancy.

In [REF:term:trg-grg] storage garages subject to
the requirements of [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part6.sect3.subsect1.art3.sent1:short]
                           [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part6.sect3.subsect1.art3.sent2:short], where motor vehicles are parked by mechanical means, the ventilation
requirements may be reduced by one half.

Except as provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part6.sect3.subsect1.art3.sent6:short], ticket and attendant booths of [REF:term:trg-grg]storage garages shall be pressurized with a supply of uncontaminated air.

The requirements of [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part6.sect3.subsect1.art3.sent1:short]
                           [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part6.sect3.subsect1.art3.sent5:short] shall not apply to [REF:term:pn-r-tr] open-air storeys in a [REF:term:trg-grg]storage garage.

Heat recovery ventilators with rated capacities of not less
than 25 L/s (metric) and not more than 200 L/s (metric) shall
be installed in accordance with [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect32.subsect3:long]
Air contaminants of concern within [REF:term:bldng]buildings shall

clauses.text:
be removed insofar as is possible at their points of origin,
and

not be permitted to accumulate in concentrations greater than
those permitted by applicable provincial or territorial requirements
or, in the absence of such requirements, by good engineering practice
such as that described in the publications listed in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part6.sect2.subsect1.art1.sent1:long], measured using the methodology described therein.

content.text:
Systems serving spaces that contain sources of contamination
and systems serving other occupied parts of the [REF:term:bldng]building but located in or running through spaces that contain
sources of contamination shall be designed in such a manner as to
prevent the spread of such contamination to other occupied parts of
the [REF:term:bldng]building.

Heating, ventilating and air-conditioning systems shall be designed
to minimize the growth and spread of bio-contaminants.

Except as provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect6.subsect3.art5:long], systems for
the ventilation of commercial cooking equipment shall be designed,
constructed and installed to conform to [REF:standard:nfpa96]

This Subsection applies to the design, construction and installation
of air duct distribution systems serving heating, ventilating and
air-conditioning systems other than those in [REF:term:dwllng-n]dwelling units covered by Part 9.

HVAC systems that
generate condensate or introduce liquid water into the airstream in
the ducts shall be equipped with drain pans that are

clauses.text: designed in accordance with Section 5.10, Drain Pans, of [REF:standard:ashrae62.1]

provided with an outlet that is piped to the outside of the
airstream in a location where condensate can be safely disposed of,
installed so that water does not stagnate and drains from the pan, and

designed and installed
so as to be accessible for cleaning and maintenance.

content.text:
Drain pans and associated piping shall be constructed of corrosion-resistant,
non-porous materials that do not promote the proliferation of disease-causing
micro-organisms.

All ducts, duct connectors, associated fittings and [REF:term:plnm]plenums used in air duct systems shall be constructed
of materials as described in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect6.subsect5.art1:long]

Ducts that are used in a location where they may be subjected
to excessive moisture shall have no appreciable loss of strength when
wet and shall be resistant to moisture-induced corrosion.

All ductwork and fittings shall be constructed and installed
as recommended in SMACNA Manuals and ASHRAE Standards.

All duct materials shall be suitable for exposure to the temperature
and humidity of the air being carried and shall be resistant to corrosion
caused by contaminants in the air being conveyed in the duct.
Air duct systems shall have tight-fitting connections throughout.

Coverings, linings and associated adhesives and insulation used
in air ducts, [REF:term:plnm]plenums and other parts of
air duct systems shall comply with [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect6.subsect5.art4:long]

Duct linings shall be installed so that they will not interfere
with the operation of volume or balancing dampers or of [REF:term:fr-dmpr]fire dampers, [REF:term:fr-tp-fl]fire stop
flaps and other [REF:term:clr]closures.

The clearance of ducts and [REF:term:plnm]plenums from [REF:term:cmbtbl]combustible materials shall comply
with [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect6.subsect5.art6:long]

In a [REF:term:ca-cc]care or [REF:term:rdntl-cc]residential occupancy, air from one [REF:term:t]suite shall not be circulated to any other [REF:term:t]suite or to a [REF:term:pblc-crr]public corridor.

Except as permitted by [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part6.sect3.subsect2.art7.sent3:short]
                           [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part6.sect3.subsect2.art10.sent6:long], air duct systems serving [REF:term:trg-grg]storage garages shall not be directly interconnected with other parts of the [REF:term:bldng]building.

[REF:term:xht-dct]Exhaust ducts referred to in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part6.sect3.subsect2.art10.sent10:long] are permitted to exhaust through an enclosed [REF:term:trg-grg]storage garage prior to exhausting to the outdoors,
provided

clauses.text:
the [REF:term:trg-grg]storage garage's exhaust system
runs continuously,

the capacity of the [REF:term:trg-grg]storage garage's exhaust system is equal to or exceeds the volume of the exhaust
entering the garage, and

a leakage rate 1 smoke/[REF:term:fr-dmpr]fire damper rated in accordance with [REF:standard:ulcs1121] is provided near the duct outlet location in the [REF:term:trg-grg]storage garage to prevent air from the [REF:term:trg-grg]storage garage from entering the exhaust ductwork
system in the event the [REF:term:bldng]building's exhaust
fan is shut down.

content.text:
In ventilating systems that exhaust air to the outdoors, provision
shall be made for the admission of a supply of makeup air in sufficient
quantity so that the operation of the exhaust system and other exhaust
equipment or combustion equipment is not adversely affected.

Makeup air facilities required by [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part6.sect3.subsect2.art8.sent1:short] shall be interlocked with the exhaust devices they
serve so that both operate together.

Where makeup air facilities are intended to introduce air directly
from the outdoors to occupied parts of the [REF:term:bldng]building in winter, they shall incorporate means of tempering that air to
maintain the indoor design temperature.

articles.title: Supply, Return, Intake and Exhaust Air Openings

content.text:
Supply, return and exhaust air openings located less than 2 m (metric) above the floor in rooms or spaces in [REF:term:bldng]buildings shall be protected by grilles having openings of
a size that will not allow the passage of a 15 mm (metric) diam
sphere.
Outdoor air intakes shall be located so that

clauses.text:
the quality of the air entering the [REF:term:bldng]building complies with [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part6.sect2.subsect1.art2.sent2:long]
                              [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part6.sect2.subsect1.art2.sent3:short], and

they are separated a minimum distance from sources of contaminants
in accordance with [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part6.sect3.subsect2.art9.table1:long]

content.title: Minimum Distances of Air Intakes from Sources of Contaminants

header_rows.content:
Minimum Distance of Outdoor Air
 Intake, m

body_rows.content:
Garage entry of a garage for 5 or more motor vehicles,
 automobile loading area and drive-in queue
Truck loading area or dock, and bus parking
Thoroughfare, arterial road, freeway, and highway
Discharge from evaporative heat rejection systems

content.text:
Outdoor air intakes shall be installed not less than 0.3
m (metric) above roofs, landscape grades or other surfaces, taking into
account anticipated snow accumulation levels.

Exterior openings for outdoor air intakes and exhaust outlets
shall be shielded from the entry of snow and rain and shall be fitted
with corrosion-resistant screens of mesh having openings not larger
than 15 mm (metric), except where experience has shown that climatic
conditions require larger openings to prevent the screen openings
from icing over.

Screens required in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part6.sect3.subsect2.art9.sent4:short] shall
be accessible for maintenance.

[REF:term:cmbtbl]Combustible grilles, diffusers and
other devices covering supply, return, intake and exhaust openings
shall comply with [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect6.subsect5.art7:long]

Except as provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part6.sect3.subsect2.art10.sent2:short], [REF:term:xht-dct]exhaust ducts of non-mechanical ventilating
systems serving separate rooms or spaces shall not be combined.

[REF:term:xht-dct]Exhaust ducts of non-mechanical
ventilating systems serving similar [REF:term:ccpnc]occupancies may be combined immediately below the point of final delivery to
the outdoors, such as at the base of a roof ventilator.

[REF:term:xht-dct]Exhaust ducts of ventilating systems
shall have provision for the removal of condensation where this may
be a problem.

Exhaust outlets shall be designed to prevent backdraft under
wind conditions.

Except as permitted in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part6.sect3.subsect2.art10.sent6:short], exhaust systems shall discharge directly to the outdoors. (See [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part6.sect10.appnote12:short].)
Exhaust systems are permitted to exhaust into a [REF:term:trg-grg]storage garage, provided

clauses.text: they serve rooms that are accessible only from that [REF:term:trg-grg]storage garage,

the exhaust contains no contaminants that would adversely affect
the air quality in the [REF:term:trg-grg]storage garage (see [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part6.sect10.appnote13:short]), and
they are designed in accordance with [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part6.sect3.subsect2.art7.sent3:long].

content.text:
[REF:term:xht-dct]Exhaust ducts connected to laundry-drying
equipment shall be

clauses.text: independent of other [REF:term:xht-dct]exhaust ducts,
accessible for inspection and cleaning, and
constructed of a smooth corrosion-resistant material.

content.text:
Where collective venting of multiple installations of laundry-drying
equipment is used, the ventilation system shall

clauses.text: be connected to a common [REF:term:xht-dct]exhaust duct that is vented by one central exhaust fan,

include an interlock to activate the central exhaust fan when
laundry-drying equipment is in use, and
be provided with make-up air.

content.text:
[REF:term:xht-dct]Exhaust ducts or vents connected
to laundry-drying equipment shall discharge directly to the outdoors.

Except as provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part6.sect3.subsect2.art10.sent12:short] and except for self-contained systems serving individual [REF:term:dwllng-n]dwelling units, [REF:term:xht-dct]exhaust
ducts serving rooms containing water closets, urinals, basins,
showers or slop sinks shall be independent of other [REF:term:xht-dct]exhaust ducts.

Except as provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part6.sect3.subsect2.art10.sent12:short] and except for self-contained systems serving individual [REF:term:dwllng-n]dwelling units, [REF:term:xht-dct]exhaust
ducts serving rooms containing residential cooking equipment
shall be independent of other [REF:term:xht-dct]exhaust ducts.

Two or more exhaust systems described in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part6.sect3.subsect2.art10.sent10:short]
                           [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part6.sect3.subsect2.art10.sent11:short] may be interconnected
or connected with [REF:term:xht-dct]exhaust ducts serving
other areas of the [REF:term:bldng]building, provided

clauses.text:
the connections are made at the inlet of an exhaust fan, and
all interconnected systems are equipped with suitable back pressure
devices to prevent the passage of odours from one system to another
when the fan is not in operation, or

the [REF:term:xht-dct]exhaust ducts discharge to
a shaft that is served by an exhaust fan having a capacity that is
equal to or greater than the combined capacity of the exhaust fans
discharging to the [REF:term:plnm]plenum multiplied by
the operation diversity factor, provided that the exhaust fan serving
the shaft operates continuously (see [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part6.sect10.appnote15:short]).

content.text:
Where [REF:term:xht-dct]exhaust ducts containing
air from [REF:term:cnd-sp]conditioned spaces pass through
or are adjacent to unconditioned spaces, the ducts shall be constructed
to prevent condensation from forming on the inside or outside of the
ducts.
Return-air systems shall comply with [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect6.subsect5.art8:long]

Where a ceiling space is used as a return-air [REF:term:plnm]plenum, the requirements of [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect6.subsect4.art3:long] shall
apply.
A [REF:term:pblc-crr]public corridor or [REF:term:xt]exit shall not be used as a return-air [REF:term:plnm]plenum.
Underground ducts shall

clauses.text:
be constructed and installed to provide interior drainage from
and access to all low points,
not be connected directly to a sewer, and

be installed and constructed of materials recommended by ASHRAE
and SMACNA Standards and HRAI Manuals.

content.text:
A clean-out or pump-out connection shall be provided in an underground
duct system at every low point of the duct system.

Air filters for air duct systems shall conform to the requirements
for Class 2 air filter units as described in [REF:standard:ulcs111]

When electrostatic-type filters are used, they shall be installed
so as to ensure that the electric circuit is automatically de-energized
when filter access doors are opened or, in [REF:term:dwllng-n]dwelling units, when the [REF:term:frnc]furnace circulation fan is not operating.

Where outdoor air quality conditions do not meet the requirements
of [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part6.sect2.subsect1.art2.sent2:long], ventilation required by [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part6.sect3.subsect1.art1.sent1:long] shall be provided by a ventilation system designed
to include devices that reduce particles and gases to the maximum
acceptable levels described in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part6.sect2.subsect1.art2.sent2:long] prior to
the introduction of outdoor air to indoor occupied spaces.

Where contaminants of concern are present in the outdoor air
of the local area of the [REF:term:bldng]building site,
ventilation required by [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part6.sect3.subsect1.art1.sent1:long] shall be provided
by a ventilation system designed to include devices that reduce the
concentrations of contaminants to those permitted in the ACGIH's [REF:standard:acgih-iv-mrp] prior to the introduction
of outdoor air to indoor occupied spaces.
Evaporative heat rejection systems shall

clauses.text:
incorporate a drift eliminator or other means to minimize the
dispersion of entrained water droplets, and

have a design discharge velocity that does not exceed the maximum
discharge velocity recommended by the manufacturer.

content.text:
Evaporative heat rejection systems shall be designed so that
water continuously circulates through all parts of the system that
are normally wetted when the system is operating.

Evaporative heat rejection systems and their components shall
be constructed of corrosion-resistant, non-porous materials that do
not promote the proliferation of disease-causing micro-organisms and
that are compatible with disinfectants, biocides and other cleaning
agents.
Evaporative heat rejection systems shall be installed such that

clauses.text:
no discharge air bypasses the drift eliminator or other means
referred to in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part6.sect3.subsect2.art15.sent1.clause1:medium], and
the systems are accessible for cleaning, inspection and maintenance.

content.text:
Except as provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part6.sect3.subsect2.art15.sent6:short], air discharged from evaporative heat rejection systems shall discharge
away from the [REF:term:bldng]building, so as to not re-enter
it, to a distance not less than

clauses.text: 2.15 m (metric) above sidewalks and driveways,
7.6 m (metric) from outdoor air intakes,

3 m (metric) horizontally or vertically from exterior doors
and operable windows, and

3 m (metric) horizontally or vertically from occupiable
outdoor spaces, excluding maintenance spaces.

content.text:
Air discharged from evaporative heat rejection systems in health
care facilities shall discharge away from the [REF:term:bldng]building in compliance with [REF:standard:csaz317.2] (See [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part6.sect10.appnote16:short].)

Air intakes of
evaporative heat rejection systems shall incorporate protective measures
to minimize the entrainment of vegetation and other organic matter.

Make-up water connections shall be equipped with backflow prevention
devices that conform to Article 2.6.2.1. of Division B of Book II, (Plumbing Systems), of this code. (See [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part6.sect10.appnote17:short].)

Water treatment systems and equipment for controlling the proliferation of disease-causing
micro-organisms shall

clauses.text:
be provided in
accordance with [REF:external:ashrae12]Section 7.6.2. of 
                              [REF:standard:ashrae12] and

include means for
drainage, dilution, cleaning, and application of chemicals for the
control of scale, corrosion and biological contamination.

content.text:
Drains, overflows and blow-downs shall be connected to the [REF:term:bldng]building's drainage system in accordance with [REF:external:npc]Clause 2.4.2.1.(1)(e) of Division B of Book II, (Plumbing Systems), of this code
                           [REF:standard:nrcc-npc].

Evaporative heat
rejection systems shall be provided with access openings, service
platforms, fixed ladders and fall-restraint connections to allow inspection, maintenance and testing.

articles.title:
Evaporative Air Coolers, Misters, Atomizers, Air Washers and
Humidifiers

content.text:
Evaporative air coolers, misters, atomizers, air washers and
humidifiers shall be designed in accordance with [REF:external:ashrae12]Sections 8 and 9 of 
                           [REF:standard:ashrae12]
Systems referred to in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part6.sect3.subsect2.art16.sent1:short] shall

clauses.text:
be designed so that water continuously circulates through all
parts of the system that are normally wetted when the system is operating,
and

incorporate a method of preventing water stagnation within the
system itself and the internal plumbing when the system is not operating.

content.text:
All components of systems referred to in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part6.sect3.subsect2.art16.sent1:short], including filters and evaporation media, shall be
constructed of corrosion-resistant, non-porous materials that do not
promote the proliferation of disease-causing micro-organisms.
Associated sumps shall

clauses.text:
be constructed of corrosion-resistant, non-porous materials
that do not promote the proliferation of disease-causing micro-organisms,

include auxiliary drains to prevent the overflow of water into
ductwork, and

be installed so that they can be flushed, drained, cleaned and
disinfected.

content.text:
Where misters, atomizers or air washers are used in ductwork,
the affected duct section shall be

clauses.text:
designed to ensure drainage of unevaporated and accumulated
water, and

constructed of corrosion-resistant, non-porous materials that
do not promote the proliferation of disease-causing micro-organisms.

content.text:
Make-up water connections shall be equipped with backflow prevention
devices that conform to Article 2.6.2.1. of Division B of Book II, (Plumbing Systems), of this code. (See [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part6.sect10.appnote19:short].)

Fans for heating, ventilating and air-conditioning systems shall
be located and installed so that their operation

clauses.text:
does not adversely affect the draft required for proper operation
of fuel-fired [REF:term:pplnc]appliances, and

does not allow the air in the duct system to be contaminated
by air or gases from the [REF:term:blr]boiler room or [REF:term:frnc] furnace room.

content.text:
Fans and associated air-handling equipment, such as air washers,
filters and heating and cooling units, when installed on the roof
or elsewhere outside the [REF:term:bldng]building, shall
be of a type designed for outdoor use.

Vibration isolation connectors in air duct systems shall comply
with [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect6.subsect5.art2:long]
Tape used for sealing joints in air ducts, [REF:term:plnm]plenums and other parts of air duct systems shall comply with [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect6.subsect5.art3:long]

Except as provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part6.sect3.subsect3.art2:long]
                           [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part6.sect3.subsect3.art3:long], the products of combustion
from oil-, gas- and solid-fuel-burning [REF:term:pplnc] appliances shall be vented in conformance with the requirements in the applicable [REF:term:pplnc]appliance installation standard listed in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part6.sect2.subsect1.art5:long]

Except as provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part6.sect2.subsect1.art5:long], vented products
of combustion, other than those referred to in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part6.sect3.subsect3.art1.sent1:short], shall be discharged away from the [REF:term:bldng]building, so as not to re-enter it, to a distance not less
than

clauses.text: 2.15 m (metric) above sidewalks and driveways,
3 m (metric) from outdoor air intakes,

3 m (metric) horizontally or vertically from doors and operable
windows, and

3 m (metric) horizontally or vertically from occupiable
outdoor spaces, excluding maintenance spaces.

content.text: Rectangular [REF:term:mnr-r-cn] masonry or concrete chimneys not more than 12 m (metric) in height shall conform to [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9:long] if they serve

clauses.text:
[REF:term:pplnc]appliances with a combined total
rated heat output of 120 kW (metric) or less, or
fireplaces.

content.text:
[REF:term:mnr-r-cn]Masonry or concrete chimneys other
than those described in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part6.sect3.subsect3.art2.sent1:short] shall
be designed and installed in conformance with the appropriate requirements
in [REF:standard:nfpa211]

Single wall metal smoke stacks shall be designed and installed
in conformance with [REF:standard:nfpa211]

Access ladders for [REF:term:chmn]chimneys, when
provided, shall consist of steel or bronze rungs, built into the walls
of the [REF:term:chmn]chimneys.
Rungs for external ladders shall begin at not less than 2.5 m (metric) from ground level.

This Subsection applies to laboratories where [REF:term:dngr-gd]dangerous goods, including [REF:term:flmmbl-l]flammable liquids and [REF:term:cmbtbl-l]combustible liquids, are used in normal laboratory operations in quantities or in a
manner that creates a fire or explosion hazard.

A laboratory shall be provided with continuous mechanical ventilation
designed to ensure that [REF:term:dngr-gd]dangerous goods vapours and particles

clauses.text: do not accumulate in the laboratory,
are prevented from migrating to other parts of the [REF:term:bldng]building,
do not accumulate in the ventilation system,
are exhausted to the outdoors, and
are not returned to the [REF:term:bldng]building.

content.text:
A ventilation system required by this Subsection shall be provided
with monitoring devices to

clauses.text: indicate that the ventilation system is in operation, and
sound an alarm if the ventilation system is malfunctioning.

content.text:
A ventilation system required by this Subsection shall be maintained
in conformance with Article 5.5.4.1. of Division B of the British Columbia Fire Code.
The ventilation system for a power-ventilated enclosure required by Sentence 5.5.4.2.(1) of Division B of the British Columbia Fire Code shall

clauses.text: conform to [REF:standard:nfpa91]

provide continuous exhaust ventilation at an air velocity sufficient to prevent the accumulation of [REF:term:cmbtbl]combustible or reactive deposits in the power-ventilated enclosure and its [REF:term:xht-dct]exhaust duct system,
confine [REF:term:dngr-gd]dangerous goods vapours and particles to the area where they are generated and exhaust them to the outdoors,
not return the exhausted air to the [REF:term:bldng]building, and
be provided with well identified control switches that are

subclauses.text: located outside of the power-ventilated enclosure, and
readily accessible in case of an emergency.

content.text: The power-ventilated enclosure required by Sentence 5.5.4.2.(1) of Division B of the British Columbia Fire Code and its [REF:term:xht-dct]exhaust duct system shall

clauses.text: except as provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part6.sect3.subsect4.art4.sent2:short] and [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part6.sect3.subsect4.art4.sent3:short], be constructed of [REF:term:ncmbtbl]noncombustible materials compatible with and chemically resistant to the [REF:term:dngr-gd]dangerous goods vapours and particles being exhausted, and
be provided with access doors to permit inspection and maintenance of the fan assembly and [REF:term:xht-dct]exhaust duct system.

content.text:
[REF:term:cmbtbl]Combustible materials are permitted
in systems described in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part6.sect3.subsect4.art4.sent1.clause1:medium] if

clauses.text:
such materials are required by the corrosive or reactive properties
of the [REF:term:dngr-gd]dangerous goods being used, and

their [REF:term:flm-prd-]flame-spread rating is not
more than 25.

content.text:
The [REF:term:flm-prd-]flame-spread rating required
by [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part6.sect3.subsect4.art4.sent2:short] is permitted to be greater
than 25 if an automatic fire suppression system is provided inside
the power-ventilated enclosure and its [REF:term:xht-dct]exhaust
duct system.

Except for [REF:term:pplnc] appliances installed
in [REF:term:dwllng-n]dwelling units, fuel-fired heating [REF:term:pplnc]appliances shall be located, enclosed or separated
from the remainder of the [REF:term:bldng]building  in
conformance with [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect6:long] (See also [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect10.subsect10:long])

Fuel-fired [REF:term:pplnc]appliances installed outside
a [REF:term:bldng]building shall be designed and constructed
for outdoor use.

Every [REF:term:nt-htr]unit heater using either steam
or hot water as the heating medium shall be installed such that the
clearances between the [REF:term:pplnc]appliance and adjacent [REF:term:cmbtbl]combustible material conform to [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part6.sect7.subsect1.art2.table1:long]

A [REF:term:ncmbtbl]noncombustible lining or backing
shall be provided for every steam or hot water radiator and convector

clauses.text: located in a recess or concealed space, or

attached to the face of a wall of [REF:term:cmbtbl-c]combustible
construction or [REF:term:ncps-mt-nstr]encapsulated mass timber construction.

content.text:
Every steam or hot water radiator and convector shall be installed
so as to conform to the clearance requirements of [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part6.sect7.subsect1.art2.table1:long]
Insulation and coverings on pipes shall comply with [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect6.subsect5.art5:long]

Insulation and coverings on pipes shall be composed of material
that will withstand deterioration from softening, melting, mildew
and mould at the operating temperature of the system.

Exposed piping or equipment subject to human contact shall be
insulated so that the temperature of the exposed surface does not
exceed 52°C. (metric) (See [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part6.sect10.appnote21:short].)

subsections.title: Refrigerating Systems and Equipment for Air-conditioning

content.text:
Where a cooling unit is combined with a fuel-fired [REF:term:frnc]furnace in the same duct system, the cooling unit
shall be installed

clauses.text: in parallel with the heating [REF:term:frnc]furnace,
upstream of the [REF:term:frnc]furnace provided the [REF:term:frnc]furnace is designed for such application, or

downstream of the [REF:term:frnc]furnace provided
the cooling unit is designed to prevent excessive temperature or pressure
in the refrigeration system.

subsections.title: Piping for Heating and Cooling Systems

content.text:
Piping shall be made from materials designed to withstand the
effects of temperatures and pressures that may occur in the system.
(See [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect1.subsect5.art19:long]
                           [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect1.subsect9.art1:long]
                           [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect10.subsect9.art6:long]
                           [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect10.subsect9.art7:long] for fire safety requirements.)

Every pipe used in a heating or air-conditioning system shall
be installed to allow for expansion and contraction due to temperature
changes.

Supports and anchors for piping in a heating or air-conditioning
system shall be designed and installed to ensure that undue stress
is not placed on the supporting structure.

Clearances between [REF:term:cmbtbl]combustible material
and bare pipes carrying steam or hot water shall conform to [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part6.sect7.subsect1.art2.table1:long]

content.title:
Clearance Between Steam or Hot Water Pipes and Combustible
Material

content.text:
The exposed surface temperature of a steam or hot water radiator
shall not exceed 70°C (metric) unless precautions are taken to
prevent human contact. (See [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part6.sect10.appnote21:long].)

Where a pipe carrying steam or hot water at a temperature above 120°C (metric) passes through a [REF:term:cmbtbl]combustible floor, ceiling or wall, the construction shall be protected by a
sleeve of metal or other [REF:term:ncmbtbl]noncombustible material not less than 50 mm (metric) larger in diameter than
the pipe.

Where piping for heating or air-conditioning systems is enclosed
in a shaft, the requirements of [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect6.subsect3.art1:long] for shafts
shall apply.

Service pipes passing through a storage bin for solid fuel shall
be protected or so located as to avoid damage to the pipes.

Except for fuel-thawing pipes, every pipe designed to operate
at a temperature of 50°C (metric) or above shall be located where
solid fuel cannot be stored in contact with it.

Any covering of an access opening through which a person could
enter shall be openable from the inside without the use of keys where
there is a possibility of the opening being accidentally closed while
the system or equipment is being serviced.

Air duct systems shall have no openings other than those required
for the proper operation and maintenance of the system.

Access openings shall be provided in duct systems to allow the
removal of material that may accumulate in [REF:term:plnm]plenums and ducts.

When odour removal equipment of the adsorption type is used,
it shall be

clauses.text:
installed to allow access so that adsorption material can be
reactivated or renewed, and

protected from dust accumulation by air filters installed on
the inlet side.

content.text:
Facilities for flushing and drainage shall be provided where
filters are designed to be washed in place.

The fire safety characteristics of heating, ventilating and
air-conditioning systems shall comply with [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect6.subsect5:long]
Characteristics referred to in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part6.sect9.subsect1.art1.sent1:short] include but are not limited to

clauses.text:
use of [REF:term:cmbtbl]combustible materials in
duct systems,

[REF:term:flm-prd-]flame-spread ratings and smoke-developed
ratings of duct and pipe materials and coverings,
installation of equipment relative to property lines, and
requirements for [REF:term:fr-dmpr]fire dampers and [REF:term:fr-tp-fl]fire stop flaps.

content.text:
Except as provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part6.sect3.subsect4:long], systems serving spaces that contain hazardous
gases, dusts or liquids shall be designed, constructed and installed
to conform to the requirements of the applicable provincial or territorial
regulations or municipal bylaws or, in the absence of such regulations
or bylaws, to good engineering practice such as that described in
the publications of the National Fire Protection Association and in
the British Columbia Fire Code. (See [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part6.sect10.appnote22:short].)

When indoor piping for Class I [REF:term:flmmbl-l]flammable
liquids is installed in a trench, the trench shall be

clauses.text: provided with positive ventilation to the outdoors, or
designed to prevent the accumulation of flammable vapours.

content.text:
Fire protection systems for commercial cooking equipment referred
to in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part6.sect3.subsect1.art6.sent1:long] using vegetable oil or animal fat
shall conform to

clauses.text: [REF:standard:ul300] or
[REF:standard:ulcc1254.6]

content.text: [REF:term:fr-dmpr]Fire dampers shall conform to [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect1.subsect8.art10:long]
Air handling systems shall incorporate [REF:term:mk-dtctr]smoke detectors where and as required by [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect2.subsect4.art12:long]

Where an [REF:term:xht-dct]exhaust duct system is
used for smoke removal in a high [REF:term:bldng]building, the requirements of [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect2.subsect6.art6:long] shall apply.

Where [REF:term:xht-dct]exhaust duct systems from
more than one [REF:term:fr-cmprt]fire compartment are connected
to an [REF:term:xht-dct]exhaust duct in a [REF:term:vrtcl-rv]vertical service space, the requirements of [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect6.subsect3.art4:long] shall apply.

Where ducts penetrate [REF:term:fr-prtn]fire separations separating [REF:term:xt]exits from the remainder of the [REF:term:bldng]building, they shall be in accordance with [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect4.subsect4.art4:long]

This Article applies to every [REF:term:bldng]building that contains an assembly occupancy, a [REF:term:ca-cc]care occupancy with individual [REF:term:t]suites or containing sleeping rooms or bed spaces not within a suite, a residential occupancy, a business and personal services occupancy, or a mercantile occupancy, and that

clauses.text: is served by or contains a fuel-burning [REF:term:pplnc]appliance, or
contains a [REF:term:trg-grg]storage garage.

content.text: Carbon monoxide (CO) alarms installed in a residential occupancy or a [REF:term:ca-cc]care occupancy as required by this Article shall

clauses.text: conform to [REF:standard:csa6.19],
be equipped with an integral alarm that satisfies the audibility requirements of [REF:standard:csa6.19],

have no disconnect switch between the overcurrent device and the CO alarm, where the CO alarm is powered by the electrical system serving the [REF:term:t]suite (see [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part6.sect10.appnote23:short]), and
be installed as recommended by the manufacturer.

content.text: Except as permitted by [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part6.sect9.subsect3.art1.sent9:short], where a fuel-burning [REF:term:pplnc]appliance is installed in a [REF:term:t]suite of [REF:term:rdntl-cc]residential occupancy or in a [REF:term:t]suite of [REF:term:ca-cc]care occupancy, a CO alarm shall be installed

clauses.text: inside each sleeping room or bed space, or
outside each sleeping room or bed space, within 5 m (metric) of each door serving a sleeping room or bed space, measured following corridors and doorways.

content.text: Except as permitted by [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part6.sect9.subsect3.art1.sent9:short], where a fuel-burning [REF:term:pplnc]appliance serves a residential occupancy or a [REF:term:ca-cc]care occupancy and is installed in a [REF:term:rvc-rm]service room that is not in a [REF:term:t]suite of [REF:term:rdntl-cc]residential occupancy nor in a [REF:term:t]suite of [REF:term:ca-cc]care occupancy, a CO alarm shall be installed

clauses.text: either inside each sleeping room or bed space, or if outside, within 5 m (metric) of each door serving a sleeping room or bed space, measured following corridors and doorways, in every [REF:term:t]suite of [REF:term:rdntl-cc]residential occupancy or [REF:term:t]suite of [REF:term:ca-cc]care occupancy that shares a wall or floor/ceiling assembly with the [REF:term:rvc-rm]service room, and
in the [REF:term:rvc-rm]service room.

content.text: Except as permitted by [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part6.sect9.subsect3.art1.sent9:short], for each [REF:term:t]suite of [REF:term:rdntl-cc]residential occupancy or [REF:term:t]suite of [REF:term:ca-cc]care occupancy that shares a wall or floor/ceiling assembly with a [REF:term:trg-grg]storage garage or that is adjacent to an attic or crawl space to which the [REF:term:trg-grg]storage garage is also adjacent, a CO alarm shall be installed

clauses.text: inside each sleeping room or bed space, or
outside each sleeping room or bed space, within 5 m (metric) of each bedroom door serving a sleeping room or bed space, measured following corridors and doorways.

content.text: CO alarms installed in an assembly occupancy, a business and personal services occupancy, or a mercantile occupancy as required by this Article shall conform to

clauses.text: [REF:standard:csa6.19], notwithstanding the scope of that standard,
[REF:standard:ul2034], notwithstanding the scope of that standard, or
good engineering practice.

content.text: Except as permitted by [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part6.sect9.subsect3.art1.sent9:short], where a fuel-burning appliance serves an assembly occupancy, business and personal services occupancy, or mercantile occupancy, a CO alarm shall be,

clauses.text: where the fuel-burning appliance is part of a system that could circulate or distribute CO to a suite of assembly occupancy, business and personal services occupancy or mercantile occupancy, installed

subclauses.text: on each storey of each suite that may be exposed, and
in a suite containing an assembly major occupancy, each classroom and dedicated gathering room or space, and

clauses.text: installed in the room or space in which the fuel-burning appliance is located.

content.text: Except as permitted by [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part6.sect9.subsect3.art1.sent9:short], for each suite of assembly occupancy, business and personal services occupancy, or mercantile occupancy that shares a wall or floor/ceiling assembly with either a [REF:term:trg-grg]storage garage or a [REF:term:rvc-rm]service room containing a fuel-burning appliance, or that is adjacent to either an attic or crawl space to which the [REF:term:trg-grg]storage garage or a [REF:term:rvc-rm]service room containing a fuel-burning appliance is also adjacent, a CO alarm shall be installed

clauses.text: on each storey of the adjacent suite,
where the adjacent suite contains an assembly major occupancy, each classroom and dedicated room or space, and
in each [REF:term:rvc-rm]service room containing a fuel-burning appliance.

content.text: CO detectors are permitted to be installed in lieu of CO alarms required by this Article provided the CO detectors

clauses.text: sound audible signals within the location they serve, as described in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part6.sect9.subsect3.art1.sent3:short] to [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part6.sect9.subsect3.art1.sent5:number], [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part6.sect9.subsect3.art1.sent7:number] and [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part6.sect9.subsect3.art1.sent8:number],
are installed in conformance with [REF:standard:ulcs524], and
form part of the fire alarm system.

content.text: Every ash storage bin shall be constructed of [REF:term:ncmbtbl]noncombustible material.

Every opening in an ash storage bin shall be protected by a
tight-fitting metal door with metal frame securely fastened to the
bin.
Fireplaces shall conform to the requirements of [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect22:long]

For the purpose of compliance with this Code as required in [REF:internal:nbc.divA.part1.sect2.subsect1.art1.sent1.clause2:long], the objectives and functional statements
attributed to the acceptable solutions in this Part shall be the objectives
and functional statements listed in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part6.sect10.subsect1.art1.table1:long] (See [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part1.sect3.appnote1:long].)

appendix.introduction:
These Notes are included for explanatory
purposes only and do not form part of the requirements. The number
that introduces each Note corresponds to the applicable requirement
in this Part.

paragraphs.content:
New buildings tend to be considerably more airtight than older
ones. Consequently, these buildings may have a reduced pressurization
requirement compared to the normal requirement in order to limit drafts
and provide a reasonable level of comfort.

The humidification and relative pressurization of buildings
and individual spaces in buildings can be significant factors in compromising
the ongoing performance of the building envelope and other environmental
separators.

In new construction, HVAC designers should take this issue into
consideration and confer with those responsible for the design of
the environmental separators so as to limit unintended effects on
the environmental separators. In existing buildings, the ability of
the environmental separators to resist or accommodate increases in
pressure differential or moisture loading should be considered before
changes are made to the HVAC system.

HVAC designers should either develop a water management plan
or complete a formal risk and hazard assessment to determine what
measures are required for the control of legionella. The risk and
hazard assessment should include inspections of the building and its
surroundings to locate potential sources of legionella and to identify
equipment or systems that could promote the growth and spread of legionella.
The assessment should also evaluate the risk to building occupants
that is associated with any identified equipment or systems, taking
into account their design, location and operating conditions.

Further information on minimizing the growth and spread of legionella
can be found in the following publications:
                           
                              [REF:standard:ashrae188]
                           
                           “Developing a Water Management Program to Reduce Legionella
Growth and Spread in Buildings” (U.S. Centers for Disease Control
and Prevention, 2017),
                           “Legionella and Legionnaires' Disease: A Policy Overview”
(European Agency for Safety and Health at Work, 2011),
                           “Legionella and the Prevention of Legionellosis” (World
Health Organization, 2007),
                           “Legionnaires' Disease: Technical Guidance: Part 1:
The Control of Legionella Bacteria in Evaporative Cooling Systems,
and Part 3: The Control of Legionella Bacteria in Other Risk Systems”
(U.K. Health and Safety Executive, 2013), and
                           “Recognition, Evaluation and Control of Legionella in Building
Water Systems” (American Industrial Hygiene Association, 2015).

Measures may be necessary to reduce the radon concentration
to a level below the guideline specified by Health Canada.

Further information on reducing the indoor concentration of
radon can be found in the following Health Canada publications:
                           
                              [REF:standard:hc_grmpb] and
                           
                              [REF:standard:hc-rgch]

In the past, the practice of ventilating buildings with outdoor
air assumed that the outdoor air was of better quality than the indoor
air. It has become evident that the outdoor air in some areas of Canada
may not be of an acceptable quality for ventilating buildings unless
certain particles and gases are first removed or reduced. For particulate
matter, the maximum acceptable level is the 98th percentile of the
average 24 hour values; for ozone, the maximum acceptable level is
the average of the average 8 hour values. A recent estimate suggests
that many Canadians are exposed to contaminated outdoor air via buildings'
ventilation systems, which may lead to health problems such as cardiovascular
and cerebral vascular diseases, respiratory irritation and illnesses,
asthma, allergies, cancer, mucus membrane disorders and possibly death.

In order to manage the air quality of a building's indoor environment,
thus reducing the potential for adverse effects on occupants' health,
the quality of outdoor air for building ventilation purposes must
be addressed. The air pollutants for which standards have been developed
are particulate matter and ground-level ozone. [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part6.sect2.subsect1.art2.sent2:long] sets limits on the maximum acceptable levels of these particles
and gas that a building's ventilation system should introduce directly
to the indoor environment. These limits form part of the Canada-wide
Standards for Particulate Matter (PM) and Ozone, which were established
pursuant to the 1998 Canada-wide Accord on Environmental Harmonization
of the Canadian Council of Ministers of the Environment (CCME) and
its Canada-wide Environmental Standards Sub-Agreement. Information
on related regulations is available from Environment and Climate Change
Canada and the provincial/territorial ministries of the environment.
A database of particle measurements for certain Canadian locations
is available from the National Air Pollution Surveillance Network
(NAPS), which is run by Environment and Climate Change Canada in conjunction
with the provinces and territories.

The outdoor air at the local area of the building site, including
its immediate surroundings, should be assessed to identify the levels
of contaminants that may be of concern if allowed to enter the building.
Examples of contaminants of concern include the following:
                        irritants from restaurant and dumpster emissions
                        visible plumes from cooling towers and incinerators
                        combustion exhaust from vehicles on loading docks and highways
                        other visible sources of contaminants on site and from adjoining
properties (e.g. manufacturing plants)
                     Factors that can influence the infiltration of contaminants,
such as the building's geometry and prevailing winds and seasonal
activity in the local area, should also be considered. Features can
be incorporated in the design of the building to mitigate the effects
of the identified contaminants of concern to the building occupants.

This
Article is intended to remind designers and installers of mechanical
systems of one aspect of the “good engineering practice” referred
to in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part6.sect2.subsect1.art1:long]

In determining how to accommodate structural movement, there
are two important principles to bear in mind:
                        The prime concern of the NBC is the safety of people in
and around the building, as opposed to protection of the mechanical
systems and equipment. 
                        The nature of the accommodation will vary with the type
of movement being considered, taking into account particularly how
often the movement is likely to be encountered over the life of the
building.

For example, a gas line supported on columns that also support
a crane must be installed in such a way that the movement of the columns,
which occurs many times daily, does not cause the lines to break,
thus creating a hazard. Even if the gas line installation could somehow
be designed to break in a non-hazardous manner, it would hardly be
recognized as good engineering practice if movement that occurs so
frequently could disrupt the operation of the mechanical system.

On the other hand, earthquakes occur far less frequently and
it would not be surprising to have a non-critical mechanical system
fail as a result of an earthquake. However, even in this situation,
the failure must occur in a manner that does not create a hazard to
building occupants. For example, heavy mechanical equipment should
be properly anchored so that it does not topple on building occupants
during an earthquake. The design of the anchors should take into account
accelerations consistent with the seismic data given in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.appendixC:long] for the location of the building. [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4:long] provides guidance on the calculation of the loads
such equipment would exert on the building structure during an earthquake;
these same loads can be used in designing the anchors.

Some mechanical equipment can be an important component of post-disaster
life safety systems. In these cases, the measures needed to accommodate
the movements caused by an earthquake become even more critical since
failure of the equipment would not be acceptable.

Clearly, complying with this requirement will, in most cases,
necessitate close coordination between the mechanical designer and
the structural designer.

For additional information on the types of structural movement
that may be encountered, see [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect3.art5:long], [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect3.art3.sent2:long] and [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect8:long]

Ducts or pipes without dampers or valves are generally not considered
to constitute “equipment” and are therefore not subject to this requirement.

application_notes.title:
Ventilation and Venting of Crawl
Spaces and Attic or Roof Spaces

paragraphs.content:
The cross-reference to [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part5:long] pertains to unconditioned and unoccupied crawl
spaces, and attic or roof spaces, which are effectively within the
building envelope. That is, unconditioned and unoccupied attic or
roof spaces are located between the roof deck and roofing above, and
the insulation, air barrier system and vapour barrier below. Unconditioned
and unoccupied crawl spaces are located between the ground cover below
and the insulation, air barrier system and vapour barrier above. Venting
of these spaces has implications for the performance of the building
envelope rather than having direct effects on indoor conditions. The
ventilation of conditioned or occupied crawl spaces and attic or roof
spaces must comply with [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part6:long].

The requirements in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part5:long] are stated in
terms of loads that must be resisted rather than in terms of building
elements. Thus, the Code user will not find explicit references in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part5:long] to crawl spaces, or attic or roof spaces. [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part5:long] makes reference to the need for venting environmental
separators, i.e., the dissipation of heat or moisture.

[REF:internal:nbc.divB.part6.sect3.subsect1.art2.sent1:long] requires that crawl spaces be ventilated
either by natural (above-grade only) or mechanical means. High moisture
levels within the crawl space can lead to problems such as the formation
of mould, lifting of flooring or long-term damage to structural components.

Crawl space ventilation cannot be expected to correct moisture-related
problems caused by other factors like inadequate surface drainage
from the foundation walls or improper protection against moisture
from the ground. These conditions must be properly addressed so that
crawl space ventilation can meet its intended objectives.

Several factors favour the use of mechanical ventilation rather
than reliance on natural drafts. Local conditions, such as areas with
high water tables, may dictate the need for mechanical ventilation
to remove excessive moisture.

Crawl spaces should be maintained at a negative pressure relative
to the conditioned area above to prevent the migration of moisture
into occupied areas. This can be achieved through the use of an exhaust
fan and relying on air transfer through floor penetrations, such as
pipes.

Areas
where motor vehicles are parked with the engine off for extended periods
of time, such as car dealership showrooms, are not considered as storage
garages.

Storage garages are ventilated to protect occupants from exposure
to carbon monoxide and other vehicular exhaust fumes. In certain cases,
such as small two- or three-bay storage garages that are used for
occasional vehicle storage, and where occupants are not present, carbon
monoxide or nitrogen dioxide monitoring devices may be omitted if
the ventilation system is interlocked with a local light switch or
other controls to ensure continuous system operation whenever the
area is occupied. In any event, the ventilation system capacity must
be designed to limit the concentrations of carbon monoxide or nitrogen
dioxide at or below the prescribed values.

Indoor air can contain complex mixtures of contaminants of concern
such as formaldehyde, legionella, mould and emissions from building
materials. While some contaminants may be knowingly introduced—as
in the case of processing and manufacturing environments—others may
be unintentionally released into indoor environments. [REF:standard:acgih-iv-mrp] published by the ACGIH, and
the [REF:standard:hc46-2.90-156e] published
by Health Canada, are useful references on the control of contaminants
in industrial workplace environments and residential settings, respectively.
These and other guidelines and manuals should be interpreted while
keeping in mind the settings and purposes for which they were developed
compared to those to which they will be applied. Note that such documents
do not necessarily consider the interactions between various contaminants.

divisions.title: Minimizing the Growth and Spread of Bio-contaminants

paragraphs.content:
Bio-contaminants, such as bacteria, mould, mildew, fungi, viruses,
and pollen, can thrive in or be spread by sources like drain pans, spray-water air-washers,
contaminated filters, poorly maintained cooling coils, water incursion
into ductwork, high humidity and stagnant water, potentially causing
a wide range of adverse health effects including respiratory allergic
reactions, asthma, and diseases ranging from influenza to legionellosis.

Some of the control measures are as follows: 
                           Air-handling equipment should be accessible for the maintenance
of filters, cooling coils and condensate drain pans located below
the cooling coils. Access doors should be large and easy to open to
facilitate thorough and regular maintenance.
                           If moisture is added to building ventilation air to maintain
humidity levels in a designated range, humidifiers that inject steam
or water vapour into central air-handling units or main supply ducts
are normally used. Injection nozzles should not be located in air-handling
unit plenums or ductwork that is insulated with internal fibrous lining.
If the lining becomes wet, conditions conducive to the growth and
spread of bio-contaminants will result.
                           HVAC systems
that generate condensate or introduce liquid water into the airstream
in the ducts require adequate drainage of excess water and, in some
cases, a means of capturing air-entrained water droplets. These measures
reduce the potential for bio-contaminants, including legionella, to
proliferate in stagnant water and for water droplets containing bio-contaminants
to be introduced into the airstream and contaminate the indoor environment.
(See also [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part6.sect3.subsect2.art2:long])

The above only addresses built-in features of an HVAC system
that can help to minimize the growth and spread of bio-contaminants.
Even more important than the built-in features is a program of regular
maintenance and cleaning of those portions of the system where such
growth is likely to occur.

It is important to eliminate stagnant water as it can promote
the proliferation of disease-causing micro-organisms, such as legionella.

Of particular concern is the potential for legionella bacteria
in water to become airborne in water droplets or mist that can be
inhaled by humans or can contaminate other water sources or systems.

The TIAC [REF:standard:tiac_bp] is
a comprehensive source of information on the selection, installation
and proper use of thermal insulation materials. (Note that [REF:external:tiac_bp]Section 4 of this Guide is not included
in the scope of this Note as it contains information on proprietary
products, which are not within the mandate of the Code.)

A frequent practice in the design of ventilation systems serving
buildings which have associated parking garages is to discharge exhaust
air from the building to the garage in order to reduce the cost of
heating the garage or reduce the length of the exhaust ducts. However,
this practice entails a certain amount of risk since, when the exhaust
system is not running, stack effect may turn the exhaust outlets into
intakes and exhaust fumes (including carbon monoxide) can be drawn
from the garage into the building. Incorporating a backdraft damper
at the exhaust outlet provides some additional protection but backdraft
dampers are generally not regarded as being very reliable. Therefore
this practice is only permitted in very limited circumstances.

For the purpose of [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part6.sect3.subsect2.art10.sent6.clause2:long], washroom exhaust
air is not considered to contain contaminants that would adversely
affect the air quality in the storage garage.

application_notes.title:
Exhaust Ducts Connected
to Laundry-Drying Equipment

paragraphs.content:
Clothes dryers are a major
cause of fires in buildings often due to a build-up of lint in the
system, which then ignites or obstructs the venting or ventilation.
Proper cleaning and regular maintenance of lint traps is directly
proportional to the ease of access to the lint traps.  It is therefore
important to ensure that lint traps in multiple installations of laundry-drying
equipment are installed in such a way as to allow easy access for
inspection, maintenance, repair and cleaning.

The operation diversity factor has to be assessed for each specific
application. Good engineering practice (see [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part6.sect2.subsect1.art1:long]) design guidelines can provide information on the subject. [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part6.sect10.appnote15.figure1:long], which originates from ASHRAE handbooks, provides
an example of factors that can be used for general applications.

figures.title: Operation diversity factor

graphic.alt_text: Operation diversity factor

paragraphs.content:
Ensuring adequate distance between the air discharge locations
of evaporative heat rejection systems and certain outdoor spaces and
building components minimizes the potential for contamination of the
air of occupiable spaces. For example, if a building's ventilation
air intake were located too close to an air discharge location of
an evaporative heat rejection system, warm discharge air and associated
drift, which could contain biological contaminants, could be introduced
to the indoor environment through the air intake.

The minimum distances stated in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part6.sect3.subsect2.art15.sent5:long]
                     [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part6.sect3.subsect2.art15.sent6:short] may need to be increased where warranted by local conditions such
as prevailing winds, adjacent structures, or special processes being
carried out, any of which would make further analysis necessary. (See
also [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part6.sect3.subsect3.art1.sent2:long].)

application_notes.title:
Assessment of System and
Make-Up Water

paragraphs.content:
The chemical characteristics of the water
in the evaporative heat rejection system and of the make-up water
should be assessed to select a suitable water treatment system.

Common strategies to prevent water stagnation include flushing,
providing an inactivity drain, and periodic activation, even with
no load.

The chemical characteristics of the make-up water should be
assessed to ensure that any chemicals added to a system referred to
in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part6.sect3.subsect2.art16.sent1:long] for precipitation control, disinfection
or another purpose will not adversely affect the system.

[REF:internal:nbc.divB.part6.sect3.subsect3.art1.sent2:long] requires that vented products of combustion
from appliances be discharged a minimum distance away from certain
outdoor spaces and building components in cases where the vented products
could contaminate the air of occupiable spaces. These minimum distances
may need to be increased due to local conditions such as prevailing
winds, adjacent structures, special processes being carried out, specific
contaminants or effluent discharges, all of which would require further
analysis.

“Occupiable outdoor spaces” refers to areas that could be occupied
for a duration of more than fifteen minutes at any time, but does
not include maintenance spaces. Occupiable outdoor spaces are located
adjacent to an indoor space and are considered to be an extension
of this indoor space: e.g. main entries, balconies, patios, decks,
green roofs and other public assembly areas. Although sidewalks and
driveways are mentioned in the provision, these areas are not considered
as occupiable outdoor spaces since they are used as transport routes
to and from the building, and people are not expected to remain there
for extended periods of time.

The requirements of [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part6.sect3.subsect3.art1.sent2:long] are not meant
to override similar requirements found in the installation standards
referenced in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part6.sect2.subsect1.art5:long] that address identical situations.

Piping carrying
steam, high-temperature hot water, or another heat transfer fluid
at high temperature is usually insulated to reduce heat losses as
an economy measure. Above a temperature of approximately 52°C (metric), however, a bare pipe can cause a burn to human skin coming in contact
with the pipe. According to [REF:standard:astmc1055] skin can be in contact with a surface at a temperature
of 52°C (metric) for up to 60 s (metric) without experiencing
irreversible damage. If pipes above this temperature
are normally out of reach of all persons other than maintenance personnel
or are properly guarded, it would be expected that no insulation would
be needed for public safety.

This Part applies to the design, construction, extension, [REF:term:ltrtn]alteration, renewal or repair of [REF:term:plmbng-t]plumbing systems.

content.text: Compliance with the British Columbia Building Code Book II (Plumbing Systems) may be achieved using alternative solutions as described in Clause 1.2.1.1.(1)(b) of Division A of this Code, using the objectives and functional statements attributed to the applicable acceptable solutions in Division B of the British Columbia Building Code Book II (Plumbing Systems).

parts.title: Safety Measures at Construction and Demolition Sites

content.text: The scope of this Part shall be as described in [REF:internal:nbc.divA.part1.sect3.subsect3:long].

This Part applies to fire safety and the protection of the public
during the construction, [REF:term:ltrtn]alteration or
demolition of every [REF:term:bldng]building, including
any incompleted or abandoned [REF:term:bldng]building.
Fire safety at construction and demolition sites shall conform to Section 5.6. of Division B of the British Columbia Fire Code.
Words that appear in italics are defined in [REF:internal:nbc.divA.part1.sect4.subsect1.art2:long].
Measures shall be taken during demolition to protect the public in conformance with Section 5.6. of Division B of the British Columbia Fire Code.

Where a [REF:term:bldng] building is undergoing construction, [REF:term:ltrtn]alteration  or demolition, measures shall be
taken at the [REF:term:bldng] building site in conformance
with this Code. (See [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part8.sect3.appnote1:short].)

Precautions shall be taken to ensure that no person is exposed
to undue risk.

Where the construction may constitute a hazard to the public,
work shall not commence on the construction, [REF:term:ltrtn]alteration or repair of a [REF:term:bldng]building until a covered
way has been provided as described in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part8.sect2.subsect1.art2:long] to
protect the public, except where

clauses.text: the work is done within a solid enclosure,

the [REF:term:bldng]building is at a distance of 2 m (metric) or more from a [REF:term:pblc-w]public way used
by pedestrians, or
site conditions warrant a distance greater than provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part8.sect2.subsect1.art1.sent1.clause2:short].

content.text: A covered way shall

clauses.text: have a clear height of not less than 2.5 m (metric),

have a clear width of not less than 1.5 m (metric) or the
width of the [REF:term:pblc-w]public way, whichever is
the lesser,

be designed and constructed to support safely all loads that
may be reasonably expected to be applied to it, but in no case less
than 2.4 kPa (metric) on the roof,

have a weathertight roof sloped towards the site or, if flat,
be equipped with a splash board not less than 300 mm (metric) high
on the [REF:term:trt]street side,

be totally enclosed on the site side with a structure having
a reasonably smooth surface facing the [REF:term:pblc-w]public
way,

have a railing 1 070 mm (metric) high on the [REF:term:trt]street side where the covered way is supported by posts on
the [REF:term:trt]street side, and
be adequately lighted when the [REF:term:pblc-w]public way is lighted.

content.text:
When a construction or demolition activity may constitute a
hazard to the public and is located 2 m (metric) or more from
a [REF:term:pblc-w]public way, a strongly constructed fence,
boarding or barricade not less than 1.8 m (metric) high shall
be erected between the site and the [REF:term:pblc-w]public way or open sides of a construction site.

Barricades shall have a reasonably smooth surface facing the [REF:term:pblc-w]public way and shall be without openings, except
those required for access.

Access openings through barricades shall be equipped with gates
that shall be

clauses.text: kept closed and locked when the site is unattended, and

maintained in place until completion of the construction or
demolition activity.

content.text:
Where any special hazard exists from which it is not possible
to protect the public by other means, persons shall be employed to
prevent the public from entering the danger zone at any time of the
day or night.

When work on a construction site is suspended or ceases so that
it will not be occupied during normal working hours, the hazardous
part of the construction site shall be protected by

clauses.text:
covering all windows, doors and other openings located within 3 m (metric) of the ground which may give access to the [REF:term:bldng]building with a securely fastened barricade,
or

a fence or barricade constructed according to the requirements
of [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part8.sect2.subsect1.art3:long]

content.text:
[REF:term:xcvtn]Excavations shall be kept reasonably
clear of water.

If the stability of adjoining [REF:term:bldng]buildings may be endangered by the work of excavating, adequate underpinning,
shoring and bracing shall be provided to prevent

clauses.text: damage to, or movement of, any part of the adjoining [REF:term:bldng]building, and
the creation of a hazard to the public.

subsections.title: Use of Streets or Public Property

content.text:
Except as provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part8.sect2.subsect3.art2:long], provisions
shall be made at all times for the safe passage of pedestrian and
vehicular traffic past the site.
Material or equipment shall not be placed on any [REF:term:trt]street or other public property except as authorized.

Except as provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part8.sect2.subsect3.art1.sent4:short], where a sidewalk exists adjacent to the site it shall be kept
clear of obstructions at all times.

Where construction operations necessitate the obstruction of
a sidewalk, a temporary sidewalk shall be provided and it shall be
kept clear of obstruction at all times.

Operations such as the hoisting of major components onto a tall [REF:term:bldng]building or other overhead activities that constitute
a hazard to pedestrians below from which the public cannot be protected
by barricades, covered ways or similar means shall not be carried
out until the [REF:term:trt]street or other [REF:term:pblc-w]public way is closed.
[REF:term:xcvtn]Excavations in [REF:term:trt]streets or public property shall

clauses.text: be adequately barricaded, and

have warning signs or lights installed on each section of the
barricades referred to in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part8.sect2.subsect3.art3.sent1.clause1:short].

content.text:
All sidewalks, [REF:term:trt]streets or other public
property that have been damaged shall be restored to a safe condition.

All obstructions on sidewalks, [REF:term:trt]streets or other public property shall be removed when the need for such
obstructions is ended.

Warning lights shall be placed and shall be in operation during
the hours of darkness at all obstructions on [REF:term:trt]streets or other [REF:term:pblc-w]public ways.

Where a hazard to vehicular traffic on a [REF:term:pblc-w]public way is created by work on a construction site, the
following shall be provided to direct the traffic:

clauses.text: one or more workers,
warning signs,
barriers,
lane control devices, or

flashing lights or flares located at a suitable distance from
the hazard.

content.text: A flag used to direct traffic shall be

clauses.text: red,
not less than 450 mm (metric) by 500 mm (metric),

mounted on a staff not less than 1 m (metric) long, with
the long side of the flag attached securely to the staff along its
entire length, and
maintained in a clean and untorn condition when being used.

content.text: A sign used to direct traffic shall be

clauses.text: diamond-shaped and of material not less rigid than 6 mm (metric) thick plywood,

not less than 450 mm (metric) by 450 mm (metric) in
size and mounted at one corner on a substantial pole not less than 1.2 m (metric) long,

red on one side with black corner areas so that the red area
is a regular 8-sided figure, and with the word “STOP” or “ARRÊT” in
clearly distinguishable white letters not less than 150 mm (metric) high located centrally on the sign,

yellow on the other side with the word “SLOW” or “LENTEMENT”
in clearly distinguishable black letters not less than 150 mm (metric) high located centrally on the sign, or symbols recognized by the
International Traffic Code, and
maintained in a clean condition when being used.

content.text: A worker who is directing traffic shall

clauses.text: be equipped as required by [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part8.sect2.subsect4.art5:long],
be instructed in the signals to be used in controlling traffic,

be provided with a copy of written instructions on the correct
methods for traffic direction, and
direct traffic by using either a flag or sign.

content.text:
A worker while directing traffic shall wear the following clothing
which shall be fluorescent and coloured either blaze orange or red:

clauses.text: a vest, or
sleeves that extend from above the elbow to the wrist.

content.text:
Waste material or other material shall not be permitted to fall
freely from one [REF:term:tr]storey to another.

Waste material shall be removed as quickly as possible by means
of

clauses.text: appropriate containers,
an enclosed shaft or chute conforming to [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part8.sect2.subsect5.art4.sent1:long], or
a hoisting apparatus if large pieces or objects are involved.

content.text: Waste material cleared as provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part8.sect2.subsect5.art2.sent1:long] shall be deposited in an enclosure

clauses.text:
so arranged as to prevent waste material from being projected
beyond the confines of the enclosure, and
not accessible to the public.

content.text:
The chute described in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part8.sect2.subsect5.art2.sent1.clause2:long] shall be
closed if it is inclined more than 45° to the horizontal.

For the purpose of compliance with this Code as required in [REF:internal:nbc.divA.part1.sect2.subsect1.art1.sent1.clause2:long], the objectives and functional statements
attributed to the acceptable solutions in this Part shall be the objectives
and functional statements listed in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part8.sect3.subsect1.art1.table1:long] (See [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part1.sect3.appnote1:long].)

The use
of streets or public property and vehicular traffic during construction
or demolition is normally controlled by regulations of authorities

content.text: The scope of this Part shall be as described in [REF:internal:nbc.divA.part1.sect3.subsect3:long] of Division A.
The application of this Part shall be as described in [REF:internal:nbc.divA.part1.sect3.subsect3:long] of Division A.

content.text: Where a [REF:term:bldng]building contains one or more [REF:term:mjr-ccpn]major occupancies listed in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part10.sect2.subsect3:long], those [REF:term:mjr-ccpn]major occupancies shall conform to the requirements of any of Steps 2 to 4, as described in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part10.sect2.subsect3.art2.sent3:long], and where the [REF:term:bldng]building contains [REF:term:mjr-ccpn]major occupancies not listed in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part10.sect2.subsect3:long], those remaining [REF:term:mjr-ccpn]major occupancies shall comply with Clause (1)(a) or (b).

Notwithstanding Article 1.1.1.1. of Division A of the NECB, where a [REF:term:bldng]building or [REF:term:mjr-ccpn]major occupancy designed and constructed to conform to any version of [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part10.sect2.subsect3:long] is altered, rehabilitated, renovated, or there is a change in [REF:term:ccpnc]occupancy, the energy performance of the [REF:term:ltrtn]alteration, rehabilitation, renovation, or change in [REF:term:ccpnc]occupancy, shall comply [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part10.sect2.subsect2.art1.sent1.clause2:medium] or [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part10.sect2.subsect2.art1.sent1.clause3:short].

This Subsection applies to [REF:term:bldng]buildings containing any of the following [REF:term:mjr-ccpn]major occupancies:

clauses.text: [REF:term:ssmbl]assembly, as described in Tables 10.2.3.3.-A, 10.2.3.3.-B, 10.2.3.3.-C and 10.2.3.3.-D,

content.text: For the purpose of this Subsection, the term "total energy use intensity" (TEUI) shall mean a metric of the energy used over a year by the [REF:term:bldng]building, estimated by using an energy model in accordance with [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part10.sect2.subsect3.art4:long], normalized per square metre of floor area of [REF:term:cndtnd-spc]conditioned space and expressed in kWh/m^{2}/year, for all of the following combined:

clauses.text: space-heating equipment,
space-cooling equipment,
fans,
interior and exterior lighting devices,
service water heating equipment,
pumps,
auxiliary HVAC equipment,
receptacle loads and miscellaneous equipment,
appliances, and
elevators and escalators.

content.text: For the purpose of this Subsection, the term "thermal energy demand intensity" (TEDI) shall mean a metric of the annual heating required by the [REF:term:bldng]building for space conditioning and for conditioning of ventilation air, estimated by using an energy model in accordance with [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part10.sect2.subsect3.art4:long], normalized per square metre of floor area of [REF:term:cndtnd-spc]conditioned space and expressed in kWh/m^{2}/year, taking into account all of the following:

clauses.text: thermal transmittance of above-ground walls and roof-ceiling assemblies,
thermal transmittance of floors and walls in contact with the ground, or space that is not [REF:term:cndtnd-spc]conditioned space,
thermal transmittance and solar heat gain of windows, doors and skylights,
air leakage through the [REF:term:r-brrr-ss]air barrier system,
internal heat gains from occupants and equipment, and
heat recovery from exhaust ventilation.

content.text: For the purpose of this Subsection, the term "Step" shall mean a Step referred to in Tables 10.2.3.3.-A to 10.2.3.3.-J.

[REF:term:bldng]Buildings and [REF:term:mjr-ccpn]major occupancies conforming to the requirements of any of Steps 2 to 4 shall be designed and constructed to conform to the applicable energy performance requirements in Tables 10.2.3.3.-A to 10.2.3.3.-J
Except as permitted by Sentence (3),

clauses.text: energy performance shall be calculated in conformance with Article 10.2.3.4., and
airtightness shall be tested in accordance with Article 10.2.3.5.

content.text: [REF:term:bldng]Buildings and [REF:term:mjr-ccpn]major occupancies designed and constructed to conform to Step 4 of Tables 10.2.3.3.-G to 10.2.3.3.-H or to Step 3 in Tables 10.2.3.3.-I and 10.2.3.3.-J, and to the Passive House Planning Package, version 9 or newer, are deemed to comply with this Subsection provided the energy model according to which the [REF:term:bldng]building or the [REF:term:mjr-ccpn]major occupancy of the [REF:term:bldng]building is designed and constructed is prepared by a Certified Passive House Designer, or Certified Passive House Consultant, who is approved by the Passive House Institute.
