content.text: Except as permitted by [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part10.sect2.subsect3.art4.sent3:short], energy modelling for [REF:term:bldng]buildings and [REF:term:mjr-ccpn]major occupancies conforming to the requirements of any of Steps 2 to 4 shall account for the air leakage rate derived in accordance with [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part10.sect2.subsect3.art5:long].

Until the air leakage rate determined by [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part10.sect2.subsect3.art4.sent2:short] is available, an air leakage rate determined in accordance with the City of Vancouver Energy Modelling Guidelines shall be used.
In case of conflict between the provisions of the NECB and the City of Vancouver Energy Modelling Guidelines, the provisions of the City of Vancouver Energy Modelling Guidelines shall govern.

Except as required by [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part10.sect2.subsect3.art5.sent2:short], [REF:term:bldng]buildings and [REF:term:mjr-ccpn]major occupancies shall be tested for airtightness in accordance with

clauses.text: ASTM E 779, "Standard Test Method for Determining Air Leakage Rate by Fan Pressurization",
USACE Version 3, "Air Leakage Test Protocol for Building Envelopes", or

content.text: [REF:term:bldng]Buildings and [REF:term:mjr-ccpn]major occupancies shall be tested for airtightness to an induced test pressure of not less than 75 Pa.
The requirements of this Section apply only to [REF:term:bldng]buildings that

clauses.text: contain any of the following major occupancies as described in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part10.sect3.subsect1.art3.table1:long]:

content.text: Modeling of greenhouse gas emissions shall conform to the City of Vancouver Energy Modeling Guidelines.
For the purposes of this Section, the term "greenhouse gas", expressed with the abbreviation "GHG", shall have the same meaning as defined in the Climate Change Accountability Act.

For the purposes of this Section, the term "greenhouse gas intensity", expressed with the abbreviation "GHGI", shall mean the total greenhouse gas emissions, expressed as kgCO_{2e} per square metre of floor area of [REF:term:cndtnd-spc]conditioned space per year, associated with the energy used by the [REF:term:bldng]building's systems.

For the purposes of this Section, the symbol "CO_{2e}" shall mean carbon dioxide or carbon dioxide equivalent, with carbon dioxide equivalent meaning one or more greenhouse gases with a global warming potential equivalent to carbon dioxide.
For the purposes of this Section, the term "Emissions Level" shall mean an Emissions Level referred to in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part10.sect3.subsect1.art3.table1:long].

For the purposes of this Section, the term "measure only" shall mean that the GHGI and the total greenhouse gases are calculated, as applicable, and the values reported in accordance with Subsection 2.2.8. of Division C.

revisions.text: [REF:term:bldng]Buildings conforming to the requirements of any of GHG Emission Levels EL-1 to EL-4 shall be designed and constructed to conform to [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part10.sect3.subsect1.art3.table1:long] based on [REF:term:ccpnc]occupancy.

[REF:term:bldng]Buildings shall conform to the requirements of any of GHG Emission Levels EL-1, EL-2, EL-3 or EL-4 and shall be designed and constructed to conform to Table 10.3.1.3. based on [REF:term:ccpnc]occupancy.

application_notes.title: Energy Requirements for Alterations to Buildings and Major Occupancies

paragraphs.content: Alterations, rehabilitation, renovations and changes of occupancy to existing [REF:term:bldng]buildings or [REF:term:mjr-ccpn]major occupancies that were originally designed and constructed to previous editions of the ANSI/ASHRAE/IES 90.1 standard are to comply with the edition of the ANSI/ASHRAE/IES 90.1 standard referenced in this Code, or the requirements of [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part10.sect2.subsect3:long]. Alterations, rehabilitation, renovations and changes of occupancy to existing [REF:term:bldng]buildings or [REF:term:mjr-ccpn]major occupancies that were originally designed and constructed to previous editions of the NECB or [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part10.sect2.subsect3:long] are to comply with the edition of the NECB referenced in this Code, or to [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part10.sect2.subsect3:long]. Existing [REF:term:bldng]buildings or [REF:term:mjr-ccpn]major occupancies that were not designed and constructed to any version of the ANSI/ASHRAE/IES 90.1 standard, the NECB or [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part10.sect2.subsect3:long], may use the edition of the ANSI/ASHRAE/IES 90.1 standard or the NECB referenced in this Code, or [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part10.sect2.subsect3:long] for alterations, rehabilitation, renovations and changes in occupancy.

[REF:internal:nbc.divA.part1.sect1.subsect1.art2.sent1:long] of Division A states that the level of [REF:term:bldng]building performance shall not be decreased below a level that already exists. For example, a new [REF:term:ccpnc]occupancy may be permitted a higher lighting power density by the ANSI/ASHRAE/IES 90.1 standard or the NECB than the lighting power density that was permitted for a previous [REF:term:ccpnc]occupancy. This does not constitute a decrease in the level of [REF:term:bldng]building performance, provided the design meets the minimum requirements of the relevant Code or standard.
TEDI does not include receptacle loads and energy use from unusual uses such as spas and computer server rooms.

Although the total energy use intensity and thermal energy demand intensity are not required for NECB conformance, they must still be calculated in conformance with [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part10.sect3.subsect1.art4:long] and reported in accordance with Subsection 2.2.9. of Division C.
<bold>Energy Model Calculations for Steps 2 to 4</bold>

Notwithstanding the requirements of Part 8 of the NECB, a reference [REF:term:bldng]building and [REF:term:bldng]building energy target are not required for compliance with the requirements of Steps 2 to 4 in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part10.sect2.subsect3.art3:long]. The performance requirements of Tables 10.2.3.3.-A. to 10.2.3.3.-J. are used to determine compliance.
<bold>Air Leakage Rate in Energy Model Calculations</bold>

The requirement to account for the air leakage rate as tested in all energy model calculations supersedes the NECB air leakage rate requirements. For [REF:term:bldng]buildings that must conform to the requirements of any of Steps 2 to 4, higher than expected air leakage may require the [REF:term:bldng]building design to be altered and the energy model calculations to be repeated. Alternatively, the air leakage rate could be retested after making alterations to the air barrier system to attain the desired air leakage rate.
<bold>Air Leakage Rate</bold>

Section 2.4. of the City of Vancouver's Energy Modelling Guidelines provides guidance on determining infiltration/air leakage rates for [REF:term:bldng]buildings conforming with [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part10.sect2.subsect3:long] at the design stage.
The intent of this testing is to quantify the airtightness level of the air barrier system, not airtightness of the [REF:term:bldng]building at in-service operating conditions.

content.text: This Part applies to all [REF:term:bldng]buildings covered in this Code. (See [REF:internal:nbc.divA.part1.sect1.subsect1.art1:long].)

Words and phrases used in Division C that are not included in
the list of definitions in [REF:internal:nbc.divA.part1.sect4.subsect1.art2:long] shall have the meanings that are commonly assigned to them in the
context in which they are used, taking into account the specialized
use of terms by the various trades and professions to which the terminology
applies.

Where objectives and functional statements are referred to in
Division C, they shall be the objectives and functional statements
described in Parts 2 and 3 of Division A.

Where acceptable solutions are referred to in Division C, they
shall be the provisions stated in Parts 2 to 9 of Division B.

Where alternative solutions are referred to in Division C, they
shall be the alternative solutions mentioned in [REF:internal:nbc.divA.part1.sect2.subsect1.art1.sent1.clause2:long].

The words and terms in italics in Division C shall have the
meanings assigned to them in [REF:internal:nbc.divA.part1.sect4.subsect1.art2:long].

The symbols and other abbreviations in Division C shall have
the meanings assigned to them in [REF:internal:nbc.divA.part1.sect4.subsect2.art1:long].
This Part applies to all [REF:term:bldng]buildings covered in this Code. (See [REF:internal:nbc.divA.part1.sect1.subsect1.art1:long].)

This Code shall be administered in conformance with the appropriate
provincial or territorial regulations, municipal bylaws or, in the
absence of such regulations or bylaws, in conformance with the Administrative
Requirements for Use with the National Building Code of Canada 1985.

For design carried out in accordance with Part 4 of Division
B, the [REF:term:dgnr]designer shall be a professional
engineer or architect skilled in the work concerned. (See [REF:internal:nbc.divC.part2.sect3.appnote1:short].)

Sufficient information shall be provided to show that the proposed
work will conform to this Code and whether or not it may affect adjacent
property.

Plans shall be drawn to scale and shall indicate the nature
and extent of the work or proposed [REF:term:ccpnc]occupancy in sufficient detail to establish  that, when completed, the work
and the proposed [REF:term:ccpnc]occupancy will conform
to this Code.

When proposed work is changed during construction, information
on the changes shall comply with the requirements of this Section
for proposed work.

Site plans shall be referenced to an up-to-date survey and,
when required to prove compliance with this Code, a copy of the survey
shall be provided.
Site plans shall show

clauses.text: by dimensions from property lines, the location of the proposed [REF:term:bldng]building,
the similarly dimensioned location of every adjacent existing [REF:term:bldng]building on the property,

existing and finished ground levels to an established datum
at or adjacent to the site, and
the access routes for firefighting.

articles.title: Information Required for Fire Protection Components

content.text:
Information shall be submitted to show the major components
of fire protection including

clauses.text: the division of the [REF:term:bldng]building by [REF:term:frwll]firewalls,
the [REF:term:bldng-r]building area,

the degree of [REF:term:fr-prtn]fire separation of [REF:term:tr]storeys, shafts and special rooms or areas, including
the location and rating of [REF:term:clr]closures in [REF:term:fr-prtn]fire separations,

the source of information for [REF:term:fr-rtnc-]fire-resistance
ratings of elements of construction (to be indicated on large-scale
sections),

the source of information
for [REF:term:ncps-rtng]encapsulation ratings of mass timber
elements of construction (to be indicated on large-scale sections),
the location of [REF:term:xt]exits, and
fire detection, suppression and alarm systems.

content.text:
Before a sprinkler system is installed or altered, plans showing
full details of the proposed sprinkler system and essential details
of the [REF:term:bldng]building in which it is to be installed
shall be drawn to an indicated scale.

subsections.title: Structural and Foundation Drawings and Calculations

content.text: This Subsection applies only to [REF:term:bldng]buildings covered in Part 4 of Division B. (See [REF:internal:nbc.divA.part1.sect3.subsect3.art2:long].)

articles.title: Professional Seal and Signature of Designer

content.text:
Structural drawings and related documents submitted with the
application to build shall be dated and shall bear the authorized
professional seal and signature of the [REF:term:dgnr]designer as defined in [REF:internal:nbc.divC.part2.sect2.subsect1.art2.sent1:long].

Structural drawings and related documents submitted with the
application to build shall indicate, in addition to those items specified
in [REF:internal:nbc.divC.part2.sect2.subsect4.art6:long] and in Part 4 of Division B applicable
to the specific material,

clauses.text:
the name and address of the person responsible for the structural
design,

the date of issue of the Code and standards to which the design
conforms,

the dimensions, location and size of all structural members
in sufficient detail to enable the design to be checked,
sufficient detail to enable the [REF:term:dd-ld]dead loads to be determined,
all effects and loads, other than [REF:term:dd-ld]dead loads, used for the design of the structural members and exterior cladding, and

the Importance
Category of the [REF:term:bldng]building.

content.text:
Structural drawings of parts or components including [REF:term:guard]guards designed by a person other than the [REF:term:dgnr]designer of the [REF:term:bldng]building shall be dated and shall bear the authorized professional seal and
signature of the [REF:term:dgnr]designer of such parts
or components.

The calculations and analysis made in the design of the structural
members, including parts and components, of a [REF:term:bldng]building shall be available for inspection upon request.

[REF:term:fndtn]Foundation  drawings submitted with
the application to build or excavate shall be provided to indicate

clauses.text:
the type and condition of the [REF:term:l]soil or [REF:term:rck]rock, as well as the [REF:term:grndwtr]groundwater conditions, as determined by the [REF:term:brfc-nvt]subsurface
investigation,

the factored bearing pressures on the [REF:term:l]soil or [REF:term:rck]rock, the factored loads when applicable
and the design loads applied to [REF:term:fndtn-nt]foundation
units, and

the earth pressures and other loads applied to the supporting
structures of supported [REF:term:xcvtn]excavations.

content.text:
When required, evidence that justifies the information on the
drawings shall be submitted with the application to excavate or build.

Where conditions as described under [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect2.subsect2.art4.sent1:long]
                           [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect2.subsect2.art4.sent2:short] are encountered, or where [REF:term:fndtn-nt] foundation
units or their locations are altered, this information shall
be recorded on appropriate drawings or new “as constructed” drawings.

articles.title: Information Required on Drawings and Specifications

content.text:
Information shown on drawings and in specifications shall be

The [REF:term:dgnr]designer or another suitably qualified
person shall review the construction of any [REF:term:bldng]building or part thereof to determine conformance with the design.

The [REF:term:dgnr]designer or another suitably qualified
person shall review all shop drawings and other related documents
relevant to the design to determine conformance with the design.

Workmanship, materials and all reports of material tests shall
be reviewed by the [REF:term:dgnr]designer or another suitably
qualified person during the process of construction.

Where a [REF:term:bldng]building or component of
a [REF:term:bldng]building is assembled off the [REF:term:bldng]building site in such a manner that it cannot

When reviewing construction dimensions related to commonly available [REF:term:bldng]building components and materials, the [REF:term:dgnr]designer or another suitably qualified person
shall consider that the prescriptive metric values in the Code may
have been converted and rounded from imperial values.

content.text:

shall include

clauses.text:
the effective thermal resistance values and  respective areas
of all opaque [REF:term:bldng]building envelope assemblies,
including all above-ground and below-ground roof/ceiling, wall, and
floor assemblies,

the overall thermal transmittance (U-value), solar heat gain
coefficient and respective areas of all fenestration and door components,

the ratio of total vertical fenestration and door area to gross
wall area,

the performance rating, energy source, and types of all equipment
required for space-heating and -cooling and service water heating,
the design basis for the ventilation rates,

where a test is used to determine the airtightness of a house,
the measured airtightness of the [REF:term:bldng]building envelope in air changes per hour, and

any additional features used in the energy model calculations
that account for a significant difference in house energy performance.

content.text:
The effective thermal resistance values and respective areas
of opaque [REF:term:bldng]building envelope assemblies
that cover less than 2% of the total area of their respective assembly
type need not be provided in the drawings and specifications required
in [REF:internal:nbc.divC.part2.sect2.subsect8.art2.sent1:short].

Where part-load characteristics are used in the modeling of
the HVAC equipment, they need not be provided in the drawings and
specifications required in [REF:internal:nbc.divC.part2.sect2.subsect8.art2.sent1:short].

The features of the proposed house that differ from those of
the reference house shall be detailed in the specifications required
in [REF:internal:nbc.divC.part2.sect2.subsect8.art2.sent1:short].

A house performance compliance calculation report shall be provided
in accordance with [REF:internal:nbc.divC.part2.sect2.subsect8.art3.sent2:short] for each
proposed house design.

In addition to the drawings and specifications required in [REF:internal:nbc.divC.part2.sect2.subsect8.art2:long], the house performance compliance calculation report
shall include

clauses.text: a project information section containing

a description of the project,
the address of the project,
the name and version of the calculation tool,

the geographic region in which the proposed house is to be built,
and
the identifier for the climatic data set used for analysis,

clauses.text:
a summary of the characteristics of the [REF:term:bldng]building envelope, HVAC system and service water heating system
reflecting the information provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divC.part2.sect2.subsect8.art2:long],
an energy performance data summary containing

subclauses.text:
the annual energy consumption of all energy sources calculated
for the proposed house (see [REF:internal:nbc.divC.part2.sect3.appnote5:short]), and

the house energy target of all energy sources calculated for
the reference house,

clauses.text: where a software program is used to determine compliance,

subclauses.text: the name of the software program(s), and

a list of any adaptations made by the user to the software relating
to input or output values, and

clauses.text:
a statement that the calculation was performed in compliance
with [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect5:long].

content.text:
Documentation conforming to this Subsection shall be provided
by the person requesting the use of an alternative solution to demonstrate
that the proposed alternative solution complies with this Code.
The documentation referred to in [REF:internal:nbc.divC.part2.sect3.subsect1.art1.sent1:short] shall include

clauses.text:
a Code analysis outlining the analytical methods and rationales
used to determine that a proposed alternative solution will achieve
at least the level of performance required by [REF:internal:nbc.divA.part1.sect2.subsect1.art1.sent1.clause2:long], and

information concerning any special maintenance or operational
requirements, including any [REF:term:bldng]building component
commissioning requirements, that are necessary for the alternative
solution to achieve compliance with the Code after the [REF:term:bldng]building is constructed.

content.text:
The Code analysis referred to in [REF:internal:nbc.divC.part2.sect3.subsect1.art1.sent2.clause1:medium] shall identify the applicable objectives, functional
statements and acceptable solutions, and any assumptions, limiting
or restricting factors, testing procedures, engineering studies or [REF:term:bldng]building performance parameters that will support
a Code compliance assessment.

The Code analysis referred to in [REF:internal:nbc.divC.part2.sect3.subsect1.art1.sent2.clause1:medium] shall include information about the qualifications,
experience and background of the person or persons taking responsibility
for the design.

The information provided under [REF:internal:nbc.divC.part2.sect3.subsect1.art1.sent3:short] shall be in sufficient detail to convey the design
intent and to support the validity, accuracy, relevance and precision
of the Code analysis.

Where the design of a [REF:term:bldng]building includes
proposed alternative solutions that involve more than one person taking
responsibility for different aspects of the design, the applicant
for the permit shall identify a single person to co-ordinate the preparation
of the design, Code analysis and documentation referred to in this
Subsection.

application_notes.title:
Information Required on Drawings
and Specifications

paragraphs.content:
Examples of information that should
be shown on architectural drawings and drawings for heating, ventilating
and air-conditioning systems are:
                        the name, type and location of the building,
                        the name of the owner,
                        the name of the architect,
                        the name of the engineer or designer,
                        the north point,
                        the dimensions and height of all rooms,
                        the intended use of all rooms,
                        the details or description of the wall, roof, ceiling and
floor construction, including insulation,
                        the details or description of the windows and outside doors,
including the size, weatherstripping, storm sashes, sills and storm
doors,
                        the size and continuity of all pipes, ducts, shafts, flues
and fire dampers,
                        the location, size, capacity and type of all principal units
of equipment,
                        the size, shape and height of all chimneys and gas vents,
                        the size and location of all combustion air and ventilation
openings, and
                        the location and fire-resistance rating of required fire
separations.

For the 1977 edition of the NBC, most imperial values in the
Code were converted to metric values. A document entitled “Metric
Values for Use with the National Building Code 1977,” published by
the NRC Associate Committee on the National Building Code, lists all
of the metric values and provides some commentary on the rationale
applied in the conversion process.

As explained in this document, the metric values of dimensions
were “rounded off to the greatest extent possible, consistent with
the sensitivity of the particular dimension to the standard of safety
to be achieved.” For more sensitive dimensions, such as heights of
handrails and guards, headroom clearances and design loads, the metric
values were rounded to a higher precision.

Dimensions dependent on product sizes were generally converted
to a metric approximation of the imperial values, a process referred
to as “soft” conversion. In many instances, the factor used to convert
inches to millimetres was taken as 25 mm (metric) instead of 25.4 mm (metric), the exact conversion factor. The resulting soft conversions
were 1.6% smaller than the corresponding exact conversions. Therefore,
the soft conversion process frequently led to metric values that were
somewhat different in magnitude from the original imperial values.

When reviewing workmanship, materials or construction for compliance
with the Code, for any measurement related to commonly available building
components and materials, the designer or another suitably qualified
person must consider the imperial value that formed the basis for
the original prescriptive requirement.

For instance, the metric values given for the spacing between
framing members are soft conversions, rather than exact conversions
of the original imperial values. However, it remains common construction
practice to arrange joists, rafters and studs in 12, 16 or 24
in. (metric) increments so as to properly align them with the edges
of sheathing materials. It is, therefore, assumed that framing members
will be spaced according to the exact metric equivalents as shown
for the examples in the following table.

The person conducting the review should also consider reasonable
construction tolerances and the inherent accuracy of their measurement
device. Furthermore, consideration should be given to the implied
tolerance of the original imperial value. For example, where the Code
originally specified framing member spacings as 12, 16 and 24
in. (metric) on centre, an acceptable tolerance of ± 0.5 in. (metric) is implied by the position of the last significant digit in the
imperial values. The corresponding acceptable tolerance for the metric
values would be ± 12.7 mm (metric).

Although the word “house” is used in the terms “proposed house,”
“reference house” and “house performance compliance calculation report”
in [REF:internal:nbc.divC.part2.sect2.subsect8:long], it is intended to include other
types of residential buildings also addressed by [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect5:long]. The terms “proposed building,” “reference
building” and “building performance compliance calculation report”
used in the [REF:standard:nrcc-necb] apply to other types of buildings.

The performance compliance calculation method detailed in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect5:long] uses a number of assumptions
regarding environmental values and operating conditions in order to
standardize the calculations and neutralize the impact of occupant
behaviour or to exclude issues that are not addressed in the requirements.
Note that the result of the energy model calculations is not a prediction
of the actual energy consumption of the proposed house.

Beyond the purposes of demonstrating compliance and acquiring
a building permit, there are other important reasons for requiring
that the proponent of an alternative solution submit project documentation
(i.e. a compliance report) to the authority having jurisdiction and
for the authority having jurisdiction to retain that documentation
for a substantial period following the construction of a building:
                        Most jurisdictions require that a building be maintained
in compliance with the codes under which it was built. Alternative
solutions made possible by objective-based codes may have special
maintenance requirements, which would be described in the documentation.
                        Documentation helps consultants perform code compliance
assessments of existing buildings before they are sold and informs
current owners or prospective buyers of existing buildings of any
limitations pertaining to their future use or development.
                        Documentation provides design professionals with the basic
information necessary to design changes to an existing building.
                        An alternative solution could be invalidated by a proposed
alteration to a building. Designers and regulators must therefore
know the details of the particular alternative solutions that were
integral to the original design. Complete documentation should provide
insight as to why one alternative solution was chosen over another.
                        Documentation is the “paper trail” of the alternative solution
negotiated between the designer and the regulator and should demonstrate
that a rational process led to the acceptance of the alternative solution
as an equivalency.
                        It is possible that over time a particular alternative solution
may be shown to be inadequate. It would be advantageous for a jurisdiction
to know which buildings included that alternative solution as part
of their design: documentation will facilitate this type of analysis.
                        Project documentation provides important information to
a forensic team that is called to investigate an accident or why a
design failed to provide the level of performance expected.

This subject is discussed in further detail in “Recommended
Documentation Requirements for Projects Using Alternative Solutions
in the Context of Objective-Based Codes,” which was prepared for the
CCBFC Task Group on Implementation of Objective-Based Codes and is
available on the NRC's website.

content.text:
Where a [REF:term:l]soil or [REF:term:rck]rock within a distance equal to twice the footing width below the [REF:term:brng-rfc]bearing surface has a lower allowable bearing
pressure than that at the [REF:term:brng-rfc]bearing surface as shown in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect4.subsect4.art1:long], the design capacity of
the [REF:term:fndtn]foundation shall not be greater than

In calculating subsurface pressures referred to in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect4.subsect4.art2.sent1:short], the loads from the footings shall
be assumed to be distributed uniformly over a horizontal plane within
a frustum extending downward from the footing at an angle of 60° (metric) to the horizontal.

sand or silt, and the water table is within a distance below the [REF:term:brng-rfc]bearing surface equal to the width of the [REF:term:fndtn]foundation, the allowable bearing pressure shall

oxidation is known to occur to the extent that it will damage a [REF:term:bldng]building, measures shall be taken to preclude

affected. (See [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.appnote14:short].)

Except for stairs within a [REF:term:dwllng-n]dwelling unit, at least 3 risers shall be provided in interior [REF:term:flght]flights.
The vertical height of any [REF:term:flght]flight of stairs shall not exceed 3.7 m (metric).

Except for stairs serving areas only used as [REF:term:rvc-rm]service
rooms or [REF:term:rvc-pc]service spaces, the rise,
which is measured as the vertical nosing-to-nosing distance, shall
comply with [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect8.subsect4.art1.table1:long]

content.title: Rise for Rectangular Treads, Tapered Treads and Winders

body_rows.content:
PrivatePrivate stairs are exterior and interior stairs that serve
                                          single [REF:term:dwllng-n]dwelling units,
                                          houses with a [REF:term:scnd-t]secondary suite including their common spaces, or
                                          garages that serve houses described in Clause a) or b).

PublicPublic stairs are all stairs not described as service stairs or private
stairs.

content.text: Except for stairs serving areas only used as [REF:term:rvc-rm]service rooms or [REF:term:rvc-pc]service spaces, the [REF:term:run]run shall comply with [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect8.subsect4.art2.table1:long]

content.title: Run for Rectangular Treads

body_rows.content:
PrivatePrivate stairs are exterior and interior stairs that serve
                                          single [REF:term:dwllng-n]dwelling units,
                                          houses with a [REF:term:scnd-t]secondary suite including their common spaces, or
                                          garages that serve houses described in Clause a) or b).

PublicPublic stairs are all stairs not described as service stairs
or private stairs.

content.text: The depth of a rectangular tread shall be not less than its [REF:term:run]run and not more than its [REF:term:run]run plus 25 mm (metric).
Except as provided in Sentence (3) and Article 9.8.4.6., [REF:term:tpr-thr]tapered treads shall have a [REF:term:run]run that

clauses.text: is not less than 150 mm at the narrow end of the tread, and

complies with the dimensions stated in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect8.subsect4.art2.table1:long] when measured at a point 300 mm (metric) from the centre line
 of the handrail at the narrow end of the tread.

content.text: [REF:term:tpr-thr]Tapered treads in required [REF:term:xt]exit stairs shall conform to the requirements in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect4.subsect6.art9:long]

The depth of a [REF:term:tpr-thr]tapered tread shall
be not less than its [REF:term:run]run at any point and
not more than its [REF:term:run]run at any point plus 25 mm (metric).

articles.title: Uniformity and Tolerances for Risers, Runs and Treads

content.text: Except as provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect8.subsect4.art4.sent2:short], risers shall be of uniform height in any one [REF:term:flght]flight, with a maximum tolerance of

clauses.text: 5 mm (metric) between adjacent treads or landings, and

10 mm (metric) between the tallest and shortest risers in
a [REF:term:flght]flight.

content.text:
Except for required [REF:term:xt]exit stairs, where
the top or bottom riser in a stair adjoins a sloping finished walking
surface, such as a garage floor, driveway or sidewalk, the height
of the riser across the stair shall vary by not more than 1
in 12 (metric).
Rectangular treads shall have a uniform [REF:term:run]run with a maximum tolerance of

clauses.text: 5 mm (metric) between adjacent treads, and

10 mm (metric) between the deepest and shallowest treads
in a [REF:term:flght]flight.

content.text:
[REF:term:tpr-thr]Tapered treads in a [REF:term:flght]flight shall have a uniform [REF:term:run]run in accordance with the construction tolerances stipulated
in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect8.subsect4.art4.sent3:short] when measured at a point 300 mm (metric) from the centre line of the handrail as described in Sentence 9.8.7.1.(5).
The slope of treads shall not exceed 1 in 50 (metric).
Individual treads in winders shall turn through an angle of

clauses.text: 30° with no deviation above or below 30°, or
45° with no deviation above or below 45°.

content.text:
Where winders are incorporated into a stair, each set shall
not turn through more than 90°.

Treads in winders shall have a [REF:term:run]run, measured at a point 200 mm (metric) from the narrow end of the tread, conforming to the minimum [REF:term:run]run requirements for a private stair in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect8.subsect4.art2.table1:long].

Except as permitted by [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect8.subsect4.art8.sent2:short], the top of the nosings of stair treads shall have a rounded or
beveled edge extending not less than 6 mm (metric) and not more
than 14 mm (metric) measured horizontally from the front of the
nosing.

If resilient material is used to cover the nosing of a stair
tread, the minimum extension of the rounded or beveled edge required
by [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect8.subsect4.art8.sent1:short] is permitted to be reduced
to 3 mm (metric).
Except as provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect8.subsect4.art9.sent2:short], stairs shall have no open risers.
Open risers are permitted in

clauses.text: interior and exterior stairs that serve a single [REF:term:dwllng-n]dwelling unit or a house with a [REF:term:scnd-t]secondary suite,
fire escape stairs,
stairs that are principally used for maintenance,

stairs that serve [REF:term:rvc-rm]service rooms,
and
stairs that serve [REF:term:ndtrl-cc]industrial occupancies other than [REF:term:trg-grg]storage garages.

content.text: This Subsection applies to pedestrian [REF:term:rmp]ramps, except [REF:term:rmp]ramps in an accessible path of travel.
[REF:term:rmp]Ramps in an accessible path of travel shall conform to the requirements in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect8.subsect3.art5:long]

Except as provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect8.subsect5.art2.sent2:short], [REF:term:rmp]ramps shall be not less than 1
100 mm (metric) wide.

[REF:term:rmp]Ramps serving a single [REF:term:dwllng-n]dwelling unit or a house with a [REF:term:scnd-t]secondary suite including their common spaces
shall be not less than 860 mm (metric) wide.

Except as permitted by [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect8.subsect5.art3.sent2:short], the clear height over [REF:term:rmp]ramps shall be
not less than 2 050 mm (metric).

The clear height over [REF:term:rmp]ramps serving
a single [REF:term:dwllng-n]dwelling unit or a house with
a [REF:term:scnd-t]secondary suite including their common
spaces shall be not less than 1 950 mm (metric).

The slope of [REF:term:rmp]ramps shall be not more
than

clauses.text: 1 in 10 for exterior [REF:term:rmp]ramps,
1 in 10 for interior [REF:term:rmp]ramps serving [REF:term:rdntl-cc]residential occupancies,
1 in 6 for [REF:term:ndtrl-cc]industrial occupancies, and
1 in 8 for all other [REF:term:ccpnc]occupancies.

content.text:
Where the slope of the [REF:term:rmp]ramp is greater
than 1 in 12, the maximum rise between floors or landings shall be 1 500 mm (metric).
This Subsection applies to landings, except landings for [REF:term:rmp]ramps in an accessible path of travel.

Landings for [REF:term:rmp]ramps in an accessible path of travel shall conform to
the requirements in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect8.subsect3.art5:long]
Finished floors, and ground surfaces with a slope not exceeding 1 in 50 (metric), at the top and bottom of stairs or [REF:term:rmp]ramps shall be considered as landings.

Except as provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect8.subsect6.art2.sent2:short]
                           [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect8.subsect6.art2.sent4:short] and [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect9.subsect6.art6.sent2:long], a landing shall be
provided

clauses.text: at the top and bottom of each [REF:term:flght]flight of interior and exterior stairs, including stairs in garages,
at the top and bottom of every [REF:term:rmp]ramp with a slope greater than 1 in 50,
where a doorway opens onto a stair or [REF:term:rmp]ramp,
where a [REF:term:rmp]ramp opens onto a stair, and
where a stair opens onto a [REF:term:rmp]ramp.

content.text:
Where a door at the top of a stair within a [REF:term:dwllng-n]dwelling unit swings away from the stair, no landing is required
between the doorway and the stair. (See [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.appnote33:short].)

A landing may be omitted at the top of an exterior [REF:term:flght]flight serving a secondary entrance to a single [REF:term:dwllng-n]dwelling unit or a house with a [REF:term:bc-scnd-t]secondary suite including their common spaces, provided

clauses.text: the stair does not contain more than 3 risers (metric),

the principal door is a sliding door or swings away from the
stair, and

only a storm or screen door, if any, swings over the stair and
is equipped with hardware to hold it open.

content.text:
A landing may be omitted at the bottom of an exterior stair
or [REF:term:rmp]ramp, provided there is no obstruction,
such as a gate or door, within the lesser of the width of the stair
or [REF:term:rmp]ramp or

clauses.text: 900 mm (metric) for stairs or [REF:term:rmp]ramps serving a single [REF:term:dwllng-n]dwelling unit or a house with a secondary suite including their common spaces, and
1 100 mm (metric) for stairs or [REF:term:rmp]ramps not described in Clause (a).

content.text:
Except as provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect8.subsect6.art3.sent2:short]
                           [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect8.subsect6.art3.sent7:short], landings shall be at least as wide and as long as
the width of the stair or [REF:term:rmp]ramp in which they
occur.

Where the landing in a stairway or [REF:term:rmp]ramp does not turn or turns less than 90°, the length of the landing
need not be more than the lesser of

clauses.text: the required width of the stair or [REF:term:rmp]ramp, or
1 100 mm (metric).

content.text:
The length of a landing shall be measured perpendicular to the
nosings of adjacent steps or to the end of the [REF:term:rmp]ramp, at a distance equal to half the length required in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect8.subsect6.art3.sent2:short] from the narrow edge of the landing.

Where stair [REF:term:flght]flights or [REF:term:rmp]ramps of different widths adjoin a single landing,
the minimum width of the landing shall be

clauses.text:
where one or more of the stair or [REF:term:rmp]ramp widths do not exceed their respective required widths, not less
than the greater required stair or [REF:term:rmp]ramp width,
or

where all of the widths of the stairs or [REF:term:rmp]ramps exceed their respective required widths, not less than the lesser
actual stair or [REF:term:rmp]ramp width.

content.text:
Where a door swings toward a stair, the full arc of the swing
shall be over the landing.
The slope of landings shall not exceed 1 in 50 (metric).

Where a doorway or stairway opens onto the side of a [REF:term:rmp]ramp, the landing shall extend for a distance of
not less than 300 mm (metric) on either side of the doorway or
stairway, except on a side abutting an end wall.

Except as permitted by [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect8.subsect6.art4.sent2:short], the clear height over landings shall be not less than 2 050
mm (metric).

The clear height over landings serving a single [REF:term:dwllng-n]dwelling unit or a house with a [REF:term:scnd-t]secondary suite including their common spaces
shall be not less than 1 950 mm (metric).
Except as provided in Sentences (2) to (4), handrails shall be installed on stairs and [REF:term:rmp]ramps in accordance with [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect8.subsect7.art1.table1:long]

Except where a stair or [REF:term:rmp]ramp serves not more than two [REF:term:dwllng-n]dwelling units, at least one handrail shall be located not more than 750 mm (metric) from the natural path of travel on the stair or [REF:term:rmp]ramp. (See Note A-9.8.7.1.(2).)
Handrails are not required for stairs and [REF:term:rmp]ramps serving a single [REF:term:dwllng-n]dwelling unit or a house with a secondary suite including their common spaces, where

clauses.text: interior stairs have not more than 2 risers (metric),
exterior stairs have not more than 3 risers (metric), or
[REF:term:rmp]ramps rise not more than 400 mm (metric).

content.text: Only one handrail is required on exterior stairs having more than 3 risers provided such stairs serve not more than one [REF:term:dwllng-n]dwelling unit or a house with a [REF:term:bc-scnd-t]secondary suite including their common spaces.

Except for stairs with winders, where a [REF:term:flght]flight of stairs within a [REF:term:dwllng-n]dwelling unit or a house with a secondary suite including their common spaces consists of [REF:term:tpr-thr]tapered treads, or a mix of [REF:term:tpr-thr]tapered treads and rectangular treads, one handrail shall be installed along the narrow end of the treads.

Except as provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect8.subsect7.art2.sent3:short], required handrails shall be continuously graspable throughout
the length of

clauses.text: [REF:term:rmp]ramps, and

[REF:term:flght]flights of stairs, from the bottom
riser to the top riser.

content.text:
Except for stairs or [REF:term:rmp]ramps serving
a single [REF:term:dwllng-n]dwelling unit or a house with
a [REF:term:scnd-t]secondary suite including their common
spaces, at least one required handrail shall be continuous throughout
the length of the stair or [REF:term:rmp]ramp, including
at the landing except where interrupted by doorways. (See [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect9.appnote162:long].)

For stairs or [REF:term:rmp]ramps serving a single [REF:term:dwllng-n]dwelling unit or a house with a [REF:term:scnd-t]secondary suite including their common spaces,
a handrail is permitted to start from a newel post or volute installed
on the bottom tread.

Handrails shall be terminated in a manner that will not obstruct
pedestrian travel or create a hazard. (See [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.appnote36:short].)

Except for stairs and [REF:term:rmp]ramps serving
only one [REF:term:dwllng-n]dwelling unit or a house with
a [REF:term:scnd-t]secondary suite including their common
spaces, at least one handrail at the sides of a stair or [REF:term:rmp]ramp shall extend horizontally not less than 300 mm (metric) beyond the top and bottom of each [REF:term:flght]flight or [REF:term:rmp]ramp. (See [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.appnote37:short].)
The height of handrails on stairs and [REF:term:rmp]ramps shall be measured vertically from the top of the handrail to

clauses.text:
a straight line drawn tangent to the tread nosings of the stair
served by the handrail, or

the surface of the [REF:term:rmp]ramp, floor or landing
served by the handrail.

content.text: Except as provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect8.subsect7.art4.sent3:short] and [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect8.subsect3.art5.sent1.clause5:long], required handrails shall be 865 mm (metric) to 1 070 mm (metric) high.

Handrails installed in addition to required handrails need not
comply with [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect8.subsect7.art4.sent2:short].

The clearance between a handrail and the surface behind it shall
be not less than

clauses.text: 50 mm (metric), or
where said surface is rough or abrasive, 60 mm (metric).

content.text:
All handrails shall be constructed so as to be continually graspable
along their entire length with no obstruction on or above them to
break a handhold. (See [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.appnote39:short].)

Handrails and constructions below handrails, including handrail
supports and stair stringers, shall not project more than 100
mm (metric) into the required width of a stair or [REF:term:rmp]ramp. (See also [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect8.subsect2.art1:long]
                           [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect8.subsect5.art2:long])

Handrails and their supports shall be designed and constructed
to withstand the following loads, which need not be considered to
act simultaneously:

clauses.text:
a concentrated load of not less than 0.9 kN (metric) applied
at any point and in any direction for all handrails, and

for handrails other than those serving a single [REF:term:dwllng-n]dwelling unit, a uniform load of not less
than 0.7 kN/m (metric).

content.text:
Where exterior or interior handrails serving a single [REF:term:dwllng-n]dwelling unit or a house with a [REF:term:scnd-t]secondary suite including their common spaces
are attached to wood studs or blocking, the attachment shall be deemed
to comply with [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect8.subsect7.art7.sent1:short], where

clauses.text: the attachment points are spaced not more than 1.2 m (metric) apart measured on the horizontal plane,

the first attachment point at either end is located no more
than 300 mm (metric) from the end of the handrail, and

the fasteners consist of not less than 2 No. 8 wood screws at
each point, penetrating not less than 32 mm (metric) into solid
wood.

content.text:
Except as provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect8.subsect8.art1.sent2:short] and except
at the leading edge at the top of a [REF:term:flght]flight, every surface to which access is provided, including
but not limited to [REF:term:flght]flights of steps and [REF:term:rmp]ramps, exterior landings, porches, balconies, [REF:term:mzznn]mezzanines, galleries and raised [REF:term:wlkw]walkways, shall be protected by a [REF:term:guard]guard on each side that is not protected by a wall for the length where the difference in elevation is more
than 600 mm (metric) between the walking surface and the adjacent
surface within 1.2 m (metric).
[REF:term:guard]Guards are not required

clauses.text: at loading docks,
at floor pits in [REF:term:rpr-grg]repair garages, or
where access is provided for maintenance purposes only.

content.text:
Doors in [REF:term:bldng]buildings of [REF:term:rdntl-cc]residential occupancy, where the finished
floor on one side of the door is more than 600 mm (metric) above
the floor or other constructed surface or ground level on the other
side of the door, shall be protected by

clauses.text: a [REF:term:guard]guard, or

a mechanism capable of controlling the free swinging or sliding
of the door so as to limit any clear unobstructed opening to not more
than 100 mm (metric).

content.text: Except as provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect8.subsect8.art1.sent5:short], openable windows in [REF:term:bldng]buildings of [REF:term:rdntl-cc]residential occupancy shall be protected by

clauses.text: a [REF:term:guard]guard, or

a mechanism that
can only be released with the use of tools or special knowledge to
control the free swinging or sliding operation of the
openable part of the window so as to limit any clear unobstructed
opening to not more than 100 mm (metric) measured either vertically
or horizontally.

content.text:
Windows need not be protected in accordance with [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect8.subsect8.art1.sent4:short], where the bottom edge of the openable portion of the window
is located

clauses.text: more than 900 mm (metric) above the finished floor, or

less than 1 800 mm (metric) above the floor or ground on
the other side of the window.

content.text: Except as provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect8.subsect8.art1.sent7:short], glazing installed over [REF:term:tr]stairs, [REF:term:rmp]ramps and landings that extends to less than 1 070 mm (metric) above the surface of the treads, [REF:term:rmp]ramp or landing shall be

clauses.text:
protected by [REF:term:guard]guards, in accordance
with this Subsection, or

non-openable and designed to withstand the specified lateral
loads for balcony [REF:term:guard]guards as provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect5.art14:long]

content.text:
In [REF:term:dwllng-n]dwelling units and houses with a [REF:term:bc-scnd-t]secondary suite including their common spaces, glazing installed
over [REF:term:tr]stairs, [REF:term:rmp]ramps and landings that extends to less than 900 mm (metric) above
the surface of the treads, [REF:term:rmp]ramp or landing
shall be

clauses.text:
protected by [REF:term:guard]guards, in accordance
with this Subsection, or

non-openable and designed to withstand the specified lateral
loads for balcony [REF:term:guard]guards as provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect5.art14:long]

content.text: Glazing installed in public areas that extends to less than 1 m (metric) from the floor and is located above the second [REF:term:tr]storey in [REF:term:bldng]buildings of [REF:term:rdntl-cc]residential occupancy shall be

clauses.text:
protected by [REF:term:guard]guards in accordance
with this Subsection, or

non-openable and designed to withstand the specified lateral
loads for balcony [REF:term:guard]guards as provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect5.art14:long]

content.text:
Except as provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect8.subsect8.art2.sent2:short]
                           [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect8.subsect8.art2.sent3:short]

articles.title: Guards for Floors and Ramps in Garages

content.text:
Except for floors of garages referred to in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect35:long], where garage floors or ramps are 600
mm (metric) or more above the adjacent ground or floor level, every
opening through a garage floor and the perimeter of floors and ramps
that have no exterior walls shall be provided with

clauses.text:
a continuous curb not less than 140 mm (metric) in height,
and

a [REF:term:guard]guard not less than 1 070
mm (metric) above the floor level.

content.text:
Vehicle guardrails shall be designed and constructed to withstand
the loading values stipulated in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect5.art15.sent1:long]. (See [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect5.appnote32:long].)

Except as permitted in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect8.subsect8.art5.sent3:short]
                           [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect8.subsect8.art5.sent4:short], openings through [REF:term:guard]guards shall be of a size that prevents the passage of a spherical object
having a diameter of 100 mm (metric). (See [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.appnote45:short].)

Except for [REF:term:guard]guards that serve [REF:term:ndtrl-cc]industrial occupancies, the triangular openings
formed by stair risers, stair treads and the bottom element of a required [REF:term:guard]guard shall be of a size that prevents the passage
of a 150 mm diam (metric) sphere.

Except where they serve [REF:term:trg-grg]storage garages, [REF:term:guard]guards in [REF:term:ndtrl-cc]industrial
occupancies are permitted to consist of

clauses.text: a top railing, and

one or more horizontal intermediate rails spaced such that the
size of the openings through the [REF:term:guard]guard prevents
the passage of a spherical object having a diameter of 535 mm (metric).

content.text:
Openings through any [REF:term:guard]guard that is
not required by [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect8.subsect8.art1:long] and that serves an [REF:term:ccpnc]occupancy other than an [REF:term:ndtrl-cc]industrial occupancy shall be of a size that

clauses.text:
prevents the passage of a spherical object having a diameter
of 100 mm (metric), or

permits the passage of a spherical object having a diameter
of 200 mm (metric).

articles.title: Design of Guards to Not Facilitate Climbing

content.text:
Except for [REF:term:guard]guards in [REF:term:ndtrl-cc]industrial occupancies, [REF:term:guard]guards required by [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect8.subsect8.art1:long] that protect
 a level located more than  4.2 m (metric) above the adjacent
level  shall be designed so that no member, attachment or opening
located  between 140 mm (metric) and 900 mm (metric) above
the level  protected by the [REF:term:guard]guard facilitates
climbing. (See [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.appnote47:short].)
Glass in [REF:term:guard]guards shall be

clauses.text: safety glazing of the laminated or tempered type conforming to [REF:standard:cgsb-12.1] or
wired glass conforming to [REF:standard:cgsb-12.11]

content.text:
Except as specified in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect8.subsect9.art4:long]
                           [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect8.subsect9.art5:long], stairs
and [REF:term:rmp]ramps shall be designed for strength
and rigidity under uniform loading criteria to support specified loads
of

clauses.text:
1.9 kPa (metric) for stairs and [REF:term:rmp]ramps serving not more than one [REF:term:dwllng-n]dwelling unit or a house with a [REF:term:scnd-t]secondary suite including
their common spaces, and
4.8 kPa (metric) for other stairs and [REF:term:rmp]ramps.

content.text:
Exterior concrete stairs with more than 2 risers and 2 treads
shall be

clauses.text:
supported on unit masonry or concrete walls or piers not less
than 150 mm (metric) in cross section, or
cantilevered from the main [REF:term:fndtn]foundation wall.

content.text:
Stairs described in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect8.subsect9.art2.sent1:short],
when cantilevered from the [REF:term:fndtn]foundation wall,
shall be constructed and installed in conformance with [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect8.subsect10:long]
The depth below ground level for [REF:term:fndtn]foundations for exterior steps shall conform to the requirements in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect12:long]

Exterior wood steps shall not be in direct contact with the
ground unless suitably treated with a wood preservative.
Wooden stair stringers shall

clauses.text:
have a minimum effective depth of 90 mm (metric), measured
perpendicularly to the bottom of the stringer at the point of minimum
cross-section, and an overall depth of not less than 235 mm (metric),
be supported and secured top and bottom,

be not less than 25 mm (metric) actual thickness if supported
along their length and 38 mm (metric) actual thickness if unsupported
along their length, and

except as permitted in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect8.subsect9.art4.sent2:short], be spaced not more than 900 mm (metric) o.c. in stairs serving
not more than one [REF:term:dwllng-n]dwelling unit or a
house with a [REF:term:scnd-t]secondary suite including
their common spaces, and 600 mm o.c. (metric) in other stairs.

content.text:
For stairs serving not more than one [REF:term:dwllng-n]dwelling unit or a house with a [REF:term:scnd-t]secondary
suite including their common spaces, where risers support the
front portion of the tread, the space between stringers shall be not
more than 1 200 mm (metric).

Stair treads of lumber, plywood or OSB within [REF:term:dwllng-n]dwelling units shall be not less than 25 mm (metric) actual thickness, except that, where open risers are permitted and
the distance between stringers exceeds 750 mm (metric), the treads
shall be not less than 38 mm (metric) actual thickness.

Stair treads of plywood or OSB that are not continuously supported
by the riser shall have their face grain or direction of face orientation
at right angles to the stringers.

The finish for treads and landings of interior stairs in [REF:term:dwllng-n]dwelling units, other than stairs to unfinished [REF:term:bmnt]basements, shall consist of hardwood, vertical
grain softwood, resilient flooring or other material providing equivalent
performance.

Treads and landings of interior and exterior stairs and [REF:term:rmp]ramps, other than those within [REF:term:dwllng-n]dwelling units or within houses with a [REF:term:scnd-t]secondary suite including their common spaces, shall have
a slip-resistant finish or be provided with slip-resistant strips
that extend not more than 1 mm (metric) above the surface.

Exterior concrete steps and their anchorage system that are
cantilevered from a [REF:term:fndtn]foundation wall shall
be designed and installed to support the loads to which they may be
subjected.

Cantilevered concrete steps referred to in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect8.subsect10.art1:long] shall be anchored to concrete [REF:term:fndtn]foundation walls not less than 200 mm (metric) thick.

articles.title: Prevention of Damage Due to Frost

content.text:
Suitable precautions shall be taken during backfilling and grading
operations to ensure that subsequent freezing of the [REF:term:l]soil will not cause uplift forces on the underside of cantilevered
concrete steps to the extent that the steps or the walls to which
they are attached will be damaged.

Stairways, handrails and [REF:term:guard]guards in
a [REF:term:mn-f-gr]means of egress shall conform to the
requirements in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect8:long] as well as to the requirements
in this Section.

In addition to the fire protection requirements provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect9.subsect4:long], [REF:term:flm-prd-]flame-spread ratings, [REF:term:fr-rtnc-]fire-resistance ratings and [REF:term:fr-prtct]fire-protection ratings for [REF:term:mn-f-gr]means of egress shall conform to [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect10:long]

Except for [REF:term:dwllng-n]dwelling units, the [REF:term:ccpnt-ld]occupant load of a [REF:term:flr-r]floor
area or part of a [REF:term:flr-r]floor area shall
be the number of persons for which such areas are designed, but not
fewer than that determined from [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect1.subsect17.art1.table1:long], unless
it can be shown that the area will be occupied by fewer persons.

The [REF:term:ccpnt-ld]occupant load for [REF:term:dwllng-n]dwelling units shall be based on 2 persons
per bedroom or sleeping area.

Except as otherwise provided in this Section, an [REF:term:xt]exit from any [REF:term:flr-r] floor area shall
be one of the following used singly or in combination:

clauses.text: an exterior doorway,
an exterior passageway,
an exterior [REF:term:rmp]ramp,
an exterior stairway,
a fire escape,
a [REF:term:hrzntl-x]horizontal exit,
an interior passageway,
an interior [REF:term:rmp]ramp, or
an interior stairway.

content.text:
Fire escapes shall only be used as [REF:term:xt]exits on existing [REF:term:bldng]buildings and shall be designed
and installed in conformance with [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect4.subsect7:long]

Where a [REF:term:hrzntl-x]horizontal exit is used,
it shall conform to [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect4.subsect1.art6.sent1:long] and [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect4.subsect6.art10:long]

An [REF:term:xt]exit shall be designed for no purpose
other than for exiting except that an [REF:term:xt]exit may also serve as an access to a [REF:term:flr-r]floor area.

articles.title: Elevators, Slide Escapes and Windows as Means of Egress

content.text:
Elevators, slide escapes and windows shall not be considered
as part of a required [REF:term:mn-f-gr]means of egress.

Except for doors serving a single [REF:term:dwllng-n]dwelling
unit or a house with a [REF:term:scnd-t]secondary suite including their common spaces, at least one door at every principal
entrance to a [REF:term:bldng]building providing access
from the exterior at ground level shall be designed in accordance
with the requirements for [REF:term:xt]exits.

Except as required by Sentences 9.9.3.3.(2) and 9.9.3.4.(3), this Subsection applies to every [REF:term:mn-f-gr]means
of egress except

clauses.text:
[REF:term:xt]exits that serve not more than one [REF:term:dwllng-n]dwelling unit or a house with a [REF:term:scnd-t]secondary suite including their common spaces,
and
[REF:term:cc-t-xt]access to exits within [REF:term:dwllng-n]dwelling units and within houses with a [REF:term:scnd-t]secondary suite including their common spaces.

content.text: Except for doors and corridors, the width of every [REF:term:xt]exit facility shall be not less than 900 mm (metric). (See [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect9.subsect6.art3:long] for doors, [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect8.subsect2.art1:long] for stairs, and [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect8.subsect5.art2:long] for [REF:term:rmp]ramps.)

The width of every [REF:term:pblc-crr]public corridor, corridor used by the public, and [REF:term:xt]exit corridor
shall be not less than 1 100 mm (metric). (See also [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect9.subsect5:long] for obstructions in corridors.)

The width of [REF:term:pblc-crr]public corridors and [REF:term:xt]exit corridors that serve only a house with a [REF:term:bc-scnd-t]secondary suite including their common spaces shall be not less than 860 mm (metric).

Except for stairways, doorways and [REF:term:trg-grg]storage
garages, the minimum clear height in [REF:term:xt]exits and [REF:term:cc-t-xt]access to exits shall be 2.1 m (metric). (See [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect8.subsect2.art2:long] for stairs, [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect8.subsect5.art3:long] for [REF:term:rmp]ramps, [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect8.subsect6.art4:long] for landings and [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect9.subsect6.art2:long] for
doorways.)

The clear height in [REF:term:xt]exits and [REF:term:cc-t-xt]access to exits in [REF:term:trg-grg]storage
garages shall be not less than 2 m (metric).

The clear height in [REF:term:pblc-crr]public corridors and [REF:term:xt]exit corridors that serve only a house with a [REF:term:bc-scnd-t]secondary suite including their common spaces shall be not less than 2 m (metric).

Except as provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect9.subsect4.art4:long]
                           [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect9.subsect4.art6:long], this Subsection applies
to the fire protection of all [REF:term:xt]exits except [REF:term:xt]exits serving not more than one [REF:term:dwllng-n]dwelling unit.

Except as provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect9.subsect4.art2.sent2:short]
                           [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect9.subsect4.art2.sent5:short] and [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect9.subsect8.art5:long], every [REF:term:xt]exit other than an exterior doorway shall be separated from
each adjacent [REF:term:flr-r]floor area  or from another [REF:term:xt]exit

clauses.text:
where there is a floor assembly above the [REF:term:flr-r]floor area, by a [REF:term:fr-prtn]fire separation having a [REF:term:fr-rtnc-]fire-resistance rating not
less than that required for the floor assembly above the [REF:term:flr-r]floor area (see [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect10.subsect9.art12:long]),
and

where there is no floor assembly above the [REF:term:flr-r]floor area, by a [REF:term:fr-prtn]fire separation having a [REF:term:fr-rtnc-]fire-resistance rating not
less than the greater of

subclauses.text:
that required by [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect10.subsect8:long] for the floor
assembly below, or
45 min.

content.text: Where an [REF:term:xt]exit is located in a house with a [REF:term:bc-scnd-t]secondary suite including their common spaces, the [REF:term:xt]exit shall be separated from adjacent [REF:term:flr-r]floor areas with a [REF:term:fr-prtn]fire separation

clauses.text: having a [REF:term:fr-rtnc-]fire-resistance rating not less than 15 min (metric) where all [REF:term:mk-lrm]smoke alarms within the house are of photo-electric type and interconnected as described in Clause 9.10.19.5.(2)(a),

having a [REF:term:fr-rtnc-]fire-resistance rating not less than 30 min (metric) where additional [REF:term:mk-lrm]smoke alarms of photo-electric type are installed and interconnected as described in Clause 9.10.19.5.(2)(b),
having a [REF:term:fr-rtnc-]fire-resistance rating not less than 45 min (metric) when [REF:term:mk-lrm]smoke alarms are not installed and interconnected as described in Clauses (a) or (b), or
that is not required to have a [REF:term:fr-rtnc-]fire-resistance rating if the [REF:term:bldng]building is [REF:term:prnklrd]sprinklered.

content.text:
A [REF:term:fr-prtn]fire separation common to 2 [REF:term:xt]exits shall be smoke-tight and not be pierced by
doorways, duct work, piping or any other opening that may affect the
continuity of the separation.

A [REF:term:fr-prtn]fire separation that separates
an [REF:term:xt]exit from the remainder of the [REF:term:bldng]building shall have no openings except those
for electrical wiring, [REF:term:ncmbtbl]noncombustible conduit and [REF:term:ncmbtbl]noncombustible piping that
serve only the [REF:term:xt]exit, and for standpipes, sprinkler
piping, [REF:term:xt]exit doorways and wired glass and
glass block permitted in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect9.subsect4.art3:long]

The requirements in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect9.subsect4.art2.sent1:short]
                           [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect9.subsect4.art2.sent2:short] do not apply to an exterior [REF:term:xt]exit passageway
provided the passageway has not less than 50% of its exterior sides
open to the outdoors and is served by an [REF:term:xt]exit stair at each end of the passageway.

This Article applies to wired glass in doors, and wired glass
or glass block in sidelights, where these are installed in [REF:term:fr-prtn]fire separations between [REF:term:xt]exit enclosures and [REF:term:flr-r]floor areas.

Except as provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect9.subsect4.art3.sent3:short], the combined area of glazing in doors and sidelights shall not
exceed 0.8 m2
                            (metric).

Where an [REF:term:xt]exit enclosure connects with
a [REF:term:flr-r]floor area through an enclosed vestibule
or corridor separated from the [REF:term:flr-r]floor area by [REF:term:fr-prtn]fire separations having not less
than a 45 min (metric)
                           [REF:term:fr-rtnc-]fire-resistance
rating, the glazed areas described in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect9.subsect4.art3.sent1:short] need not be limited as required in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect9.subsect4.art3.sent2:short].

articles.title: Openings Near Unenclosed Exterior Exit Stairs and Ramps

content.text:
[REF:term:nprtctd-]Unprotected openings in exterior
walls of the [REF:term:bldng]building shall be protected
with wired glass in fixed steel frames or glass block conforming to [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect10.subsect13.art5:long]
                           [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect10.subsect13.art7:long], where

clauses.text:
an unenclosed exterior [REF:term:xt]exit stair or [REF:term:rmp]ramp provides the only [REF:term:mn-f-gr]means
of egress from a [REF:term:t]suite and is exposed
to fire from [REF:term:nprtctd-]unprotected openings in
the exterior walls of

subclauses.text: another [REF:term:fr-cmprt]fire compartment, or

another [REF:term:dwllng-n]dwelling unit, ancillary
space or common space in a house with a [REF:term:scnd-t]secondary
suite, and

clauses.text:
[REF:term:nprtctd-]unprotected openings in the exterior
walls of the [REF:term:bldng]building are within 3
m (metric) horizontally and less than 10 m (metric) below or less
than 5 m (metric) above the [REF:term:xt]exit stair
or [REF:term:rmp]ramp.

articles.title: Openings in Exterior Walls of Exits

content.text:
Either openings in exterior walls of an [REF:term:xt]exit or openings in adjacent exterior walls of the [REF:term:bldng]building the [REF:term:xt]exit serves shall be
protected with wired glass in fixed steel frames or glass block installed
in accordance with [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect10.subsect13.art5:long]
                           [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect10.subsect13.art7:long], where

clauses.text:
the [REF:term:xt]exit enclosure has exterior walls
that intersect the exterior walls of the [REF:term:bldng]building at an angle of less than 135° (metric) measured on the outside
of the [REF:term:bldng] building, and

the openings in the exterior walls of the [REF:term:bldng]building  are within 3 m (metric) horizontally and less
than 2 m (metric) above the openings in the exterior walls of
the [REF:term:xt]exit.

content.text: Where an exterior [REF:term:xt]exit door in one [REF:term:fr-cmprt]fire compartment is within 3 m (metric) horizontally of an [REF:term:nprtctd-]unprotected opening in another [REF:term:fr-cmprt]fire compartment and the exterior walls of these [REF:term:fr-cmprt]fire compartments intersect at an exterior angle of less than 135°, the opening shall be protected with

clauses.text: wired glass in fixed steel frames conforming to [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect10.subsect13.art5:long], or
glass block conforming to [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect10.subsect13.art7:long].

articles.title: Stairways in 2 Storey, Group D or E Buildings

content.text:
Where a [REF:term:t]suite of Group D or E [REF:term:ccpnc]occupancy is located partly on the [REF:term:frt-tr]first storey and partly on the second [REF:term:tr]storey, stairways serving the second [REF:term:tr]storey of that [REF:term:t]suite need not be constructed
as [REF:term:xt]exit stairs provided,

clauses.text:
the [REF:term:bldng]building is not greater than
2 [REF:term:tr]storeys in [REF:term:bldng-hg]building
height,

the [REF:term:t]suite is separated from other [REF:term:ccpnc]occupancies by at least a 45 min (metric)
                              [REF:term:fr-prtn]fire separation,

the area occupied by the [REF:term:t]suite is not
greater than 100 m2
                               (metric) per [REF:term:tr]storey,

the maximum travel distance from any point in the [REF:term:t]suite to an exterior [REF:term:xt]exit is not greater
than 25 m (metric),

the floor assemblies have a [REF:term:fr-rtnc-]fire-resistance
rating of not less than 45 min (metric) or are of [REF:term:ncmbtbl-]noncombustible construction, and

the [REF:term:bmnt]basement and [REF:term:frt-tr]first storey are separated by a [REF:term:fr-prtn]fire
separation having a [REF:term:fr-rtnc-]fire-resistance
rating of not less than 45 min (metric).

subsections.title: Obstructions and Hazards in Means of Egress

content.text: This Subsection applies to obstructions and hazards in every [REF:term:mn-f-gr]means of egress except those within a [REF:term:dwllng-n]dwelling unit or serving not more than one [REF:term:dwllng-n]dwelling unit.

Where a corridor contains an [REF:term:ccpnc]occupancy, the [REF:term:ccpnc]occupancy shall not reduce the unobstructed
width of the corridor to less than the required width of the corridor.

Except as permitted in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect9.subsect5.art3.sent2:short], obstructions located within 1 980 mm (metric) of the floor
shall not project horizontally more than 100 mm (metric) into [REF:term:xt]exit passageways, corridors used by the public or [REF:term:pblc-crr]public corridors in a manner that would create
a hazard for visually impaired persons travelling adjacent to walls.

The horizontal projection of an obstruction referred to in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect9.subsect5.art3.sent1:short] is permitted to exceed 100 mm (metric) where the obstruction extends to less than 680 mm (metric) above
the floor. (See [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect9.appnote129:long].)

Except as permitted in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect9.subsect6:long] and [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect8.subsect7.art6:long], no fixture, turnstile or construction shall project
within the required width of an [REF:term:xt]exit.

No obstructions such as posts or turnstiles shall be placed
so as to restrict the width of a required [REF:term:mn-f-gr]means
of egress from a [REF:term:flr-r]floor area or part
of a [REF:term:flr-r]floor area to less than 750
mm (metric) unless an alternate unobstructed [REF:term:mn-f-gr]means
of egress is provided adjacent to and plainly visible from
the restricted egress.

Except as provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect9.subsect5.art5.sent3:short], no obstructions, such as counter gates, that do not meet the requirements
for [REF:term:xt]exit doors, shall be placed in a required [REF:term:mn-f-gr]means of egress from a [REF:term:flr-r]floor area  or part of a [REF:term:flr-r]floor area unless an alternate unobstructed [REF:term:mn-f-gr]means of
egress is provided adjacent to and plainly visible from the
restricted egress.

Obstructions, such as counter gates, that do not satisfy [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect9.subsect5.art5.sent2:short], are permitted to be placed in a required [REF:term:mn-f-gr]means of egress from a part of a [REF:term:flr-r] floor area in [REF:term:mrcntl-c]mercantile
occupancies and [REF:term:bn-nd-pr]business and personal
services occupancies, provided that the part of the [REF:term:flr-r]floor area served by the obstructed [REF:term:mn-f-gr]means of egress is not generally accessible
to the public.
No mirror shall be placed in or adjacent to any [REF:term:xt]exit so as to confuse the direction of [REF:term:xt]exit, and no mirror or draperies shall be placed on or over [REF:term:xt]exit doors.

Fuel-fired [REF:term:pplnc]appliances shall not be
installed in an [REF:term:xt]exit or corridor serving as
an [REF:term:cc-t-xt]access to exit.

[REF:term:rvc-rm]Service rooms containing equipment
subject to possible explosion, such as [REF:term:blr]boilers designed to operate at a pressure in excess of 100 kPa (metric), and certain types of refrigerating and transformer equipment, shall
not be located under required [REF:term:xt]exits.

Ancillary rooms such as storage rooms, washrooms, toilet rooms,
laundry rooms and [REF:term:rvc-rm]service rooms shall
not open directly into an [REF:term:xt]exit.

subsections.title: Doors in a Means of Egress

content.text:
Except as provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect9.subsect6.art1.sent4:short], obstructions created by doors shall be limited in accordance with [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect9.subsect6.art1.sent2:short]
                           [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect9.subsect6.art1.sent3:short]

clauses.text: at [REF:term:xt]exit doors,
at doors that open into or are located within a [REF:term:pblc-crr]public corridor, and

at doors that open into or are located within another facility
that provides [REF:term:cc-t-xt]access to exit from a [REF:term:t]suite.

content.text: When fully open, doors described in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect9.subsect6.art1.sent1:short] shall not decrease the required [REF:term:xt]exit width by more than

clauses.text:
100 mm (metric) in [REF:term:xt]exit corridors,
and
50 mm (metric) for other [REF:term:xt]exit facilities.

content.text:
The swing of doors described in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect9.subsect6.art1.sent1:short] shall not reduce the width of the path of travel to
less than

clauses.text: the required [REF:term:xt]exit width in [REF:term:xt]exit corridors and passageways, and

750 mm (metric) on [REF:term:xt]exit stairs or
landings.

content.text:
Doors serving a single [REF:term:dwllng-n]dwelling unit or a house with a [REF:term:scnd-t]secondary suite need
not comply with [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect9.subsect6.art1.sent2:short]
                           [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect9.subsect6.art1.sent3:short].

Except as provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect9.subsect6.art2.sent2:short]
                           [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect9.subsect6.art2.sent3:short], the clear opening height of doorways shall be not
less than 2 030 mm (metric) high at

clauses.text: [REF:term:xt]exit doors,
doors that open into or are located within a [REF:term:pblc-crr]public corridor, and

doors that open into or are located within another facility
that provides [REF:term:cc-t-xt]access to exit from a [REF:term:t]suite.

content.text:
The clear opening height under door closers and other devices
in doorways described in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect9.subsect6.art2.sent1:short] shall
be not less than 1 980 mm (metric).

Doorways serving a single [REF:term:dwllng-n]dwelling unit or a house with a [REF:term:scnd-t]secondary suite need
not comply with [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect9.subsect6.art2.sent1:short]
                           [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect9.subsect6.art2.sent2:short]. (See also [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect5.subsect5.art1:long])

Except as permitted by [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect9.subsect6.art2.sent3:short], the clear opening height of doorways described in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect9.subsect6.art2.sent1:short] serving a house with a [REF:term:bc-scnd-t]secondary suite including their common spaces shall be not less than 1 980 mm (metric) high.

Except as provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect9.subsect6.art3.sent4:short], the clear opening width of doorways shall comply with [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect9.subsect6.art3.sent2:short] at

clauses.text: [REF:term:xt]exit doors, and
doors that open into or are located within a [REF:term:pblc-crr]public corridor or other facility that provides [REF:term:cc-t-xt]access to exit from a [REF:term:t]suite.

content.text: Doorways described in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect9.subsect6.art3.sent1:short] shall be

clauses.text:
not less than 850 mm (metric) wide where there is only one
door leaf,

not less than 850 mm (metric) wide where multiple-leaf doors
are installed with only one active leaf having a latching mechanism
described in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect9.subsect6.art7:long], and

not less than 1 210 mm (metric) wide where multiple-leaf
doors are installed with two active leaves.

content.text: In doorways described in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect9.subsect6.art3.sent1:short] that have multiple-leaf doors installed,

clauses.text:
no active leaf shall be less than 850 mm (metric) wide where
only one leaf is active, and

no single leaf shall be less than 610 mm (metric) wide where
two leaves are active.

content.text:
Doorways serving a single [REF:term:dwllng-n]dwelling unit or a house with a [REF:term:bc-scnd-t]secondary suite including their common spaces need
not comply with [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect9.subsect6.art3.sent2:short]. (See also [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect5.subsect5.art1:long])

Except as provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect9.subsect6.art4.sent4:short]
                           [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect9.subsect6.art4.sent5:short], required [REF:term:xt]exit doors and doors
in required [REF:term:mn-f-gr]means of egress, except doors
