that lesser depths are satisfactory, or where the [REF:term:fndtn]foundation is designed
for lesser depths.
The [REF:term:fndtn]foundation depths required by [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect12.subsect2.art2.sent1:short] do not apply to [REF:term:fndtn]foundations for

clauses.text: [REF:term:bldng]buildings

subclauses.text: that are not of masonry or masonry veneer construction, and

whose superstructure conforms to the requirements of the deformation
resistance test in [REF:standard:csaz240.2.1] or

clauses.text: accessory [REF:term:bldng]buildings

subclauses.text: that are not of masonry or masonry veneer construction,

not more than 1 storey
                                  (metric) in
height,

not more than 55 m2
                                  (metric) in [REF:term:bldng-r]building area, and

where the distance from finished ground to the underside of
the floor joists is not more than 600 mm (metric).

content.text: The [REF:term:fndtn]foundation depths required by [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect12.subsect2.art2.sent1:short] do not apply to [REF:term:fndtn]foundations for decks and other accessible exterior platforms

clauses.text:
of not more than 1 storey
                               (metric),

not more than 55 m2
                               (metric) in area,

where the distance from finished ground to the underside of
the joists is not more than 600 mm (metric),
not supporting a roof, and

not attached to another structure, unless it can be demonstrated
that differential movement will not adversely affect the performance
of that structure.

content.text:
Where decks or other accessible exterior platforms are supported
on surface [REF:term:fndtn]foundations supported on other
than coarse-grained [REF:term:l]soil with good drainage
or [REF:term:rck]rock, access to the [REF:term:fndtn]foundation positions to permit re-levelling of the platform
shall be provided

clauses.text:
by passageways with a clear height under the platform of not
less than 600 mm (metric) and a width of not less than 600
mm (metric), or
by installing the decking in a manner that allows easy removal.

content.text:
Backfill shall be placed to avoid damaging the [REF:term:fndtn]foundation wall, the drainage tile, externally applied thermal
insulation and waterproofing or dampproofing of the wall.
Backfill shall be graded to prevent drainage towards the [REF:term:fndtn]foundation after settling.

Backfill that is within 600 mm (metric) of the [REF:term:fndtn]foundation shall be free of deleterious debris
and boulders larger than 250 mm (metric) diam. (See [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.appnote86:short].)

Except as provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect12.subsect3.art3.sent3:short], backfill shall not contain pyritic material or material that is
susceptible to ice lensing in concentrations that will damage the [REF:term:bldng]building to a degree that would adversely affect
its stability or the performance of assemblies. (See [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.appnote14:long].)

Backfill with material of any concentration that is susceptible
to ice lensing is permitted where [REF:term:fndtn]foundation walls are

clauses.text: cast-in-place concrete,
concrete block insulated on the exterior, or

concrete block protected from the backfill by a material that
serves as a slip plane.

content.text:
The [REF:term:l]soil in trenches beneath footings
for sewers and watermains shall be compacted by tamping up to the
level of the footing base, or shall be filled with concrete having
a strength not less than 10 MPa (metric) to support the footing.

sections.title: Dampproofing, Waterproofing and Soil Gas Control

content.text:
This Section presents measures to control the ingress of water,
moisture and [REF:term:l]soil gas.

[REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect13.subsect2:long] applies to below-ground walls
and floors-on-ground where drainage is provided in accordance with [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect14:long] over and along the entire below-ground portion
of the [REF:term:fndtn]foundation wall.

[REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect13.subsect3:long] applies to below-ground walls,
floors-on-ground and roofs of underground structures that are subject
to hydrostatic pressure.

[REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect13.subsect4:long] applies to walls, roofs and
floors that are in contact with the ground.

Except as provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect13.subsect3.art1:long], where the
exterior finished ground level is at a higher elevation than the ground
level inside the [REF:term:fndtn]foundation walls, exterior
surfaces of [REF:term:fndtn]foundation walls below ground
level shall be dampproofed.
Except as provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect13.subsect2.art1.sent3:short] and [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect13.subsect3.art1:long], floors-on-ground shall be dampproofed.
Dampproofing required in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect13.subsect2.art1.sent2:short] need not be provided for

clauses.text: floors in garages,
floors in unenclosed portions of [REF:term:bldng]buildings, or

floors installed over not less than 100 mm (metric) of coarse
clean granular material containing not more than 10% of material that
will pass a 4 mm (metric) sieve.

content.text: Materials installed to provide required dampproofing shall be

clauses.text:
capable of protecting assemblies against moisture transfer from
the ground,
compatible with adjoining materials, and

resistant to mechanisms of deterioration that may reasonably
be expected, given the nature, function and exposure of the materials.

content.text:
Except as otherwise specified in this Section, materials used
for exterior dampproofing shall

clauses.text: conform to one of the following standards:

subclauses.text: [REF:standard:astmd1227] Type III, Class I,
[REF:standard:astmd4479m] Type III,
[REF:standard:cgsb-51.34] or
[REF:standard:csaa123.4]or

clauses.text:
have a water vapour permeance of not more than 43 ng/(Pa×s×m2) (metric) when tested in accordance with Procedure A (wet
cup) of [REF:standard:astme96m] and consist of one of the
following material types:

subclauses.text: a vapour-resistant coating,

a cold-fluid-applied or hot-rubberized bituminous dampproofing
membrane,

a liquid-applied or spray-applied asphalt-based emulsion dampproofing,
or
a type III hot-applied asphalt.

content.text:
The area in which dampproofing is to be carried out shall be
kept free of water during the application and curing of the dampproofing
system.

The surface to be dampproofed shall be prepared in accordance
with the instructions of the dampproofing material manufacturer.

Where the dampproofing material is to be applied on insulating
concrete form (ICF) walls, the instructions of the ICF wall manufacturer
shall be followed.

Unit masonry walls to be dampproofed shall be parged on the
exterior face below ground level with not less than 6 mm (metric) of mortar conforming to [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect20:long] coved over
the footing.

Concrete walls to be dampproofed shall have holes and recesses
sealed with cement mortar or a mastic or sealant that is suitable
for vertical applications and compatible with the dampproofing material.

The surface required to be dampproofed shall be clean and dry
and free of ice, snow, frost, dust, dirt, oil, grease, cracks, projections
and depressions, loose particles and debris that could be detrimental
to the performance of the material to be applied.

Exterior dampproofing shall be applied from finished ground
level to the top of the exterior of the footing.

Unless otherwise stated in this Subsection, dampproofing shall
be installed in accordance with the manufacturer's instructions with
regard to

clauses.text: surface priming,
conditions during application,
application quantity and rate, and
curing times.

content.text:
Joints, cracks and penetrations shall be sealed to maintain
the continuity of the dampproofing, where the dampproofing material
is not capable of bridging such discontinuities.

The interior surface of [REF:term:fndtn]foundation walls below ground level shall be protected by means that minimize
the ingress of moisture from the [REF:term:fndtn]foundation wall into interior spaces, where

clauses.text:
a separate interior finish is applied to a concrete or unit
masonry wall that is in contact with the [REF:term:l]soil, or

wood members are placed in contact with such walls for the installation
of insulation or finish.

content.text: Except as provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect13.subsect2.art5.sent3:short], where the protection of interior finishes required in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect13.subsect2.art5.sent1:short] consists of membranes or coatings,

clauses.text:
the membrane or coating shall extend from the [REF:term:bmnt]basement floor surface up to the highest extent of the interior
insulation or finish, but not higher than the exterior finished ground
level, and

no membrane or coating with a permeance less than 170 ng/(Pa×s×m2) (metric) shall be applied to the interior surface of the [REF:term:fndtn]foundation wall above ground level between the
insulation and the [REF:term:fndtn] foundation wall.

content.text:
Where insulation functions as both moisture protection for interior
finishes and as a [REF:term:vpr-brrr]vapour barrier in
accordance with [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect25.subsect4:long], it shall be applied
over the entire interior surface of the [REF:term:fndtn]foundation wall.

Where dampproofing is installed below the floor, it shall consist
of

clauses.text:
polyethylene not less than 0.15 mm thick with joints lapped
not less than 100 mm (metric),

type S roll roofing with joints lapped not less than 100
mm (metric), or

rigid extruded/expanded polystyrene with sealed or ship-lapped
joints that has

subclauses.text:
sufficient compressive strength to support the floor assembly,
and
a water vapour permeance complying with [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect13.subsect2.art2.sent2.clause1:long].

content.text:
Where dampproofing is installed between a floor-on-ground and
a finished floor, it shall consist of

clauses.text:
rigid extruded/expanded polystyrene with sealed or ship-lapped
joints that has

subclauses.text:
sufficient compressive strength to support the floor assembly,
and
a water vapour permeance complying with [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect13.subsect2.art2.sent2.clause2:long], or

clauses.text:
polyethylene not less than 0.05 mm (metric) thick with joints
lapped not less than 100 mm (metric).

content.text:
Where hydrostatic pressure occurs, waterproofing is required
for assemblies separating interior space from the ground to prevent
the ingress of water into [REF:term:bldng]building assemblies
and interior spaces.

Waterproofing is required for roofs of underground structures
to prevent the ingress of water into [REF:term:bldng]building assemblies and interior spaces.

Materials installed to provide required waterproofing shall
be

clauses.text: compatible with adjoining materials, and

resistant to mechanisms of deterioration that may reasonably
be expected, given the nature, function and exposure of the materials.

content.text: Materials used for exterior waterproofing shall conform to

clauses.text:
[REF:standard:astmd1227] in which case, they shall be
installed in accordance with [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect13.subsect3.art3.sent3:long],

[REF:standard:astmd3019] where non-fibered and non-asbestos-fibered
(Types I and III) asphalt roll roofing are permitted,

[REF:standard:astmd4479m] in which case, they shall
be installed in accordance with [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect13.subsect3.art3.sent3:long] and with
reinforcing material,
[REF:standard:astmd4637m]
[REF:standard:astmd4811m]
[REF:standard:astmd6878m]
[REF:standard:cgsb37-gp-9ma] where a primer is required,
[REF:standard:cgsb-37.50]
[REF:standard:cgsb-37.54]
[REF:standard:cgsb37-gp-56m]
[REF:standard:cgsb-37.58]
[REF:standard:csaa123.2]

[REF:standard:csaa123.4] in which case, they shall be installed with reinforcing material,
or
[REF:standard:csaa123.17]

content.text:
Surfaces to be waterproofed shall be prepared in accordance
with the instructions of the waterproofing material manufacturer.

Where the waterproofing material is to be applied on ICF walls,
the instructions of the ICF wall manufacturer shall be followed.

Unit masonry walls that are to be waterproofed shall be parged
on exterior surfaces below ground level with not less than 6
mm (metric) of mortar conforming to [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect20:long] coved
over the footing.

Concrete walls that are to be waterproofed shall have all holes
and recesses sealed with mortar or waterproofing material.

Surfaces required to be waterproofed shall be clean and dry
and free of ice, snow, frost, dust, dirt, oil, grease, cracks, projections
and depressions, loose particles and debris that could be detrimental
to the performance of the waterproofing material.

Unless otherwise stated in this Subsection, waterproofing shall
be installed in accordance with the manufacturer's instructions with
regard to

clauses.text: surface priming,
conditions during application,

the required number of layers of reinforcing fabric on [REF:term:fndtn]foundation, footings, floors, walls and structural
slabs,
application quantity and rate, and
curing times.

content.text:
Waterproofing shall be continuous across joints and at junctions
between different [REF:term:bldng]building elements.

The waterproofed surface shall be protected with a suitable
material to minimize mechanical damage during backfilling.

The area in which the waterproofing is to be carried out shall
be kept free of water during the application and curing of the waterproofing
system.

[REF:term:bmnt]Basement floors-on-ground to be waterproofed
shall have a system of membrane waterproofing provided between 2 layers (metric) of concrete, each of which shall be not less than 75 mm (metric) thick, with the floor membrane made continuous with
the wall membrane to form a complete seal.
This Subsection applies to

clauses.text: a [REF:term:cnd-sp]conditioned space that has a wall, roof or floor assembly, or part thereof, that is in contact with the ground, and
the protection of the [REF:term:cnd-sp]conditioned space described in Clause (a).

content.text: This Subsection addresses the leakage of [REF:term:l]soil gas from the ground into the [REF:term:bldng]building.

All wall, roof and floor assemblies separating [REF:term:cnd-sp]conditioned space from the  ground shall be
protected by an [REF:term:r-brrr]air barrier system conforming
to [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect25.subsect3:long]

Unless the space between the [REF:term:r-brrr]air barrier system and the ground is designed to be accessible for the future installation of a subfloor depressurization system, [REF:term:bldng]buildings shall

clauses.text: be provided with the rough-in for a subfloor depressurization system conforming to [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect13.subsect4.art3:long], or

conform to Parts 5 and 6 for the protection from radon ingress and the means to address high radon concentrations in the future (see [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part5.sect4.subsect1.art1:long] and [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part6.sect2.subsect1.art1:long]).

revisions.title: Rough-in for a Subfloor Depressurization System

content.text: Floors-on-ground shall accommodate the future installation of a subfloor depressurization system by installing a radon vent pipe, and a contiguous gas-permeable layer between the [REF:term:r-brrr]air barrier system and the ground consisting of

clauses.text: a material or materials that allow effective depressurization of that space (see [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect16.subsect2.art1.sent1:long]), or
not less than 100 mm (metric) of coarse clean granular material containing not more than 10% of material that would pass a 4 mm (metric) sieve.

content.text: The radon vent pipe required by [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect13.subsect4.art3.sent1:short] shall

clauses.text: be sealed to maintain the integrity of the [REF:term:r-brrr]air barrier system, with no perforations along the pipe above the [REF:term:r-brrr]air barrier system,
have one or more inlets that allow for the effective depressurization of the gas-permeable layer (see Note A-9.13.4.3.(2)(b) and (3)(b)), and
permit connection to depressurization equipment,
where it passes through [REF:term:cnd-sp]conditioned space, be completely surrounded by [REF:term:cnd-sp]conditioned space,
consist of pipe and fittings in accordance with 7.1.3 of CAN/CGSB-149.11, "Radon control options for new construction in low-rise residential buildings,"
terminate outside the [REF:term:bldng]building in a manner that does not constitute a hazard,
be installed to prevent the accumulation of moisture and away from locations where snow and ice accumulate, and
be clearly labeled every 1.8 m (metric) and at every change in direction to indicate that it is intended only for the future removal of radon from below the floor-on-ground.

content.text: A radon vent pipe shall be deemed to comply with

clauses.text: [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect13.subsect4.art3.sent2.clause2:medium] where its inlet or inlets below the [REF:term:r-brrr]air barrier system are located at or near the centre of the floor-on-ground with gas-permeable material extending not less than 100 mm (metric) beyond any inlet, and

[REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect13.subsect4.art3.sent2.clause6:medium] where it terminates outside the [REF:term:bldng]building, not less than 1.8 m (metric) from a property line, and located in accordance with either 7.2.4.6 or 7.3.4 of CAN/CGSB-149.11, "Radon control options for new construction in low-rise residential buildings," with the opening of the pipe fitted with a corrosion-resistant screen or grille with a mesh opening size of 10 mm (metric) to 12.5 mm (metric) or a product of equivalent air flow performance.

revisions.title: Rough-in for a Subfloor Depressurization System
revisions.change_summary: Struck out "Providing for the" from title

content.text: This Section applies to subsurface drainage and to surface drainage.
Drainage for crawl spaces shall conform to [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect18:long]

Drainage requirements beneath floors-on-ground shall conform
to [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect16:long]

Unless it can be shown to be unnecessary, the bottom of every
exterior [REF:term:fndtn]foundation  wall shall be drained
by drainage tile or pipe laid around the exterior of the [REF:term:fndtn]foundation in conformance with [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect14.subsect3:long] or by a layer of gravel or crushed [REF:term:rck]rock in conformance with [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect14.subsect4:long]

Where mineral fibre insulation or crushed [REF:term:rck]rock backfill is provided adjacent to the exterior surface
of a [REF:term:fndtn]foundation wall,

clauses.text:
the insulation or backfill shall extend to the footing level
to facilitate the drainage of ground water to the [REF:term:fndtn]foundation's drainage system (see [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.appnote92:short]), and

any pyritic material in the crushed [REF:term:rck]rock shall be limited to a concentration that will not damage the [REF:term:bldng]building to a degree that would adversely affect
its stability or the performance of assemblies (see [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect12.subsect3.art3.sent2:long] and [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.appnote14:long]).

content.text: Drain tile and drain pipe for [REF:term:fndtn]foundation drainage shall conform to

clauses.text: [REF:standard:astmc4]
[REF:standard:astmc412m]
[REF:standard:astmc444m]
[REF:standard:astmc700]
[REF:standard:bnq3624-115]
[REF:standard:csab182.1] or
[REF:standard:csag401]

content.text: Drain tile or pipe used for [REF:term:fndtn]foundation drainage shall be not less than 100 mm (metric) in diam.

Drain tile or pipe shall be laid on undisturbed or well-compacted [REF:term:l]soil so that the top of the tile or pipe is below
the bottom of the floor slab or the ground cover of the crawl space.
Drain tile or pipe with butt joints shall be laid with 6 mm (metric) to 10 mm (metric) open joints.

The top half of joints referred to in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect14.subsect3.art3.sent2:short] shall be covered with sheathing paper, 0.10 mm (metric) polyethylene or No. 15 asphalt or tar-saturated felt.

The top and sides of drain pipe or tile shall be covered with
not less than 150 mm (metric) of crushed stone or other coarse
clean granular material containing not more than 10% of material that
will pass a 4 mm (metric) sieve.

Granular material used to drain the bottom of a [REF:term:fndtn]foundation shall consist of a continuous layer
of crushed stone or other coarse clean granular material containing

clauses.text: not more than 10% of material that will pass a 4 mm (metric) sieve, and

no pyritic material in a concentration that will damage the [REF:term:bldng]building to a degree that would adversely affect
its stability or the performance of assemblies (see [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.appnote14:long]).

content.text:
Granular material described in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect14.subsect4.art1:long] shall
be laid on undisturbed or compacted [REF:term:l]soil to
a minimum depth of not less than 125 mm (metric) beneath the footing
of the [REF:term:bldng]building and extend not less than 300 mm (metric) beyond the outside edge of the footings.

The bottom of an [REF:term:xcvtn]excavation drained
by a granular layer shall be graded so that the entire area described
in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect14.subsect4.art2:long] is drained to a sump conforming to [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect14.subsect5.art2:long]

Where because of wet site conditions [REF:term:l]soil becomes mixed with the granular drainage material, sufficient additional
granular material shall be provided so that the top 125 mm (metric) are kept free of [REF:term:l]soil.

[REF:term:fndtn]Foundation drains shall drain to
a sewer, drainage ditch or dry well.
Where a sump pit is provided it shall be

clauses.text: not less than 750 mm (metric) deep,

not less than 0.25 m2
                               (metric) in area, and
provided with a cover.

content.text: Covers for sump pits shall be designed

clauses.text: to resist removal by children, and
to be airtight in accordance with [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect25.subsect3.art3.sent7:long].

content.text:
Where gravity drainage is not practical, an automatic sump pump
shall be provided to discharge the water from the sump pit described
in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect14.subsect5.art2.sent1:short] into a sewer, drainage
ditch or dry well.

Dry wells may be used only when located in areas where the natural [REF:term:grndwtr-]groundwater level is below the bottom of the
dry well.

Dry wells shall be not less than 5 m (metric) from the [REF:term:bldng]building
                           [REF:term:fndtn]foundation and located so that drainage is away from the [REF:term:bldng]building.

The [REF:term:bldng]building shall be located or
the [REF:term:bldng]building site graded so that water
will not accumulate at or near the [REF:term:bldng]building.

articles.title: Drainage away from Wells or Septic Disposal Beds

content.text:
Surface drainage shall be directed away from the location of
a water supply well or septic tank disposal bed.

Every window well shall be drained to the footing level or other
suitable location.

Where runoff water from a driveway is likely to accumulate or
enter a garage, a catch basin shall be installed to provide adequate
drainage.
Downspouts shall conform to [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect26.subsect18.art2:long]

Except as provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect15.subsect1.art2:long]
                           [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect15.subsect1.art3:long], this Section applies
to

clauses.text: concrete or unit masonry [REF:term:fndtn]foundation walls and concrete footings not subject to surcharge

subclauses.text:
on stable [REF:term:l]soils with an allowable bearing
pressure of 75 kPa (metric) or greater, and

for [REF:term:bldng]buildings of wood-frame or masonry
construction,

clauses.text:
wood-frame [REF:term:fndtn]foundation walls and wood
or concrete footings not subject to surcharge

subclauses.text:
on stable [REF:term:l]soils with an allowable bearing
pressure of 75 kPa (metric) or greater, and

for [REF:term:bldng]buildings of wood-frame construction,
and

clauses.text: flat insulating concrete form [REF:term:fndtn]foundation walls and concrete footings not subject to surcharge (see [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.appnote94:short])

subclauses.text:
on stable [REF:term:l]soils with an allowable bearing
pressure of 75 kPa (metric) or greater, and

for [REF:term:bldng]buildings of light-frame or flat
insulating concrete form construction that are not more than 2 storeys
                                  (metric) in [REF:term:bldng-hg]building height, with a maximum floor-to-floor height of 3 m (metric).

content.text:
[REF:term:fndtn]Foundations  for applications other
than as described in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect15.subsect1.art1.sent1:short] shall
be designed in accordance with [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect4:long]

[REF:term:bldng]Buildings  erected on permafrost
shall have [REF:term:fndtn]foundations designed by a [REF:term:dgnr]designer competent in this field in accordance
with the appropriate requirements of [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4:long].

Where the superstructure of a detached [REF:term:bldng]building conforms to the requirements of the deformation resistance test
in [REF:standard:csaz240.2.1] the [REF:term:fndtn]foundation shall be constructed in conformance
with

clauses.text: the remainder of this Section, or
[REF:standard:csaz240.10.1]

content.text: Concrete shall conform to [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect3:long]

Concrete block shall conform to [REF:standard:csaa165.1] and shall have a compressive strength over the average
net cross-sectional area of the block of not less than 15 MPa (metric).

Mortar, grout, mortar joints, corbelling and protection for
unit masonry shall conform to [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect20:long]

For concrete block [REF:term:fndtn]foundation walls
required to be reinforced,

clauses.text: mortar shall be Type S, conforming to [REF:standard:csaa179]
grout shall be coarse, conforming to [REF:standard:csaa179] and
placement of grout shall conform to [REF:standard:csaa371]

content.text:
Where pier-type [REF:term:fndtn]foundations are used,
the piers shall be designed to support the applied loads from the
superstructure.

Where piers are used as a [REF:term:fndtn]foundation system in a [REF:term:bldng]building of 1 [REF:term:tr]storey in [REF:term:bldng-hg]building height, the
piers shall be installed to support the principal framing members
and shall be spaced not more than 3.5 m (metric) apart along the
framing, unless the piers and their footings are designed for larger
spacings.

Where concrete block is used for piers described in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect15.subsect2.art3.sent2:short], they shall be laid with cores placed

content.text: The minimum strip footing widths for interior [REF:term:ldbrng]loadbearing masonry walls shown in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect15.subsect3.art4.table1:long] shall be increased by 100 mm (metric) for each [REF:term:tr]storey of masonry construction supported by the footing.

Footings for interior non-[REF:term:ldbrng]loadbearing masonry walls shall be not less than 200 mm (metric) wide for
walls up to 5.5 m (metric) high and the width shall be increased
by 100 mm (metric) for each additional 2.7 m (metric) of height.

between columns.
Footing thickness shall be not less than the greater of

the width of the projection of the footing beyond the supported
element.

content.text: Where step footings are used,

the horizontal distance between risers shall not be less than 600 mm (metric).

content.text:
For concrete block walls required to be reinforced, continuous
vertical reinforcement shall

clauses.text:
be provided at wall corners, wall ends, wall intersections,

joints,

supported at the top, have not less than 50 mm (metric) embedment
into the footing, if the floor slab does not provide lateral support
at the wall base.

content.text:
For concrete block walls required to be reinforced, a continuous

installed

clauses.text: along the top of the wall,

at the sill and head of all openings greater than 1.20
m (metric) in width, and
at structurally connected floors.

[REF:term:fndtn]Foundation walls shall be considered

clauses.text:
such walls support a [REF:term:sld-m]solid masonry superstructure or flat
insulating concrete form wall,

may run either parallel or perpendicular to the [REF:term:fndtn]foundation walls,
or

ground level and are backfilled on both sides such that the difference

content.text:
Unless the wall around an opening is reinforced to withstand
earth pressure, the portion of the [REF:term:fndtn]foundation wall beneath an opening shall be considered laterally unsupported
if

content.text:

between them.

Flat insulating concrete form [REF:term:fndtn]foundation walls shall be considered to be laterally supported at the top if

of the concrete.

content.text: Vertical reinforcement in flat insulating concrete form [REF:term:fndtn]foundation walls shall be

clauses.text:
located in the inside half of the wall section with a minimum
cover of 30 mm (metric) from the inside face of the concrete wall,
and
where interrupted by wall openings, placed not more than 600 mm (metric) from each side of the openings.

content.text:
Cold joints in flat insulating concrete form [REF:term:fndtn]foundation walls shall be reinforced with no less than one
15M bar spaced at not more than 600 mm (metric) o.c. and embedded 300 mm (metric) on both sides of the joint.

content.text:
Exterior [REF:term:fndtn]foundation walls shall extend
not less than 150 mm (metric) above finished ground level.

Where the top of a [REF:term:fndtn]foundation wall
is reduced in thickness to permit the installation of floor joists,
the reduced section shall be not more than 350 mm (metric) high
and not less than 90 mm (metric) thick.

Where the top of a [REF:term:fndtn]foundation wall
is reduced in thickness to permit the installation of a masonry exterior
facing, the reduced section shall be

clauses.text: not less than 90 mm (metric) thick, and
tied to the facing material with metal ties conforming to [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect20.subsect9.art4.sent3:long] spaced not more than

subclauses.text: 200 mm (metric) o.c. vertically, and
900 mm (metric) o.c. horizontally.

content.text: The space between wall and facing described in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect15.subsect4.art7.sent2:short] shall be filled with mortar.

Corbelling of masonry [REF:term:fndtn]foundation walls supporting [REF:term:cvt-wll]cavity walls shall
conform to [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect20.subsect12.art2:long]

Crack control joints shall be provided in [REF:term:fndtn]foundation walls more than 25 m (metric) long at intervals
of not more than 15 m (metric).

Joints required in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect15.subsect4.art9.sent1:short] shall
be designed to resist moisture penetration and shall be keyed to prevent
relative displacement of the wall portions adjacent to the joint.

Interior masonry [REF:term:fndtn] foundation walls
not subject to lateral earth pressure shall conform to [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect20:long]

subsections.title: Support of Joists and Beams on Masonry Foundation Walls

content.text:
Except as permitted in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect15.subsect5.art1.sent2:short], [REF:term:fndtn]foundation walls of hollow masonry
 units supporting floor joists shall be capped with

clauses.text: not less than 50 mm (metric) of concrete,

[REF:term:sld-m-u]solid masonry units that are 100%
solid and not  less than 50 mm (metric) high, or

semi-solid or hollow [REF:term:sld-m-u]solid masonry units that have  the top course completely filled with mortar, grout or
concrete.

content.text:
Capping required in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect15.subsect5.art1.sent1:short] need
not be provided

clauses.text: in localities where termites are not known to occur,
when the joists are supported on a wood plate not less than 38 mm (metric) by 89 mm (metric), and
when the siding overlaps the [REF:term:fndtn]foundation wall not less than 12 mm (metric).

content.text:
Not less than 190 mm (metric) depth of [REF:term:sld-m]solid masonry shall be provided beneath beams supported on
masonry.

Where the beam referred to in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect15.subsect5.art2.sent1:short] is supported below the top of the [REF:term:fndtn]foundation walls, the ends of such beams shall be protected
from the weather.

Pilasters shall be provided under beams that frame into unit
masonry [REF:term:fndtn]foundation walls 140 mm (metric) or less in thickness.
Pilasters required in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect15.subsect5.art3.sent1:short] shall be not less than 90 mm (metric) by 290 mm (metric) and shall be bonded or tied into the wall.

The top 200 mm (metric) of pilasters required in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect15.subsect5.art3.sent1:short] shall be [REF:term:sld-m-u]solid
masonry with the cells of hollow or semi-solid units  filled
with mortar, grout or concrete.

subsections.title: Parging and Finishing of Masonry Foundation Walls

content.text:
Concrete block [REF:term:fndtn]foundation walls shall
be parged on the exterior face below ground level as required in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect13:long]

Exterior surfaces of concrete block [REF:term:fndtn]foundation walls above ground level shall have tooled joints, or shall be parged
or otherwise suitably finished.

All form ties shall be removed at least flush with the concrete
surface.

This Section applies to floors supported on ground or on granular [REF:term:fll]fill that do not provide structural support for
the superstructure.

Floors-on-ground that support loads from the superstructure
shall be designed in conformance with [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4:long].

All spaces within [REF:term:dwllng-n]dwelling units, except crawl spaces, shall be provided with a floor-on-ground,
where

clauses.text: access is provided to the space, and
a floor supported by the structure is not provided.

content.text: Dampproofing and waterproofing shall conform to [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect13:long]

Except as provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect16.subsect2.art1.sent2:short], not less than 100 mm (metric) of coarse clean granular material
containing not more than 10% of material that will pass a 4
mm  (metric) sieve shall be placed beneath floors-on-ground. (See Note A-9.16.2.1.(1) and see also [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect13.subsect4:long] and [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.appnote88:long])
Granular material need not be installed under

clauses.text: slabs in garages, carports or accessory [REF:term:bldng]buildings, or

[REF:term:bldng]buildings of [REF:term:ndtrl-cc]industrial occupancy where the nature of the process contained
therein permits or requires the use of large openings in the [REF:term:bldng]building envelope even during the winter.

content.text:
Material that is susceptible to changes in volume due to variations
in moisture content or chemical-microbiological oxidation shall not
be used as [REF:term:fll]fill beneath floors-on-ground
in a concentration that will damage the [REF:term:bldng]building to a degree that would adversely affect its stability or the performance
of assemblies. (See also [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect4.subsect4.art4:long] and [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.appnote14:long].)

Material that is susceptible to changes in volume due to freezing
shall not be used as [REF:term:fll]fill beneath floors-on-ground
that will be subjected to freezing temperatures. (See also [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect4.subsect4.art4:long] and [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.appnote14:long].)

Except as provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect16.subsect2.art2.sent4:short], [REF:term:fll]fill beneath floors-on-ground shall be
compacted.

[REF:term:fll]Fill beneath floors-on-ground need
not be compacted where the material is clean coarse aggregate containing
not more than 10% of material that will pass a 4 mm (metric) sieve.

Except as provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect16.subsect3.art2:long] or where it
can be shown to be unnecessary, ingress of water underneath a floor-on-ground
shall be prevented by grading or drainage.

Where [REF:term:grndwtr-]groundwater levels may cause
hydrostatic pressure beneath a floor-on-ground, the floor-on-ground
shall be

clauses.text: a poured concrete slab, and
designed to resist such pressures.

content.text: When floor drains are required (see [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect31:long]), the floor surface shall be sloped so that no water can accumulate.

The finished surface of concrete floor slabs shall be trowelled
smooth and even.

Dry cement shall not be added to the floor surfaces to absorb
surplus water.

When a topping course is provided for a concrete floor slab,
it shall consist of 1 part cement to 2.5 parts clean, well graded
sand by volume, with a water/cement ratio approximately equal to that
of the base slab.
When concrete topping is provided, it shall not be less than 20 mm (metric) thick.

Concrete slabs shall not be less than 75 mm (metric) thick
exclusive of concrete topping.

A bond-breaking material shall be placed between the slab and
footings or [REF:term:rck]rock.
Floors-on-ground constructed of wood shall conform to [REF:standard:csas406]
This Section applies to columns used to support

clauses.text:
beams carrying loads from not more than 2 wood-frame floors
where

subclauses.text:
the supported length of joists bearing on such beams does not
exceed 5 m (metric), and

the [REF:term:lv-ld]live load on any floor does not
exceed 2.4 kPa (metric) (see [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect5.art3.table1:long]),

clauses.text:
beams or header joists carrying loads from not more than 2 levels
of wood-frame balconies, decks or other accessible exterior platforms,
or 1 level plus the roof, where

subclauses.text:
the supported length of joists bearing on such beams or joists
does not exceed 5 m (metric),

the sum of the specified snow and [REF:term:ccpnc]occupancy loads does not exceed 4.8 kP (metric)a (see [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect4.subsect2.art3.sent1:long] for the determination of load on platform-type
constructions), and
the platform serves only a single [REF:term:t]suite of [REF:term:rdntl-cc]residential occupancy, or

clauses.text: carport roofs (see [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect35:long]).

content.text: Columns for applications other than as described in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect17.subsect1.art1.sent1:short] shall be designed in accordance with [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4:long].
Columns shall be centrally located on a footing conforming to [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect15:long]

Columns shall be securely fastened to the supported member to
reduce the likelihood of lateral differential movement between the
column and the supported member. (See also [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect6.art2:long])
Except as permitted by [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect17.subsect2.art2.sent3:short], columns shall be laterally supported to resist racking

clauses.text: directly, or
by connection to the supported members.

content.text:
Columns need not be provided with lateral support as described
in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect17.subsect2.art2.sent2:short], where

clauses.text:
the distance from finished ground to the underside of the joists
is not more than 600 mm (metric), and
the columns support a deck with no superstructure.

content.text:
Except as permitted in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect17.subsect3.art1.sent2:short], steel pipe columns shall have an outside diameter of not less
than 73 mm (metric) and a wall thickness of not less than 4.76 mm (metric).

Columns of sizes other than as specified in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect17.subsect3.art1.sent1:short] are permitted to be used where the [REF:term:ldbrng]loadbearing capacities are shown to be adequate.

Except as permitted in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect17.subsect3.art2.sent2:short], steel columns shall be fitted with not less than 100 mm (metric) by 100 mm (metric) by 6.35 mm (metric) thick steel plates
at each end, and where the column supports a wooden beam, the top
plate shall extend across the full width of the beam.

The top plate required in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect17.subsect3.art2.sent1:short] need not be provided where a column supports a steel beam and provision
is made for the attachment of the column to the beam.

Exterior steel columns shall be treated on the outside surface
with at least one coat of rust-inhibitive paint.

Where the imposed load does not exceed 36 kN (metric), adjustable
steel columns shall conform to [REF:standard:cgsb-7.2]

Steel columns other than those described in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect17.subsect3.art4.sent1:short] shall be designed in accordance with
Part 4.

The width or diameter of a wood column shall be not less than
the width of the supported member.

Except as provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect35.subsect4.art2:long], columns shall
be not less than 184 mm (metric) for round columns and 140 mm (metric) by 140 mm (metric) for rectangular columns, unless calculations
are provided to show that lesser sizes are adequate.
Wood columns shall be either solid, glued-laminated or built-up.
Built-up columns shall consist of not less than 38 mm (metric) thick full-length members

clauses.text:
bolted together with not less than 9.52 mm (metric) diam
bolts spaced not more than 450 mm (metric) o.c., or

nailed together with not less than 76 mm (metric) nails
spaced not more than 300 mm (metric) o.c.

content.text: Glued-laminated columns shall conform to [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect3:long]

Wood columns shall be separated from concrete in contact with
the ground by 0.05 mm (metric) polyethylene film or Type S roll
roofing.
Unit masonry columns shall be built of masonry units

clauses.text: conforming to [REF:standard:csaa165.1] and

having a compressive strength over the net area of the block
of not less than 15 MPa (metric).

content.text: Unit masonry columns shall be not less than 290 mm (metric) by 290 mm (metric) or 240 mm (metric) by 380 mm (metric) in size.
Concrete shall conform to [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect3:long]

Concrete columns shall be not less than 200 mm (metric) by 200 mm (metric) for rectangular columns and 230 mm (metric) diam
for circular columns.

This Section applies to crawl spaces whose exterior walls have
less than 25% of their total area above exterior ground level open
to the outdoors.

[REF:term:fndtn]Foundations  enclosing crawl spaces
shall conform to [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect15:long]
Crawl spaces shall be considered to be heated where the space

clauses.text: is used as a hot air [REF:term:plnm]plenum,

contains heating ducts that are not sealed and insulated to
minimize heat loss to the space, or
is not separated from heated space in accordance with [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect25:long]

content.text: Heating of heated crawl spaces shall conform to [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect33:long]

Insulation, an [REF:term:r-brrr]air barrier system and a [REF:term:vpr-brrr]vapour barrier shall be installed
in the walls of heated crawl spaces in accordance with [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect25:long]

An access opening of not less than 500 mm (metric) by 700 mm (metric) shall be provided to each crawl space where the crawl
space serves a single [REF:term:dwllng-n]dwelling unit,
and not less than 550 mm (metric) by 900 mm (metric) for other
crawl spaces.

Access openings shall be fitted with a door or hatch, except
when the crawl space is heated and the access opening into the crawl
space is from an adjacent heated space.

Unheated crawl spaces shall be ventilated by natural or mechanical
means.

Where an unheated crawl space is ventilated by natural means,
ventilation shall be provided to the outside air by not less than 0.1 m2
                            (metric) of unobstructed vent area for every 50 m2
                            (metric) of [REF:term:flr-r]floor area.
Vents shall be

clauses.text: uniformly distributed on opposite sides of the [REF:term:bldng]building, and
designed to prevent the entry of snow, rain and insects.

content.text: Heated crawl spaces shall be ventilated in accordance with [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect32:long]

Where equipment requiring service such as plumbing cleanouts,
traps and burners is located in crawl spaces, an access way with a
height and width of not less than 600 mm (metric) shall be provided
from the access door to the equipment and for a distance of 900 mm (metric) on the side or sides of the equipment to be serviced.

Except where it can be shown to be unnecessary, the ingress
of water into a crawl space shall be controlled by grading or drainage.

Drainage of [REF:term:fndtn]foundation walls shall
conform to [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect14.subsect2.art1:long]

Drainage of the ground cover or floor-on-ground in the crawl
space shall conform to [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect16.subsect3:long]
Drains shall conform to [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect14:long]

articles.title: Ground Cover in Unheated Crawl Spaces

content.text:
Where a crawl space is unheated, a ground cover shall be provided
consisting of not less than

clauses.text: 50 mm (metric) of asphalt,
100 mm (metric) of 15 MPa (metric) Portland cement concrete,
Type S roll roofing, or
0.10 mm (metric) polyethylene.

content.text: Joints in sheet-type ground cover required in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect18.subsect6.art1.sent1:short] shall be lapped not less than 100 mm (metric) and weighted down.

articles.title: Ground Cover in Heated Crawl Spaces

content.text:
Where a crawl space is heated, a ground cover consisting of
not less than 0.15 mm (metric) polyethylene sheet conforming to [REF:standard:cgsb-51.34] shall be installed as part
of an [REF:term:r-brrr]air barrier system in accordance
with [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect25.subsect3:long]

The ground cover required in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect18.subsect6.art2.sent1:short] shall have its joints lapped not less than 300
mm (metric), and

clauses.text: be sealed and evenly weighted down, or
be covered with concrete not less than 50 mm (metric) thick.

content.text:
The perimeter of the ground cover required in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect18.subsect6.art2.sent1:short] shall be sealed to the [REF:term:fndtn]foundation wall. (See [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.appnote88:long]
                           [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.appnote145:long], [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.appnote146:long].)

All penetrations of the ground cover required in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect18.subsect6.art2.sent1:short] shall be sealed against air leakage.
(See [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect25.subsect3:long])

articles.title: Crawl Spaces as Warm Air Plenums

content.text:
Only crawl spaces under 1-[REF:term:tr]storey portions
of [REF:term:dwllng-n]dwelling units shall be used as warm-air [REF:term:plnm]plenums.

Enclosing material in crawl spaces described in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect18.subsect7.art1.sent1:short], including insulation, shall have
a surface [REF:term:flm-prd-]flame-spread rating  not greater
than 150.

[REF:term:cmbtbl]Combustible ground cover in crawl
spaces described in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect18.subsect7.art1.sent1:short] shall
be protected beneath each register opening with [REF:term:ncmbtbl]noncombustible material.

The [REF:term:ncmbtbl]noncombustible register protection
described in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect18.subsect7.art1.sent3:short] shall

clauses.text:
extend not less than 300 mm (metric) beyond the projection
of the register opening, and
have up-turned edges.

content.text:
Except where it can be shown to be unnecessary, where insulation
is installed between a ceiling and the underside of the roof sheathing,
a space shall be provided between the insulation and the sheathing,
and vents shall be installed to permit the transfer of moisture from
the space to the exterior. (See [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.appnote101:short].)

Except as provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect19.subsect1.art2.sent2:short], the unobstructed vent area shall be not less than 1/300 of the
insulated ceiling area.

Where the roof slope is less than 1 in 6 or in roofs that are
constructed with roof joists, the unobstructed vent area shall be
not less than 1/150 of the insulated ceiling area.

Required vents may be roof type, eave type, gable-end type or
any combination thereof, and shall be distributed

clauses.text: uniformly on opposite sides of the [REF:term:bldng]building,

with not less than 25% of the required openings located at the
top of the space, and

with not less than 25% of the required openings located at the
bottom of the space.

content.text:
Except where each joist space is separately vented, roof joist
spaces shall be interconnected by installing purlins not less than 38 mm (metric) by 38 mm (metric) on the top of the roof joists.
Vents shall comply with [REF:standard:csaa93]

Except as provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect19.subsect1.art3.sent2:short], not less than 63 mm (metric) of space shall be provided between
the top of the insulation and the underside of the roof sheathing.

At the junction of sloped roofs and exterior walls, where preformed
baffles are used to contain the insulation, the baffles shall

clauses.text:
provide an unobstructed air space, between the insulation and
the underside of the roof sheathing, that is

subclauses.text: not less than 25 mm (metric) in dimension, and
of sufficient cross area to meet the [REF:term:ttc-r-rf]attic or roof space venting requirements of [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect19.subsect1.art2:long], and

clauses.text:
extend vertically not less than 50 mm (metric) above the
top of the insulation.

content.text:
Ceiling insulation shall be installed in a manner that will
not restrict the free flow of air through roof vents or through any
portion of the [REF:term:ttc-r-rf]attic or roof space.

The lower portion of a mansard or gambrel style roof need not
be ventilated.

The upper portion of roofs described in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect19.subsect1.art4.sent1:short] shall be ventilated in conformance with [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect19.subsect1.art1:long]
                           [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect19.subsect1.art3:long]

Every [REF:term:ttc-r-rf]attic or roof space shall
be provided with an access hatch where the open space in the [REF:term:ttc-r-rf]attic or roof space  measures

clauses.text:
3 m2
                               (metric) or more in area,
1 m (metric) or more in length or width, and

600 mm (metric) or more in height over at least the area
described in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect19.subsect2.art1.sent1.clause1:short]
                              [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect19.subsect2.art1.sent1.clause2:short].

content.text:
The hatch required in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect19.subsect2.art1.sent1:short] shall be not less than 550 mm (metric) by 900 mm (metric) except that, where the hatch serves not more than one [REF:term:dwllng-n]dwelling unit, the hatch may be reduced to 0.32 m2
                            (metric) in area with no dimension less than 500 mm (metric).
Hatchways to [REF:term:ttc-r-rf]attic or roof spaces shall be fitted with doors or covers.

sections.title:
Masonry and Insulating Concrete Form Walls Not In Contact with
the Ground

content.text:
Except as provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect20.subsect1.art2:long], this Section
applies to

clauses.text:
unreinforced masonry and masonry veneer walls not in contact
with the ground, where

subclauses.text: the height of the walls constructed on the [REF:term:fndtn]foundation walls does not exceed 11 m (metric), and

the roof or floor assembly above the [REF:term:frt-tr]first
storey is not of concrete construction, and

clauses.text:
flat insulating concrete form walls not in contact with the
ground that (see [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.appnote94:short])

subclauses.text: have a maximum floor-to-floor height of 3 m (metric),

are erected in [REF:term:bldng]buildings not more
than 2 storeys
                                  (metric) in [REF:term:bldng-hg]building height, and

are erected in locations where the seismic design parameter,
S_{max}, for Site Class C is not greater than 0.27 (see also [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect4.subsect2.art5:long]).

content.text:
For walls other than those described in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect20.subsect1.art1.sent1:short], or where the masonry walls or insulating concrete
form walls not in contact with the ground are designed for specified
loads on the basis of ultimate and serviceability limit states, [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect3.subsect2:long] shall apply.

In locations where the seismic design parameter, S_{max}, for Site
Class C is greater than 0.37, [REF:term:ldbrng]loadbearing elements
of masonry [REF:term:bldng]buildings more than 1 [REF:term:tr]storey in [REF:term:bldng-hg]building height shall be reinforced with not less than the minimum amount of reinforcement
required by [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect20.subsect15:long]

In locations where the seismic design parameter, S_{max}, for Site
Class C is greater than 0.23 but not greater than 0.37, [REF:term:ldbrng]loadbearing elements of masonry [REF:term:bldng]buildings 3 [REF:term:tr]storeys  in [REF:term:bldng-hg]building height shall be reinforced with not
less than the minimum amount of reinforcement required by [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect20.subsect15:long]
Masonry units shall comply with

clauses.text: [REF:standard:astmc73]
[REF:standard:astmc126]
[REF:standard:astmc212]
[REF:standard:csaa82]
[REF:standard:csaa165.1]
[REF:standard:csaa165.2] or
[REF:standard:csaa165.3]

content.text:
Used bricks shall be free of old mortar, soot or other surface
coating and shall conform to [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect20.subsect2.art1:long]
Glass blocks shall not be used as [REF:term:ldbrng]loadbearing units or in the construction of fireplaces or [REF:term:chmn]chimneys.

Masonry made with cellular concrete shall not be used in contact
with the [REF:term:l]soil or exposed to the weather.
Stone shall be sound and durable.

articles.title: Concrete Blocks Exposed to the Weather

content.text:
Concrete blocks exposed to the weather shall have density and
water absorption characteristics conforming to concrete types A, B,
C, or D described in [REF:standard:csaa165.1]
The compressive strength of concrete blocks shall conform to [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect20.subsect2.art7.table1:long]

content.title: Compressive Strength of Concrete Blocks

header_rows.content:
Minimum
Compressive Strength Over Net Area, MPa

content.text:
Cementitious materials and aggregates for mortar and grout shall
comply with [REF:standard:csaa179]

Water and aggregate shall be clean and free of significant amounts
of deleterious materials.
Lime used in mortar shall be hydrated.

If lime putty is used in mortar, it shall be made by slaking
quicklime in water for not less than 24 h (metric) or soaking
hydrated lime in water for not less than 12 h (metric).
Mortar types shall be in accordance with [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect20.subsect3.art2.table1:long].
Mortar for glass block masonry shall be

clauses.text: Type S Portland cement-lime where exposed to the exterior, or
Type S or N where protected from the exterior.

content.text:
Mortar shall be mixed within the proportion limits provided
in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect20.subsect3.art2.table2:long], with sufficient water to bring the
mixture to a consistency adequate for laying masonry units.

Grout shall be mixed within the proportion limits provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect20.subsect3.art2.table3:long], with sufficient water to provide a suitable flow
to fill all voids completely, without excessive segregation or bleeding.
Except as provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect20.subsect3.art2.sent6:short], mortar shall be used and placed in final position

clauses.text:
within 1.5 h (metric) after mixing when the air temperature
is 25°C or higher, or

within 2.5 h (metric) after mixing when the air temperature
is less than 25°C.

content.text:
Mortar and grout containing a set-control admixture shall be
manufactured off-site in a batching plant and shall be used and placed
in final position within a time not exceeding the useful life stipulated
by the manufacturer.

Grout used for reinforced masonry shall be placed in accordance
with the requirements of [REF:standard:csaa371]

content.title: Mortar Use
Mortar Mix Proportions (by volume)
Grout Mix Proportions (by volume)

body_rows.content: 2¼ to 3 times the sum of the cement and lime volumes
1 to 2 times the sum of the cement and lime volumes

content.text:
Except as provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect20.subsect4.art1.sent2:short], mortar joint thickness for burned clay brick and concrete masonry
units shall be 10 mm (metric).

Permitted tolerances in head and bed joints shall be not more
than ± 5 mm (metric).

Hollow masonry units shall be laid with mortar applied to head
and bed joints of both inner and outer face shells.

Vertically aligned webs of hollow masonry units shall be laid
in a full bed of mortar

clauses.text: under the starting course,
in all courses of columns, and

where adjacent to cells or cavities that are to be filled with
grout.

content.text:
Except for head joints left open for weep holes and ventilation, [REF:term:sld-m-u]solid masonry units shall be laid with full
head and bed joints.

All masonry shall be supported on masonry, concrete or steel,
except that masonry veneer walls may be supported on [REF:term:fndtn]foundations of wood frame constructed in conformance with [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect15.subsect2.art4.sent1:long]. (See [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.appnote104:short].)

Every masonry wall shall be at least as thick as the wall it
supports, except as otherwise permitted in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect20.subsect12.art2:long]

Masonry over openings shall be supported by steel, masonry or
reinforced concrete lintels, or masonry arches.

Steel angle lintels supporting masonry veneer above openings
shall

clauses.text: conform to [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect20.subsect5.art2.table1:long], and
have a bearing length not less than 90 mm (metric).

content.title:
Maximum Allowable Spans for Steel Lintels Supporting Masonry
Veneer

content.text:
Steel angle lintels supporting masonry other than veneer, masonry
and reinforced concrete lintels, and masonry arches shall be designed
in accordance with [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4:long] to support the imposed
load.

Steel angle lintels supporting masonry shall be prime painted
or otherwise protected from corrosion.

Masonry exterior walls, other than [REF:term:cvt-wll]cavity
walls, in 1-[REF:term:tr]storey
                           [REF:term:bldng]buildings and the top [REF:term:tr] storeys of
2- and 3-[REF:term:tr]storey
                           [REF:term:bldng] buildings shall be not less than 140 mm (metric) thick, provided the walls
are not more than 2.8 m (metric) high at the eaves and  4.6
m (metric) high at the peaks of gable ends.

The exterior walls of the bottom [REF:term:tr]storeys of 2-[REF:term:tr]storey
                           [REF:term:bldng]buildings, and exterior walls of the bottom 2 [REF:term:tr]storeys of 3-[REF:term:tr]storey
                           [REF:term:bldng]buildings shall be not less than 190 mm (metric) thick.

In exterior walls composed of more than one wythe, each wythe
shall be not less than 90 mm (metric) thick.

[REF:term:cvt-wll]Cavity walls shall be made with
not less than 90 mm (metric) wide units if the joints are raked
and not less than 75 mm (metric) wide units if the joints are
not raked.
The width of a cavity in a [REF:term:cvt-wll]cavity wall  shall be not less than 50 mm (metric) and not greater than 150 mm (metric).

The minimum thickness of [REF:term:cvt-wll]cavity walls  above the supporting base shall be 230 mm (metric) for the top  7.6 m (metric) and 330 mm (metric) for the remaining portion,
except that where 75 mm (metric) wide units are used, the wall
height above the top of the [REF:term:fndtn]foundation wall
shall not exceed  6 m (metric).

The thickness of [REF:term:ldbrng] loadbearing interior
walls shall be determined on the basis of the maximum lateral support
spacing as provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect20.subsect10.art1.sent2:long]
                           [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect20.subsect10.art1.sent3:short].
The thickness of interior non-[REF:term:ldbrng]loadbearing walls shall be

clauses.text:
determined on the basis of the maximum lateral support spacing
as provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect20.subsect10.art1.sent2:long]
                              [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect20.subsect10.art1.sent3:short], and
in any case, not less than 65 mm (metric).

content.text:
Except for masonry veneer where each masonry unit is supported
individually by the structural backing, masonry veneer shall consist
of [REF:term:sld-m-u]solid masonry units not less than 75 mm (metric) thick.

Veneer described in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect20.subsect6.art4.sent1:short] over
wood-frame walls shall have not less than a 25 mm (metric) air
space behind the veneer.

Masonry veneer less than 90 mm (metric) thick shall have
unraked joints.

Masonry veneer shall conform to [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect3.subsect2:long], where the masonry units are required to be individually supported
by the structural backing.

The height of parapet walls above the adjacent roof surface
shall be not more than 3 times (metric) the parapet wall thickness.
Parapet walls shall be [REF:term:sld-m]solid masonry

clauses.text:
with the cells of hollow or semi-solid units filled with mortar,
grout, or concrete, and
that extends from the top of the parapet to not less than 300 mm (metric) below the adjacent roof level.

content.text:
Slab and panel facings of precast concrete and natural or artificial
stone shall conform to [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect3.subsect2:long]

Except as permitted in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect20.subsect7.art2.sent2:long] and [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect20.subsect7.art4:long], the depth of any chase or recess shall not exceed
one third the thickness of the wall, and the width of the chase or
recess shall not exceed 500 mm (metric).

Except as permitted in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect20.subsect7.art2.sent2:short] and [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect20.subsect7.art4:long], no chase or recess shall be constructed
in any wall 190 mm (metric) or less in thickness.

Recesses may be constructed in 190 mm (metric) walls provided
they do not exceed 100 mm (metric) in depth, 750 mm (metric) in height and 500 mm (metric) in width.
Chases and recesses shall be not less than

clauses.text: 4 times the wall thickness apart, and

600 mm (metric) away from any pilaster, cross wall, buttress
or other vertical element providing required lateral support for the
wall.

content.text:
Chases or recesses that do not conform to the limits specified
in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect20.subsect7.art1:long]
                           [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect20.subsect7.art3:long] shall be considered as openings, and any masonry
supported above such a chase or recess shall be supported by a lintel
or arch as provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect20.subsect5.art2:long]

articles.title: Chases or Recesses Cut into Walls

content.text:
Chases and recesses shall not be cut into walls made with hollow
units after the masonry units are in place.

Except as permitted in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect20.subsect8.art1.sent2:short], [REF:term:ldbrng]loadbearing walls of hollow masonry
units supporting roof or floor framing members shall be capped with
not less than 50 mm (metric) of [REF:term:sld-m]solid masonry or have the top course filled with concrete.

Capping required in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect20.subsect8.art1.sent1:short] may
be omitted where the roof framing is supported on a wood plate not
less than 38 mm (metric) by 89 mm (metric).
Floor joists supported on [REF:term:cvt-wll]cavity walls  shall be supported on [REF:term:sld-m-u]solid masonry units not less than 57 mm (metric) high.
Floor joists described in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect20.subsect8.art2.sent1:short] shall not project into the cavity.
Roof and ceiling framing members bearing on [REF:term:cvt-wll]cavity walls shall be supported on

clauses.text: [REF:term:sld-m-u]solid masonry units not less than 57 mm (metric) high that bridge the full thickness of the wall, or

a wood plate not less than 38 mm (metric) thick, bearing
 not less than 50 mm (metric) on each wythe.

content.text:
The bearing area under beams and joists shall be sufficient
to carry the supported load.

In no case shall the minimum length of end bearing of beams
supported on masonry be less than 90 mm (metric).

The length of end bearing of floor, roof or ceiling joists supported
on masonry shall be not less than 40 mm (metric).

Beams and columns supported on masonry walls shall be supported
on pilasters where the thickness of the masonry wall or wythe is less
than 190 mm (metric).

Not less than 190 mm (metric) depth of [REF:term:sld-m]solid masonry or concrete shall be provided under the beam
or column referred to in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect20.subsect8.art4.sent1:short].
Pilasters required in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect20.subsect8.art4.sent1:short] shall be bonded or tied to masonry walls.
Concrete pilasters required in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect20.subsect8.art4.sent1:short] shall be not less than 50 mm (metric) by 300 mm (metric).
Unit masonry pilasters required in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect20.subsect8.art4.sent1:short] shall be not less than 100 mm (metric) by 290 mm (metric).

articles.title: Projection of Masonry Veneer Beyond Supporting Members

content.text:
Masonry veneer of [REF:term:sld-m-u]solid masonry units resting on a bearing support shall not project more than one third
of the thickness of the veneer. (See [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.appnote105:short].)
Where the masonry veneer described in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect20.subsect8.art5.sent1:short] is rough stone masonry,

clauses.text:
the projection shall be measured as the average projection of
the units, and

the thickness of the veneer shall be measured as the average
thickness of the veneer.

articles.title: Joints to be Offset or Reinforced

content.text:
Vertical joints in adjacent masonry courses shall be offset
unless each wythe of masonry is reinforced with the equivalent of
not less than 2 corrosion-resistant (metric) steel bars of 3.76 mm (metric) diam placed in the horizontal joints at vertical intervals
not exceeding  460 mm (metric).

Where joints in the reinforcing referred to in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect20.subsect9.art1.sent1:short] occur, the bars shall be lapped not
less than 150 mm (metric).

articles.title: Bonding or Tying of Other than Masonry Veneer

content.text:
Except as provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect20.subsect9.art5:long] regarding
masonry veneer, masonry walls that consist of 2 or more wythes shall
have the wythes bonded or tied together with masonry bonding units
as described in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect20.subsect9.art3:long] or with metal ties as
described in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect20.subsect9.art4:long]

Where wythes are bonded together with masonry units, the bonding
units shall comprise not less than 4% of the wall surface area.

Bonding units described in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect20.subsect9.art3.sent1:short] shall be spaced not more than 600 mm (metric) vertically and
horizontally in the case of brick masonry and 900 mm o.c. (metric) in the case of block or tile.

Units described in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect20.subsect9.art3.sent1:short] shall
extend not less than 90 mm (metric) into adjacent wythes.

Where 2 or more wythes are tied together with metal ties of the individual rod type, the ties
shall conform to the requirements in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect20.subsect9.art4.sent3:short]
                           [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect20.subsect9.art4.sent6:short].

Other ties may be used where it can be shown that such ties
provide walls that are at least as strong and as durable as those
made with the individual
rod type.
Metal ties of the individual rod type shall

clauses.text: be corrosion-resistant,

have a minimum cross-sectional area of not less than 17.8
mm2
                               (metric), and

have not less than a 50 mm (metric) portion bent at right
angles at each end.

content.text: Metal ties of the individual rod type shall

clauses.text:
extend from within 25 mm (metric) of the outer face of the
wall to within 25 mm (metric) of the inner face of the wall,

be completely embedded in mortar except for the portion exposed
in [REF:term:cvt-wll]cavity walls, and
be staggered from course to course.

content.text:
Where 2 or more wythes in walls other than [REF:term:cvt-wll]cavity walls and masonry veneer/masonry backing walls are
tied together with metal ties of the individual rod type, the space
between wythes shall be completely filled with mortar.

Ties described in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect20.subsect9.art4.sent5:short] shall
be

clauses.text:
located within 300 mm (metric) of openings and spaced not
more than 900 mm (metric) apart around openings, and

spaced not more than 900 mm (metric) apart horizontally
and 460 mm (metric) apart vertically at other locations.

content.text:
Except as required in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect20.subsect9.art4.sent8:short]
                           [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect20.subsect9.art4.sent9:short], where the inner and outer wythes of [REF:term:cvt-wll]cavity walls are tied with individual wire
ties, the ties shall be spaced not more than  900 mm (metric) apart
horizontally and  400 mm (metric) apart vertically.

Within 100 mm (metric) of the bottom of each floor or roof
assembly where the cavity extends below the assemblies, the ties described
in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect20.subsect9.art4.sent7:short] shall be spaced not more
than 600 mm (metric) apart horizontally.

Within 300 mm (metric) of any openings, the ties described
in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect20.subsect9.art4.sent7:short] shall be spaced not more
than 900 mm (metric) apart.

Masonry veneer 75 mm (metric) or more in thickness and resting
on a bearing support shall be tied to masonry backing or to wood framing
members with straps that are

clauses.text: corrosion-resistant,
not less than 0.76 mm thick (metric),
not less than 22 mm wide (metric),
shaped to provide a key with the mortar,

pre-bent during manufacture to a right angle within 6
mm (metric) of the fastener hole,
fastened with

subclauses.text:
corrosion-resistant wood screws conforming to [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect3.art1.sent3:long] that have a minimum diameter of 4.16 mm (metric)
                                 (No. 8) (metric) and a wood penetration of not less than 38 mm (metric), or

corrosion-resistant common spiral nails conforming to [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect3.art1.sent1:long] that are not less than 76 mm long (metric) and
have a wood penetration of not less than 63 mm (metric), and

clauses.text: spaced in accordance with [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect20.subsect9.art5.table1:long]

content.title: Veneer Tie Spacing

content.text:
Where hot-dipped,
zinc-coated straps are used to meet the requirements of [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect20.subsect9.art5.sent1:short], they shall be pre-bent and pre-drilled
or pre-punched prior to hot-dip, zinc-coated galvanizing.

Masonry veneer individually supported by masonry or wood-frame
backing shall be secured to the backing in conformance with [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect3.subsect2:long]

Glass block shall have horizontal joint reinforcement of 2 corrosion-resistant
bars of not less than 3.76 mm (metric) diam or expanded metal
strips not less than 75 mm (metric) wide

clauses.text: spaced at vertical intervals of not more than 600 mm (metric) for units 200 mm (metric) or less in height, and
installed in every horizontal joint for units higher than 200 mm (metric).

content.text: Reinforcement required in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect20.subsect9.art6.sent1:short] shall be lapped not less than 150 mm (metric).

Masonry walls shall be laterally supported by floor or roof
construction or by intersecting masonry walls or buttresses.
The spacing of supports required in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect20.subsect10.art1.sent1:short] shall be not more than

clauses.text:
20 times the wall thickness for all [REF:term:ldbrng]loadbearing  walls and exterior non-[REF:term:ldbrng]loadbearing walls,
and
36 times the wall thickness for interior non-[REF:term:ldbrng]loadbearing  walls.

content.text:
In applying [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect20.subsect10.art1.sent2:short], the thickness
of [REF:term:cvt-wll]cavity walls shall be taken as the
greater of

clauses.text: two-thirds of the sum of the thicknesses of the wythes, or
the thickness of the thicker wythe.

content.text:
Floor and roof constructions providing lateral support for walls
as required in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect20.subsect10.art1.sent1:short] shall be constructed
to transfer lateral loads to walls or buttresses approximately at
right angles to the laterally supported walls.

subsections.title: Anchorage of Roofs, Floors and Intersecting Walls

articles.title:
Anchorage to Floor or Roof Assemblies where Masonry Walls Require
Lateral Support

content.text:
Where required to receive lateral support (see [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect20.subsect10:long]), masonry walls shall be anchored to each
floor or roof assembly at maximum intervals of 2 m (metric), except
that anchorage to floor joists not more than 1 m (metric) above [REF:term:grade]grade may be omitted.

Anchors required in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect20.subsect11.art1.sent1:short] shall
be corrosion-resistant and be not less than the equivalent of 40 mm (metric) by 4.76 mm (metric) thick steel straps.

Anchors required in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect20.subsect11.art1.sent1:short] shall
be shaped to provide a mechanical key with the masonry and shall be
securely fastened to the horizontal support to develop the full strength
of the anchor.

When joists are parallel to the wall, anchors required in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect20.subsect11.art1.sent1:short] shall extend across not less than
3 joists.

articles.title:
Bonding and Tying Intersecting Masonry Walls where Walls Require
Lateral Support

content.text:
Where required to provide lateral support, intersecting walls
shall be bonded or tied together.

Where bonding is used to satisfy the requirements of [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect20.subsect11.art2.sent1:short], 50% of the adjacent masonry units
in the intersecting wall, distributed uniformly over the height of
the intersection, shall be embedded in the laterally supported wall.
Where tying is used to satisfy the requirements of [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect20.subsect11.art2.sent1:short], the ties shall be

clauses.text: corrosion-resistant metal,

equivalent to not less than 4.76 mm (metric) by 40
mm (metric) steel strapping,
spaced not more than 800 mm (metric) o.c. vertically, and

shaped at both ends to provide sufficient mechanical key to
develop the strength of the ties.

articles.title: Anchoring Intersecting Wood-Frame Walls to Masonry Walls

content.text:
Wood-frame walls shall be anchored to masonry walls that they
intersect with not less than 4.76 mm (metric) diam corrosion-resistant
steel rods spaced not more than 900 mm (metric) o.c. vertically.

Anchors required in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect20.subsect11.art3.sent1:short] shall
be fastened to the wood framing at one end and shaped to provide a
mechanical key at the other end to develop the strength of the anchor.

articles.title: Anchoring Wood-Frame Roof Systems to Masonry Walls

content.text:
Except as permitted in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect20.subsect11.art4.sent2:short], roof systems of wood-frame construction shall be anchored to exterior
masonry walls by not less than 12.7 mm (metric) diam anchor bolts,

clauses.text: spaced not more than 2.4 m (metric) apart,

embedded not less than 90 mm (metric) into the masonry,
and
fastened to a rafter plate of not less than 38 mm (metric) thick lumber.

content.text:
The roof system described in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect20.subsect11.art4.sent1:short] is permitted to be anchored by nailing the wall furring strips to the side of the
rafter plate.

articles.title: Anchoring Masonry Cornices, Sills and Trim to Masonry Walls

content.text:
Cornices, sills or other trim of masonry material which project
beyond the wall face shall have not less than 65% of their mass, but
not less than 90 mm (metric), within the wall or shall be adequately
anchored to the wall with corrosion-resistant anchors.

Where anchor bolts are to be placed in the top of a masonry
pier, the pier shall conform to the requirements of [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect15.subsect2.art3.sent4:long] and shall be capped with concrete or reinforced
masonry not less than 200 mm (metric) thick.

All corbelling shall consist of [REF:term:sld-m-u]solid
masonry units.

The units referred to in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect20.subsect12.art1.sent1:short] shall be corbelled so that the horizontal projection of any unit
does not exceed 25 mm (metric) and the total projection does not
exceed one third of the total wall thickness.

[REF:term:cvt-wll]Cavity walls of greater thickness
than the [REF:term:fndtn]foundation wall on which they
rest shall not be corbelled but may project 25 mm (metric) over
the outer face of the [REF:term:fndtn]foundation wall disregarding
parging.

Where the [REF:term:fndtn] foundation wall referred
to in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect20.subsect12.art2.sent1:short] is unit masonry, it
is permitted to be corbelled to meet flush with the inner face of
a [REF:term:cvt-wll]cavity wall provided

clauses.text:
the projection of each course does not exceed half the height
or one third the thickness of the corbelled unit, and
the total corbel does not exceed one third of the [REF:term:fndtn]foundation wall thickness.

content.text:
Masonry veneer resting on a bearing support shall not project
more than 25 mm (metric) beyond the supporting base where the
veneer is not less than 90 mm (metric) thick, and 12 mm (metric) beyond the supporting base where the veneer is less than 90 mm (metric) thick.

In the case of rough stone veneer, the projection, measured
as the average projection of the stone units, shall not exceed one-third
the bed width beyond the supporting base.
