Materials used for flashing shall conform to [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect20.subsect13.art1.table1:long]

content.title: Flashing Materials

body_rows.content:
Copper or aluminum laminated to felt or kraft
paper

content.text:
Aluminum flashing in contact with masonry or concrete shall
be effectively coated or separated from the masonry or concrete by
an impervious membrane.

Fastening devices for flashing shall be corrosion-resistant
and, where metal flashing is used, shall be compatible with the flashing
with respect to galvanic action.
Flashing shall be installed in masonry and masonry veneer walls

clauses.text: beneath jointed masonry window sills,
over the back and top of parapet walls,
over the heads of glass block panels,
beneath weep holes, and

over the heads of window or door openings in exterior walls
when the vertical distance between the top of a window or door frame
and the bottom edge of the eave exceeds one-quarter of the horizontal
eave overhang.

content.text:
When installed beneath jointed masonry window sills or over
the heads of openings, flashing shall extend from the front edge of
the masonry up behind the sill or lintel.

articles.title: Flashing for Weep Holes in Masonry/Masonry Walls

content.text:
Flashing beneath weep holes in [REF:term:cvt-wll]cavity
walls and masonry veneer/masonry backing walls shall

clauses.text: be bedded not less than 25 mm (metric) in the inside wythe,

extend to not less than 5 mm (metric) beyond the outer face
of the [REF:term:bldng]building element below the flashing,
and

be installed with a nominally horizontal slope toward the outside
wythe.

articles.title: Flashing for Weep Holes in Masonry Veneer

content.text:
Flashing beneath weep holes in masonry veneer over masonry backing
walls shall conform to the flashing requirements for [REF:term:cvt-wll]cavity walls and masonry veneer/masonry backing
walls in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect20.subsect13.art5:long]

Flashing beneath weep holes in masonry veneer over wood-frame
walls shall be installed so that it extends from a point not less
than 5 mm (metric) beyond the outer face of the [REF:term:bldng]building element below the flashing to a point 150 mm (metric) up the wood-frame wall.

Where the frame wall is sheathed with a sheathing membrane,
a non-wood-based rigid exterior insulating sheathing or a semi-rigid
insulating sheathing with an integral sheathing membrane, the flashing
shall be installed behind the sheathing membrane or insulating sheathing.

Flashing described in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect20.subsect13.art6.sent2:short] is permitted to conform to the requirements for concealed flashing
in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect20.subsect13.art1.table1:long]
Joints in flashing shall be made watertight.

Weep holes spaced not more than 800 mm (metric) apart shall
be provided at the bottom of

clauses.text: cavities in [REF:term:cvt-wll]cavity walls, and
cavities or air spaces in masonry veneer walls.

content.text:
The cavities or air spaces described in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect20.subsect13.art8.sent1:short] shall include those above lintels over window and door
openings required to be flashed in conformance with [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect20.subsect13.art3:long]

Except as provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect20.subsect13.art9.sent3:short], where the interior finish of the exterior walls of a [REF:term:bldng]building is a type that may be damaged by moisture,
exterior masonry walls, other than [REF:term:cvt-wll]cavity walls or walls that are protected for their full height by a roof of a
carport or porch, shall be covered on the interior surface with sheathing
membrane conforming to [REF:standard:cgsb-51.32] lapped not less than 100 mm  (metric) at the joints.

In situations described in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect20.subsect13.art9.sent1:short], flashing shall be provided where water will accumulate, to lead
it to the exterior.

Where insulation that effectively limits the passage of water
is applied by a waterproof adhesive or mortar directly to parged masonry,
the requirements for sheathing membrane in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect20.subsect13.art9.sent1:short] do not apply. (See [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.appnote107:short].)

[REF:term:cvt-wll]Cavity walls shall be constructed
so that mortar droppings are prevented from forming a bridge to allow
the passage of rain water across the cavity.

articles.title: Caulking at Door and Window Frames

content.text:
The junction of door and window frames with masonry shall be
caulked in conformance with [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect27.subsect4:long]

Where no flashing is installed beneath window sills, such sills
shall be provided with a drip not less than 25 mm (metric) from
the wall surface.

articles.title: Laying Temperature of Mortar and Masonry

content.text:
Mortar and masonry shall be maintained at a temperature not
below 5°C during installation and for not less than 48 h (metric) after installation.
No frozen material shall be used in mortar mix.

The top surface of uncompleted masonry exposed to the weather
shall be completely covered with a waterproofing material when construction
is not in progress.

Where reinforcement is required in this Section, masonry walls
shall be reinforced horizontally and vertically with steel having
a total cross-sectional area of not less than 0.002 times the horizontal
cross-sectional area of the wall, so that not less than one-third
of the required steel area is installed either horizontally or vertically
and the remainder in the other direction.

Where reinforcement for masonry is required in this Section,
it shall be installed in conformance with the requirements for reinforced
masonry as contained in [REF:standard:csaa371]

Carbon steel connectors required to be corrosion-resistant shall
be galvanized to at least the minimum standards in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect20.subsect16.art1.table1:long]

content.title: Minimum Requirements for Galvanizing

body_rows.content:
Wire ties and continuous
reinforcing (hot-dipped galvanizing)

Strip, plate, bars and
rolled sections (not less than 3.18 mm thick (metric))

460 g/m2
                                     (metric) on material 0.76 mm thick (metric)
                                    
                                       [REF:standard:astma123m] does not apply to metal less than  0.76 mm
thick (metric). Galvanizing coatings may be interpolated for thicknesses
between 3.18 mm (metric) and 0.76 mm (metric).

subsections.title: Above-Ground Flat Insulating Concrete Form Walls

articles.title: Thickness of Flat Insulating Concrete Form Walls

content.text:
The thickness of the concrete in flat insulating concrete form
walls not in contact with the ground shall be

clauses.text: not less than 140 mm (metric), and
constant for the entire height of the wall.

articles.title: Reinforcement for Flat Insulating Concrete Form Walls

content.text:
Horizontal reinforcement in above-grade flat insulating concrete
form walls shall

clauses.text: consist of

subclauses.text:
one 10M bar placed not more than 300 mm (metric) from the
top of the wall, and
10M bars at 600 mm (metric) o.c., and

clauses.text: be placed in the middle third of the wall section.

content.text:
Vertical reinforcement in above-grade flat insulating concrete
form walls shall

clauses.text: consist of 10M bars at 400 mm (metric) o.c., and
be placed in the middle third of the wall section.

content.text:
Vertical reinforcement required by [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect20.subsect17.art2.sent2:short] and interrupted by wall openings shall be placed not
more than 600 mm (metric) from each side of the opening.

articles.title: Openings in Non-Loadbearing Flat Insulating Concrete Form Walls

content.text:
No openings shall occur within 1 200 mm (metric) of interior
and exterior corners of exterior non-[REF:term:ldbrng]loadbearing flat insulating concrete form walls.

Portions of walls above openings in non-[REF:term:ldbrng]loadbearing flat insulating concrete form walls shall have
a minimum depth of concrete of no less than 200 mm (metric) across
the width of the opening.

Openings that are more than 600 mm (metric) but not more
than 3 000 mm (metric) in width in non-[REF:term:ldbrng]loadbearing flat insulating concrete form walls shall be reinforced at the top
and bottom with one 10M bar.

Openings more than 3 000 mm (metric) in width in non-[REF:term:ldbrng]loadbearing flat insulating concrete form walls
shall be reinforced on all four sides with two 10M bars.

Reinforcing bars described in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect20.subsect17.art3.sent3:short]
                           [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect20.subsect17.art3.sent4:short] shall extend 600 mm (metric) beyond the edges of
the opening.

The cumulative width of openings in non-[REF:term:ldbrng]loadbearing flat insulating concrete form walls shall not
make up more than 70% of the length of any wall.

articles.title: Openings in Loadbearing Flat Insulating Concrete Form Walls

content.text:
No openings shall occur within 1 200 mm (metric) of interior
and exterior corners of exterior [REF:term:ldbrng]loadbearing flat insulating concrete form walls.

In [REF:term:ldbrng]loadbearing flat insulating concrete
form walls, lintels shall be provided over all openings wider than 900 mm (metric).

Lintels described in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect20.subsect17.art4.sent2:short] shall be constructed in accordance with [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.spectables2.table1:long], [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.spectables2.table2:number] or [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.spectables2.table3:number].

Lintels described in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect20.subsect17.art4.sent2:short] over openings wider than 1 200 mm (metric) shall be reinforced
for shear with 10M stirrups at a maximum spacing of half the distance
from the bottom reinforcing bar to the top of the lintel.

articles.title: Framing Supported on Flat Insulating Concrete Form Walls

content.text:
Floor joists supported on the side of flat insulating concrete
form walls shall be supported with joist hangers secured to wood ledger
boards.
The ledger boards referred to in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect20.subsect17.art5.sent1:short] shall be not less than

clauses.text: 38 mm (metric) thick, and
the depth of the floor joists.

content.text:
Anchor bolts shall be used to secure ledger boards to flat insulating
concrete form walls and shall be

clauses.text: embedded in the wall to a depth not less than 100 mm (metric), and
spaced in accordance with [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect20.subsect17.art5.table1:long]

content.text:
Floor joists and [REF:term:bldng]building frames
supported on the top of flat insulating concrete form walls shall
be anchored in conformance with [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect6.art1:long]

content.title:
Maximum Anchor Bolt Spacing for the Connection of Floor
Ledgers to Flat Insulating Concrete Form Walls

articles.title:
Anchoring of Roof Framing to the Top of Flat Insulating Concrete
Form Walls

content.text:
Roof framing supported on the top of flat insulating concrete
form walls shall be fixed to the top plates, which shall be anchored
to the wall with anchor bolts

clauses.text: not less than 12.7 mm (metric) in diameter, and
spaced at not more than 1 200 mm (metric) o.c.

content.text:
The anchor bolts described in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect20.subsect17.art6.sent1:short] shall be placed in the centre of the flat insulating
concrete form wall and shall be embedded no less than 100 mm (metric) into the concrete.

Attachment of roof framing to wood top plates shall be in accordance
with [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect3.art4.table1:long]

Above-ground flat insulating concrete form walls shall be protected
from precipitation and damage in conformance with [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect27:long]

sections.title: Masonry and Concrete Chimneys and Flues

content.text: This Section applies to

clauses.text:
rectangular [REF:term:mnr-r-cn]masonry or concrete chimneys not more than 12 m in height serving fireplaces or serving [REF:term:pplnc]appliances having a combined total rated heat
output of 120 kW (metric) or less, and
[REF:term:fl-pp]flue pipes connected to such [REF:term:chmn]chimneys.

content.text:
[REF:term:chmn]Chimneys, other than those described
in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect21.subsect1.art1.sent1:short], [REF:term:g-vnt]gas
vents and [REF:term:fl-pp]flue pipes serving gas-,
oil- or solid-fuel-burning [REF:term:pplnc]appliances and
their associated equipment, including [REF:term:tv]stoves, [REF:term:cktp]cooktops, ovens and [REF:term:pc-htr]space heaters, covered by the standards referenced in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect33.subsect5.art2.sent1:long]
                           [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect33.subsect5.art3.sent1:long] shall conform to [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect33.subsect10:long]

[REF:term:chmn]Chimneys and [REF:term:fl-pp]flue
pipes other than those described in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect21.subsect1.art1.sent1:short]
                           [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect21.subsect1.art1.sent2:short] shall conform to [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part6.sect3:long]

The walls of any [REF:term:chmn]chimney or [REF:term:fl-pp]flue pipe shall be constructed so as to be smoke-
and flame-tight.

A [REF:term:chmn]chimney
                           [REF:term:fl]flue that serves a fireplace or incinerator shall not serve any other [REF:term:pplnc]appliance.

A [REF:term:chmn]chimney
                           [REF:term:fl]flue that serves a solid-fuel-burning [REF:term:pplnc]appliance shall not be connected to a natural-gas- or propane-fired [REF:term:pplnc]appliance.

A [REF:term:chmn]chimney
                           [REF:term:fl]flue that serves a solid-fuel-burning [REF:term:pplnc]appliance shall not be connected to an oil-burning [REF:term:pplnc]appliance unless the solid-fuel-burning [REF:term:pplnc]appliance is certified for such installation and the installation of both [REF:term:pplnc]appliances meets the requirements of the relevant
standards referenced in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect33.subsect5.art2:long]

articles.title: Connections of More Than One Appliance

content.text:
Except as required by [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect21.subsect2.art1:long], where two
or more fuel-burning [REF:term:pplnc]appliances are connected
to the same [REF:term:chmn]chimney
                           [REF:term:fl]flue, the connections shall be made as described in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect21.subsect2.art2.sent2:short]
                           [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect21.subsect2.art2.sent4:short] and an adequate draft
shall be provided for the connected [REF:term:pplnc]appliances in conformance with the requirements of applicable provincial or
territorial regulations or municipal bylaws or, in the absence of
such regulations or bylaws, with the requirements of the relevant
standards listed in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect33.subsect10:long]

Where 2 or more fuel-burning [REF:term:pplnc]appliances are connected to the same [REF:term:chmn]chimney
                           [REF:term:fl]flue, the [REF:term:pplnc]appliances shall
be located on the same [REF:term:tr]storey.

The connection referred to in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect21.subsect2.art2.sent2:short] for a solid-fuel-burning [REF:term:pplnc]appliance shall be made below connections for [REF:term:pplnc]appliances burning other fuels.

The connection referred to in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect21.subsect2.art2.sent2:short] for a liquid-fuel-burning [REF:term:pplnc]appliance shall be made below any connections for [REF:term:pplnc]appliances burning natural gas or propane.

[REF:term:chmn]Chimney
                           [REF:term:fl]flues shall not be inclined more than 45° (metric) to the vertical.

Except for [REF:term:chmn] chimneys serving fireplaces,
the size of a [REF:term:chmn]chimney 
                           [REF:term:fl]flue shall conform to the requirements of the [REF:term:pplnc]appliance installation standards referenced in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect33.subsect5.art2.sent1:long]
                           [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect33.subsect5.art3.sent1:long].

Where a [REF:term:chmn]chimney
                           [REF:term:fl]flue serves only one [REF:term:pplnc]appliance, the [REF:term:fl]flue area shall be at least equal to that of the [REF:term:fl-pp]flue pipe connected to it.

The size of a [REF:term:chmn]chimney
                           [REF:term:fl]flue serving a masonry fireplace shall conform to [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect21.subsect2.art5.table1:long]
                           [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect21.subsect2.art5.table2:long].

content.title: Diameter of Round Flues for Fireplace Chimneys
Rectangular Flue Sizes for Fireplace Chimneys

content.text:
The width of an oval [REF:term:chmn]chimney
                           [REF:term:fl]flue shall be not less than two-thirds its breadth.
Every [REF:term:mnr-r-cn]masonry or concrete chimney shall have a lining of clay, concrete, firebrick or metal.

Joints of [REF:term:chmn-lnr]chimney liners shall
be sealed to provide a barrier to the passage of [REF:term:fl]flue gases and condensate into the cavity between the liner
and the surrounding masonry.

Joints of clay, concrete or firebrick [REF:term:chmn-lnr]chimney liners shall be struck flush to provide a straight,
smooth, aligned [REF:term:chmn]chimney
                           [REF:term:fl]flue.
Clay liners shall conform to [REF:standard:csaa324]

Liners referred to in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect21.subsect3.art3.sent1:short] shall be not less than 15.9 mm (metric) thick and shall be
capable of resisting, without softening or cracking, a temperature
of 1 100°C (metric).
Firebrick liners shall conform to [REF:standard:astmc27]

Firebrick liners shall be laid with high temperature cement
mortar conforming to [REF:standard:cgsb-10.3]

Concrete [REF:term:fl]flue liners shall conform to [REF:external:csaa405]Clause 4.2.6.4 of 
                           [REF:standard:csaa405]
Metal liners shall be constructed of not less than 0.3 mm (metric) thick stainless steel.

Metal liners referred to in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect21.subsect3.art6.sent1:short] shall only be used in [REF:term:chmn] chimneys serving
gas- or oil-burning [REF:term:pplnc] appliances. (See [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.appnote108:short].)

[REF:term:chmn-lnr]Chimney liners shall be installed
when the surrounding masonry or concrete is placed.

articles.title: Spaces between Liners and Surrounding Masonry

content.text:
A space not less than 10 mm (metric) wide shall be left
between a [REF:term:chmn-lnr]chimney liner and surrounding
masonry.
The space required in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect21.subsect3.art8.sent1:short] shall not be filled with mortar.
[REF:term:chmn-lnr]Chimney liners used in [REF:term:chmn]chimneys for solid-fuel-burning [REF:term:pplnc]appliances shall be laid in a full bed of

clauses.text: high temperature cement mortar conforming to [REF:standard:cgsb-10.3] or

mortar consisting of 1 part Portland cement to 3 parts sand
by volume.

content.text:
[REF:term:chmn-lnr]Chimney liners used in [REF:term:chmn]chimneys for oil- or gas-burning [REF:term:pplnc]appliances shall be laid in a full bed of mortar consisting
of 1 part Portland cement to 3 parts sand by volume.

[REF:term:chmn-lnr]Chimney liners shall extend from
a point not less than 200 mm (metric) below the lowest [REF:term:fl-pp]flue pipe connection to a point not less than 50 mm (metric) or more than 100 mm (metric) above the [REF:term:chmn]chimney cap.
Unit masonry shall conform to [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect20:long]
Concrete shall conform to [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect3:long]

Footings for [REF:term:mnr-r-cn] masonry chimneys and [REF:term:mnr-r-cn]concrete chimneys shall conform
to [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect15:long]

A [REF:term:chmn]chimney 
                           [REF:term:fl]flue shall extend not less than

clauses.text: 900 mm (metric) above the highest point at which the [REF:term:chmn] chimney comes in contact with the roof, and

600 mm (metric) above the highest roof surface or structure
within  3 m (metric) of the [REF:term:chmn]chimney.

content.text:
Except as provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect21.subsect4.art5.sent2:short], [REF:term:chmn]chimneys shall be braced in accordance
with [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect3.subsect2:long] to provide lateral stability
under wind loads.

A [REF:term:chmn]chimney need not be laterally braced
provided

clauses.text: no horizontal outside dimension is less than 400 mm (metric), and

the [REF:term:chmn]chimney extends not more than 3.6 m (metric) above a roof or the masonry wall of which it forms a
part.

content.text:
The top of a [REF:term:chmn]chimney shall have a
waterproof cap of reinforced concrete, masonry or metal.

The cap required in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect21.subsect4.art6.sent1:short] shall
slope from the lining and be provided with a drip not less than 25 mm (metric) from the [REF:term:chmn]chimney wall.

Cast-in-place concrete caps shall be separated from the [REF:term:chmn-lnr]chimney liner by a bond break and be sealed
at that location.

Jointed precast concrete or masonry [REF:term:chmn]chimney caps shall have flashing installed beneath the cap extending from
the liner to the drip edge.

A cleanout opening with a metal frame and a tight-fitting metal
door shall be installed near the base of the [REF:term:chmn]chimney
                           [REF:term:fl]flue.

The walls of a masonry [REF:term:chmn]chimney shall
be built of [REF:term:sld-m-u]solid masonry units not less
than 75 mm (metric) thick.

[REF:term:fl]Flue liners in the same [REF:term:chmn]chimney shall be separated by not less than 75 mm (metric) of masonry or concrete exclusive of liners where clay liners are
used, or 90 mm (metric) of firebrick where firebrick liners are
used.

[REF:term:fl]Flue liners referred to in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect21.subsect4.art9.sent1:short] shall be installed to prevent significant
lateral movement.

Junctions with adjacent materials shall be adequately flashed
to shed water.

The clearance between [REF:term:mnr-r-cn]masonry or concrete
chimneys and [REF:term:cmbtbl] combustible framing
shall be not less than

clauses.text: 50 mm (metric) for interior [REF:term:chmn]chimneys, and
12 mm (metric) for exterior [REF:term:chmn]chimneys.

content.text:
A clearance of not less than 150 mm (metric) shall be provided
between a cleanout opening and [REF:term:cmbtbl]combustible material.

[REF:term:cmbtbl]Combustible flooring and subflooring
shall have not less than a 12 mm (metric) clearance from [REF:term:mnr-r-cn]masonry or concrete chimneys.

All spaces between [REF:term:mnr-r-cn]masonry or concrete
chimneys and [REF:term:cmbtbl]combustible framing
shall be sealed top or bottom with [REF:term:ncmbtbl]noncombustible material.

Joists or beams may be supported on masonry walls which enclose [REF:term:chmn]chimney
                           [REF:term:fl]flues provided
the [REF:term:cmbtbl]combustible members are separated
from the [REF:term:fl]flue by not less than 290 mm (metric) of [REF:term:sld-m]solid masonry.

Except when otherwise specifically stated herein, this Section
applies to masonry fireplaces constructed on-site.

Except as otherwise stated in this Section, unit masonry shall
conform to [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect20:long] and concrete to [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect3:long]

Masonry above openings shall be supported by steel lintels conforming
to [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect20.subsect5.art2.sent2:long], reinforced concrete or a masonry arch.
Footings for masonry and concrete fireplaces shall conform to [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect15:long]

Where a supply of combustion air is provided directly to the
fire chamber of a fireplace, including a factory-built fireplace,
the installation shall comply with the “Outdoor Air Supply” requirements
provided in [REF:standard:csaa405]

Except where a fireplace is equipped with a steel liner, every
fireplace shall have a firebrick liner.
Firebrick liners shall be not less than

clauses.text: 50 mm (metric) thick for the sides and back, and
25 mm (metric) thick for the floor.

content.text:
Firebrick liners shall be laid with high temperature cement
mortar conforming to [REF:standard:cgsb-10.3]

Joints between a firebrick liner and the adjacent backing masonry
shall be offset.

Steel liners for fireplaces shall conform to [REF:standard:ulcs639] and shall be installed in accordance
with the installation instructions in that standard.

Except as provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect22.subsect3.art1.sent2:short], the thickness of the back and sides of a fireplace, including
the thickness of any firebrick liner, shall be not less than 190 mm (metric) where a metal liner or a firebrick liner less than 51 mm (metric) thick is used.

When a steel fireplace liner is used with an air circulating
chamber surrounding the firebox, the back and sides of the fireplace
shall consist of

clauses.text: [REF:term:sld-m-u]solid masonry units not less than 90 mm (metric) thick, or
hollow masonry units not less than 190 mm (metric) thick.

content.text:
The distance from the back of the fire chamber to the plane
of the fireplace opening shall be not less than 300 mm (metric).

Except as required in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect22.subsect5.art1.sent2:short], fireplaces shall have a [REF:term:ncmbtbl]noncombustible hearth extending not less than 400 mm (metric) in front of the
fireplace opening and not less than 200 mm (metric) beyond each
side of the fireplace opening.

Where the fire chamber floor is elevated more than 150
mm (metric) above the hearth, the dimension of the hearth measured perpendicular
to the plane of the fireplace opening shall be increased by not less
than

clauses.text: 50 mm (metric) for an elevation above 150 mm (metric) and not more than 300 mm (metric), and
an additional 25 mm (metric) for every 50 mm (metric) in elevation above 300 mm (metric).

content.text:
Except as permitted in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect22.subsect5.art2.sent2:short], the fire chamber floor and hearth shall be supported on a reinforced
concrete slab not less than 100 mm (metric) thick at its supports
and, if cantilevered, not less than 50 mm (metric) thick at its
unsupported edge.

A hearth for a fireplace with an opening raised not less than 200 mm (metric) from a [REF:term:cmbtbl]combustible floor
is permitted to be supported on that floor provided the requirements
of [REF:external:csaa405]Clauses 5.3.6.5. to 5.3.6.7. of 
                           [REF:standard:csaa405] are
followed.

The throat of every fireplace shall be equipped with a metal
damper sufficiently large to cover the full area of the throat opening.

The sides of the smoke chamber connecting a fireplace throat
with a [REF:term:fl]flue shall not be sloped at an angle
greater than 45° (metric) to the vertical.

The thickness of masonry walls surrounding the smoke chamber
shall be not less than 190 mm (metric) at the sides, front and
back, except that the portions of the back exposed to the outside
may be 140 mm (metric) thick.

Factory-built fireplaces and their installation shall conform
to [REF:standard:ulcs610]

[REF:term:cmbtbl]Combustible material shall not be
placed on or near the face of a fireplace within 150 mm (metric) of the fireplace opening, except that where the [REF:term:cmbtbl]combustible material projects more than 38 mm (metric) out from the face of the fireplace above the opening, such material
shall be not less than 300 mm (metric) above the top of the opening.

Metal exposed to the interior of a fireplace such as the damper
control mechanism shall have not less than a 50 mm (metric) clearance
from any [REF:term:cmbtbl]combustible material on the face
of the fireplace where such metal penetrates through the face of the
fireplace.

Not less than a 100 mm (metric) clearance shall be provided
between the back and sides of a fireplace and [REF:term:cmbtbl]combustible framing, except that a 50 mm (metric) clearance
is permitted where the fireplace is located in an exterior wall.

Not less than a 50 mm (metric) clearance shall be provided
between the back and sides of the smoke chamber of a fireplace and [REF:term:cmbtbl]combustible framing, except that a 25 mm (metric) clearance is permitted where the fireplace is located in an exterior
wall.

The clearance of [REF:term:cmbtbl]combustible material
above heat-circulating duct outlets from those outlets shall be not
less than

clauses.text:
300 mm (metric) where the [REF:term:cmbtbl]combustible material projects not less than 38 mm (metric) from the face,
and
150 mm (metric) where the projection is less than 38 mm (metric).

content.text: Fireplace inserts and hearth-mounted [REF:term:tv]stoves vented through the throat of a fireplace shall conform to [REF:standard:ulcs628]

The installation of fireplace inserts and hearth-mounted [REF:term:tv]stoves vented through the throat of a fireplace
shall conform to [REF:standard:csab365]

Subject to the application limitations defined elsewhere in this Part, this Section applies to constructions where wall, floor and
roof planes are generally comprised of lumber frames of small repetitive
structural members, or engineered components, and where

clauses.text:
roof and wall planes are clad, sheathed or braced on at least
one side,

the small repetitive structural members are spaced not more
than 600 mm o.c. (metric),
the constructions do not serve as [REF:term:fndtn]foundations,

the specified [REF:term:lv-ld]live load on supported
subfloors and floor framing does not exceed 2.4 kPa (metric),
and

the span of any structural member does not exceed 12.20
m (metric).

content.text:
Where the conditions in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect1.art1.sent1:short] are exceeded for wood constructions, the design of the framing
and fastening shall conform to [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect3.subsect1:long]

All members shall be so framed, anchored, fastened, tied and
braced to provide the necessary strength and rigidity.

Ends of wood joists, beams and other members framing into masonry
or concrete shall be treated to prevent decay where the bottom of
the member is at or below ground level, or a 12 mm (metric) air
space shall be provided at the end and sides of the member.

Air spaces required in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect2.art2.sent1:short] shall not be blocked by insulation, [REF:term:vpr-brrr]vapour
barriers or airtight materials.

Except as permitted in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect2.art3.sent2:short], wood framing members that are not pressure-treated with a wood
preservative and that are supported on concrete in contact with the
ground or [REF:term:fll]fill shall be separated from the
concrete by not less than 0.05 mm (metric) polyethylene film or
Type S roll roofing.
Dampproofing material referred to in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect2.art3.sent1:short] is not required where the wood member is at least 150 mm (metric) above the ground.

Except as provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect2.art4.sent3:short], connectors in contact with preservative-treated wood shall be
made of

clauses.text:
hot-dipped, zinc-coated galvanized steel with a coating weight
not less than Z550 conforming to [REF:standard:astma653m], "Standard Specification for Steel Sheet, Zinc-Coated (Galvanized) or Zinc-Iron Alloy-Coated (Galvannealed) by the Hot-Dip Process,"

a material that provides an equivalent level of corrosion protection
to that provided by the material described in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect2.art4.sent1.clause1:short], or
stainless steel.

content.text: Fasteners used to attach the connectors referred to in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect2.art4.sent1:short] shall be made of

clauses.text: galvanized steel coated with zinc in accordance with [REF:standard:astma153m], "Standard Specification for Zinc Coating (Hot-Dip) on Iron and Steel Hardware," or

a material that provides an equivalent level of performance
and is compatible with the connector.

content.text:
Connectors and fasteners that are in contact with wood that
has been treated with a disodium octaborate tetrahydrate (SBX (DOT))
or zinc borate preservative and is installed in a dry interior environment
are permitted to be made of uncoated carbon steel. (See [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.appnote114:short].)
Lumber shall conform to [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect3.subsect2:long]

Except as provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect3.art1.sent2:short] and unless otherwise indicated, nails specified in this Section shall be common steel wire nails or common spiral nails conforming to

clauses.text: [REF:standard:astmf1667], "Standard Specification for Driven Fasteners: Nails, Spikes, and Staples," or
[REF:standard:csab111], "Wire Nails, Spikes and Staples."

content.text:
Nails used to comply with [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect3.art4.table1:long] and 9.23.3.5.-A to 9.23.3.5.-C shall
have a diameter not less than that stated in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect3.art1.table1:long] (See [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.appnote115:short].)

content.title: Diameter of Nails

content.text: Wood screws specified in this Section shall conform to [REF:standard:asmeb18.6.1] (See [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.appnote116:short].)

All nails shall be long enough so that not less than half their
required length penetrates into the second member.

Splitting of wood members shall be minimized by staggering the
nails in the direction of the grain and by keeping nails well in from
the edges. (See [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.appnote117:short].)
Except as provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect3.art4.sent2:short], nailing of framing shall conform to [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect3.art4.table1:long]

Where the bottom wall plate or sole plate of an exterior wall
is not nailed to floor joists, [REF:term:rm-jst]rim joists or blocking in conformance with [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect3.art4.table1:long], the
exterior wall is permitted to be fastened to the floor framing by

clauses.text:
having plywood, OSB or waferboard sheathing extend down over
floor framing and fastened to the floor framing by nails or staples
conforming to [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect3.art5:long], or
tying the wall framing to the floor framing by galvanized-metal strips

subclauses.text: 50 mm (metric) wide,
not less than 0.41 mm (metric) thick,
spaced not more than 1.2 m (metric) apart, and
fastened at each end with at least two 63 mm (metric) nails.

the depth of the stud if the stud is [REF:term:ldbrng]loadbearing or 40 mm (metric) if the stud is non-[REF:term:ldbrng]loadbearing, unless the weakened studs are suitably reinforced.

Top plates in walls shall not be notched, drilled or otherwise
weakened to reduce the undamaged width to less than 50 mm (metric) unless the weakened plates are suitably reinforced.

Roof truss members shall not be notched, drilled or otherwise
weakened unless such notching or drilling is allowed for in the design

m (metric) wide and not more than 1 [REF:term:tr]storey in [REF:term:bldng-hg]building height that are not anchored in accordance

articles.title: Levelling and Sealing of Sill Plates

content.text: Sill plates shall be

clauses.text: levelled by setting them on a full bed of mortar, or

laid directly on the [REF:term:fndtn]foundation if

content.text: The joint between the sill plate for exterior walls and the [REF:term:fndtn]foundation shall be sealed in accordance with [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect25.subsect3:long]

Beams shall have even and level bearing and the bearing at end
supports shall be not less than 89 mm (metric) long, except as
stated in the notes to [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.spectables2.table11:long]
                           [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.spectables2.table14:long].
Exterior steel beams shall be shop primed.

Where a beam is made up of individual pieces of lumber that
are nailed together, the individual members shall be 38 mm (metric) or greater in thickness and installed on edge.

Except as permitted in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect8.art3.sent3:short], where individual members of a built-up beam are butted together
to form a joint, the joint shall occur over a support.

Where a beam is continuous over more than one span, individual
members are permitted to be butted together to form a joint at or
within 150 mm (metric) of the end quarter points of the clear
spans, provided the quarter points are not those closest to the ends
of the beam.

Members joined at quarter points shall be continuous over adjacent
supports.

Joints in individual members of a beam that are located at or
near the end quarter points shall not occur in adjacent members at
the same quarter point and shall not reduce the effective beam width
by more than half.

Not more than one butt joint shall occur in any individual member
of a built-up beam within any one span.

Except as provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect8.art3.sent8:short], where 38 mm (metric) members are laid on edge to form a built-up
beam, individual members shall be nailed together with a double row
of nails not less than 89 mm (metric) in length, spaced not more
than 450 mm (metric) apart in each row with the end nails located 100 mm (metric) to 150 mm (metric) from the end of each piece.

Where 38 mm (metric) members in built-up wood beams are
not nailed together as provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect8.art3.sent7:short], they shall be bolted together with not less than 12.7 mm (metric) diam bolts equipped with washers and spaced not more
than 1.2 m (metric) o.c., with the end bolts located not more
than 600 mm (metric) from the ends of the members.

Except when supported on ribbon boards, floor joists shall have
not less than 38 mm (metric) length of end bearing.
Ribbon boards referred to in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect9.art1.sent1:short] shall be not less than 19 mm (metric) by 89 mm (metric) lumber let into the studs.

Floor joists may be supported on the tops of beams or may be
framed into the sides of beams.

When framed into the side of a wood beam, joists referred to
in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect9.art2.sent1:short] shall be supported on

clauses.text: joist hangers or other acceptable mechanical connectors, or

not less than 38 mm (metric) by 64 mm (metric) ledger
strips nailed to the side of the beam, except that 38 mm (metric) by 38 mm (metric) ledger strips may be used provided each joist
is nailed to the beam by not less than four 89 mm (metric) nails,
in addition to the nailing for the ledger strip required in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect3.art4.table1:long]

content.text:

in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect9.art2.sent1:short] shall be supported on
the bottom flange of the beam or on not less than 38 mm (metric) by 38 mm (metric) lumber bolted to the web with not less than 6.3 mm (metric) diam bolts spaced not more than 600 mm (metric) apart.

Joists referred to in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect9.art2.sent3:short] shall be spliced above the beam with not less than 38 mm (metric) by 38 mm (metric) lumber at least 600 mm (metric) long to

Not less than a 12 mm (metric) space shall be provided between
the splice required in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect9.art2.sent4:short] and
the beam to allow for shrinkage of the wood joists.

Except as provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect9.art4.sent1:long], bottoms of
floor joists shall be restrained from twisting at each end by toe-nailing
to the supports, end-nailing to the header joists or by providing
continuous strapping, blocking between the joists or cross-bridging
near the supports.

furring strips complying with [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect29.subsect3.art1.table1:long] are

a panel-type ceiling finish complying with [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect29.subsect5:long], [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect29.subsect6:number], [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect29.subsect7:number], [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect29.subsect8:number], or [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect29.subsect9:number] is attached directly to the joists.

content.text: Where a ceiling attached to wood furring is specified in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.spectables2.table5:long],

clauses.text:
the ceiling finish shall consist of gypsum board, plywood or
OSB not less than 12.7 mm (metric) thick, and
the furring shall be

subclauses.text:
19 mm (metric) by 89 mm (metric) wood furring spaced
at not more than 600 mm (metric) o.c., or

19 mm (metric) by 64 mm (metric) wood furring spaced
at not more than 400 mm (metric) o.c.

content.text:
Header joists around floor openings shall be doubled when they
exceed 1.2 m (metric) in length.

The size of header joists exceeding 3.2 m (metric) in length
shall be determined by calculations.

Trimmer joists around floor openings shall be doubled when the
length of the header joist exceeds 800 mm (metric).

When the header joist exceeds 2 m (metric) in length the
size of the trimmer joists shall be determined by calculations.

articles.title: Support of Tail and Header Joists

content.text:
When tail joists and header joists are supported by the floor
framing, they shall be supported by suitable joist hangers or nailing
in accordance with [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect3.art4.table1:long]

Non-[REF:term:ldbrng]loadbearing walls parallel to
the floor joists shall be supported by joists beneath the wall or
on blocking between the joists.

Blocking referred to in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect9.art8.sent1:short] for the support of non-[REF:term:ldbrng]loadbearing walls
shall be

clauses.text:
not less than 38 mm (metric) by 89 mm (metric) lumber,
and

except as required for the fastening of walls constructed with
required [REF:term:br-wl-pnl]braced wall panels, spaced
not more than 1.2 m (metric) apart.

content.text:
Except as provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect9.art8.sent6:short], non-[REF:term:ldbrng]loadbearing interior walls at
right angles to the floor joists are not restricted as to location.

[REF:term:ldbrng]Loadbearing interior walls parallel
to floor joists shall be supported by beams or walls of sufficient
strength to safely transfer the specified [REF:term:lv-ld]live
loads to the vertical supports.

Unless the joist size is designed to support such loads, [REF:term:ldbrng]loadbearing interior walls at right angles to
floor joists shall be located

clauses.text:
not more than 900 mm (metric) from the joist support where
the wall does not support a floor, and

not more than 600 mm (metric) from the joist support where
the wall supports one or more floors.

content.text:
[REF:term:ldbrng]Loadbearing and non-[REF:term:ldbrng]loadbearing walls constructed with required [REF:term:br-wl-pnl]braced wall panels shall be continuously
supported by floor joists, blocking or [REF:term:rm-jst]rim joists to allow for the required fastening (see [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect3.art4.table1:long]).

Floor joists supporting roof loads shall not be cantilevered
more than 400 mm (metric) beyond their supports where 38 mm (metric) by 184 mm (metric) joists are used and not more than 600 mm (metric) beyond their supports where 38 mm (metric) by 235 mm (metric) or larger joists are used.

The cantilevered portions referred to in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect9.art9.sent1:short] shall not support floor loads from other [REF:term:tr]storeys unless calculations are provided to show that the
design resistances of the cantilevered joists are not exceeded.

Where cantilevered floor joists described in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect9.art9.sent1:short]
                           [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect9.art9.sent2:short] are at right angles
to the main floor joists, the tail joists in the cantilevered portion
shall extend inward away from the cantilever support a distance equal
to not less than 6 times the length of the cantilever, and shall be
end nailed to an interior doubled header joist in conformance with [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect3.art4.table1:long]
The size and spacing of studs shall conform to [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect10.art1.table1:long]

content.text:
Where [REF:term:ldbrng]loadbearing interior walls
are not finished in accordance with [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect29:long], blocking or strapping shall be fastened to the studs
at mid-height to prevent sideways buckling.

Except as permitted in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect10.art3.sent2:short]
                           [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect10.art3.sent3:short], all studs shall be placed at right angles to the wall
face.

Studs on the flat are permitted to be used in gable ends of
roofs that contain only unfinished space or in non-[REF:term:ldbrng]loadbearing interior walls within the limits described in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect10.art1:long]

Wall studs that support only a load from an attic not accessible
by a stairway are permitted to be placed on the flat within the limits
permitted in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect10.art1:long] provided

clauses.text:
the studs are clad on not less than one side with plywood, OSB
or waferboard sheathing fastened to the face of the studs with a structural
adhesive, and
the portion of the roof supported by the studs does not exceed 2.1 m (metric) in width.

content.text:
Wall studs shall be continuous for the full [REF:term:tr]storey height except at openings and shall not be spliced
except by fingerjoining with a structural adhesive. (See [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.appnote125:short].)

articles.title: Support for Cladding, Sheathing and Finishing Materials

content.text:
Corners and intersections shall be designed to provide adequate
support for the vertical edges of interior finishes, sheathing and
cladding materials, and in no instance shall exterior corners be framed
with less than the equivalent of 2 studs.

Where the vertical edges of interior finishes at wall intersections
are supported at vertical intervals by blocking or furring, the vertical
distance between such supports shall not exceed the maximum distance
between supports specified in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect29:long]
Where the lintel spanning the opening is more than 3 m (metric) long, studs shall be tripled on each side of the opening so that

clauses.text:
the two inner studs on each side extend from the bottom of the
supported lintel to the top of the bottom wall plate, and

the outer stud on each side extends from the bottom of the top
wall plate to the bottom wall plate.

content.text:
Except as provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect10.art6.sent3:short], where the lintel spanning the opening is not more than 3
m (metric) long, studs shall be doubled on each side of the opening
so that

clauses.text:
the inner studs on each side extend from the bottom of the supported
lintel to the top of the bottom wall plate, and

the outer stud on each side extends from the bottom of the top
wall plate to the bottom wall plate.

content.text: Single studs are permitted to be used on either side of openings

clauses.text:
in non-[REF:term:ldbrng]loadbearing interior walls
not required to have [REF:term:fr-rtnc-]fire-resistance ratings, provided the studs extend from the top wall plate to the bottom
wall plate, or
in [REF:term:ldbrng]loadbearing or non-[REF:term:ldbrng]loadbearing interior or exterior walls, provided

subclauses.text:
the opening is less than and within the required stud spacing,
and

no 2 such openings of full stud-space width are located in adjacent
stud spaces.

content.text: Except as provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect11.art1.sent2:short], wall plates shall be

clauses.text: not less than 38 mm (metric) thick, and
not less than the required width of the wall studs.

content.text:
In non-[REF:term:ldbrng]loadbearing walls and in [REF:term:ldbrng]loadbearing walls where the studs are located
directly over framing members, the bottom wall plate is permitted
to be 19 mm (metric) thick.
A bottom wall plate shall be provided in all cases.

The bottom plate in exterior walls shall not project more than
one-third the plate width over the support.

Except as permitted in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect11.art3.sent2:short]
                           [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect11.art3.sent4:short], at least 2 top plates shall be provided in [REF:term:ldbrng]loadbearing walls.

A single top plate is permitted to be used in a section of a [REF:term:ldbrng]loadbearing wall containing a lintel provided
the top plate forms a tie across the lintel.

A single top plate is permitted to be used in [REF:term:ldbrng]loadbearing walls where the concentrated loads from ceilings,
floors and roofs are not more than 50 mm (metric) to one side
of the supporting studs and in all non-[REF:term:ldbrng]loadbearing walls.

The top plates need not be provided in a section of [REF:term:ldbrng]loadbearing wall containing a lintel provided
the lintel is tied to the adjacent wall section with not less than

clauses.text: 75 mm (metric) by 150 mm (metric) by 0.91 mm (metric) thick galvanized steel, or
19 mm (metric) by 89 mm (metric) by 300 mm (metric) wood splice nailed to each wall section with at least three 63 mm (metric) nails.

content.text: Joints in the top plates of [REF:term:ldbrng]loadbearing walls shall be staggered not less than

clauses.text: one stud spacing where the number of nails required by [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect11.art4.sent5:short] is not more than 16,
two stud spacings where the number of nails required by [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect11.art4.sent5:short] is greater than 16 and not more than 32, and
three stud spacings where the number of nails required by [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect11.art4.sent5:short] is greater than 32.

content.text: The top plates in [REF:term:ldbrng]loadbearing walls shall be lapped or otherwise tied at corners and intersecting walls in accordance with [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect11.art4.sent4:short].
Joints in single top plates used with [REF:term:ldbrng]loadbearing walls shall be tied in accordance with [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect11.art4.sent4:short].

Ties referred to in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect11.art4.sent2:short]
                           [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect11.art4.sent3:short] shall be the equivalent of not less than 75 mm (metric) by 150 mm (metric) by 0.91 mm (metric) thick galvanized steel nailed to each wall with at least three 63 mm (metric) nails.

Except as provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect11.art4.sent7:short], doubled top plates in [REF:term:br-wl-bnd]braced wall bands shall be fastened on each side of a splice with not less than 76 mm (metric) long common steel wire nails or spiral nails in accordance with the minimum number of nails required by Table 9.23.11.4.-B or [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect11.art4.table2:long], whichever is greater, where

content.text: This Article applies where

1-in-50-year hourly wind pressure (HWP) is not greater than 1.2 kPa (metric),

the lowest exterior frame wall supports a roof and not more than

subclauses.text: 2 floors in a [REF:term:bldng]building of normal-weight construction, or
1 floor in a [REF:term:bldng]building of heavyweight construction or clad at full height with masonry veneer or stone veneer.

clauses.text:

Part 4, or
good engineering practice such as that provided in [REF:standard:cwc-egwfc].

content.text: For the purposes of [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect13.art2.sent1:short] and this Part,

clauses.text: in a [REF:term:bldng]building of normal-weight construction, the average dead weight per [REF:term:tr]storey shall not exceed

0.5 kPa (metric) for the roof, and
0.4 kPa (metric) for exterior walls,

clauses.text: in a [REF:term:bldng]building of heavyweight construction, the average dead weight per [REF:term:tr]storey shall conform to [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect13.art2.sent3.clause1:short], except that the average dead weight per [REF:term:tr]storey shall not exceed

1.0 kPa (metric) for the roof, or
1.2 kPa (metric) for exterior walls,

in a [REF:term:bldng]building clad with stone veneer, the average dead weight of the stone veneer shall not exceed 3.2 kPa (metric). (See Note A-9.23.13.2.(3).)

content.text: In [REF:term:bmnt]basements or crawl spaces where the perimeter [REF:term:fndtn]foundation walls extend from the footings to the underside of the supported floor, [REF:term:br-wl-bnd]braced wall bands constructed with [REF:term:br-wl-pnl]braced wall panels shall(See Note A-9.23.13.5.(2).)

clauses.text: have a total length of braced wall panels not less than the total length in the [REF:term:br-wl-bnd]braced wall band in the storey above, and
be spaced not more than

subclauses.text: 15 m (metric) from the perimeter [REF:term:fndtn]foundation walls,
15 m (metric) from interior [REF:term:fndtn]foundation walls, and
15 m (metric) from adjacent [REF:term:br-wl-bnd]braced wall bands constructed with [REF:term:br-wl-pnl]braced wall panels.

content.text: Interior or exterior wood-sheathed [REF:term:br-wl-pnl]braced wall panels, other than panels of WSP-A framing in the uppermost storey shall(See Note A-9.23.13.5.(3) and (4).)

clauses.text: extend to the roof framing, and
have their the top plate connected to

subclauses.text: top chords of perpendicular or offset parallel trusses by using blocking panels or other methods of lateral load transfer designed by the roof truss manufacturer,
perpendicular or offset parallel joists or rafters by using blocking of the same construction as the [REF:term:br-wl-pnl]braced wall panel below, or
rafters, joists or trusses by using methods of lateral load transfer designed in accordance with good engineering practice.

content.text: The top plates of braced wall panels described in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect13.art5.sent3:short] shall be fastened in accordance with [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect3.art4.table1:long].(See Note A-9.23.13.5.(3) and (4).)
Required [REF:term:br-wl-pnl]braced wall panels shall be

clauses.text: sheathed on the exterior side with plywood, OSB, waferboard or diagonal lumber complying with [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect17:long] fastened in accordance with [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect3.art5.sent3:short] and finished on the interior side with gypsum board complying with [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect29.subsect5:long], or

sheathed on the interior side or exterior side with gypsum board complying with [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect29.subsect5:long] and fastened in accordance with [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect3.art5.sent3:short]. (See Note A-9.23.13.6.(1).)

content.text: Except as provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect13.art6.sent4:short] and [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect13.art6.sent5:short], [REF:term:br-wl-bnd]braced wall bands shall be constructed of [REF:term:br-wl-pnl]braced wall panels of the same sheathing material.
[REF:term:br-wl-pnl]Braced wall panels in [REF:term:bmnt]basements and crawl spaces shall be sheathed with OSB, plywood, waferboard or diagonal lumber

clauses.text: at [REF:term:br-wl-bnd]braced wall band spacing intervals of not more than 15 m (metric), and
under all interior [REF:term:br-wl-bnd]braced wall bands containing wood-sheathed [REF:term:br-wl-pnl]braced wall panels. (See Note A-9.23.13.6.(3).)

content.text: Mixing of [REF:term:br-wl-pnl]braced wall panel framing types is permitted in stacked [REF:term:br-wl-bnd]braced wall bands, provided that wood-sheathed [REF:term:br-wl-pnl]braced wall panels are not above any [REF:term:br-wl-bnd]braced wall bands containing

clauses.text: gypsum-sheathed [REF:term:br-wl-pnl]braced wall panels, or
diagonal-lumber-sheathed [REF:term:br-wl-pnl]braced wall panels.

content.text: Mixing of [REF:term:br-wl-pnl]braced wall panel framing types is permitted along a [REF:term:br-wl-bnd]braced wall band within the same storey, provided that(See Note A-9.23.13.6.(5).)

clauses.text: panels of WSP-A or WSP-B framing type are substituted for panels of a GWB framing type and the total length of all of the [REF:term:br-wl-pnl]braced wall panels is determined based on the GWB framing type, or
the lengths of the [REF:term:br-wl-pnl]braced wall panels of mixed framing types are based on accepted engineering principles.

content.text: Except as provided in Tables 9.23.13.7.-B and 9.23.13.7.-D, all adjustment factors required for the calculation of the minimum total length of [REF:term:br-wl-pnl]braced wall panels in accordance with this Article shall be taken as 1.

The minimum total length of all [REF:term:br-wl-pnl]braced wall panels in a [REF:term:br-wl-bnd]braced wall band shall be taken as the greater of L_{w} determined in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect13.art7.sent3:short] for the appropriate 1-in-50-year hourly wind pressure (HWP) and L_{s} as determined in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect13.art7.sent4:short] for the appropriate seismic design parameter, S_{max}, where

clauses.text: HWP is not greater than 1.2 kPa (metric), and
S_{max} for Site Class C, is not greater than 2.6.

content.text:
For resistance to wind pressure, the minimum total length of [REF:term:br-wl-pnl]braced wall panels in each [REF:term:br-wl-bnd]braced wall band, L_{w}, shall be determined by applying the adjustment factors provided in Table 9.23.13.7.-B to the unadjusted minimum total [REF:term:br-wl-pnl]braced wall panel length L_{uw} provided in Table 9.23.13.7.-A using the following equation:L_{w} = L_{uw}K_{exp}K_{roof}K_{Wspacing}K_{Wnumber}K_{gyp}K_{sheath} ≥ BWP_{min}
                        whereK_{exp} = wind exposure adjustment factor, and = 1 for rough terrain (suburban, urban or wooded terrain extending upwind from the [REF:term:bldng]building uninterrupted for at least 1 km),K_{roof} = roof eave-to-ridge height adjustment factor, and = 1 for a roof eave-to-ridge height of 3 m (metric)
                        K_{Wspacing} = [REF:term:br-wl-bnd]braced wall band spacing adjustment factor for wind (see [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect13.art7.sent5:short]),per [REF:term:bldng]building plan direction, and = 1 for a [REF:term:br-wl-bnd]braced wall band spacing of 7.6 m (metric)
                        K_{Wnumber} = number of parallel [REF:term:br-wl-bnd]braced wall bands adjustment factor for wind, per [REF:term:bldng]building plan direction, and = 1 for two exterior walls and no intermediate [REF:term:br-wl-bnd]braced wall bands,K_{gyp} = interior gypsum board adjustment factor, and = 1 for [REF:term:br-wl-pnl]braced wall panels with gypsum board installed on the interior side,K_{sheath} = intermittent [REF:term:br-wl-pnl]braced wall panels adjustment factor, and = 1 for continuously sheathed [REF:term:br-wl-bnd]braced wall bands, andBWP_{min} = Minimum length of individual [REF:term:br-wl-pnl]braced wall panels as per [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect13.art5.table1:long].(See Note A-9.23.13.7.(3) for an alternative procedure to calculate L_{w}, directly and Note A-9.23.13.7.(4).)

content.text: For 3 or more parallel [REF:term:br-wl-bnd]braced wall bands that are not evenly spaced, an average [REF:term:br-wl-bnd]braced wall band spacing is permitted to be used for the determination of K_{Wspacing} or K_{Sspacing}, provided that no single [REF:term:br-wl-bnd]braced wall band spacing exceeds 10.6 m (metric), except as provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect13.art6.sent3:short].

Where [REF:term:br-wl-pnl]braced wall panels of a gypsum-sheathed framing type have gypsum board installed on both sides, the minimum total length of the [REF:term:br-wl-pnl]braced wall panels determined in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect13.art7.sent3:short]
                           [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect13.art7.sent4:short] is permitted to be reduced by 50%.

Except as provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect13.art8.sent2:short]
                           [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect13.art8.sent3:short], [REF:term:fndtn]foundation cripple walls supporting [REF:term:br-wl-pnl]braced wall panels shall be

clauses.text: considered as an additional [REF:term:tr]storey, or
designed in accordance with Part 4.

content.text: Where the seismic design parameter, S_{max}, is less than or equal to 0.60, [REF:term:fndtn]foundation cripple walls need not comply with [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect13.art8.sent1:short], provided they

clauses.text: are not more than 1.2 m (metric) in height,
are not more than 6 m (metric) in length,
are either

subclauses.text: framed with solid blocking, or

of the same construction as the [REF:term:br-wl-pnl]braced wall panels of the [REF:term:tr]storey above but sheathed with wood sheathing regardless of the construction, where the length of the cripple wall bracing is equal to the length of the [REF:term:br-wl-pnl]braced wall panels multiplied by an adjustment factor of 1.2, in addition to any adjustments required by [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect13.art7.sent1:short]
                                 [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect13.art7.sent2:short], and

clauses.text: do not support heavyweight construction, masonry or stone veneer.

content.text: Where the seismic design parameter, S_{max}, is greater than 0.60, [REF:term:fndtn]foundation cripple walls need not comply with [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect13.art8.sent1:short], provided they

clauses.text:
comply with [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect13.art8.sent2.clause3:long]
                              [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect13.art8.sent2.clause4:short],
are not more than 350 mm (metric) in height, and
are not more than 5 m (metric) length,

content.text: Where interior finish, such as gypsum board, is omitted from the interior side of the cripple wall referred to in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect13.art8.sent2:short] or [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect13.art8.sent3:short], the interior gypsum board adjustment factor described in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect13.art7.sent3:short] or [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect13.art7.sent4:short] shall be applied to the length of the cripple wall bracing.

Cripple walls in stepped [REF:term:fndtn]foundations need not be braced in accordance with [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect13.art8.sent2:short] to [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect13.art8.sent4:short], provided

clauses.text: the lowest floor framing rests directly on a sill plate anchored to a [REF:term:fndtn]foundation not less than 2.4 m (metric) in length within a [REF:term:br-wl-bnd]braced wall band not more than 7.6 m (metric) in length,
the top plate of the cripple wall extends not less than 1.2 m (metric) along the [REF:term:fndtn]foundation, and
anchor bolts are located not more than 300 mm (metric) and 900 mm (metric) from the step in the [REF:term:fndtn]foundation.

content.text: This Article applies where

clauses.text: the seismic design parameter, S_{max}, is not greater than 1.2, and
the 1-in-50-year hourly wind pressure (HWP) is not greater than 1.2 kPa (metric).

content.text: Portions of the perimeter of a single open or enclosed space need not comply with [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect13.art5.sent1:short], where

clauses.text: the roof of the space projects not more than

subclauses.text: 3.5 m (metric) from the face of the framing of the nearest parallel [REF:term:br-wl-bnd]braced wall band, and

clauses.text: that portion of the perimeter structure does not support a floor,
the roof of the space is

subclauses.text: integral with the roof of the rest of the [REF:term:bldng]building with framing members not more than 400 mm (metric) o.c. where roof sheathing edges are not supported on blocking and not more than 600 mm (metric) o.c. where roof sheathing edges are supported on blocking securely fastened between framing members, or

constructed with roof framing not more than 400 mm (metric) o.c. where roof sheathing edges are not supported on blocking and not more than 600 mm (metric) o.c. where roof sheathing edges are supported on blocking securely fastened between framing members, and fastened to the wall framing (see [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect3.art4.table1:long] and [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect9.art1:long] for balloon framing), and

clauses.text: the end-joists or end-rafters for the roof of the space are fastened to a 3-ply, 38 mm × 140 mm (metric) built-up column or a 5-ply, 38 mm × 89 mm (metric) built-up column that is integral with the wall framing.

content.text: Walls in detached garages and in accessory [REF:term:bldng]buildings serving a single [REF:term:dwllng-nt]dwelling unit, and the front wall of attached garages serving a single [REF:term:dwllng-nt]dwelling unit need not comply with [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect13.art5.sent1:short] where these walls do not support a floor.

[REF:term:br-wl-pnl]Braced wall panels in the [REF:term:br-wl-bnd]braced wall band at the front of an attached garage serving a single [REF:term:dwllng-nt]dwelling unit need not comply with [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect13.art5.sent1:short], provided

clauses.text: the maximum spacing between the front of the garage and the back wall of the garage does not exceed 7.6 m (metric),
there is not more than one floor above the garage,
not less than 50% of the length of the back wall of the garage is constructed of wood-sheathed [REF:term:br-wl-pnl]braced wall panels, and
not less than 25% of the length of the side walls is constructed of wood-sheathed [REF:term:br-wl-pnl]braced wall panels.

content.text:
Except as provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect13.art10.sent6:short]
                           [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect13.art10.sent7:short], one exterior wall of the uppermost [REF:term:tr]storey in each orthogonal direction may be set back from the exterior wall of the [REF:term:tr]storey below, provided the adjacent interior [REF:term:br-wl-bnd]braced wall band of the [REF:term:tr]storey below the setback

clauses.text: is spaced not more than 10.6 m (metric) from the exterior wall of the [REF:term:tr]storey below the setback wall,
consists of [REF:term:br-wl-pnl]braced wall panels that are constructed of a wood-based material in conformance with [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect13.art6.sent1:short],
extends to the [REF:term:fndtn]foundation, and

is not taken into consideration when providing [REF:term:br-wl-pnl]braced wall panels constructed of a wood-based material at spacing intervals of not more than 15 m (metric) as per [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect13.art6.sent3:short].

revisions.text: Where the exterior wall of the uppermost [REF:term:tr]storey is set back from the exterior wall of the [REF:term:tr]storey below, the roof and floor space supporting the setback wall shall be sheathed with a wood-based material between the exterior wall of the [REF:term:tr]storey below the setback and the adjacent interior [REF:term:br-wl-bnd]braced wall bands of the [REF:term:tr]storey below the setback.

The [REF:term:flr]floor system shall be anchored to the [REF:term:fndtn]foundation at intervals not exceeding 3 m (metric) along the length of the [REF:term:fndtn]foundation wall, except that where the [REF:term:flr]floor is anchored to the [REF:term:fndtn]foundation at adjacent [REF:term:bng-wl]bearing walls or [REF:term:bm]beams, the maximum spacing shall be 6 m (metric).

content.text: Where the exterior wall of the uppermost [REF:term:tr]storey is set back from the exterior wall of the [REF:term:tr]storey below, the exterior walls perpendicular to the setback wall shall

clauses.text: have their top plate connected with nails that are spaced at no greater than half the spacing required in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect3.art4.table1:long], and

have their top plate splices fastened with twice the number of nails specified in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect11.art4.sent5:short]
                              [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect11.art4.sent6:short].

content.text: The maximum distance between adjacent required [REF:term:br-wl-pnl]braced wall panels in a [REF:term:br-wl-bnd]braced wall band, measured from the edge of the panels, may be increased to 7.3 m (metric) provided that, throughout the height of the [REF:term:bldng]building, the length of any [REF:term:br-wl-pnl]braced wall panel within the [REF:term:br-wl-bnd]braced wall band is not less than 1.2 m (metric).

articles.title: Simplified Approach for Braced Wall Panel Length

content.text: This Article applies to [REF:term:bldng]buildings where

clauses.text: the seismic design parameter, S_{max}, is not greater than 0.47,
the 1-in-50-year hourly wind pressure (HWP) is not greater than 0.60 kPa (metric),
the specified roof snow load, as calculated in accordance with [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect4.subsect2.art2:long], is not greater than 2 kPa (metric),
the plan dimensions of the [REF:term:bldng]building are each not greater than 21.2 m (metric),
the [REF:term:bldng]building is located in rough terrain, as described in Note A-9.23.13.7.(3) and (4),
the greatest eave-to-ridge height of the roof is not greater than 3 m (metric),
the [REF:term:br-wl-pnl]braced wall panels are constructed with gypsum board on at least one side,
