content.text: Wall portions clad with masonry veneer that are located both perpendicular to a [REF:term:br-wl-bnd]braced wall band and within a [REF:term:br-wl-bnd]braced wall band are permitted to be considered as normal-weight construction.

Bracing to resist lateral loads shall be designed and constructed in accordance with [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect13.art4:long] to [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect13.art6:long] and [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect13.art8:long] to [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect13.art10:long].

Roof rafters and joists and ceiling joists shall be continuous
or shall be spliced over vertical supports that extend to suitable
bearing.

Roof and ceiling framing members shall be doubled on each side
of openings greater than 2 rafter (metric) or joist spacings wide.

The length of end bearing of joists and rafters shall be not
less than 38 mm (metric).

Rafters shall be located directly opposite each other and tied
together at the peak, or may be offset by their own thickness if nailed
to a ridge board not less than 17.5 mm (metric) thick.

Except as permitted in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect14.art4.sent3:short], framing members shall be connected by gusset plates or nailing
at the peak in conformance with [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect3.art4.table1:long]

Where the roof framing on opposite sides of the peak is assembled
separately, such as in the case of factory-built houses, the roof
framing on opposite sides is permitted to be fastened together with
galvanized-steel strips not less than 200 mm (metric) by 75 mm (metric) by 0.41 mm (metric) thick spaced not more than 1.2 m (metric) apart and nailed at each end to the framing by at least
two 63 mm (metric) nails.

Rafters shall be shaped at supports to provide even bearing
surfaces and supported directly above the exterior walls.
Hip and valley rafters shall be not less than 50 mm (metric) greater in depth than the common rafters and not less than 38 mm (metric) thick, actual dimension.

articles.title: Intermediate Support for Rafters and Joists

content.text:
Ceiling joists and collar ties of not less than 38 mm (metric) by 89 mm (metric) lumber are permitted to be assumed to provide
intermediate support to reduce the span for rafters and joists where
the roof slope is 1 in 3 or greater.

Collar ties referred to in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect14.art7.sent1:short] more than 2.4 m (metric) long shall be laterally supported
near their centres by not less than 19 mm (metric) by 89
mm (metric) continuous members at right angles to the collar ties.

Dwarf walls and struts are permitted to be used to provide intermediate
support to reduce the span for rafters and joists.

When struts are used to provide intermediate support they shall
be not less than 38 mm (metric) by 89 mm (metric) material
extending from each rafter to a [REF:term:ldbrng]loadbearing wall at an angle of not less than 45° (metric) to the horizontal.

When dwarf walls are used for rafter support, they shall be
framed in the same manner as [REF:term:ldbrng]loadbearing walls and securely fastened top and bottom to the roof and ceiling
framing to prevent over-all movement.

Solid blocking shall be installed between floor joists beneath
dwarf walls referred to in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect14.art7.sent5:short] that enclose finished rooms.

Except as provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect14.art8.sent4:short], roof rafters and joists shall be supported at the ridge of the
roof by

clauses.text:
a [REF:term:ldbrng]loadbearing wall extending from
the ridge to suitable bearing, or

a ridge beam supported by not less than 89 mm (metric) length
of bearing.

content.text: Except as provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect14.art8.sent3:short], the ridge beam referred to in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect14.art8.sent1:short] shall conform to the sizes and spans shown in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.spectables2.table15:long], provided

clauses.text:
the supported rafter or joist length does not exceed 4.9
m (metric), and
the roof does not support any concentrated loads.

content.text: The ridge beam referred to in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect14.art8.sent1:short] need not comply with [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect14.art8.sent2:short] where

clauses.text:
the beam is of not less than 38 mm (metric) by 140
mm (metric) material, and

the beam is supported at intervals not exceeding 1.2 m (metric) by not less than 38 mm (metric) by 89 mm (metric) members
extending vertically from the ridge to suitable bearing.

content.text:
Where the roof
slope is 1 in 3 or steeper, ridge support need not be
provided when the lower ends of the rafters are adequately tied to
prevent outward movement.

Ties required in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect14.art8.sent4:short] are
permitted to consist of tie rods or ceiling joists forming a continuous
tie for opposing rafters and nailed in accordance with [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect14.art8.table1:long]

content.title: Rafter-to-Joist Nailing (Unsupported Ridge)

header_rows.content:
Minimum
Number of Nails Not Less Than 76 mm (metric) Long and 3.66
mm (metric) in DiameterNails with a
diameter less than 3.66 mm (metric) are permitted to be used,
provided the minimum number of nails stated in the Table is modified
as follows:
                                          For a nail diameter greater than or equal to 2.86
mm (metric) and less than 3.25 mm (metric), add 3 nails (metric) to the minimum number of nails, up to a maximum of 10 nails (metric).
                                          For a nail diameter greater than or equal to 3.25
mm (metric) and less than 3.66 mm (metric), add 2 nails (metric) to the minimum number of nails, up to a maximum of 10 nails (metric).
                                       Where more than 10 nails (metric) are required, the connections
between the rafters and the ceiling joists shall be designed in accordance
with [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect4.subsect1.art1.sent1.clause2:long]
                                       [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect4.subsect1.art1.sent1.clause3:short].
                                    The minimum number of nails stated in the
Table is applicable to Spruce-Pine-Fir, Douglas Fir-Larch and Hem-Fir
members. For Northern Species members, add 2 nails (metric) to
the minimum number of nails, up to a maximum of 10 nails. (metric) Where more than 10 nails (metric) are required, the connections
between the rafters and the ceiling joists shall be designed in accordance
with [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect4.subsect1.art1.sent1.clause2:long]
                                       [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect4.subsect1.art1.sent1.clause3:short].
                                    To accommodate nail spacing, not less than 38 mm (metric) × 140 mm (metric) joists shall be used where 6 or
more nails are required, and not less than 38 mm (metric) × 184 mm (metric) joists shall be used where 8 or more nails are required.
                                    The minimum number of nails
in the Table is applicable for a maximum roof [REF:term:dd-ld]dead load of 0.5 kPa (metric).

body_rows.content:
The
connections between the rafters and the ceiling joists shall be designed
in accordance with [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect4.subsect1.art1.sent1.clause2:long]
                                       [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect4.subsect1.art1.sent1.clause3:short].

content.text: Except as permitted in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect14.art8.sent7:short], ceiling joists referred to in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect14.art8.sent5:short] shall be tied to the base of every rafter.

Where ceiling joists referred to in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect14.art8.sent5:short] are raised above the base of the rafters, the connections
between the rafters and the ceiling joists shall be designed in accordance
with [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect4.subsect1.art1.sent1.clause2:long]
                           [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect4.subsect1.art1.sent1.clause3:short].

Ceiling joists referred to in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect14.art8.sent5:short] that are
spliced to make a continuous joist shall be fastened together at each
splice with at least one more nail than required for the rafter-to-joist connection shown in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect14.art8.table1:long]

Members referred to in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect14.art8.sent6:short]
                           [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect14.art8.sent8:short] are permitted
to be fastened together either directly or through a gusset plate.

Roof joists supporting a finished ceiling, other than plywood,
OSB or waferboard, shall be restrained from twisting along the bottom
edges by means of furring, blocking, cross bridging or strapping conforming
to [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect9.art3:long]

Except as permitted in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect14.art10.sent2:short], ceiling joists supporting part of the roof load from the rafters
shall be not less than 25 mm (metric) greater in depth than required
for ceiling joists not supporting part of the roof load.

When the roof slope is 1 in 4 or less, the ceiling joist sizes
referred to in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect14.art10.sent1:short] shall be determined
from [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.spectables2.table6:long]
                           [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.spectables2.table9:long]
                           [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.spectables2.table15:long] for roof joists.

Wood roof trusses
shall be designed in accordance with good engineering practice such
as that described in TPIC 2019, "Truss Design Procedures and Specifications for Light Metal Plate Connected Wood Trusses."

The joint connections used in trusses described in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect14.art11.sent1:short] shall be designed in conformance with
the requirements in Subsection 4.3.1. (See [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.appnote135:short].)

All member bracing
shall be installed as per the truss design drawings, and continuous
lateral bracing shall be adequately anchored to the roof and ceiling
diaphragms at intervals no greater than 6.10 m o.c. (metric)

Subflooring shall be provided beneath finish flooring where
the finish flooring does not have adequate strength to support the
specified [REF:term:lv-ld]live loads (see Subsection 9.30.3.).
Except as provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect15.art2.sent2:short], wood-based panels for subfloors shall conform to

clauses.text: CSA O121, "Douglas fir plywood,"
CSA O151, "Canadian softwood plywood,"
CSA O153, "Poplar plywood,"
CSA O325, "Construction sheathing," or
CSA O437.0, "OSB and Waferboard."

content.text:
Particleboard subflooring may be used only where a [REF:term:bldng]building is constructed in a factory so that
the subfloor will not be exposed to the weather.
Subflooring described in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect15.art2.sent2:short] shall conform to grade D-2 or D-3 in ANSI A208.1, "Particleboard."

Subflooring described in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect15.art2.sent2:short] shall have its upper surface and all edges treated to restrict
water absorption, where the subfloor is used in bathrooms, kitchens,
laundry rooms or other areas subject to periodic wetting. (See [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.appnote136:short].)

Where the edges of panel-type subflooring are required to be
supported (see Sentence 9.30.2.1.(2)), such support shall consist
of tongue-and-groove panel edges or not less than 38 mm (metric) by 38 mm (metric) blocking securely nailed between framing members.

Plywood subflooring shall be installed with the surface grain
at right angles to the joists and with joints parallel to floor joists
staggered.

OSB subflooring conforming to CSA O325, "Construction sheathing," or to O-1 and O-2 grades in CSA O437.0, "OSB and Waferboard," and waferboard subflooring conforming
to R-1 grade in CSA O437.0 shall be installed so that the direction of face
orientation is at right angles to the joists and the joints parallel
to the floor joists are staggered. (See [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.appnote137:short].)

Except as provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect15.art5.sent2:short]
                           [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect15.art5.sent3:short], subfloors shall conform to either [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect15.art5.table1:long]
                           [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect15.art5.table2:long].

content.title: Thickness of Subflooring

header_rows.content: OSB, O-1 Grade, and Waferboard, R-1 Grade

content.title: Rating for Subfloor when Applying CSA O325

content.text:
Where the finished flooring consists of not less than 19 mm (metric) matched wood strip flooring laid at right angles to
joists spaced not more than 600 mm o.c. (metric), subflooring
shall be permitted to consist of not less than

clauses.text: 12.5 mm (metric) thick plywood,
12.5 mm (metric) thick OSB conforming to O-2 grade,
12.7 mm (metric) thick OSB conforming to O-1 grade,

12.7 mm (metric) thick waferboard conforming to R-1 grade,
or
OSB conforming to 2R32/2F16 grade.

content.text:
Except where the flooring consists of ceramic tiles applied
with adhesive, where a separate panel-type underlay or concrete topping
is applied to a subfloor on joists spaced not more than 400
mm (metric) o.c., the subfloor is permitted to consist of not less than

clauses.text: 12.5 mm (metric) thick plywood,
12.5 mm (metric) thick OSB conforming to O-2 grade,
12.7 mm (metric) thick OSB conforming to O-1 grade,

12.7 mm (metric) thick waferboard conforming to R-1 grade,
or
OSB conforming to 2R32/2F16 grade.

content.text:
When resilient flooring is applied directly to an OSB, waferboard,
particleboard or plywood subfloor, the subfloor shall be fastened
to the supports with annular grooved nails.
Lumber subflooring shall be laid at an angle of not less than 45° (metric) to the joists.

Lumber subflooring shall be fully supported at the ends on solid
bearing.

Lumber for subflooring shall be of uniform thickness and not
more than 184 mm (metric) wide.

Except where the 1-in-50-year hourly wind pressure (HWP) is less than 0.8 kPa (metric) and the seismic design parameter, S_{max}, for Site Class C, is less than or equal to 0.47, continuous lumber or panel-type
roof sheathing shall be installed to support the roofing.
Wood-based panels used for roof sheathing shall conform to the requirements of

clauses.text: CSA O121, "Douglas fir plywood,"
CSA O151, "Canadian softwood plywood,"
CSA O153, "Poplar plywood,"
CSA O325, "Construction sheathing," or
CSA O437.0, "OSB and Waferboard."

content.text:
Plywood roof sheathing shall be installed with the surface grain
at right angles to the roof framing.

OSB roof sheathing conforming to CSA O325, "Construction sheathing," or to O-1 and O-2 grades as specified
in CSA O437.0, "OSB and Waferboard," shall be installed
with the direction of face orientation at right angles to the roof
framing members. (See Note A-9.23.15.4.(2).)

Panel-type sheathing board shall be applied so that joints perpendicular
to the roof ridge are staggered where

clauses.text:
the sheathing is applied with the surface grain parallel to
the roof ridge, and

the thickness of the sheathing is such that the edges are required
to be supported.

content.text:
A gap of not less than 2 mm (metric) shall be left between
sheets of plywood, OSB or waferboard.

Lumber roof sheathing shall not be more than 286 mm (metric) wide and shall be applied so that all ends are supported with end
joints staggered.
Lumber roof sheathing shall be installed diagonally, where

clauses.text: the seismic design parameter, S_{max}, for Site Class C is greater than 0.47 but not greater than 0.8, or
the 1-in-50 hourly wind pressure is equal to or greater than 0.80 kPa (metric) but less than 1.20 kPa (metric).

content.text:
Lumber roof sheathing shall be designed according to Part 4,
where

clauses.text:
the seismic spectral acceleration, S_{a}(0.2), is greater
than 1.2, or
the 1-in-50 hourly wind pressure is equal to or greater than 1.20 kPa (metric).

content.text:
Where panel-type roof sheathing requires edge support, the support
shall consist of metal H clips or not less than 38 mm (metric) by 38 mm (metric) blocking securely nailed between framing members.

The thickness or rating of roof sheathing on a flat roof used
as a walking deck shall conform to either [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect15.art5.table1:long]
                           [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect15.art5.table2:long] for subfloors.

The thickness or rating of roof sheathing on a roof not used
as a walking deck shall conform to either [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect16.art7.table1:long]
                           [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect16.art7.table2:long].

Asphalt-coated or asphalt-impregnated fibreboard not less than 11.1 mm (metric) thick conforming to CAN/ULC-S706.1, "Standard for Wood Fibre Insulating Boards for Buildings," is permitted to be used as a roof sheathing over
supports spaced not more than  400 mm (metric) o.c. provided the
roofing consists of

clauses.text:
a continuous sheet of galvanized steel not less than 0.33
mm (metric) in thickness, or
a continuous sheet of aluminum not less than 0.61 mm (metric) in thickness.

content.text: All edges of sheathing described in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect16.art7.sent3:short] shall be supported by blocking or framing.

content.title: Thickness of Roof Sheathing

header_rows.content: OSB, O-1 Grade, and Waferboard, R-1 Grade

content.title: Rating for Roof Sheathing When Applying CSA O325

content.text:
Exterior walls and gable ends shall be sheathed when the exterior
cladding requires intermediate fastening between supports or if the
exterior cladding requires solid backing.

Where wall sheathing is required for the purpose of complying
with this Section, it shall conform to either [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect17.art2.table1:long]
                           [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect17.art2.table2:short]. (See also Article 9.25.5.1.)

content.title: Wall Sheathing Thickness and Specifications

body_rows.content: OSB, O-1 Grade, and Waferboard, R-1 Grade
CSA O121 CSA O151 CSA O153
Polyurethane and Polyisocyanurate Types 2 and 3, faced

content.title: Rating for Wall Sheathing when Applying CSA O325

content.text:
Gypsum sheathing, rigid insulation and fibreboard shall not
be used for the attachment of cladding materials.

Lumber wall sheathing shall be applied so that all ends are
supported.

Where lumber wall sheathing is required to provide bracing according
to Article 9.23.10.2., it shall be applied with end joints
staggered.

A gap of not less than 2 mm (metric) shall be left between
sheets of plywood, OSB, waferboard or fibreboard.

Where the bottom portions of mansard style roofs are vented,
the vertical framing members behind the sloping portions shall be
considered on the same basis as exterior wall studs and shall conform
to Articles 9.27.3.2. to 9.27.3.6.
This Section applies to sheet steel studs for use in non-[REF:term:ldbrng]loadbearing exterior and interior walls.

Where [REF:term:ldbrng] loadbearing steel studs are
used, they shall be designed in conformance with [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4:long].
Steel studs and runners shall conform to [REF:standard:aisis201]

Metal thickness specified in this Section shall be the minimum
base steel thickness exclusive of coatings.

Screws for the application of cladding, sheathing or interior
finish materials to steel studs, runners and furring channels shall
conform to

clauses.text: [REF:standard:astmc954] or
[REF:standard:astmc1002]

articles.title: Cladding, Sheathing and Interior Finish Required

content.text:
Cladding or sheathing, and interior finish shall be installed
on steel stud framing and shall be fastened with screws

clauses.text: spaced at the appropriate spacing described in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect29:long], and
penetrating not less than 10 mm (metric) through the metal.

articles.title: Size and Spacing of Studs in Interior Walls

content.text:
Except as required in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect24.subsect2.art3:long]
                           [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect24.subsect2.art4:long], the size and spacing
of steel studs for non-[REF:term:ldbrng]loadbearing  interior
walls shall conform to [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect24.subsect2.art1.table1:long]

content.title:
Steel Studs for Non-Loadbearing Interior WallsThe values in the Table are based on a
single layer of 12.7 mm (metric) gypsum panel sheathing installed
on each side of the studs. Where one side is not accessible, gypsum
panels on only one side will suffice. The values are also based on
attaching gypsum panel sheathing using screws not smaller than No.
6 spaced at a maximum of 300 mm (metric) at edges and at intermediate
supports.

content.text:
Except as required in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect24.subsect2.art4:long], steel studs
in non-[REF:term:ldbrng]loadbearing interior walls shall
have a metal thickness of not less than 0.46 mm (metric).

Runners for interior and exterior non-[REF:term:ldbrng]loadbearing walls shall have a thickness not less than the thickness of the
corresponding studs and shall have not less than 30 mm (metric) flanges.

Where openings for doors in non-[REF:term:ldbrng]loadbearing
                           [REF:term:fr-prtn]fire separations required to have a [REF:term:fr-rtnc-]fire-resistance rating do not exceed 1 200 mm (metric) in width,

clauses.text: the width of steel studs shall be not less than 63 mm (metric), and
the metal thickness shall be not less than 0.46 mm (metric).

content.text: Where openings described in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect24.subsect2.art4.sent1:short] exceed 1 200 mm (metric) in width,

clauses.text: the width of steel studs shall be not less than 91 mm (metric), and
the metal thickness shall be not less than 0.85 mm (metric).

content.text:
The distance to the first stud beyond the jamb of any door opening
in a [REF:term:fr-prtn]fire separation required to have
a [REF:term:fr-rtnc-]fire-resistance rating shall not exceed 400 mm (metric).

Where the distance between the framing over the opening referred
to in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect24.subsect2.art4.sent3:short] and the top runner
exceeds 400 mm (metric) in such walls, intermediate support shall
be installed at intervals of not more than 400 mm (metric) above
the opening.

articles.title: Size and Spacing of Studs in Exterior Walls

content.text: The size and spacing of non-[REF:term:ldbrng]loadbearing steel studs for exterior walls shall conform to [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect24.subsect2.art5.table1:long]

content.title:
Size and Spacing of Steel Studs for Non-Loadbearing Exterior
Walls

content.text: Runners shall be provided at the tops and bottoms of walls.

Runners required in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect24.subsect3.art1.sent1:short] shall
be securely attached to the [REF:term:bldng]building at
approximately 50 mm (metric) from the ends, and at intervals of
not more than 600 mm (metric) o.c. for interior walls and 300 mm (metric) o.c. for exterior walls.
Fasteners used for attachment described in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect24.subsect3.art1.sent2:short] shall consist of the equivalent of 63 mm (metric) nails or 25 mm (metric) screws.

Studs at openings and which are not full wall height shall be
supported by a runner at the ends of the studs, securely fastened
to the full length studs at the sides of the opening.

Steel studs used in walls required to have a [REF:term:fr-rtnc-]fire-resistance rating shall be installed
so that there is not less than a 12 mm (metric) clearance between
the top of the stud and the top of the runner to allow for expansion
in the event of fire.

Except as provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect24.subsect3.art6:long], studs in
walls referred to in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect24.subsect3.art2.sent1:short] shall
not be attached to the runners in a manner that will prevent such
expansion.

Framing above doors with steel door frames in non-[REF:term:ldbrng]loadbearing
                           [REF:term:fr-prtn] fire separations required to have a [REF:term:fr-rtnc-]fire-resistance rating shall consist of 2 runners (metric) on the flat fastened back
to back. (See [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.appnote138:short].)

The upper runner required in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect24.subsect3.art2.sent3:short] shall be bent at each end to extend upwards not less
than 150 mm (metric) and fastened to the adjacent studs.

A gypsum board filler piece, the width and length of the runner,
shall be provided between the door frame referred to in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect24.subsect3.art2.sent3:short] and the adjacent runner.

Steel studs shall be installed with webs at right angles to
the wall face and, except at openings, shall be continuous for the
full wall height.

Corners and intersections of walls shall be constructed to provide
support for the cladding materials.

Studs shall be doubled on each side of every opening where such
openings involve more than one stud space, and shall be tripled where
the openings in exterior walls exceed 2.4 m (metric) in width.

Studs described in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect24.subsect3.art5.sent1:short] shall
be fastened together by screws, crimping or welding to act as a single
structural unit in resisting transverse loads.

Studs shall be attached to runners by screws, crimping or welding
around wall openings and elsewhere where necessary to keep the studs
in alignment during construction.

Where clearance for expansion is required in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect24.subsect3.art2:long], attachment required in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect24.subsect3.art6.sent1:short] shall be applied between studs and bottom runners only.

Openings for [REF:term:fr-dmpr]fire dampers in non-[REF:term:ldbrng]loadbearing
                           [REF:term:fr-prtn]fire separations required to have a [REF:term:fr-rtnc-]fire-resistance rating shall be framed with double studs on each side of the opening.

The sill and header for openings described in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect24.subsect3.art7.sent1:short] shall consist of a runner track with
right angle bends made on each end so as to extend 300 mm (metric) above the header or below the sill and fastened to the studs.

The openings described in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect24.subsect3.art7.sent1:short] shall be lined with a layer of gypsum board not less than 12.7 mm (metric) thick fastened to stud and runner webs.

sections.title: Heat Transfer, Air Leakage and Condensation Control

content.text:
This Section is concerned with heat, air and water vapour transfer
and measures to control condensation.

All walls, ceilings and floors separating [REF:term:cnd-sp]conditioned space from unconditioned space, the exterior air
or the ground shall be

clauses.text: provided with

subclauses.text: thermal insulation conforming to [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect25.subsect2:long] and [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36:long],
an air barrier conforming to [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect25.subsect3:long] and [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36:long], and
a [REF:term:vpr-brrr]vapour barrier conforming to [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect25.subsect4:long], and

clauses.text:
constructed in such a way that the properties and relative position
of all materials conform to [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect25.subsect5:long]

content.text:
Insulation and sealing of heating and ventilating ducts shall
conform to [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect32:long]
                           [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect33:long]
                           [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36:long]

All walls, ceilings and floors separating heated space from
unheated space, the exterior air or the exterior [REF:term:l]soil shall be provided with sufficient thermal insulation to prevent
moisture condensation on their room side during the winter and to
ensure comfortable conditions for the occupants. (See [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.appnote1:long].)
Except as required in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect25.subsect2.art2.sent2:short], thermal insulation shall conform to the requirements of

clauses.text: [REF:standard:astmc726]
[REF:standard:cgsb-51.25]
[REF:standard:cgsb51-gp-27m]
[REF:standard:ulcs701]
[REF:standard:ulcs702]
[REF:standard:ulcs703]
[REF:standard:ulcs704]
[REF:standard:ulcs705.1] or
[REF:standard:ulcs706]

content.text:
The [REF:term:flm-prd-]flame-spread ratings requirements
contained in the standards listed in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect25.subsect2.art2.sent1:short] shall not apply. (See [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.appnote140:short].)

Insulation in contact with the ground shall be inert to the
action of [REF:term:l]soil and water and shall be such
that its insulative properties are not significantly reduced by moisture.

Insulation shall be installed so that there is a reasonably
uniform insulating value over the entire face of the insulated area.

Insulation shall be applied to the full width and length of
the space between furring or framing.

Except where the insulation provides the principal resistance
to air leakage, thermal insulation shall be installed so that at least
one face is in full and continuous contact with an element with low
air permeance. (See [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.appnote141:short].)

Insulation shall
be installed over the full height of [REF:term:fndtn-nt]foundation walls enclosing a [REF:term:bmnt]basement or heated crawl
space. (See also [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.appnote229:long].)

Insulation around concrete slabs-on-ground shall be located
so that heat from the [REF:term:bldng]building is not restricted
from reaching the ground beneath the perimeter, where exterior walls
are not supported by footings extending below frost level.

Where insulation is exposed to the weather and subject to mechanical
damage, it shall be protected with not less than

clauses.text: 6 mm (metric) preservative-treated plywood, or

12 mm (metric) cement parging on wire lath applied to the
exposed face and edge.

content.text:
Insulation located in areas where it may be subject to mechanical
damage shall be protected by a covering such as gypsum board, plywood,
particleboard, OSB, waferboard or hardboard.
Insulation in factory-built [REF:term:bldng]buildings shall be installed so that it will not become dislodged during transportation.

Except as provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect25.subsect2.art4.sent2:short]
                           [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect25.subsect2.art4.sent6:short], loose-fill insulation shall be used on horizontal
surfaces only.

Where loose-fill insulation is installed in an unconfined sloped
space, such as an attic space over a sloped ceiling, the supporting
slope shall not be more than

clauses.text: 4.5 in 12 for mineral fibre or cellulose fibre insulation, and
2.5 in 12 for other types of insulation.

content.text:
Loose-fill insulation is permitted to be used in wood-frame
walls of existing [REF:term:bldng]buildings. (See [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.appnote142:short].)

Where blown-in insulation is installed in above-ground or below-ground
wood-frame walls of new [REF:term:bldng]buildings,

clauses.text:
the density of the installed insulation shall be sufficient
to preclude settlement,

the insulation shall be installed behind a membrane that will
permit visual inspection prior to the installation of the interior
finish,

the insulation shall be installed in a manner that will not
interfere with the installation of the interior finish, and

no water shall be added to the insulation, unless it can be
shown that the added water will not adversely affect other materials
in the assembly.

content.text:
Water repellent loose-fill insulation is permitted to be used
between the outer and inner wythes of masonry [REF:term:cvt-wll]cavity walls. (See [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.appnote143:short].)
Where soffit venting is used, measures shall be taken

clauses.text:
to prevent loose-fill insulation from blocking the soffit vents
and to maintain an open path for circulation of air from the vents
into the [REF:term:ttc-r-rf]attic or roof space, and

to minimize airflow into the insulation near the soffit vents
to maintain the thermal performance of the material. (See [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect19.subsect1.art3:long])

content.text:
Spray-applied polyurethane insulation shall be installed in
accordance with [REF:standard:ulcs705.2]

Wall, ceiling and floor assemblies separating [REF:term:cnd-sp]conditioned space from unconditioned space or from the ground
shall be constructed so as to include an [REF:term:r-brrr] air
barrier system that will provide a continuous barrier to air
leakage

clauses.text:
from the interior of the [REF:term:bldng]building into wall, floor, [REF:term:ttc-r-rf]attic or roof spaces, sufficient to prevent
excessive moisture condensation in such spaces during the winter,
and
from the exterior or the ground inward sufficient to

subclauses.text: prevent moisture condensation on the room side during winter,
ensure comfortable conditions for the occupants, and
minimize the ingress of [REF:term:l]soil gas.

content.text:
[REF:term:r-brrr]Air barrier systems shall possess
the characteristics necessary to provide an effective barrier to air
infiltration and exfiltration under differential air pressure due
to stack effect, mechanical systems or wind.

Where polyethylene sheet is used to provide airtightness in the [REF:term:r-brrr]air barrier
system, it shall conform to [REF:standard:cgsb-51.34]

articles.title: Continuity of the Air Barrier System

content.text:
Where the [REF:term:r-brrr]air barrier system consists
of an air-impermeable panel-type material, all joints shall be sealed
to prevent air leakage.

Except as provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect25.subsect3.art6.sent3:long], where the [REF:term:r-brrr]air barrier system consists of flexible sheet
material, all joints shall be

clauses.text: sealed, or

lapped not less than 100 mm (metric) and clamped, such as
between framing members, furring or blocking, and rigid panels.

content.text:
Where an interior wall meets an exterior wall, ceiling, floor
or roof required to be provided with air barrier protection, the [REF:term:r-brrr]air barrier system shall extend across the intersection.

Where an interior wall projects through a ceiling or extends
to become an exterior wall, spaces in the wall shall be blocked to
provide continuity across those spaces with the [REF:term:r-brrr]air barrier system in the abutting walls or ceiling.

Where an interior floor projects through an exterior wall or
extends to become an exterior floor, continuity of the [REF:term:r-brrr]air barrier system shall be maintained from
the abutting walls across the floor assembly.

Penetrations of the [REF:term:r-brrr]air barrier system, such as those created by the installation of doors, windows, electrical
wiring, electrical boxes, piping or ductwork, shall be sealed to maintain
the integrity of the [REF:term:r-brrr]air barrier system over the entire surface.

Where access hatches and sump pit covers are installed through
assemblies constructed with an [REF:term:r-brrr]air barrier system, they shall be weatherstripped around their perimeters to prevent
air leakage.

Clearances between [REF:term:chmn]chimneys or [REF:term:g-vnt]gas vents and the surrounding construction that
would permit air leakage
from within the [REF:term:bldng]building into a wall or [REF:term:ttc-r-rf]attic or roof space shall be sealed by [REF:term:ncmbtbl]noncombustible material to prevent such leakage.

articles.title: Air Leakage Control in Masonry Walls

content.text:
Masonry walls required to provide a barrier to the ingress of
air from the ground shall

clauses.text: include a course of masonry units without voids, or

be sealed with flashing material extending across the full width
of the masonry.

content.text: The masonry course or flashing described in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect25.subsect3.art4.sent1:short] shall

clauses.text:
be located at the level of the adjoining floor and be sealed
to it in accordance with [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect25.subsect3.art6:long], or

in the absence of a floor, be located at the level of the ground
cover required by [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect18.subsect6.art1:long] and be sealed to it.

articles.title: Air Leakage Control in Underground Roofs

content.text:
Waterproofing systems for roofs of underground structures shall
be sealed to the air barrier in the walls.

Materials used to provide a barrier to the ingress of air through
floors-on-ground shall conform to [REF:standard:cgsb-51.34]

Where the floor-on-ground is a concrete slab, the air barrier
shall be

clauses.text: installed below the slab, or

applied to the top of the slab, provided a separate floor is
installed over the slab.

content.text:
Where the air barrier installed below a floor-on-ground is flexible
sheet material, joints in the barrier shall be lapped not less than 300 mm (metric). (See [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.appnote146:short].)

Where installed in conjunction with a framed floor-on-ground
or above a floor-on-ground, the air barrier shall be installed in
accordance with [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect25.subsect3.art3:long]

A floor-on-ground shall be sealed around its perimeter to the
inner surfaces of adjacent walls using flexible sealant.

All penetrations of a floor-on-ground that are required to drain
water from the floor surface shall be sealed in a manner that prevents
the upward flow of air without preventing the downward flow of liquid
water.

Thermally insulated wall, ceiling and floor assemblies shall
be constructed with a [REF:term:vpr-brrr]vapour barrier so as to provide a barrier to diffusion of water vapour from the
interior into wall spaces, floor spaces or [REF:term:ttc-r-rf]attic or roof spaces.

Except as provided
in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect25.subsect4.art2.sent2:short], [REF:term:vpr-brrr]vapour barriers shall have a permeance not greater
than 60 ng/(Pa×s×m2) (metric) measured in accordance
with [REF:standard:astme96m] using the desiccant method (dry
cup).

Thermally insulated [REF:term:fndtn]foundation wall
assemblies are permitted to be constructed with variable-permeance [REF:term:vpr-brrr]vapour barriers having a permeance not greater
than 60 ng/(Pa×s×m2) (metric) using the desiccant
method (dry cup) and greater than 300 ng/(Pa×s×m2) (metric) using the water method (wet cup) measured in accordance
with [REF:standard:astme96m](See [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.appnote147:short].)

Where the intended use of the interior space will result in
high moisture generation, the assembly shall be designed according
to Part 5. (See [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.appnote148:short].)

Where polyethylene is installed to serve only as the [REF:term:vpr-brrr]vapour barrier, it shall comply with [REF:external:cgsb-51.34]Clause 4.4, Thermal Stability, and Clause 5.7,
Oxidative Induction Time, of 
                           [REF:standard:cgsb-51.34]

Membrane-type [REF:term:vpr-brrr]vapour barriers other
than polyethylene shall conform to the requirements of [REF:standard:cgsb-51.33]

Membrane-type [REF:term:vpr-brrr]vapour barriers other
than polyethylene that are susceptible to deterioration under prolonged
exposure to direct ultraviolet radiation shall

clauses.text: be covered, or

only be installed in locations that are not exposed to direct
ultraviolet radiation after the completion of construction.

content.text:
Where a coating is applied to gypsum board to function as the [REF:term:vpr-brrr]vapour barrier, the permeance of the coating
shall be determined in accordance with [REF:standard:cgsb-1.501]

Where foamed plastic insulation functions as the [REF:term:vpr-brrr]vapour barrier, it shall be sufficiently thick
so as to meet the requirement of [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect25.subsect4.art2.sent1:short].

Products installed to function as the [REF:term:vpr-brrr]vapour barrier shall protect the warm side of wall, ceiling
and floor assemblies.

Where different products are used for the [REF:term:vpr-brrr]vapour barrier and the insulation, the [REF:term:vpr-brrr]vapour barrier shall be installed sufficiently close to the
warm side of the insulation to prevent condensation at design conditions.
(See [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.appnote150:short]
                           [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.appnote152:long].)

Where the same product is used for the [REF:term:vpr-brrr]vapour barrier and the insulation, the product shall be installed
sufficiently close to the warm side of the assembly to prevent condensation
at design conditions. (See [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.appnote150:long], [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.appnote152:number] and [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.appnote155:number])

subsections.title: Properties and Position of Materials in the Building Envelope

content.text:
Except as provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect25.subsect5.art1.sent2:short]
                           [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect25.subsect5.art1.sent4:short], sheet and panel-type materials incorporated into assemblies
described in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect25.subsect1.art1:long] shall conform to [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect25.subsect5.art2:long], where

clauses.text: the material has

subclauses.text: an air leakage characteristic less than 0.1 L/(s×m2) (metric) at 75 Pa (metric), and

a water vapour permeance less than 60 ng/(Pa×s×m2) (metric) when measured in accordance with [REF:standard:astme96m] using the desiccant method (dry cup) (see [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.appnote153:short]), and

clauses.text:
the intended use of the interior space where the materials are
installed will not result in high moisture generation.

content.text:
Where the intended use of the interior space will result in
high moisture generation, the assembly shall be designed according
to Part 5.

Wood-based sheathing materials not more than 12.5 mm (metric) thick and complying with [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect17.art2:long] need not comply
with [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect25.subsect5.art1.sent1:short]. (See [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.appnote154:short].)

Where a material has a water vapour permeance not less than 30 ng/(Pa×s×m2)  (metric) and a thermal resistance not
less than 0.7 (m2×K)/W (metric) and the heating
degree-days of the [REF:term:bldng]building location are
less than 6000 (metric), the assembly need not comply with [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect25.subsect5.art1.sent1:short].
Sheet and panel-type materials described in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect25.subsect5.art1:short] shall be installed

clauses.text: on the warm face of the assembly (see also [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect25.subsect4.art2:long]),

at a location where the ratio between the total thermal resistance
of all materials outboard of its innermost impermeable surface and
the total thermal resistance of all materials inboard of that surface
is not less than that required by [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect25.subsect5.art2.table1:long], or
outboard of an air space that is vented to the outdoors.

content.text: For walls, the air space described in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect25.subsect5.art2.sent1.clause3:medium] shall comply with [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect27.subsect2.art2.sent1.clause1:long].

content.title: Ratio of Outboard to Inboard Thermal Resistance

header_rows.content: Heating Degree-Days of [REF:term:bldng] Building LocationSee [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part1.sect1.subsect3.art1.sent1:long]., Celsius degree-days

Minimum Ratio of Total Thermal
Resistance Outboard of Material's Inner Surface to Total Thermal Resistance
Inboard of Material's Inner Surface

content.text:
For the purpose of this Section, the term “roof” shall mean
sloped or near-horizontal assemblies that protect the spaces beneath
them, including platforms that effectively serve as roofs with respect
to the accumulation or drainage of precipitation. (See [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.appnote156:short].)

For the purpose of this Section, the term “roofing” shall mean
the primary covering for roofs.

Roofs shall be protected with roofing, including flashing, installed
so as to

clauses.text: effectively shed water,
prevent the ingress of water and moisture into [REF:term:bldng]building assemblies and occupied space, and
minimize the ingress of water due to ice damming into [REF:term:bldng]building assemblies.

content.text:
Compliance with [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect26.subsect1.art2.sent1:short] shall
be demonstrated by conforming to

clauses.text: the remainder of this Section, or
Part 5.

content.text:
Methods described in [REF:standard:csaa123.51] are
permitted to be used for the installation of asphalt shingles in lieu
of the methods described in this Section.
Materials used for the preparation of the substrate for roofing shall conform to the requirements of the applicable standards in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect26.subsect2.art1.table1:long].

content.title: Materials for Preparation of the Substrate for Roofing

content.text: Roofing materials shall conform to the requirements of the applicable standards in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect26.subsect2.art1.table2:long].

content.title: Roofing Materials

body_rows.content:
[REF:standard:astmd3019]
                                    For the purpose of this Subsection, [REF:standard:astmd3019] shall only apply
to the non-fibered and non-asbestos-fibered types (I and III) of asphalt
roll roofing.

content.text:
Materials listed in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect26.subsect2.art1.table1:long]
                           [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect26.subsect2.art1.table2:long] shall be installed in
conformance with the manufacturer's written instructions. (See [REF:internal:nbc.divA.part1.sect5.subsect1.art2.sent1:long].)

Nails used for roofing shall be corrosion-resistant roofing
or shingle nails conforming to

clauses.text: [REF:standard:astmf1667] or
[REF:standard:csab111]

content.text: Nails shall have sufficient length to penetrate through, or 12 mm (metric) into, roof sheathing.

Nails used with asphalt roofing shall have a head diameter of
not less than 9.5 mm (metric) and a shank thickness of not less
than 2.95 mm (metric).

Nails used with wood shingles or shakes shall have a head diameter
of not less than 4.8 mm (metric) and a shank thickness of not
less than 2.0 mm (metric) and shall be stainless steel, aluminum
or hot-dipped galvanized. (See [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.appnote157:short].)

Staples used to apply asphalt or wood shingles shall be corrosion-resistant
and shall be driven with the crown parallel to the eaves.

Staples used with asphalt shingles shall be not less than 19 mm (metric) long, 1.6 mm (metric) diam or thickness, with not
less than a 25 mm (metric) crown, except that an 11 mm (metric) crown may be used as provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect26.subsect7.art4.sent2:long].

Staples used with wood shingles shall be not less than 29 mm (metric) long, 1.6 mm (metric) diam or thickness, with not
less than a 9.5 mm (metric) crown and shall be stainless steel
or aluminum. (See [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.appnote157:long].)

Except as provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect26.subsect3.art1.sent2:short]
                           [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect26.subsect3.art1.sent3:short], the slopes on which roof coverings may be applied
shall conform to [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect26.subsect3.art1.table1:long]

Asphalt and gravel or coal tar and gravel roofs may be constructed
with lower slopes than required in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect26.subsect3.art1.sent1:short] when effective drainage is provided by roof drains
located at the lowest points on the roofs.

Profiled metal roof cladding systems specifically designed for
low-slope applications are permitted to be installed with lower slopes
than required by [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect26.subsect3.art1.sent1:short], provided
they are installed in conformance with the manufacturer's written
recommendations.

Except where back-slope will not adversely affect adjacent supported
or supporting constructions due to water ingress, roofs and constructions
that effectively serve as roofs shall be constructed with sufficient
slope away from

clauses.text: exterior walls, and

[REF:term:guard]guards that are connected to the
roof, or to a construction that effectively serves as a roof, by more
than pickets or posts.

content.text: The slope required by [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect26.subsect3.art1.sent4:short] shall be sufficient to maintain a positive slope

clauses.text:
after expected shrinkage of the [REF:term:bldng]building frame, where these surfaces are supported by exterior walls and
exterior columns (see [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.appnote170:long]), and

once design loading is taken into consideration, where these
surfaces are cantilevered from exterior walls.

content.title: Roofing Types and Slope Limits

body_rows.content:
Glass Fibre Reinforced Polyester
Roofing Panels

content.text:
Except where the omission of flashing will not adversely affect
adjacent supported or supporting constructions, flashing shall be
installed at junctions between roofs and

clauses.text: walls that rise above the roof, and

[REF:term:guard]guards that are connected to the
roof by more than pickets or posts.

content.text:
For the purpose of [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect26.subsect4.art1.sent1:short],
roofs shall include platforms that effectively serve as roofs with
respect to the accumulation or drainage of precipitation.
Sheet metal flashing shall consist of not less than

clauses.text: 1.73 mm (metric) thick sheet lead,
0.33 mm (metric) thick galvanized steel,
0.33 mm (metric) thick copper,
0.35 mm (metric) thick zinc, or
0.48 mm (metric) thick aluminum.

content.text:
Where sloping surfaces of shingled roofs intersect to form a
valley, the valley shall be flashed.
Valley flashing shall be installed over continuous sheathing.

Closed valleys shall not be used with rigid shingles on slopes
of less than 1 in 1.2.
Open valleys shall be flashed with at least

clauses.text:
one layer of sheet metal not less than 600 mm (metric) wide,
or
2 layers of roll roofing.

content.text:
The bottom layer of roofing required in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect26.subsect4.art3.sent4:short] shall consist of at least Type S smooth roll roofing
or Type M mineral surface roll roofing (mineral surface down) not
less than 457 mm (metric) wide, centred in the valley and fastened
with nails spaced not more than 450 mm (metric) o.c. located 25 mm (metric) away from the edges.

The top layer of roofing required in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect26.subsect4.art3.sent4:short] shall consist of at least Type M mineral surface roll
roofing (mineral surface up), 914 mm (metric) wide, centred in
the valley, applied over a 100 mm (metric) wide strip of cement
along each edge of the bottom layer, and fastened with a sufficient
number of nails to hold it in place until the shingles are applied.

articles.title: Intersection of Shingle Roofs and Masonry

content.text: The intersection of shingle roofs and masonry walls or [REF:term:chmn]chimneys shall be protected with flashing.

Counter flashing required in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect26.subsect4.art4.sent1:short] shall be embedded not less than 25 mm (metric) in
the masonry and shall extend not less than 150 mm (metric) down
the masonry and lap the lower flashing not less than 100 mm (metric).

Flashing along the slopes of a roof described in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect26.subsect4.art4.sent1:short] shall be stepped so that there is
not less than a 75 mm (metric) head lap in both the lower flashing
and counter flashing.

Where the roof described in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect26.subsect4.art4.sent1:short] slopes upwards from the masonry, the flashing shall extend up the
roof slope to a point equal in height to the flashing on the masonry,
but not less than 1.5 times the shingle exposure.

articles.title: Intersection of Shingle Roofs and Walls other than Masonry

content.text:
The intersection of shingle roofs and walls clad with other
than masonry shall be protected with flashing.

Flashing required in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect26.subsect4.art5.sent1:short] shall be installed so that it extends up the wall not less than 75 mm (metric) behind the sheathing paper, and extends not less than 75 mm (metric) horizontally.

Along the slope of the roof, the flashing required in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect26.subsect4.art5.sent1:short] shall be stepped with not less than
a 75 mm (metric) head lap.

articles.title: Intersection of Built-Up Roofs and Masonry

content.text:
The intersection of built-up roofs with masonry walls or [REF:term:chmn]chimneys shall have a cant strip at the intersection,
and a roofing membrane shall be mopped over the cant strip and not
less than 150 mm (metric) up the wall.

Counter flashing installed over the intersection referred to
in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect26.subsect4.art6.sent1:short] shall be embedded not
less than 25 mm (metric) in the masonry, and shall be of sufficient
length to extend down not less than 150 mm (metric), lapping the
membrane on the masonry not less than 100 mm (metric).

articles.title: Intersection of Built-Up Roofs and Walls other than Masonry

content.text:
The intersection of built-up roofs with walls clad with other
than masonry shall have a cant strip at the intersection.

The roofing membrane shall be mopped over the cant strip referred
to in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect26.subsect4.art7.sent1:short].
Flashing plies shall extend not less than 150 mm (metric) up the wall referred to in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect26.subsect4.art7.sent1:short] behind the sheathing paper.

Except as otherwise permitted in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect26.subsect4.art8.sent5:short], [REF:term:chmn]chimney saddles shall be
installed where the upper side of a [REF:term:chmn]chimney on a sloping roof is more than 750 mm (metric) wide.

[REF:term:chmn]Chimney saddles shall be covered with
sheet metal or roofing material of weight and quality equivalent to
the roofing.
Saddles shall be flashed where they intersect the roof.
The intersection of the saddle and the [REF:term:chmn]chimney shall be flashed and counterflashed as described in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect26.subsect4.art4:long]

A [REF:term:chmn]chimney saddle need not be installed
if the intersection between the [REF:term:chmn]chimney and
roof is protected by sheet metal flashing that extends up the [REF:term:chmn]chimney to a height equal to at least one sixth
the width of the [REF:term:chmn]chimney, but not less than 150 mm (metric), and up the roof slope to a point equal in height to
the flashing on the [REF:term:chmn]chimney, but not less
than 1.5 times the shingle exposure.

Flashing described in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect26.subsect4.art8.sent5:short] at the [REF:term:chmn]chimney shall be counterflashed
as required by [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect26.subsect4.art4:long]

subsections.title: Eave Protection for Shingles and Shakes

content.text:
Except as provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect26.subsect5.art1.sent2:short], eave protection shall be provided on shingle, shake or tile roofs,
extending from the edge of the roof a minimum of 900 mm (metric) up the roof slope to a line not less than 300 mm (metric) inside
the inner face of the exterior wall.
Eave protection is not required

clauses.text: over unheated garages, carports and porches,

where the roof overhang exceeds 900 mm (metric) measured
along the roof slope from the edge of the roof to the inner face of
the exterior wall,
on roofs of asphalt shingles installed in accordance with [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect26.subsect8:long],
on roofs with slopes of 1 in 1.5 or greater, or
in regions with 3 500 or fewer degree-days.

content.text:
Eave protection shall be laid beneath the starter strip and
shall consist of

clauses.text: No. 15 asphalt-saturated felt laid in two plies lapped 480 mm (metric) and cemented together with lap cement,
Type M or S roll roofing laid with not less than 100 mm (metric) head and end laps cemented together with lap cement,
glass fibre or polyester fibre coated base sheets, or

self-sealing composite membranes consisting of modified bituminous
coated material.

content.text: Except as required in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect26.subsect6.art1.sent2:short], when underlay is used beneath shingles, it shall be

clauses.text:
asphalt-saturated sheathing paper weighing not less than 0.195 kg/m2
                               (metric), or
No. 15 plain or perforated asphalt-saturated felt.

content.text: Underlay used beneath wood shingles shall be breather type.

When used with shingles, underlay shall be installed parallel
to the eaves with head and end lap of not less than 50 mm (metric).

The top edge of each strip of underlay referred to in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect26.subsect6.art2.sent1:short] shall be fastened with sufficient
roofing nails to hold it in place until the shingles are applied.

The underlay referred to in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect26.subsect6.art2.sent1:short] shall overlap the eave protection by not less than 100 mm (metric). (See [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect26.subsect10.art2:long] for underlay beneath wood shakes.)

subsections.title: Asphalt Shingles on Slopes of 1 in 3 or Greater

content.text:
Coverage shall be not less than 2 thicknesses of shingle over
the entire roof, disregarding cutouts.

A starter strip shall be installed along the lower edge of the
roof so that it extends approximately 12 mm (metric) beyond the
eaves and rake of the roof and fastened along the bottom edge with
nails spaced not more than 300 mm (metric) o.c.
Starter strips shall be

clauses.text: at least Type M mineral-surfaced roll roofing not less than 300 mm (metric) wide,

shingles of the same weight and quality as those used as a roof
covering with tabs facing up the roof slope, or

pre-manufactured starter strips installed with sealant at the
eaves.

content.text:
Starter strips need not be provided where eave protection of
not less than Type M mineral-surfaced roll roofing is provided.
Shingles shall have a head lap of not less than 50 mm (metric).

Except as provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect26.subsect7.art4.sent2:short], shingles shall be fastened with at least 4 nails or staples for 1 m (metric) wide shingles so that no nails or staples are exposed.

Where staples with an 11 mm (metric) crown are used, shingles
shall be fastened with at least 6 staples.

Fasteners may be reduced for narrower shingles in proportion
to the width of the shingle or when shingles incorporating interlocking
devices are used.

Fasteners referred to in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect26.subsect7.art4.sent1:short]
                           [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect26.subsect7.art4.sent2:short] shall be located 25 mm (metric) to 40 mm (metric) from each end of each strip shingle with other fasteners equally
spaced between them.

Fasteners referred to in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect26.subsect7.art4.sent1:short]
                           [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect26.subsect7.art4.sent2:short] shall be located not less than  12 mm (metric) above
the tops of the cutouts.

Shingle tabs shall be secured by a spot of plastic cement not
exceeding 25 mm (metric) diam under the centre of each tab or
by interlocking devices or self-sealing strips.

Shingles on hips and ridges shall be applied so they extend
not less than 100 mm (metric) on either side of the hip or ridge,
and shall be lapped not less than 150 mm (metric).

Shingles referred to in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect26.subsect7.art6.sent1:short] shall be fastened with nails or staples on each side located not
more than 25 mm (metric) from the edge and 25 mm (metric) above
the butt of the overlying shingle.
Eave protection shall conform to [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect26.subsect5:long]
Flashing shall conform to [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect26.subsect4:long]

subsections.title: Asphalt Shingles on Slopes of less than 1 in 3

content.text:
Except for the first 2 courses, coverage shall be not less than
3 thicknesses of shingle over the entire roof, disregarding cutouts.
A starter strip shall be installed as in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect26.subsect7.art2:long]
Starter strips required in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect26.subsect8.art2.sent1:short] shall be laid in a continuous band of cement not less than 200 mm (metric) wide.

Shingle tabs shall be secured with cold application cement applied
at the rate of not less than 0.5 L/m2
                            (metric) of
cemented area, or hot application asphalt applied at the rate of 1 kg/m2
                            (metric) of cemented area.

The first course of shingles shall be secured by a continuous
band of cement along the eaves applied so that the width of the band
equals the shingle exposure plus 100 mm (metric).

The succeeding courses of shingles shall be secured by a continuous
band of cement applied so that the width of the band equals the shingle
exposure plus 50 mm (metric).

The band required in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect26.subsect8.art4.sent2:short] shall be located not more than 50 mm (metric) above the butt
of the overlying course of shingles.
Shingles on hips and ridges shall be not less than 300 mm (metric) wide applied to provide triple coverage.

Shingles referred to in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect26.subsect8.art5.sent1:short] shall be cemented to the roof shingles and to each other with a
coat of cement and fastened with nails or staples located 40
mm (metric) above the butt of the overlying shingle and 50 mm (metric) from each edge.
Flashing shall conform to [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect26.subsect4:long]
Shingles shall be fastened in accordance with [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect26.subsect7.art4:long]

Except as provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect16.art1.sent1:long], decking for
wood shingled roofs may be continuous or spaced.
Western cedar shingles shall be not less than No. 2 grade.

Eastern white cedar shingles shall be not less than B (clear)
grade.

Wood shingles shall be not less than 400 mm (metric) long
and not less than 75 mm (metric) or more than 350 mm (metric) wide.

Shingles shall be spaced approximately 6 mm (metric) apart
and offset at the joints in adjacent courses not less than 40 mm (metric) so that joints in alternate courses are staggered.
Shingles shall be fastened with 2 nails or staples located approximately 20 mm (metric) from the sides of the shingle and 40 mm (metric) above the exposure line.
The exposure of wood roof shingles shall conform to [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect26.subsect9.art6.table1:long]

content.text: Flashing shall conform to [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect26.subsect4:long]
Eave protection shall conform to [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect26.subsect5:long]

Shakes shall be not less than 450 mm (metric) long and not
less than 100 mm (metric) nor more than 350 mm (metric) wide
with a butt thickness of not more than 32 mm (metric) and not
less than 9 mm (metric).

Where eave protection is not provided, an underlay conforming
to the requirements in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect26.subsect6.art1:long] for wood shingles
shall be laid as a strip not less than 900 mm (metric) wide along
the eaves.

A strip of material similar to that described in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect26.subsect10.art2.sent1:short] not less than 450 mm (metric) wide
shall be interlaid between each course of shakes with the bottom edge
of the strip positioned above the butt line at a distance equal to
double the exposure of the shakes.

Interlaid strips referred to in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect26.subsect10.art2.sent2:short] shall be lapped not less than 150 mm (metric) at
hips and ridges in a manner that will prevent water from reaching
the roof sheathing.

Shakes shall be spaced 6 mm (metric) to 9 mm (metric) apart and the joints in any one course shall be separated not less
than 40 mm (metric) from joints in adjacent courses.

Shakes shall be fastened with nails located approximately 20 mm (metric) from the sides of the shakes and 40 mm (metric) above
the exposure line.
The exposure of wood shakes shall not exceed

clauses.text: 190 mm (metric) for shakes not less than 450 mm (metric) long, and
250 mm (metric) for shakes not less than 600 mm (metric) long.

content.text: Flashing shall conform to [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect26.subsect4:long]
Eave protection shall conform to [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect26.subsect5:long]
Shakes shall be not less than No. 1 or Handsplit grade.

The quantities of bituminous materials used on built-up roofs
shall conform to [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect26.subsect11.art1.table1:long]

content.title: Quantities of Bitumen for Built-up Roofs

header_rows.content: Amount of Bitumen per Square Metre of Roof Surface

content.text:
Coal-tar products and asphalt products shall not be used together
in built-up roof construction.
Bitumen roofing felts shall be at least No. 15 felt.

Aggregate used for surfacing built-up roofs shall be clean,
dry and durable and shall consist of particles of gravel, crushed
stone or air-cooled blast [REF:term:frnc]furnace slag having
a size of from 6 mm (metric) to 15 mm (metric).

The minimum amount of aggregate surfacing per square metre of
roof surface shall be 15 kg (metric) gravel or crushed stone or 10 kg (metric) crushed slag.
Flashing for built-up roofs shall conform to [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect26.subsect4:long]

Built-up roofing shall consist of not less than 3 mopped-down
layers of roofing felt flood coated with bitumen.

In hot process applications each layer of bitumen-saturated
felt shall be laid while the bitumen is hot, with each layer overlapping
the previous one.

The full width under each lap referred to in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect26.subsect11.art7.sent1:short] shall be coated with bitumen so that
in no place does felt touch felt.

Felt shall be laid free of wrinkles and shall be rolled directly
into the hot bitumen and broomed forward and outward from the centre
to ensure complete adhesion.

Except as permitted in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect26.subsect11.art8.sent2:short], built-up roofing applied over wood, plywood, OSB or waferboard
roof sheathing shall be laid over an additional base layer of felt laid dry over the entire roof deck
with not less than a 50 mm (metric) headlap and a 50 mm (metric) sidelap between each sheet.

Where plywood, OSB or waferboard roof sheathing is used, the
dry layer of felt required in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect26.subsect11.art8.sent1:short] may be omitted when the joints are taped and the sheathing is primed
with asphalt.

Roofing shall be securely attached to the decking or where insulation
is applied above the deck, the insulation shall be securely attached
to the deck before the first layer of felt is fastened to the insulation.
Except as permitted in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect26.subsect11.art10.sent4:short], a cant strip shall be provided at the edges of roofs.

At least 2 plies of the roofing membrane shall be carried over
the top of the cant strip.

Flashing shall extend over the top of the cant strip and be
shaped to form a drip.
The cant strip required in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect26.subsect11.art10.sent1:short] need not be provided where a gravel stop is installed at the edge of roofs.

The roofing membranes shall be carried over the edge of the
roof before the gravel stop referred to in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect26.subsect11.art10.sent4:short] is fastened and 2 plies of roofing membrane mopped
to the top surface of the gravel stop before the flood coat is applied.

The gravel stop referred to in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect26.subsect11.art10.sent4:short] shall extend over the edge of the roof to form a drip
or shall be flashed so that the flashing extends over the edge to
form a drip.

Wide selvage asphalt roofing shall provide double coverage over
the entire roof surface.

Plies of selvage roofing shall be cemented together to ensure
a watertight joint.
Sheet metal roofing shall be not less than

clauses.text: 0.33 mm (metric) thick galvanized steel,
0.46 mm (metric) thick copper,
0.46 mm (metric) thick zinc, or
0.48 mm (metric) thick aluminum.

content.text:
Except as provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect16.art1.sent1:long], where sheet
metal roofing is not supported by roof decking but spans between spaced
supports, the panels shall be designed to support the specified [REF:term:lv-ld]live loads for roofs.

Except as provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect16.art1.sent1:long], where glass-reinforced
polyester roofing panels are not supported by roof decking but span
between spaced supports, the panels shall be designed to support the
specified live roof loads.

Hot applied rubberized asphalt roofing shall be installed in
accordance with [REF:standard:cgsb-37.51]

Polyvinyl chloride sheet applied roofing membrane shall be installed
in accordance with [REF:standard:cgsb37-gp-55m]

Except as provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect16.art1.sent1:long], concrete
roof tiles shall be installed according to [REF:standard:csaa220s] (See [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.appnote159:short].)
When roof drains are provided they shall conform to Part 7.

Where downspouts are provided and are not connected to a sewer,
extensions shall be provided to carry rainwater away from the [REF:term:bldng]building in a manner which will prevent [REF:term:l]soil erosion.

Where lumber, wood shingles, shakes, fibre-cement shingles,
planks and sheets, plywood, OSB, waferboard, hardboard, vinyl, insulated vinyl, polypropylene, aluminum or steel, including trim and soffits, are installed as
cladding on wood-frame walls or above-ground flat insulating concrete form walls exposed to precipitation, the cladding assembly shall comply with

clauses.text:
[REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect27.subsect2:long]
                              [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect27.subsect13:long], or
Part 5.

content.text:
Where stucco is installed as cladding on wood-frame walls, above-ground flat insulating
concrete form walls or masonry walls exposed to precipitation,
the cladding assembly shall comply with

clauses.text:
[REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect27.subsect2:long]
                              [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect27.subsect5:long], and [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect28:long], or
Part 5.

content.text:
Where masonry serves as cladding on wood-frame walls, above-ground flat insulating
concrete form walls or masonry walls exposed to precipitation,
the cladding assembly shall comply with

clauses.text:
[REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect27.subsect2:long]
                              [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect27.subsect4:long], and [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect20:long], except for masonry
veneer, which shall be attached to above-ground flat insulating concrete
form walls in accordance with [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect27.subsect5.art4.sent2:long], or
Part 5.

content.text:
Where asphalt shingles are installed as cladding on wood-frame
walls exposed to precipitation, the cladding assembly shall comply
with

clauses.text:
[REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect26.subsect7:long]
                              [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect27.subsect2:long]

Part 5.

Where an exterior insulation finish system is installed as cladding
on wood-frame, masonry, cold-formed steel stud, above-ground flat insulating concrete form or cast-in-place concrete walls exposed to precipitation, the cladding
assembly shall comply with(See [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.appnote160:short].)
