content.text:
Nails or staples for the attachment of cladding and wood trim
shall be corrosion-resistant and shall be compatible with the cladding
material.

Fasteners for metal cladding shall be positioned to permit expansion
and contraction of the cladding.

Fasteners for vinyl siding, insulated vinyl siding and polypropylene
siding shall be installed in the centre of the slots of the nail hem.

Fasteners for shakes and shingles shall penetrate through the
nail-holding base or not less than 19 mm (metric) into the framing.

Fasteners for vinyl cladding, insulated vinyl cladding and polypropylene
cladding shall penetrate through the nail-holding base or not less
than 32 mm (metric) into the framing.

Fasteners for cladding other than that described in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect27.subsect5.art7.sent1:short]
                           [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect27.subsect5.art7.sent2:short] shall penetrate through the nail-holding
base or not less than 25 mm  (metric) into the framing.

Lumber siding shall be sound, free of knot holes, loose knots,
through checks or splits.

Drop, rustic, novelty, lapped board and vertical wood siding
shall be not less than 14.3 mm (metric) thick and not more than 286 mm (metric) wide.
Bevel siding shall be

clauses.text: not less than 5 mm (metric) thick at the top, and
not less than

subclauses.text: 12 mm (metric) thick at the butt for siding 184 mm (metric) or less in width, and
14.3 mm (metric) thick at the butt for siding wider than 184 mm (metric).

content.text: Bevel siding shall be not more than 286 mm (metric) wide.

Lumber siding shall prevent water from entering at the joints
by the use of lapped or matched joints or by vertical wood battens.
Siding shall overlap not less than 1 mm (metric) per 16 mm (metric) width of lumber, but not less than

clauses.text: 9.5 mm (metric) for matched siding,
25 mm (metric) for lapped bevel siding, or
12 mm (metric) for vertical battens.

content.text: Shingles and shakes shall conform to

clauses.text: [REF:standard:csao118.1] or
[REF:standard:csao118.2]

content.text:
Western cedar shakes shall be not less than No. 1 (metric) or Handsplit grade, and western cedar shingles not less than No. 2 (metric) grade, except that No. 3 (metric) grade may be used
for undercoursing.

Eastern white cedar shingles shall be at least B (clear) grade,
except that C grade may be used for the lower course of double course
applications.
Shingles and shakes shall be not less than 65 mm (metric) or more than 350 mm (metric) wide.

Shingles or shakes shall be fastened with nails or staples located
approximately 20 mm (metric) from each edge and not less than 25 mm (metric) above the exposure line for single-course applications,
or approximately 50 mm (metric) above the butt for double-course
applications.

In single-course application, joints in succeeding courses shall
be offset not less than 40 mm (metric) so that joints in any 2
of 3 consecutive courses are staggered.

In double-course application, joints in the outer course shall
be offset from joints in the under-course by not less than 40 mm (metric), and joints in succeeding courses shall be offset not less than 40 mm (metric).

When lath is used with double-course application [see [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect27.subsect5.art1.sent4:long]], it shall be spaced according to the exposure
and securely fastened to the framing.

The butts of the under-course of the application referred to
in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect27.subsect7.art5.sent1:short] shall rest on the top
edge of the lath.

The outer course of the application referred to in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect27.subsect7.art5.sent1:short] shall be fastened to the lath with
nails of sufficient length to penetrate through the lath.

The butts of the shingles or shakes shall be so located that
they project not less than 12 mm (metric) below the bottom edge
of the lath referred to in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect27.subsect7.art5.sent1:short].

If wood lath is not used, the butts of the under-course shingles
or shakes of the application referred to in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect27.subsect7.art5.sent1:short] shall be located 12 mm (metric) above the butts
of the outer course.

The exposure and butt thickness of shingles and shakes shall
conform to [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect27.subsect7.art6.table1:long]

content.title: Exposure and Thickness of Wood Shingles and Shakes

content.text: Plywood cladding shall be exterior type conforming to

clauses.text: [REF:standard:hpvahp1]
[REF:standard:csao121]
[REF:standard:csao151] or
[REF:standard:csao153]

content.text:
Plywood cladding shall be not less than 6 mm (metric) thick
when applied directly to sheathing.

When applied directly to framing or over furring strips, plywood
cladding thickness shall conform to [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect27.subsect8.art2.table1:long]

content.title: Minimum Plywood Cladding Thickness

header_rows.content: Face Grain Right Angles to Supports

content.text:
The thickness of grooved or textured plywood cladding shall
be measured at the point of least thickness.

The edges of plywood cladding shall be treated with a suitable
paint or sealer.
Plywood applied in panels shall have all edges supported.

Not less than a 2 mm (metric) gap shall be provided between
panels referred to in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect27.subsect8.art4.sent1:short].

Vertical joints in cladding referred to in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect27.subsect8.art4.sent1:short] shall be protected with batten strips
or sealant when the plywood joints are not matched.
Horizontal joints in cladding referred to in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect27.subsect8.art4.sent1:short] shall be lapped not less than 25 mm (metric) or shall be suitably flashed.

Plywood applied in horizontal lapped strips shall have not less
than a 2 mm (metric) gap provided at the butted ends, which shall
be caulked.
The horizontal joints of siding described in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect27.subsect8.art5.sent1:short] shall be lapped not less than 25 mm (metric).

Wedges shall be inserted under all vertical butt joints and
at all corners when horizontal lapped plywood is applied without sheathing.

Hardboard cladding
shall conform to [REF:standard:ansia135.6]
Hardboard cladding shall be not less than

clauses.text:
9.5 mm (metric) thick when applied over sheathing that provides continuous support
or over furring or framing members not more than 400 mm o.c. (metric), or
11.1 mm (metric) thick when applied over furring or framing members not more than 600 mm o.c. (metric)

content.text:
Where hardboard cladding is grooved, the grooves shall not extend
more than 1.5 mm (metric) into the minimum required thickness. (See [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.appnote175:short].)

Hardboard cladding applied in panels shall have all edges supported
with not less than a 5 mm (metric) gap provided between sheets.

Vertical joints in cladding described in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect27.subsect9.art3.sent1:short] shall be protected with batten strips or sealant when
the joints are not matched.
Horizontal joints in cladding described in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect27.subsect9.art3.sent1:short] shall be lapped not less than 25 mm (metric) or shall be suitably flashed.

Hardboard applied in horizontal lapped strips shall have not
less than a 5 mm (metric) gap provided at the butted ends, which
shall be sealed or otherwise protected with suitable mouldings.

The horizontal joints of siding described in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect27.subsect9.art4.sent1:short] shall overlap not less than 1 mm (metric) per 16 mm (metric) width of siding board but not
less than 9.5 mm (metric) for matched joint siding or 25
mm (metric) for lapped siding.

Not less than 3 mm (metric) clearance shall be provided
between hardboard cladding and door or window frames.
OSB and waferboard cladding shall conform to [REF:standard:csao437.0]

OSB conforming to O-2 grade shall be not less than 6.0 mm thick
where applied directly to sheathing.

OSB conforming to O-2 grade applied directly to framing or over
furring strips shall conform to the thickness shown for plywood in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect27.subsect8.art2.table1:long] (See [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.appnote176:short].)

OSB conforming to O-1 grade and waferboard conforming to R-1
grade shall be not less than 7.9 mm (metric) thick where applied
directly to sheathing.

Where applied directly to framing or over furring strips, OSB
conforming to O-1 grade and waferboard conforming to R-1 grade shall
be not less than

clauses.text: 9.5 mm (metric) thick on supports spaced not more than 400 mm (metric) o.c., and
12.7 mm (metric) thick on supports spaced not more than 600 mm (metric) o.c.

content.text:
OSB and waferboard applied in panels shall have all edges supported
and treated with a primer or sealer.

Not less than a 3 mm (metric) gap shall be provided between
sheets in cladding described in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect27.subsect10.art3.sent1:short].

Vertical joints in cladding described in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect27.subsect10.art3.sent1:short] shall be protected with batten strips or sealant when
the OSB and waferboard joints are not matched.
Horizontal joints in cladding described in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect27.subsect10.art3.sent1:short] shall be lapped not less than 25 mm (metric) or shall be suitably flashed.

Not less than a 3 mm (metric) clearance shall be provided
between OSB and waferboard cladding and door or window frames.

Steel sheet cladding, including horizontal and vertical strip steel siding, flashing
and trim accessories, shall

clauses.text: have a minimum thickness of 0.33 mm (metric), and
conform to [REF:standard:cssbi23m]

content.text:
Horizontal and vertical strip aluminum siding, including flashing
and trim accessories, shall conform to [REF:standard:cgsb-93.2] (See [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.appnote178:short].)

Aluminum sheet cladding shall conform to [REF:standard:cgsb-93.1] and shall have a thickness
of not less than 0.58 mm (metric), except that siding supported
by backing or sheathing shall have a thickness of not less than 0.46 mm (metric). (See [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.appnote178:short].)

subsections.title:
Vinyl Siding,
Insulated Vinyl Siding and Vinyl Soffits

content.text:
Vinyl siding  shall
conform to [REF:standard:astmd3679]
Insulated vinyl siding shall conform to [REF:standard:astmd7793]
Rigid vinyl soffits shall conform to [REF:standard:astmd4477]

Where vinyl siding, insulated vinyl siding or rigid vinyl soffits
are required to have a [REF:term:flm-prd-]flame-spread rating, the rating shall be determined in accordance with [REF:standard:ulcs102.2]

The attachment of vinyl siding and insulated vinyl siding shall conform
to the requirements in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect27.subsect5:long]
Polypropylene siding shall conform to [REF:standard:astmd7254]

Where polypropylene siding is required to have a [REF:term:flm-prd-]flame-spread rating, the rating shall be determined
in accordance with [REF:standard:ulcs102.2]

The attachment of polypropylene siding shall conform to the
requirements in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect27.subsect5:long]

Except as provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect27.subsect14.art1.sent2:short], this Subsection applies to exterior insulation finish systems
(EIFS) that

clauses.text: are covered in the scope of [REF:standard:ulcs716.1] and

have a geometrically defined drainage cavity with a minimum
cavity depth of 9.5 mm (metric) and an open area equal to not less
than 13% of the area of a full-size EIFS panel.

content.text: EIFS that are not covered by [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect27.subsect14.art1.sent1:short] shall comply with Part 5.
The materials used in EIFS shall conform to [REF:standard:ulcs716.1]
The substrate on which the EIFS is installed shall

clauses.text: be compatible with that particular system (see [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.appnote180:short]), and

comply with the structural requirements for sheathing materials
stated in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23:long]

content.text:
The design and installation of EIFS on the substrate described
in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect27.subsect14.art2.sent2:long] shall comply with

clauses.text: [REF:standard:ulcs716.2] and
[REF:standard:ulcs716.3]

content.text:
Sheathing shall be provided beneath stucco applied over wood-frame
walls except as permitted in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect28.subsect4.art2:long]
Where applied beneath stucco, sheathing shall conform to [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect17:long]

Stucco lath or reinforcing shall be used to attach stucco to
any substrate other than masonry.

Stucco lath or reinforcing shall be used to attach stucco to
masonry where

clauses.text:
the masonry is soft-burned tile or brick of less strength than
the stucco, or

the masonry surface is not sound, clean and sufficiently rough
to provide a good key.

content.text: Stucco applied over masonry [REF:term:chmn]chimneys shall be reinforced.

Stucco finish shall not be applied over concrete masonry units
less than one month old unless the units have been cured by the autoclave
process.

Stucco shall be not less than 200 mm (metric) above finished
ground level except when it is applied over concrete or masonry.

Flashing and caulking used with stucco shall conform to [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect27.subsect3:long] and [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect27.subsect4:number], except that if aluminum flashing
is used, it shall be separated from the stucco by an impervious membrane
or coating. (See [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect7.subsect6.art2:long] for caulking around window
frames.)
Portland cement shall conform to [REF:standard:csaa3001]

Aggregate shall be clean, well-graded natural sand or sand manufactured
from crushed stone, gravel or air-cooled blast furnace slag and shall
contain no significant amounts of deleterious material.
Aggregate grading shall conform to [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect28.subsect2.art2.table1:long]

content.title: Aggregate Grading for Stucco

content.text:
Water shall be clean and free of significant amounts of deleterious
material.

Fasteners for stucco lath or reinforcing shall be corrosion-resistant
and of a material other than aluminum.
Nails for stucco lath or reinforcing shall be not less than 3.2 mm (metric) diam with a head diameter of not less than 11.1 mm (metric).
Staples for stucco lath or reinforcing shall be not less than 1.98 mm (metric) diam or thickness.

Staples and nails for attaching stucco lath or reinforcing to
vertical surfaces shall be of sufficient length to penetrate 25 mm (metric) into framing members or to the full depth of the sheathing
where the sheathing is used for attachment.

On horizontal surfaces nails for stucco lath or reinforcing
shall be not less than 38 mm (metric) long.
Rib lath or expanded metal stucco mesh shall be

clauses.text:
copper-alloy steel coated with rust-inhibitive paint after fabrication,
or
galvanized.

content.text: Woven or welded wire mesh shall be galvanized.

Sheathing need not be provided beneath stucco where not less
than 1.19 mm (metric) diam galvanized wire is applied horizontally
to the framing at vertical intervals of not more than 150 mm (metric), or where paper-backed welded wire metal lath is used.
Stucco lath shall conform to [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect28.subsect4.art3.table1:long]

content.title: Stucco Lath

content.text:
Stucco lath shall be held not less than 6 mm (metric) away
from the backing by means of suitable self-furring devices.
Stucco lath shall be applied with the long dimension horizontal.

Horizontal and vertical joints in stucco lath shall be lapped
not less than 50 mm (metric).

End joints of stucco lath shall be staggered and shall occur
over framing members.

External corners of stucco lath shall be reinforced with a vertical
strip of lath or reinforcing extending not less than 150 mm (metric) on both sides of the corner, or the lath or reinforcing shall extend
around corners not less than 150 mm (metric).
Stucco lath shall be fastened in conformance with [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect27.subsect5:long]
Fasteners on vertical surfaces shall be spaced not more than

clauses.text:
150 mm (metric) o.c. vertically and 400 mm (metric) o.c.
horizontally, or

100 mm (metric) o.c. vertically and 600 mm (metric) o.c.
horizontally.

content.text:
Nailing patterns other than those required in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect28.subsect4.art6.sent2:short] are permitted to be used provided
there are at least 20 fasteners per square metre of wall surface.
Fasteners on horizontal surfaces shall be spaced not more than

clauses.text:
150 mm (metric) o.c. along the framing members when members
are spaced not more than 400 mm (metric) o.c., and

100 mm (metric) o.c. along members when members are spaced
not more than 600 mm (metric) o.c.

content.text: Stucco mixes shall conform to [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect28.subsect5.art1.table1:long]

content.title: Stucco Mixes

body_rows.content: 3.25 to 4 parts per part of cementitious material

content.text:
Pigment if used shall consist of pure mineral oxides inert to
the action of sun, lime and cement.
Pigment shall not exceed 6% of the Portland cement by weight.

Materials shall be thoroughly mixed before and after water is
added.

Stucco shall be applied not later than 3 h (metric) after
the initial mixing.
The base for stucco shall be maintained above freezing.
Stucco shall be maintained at a temperature of not less than 10°C (metric) during application, and for not less than 48 h (metric) afterwards.

articles.title: Number of Coats and Total Thickness

content.text:
Stucco shall be applied with at least 2 base coats and one finish
coat, providing a total thickness of not less than 15 mm (metric), measured from the face of the lath or the face of the masonry where
no lath is used.

The first coat shall be not less than 6 mm (metric) thick,
measured from the face of the lath or masonry, fully embedding the
lath.

The surface of the first coat shall be scored to provide a key
with the second coat.
The second coat shall be not less than 6 mm (metric) thick.

The surface of the second coat shall be lightly roughened to
provide a key with the finish coat if the finish coat is other than
stone dash.

When the finish coat is other than stone dash, the base shall
be dampened but not saturated before the finish coat is applied.
The thickness of the finish coat shall be not less than 3 mm (metric).

When a stone dash finish is used, the stone shall be partially
embedded in the second coat before the second coat starts to set or
stiffen.

A wall or ceiling finish shall also conform to the appropriate
requirements in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect10:long] and [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect11:number], in addition to the requirements
in this Section.

Waterproof finish shall be provided to a height of not less
than

clauses.text: 1.8 m (metric) above the floor in shower stalls,

1.2 m (metric) above the rims of bathtubs equipped with
showers, and

400 mm (metric) above the rims of bathtubs not equipped
with showers.

content.text:
Waterproof finish shall consist of ceramic, plastic or metal
tile, sheet vinyl, tempered hardboard, laminated thermosetting decorative
sheets or linoleum.

Wood furring for the attachment of wall and ceiling finishes
shall conform to [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect29.subsect3.art1.table1:long]

content.title: Size and Spacing of Furring

content.text:
Furring shall be fastened to the framing or to wood blocks with
not less than 51 mm (metric) nails.

Application of plaster wall and ceiling finishes, including
installation of metal or gypsum lath, shall conform to [REF:standard:csaa82.30]

The requirements for application of gypsum board in this Subsection
apply to the single layer application of gypsum board to wood furring
or framing using nails or screws.

Except as provided
in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect29.subsect5.art1.sent3:short], gypsum board
applications not described in this Subsection shall conform to [REF:standard:csaa82.31]

The application of gypsum board to flat insulating concrete
form (ICF) walls shall conform to [REF:standard:astmc840] (See [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.appnote182:short].)
Gypsum products shall conform to

clauses.text: [REF:standard:astmc1178m] or

[REF:standard:astmc1396m] except that the [REF:term:flm-prd-]flame-spread rating of gypsum board  shall
be determined in accordance with [REF:standard:ulcs102]

content.text:
Maximum spacing of supports for gypsum board applied as a single
layer shall conform to [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect29.subsect5.art3.table1:long]

content.title: Spacing of Supports for Gypsum Board

header_rows.content:
Maximum
Spacing of Supports, mm o.c.

body_rows.content:
Gypsum board conforming to [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect29.subsect5.art2.sent1:long] (except[REF:external:astmc1396m] Sections 9
and 12 of 
                                    [REF:standard:astmc1396m])

Gypsum ceiling board conforming
to [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect29.subsect5.art2.sent1.clause2:long] (only[REF:external:astmc1396m] Section 12 of 
                                    [REF:standard:astmc1396m])

content.text: Gypsum board supporting insulation shall be not less than 12.7 mm (metric) thick.

The length of fasteners for gypsum board shall conform to [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect29.subsect5.art5.table1:long], except that lesser depths of penetration are permitted
for assemblies required to have a [REF:term:fr-rtnc-]fire-resistance
rating provided it can be shown, on the basis of fire tests,
that such depths are adequate for the required rating.

content.title: Fastener Penetration into Wood Supports

content.text:
Nails for fastening gypsum board to wood supports shall conform
to

clauses.text: [REF:standard:astmf1667] or
[REF:standard:csab111]

content.text:
Screws for fastening gypsum board to wood supports shall conform
to [REF:standard:astmc1002]
For single-layer application on a ceiling, nails shall be spaced

clauses.text:
not more than 180 mm (metric) o.c. on ceiling supports,
or

every 300 mm (metric) o.c. along ceiling supports, in pairs
about 50 mm (metric) apart.

content.text:
Where the ceiling sheets are supported by the wall sheets around
the perimeter of the ceiling, this support may be considered as equivalent
to nailing at this location.
Except as required by [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect29.subsect5.art8.sent4:short], for single-layer application on walls, nails shall be spaced

clauses.text:
not more than 200 mm o.c. (metric) on vertical wall supports,
or

every 300 mm o.c. (metric) along vertical wall supports,
in pairs about 50 mm (metric) apart.

content.text:
For single-layer application on walls, where gypsum board provides
required bracing in [REF:term:br-wl-pnl]braced wall panels, lateral support for studs, or fire protection, nails shall be spaced
not more than 200 mm o.c. (metric) on

clauses.text: vertical wall supports, and
top and bottom plates.

content.text:
The uppermost nails on vertical wall supports shall be not more
than 200 mm (metric) below the ceiling.

Nails shall be located not less than 10 mm (metric) from
the side or edge of the board.

Nails shall be driven so that the heads do not puncture the
paper.

For single-layer application on a ceiling, screws shall be spaced
not more than 300 mm (metric) o.c. on ceiling supports.

Where the ceiling sheets are supported by the wall sheets around
the perimeter of the ceiling, this support may be considered as equivalent
to screwing at this location.
Except as required by [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect29.subsect5.art9.sent4:short], for single-layer application on walls, screws shall be spaced

clauses.text:
not more than 300 mm o.c. (metric) on vertical wall supports
where the supports are more than 400 mm o.c. (metric), or

not more than 400 mm o.c. (metric) on vertical wall supports
where the supports are not more than 400 mm o.c. (metric)

content.text:
Except as provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect29.subsect5.art9.sent5:short], for single-layer application on walls, where gypsum board provides
required bracing in [REF:term:br-wl-pnl]braced wall panels, lateral support for studs, or fire protection, screws shall be
spaced not more than 300 mm (metric) o.c. on

clauses.text: vertical wall supports, and
top and bottom plates.

content.text:
Where a [REF:term:fr-rtnc-]fire-resistance rating is determined based on [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.spectables1.table1:long], [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect29.subsect5.art9.sent4:short] need not apply for the purpose of
fire protection.

Screws shall be located not less than 10 mm (metric) from
the edge of the board.

Screws shall be driven so that the heads do not puncture the
paper.

In cold weather, heat shall be provided to maintain a temperature
not below 10°C (metric) for 48 h (metric) prior to taping
and finishing and maintained for not less than 48 h (metric) thereafter.

Except as provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect29.subsect6.art1.sent2:short]
                           [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect29.subsect6.art1.sent3:short], the minimum thickness of plywood interior finish shall conform to [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect29.subsect6.art1.table1:long]

content.title: Thickness of Plywood Interior Finish

header_rows.content: Maximum Spacing of Supports, mm o.c.
On Supports with no Horizontal Blocking
On Supports with Blocking at Vertical Intervals not Exceeding 1.2 m (metric)

content.text: A manufacturing tolerance of −0.4 mm (metric) may be applied to the thicknesses listed in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect29.subsect6.art1.table1:long]
No minimum thickness is required where plywood is applied over continuous backing.

Except as permitted in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect29.subsect6.art2.sent2:short], where plywood for interior finish is grooved, the grooves shall
not extend through the face ply and into the plies below the face
ply unless the groove is supported by framing or furring.

If the grain of the face ply is at right angles to the supporting
members, the groove is permitted to extend into plies below the face
ply provided the thickness of the plywood exceeds the value shown
in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect29.subsect6.art1.table1:long] by an amount equal to not less than
the depth of penetration of the grooves into the plies below the face
ply.

Except as provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect29.subsect6.art3.sent2:short], nails for attaching plywood finishes shall not be less than 38 mm (metric) casing or finishing nails spaced not more than 150 mm (metric) o.c. along edge supports and 300 mm (metric) o.c.
along intermediate supports, except that staples providing equivalent
lateral resistance may also be used.

Where plywood finish provides required bracing in [REF:term:br-wl-pnl]braced wall panels, the plywood shall be
fastened in accordance with the fastening requirements for sheathing
stated in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect3.art5.sent2:long].

All plywood edges shall be supported by furring, blocking or
framing.
Hardboard shall conform to [REF:standard:cgsb-11.3]
Hardboard shall be not less than

clauses.text: 3 mm (metric) thick where applied over continuous backing,

6 mm (metric) thick when applied over supports spaced not
more than 400 mm (metric) o.c., and

9 mm (metric) thick when applied over supports spaced not
more than 600 mm (metric) o.c.

content.text:
Nails for fastening hardboard shall be casing or finishing nails
not less than 38 mm (metric) long, spaced not more than 150 mm (metric) o.c. along edge supports and 300 mm (metric) o.c.
along intermediate supports.

All hardboard edges shall be supported by furring, blocking
or framing where the backing is not continuous.
Insulating fibreboard shall conform to [REF:standard:ulcs706]
Insulating fibreboard sheets shall be not less than 11.1 mm (metric) thick on supports not more than 400 mm (metric) o.c.
Insulating fibreboard tile shall be not less than 12.7 mm (metric) thick on supports spaced not more than 400 mm (metric) o.c.

Nails for fastening fibreboard sheets shall be not less than 2.6 mm (metric) shank diameter casing or finishing nails of sufficient
length to penetrate not less than 20 mm (metric) into the supports.

Nails shall be spaced not more than 100 mm (metric) o.c.
along edge supports and 200 mm (metric) o.c. along intermediate
supports.

All fibreboard edges shall be supported by blocking, furring
or framing.
Particleboard finish shall conform to [REF:standard:ansia208.1]
OSB or waferboard finish shall conform to

clauses.text: [REF:standard:csao325] or
[REF:standard:csao437.0]

content.text:
Except as provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect29.subsect9.art2.sent2:short]
                           [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect29.subsect9.art2.sent3:short], the minimum thickness of O-2 grade OSB used as an
interior finish shall conform to that shown for plywood in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect29.subsect6.art1.table1:long]

Thicknesses listed in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect29.subsect6.art1.table1:long] shall permit
a manufacturing tolerance of −0.4 mm (metric).

No minimum thickness is required where O-2 grade OSB is applied
over continuous backing.

OSB conforming to O-1 grade, waferboard conforming to R-1 grade
and particleboard shall be

clauses.text:
not less than 6.35 mm (metric) thick on supports not more
than 400 mm o.c. (metric),

not less than 9.5 mm (metric) thick on supports not more
than 600 mm o.c. (metric), and

not less than 6.35 mm (metric) thick on supports not more
than 600 mm o.c. (metric) in walls where blocking is provided
at midwall height.

content.text: OSB conforming to [REF:standard:csao325] shall meet the minimum panel mark of

clauses.text: W16, on supports not more than 400 mm (metric) o.c.,
W24, on supports not more than 600 mm (metric) o.c., and

W16, on supports not more than 600 mm (metric) o.c. where
blocking is provided at mid-wall height.

content.text:
Except as provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect29.subsect9.art3.sent2:short], nails for fastening particleboard, OSB or waferboard shall be
not less than 38 mm (metric) casing or finishing nails spaced
not more than 150 mm o.c. (metric) along edge supports and 300 mm (metric) o.c. along intermediate supports.

Where OSB or waferboard provides required bracing in [REF:term:br-wl-pnl]braced wall panels, the OSB or waferboard
shall be fastened in accordance with the fastening requirements for
sheathing stated in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect3.art5.sent2:long].

All particleboard, OSB or waferboard edges shall be supported
by furring, blocking or framing.

Ceramic tile shall be set in a mortar base or applied with an
adhesive.
Plastic tile shall be applied with an adhesive.

When ceramic tile is applied to a mortar base the cementitious
material shall consist of one part Portland cement to not more than
one-quarter part lime by volume.

The cementitious material described in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect29.subsect10.art2.sent1:short] shall be mixed with not less than 3 nor more than 5
parts of aggregate per part of cementitious material by volume.
Mortar shall be applied over metal lath or masonry.

Ceramic tile applied to a mortar base shall be thoroughly soaked
and pressed into place forcing the mortar into the joints while the
tile is wet.

Adhesives to attach ceramic and plastic tile shall be applied
to the finish coat or brown coat of plaster that has been steel-trowelled
to an even surface or to gypsum board or to masonry provided the masonry
has an even surface.

Ceramic and plastic tile installed on walls around bathtubs
or showers shall be applied over moisture-resistant backing.

The joints between wall tiles and a bathtub shall be suitably
caulked with material conforming to [REF:standard:cgsb-19.22]
Finished flooring shall be provided in all [REF:term:rdntl-cc]residential occupancies.

Where water permeable finished flooring in bathrooms, kitchens,
public entrance halls and laundry areas is supported by a subfloor
of a type that would be damaged by water, such flooring shall be installed
over a membrane with a water permeance not exceeding 18 ng/(Pa×s×m2) (metric) when tested in accordance with [REF:standard:astme96m] (See [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.appnote183:short].)

Wood sleepers supporting finished flooring over a concrete base
supported on the ground shall be not less than 19 mm (metric) by 38 mm (metric) and shall be treated with a wood preservative.

Finished flooring shall have a surface that is smooth, even
and free from roughness or open defects.

A panel-type underlay shall be provided under resilient flooring,
parquet flooring, ceramic tile, felted-synthetic-fibre floor coverings
or carpeting laid over lumber subflooring. (See [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect30.subsect3.art2.sent1:long].)

Panel-type underlay shall be provided under resilient flooring,
parquet flooring, felted-synthetic-fibre floor coverings or carpeting
on panel-type subflooring whose edges are unsupported. (See [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect15.art3:long])

Panel-type underlay shall be provided under ceramic tile applied
with adhesive.
Panel-type underlay shall be not less than 6 mm (metric) thick and shall conform to

clauses.text: [REF:standard:ansia208.1]
[REF:standard:cgsb-11.3]
[REF:standard:hpvahp1]
[REF:standard:csao121]
[REF:standard:csao151]
[REF:standard:csao153] or
[REF:standard:csao437.0]

content.text:
Panel-type underlay under ceramic tile applied with adhesive
shall be not less than

clauses.text: 6 mm (metric) thick where the supports are spaced up to 300 mm (metric) o.c., and

11 mm (metric) thick where the supports are spaced wider
than 300 mm (metric) o.c.

content.text:
Panel-type underlay shall be fastened to the subfloor with staples,
annular grooved flooring nails or spiral nails, spaced not more than 150 mm o.c. (metric) along the edges and 200 mm o.c. (metric) both
ways at other locations.
Nails for panel-type underlay shall be not less than 19 mm (metric) long for 6 mm (metric) thick underlay and 22 mm (metric) long for 7.9 mm (metric) thick underlay.
Staples for panel-type underlay shall

clauses.text:
have not less than a 1.2 mm (metric) shank diameter or thickness
with a 4.7 mm (metric) crown, and
be not less than

subclauses.text: 22 mm (metric) long for 6 mm (metric) underlay, and

28 mm (metric) long for 7.9 mm (metric) and 9.5
mm (metric) underlay.

content.text:
Where panel-type underlay is required to be installed over plywood,
OSB or waferboard, the joints in the underlay shall be offset not
less than 200 mm (metric) from the joints in the underlying subfloor.

Underlay beneath resilient or ceramic floors applied with an
adhesive shall have all holes or open defects on the surface patched
so that the defects will not be transmitted to the finished surface.
The thickness of wood strip flooring shall conform to [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect30.subsect3.art1.table1:long]

content.title: Thickness of Wood Strip Flooring

content.text:
Wood strip flooring shall not be laid parallel to lumber subflooring
unless a separate underlay is provided.

If wood strip flooring is applied without a subfloor, it shall
be laid at right angles to the joists so that the end joints are staggered
and occur over supports or are end matched.

If the flooring is end matched, it shall be laid so that no
2 adjoining strips break joints in the same space between supports
and each strip bears on no fewer than 2 supports.

When nails are used, wood strip flooring shall be toe nailed
or face nailed with not less than one nail per strip at the spacings
shown in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect30.subsect3.art3.table1:long], except that face nailed strips
more than 25 mm (metric) in width shall have at least 2 nails
per strip.

content.title: Nailing of Wood Strip Flooring

header_rows.content: Minimum Length of Flooring Nails, mm
Maximum Spacing of Flooring Nails, mm

content.text: Face nails shall be countersunk.

Staples are permitted to be used to fasten wood strip flooring
not more than 7.9 mm (metric) in thickness provided the staples
are not less than 29 mm (metric) long with a shank diameter of 1.19 mm (metric) and with 4.7 mm (metric) crowns.

Adhesive used to attach parquet block flooring shall be suitable
for bonding wood to the applicable subfloor material.

Resilient flooring used on concrete slabs supported on ground
shall consist of asphalt, rubber, unbacked vinyl or vinyl with an
inorganic type backing.

Flooring described in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect30.subsect5.art1.sent1:short] shall be attached to the base with a suitable waterproof and alkali-resistant
adhesive.

Ceramic tile shall be set in a mortar bed or applied to a sound
smooth base with a suitable adhesive.

Panel-type subfloor to which ceramic tile is to be applied with
adhesive shall have its edges supported according to [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect15.art3:long]
This Section applies to the plumbing facilities and [REF:term:plmbng-t] plumbing systems within [REF:term:dwllng-n]dwelling units.

In [REF:term:ccpnc]occupancies other than [REF:term:dwllng-n]dwelling units, plumbing facilities, grab
bars, floor drains, and floor and wall finishes around urinals shall
conform to [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect7.subsect2:long] (See also [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect8:long] regarding [REF:term:brrr-fr]accessible plumbing facilities.)
Medical gas piping systems shall conform to [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect7.subsect3:long]

Systems used for service water heating shall conform to the
energy efficiency requirements in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36:long]
The construction, extension, [REF:term:ltrtn]alteration, renewal or repair of [REF:term:plmbng-t]plumbing systems and sewage disposal systems shall conform to Part 7.

Metal pipes in contact with cinders or other corrosive material
shall be protected by a heavy coating of bitumen or other corrosion
protection.

When provided, grab bars shall be capable of resisting a load
of not less than 1.3 kN (metric) applied vertically or horizontally.

Every [REF:term:dwllng-n]dwelling unit shall be supplied
with potable water.

Where a piped water supply is available, piping for hot and
cold water shall be connected to every kitchen sink, lavatory, bathtub,
shower, slop sink and laundry area.
Piping for cold water shall be run to every water closet.

A kitchen sink, lavatory, bathtub or shower, and water closet
shall be provided for every [REF:term:dwllng-n]dwelling unit where a piped water supply is available.

Where a piped water supply is available a hot water supply shall
be provided in every [REF:term:dwllng-n]dwelling unit.

Where gravity drainage to a sewer, drainage ditch or dry well
is possible, a floor drain shall be installed in a [REF:term:bmnt]basement forming part of a [REF:term:dwllng-n]dwelling
unit.

A floor drain shall be provided in a garbage room, incinerator
room or [REF:term:blr]boiler room serving more than one [REF:term:dwllng-n]dwelling unit.
Wastes from every plumbing fixture shall be piped to the [REF:term:bldng]building sewer.

[REF:term:bldng]Building sewers shall discharge into
a public sewage system where such system is available.
Where a public sewage system is not available, the [REF:term:bldng]building sewer shall discharge into a [REF:term:prvt-wg-]private sewage disposal system.
Where hot water is required to be supplied in accordance with [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect31.subsect4.art2:long], equipment shall

clauses.text: provide an adequate supply of hot water, and
be installed in conformance with Part 7.

revisions.text:
[REF:term:rvc-wtr-]Service water heaters shall conform
to appropriate provincial or territorial requirements or, in the absence
of such requirements, to the [REF:standard:nrcc-npc].

[REF:term:rvc-wtr-]Service water heaters shall conform
to appropriate provincial or territorial requirements or, in the absence
of such requirements, to Book II (Plumbing Systems) of this Code.
revisions.change_summary: Struck out 'the NPC' and substituted 'Book II (Plumbing Systems) of this Code'

content.text: The installation of [REF:term:rvc-wtr-]service water heaters, including provisions for mounting, clearances and air supply, shall conform to

clauses.text: the Safety Standards Act and pursuant regulations,
[REF:standard:csab139] Series,
reserved,
[REF:standard:csab365], or
a combination thereof.

content.text:
Where the [REF:term:bldng]building is in a location
where the seismic design parameter, S_{max}, for Site Class C is greater than
0.37, [REF:term:rvc-wtr-] service water heaters shall be
secured to the structure to prevent overturning. (See [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.appnote184:short].)

Where storage tanks for [REF:term:rvc-wtr-]service water
heaters are of steel, they shall be coated with zinc, vitreous
enamel (glass lined), hydraulic cement or other corrosion-resistant
material.

Fuel-burning [REF:term:rvc-wtr-] service water heaters shall be connected to a [REF:term:chmn]chimney 
                           [REF:term:fl]flue conforming to [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect21:long]

Heating coils of [REF:term:rvc-wtr-]service water heaters shall not be installed in a [REF:term:fl]flue or in the
combustion chamber of a [REF:term:blr]boiler or [REF:term:frnc]furnace heating a [REF:term:bldng]building.

Except as required by [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect32.subsect4.art2:long], this Section applies to the ventilation of rooms and spaces in [REF:term:rdntl-cc]residential occupancies by natural ventilation and to self-contained mechanical ventilation systems serving only

clauses.text: one [REF:term:dwllng-n]dwelling unit, or
a house with a [REF:term:scndr-st]secondary suite including their common spaces.

content.text: Mechanical ventilation systems other than self-contained systems serving a single [REF:term:dwllng-n]dwelling unit or a house with a [REF:term:scndr-st]secondary suite including their common spaces shall conform to Part 6.
A [REF:term:trg-grg]storage garage for more than 5 motor (metric) vehicles shall be ventilated in accordance with Part 6.
Systems used for ventilation shall conform to the energy efficiency requirements in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36:long]
Every [REF:term:dwllng-n]dwelling unit shall incorporate

clauses.text: provisions for non-heating-season ventilation in accordance with [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect32.subsect2:long], and

except as required by [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect32.subsect1.art2.sent2:short]
                              [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect32.subsect1.art2.sent3:short], if supplied with electrical power, provisions for heating-season ventilation in accordance with [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect32.subsect3:long].

content.text: A self-contained heating-season ventilation system serving a single [REF:term:dwllng-n]dwelling unit or a house with a [REF:term:scndr-st]secondary suite including their common spaces shall comply with [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect32.subsect3:long] (See [REF:internal:en001526:short].)
In houses that contain a [REF:term:scndr-st]secondary suite including their common spaces, heating-season ventilation need not be provided for

clauses.text: [REF:term:xt]exits,
[REF:term:pblc-crr]public corridors, and
ancillary spaces that are not within a [REF:term:dwllng-n]dwelling unit, except as provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect32.subsect1.art2.sent4:short].

content.text: Where ancillary spaces described in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect32.subsect1.art2.sent3.clause3:medium] contain exhaust devices, these spaces shall be provided with make-up air in accordance with [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect32.subsect4.art1:long]

[REF:term:xht-dct]Exhaust ducts or vents connected
to laundry-drying equipment shall discharge directly to the outdoors.

[REF:term:xht-dct]Exhaust ducts connected to laundry-drying
equipment shall be

clauses.text: independent of other [REF:term:xht-dct]exhaust ducts,
accessible for cleaning, and
constructed of a smooth corrosion-resistant material.

content.text:
Where collective venting of multiple installations of laundry-drying
equipment is used, the ventilation system shall

clauses.text: be connected to a common [REF:term:xht-dct]exhaust duct that is vented by one central exhaust fan,

include an interlock to activate the central exhaust fan when
laundry-drying equipment is in use, and

where required by [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect32.subsect3.art8:long], be provided with
make-up air.

content.text: Rooms or spaces in [REF:term:dwllng-n]dwelling units shall be ventilated during the non-heating season by

clauses.text: natural ventilation in accordance with [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect32.subsect2.art2:long], or

content.text: Where a habitable room or space is not provided with natural ventilation as described in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect32.subsect2.art1.sent1.clause1:medium], mechanical ventilation shall be provided to exhaust inside air from, or to introduce outside air to, that room or space at the rate of

clauses.text: one-half air change per hour if the room or space is mechanically cooled during the non-heating season, or
one air change per hour if the room or space is not mechanically cooled during the non-heating season.

content.text:
The unobstructed openable ventilation area to the outdoors for
rooms and spaces in residential [REF:term:bldng]buildings ventilated by natural means shall conform to [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect32.subsect2.art2.table1:long]

content.title: Natural Ventilation Area

body_rows.content:
Dining rooms, living
rooms, bedrooms, kitchens, combined rooms, dens, recreation rooms
and all other finished rooms

0.28 m^{2} per room
or combination of rooms

Corridors, storage rooms and other
similar public rooms or spaces
Unfinished [REF:term:bmnt]basement space not used on a shared basis

content.text:
Where a vestibule opens directly off a living or dining room
within a [REF:term:dwllng-n]dwelling unit, ventilation
to the outdoors for such rooms may be through the vestibule.

Openings for natural ventilation other than windows shall provide
protection from the weather and insects.
Screening shall be of corrosion-resistant material.
Every [REF:term:dwllng-n]dwelling unit that is supplied with electrical power shall be provided by a mechanical ventilation system that conforms to

clauses.text: [REF:standard:csaf326], "Residential Mechanical Ventilation Systems,"
this Subsection, or

for ducted mechanical ventilation systems serving more than one [REF:term:dwllng-n]dwelling unit in a house with a [REF:term:scndr-st]secondary suite including their common spaces, the mechanical ventilation system shall comply with this Subsection or Part 6.

content.text: Aspects of mechanical ventilation systems not specifically described in this Subsection shall be designed, constructed and installed in accordance with good practice such as that described in the ASHRAE Handbooks and Standards, the [REF:standard:hraisar-g1] the HRAI Residential Mechanical Ventilation Manual, the Hydronics Institute Manuals and the SMACNA Manuals.
Exhaust fans and supply fans shall be installed in accordance with this Subsection and the manufacturer's instructions.
The mechanical components of a mechanical ventilation system shall be installed so as to be accessible for inspection, maintenance, repair, and cleaning.

In a house with a [REF:term:scndr-st]secondary suite including their common spaces, where a heating or ventilation system serves more than a single [REF:term:dwllng-n]dwelling unit, the system shall be designed and installed to prevent the circulation of smoke upon a signal from a duct-type [REF:term:mk-dtctr]smoke detector. (See Note A-9.32.3.2.(4).)

revisions.text: Except as provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect10.subsect9.art6.sent14:short], ducts penetrating [REF:term:fr-sprtn]fire separations shall be equipped with [REF:term:fr-dmpr]fire dampers in conformance with [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect1.subsect8.art10:long].

Where [REF:term:bldng]buildings are sprinklered in accordance with [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect32.subsect3.art1.sent1:short], the sprinkler system shall be designed, constructed, installed and tested in accordance with [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect2.subsect5.art12.sent1:long], except that the maximum distance between sprinklers shall be in accordance with [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect10.subsect9.art9.sent6:short].
revisions.change_summary: Struck out 'Sentence 9.10.9.6.(14)' and substituted 'Sentence 9.10.9.9.(6)'

content.text: A mechanical ventilation system shall include:

clauses.text: a principal ventilation fan system that

subclauses.text: provides supply air in accordance with [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect32.subsect3.art4:long], and
includes an exhaust fan that conforms with [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect32.subsect3.art5:long],

clauses.text: the kitchen and bathroom exhaust fans that are required by [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect32.subsect3.art6:long], and
if the [REF:term:bldng]building includes a heated crawl space, the components that are required by [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect32.subsect3.art7:long].

content.text: Except as provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect32.subsect3.art4.sent6:short], a principal ventilation system shall mechanically provide supply air in accordance with [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect32.subsect3.art4.sent2:short], [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect32.subsect3.art4.sent3:short], [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect32.subsect3.art4.sent4:short] or [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect32.subsect3.art4.sent5:short].
Where the principal ventilation system is a ducted forced-air heating system, the ducted forced-air heating system shall

clauses.text: provide supply air through the ducting to

subclauses.text: each bedroom,
each floor level without a bedroom, and

ancillary spaces that contain an exhaust device, where the space is not within a [REF:term:dwllng-n]dwelling unit in a house with a [REF:term:scndr-st]secondary suite and where the house with a [REF:term:scndr-st]secondary suite contains a fuel-fired [REF:term:spc-htng-pplnc]space-heating appliance or fuel-fired water-heating [REF:term:pplnc]appliance of other than [REF:term:drct-vntd]direct-vented or [REF:term:mchncll-vntd]mechanically vented types,

clauses.text: draw supply air from an outdoor inlet that is connected to the cabinet containing the furnace air circulating fan required by [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect32.subsect3.art4.sent2.clause4:medium] by ducting that measures, from that cabinet to the point at which the ducting intersects the return air plenum,

subclauses.text: between 3 m and 4.5 m in length, or
if a flow control device is used, not more than 4.5 m in length,

clauses.text: draw supply air through ducting that is

subclauses.text: rigid ducting with an equivalent diameter of at least 100 mm, or
flexible ducting with an equivalent diameter of at least 125 mm, and

clauses.text: have a furnace air circulating fan set to run continuously.

content.text: Where the principal ventilation system is a ducted forced-air heating system used in combination with a heat-recovery ventilator,

clauses.text: the ducted forced-air heating system shall conform to [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect32.subsect3.art4.sent2.clause1:medium], [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect32.subsect3.art4.sent2.clause3:medium] and [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect32.subsect3.art4.sent2.clause4:medium],
the heat-recovery ventilator shall draw supply air from an outdoor inlet into the return air plenum of the ducted forced-air heating system, and
the heat-recovery ventilator shall draw exhaust air, through dedicated ducting,

subclauses.text: from one or more indoor inlets, at least one of which is located at least 2 m above the floor of the uppermost floor level, and
at the capacity rating of the heat-recovery ventilator, which shall be no less than the air-flow rate specified in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect32.subsect3.art5.table1:long].

content.text: Where the principal ventilation system is a ducted central-recirculation ventilation system, the ducted central-recirculation ventilation system shall

clauses.text: draw supply air from an outdoor inlet connected upstream of the fan,
draw air from

subclauses.text: each bedroom and deliver it to a common area, or
a common area and deliver it to each bedroom, and

clauses.text: deliver air to each ancillary space described in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect32.subsect3.art4.sent2.clause1.subclause3:medium].

content.text: A principal ventilation system need not conform to [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect32.subsect3.art4.sent1:short] if the principal ventilation system

clauses.text: services a [REF:term:dwllng-n]dwelling unit that

subclauses.text: is located where the January design temperature, on a 2.5% basis determined in conformance with [REF:internal:nbc.divA.sect1.subsect1.art3.sent1:long], is greater than −20°C,

has only 1 [REF:term:str]storey and a [REF:term:flr-r]floor area of less than 168 m2
                                  (metric) within the [REF:term:bldng-nvlp]building envelope,
does not have a ducted forced-air heating system, and

except for a [REF:term:scndr-st]secondary suite, is not located in a [REF:term:bldng]building conforming to [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect6:long] or [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part2.sect2.subsect3:long], and

clauses.text: provides supply air passively from outdoors through dedicated inlets that

subclauses.text: are located in each bedroom, at least one common area and each ancillary space described in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect32.subsect3.art4.sent2.clause1.subclause3:medium],
are located at least 1 800 mm above the floor, and

have an unobstructed vent area of not less than 25 cm2
                                  (metric).

content.text: A principal ventilation system exhaust fan shall

clauses.text: run continuously, and
provide at least the air-flow rate specified in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect32.subsect3.art5.table1:long].

content.title: Principal Ventilation System Exhaust Fan Minimum Air-flow Rate

content.text: For the purposes of [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect32.subsect3.art5.sent1:short], the capacity rating of the principal ventilation system exhaust fan shall be determined, based on air-flow performance at 50 pa of external static pressure, in accordance with

clauses.text: HVI Publication 916, "Airflow Test Procedure," or
CAN/CSA-C260-M, "Rating the Performance of Residential Mechanical Ventilating Equipment."

content.text: The principal ventilation system exhaust fan shall be

clauses.text: designed to run continuously, and
controlled by a dedicated switch that

subclauses.text: has 2 settings, on and off,
is located where it will be accessible for the purposes of servicing the exhaust fan but not likely to be turned off inadvertently, and
is clearly marked "PRINCIPAL VENTILATION EXHAUST FAN."

content.text: If the principal ventilation system exhaust fan is designed to run at multiple air-flow rates,

clauses.text: the air-flow rate of the fan shall be controlled by a switch other than the switch described in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect32.subsect3.art5.sent3.clause2:medium], and
the lowest air-flow rate shall not be less than the air-flow rate specified in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect32.subsect3.art5.table1:long].

content.text: The sound rating of the principal ventilation system exhaust fan shall not exceed 1.0 sone when running continuously at the air-flow rate specified in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect32.subsect3.art5.table1:long] as determined in accordance with

clauses.text: HVI Publication 915, "Loudness Testing and Rating Procedure," or
CAN/CSA-C260-M, "Rating the Performance of Residential Mechanical Ventilating Equipment."

content.text: An exhaust fan that provides at least the air-flow rate specified in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect32.subsect3.art6.table1:long] shall be installed in

clauses.text: every kitchen, and

every bathroom or water-closet room, unless the bathroom or water-closet room is served by the principal ventilation system exhaust fan that complies with [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect32.subsect3.art5:long].

content.text: For the purposes of [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect32.subsect3.art6.sent1:short], the capacity rating of the exhaust fan shall be determined, based on air-flow performance at 50 pa of external static pressure, in accordance with

clauses.text: HVI Publication 916, "Airflow Test Procedure," or
CAN/CSA-C260-M, "Rating the Performance of Residential Mechanical Ventilating Equipment."

content.title: Kitchen/Bathroom Exhaust Fan Minimum Air-flow Rate

header_rows.content: Minimum Exhaust Fan Air-flow Rate, L/s

content.text: Where a crawl space is heated by a ducted forced-air heating system that does not draw air from the crawl space to the furnace through the return air plenum, the crawl space shall be connected to the floor space above the crawl space by at least one air-transfer grille.
Where a crawl space is heated other than by a ducted forced-air heating system, the crawl space shall

clauses.text: be connected to

subclauses.text: the floor space above the crawl space by at least one air-transfer grille, and
the principal ventilation system by a supply air outlet or an exhaust air inlet,

clauses.text:
be connected to the floor space above the crawl space by at least 2 air-transfer grilles for every 30 m2
                               (metric) of crawl space area, or
be connected to

subclauses.text: the floor space above the crawl space by at least one air-transfer grille, and
the outdoors by a dedicated exhaust fan that complies with [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect32.subsect3.art7.sent4:short].

content.text: An air-transfer grille required by [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect32.subsect3.art7.sent1:short] or [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect32.subsect3.art7.sent2:short] shall have an unobstructed vent area of the greater of

clauses.text:
25 cm2
                               (metric), and

0.83 cm2
                               (metric) for every m2
                               (metric) of crawl space area.

content.text: Where a dedicated exhaust fan is installed in accordance with [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect32.subsect3.art7.sent2.clause3.subclause2:medium], the dedicated exhaust fan shall

clauses.text: provide an air-flow rate of at least 23 L/s, and
be controlled by

subclauses.text: a humidity control device, or
an adjustable time control device that is capable of providing not less than 8 total hours of ventilation per 24 hour period.

content.text: Where a crawl space is divided into 2 or more compartments, each heated compartment shall conform to [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect32.subsect3.art7.sent1:short] or [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect32.subsect3.art7.sent2:short].

Except as required by [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect32.subsect3.art8.sent3:short], this Article applies to air ducts other than those described in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect32.subsect1.art3:long].
[REF:term:xht-dct]Exhaust ducts shall discharge to the outdoors.
[REF:term:xht-dct]Exhaust ducts that are downstream of an exhaust fan shall have no connections to other fans or ducts.
[REF:term:xht-dct]Exhaust ducts, and [REF:term:ppl-dct]supply ducts that conduct heated or cooled air, shall

clauses.text: be sized in accordance with the requirements of the manufacturer of the fans to which they are connected, and
have an equivalent diameter not less than that specified by [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect32.subsect3.art8.table1:long].

content.title: Maximum Equivalent Duct Length^{(1)}, m

header_rows.content: Equivalent Diameter, mm (Cross Section Area for Rectangular Ducts, cm^{2})

body_rows.content: Equivalent Diameter, mm (Cross Section Area for Rectangular Ducts, cm^{2})

content.text: Where an [REF:term:xht-dct]exhaust duct passes through or is located adjacent to a space that is not [REF:term:cnd-sp]conditioned space, the duct shall conform to [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect3.art2:long], except that in no case shall such a duct be insulated to less than RSI 0.75.
Where a principal ventilation system [REF:term:ppl-dct]supply duct passes through or is located adjacent to a [REF:term:cnd-sp]conditioned space, the duct shall be

clauses.text: insulated to not less than RSI 0.75, and
provided with an effective vapour barrier.

content.text: Where a kitchen exhaust fan grille is installed within 1.2 m horizontally of a [REF:term:cktp]cooktop, the exhaust fan duct shall

clauses.text: be constructed of a material that is noncombustible, corrosion-resistant, and cleanable, and
be equipped with a grease filter at the intake end.

content.text: Except for a supply air system described in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect32.subsect3.art4.sent2:short] or [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect32.subsect3.art4.sent3:short], all joints in [REF:term:xht-dct]exhaust ducts, and in [REF:term:ppl-dct]supply ducts that conduct conditioned air, shall be sealed against air leakage with

clauses.text: sealants or gaskets made from liquids, mastics or heat-applied materials,
mastic with embedded fabric,
foil-faced butyl tape, or
aluminum foil tape.

content.text: [REF:term:ppl-dct]Supply ducts for a mechanical ventilation system shall not be used to provide combustion or dilution air to fuel-burning [REF:term:pplnc]appliances.
Outdoor air inlets and exhaust outlets shall be shielded from the weather, birds and rodents by using hoods incorporating a screen of corrosion-resistant material with openings of 6 to 12 mm.

Interior doors shall be undercut by a minimum of 12 mm above the finished floor or the rooms shall be provided with an air-transfer grille with an unobstructed vent area that is not less than 100 cm2
                            (metric).

Additional make-up air for the actual [REF:term:pplnc]appliance exhaust rate shall be provided for any [REF:term:pplnc]appliance that discharges air to the exterior at an installed rate exceeding 0.5 air changes per hour when it is located within a [REF:term:dwllng-n]dwelling unit or house with a [REF:term:bc-scnd-t]secondary suite that contains a vented [REF:term:pplnc]appliance that is subject to back drafting (Naturally Aspirating Fuel Fired Vented Appliance). (See Note A-9.32.4.1.)

Where additional make-up air is required for [REF:term:pplnc]appliances described in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect32.subsect4.art1.sent1:short], it shall be provided by a supply fan rated to deliver outdoor air at the rate of the installed exhaust [REF:term:pplnc]appliance.
The supply fan as required in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect32.subsect4.art1.sent2:short] shall be interconnected with the exhaust fan for which make-up air is required.
The outdoor air required by [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect32.subsect4.art1.sent3:short] shall be

clauses.text: tempered to at least 1°C before being introduced to a normally unoccupied area of the [REF:term:dwllng-n]dwelling unit or house with a [REF:term:bc-scnd-t]secondary suite including their common spaces, or
tempered to at least 12°C before being introduced to occupied areas either by passive transfer grille or directly from outside.

content.text: This Article applies to every [REF:term:bldng]building that contains a [REF:term:rdntl-cc]residential occupancy, a business and personal services occupancy, or a mercantile occupancy and that

clauses.text: is served by or contains a fuel-burning [REF:term:pplnc]appliance, or
contains a [REF:term:trg-grg]storage garage.

content.text: Carbon monoxide (CO) alarms installed in a residential occupancy required by this Article shall

clauses.text: conform to [REF:standard:csa6.19],
be equipped with an integral alarm that satisfies the audibility requirements of [REF:standard:csa6.19],
have no disconnect switch between the overcurrent device and the CO alarm, where the CO alarm is powered by the [REF:term:dwllng-n]dwelling unit's electrical system, and
be installed as recommended by the manufacturer.

content.text: Where a room in a residential occupancy contains a solid-fuel-burning [REF:term:pplnc]appliance, a CO alarm conforming to [REF:standard:csa6.19] shall be

clauses.text: installed as recommended by the manufacturer where these instructions specifically mention solid-fuel-burning [REF:term:pplnc]appliances, or
in the absence of specific instructions related to solid-fuel-burning [REF:term:pplnc]appliances, on or near the ceiling.

content.text: Where a fuel-burning [REF:term:pplnc]appliance is installed in a [REF:term:t]suite of [REF:term:rdntl-cc]residential occupancy, a CO alarm shall be installed

clauses.text: inside each bedroom, or
outside each bedroom, within 5 m (metric) of each bedroom door, measured following corridors and doorways.

content.text: Where a fuel-burning [REF:term:pplnc]appliance serves a residential occupancy and is installed in a [REF:term:rvc-rm]service room that is not in a [REF:term:t]suite of [REF:term:rdntl-cc]residential occupancy, a CO alarm shall be installed

clauses.text: either inside each bedroom, or if outside, within 5 m (metric) of each bedroom door, measured following corridors and doorways, in every [REF:term:t]suite of [REF:term:rdntl-cc]residential occupancy that shares a wall or floor/ceiling assembly with the [REF:term:rvc-rm]service room, and
in the [REF:term:rvc-rm]service room.

content.text: For each [REF:term:t]suite of [REF:term:rdntl-cc]residential occupancy that shares a wall or floor/ceiling assembly with a [REF:term:trg-grg]storage garage or that is adjacent to an attic or crawl space to which the [REF:term:trg-grg]storage garage is also adjacent, a CO alarm shall be installed

clauses.text: inside each bedroom, or
outside each bedroom, within 5 m (metric) of each bedroom door, measured following corridors and doorways.

content.text: Where CO alarms are installed in a house with a [REF:term:bc-scnd-t]secondary suite including their common spaces, the CO alarms shall be interconnected so that the actuation of any one CO alarm causes all CO alarms within the house with a [REF:term:bc-scnd-t]secondary suite including their common spaces to sound.
CO alarms installed in a business and personal services occupancy, or a mercantile occupancy as required by this Article shall conform to

clauses.text: CAN/CSA-6.19, "Residential carbon monoxide alarming devices," notwithstanding the scope of that standard,
UL 2034, "Standard for Single and Multiple Station Carbon Monoxide Alarms," notwithstanding the scope of that standard, or
good engineering practice.

content.text: Where a fuel-burning appliance serves a business and personal services occupancy, or mercantile occupancy, a CO alarm shall be,

clauses.text: where the fuel-burning appliance is part of a system that could circulate or distribute CO to a suite of business and personal services occupancy or mercantile occupancy, installed on each storey of each suite that may be exposed, and
installed in the room or space in which the fuel-burning appliance is located.

content.text: For each suite of business and personal services occupancy or mercantile occupancy that shares a wall or floor/ceiling assembly with either a storage garage, or a service room containing a fuel-burning appliance, or that is adjacent to an attic or crawl space to which either a storage garage, or a service room containing a fuel-burning appliance is also adjacent, a CO alarm shall be installed

clauses.text: on each storey of the adjacent suite, and
in each service room containing a fuel-burning appliance.

content.text: This Section applies to the design and installation of

clauses.text: heating systems, including requirements for combustion air, and air-conditioning systems serving only one [REF:term:dwllng-n]dwelling unit or houses with a [REF:term:bc-scnd-t]secondary suite including their common spaces, and
reserved.

content.text: The design and installation of heating systems, including requirements for combustion air, and air-conditioning systems other than those described in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect33.subsect1.art1.sent1:short] shall conform to [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part6:long]. (See [REF:internal:en000354:short] and [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect10.subsect10:long])

Unless the air duct distribution systems serving one of the [REF:term:dwllng-n]dwelling units in a house with a [REF:term:bc-scnd-t]secondary suite are designed and installed to prevent the circulation of smoke in accordance with [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect32.subsect3.art2.sent4:long] and equipped with fire dampers in accordance with [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect32.subsect3.art2.sent5:long], the air duct distribution system shall not be directly interconnected with other parts of the house.
Systems used for heating and air-conditioning shall conform to the energy efficiency requirements in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36:long]
Residential [REF:term:bldng]buildings intended for use in the winter months on a continuing basis shall be equipped with heating facilities conforming to this Section.

Except where determination according to [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect33.subsect5.art1:long] or good engineering practice according to [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part6.sect2.subsect1.art1:long] can show it to be unnecessary, [REF:term:dwllng-n]dwelling units intended for use in the summer months on a continuing basis shall be equipped with cooling facilities conforming to this Section. (See [REF:internal:en001271:short])
At the outside winter design temperature, required heating facilities shall be capable of maintaining an indoor air temperature of not less than

clauses.text: 22°C (metric) in all living spaces,
18°C (metric) in unfinished [REF:term:bmnt]basements,
18°C (metric) in common [REF:term:rvc-rm]service rooms, ancillary spaces and [REF:term:xt]exits in houses with a [REF:term:bc-scnd-t]secondary suite, and
15°C (metric) in heated crawl spaces.

content.text: At the outside summer design temperature, required cooling facilities shall be capable of maintaining an indoor air temperature of not more than 26°C (metric) in at least one living space in each [REF:term:dwllng-n]dwelling unit.

The outdoor conditions to be used in designing heating and air-conditioning
systems shall be determined in conformance with [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part1.sect1.subsect3.art1:long]

subsections.title: General Requirements for Heating and Air-conditioning Systems

articles.title: Design of Heating and Air-conditioning Systems

content.text: Aspects of heating and air-conditioning systems not specifically addressed in this Subsection, including ducting, and mechanical heating and refrigeration equipment, shall be designed, constructed and installed in accordance with good practice such as that described in the ASHRAE Handbooks and Standards, the [REF:standard:hraisar-g1] the CHC Handbook on Hydronic Heating Systems, the Hydronics Institute Manuals, the SMACNA Manuals and the TECA Quality First Manuals. (See also [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect32.subsect3:long] for the design of systems that also provide ventilation.)
The installation of a hydronic heating system shall conform to [REF:standard:csab214].

Where a single heating system serves a house with a [REF:term:scnd-t]secondary suite, individual temperature controls
shall be provided in each [REF:term:dwllng-n]dwelling unit served by the system. (See [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.appnote204:short].)

Equipment forming part of a heating or air-conditioning system,
with the exception of embedded pipes or ducts, shall be installed
with provision for access for inspection, maintenance, repair and
cleaning.

Where a heating or air-conditioning system serves more than one [REF:term:dwllng-n]dwelling unit in a house with a [REF:term:bc-scnd-t]secondary suite including their common spaces, access required by [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect33.subsect4.art4.sent1:short] from more than one [REF:term:dwllng-n]dwelling unit, common space or ancillary space is not required.

Equipment forming part of a heating or air-conditioning system
that may be adversely affected by freezing temperatures and that is
located in an unheated area shall be protected from freezing.

Heating and cooling systems shall be designed to allow for expansion
and contraction of the heat transfer fluid and to maintain the system
pressure within the rated working pressure limits of all components
of the system.

Mechanical systems and equipment shall be designed and installed
to accommodate the maximum amount of structural movement provided
for in the construction of the [REF:term:bldng]building.

Where the [REF:term:bldng]building is in a location
where the seismic design parameter, S_{max}, for Site Class C is greater than
0.37, heating and air-conditioning equipment with fuel or power connections
shall be secured to the structure to resist overturning and displacement.
(See [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.appnote184:long].)
Asbestos shall not be used in air distribution systems or equipment.

Systems serving garages, and systems serving other occupied
parts of a [REF:term:dwllng-n]dwelling unit but located
in or running through a garage, shall be designed and constructed
in a manner such that means are not provided for the transfer of contaminants
from the garage into other spaces in the [REF:term:dwllng-n]dwelling
unit.

Design, Construction and Installation Standard for Solid-Fuel-Burning
Appliances

content.text:
The design, construction and installation, including the provision
of combustion air, of solid-fuel-burning [REF:term:pplnc]appliances and equipment, including [REF:term:tv]stoves, [REF:term:cktp]cooktops, ovens and [REF:term:pc-htr]space
heaters, shall conform to [REF:standard:csab365]

(See also Subclause 9.33.5.2.(1)(a)(ii).)
