content.text: Fireplaces shall conform to [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect22:long]

The design, construction and installation of air duct distribution
systems serving heating systems in which the rated heat input does
not exceed 120 kW (metric) shall conform to this Subsection.

Air duct distribution systems in which the rated heat input
exceeds 120 kW (metric) shall conform to [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part6:long] and [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect6.subsect5:long]

Except as provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect33.subsect6.art2.sent2:short]
                           [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect33.subsect6.art2.sent6:short] and in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect6.subsect4.art3:long], all ducts, duct
connectors, associated fittings and [REF:term:plnm]plenums used in air duct systems shall be constructed of steel, aluminum
alloy, copper, clay or similar [REF:term:ncmbtbl]noncombustible material.
Ducts, associated fittings and [REF:term:plnm]plenums are permitted to contain [REF:term:cmbtbl]combustible material provided they

clauses.text:
conform to the appropriate requirements for Class 1 duct materials
in [REF:standard:ulcs110]
conform to [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect1.subsect5.art18:long] and [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect1.subsect9:long],

are not used in vertical runs serving more than 2 storeys
                               (metric), and

are not used in air duct systems in which the air temperature
may exceed 120°C (metric).

content.text:
Duct sealants shall have a [REF:term:flm-prd-]flame-spread
rating of not more than 25 and a smoke developed classification
of not more than 50.
Duct connectors that contain [REF:term:cmbtbl]combustible materials and that are used between ducts and air outlet units shall

clauses.text:
conform to the appropriate requirements for Class 1 air duct
materials in [REF:standard:ulcs110]
be limited to 4 m (metric) in length,
be used only in horizontal runs, and
not penetrate required [REF:term:fr-prtn]fire separations.

content.text:
[REF:term:cmbtbl]Combustible ducts that are part
of a duct system carrying only ventilation air and that are contained
entirely within a [REF:term:dwllng-n]dwelling unit need
not comply with the requirements of [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect33.subsect6.art2.sent1:short]
                           [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect33.subsect6.art2.sent4:short].

Except as provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect33.subsect6.art13.sent2:long]
                           [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect33.subsect6.art13.sent3:short], ducts that are part of a return-air duct system and that are contained
entirely within a [REF:term:dwllng-n]dwelling unit need
not comply with the requirements of [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect33.subsect6.art2.sent1:short]
                           [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect33.subsect6.art2.sent4:short].

Materials referred to in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect33.subsect6.art2.sent1:short]
                           [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect33.subsect6.art2.sent6:short], when used in a location where they may be subjected
to excessive moisture, shall

clauses.text: have no appreciable loss of strength when wet, and
be corrosion-resistant.

content.text:
Tape used for sealing duct joints in air ducts, [REF:term:plnm]plenums and other parts of air duct systems shall meet the
flame-resistance requirements for fabric in [REF:standard:ulcs109], "Standard Method for Flame Tests of Flame-Resistant Fabrics and Films."

Coverings, linings and associated adhesives and insulation of
air ducts, [REF:term:plnm]plenums and other parts of air
duct systems shall be of [REF:term:ncmbtbl]noncombustible material when exposed to heated air or radiation from heat sources
that would result in the exposed surface exceeding a temperature of 120°C (metric).

Except as provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect33.subsect6.art4.sent3:short], when [REF:term:cmbtbl]combustible coverings and linings,
including associated adhesives and insulation, are used, they shall
have

clauses.text:
a [REF:term:flm-prd-]flame-spread rating of not more
than 25 on any exposed surface, or any surface that would be exposed
by cutting through the material in any direction, and
a smoke developed classification of not more than 50.

content.text:
The outer covering of ducts, [REF:term:plnm]plenums and other parts of air duct systems used within an assembly of [REF:term:cmbtbl-c]combustible construction are permitted to
have

clauses.text: an exposed surface [REF:term:flm-prd-]flame-spread rating of not more than 75, and
a smoke developed classification greater than 50.

content.text:
[REF:term:cmbtbl]Combustible  coverings, linings
and foamed plastic insulation described in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect33.subsect6.art4.sent2:short]
                           [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect33.subsect6.art4.sent3:short]
                           [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect33.subsect6.art4.sent6:short] shall not flame, glow, smoulder or smoke when tested in accordance
with the method of test in [REF:standard:astmc411], "Standard Specification for Hot-Surface Performance of High-Temperature Thermal Insulation," at the
maximum temperature to which they are to be exposed in service.

Except as provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect33.subsect6.art4.sent6:short]
                           [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect33.subsect6.art4.sent7:short], foamed plastic insulation shall not be used as part
of an air duct.

Foamed plastic insulation conforming to [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect25.subsect2.art2:long] is permitted to be used to insulate a galvanized steel, stainless
steel or aluminum air duct, provided

clauses.text:
the foamed plastic insulation applied to supply ductwork is
not less than 3 m (metric) from the [REF:term:frnc]furnace bonnet,

the temperature within the ductwork where the insulation is
installed is not greater than 50°C (metric),
duct joints are taped with a product conforming to [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect33.subsect6.art3.sent1:long],

return air [REF:term:plnm]plenums are separated from
the foamed plastic insulation, and
the foamed plastic insulation is protected

subclauses.text:
by one of the interior finishes described in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect29.subsect4:long]
                                 [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect29.subsect9:long],

provided the [REF:term:bldng]building does not contain
a Group C [REF:term:mjr-ccpn]major occupancy, by sheet
metal that is mechanically fastened to the supporting assembly independent
of the insulation, is not less than 0.38 mm (metric) thick and
has a melting point of 650°C (metric) or more, or
by any thermal barrier that meets the requirements of [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect1.subsect5.art15.sent2.clause5:long].

content.text:
Foamed plastic insulation is permitted to be used in a ceiling
space that acts as a return air [REF:term:plnm]plenum provided
the foamed plastic insulation is protected from exposure to the [REF:term:plnm] plenum in accordance with [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect1.subsect5.art14.sent4:long].

[REF:term:cmbtbl]Combustible coverings and linings
of ducts, including associated adhesives and insulation, shall be
interrupted

clauses.text:
at the immediate area of operation of heat sources in a duct
system, such as electric resistance heaters or fuel-burning heaters
or [REF:term:frnc]furnaces, and
where the duct penetrates a [REF:term:fr-prtn]fire separation.

content.text:
Linings of ducts shall be installed so that they will not interfere
with the operation of volume or balancing dampers or of [REF:term:fr-dmpr]fire dampers, [REF:term:fr-tp-fl]fire stop
flaps and other closures.

articles.title: Galvanized Steel or Aluminum Supply Ducts

content.text: Galvanized steel or aluminum [REF:term:ppl-dct]supply ducts shall conform to [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect33.subsect6.art5.table1:long]

shall conform to [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect33.subsect6.art5.table1:long]

content.text:
Where the installation of heating [REF:term:ppl-dct]supply
ducts in walls and floors creates a space between the duct
and construction material, the space shall be firestopped with [REF:term:ncmbtbl]noncombustible material at each end.

Ducts shall be securely supported by metal hangers, straps,
lugs or brackets, except that, where zero clearance is permitted,
wooden brackets are permitted to be used.

All round duct joints shall be tight-fitting and lapped not
less than 25 mm (metric).

Rectangular duct connections shall be made with S and drive
cleats or equivalent mechanical connections.

Duct systems shall have no openings other than those required
for the proper operation and maintenance of the system.

Air duct systems serving garages shall not be interconnected
with other parts of the [REF:term:dwllng-n]dwelling unit.

Trunk [REF:term:ppl-dct]supply ducts shall not be
nailed directly to wood members.

Branch ducts shall be supported at suitable spacings to maintain
alignment and prevent sagging.

Ducts passing through unheated spaces shall have all joints
taped or otherwise sealed to ensure that the ducts are airtight throughout
their length.

[REF:term:cmbtbl]Combustible ducts in concrete slabs-on-ground
that are connected to a [REF:term:frnc]furnace supply [REF:term:plnm]plenum shall be located not closer than 600 mm (metric) to that [REF:term:plnm]plenum and not less
than 600 mm (metric) from its connection to a riser or register.

Ducts in or beneath concrete slabs-on-ground shall be watertight
and corrosion-, decay-, and mildew-resistant.
Underground ducts shall

clauses.text:
be constructed to provide interior drainage from and access
to all low points, and
not be connected directly to a sewer.

content.text:
The clearance of [REF:term:frnc]furnace
                           [REF:term:plnm]plenums from [REF:term:cmbtbl]combustible material shall conform to the appropriate standards in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect33.subsect5.art2.sent1:long].

Where the [REF:term:plnm]plenum clearance required
in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect33.subsect6.art8.sent1:short] is 75 mm (metric) or
less, the clearance between a [REF:term:ppl-dct] supply duct and [REF:term:cmbtbl]combustible material shall

clauses.text:
be equal to the required [REF:term:plnm]plenum clearance
within 450 mm (metric) of the [REF:term:plnm]plenum, and

be not less than 12 mm (metric) at a distance of 450
mm (metric) or more from the [REF:term:plnm]plenum, except
that this clearance may be reduced to zero beyond a bend or offset
in the duct sufficiently large to shield the remainder of the [REF:term:ppl-dct]supply duct from direct radiation from the [REF:term:frnc]furnace heat exchanger. (See Note A-3.6.5.6.(2).)

content.text:
Where the [REF:term:plnm] plenum clearance required
in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect33.subsect6.art8.sent1:short] is more than 75
mm (metric) but not more than 150 mm (metric), the clearance between
a [REF:term:ppl-dct]supply duct and [REF:term:cmbtbl] combustible material shall be

clauses.text:
equal to the required [REF:term:plnm]plenum clearance
within a horizontal distance of 1.8 m (metric) of the [REF:term:plnm]plenum, and

not less than 12 mm (metric) at a horizontal distance of  1.8 m (metric) or more from the [REF:term:plnm]plenum,
except that this distance may be reduced to zero beyond a bend or
offset in the duct sufficiently large to shield the remainder of the
duct from direct radiation from the [REF:term:frnc]furnace heat exchanger. (See Note A-3.6.5.6.(3).)

content.text:
Where the [REF:term:plnm] plenum clearance required
in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect33.subsect6.art8.sent1:short] is more than 150
mm (metric), the clearance between a [REF:term:ppl-dct] supply duct and [REF:term:cmbtbl]combustible material shall be

clauses.text:
equal to the required [REF:term:plnm]plenum clearance
within a horizontal distance of 1 m (metric) of the [REF:term:plnm]plenum,

not less than 150 mm (metric) within a horizontal distance
between  1 m (metric) and 1.8 m (metric) from the [REF:term:plnm]plenum, and

not less than 25 mm (metric) at a horizontal distance of  1.8 m (metric) or more from the [REF:term:plnm]plenum,
except that this distance may be reduced to 8 mm (metric) beyond
a bend or offset in the duct sufficiently large to shield the remainder
of the [REF:term:ppl-dct] supply duct from direct radiation
from the [REF:term:frnc]furnace  heat exchanger. (See Note A-3.6.5.6.(4).)

content.text:
Where a register is installed in a floor directly over a pipeless [REF:term:frnc]furnace, a double-walled register box with not
less than 100 mm (metric) between walls, or a register box with
the warm-air passage completely surrounded by the cold-air passage,
shall be permitted in lieu of the clearances listed in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect33.subsect6.art8.sent2:short]
                           [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect33.subsect6.art8.sent4:short].

All branch [REF:term:ppl-dct] supply ducts that are
not fitted with diffusers with adjustable balance stops shall be supplied
with adjustable dampers and fitted with devices to indicate the positions
of the dampers.

articles.title: Warm-Air Supply Outlets and Return Inlets --- General

content.text:
Supply outlets and return openings in the [REF:term:dwllng-n]dwelling unit, when located less than 2 m (metric) above
the floor, shall be protected by grilles having openings of a size
that will not allow the passage of a 15 mm (metric) diam sphere.

[REF:term:cmbtbl]Combustible grilles, diffusers and
other devices for the supply and return air openings installed in
walls and ceilings shall have a [REF:term:flm-prd-]flame-spread
rating of

clauses.text: not more than 200 in bathrooms, and
not more than 150 in rooms or spaces other than bathrooms.

content.text:
In a [REF:term:dwllng-n] dwelling unit, a warm-air
supply outlet shall be provided in each finished room that is located
adjacent to unheated space.

Except as provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect33.subsect6.art11.sent3:short], when a room described in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect33.subsect6.art11.sent1:short] is located adjacent to exterior walls, such outlet shall be located
so as to bathe at least one exterior wall or window with warm air,
except in bathrooms, utility rooms or kitchens, where this may not
be practical.

Where the heating system is also designed to provide ventilation
air, ceiling outlets or outlets located high on interior walls are
permitted to be installed, provided the outlets are designed for this
purpose and are installed with diffusers.

At least one warm-air supply outlet shall be provided for each 40 m2
                            (metric) of floor surface area in unfinished [REF:term:bmnt]basements serving [REF:term:dwllng-n]dwelling
units, and it shall be located so as to provide adequate distribution
of warm air throughout the [REF:term:bmnt]basement.

At least one warm-air supply outlet shall be provided for each 80 m2
                            (metric) of floor surface area in heated crawl
spaces serving [REF:term:dwllng-n]dwelling units, and it
shall be located so as to provide adequate distribution of warm air
throughout the crawl space.

Except for pipeless [REF:term:frnc]furnaces, the
capacity of warm-air supply outlets serving [REF:term:dwllng-n]dwelling units shall be not less than the design heat loss
from the area served and shall not exceed 3 kW (metric) per outlet.

In [REF:term:bmnt]basements and heated crawl spaces,
the calculated heat gain from the [REF:term:ppl-dct]supply ducts and [REF:term:plnm]plenum surfaces is permitted to be
considered in calculating the design heat loss.

The temperature of supply air at warm-air supply outlets shall
not exceed 70°C (metric).

Warm-air supply outlets located in finished areas shall be provided
with diffusers and adjustable openings and shall not be located on
a [REF:term:frnc]furnace
                           [REF:term:plnm]plenum.

Return-air inlets shall not be installed in an enclosed room
or crawl space that provides combustion air to a [REF:term:frnc]furnace.

Except for unfinished areas and floor levels which are less
than 900 mm (metric) above or below an adjacent floor level which
is provided with a return-air inlet, at least one return-air inlet
shall be provided in each floor level in a [REF:term:dwllng-n]dwelling unit.

Provision shall be made for the return of air from all rooms
by leaving gaps beneath doors, using louvred doors or installing [REF:term:rtrn-dct]return duct inlets.

The return-air system shall be designed to handle the entire
air supply.

Where any part of a [REF:term:rtrn-dct]return duct will be exposed to radiation from the [REF:term:frnc]furnace heat exchanger or other radiating part within the [REF:term:frnc]furnace, such part of a [REF:term:rtrn-dct]return duct directly above or within 600 mm (metric) of the outside [REF:term:frnc]furnace casing shall be [REF:term:ncmbtbl]noncombustible.
[REF:term:rtrn-dct]Return ducts serving solid-fuel-burning [REF:term:frnc]furnaces shall be constructed of [REF:term:ncmbtbl]noncombustible material.

[REF:term:cmbtbl]Combustible
                           [REF:term:rtrn-dct]return ducts shall be lined with [REF:term:ncmbtbl]noncombustible material

clauses.text: below floor registers,
at the bottom of vertical ducts, and
under [REF:term:frnc]furnaces having a bottom return.

content.text:
Spaces between studs or joists used as [REF:term:rtrn-dct]return ducts shall be separated from the unused portions of
such spaces by tight-fitting metal stops or wood blocking.

A vertical [REF:term:rtrn-dct]return duct shall have
openings to return air on not more than one floor.

The return-air system shall be designed so that the negative
pressure from the circulating fan cannot

clauses.text:
affect the [REF:term:frnc]furnace combustion air
supply, nor
draw combustion products from joints or openings in the [REF:term:frnc]furnace or [REF:term:fl-pp]flue pipe.

content.text:
Air filters for air duct systems shall conform to the requirements
for Class 2 air filter units as described in [REF:standard:ulcs111]

When electrostatic-type filters are used, they shall be installed
so as to ensure that the electric circuit is automatically de-energized
when filter access doors are opened or, in [REF:term:dwllng-n]dwelling units, when the [REF:term:frnc] furnace circulation fan is not operating.

When odour removal equipment of the adsorption type is used
it shall be

clauses.text:
installed to provide access so that adsorption material can
be reactivated or renewed, and

protected from dust accumulation by air filters installed on
the inlet side.

content.text:
Every steam or hot water radiator and convector located in a
recess or concealed space or attached to the face of a wall of [REF:term:cmbtbl-c]combustible construction shall be provided
with a [REF:term:ncmbtbl]noncombustible lining or backing.

The exposed surface temperature of a steam or hot water radiator
shall not exceed 70°C (metric) unless precautions are taken to
prevent human contact.

subsections.title: Piping for Heating and Cooling Systems

content.text:
Piping shall be made from materials designed to withstand the
effects of temperatures and pressures that may occur in the system.
(See [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect1.subsect5.art19:long]
                           [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect1.subsect9.art1:long]
                           [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect10.subsect9.art7:long], and [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect10.subsect9.art9.sent3:long] for fire safety requirements.)

Every pipe used in a heating or air-conditioning system shall
be installed to allow for expansion and contraction due to temperature
changes.

Supports and anchors for piping in a heating or air-conditioning
system shall be designed and installed to ensure that undue stress
is not placed on the supporting structure.

Insulation and coverings on pipes shall be composed of material
suitable for the operating temperature of the system to withstand
deterioration from softening, melting, mildew and mould.

Insulation and coverings on pipes in which the temperature of
the fluid exceeds 120°C (metric)

clauses.text: shall be made of [REF:term:ncmbtbl]noncombustible material, or

shall not flame, glow, smoulder or smoke when tested in accordance
with [REF:standard:astmc411], "Standard Specification for Hot-Surface Performance of High-Temperature Thermal Insulation," at the maximum temperature to
which such insulation or covering is to be exposed in service.

content.text:
Except as provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect33.subsect8.art2.sent6:short], where [REF:term:cmbtbl]combustible insulation is used
on piping in a horizontal or [REF:term:vrtcl-rv]vertical service
space, the insulation and coverings on such pipes shall have
a [REF:term:flm-prd-]flame-spread rating throughout the
material of not more than

clauses.text: 25 in [REF:term:bldng]buildings of [REF:term:ncmbtbl]noncombustible construction, and
75 in [REF:term:bldng]buildings of [REF:term:cmbtbl-c]combustible construction.

content.text:
Except as provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect33.subsect8.art2.sent6:short], insulation and coverings on piping located in rooms and spaces
other than the [REF:term:rvc-pc]service spaces described
in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect33.subsect8.art2.sent3:short] shall have a [REF:term:flm-prd-]flame-spread rating not more than that required
for the interior finish for the ceiling of the room or space.

Pipes that are exposed to human contact shall be insulated so
that the exposed surface does not exceed  70°C (metric). (See Note A-6.5.1.1.(3).)

No [REF:term:flm-prd-]flame-spread rating or smoke
developed classification limitations are required where [REF:term:cmbtbl]combustible insulation and coverings are used
on piping when such piping is

clauses.text: located within a concealed space in a wall,
located in a floor slab, or

enclosed in a [REF:term:ncmbtbl]noncombustible raceway
or conduit.

content.text:
Clearances between [REF:term:cmbtbl]combustible material
and bare pipes carrying steam or hot water shall conform to [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect33.subsect8.art3.table1:long]

content.title:
Clearance between Steam or Hot Water Pipes and Combustible
Material

content.text:
Where a pipe carrying steam or hot water at a temperature above 120°C (metric) passes through a [REF:term:cmbtbl]combustible floor, ceiling or wall, the construction shall be protected by a
sleeve of metal or other [REF:term:ncmbtbl]noncombustible material not less than 50 mm (metric) larger in diameter than
the pipe.

Unprotected steam or hot water pipes that pass through a storage
space shall be covered with not less than 25 mm (metric) thickness
of [REF:term:ncmbtbl]noncombustible insulation to prevent
direct contact with the material stored.

subsections.title: Refrigerating Systems and Equipment for Air-conditioning

content.text:
Where a cooling unit is combined with a fuel-fired [REF:term:frnc]furnace in the same duct system, the cooling unit
shall be installed

clauses.text: in parallel with the heating [REF:term:frnc]furnace,

upstream of the [REF:term:frnc]furnace, provided
the [REF:term:frnc]furnace is designed for such application,
or

downstream of the [REF:term:frnc]furnace, provided
the cooling unit is designed to prevent excessive temperature or pressure
in the refrigeration system.

content.text:
Except as provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect33.subsect10.art2:long]
                           [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect33.subsect10.art3:long], the products of combustion
from oil-, gas- and solid-fuel-burning [REF:term:pplnc]appliances, including [REF:term:tv]stoves, [REF:term:cktp]cooktops, ovens and [REF:term:pc-htr]space heaters, shall be vented
in conformance with the applicable [REF:term:pplnc]appliance installation standard listed in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect33.subsect5.art2.sent1:long]
                           [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect33.subsect5.art3.sent1:long].

[REF:term:fctr-blt]Factory-built chimneys serving
solid-fuel-burning [REF:term:pplnc]appliances, and their
installation, shall conform to [REF:standard:ulcs629], "Standard for 650°C Factory-Built Chimneys." (See Note A-9.33.10.2.(1).)

[REF:term:mnr-r-cn]Masonry or concrete chimneys shall
conform to [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect21:long]

Electrical installations, including the service capacity of
the installation and the number and distribution of circuits and receptacles,
shall meet the requirements of the appropriate provincial, territorial
or municipal legislation or, in the absence of such legislation, shall
conform to the Safety Standards Act and pursuant regulations

Where electrical services are available, electrical facilities
shall be provided for every [REF:term:bldng]building in
conformance with this Section.

articles.title: Location of Equipment in Public Areas

content.text:
Entrance switches, meters, panel boxes, splitter boxes, time
clocks and other similar equipment shall not be located in any public
area unless adequate precautions are taken to prevent interference
with the equipment.

Recessed lighting fixtures shall not be located in insulated
ceilings unless the fixtures are designed for such installations.

Except as required in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect34.subsect1.art5.sent2:short], optical fibre cables and electrical wires and cables installed
in [REF:term:bldng]buildings permitted to be of [REF:term:cmbtbl-c] combustible construction shall

clauses.text:
not convey flame or continue to burn for more than 1 min (metric) when tested in conformance with the Vertical Flame Test (FT1 rating)
in [REF:standard:csac22.2no.0.3] or
be located in

subclauses.text: totally enclosed [REF:term:ncmbtbl]noncombustible raceways (see [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect9.appnote10:long]),
masonry walls,
concrete slabs, or
totally enclosed non-metallic raceways conforming to [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect1.subsect5.art23.sent1.clause2:long].

content.text:
Except as permitted in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect34.subsect1.art5.sent3:short], where a concealed space in a floor or ceiling assembly is used
as a [REF:term:plnm]plenum, electrical wires and cables
with [REF:term:cmbtbl]combustible insulation, jackets or
sheathes that are used for the transmission of voice, sound or data
and optical fibre cables installed within the [REF:term:plnm]plenum shall conform to [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect6.subsect4.art3.sent1.clause1:long].

Wires or cables within [REF:term:plnm]plenum spaces
that are used for the transmission of signals in fire alarm, security,
radio, and television broadcasting, closed circuit television or community
television systems need not meet the requirements of [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect34.subsect1.art5.sent2:short].

An exterior lighting outlet with fixture controlled by a wall
switch located within the [REF:term:bldng]building shall
be provided at every entrance to [REF:term:bldng]buildings of [REF:term:rdntl-cc]residential occupancy.

Except as provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect34.subsect2.art2.sent2:short], a lighting outlet with fixture controlled by a wall switch shall
be provided in kitchens, bedrooms, living rooms, utility rooms, laundry
rooms, dining rooms, bathrooms, water-closet rooms, vestibules and
hallways in [REF:term:dwllng-n]dwelling units.

Where a receptacle controlled by a wall switch is provided in
bedrooms or living rooms, such rooms need not conform to the requirements
in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect34.subsect2.art2.sent1:short].
Every stairway shall be lighted.

Except as provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect34.subsect2.art3.sent3:short], 3-way wall switches located at the head and foot of every stairway
shall be provided to control at least one lighting outlet with fixture
for stairways with 4 or more risers in [REF:term:dwllng-n]dwelling
units and houses with a [REF:term:scnd-t]secondary suite including their common spaces.

The stairway lighting for [REF:term:bmnt]basements that do not contain finished space or lead to an outside entrance
or built-in garage and which serve not more than one [REF:term:dwllng-n]dwelling unit is permitted to be controlled
by a single switch located at the head of the stairs.

A lighting outlet with fixture shall be provided for each 30 m2
                            (metric) or fraction thereof of [REF:term:flr-r]floor area in unfinished [REF:term:bmnt]basements.

The outlet required in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect34.subsect2.art4.sent1:short] nearest the stairs shall be controlled by a wall switch located
at the head of the stairs.

A lighting outlet with fixture shall be provided in storage
rooms.

A lighting outlet with fixture shall be provided for an attached,
built-in or detached garage or carport.

Except as provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect34.subsect2.art6.sent3:short], outlets required in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect34.subsect2.art6.sent1:short] shall
be controlled by a wall switch near the doorway.

Where the outlet and fixture required in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect34.subsect2.art6.sent1:short] are ceiling mounted above an area not normally occupied
by a parked car, or are wall mounted, a fixture with a built-in switch
accessible to an adult of average height is permitted to be used.

Where a carport is lighted by a light at the entrance to a [REF:term:dwllng-n]dwelling unit, additional carport lighting
is not required.

Every public or service area in [REF:term:bldng]buildings shall be provided with lighting outlets with fixtures controlled
by a wall switch or panel to illuminate every portion of such areas.

When provided by incandescent lighting, illumination required
in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect34.subsect2.art7.sent1:short] shall conform to [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect34.subsect2.art7.table1:long] (See [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect9.subsect12.art2:long] for lighting in [REF:term:mn-f-gr]means of egress.)

When other types of lighting are used, illumination equivalent
to that shown in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect34.subsect2.art7.table1:long] shall be provided.

Notwithstanding [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect34.subsect2.art7.sent1:short] to [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect34.subsect2.art7.sent3:short], rooms and spaces used by the public shall be equipped to provide illumination as described in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect2.subsect7.art1.sent4:short] to [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect2.subsect7.art1.sent7:short].

content.title: Lighting for Public Areas

body_rows.content: Rooms for storage of combustible refuse

content.text: Emergency lighting shall conform to [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect9.subsect12:long]

This Section applies to garages and carports serving not more
than one [REF:term:dwllng-n]dwelling unit.

The construction of a garage or carport shall conform to the
requirements for other [REF:term:bldng]buildings in this
Part except as provided in this Section.

Where a roofed enclosure used for the storage or parking of
motor vehicles has more than 60% of the total perimeter enclosed by
walls, doors or windows, the enclosure shall be considered a garage.

Where an attached or built-in garage is provided and where adjacent
spaces in the [REF:term:bldng]building are less than 50 mm (metric) above the garage floor, (See Note A-9.35.2.2.(1).)

clauses.text: the garage floor shall be sloped to the outdoors, or

where the garage can accommodate not more than 3 vehicles (metric), an airtight curb or [REF:term:prttn]partition not less
than 50 mm (metric) high shall be installed at the edges of the
garage floor adjacent to interior space.

content.text:
Except as permitted in this Subsection, [REF:term:fndtn]foundations conforming to [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect12:long]
                           [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect15:long] shall
be provided for the support of carport and garage super-structures,
including that portion beneath garage doors.

Detached garages of less than 55 m2
                            (metric)
                           [REF:term:flr-r]floor area and not more than 1 [REF:term:tr]storey in height that are not of masonry or masonry
veneer construction are permitted to be supported on

clauses.text: wood mud sills, or
a 100 mm thick concrete floor slab.

articles.title: Protection from Damage due to Soil Movement

content.text:
In clay-type [REF:term:l]soils subject to significant
movement with a change in [REF:term:l]soil moisture content,
the [REF:term:fndtn]foundation depth of carports or garages
connected to a [REF:term:dwllng-n]dwelling unit directly
or by a breezeway shall be approximately the same depth as the main [REF:term:bldng]building
                           [REF:term:fndtn]foundation.

Where slab-on-ground construction is used, a construction joint
shall be provided between the main [REF:term:bldng]building slab and a slab serving an attached garage, breezeway or carport.

Except as provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect12:long], [REF:term:fndtn]foundations for attached unheated garages or
carports shall be below frost level.

Detached garages of less than 55 m2
                            (metric)
                           [REF:term:flr-r]floor area and not more than 1 storey
                            (metric) in height that are  not of masonry
or masonry veneer construction need not conform with  the [REF:term:fndtn]foundation drainage requirements stated in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect14:long], where the finished ground level is at or near
 the elevation of the garage's floor and where the ground slopes away
 from the [REF:term:bldng]building.

Piers for the support of carport columns shall extend not less
than 150 mm (metric) above ground level.

Piers referred to in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect35.subsect3.art4.sent1:short] shall project not less than 25 mm (metric) beyond the base
of the column but in no case be less than 190 mm (metric) by 190 mm (metric) in size.
Interior finish need not be applied to garage and carport walls.

Columns for garages and carports shall conform to [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect17:long], except that 89 mm (metric) by 89
mm (metric) wood columns may be used.

Garage or carport walls and columns shall be anchored to the [REF:term:fndtn]foundation to resist wind uplift in conformance
with [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect6:long], except that where a garage
is supported on the surface of the ground, ground anchors shall be
provided to resist wind uplift.
This Section is concerned with the energy used by [REF:term:bldng]buildings as a result of

clauses.text: the design and construction of the [REF:term:bldng]building envelope, and

the design and construction or specification of systems and
equipment for

subclauses.text: heating, ventilating or air-conditioning, and
service water heating.

content.text:
For the purpose of this Section, the term “common space” shall
mean all spaces required to be [REF:term:cnd-sp]conditioned spaces in accordance with the requirements of the Code that are not within
a [REF:term:t]suite but shall not include crawl spaces
and [REF:term:vrtcl-rv]vertical service spaces. (See [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.appnote216:long].)

For the purpose of this Section, the term “overall thermal transmittance,”
or U-value, shall mean the rate, in W/(m2×K) (metric), at which heat is transferred through a [REF:term:bldng]building assembly that is subject to temperature differences. (See [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.appnote211:short].)

For the purpose of this Section, the term “effective thermal
resistance,” or RSI value, shall mean the inverse of the overall thermal
transmittance of an assembly, in (m2×K)/W (metric). (See [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.appnote212:short].)

For the purpose of this Section, the term “fenestration” shall
mean all [REF:term:bldng]building envelope assemblies,
including their frames, that transfer visible light, such as windows,
clerestories, skylights, translucent wall panels, glass block assemblies,
transoms, sidelights, sliding, overhead or swinging glass doors, and
glazed inserts in doors, etc. (See [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.appnote213:short].)

revisions.text:
For the purpose of this Section, the term “annual energy consumption”
shall mean the annual sum of service water heating and space-conditioning
energy consumption of the proposed house design, calculated in accordance
with [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect5.art4:long]
                                 [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect8.art3:short], as applicable. (See [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.appnote214:short].)

For the purpose of this Section, the term "annual energy consumption" shall mean the annual sum of service water heating and space-conditioning energy consumption of the proposed house design, calculated in accordance with [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect5.art4:long]
                                    [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect6.art5:short], as applicable. (See [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.appnote214:short].)

For the purpose of this Section, the term “house energy target”
shall mean the annual energy consumption of the reference house, calculated
in accordance with [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect5.art4:long]
                                 [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect8.art3:short], as applicable. (See [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.appnote214:short].)

articles.title:
Determination of Thermal Characteristics of Materials, Components
and Assemblies

content.text:
The thermal characteristics of materials shall be determined
by calculation or by testing in accordance with the applicable product
standards listed in the Code or, in the absence of such standards
or where such standards do not address the determination of thermal
resistance, in accordance with

clauses.text: [REF:standard:astmc177] or
[REF:standard:astmc518]

see_also.content:
(See [REF:internal:et001352:long] for the thermal characteristics
of commonly used materials.)

content.text:
Calculations and tests performed in accordance with [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect2.art2.sent1:short] shall be carried out at an average
temperature of 24±2°C (metric) and under a temperature differential
of 22±2°C (metric).

The thermal characteristics of windows, doors and skylights
shall be determined by calculation or testing in accordance with

clauses.text:
[REF:standard:csaa440.2a440.3] for the
reference sizes listed therein, or
[REF:standard:nfrc100] and [REF:standard:nfrc200] for the reference sizes listed therein.

content.text: The effective thermal resistance of opaque [REF:term:bldng]building assemblies shall be determined from

clauses.text: calculations conforming to [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect2.art4:long], or
laboratory tests performed in accordance with [REF:standard:astmc1363] using an indoor air temperature of 21±1°C (metric) and an outdoor air temperature of –18±1°C (metric).

content.text:
The thermal characteristics of log walls shall be determined
by calculation in accordance with [REF:external:icc400]Section
305 of 
                           [REF:standard:icc400] (See [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.appnote220:short].)

articles.title: Calculation of Ceiling, Wall, Fenestration and Door Areas

content.text:
The gross ceiling or roof area shall be calculated as the sum
of the interior surface areas of insulated ceiling and/or roof assemblies
and of skylight openings.

Except as permitted by [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect2.art3.sent3:short], the gross wall area shall be calculated as the sum of the interior
surface areas of all exterior [REF:term:bldng]building envelope
assemblies above the finished ground level that are inclined 60° or
more from the horizontal, including

clauses.text: [REF:term:rm-jst]rim joists,
fenestration and opaque portions of doors,

insulated walls extending from finished ground level to the
interior side of the insulated ceiling and/or roof assembly, and

the exposed areas of below-ground [REF:term:bldng]building envelope assemblies, where fenestration or doors are located below
the plane of the adjacent finished ground.

content.text:
Where a [REF:term:bldng]building of [REF:term:rdntl-cc]residential occupancy contains more than two dwelling units
                            (metric), the gross
wall area enclosing [REF:term:cnd-sp]conditioned space shall
be permitted to include the interior surface areas of walls that enclose
a [REF:term:t]suite, measured from the top surface of the
lowest floor to the underside of the highest ceiling in the [REF:term:t]suite. (See [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.appnote221:short].)

Fenestration and door areas shall be the actual sizes of windows,
doors and skylights including all related frame and sash members.

The fenestration area made of flat panes that are not all in
the same plane or curved panes shall be measured along the surface
of the glass. (See [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.appnote222:short].)

articles.title: Calculation of Effective Thermal Resistance of Assemblies

content.text:
In calculating the thermal resistance of assemblies for the
purpose of comparison with the requirements of [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect2.art6:long]
                           [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect2.art8:long], the thermal bridging effect of closely spaced,
repetitive structural members, such as studs and joists, and of ancillary
members, such as lintels, sills and plates, shall be accounted for.
(See [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.appnote223:short].)

Minor penetrations through assemblies, such as pipes, ducts,
equipment with through-the-wall venting, packaged terminal air conditioners
or heat pumps, shelf angles, anchors and ties and associated fasteners,
and minor structural members that must partially or completely penetrate
the [REF:term:bldng]building envelope to perform their
intended function need not be taken into account in the calculation
of the effective thermal resistance of that assembly.

Major structural penetrations, such as balcony and canopy slabs,
beams, columns and ornamentation or appendages that must completely
penetrate the [REF:term:bldng]building envelope to perform
their intended function, need not be taken into account in the calculation
of the effective thermal resistance of the penetrated assembly, provided

clauses.text:
the insulation is installed tight against the outline of the
penetration, and

the sum of the areas of all such major structural penetrations
is limited to a maximum of 2% of the gross wall area calculated as
described in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect2.art3.sent2:long].

content.text:
Where a component of the [REF:term:bldng]building envelope is protected by an enclosed unconditioned space, such as
a sun porch, enclosed veranda, vestibule or attached garage, the required
effective thermal resistance of the [REF:term:bldng]building envelope component between the [REF:term:bldng]building and the unconditioned enclosure is permitted to be reduced by 0.16 (m2×K)/W (metric). (See [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.appnote225:short].)

Except as provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect2.art5.sent2:short]
                           [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect2.art5.sent10:short] and in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect2.art4.sent3:long] regarding balcony
and canopy slabs, and except for clearances around components required
for fire safety reasons, interior [REF:term:bldng]building components that meet [REF:term:bldng]building envelope
components and major structural members that partly penetrate the [REF:term:bldng]building envelope shall not break the continuity
of the insulation and shall not decrease the effective thermal resistance
at their projected area to less than that required in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect2.art6:long]
                           [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect2.art8:long] (See [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.appnote226:short].)

Where an interior wall, [REF:term:fndtn]foundation wall, [REF:term:frwll]firewall, [REF:term:prt-wll]party wall or structural element penetrates an exterior wall
or insulated roof or ceiling and breaks the continuity of the plane
of insulation, the penetrating element shall be insulated

clauses.text:
on both of its sides, inward or outward from the [REF:term:bldng]building envelope, for a distance equal to 4
times its uninsulated thickness to an effective thermal resistance
not less than that required for exterior walls as stated in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect2.art6.table1:long]
                              [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect2.art6.table2:short],

within the plane of insulation of the penetrated element to
an effective thermal resistance not less than 60% of that required
for the penetrated element, or

within itself to an effective thermal resistance not less than
that required for the penetrated element.

content.text:
Where a masonry fireplace or flue penetrates an exterior wall
and breaks the continuity of the plane of insulation, it shall be
insulated within the plane of insulation of the wall or within itself
to an effective thermal resistance not less than 55% of that required
for the exterior wall as stated in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect2.art6.table1:long]
                           [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect2.art6.table2:short] (See [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.appnote228:short].)

Where an ornamentation or appendage penetrates an exterior wall
and breaks the continuity of the plane of insulation, the penetrating
element shall be insulated

clauses.text:
on both of its sides, inward or outward from the [REF:term:bldng]building envelope, for a distance equal to 4
times the insulated thickness of the exterior wall to an effective
thermal resistance not less than that required for the wall as stated
in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect2.art6.table1:long]
                              [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect2.art6.table2:short],

within the plane of insulation of the wall to an effective thermal
resistance not less than 55% of that required for the exterior wall,
or

within the penetrating element to an effective thermal resistance
not less than that required for the exterior wall.

content.text:
Except as provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect2.art5.sent9:short]
                           [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect2.art5.sent10:short], where two planes of insulation are separated by a [REF:term:bldng]building envelope assembly and cannot be physically
joined, one of the planes of insulation shall be extended for a distance
equal to at least 4 times the thickness of the assembly separating
the two planes. (See [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.appnote229:short].)

Except as provided
in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect2.art5.sent7:short] and [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect2.art11:long], where mechanical, plumbing or electrical
system components, such as pipes, ducts, conduits, cabinets, chases,
panels or recessed heaters, are placed within and parallel to a wall
assembly required to be insulated, the effective thermal resistance
of that wall at the projected area of the system component shall be
not less than that required by [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect2.art6.table1:long]
                           [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect2.art6.table2:long]
                           [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect2.art8.table1:long]
                           [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect2.art8.table2:long] (See [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.appnote230:short].)

The effective thermal resistance of a wall at the projected
areas of plumbing and electrical system components, such as plumbing
vent pipes, conduits, and electrical outlet and switch boxes, need
not comply with [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect2.art5.sent6:short], provided

clauses.text:
the effective thermal resistance at the projected area of the
system component is not less than 60% of that required in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect2.art6:long]
                              [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect2.art8:long], and

the insulation is continuous on the cold side behind the system
component.

content.text:
Except as permitted by [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect2.art11:long], where mechanical
ducts, plumbing pipes, conduits for electrical services or communication
cables are placed within the insulated portion of a floor or ceiling
assembly, the effective thermal resistance of the assembly at the
projected area of the ducts, pipes, conduits or cables shall be not
less than 2.78 (m^{2}×K)/W.

Joints and junctions between walls and other [REF:term:bldng]building envelope components shall be insulated in a manner
that provides an effective thermal resistance that is no less than
the lower of the minimum values required for the respective adjoining
components. (See [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.appnote231:short].)

[REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect2.art5.sent1:short] does not apply where
the continuity of the insulation is interrupted

clauses.text: between the insulation in the [REF:term:fndtn]foundation wall and that of the floor slab,

by an integral perimeter footing of a slab-on-grade (see [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect25.subsect2.art3.sent5:long]
                              [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect2.art8.sent8:long]), or
at the horizontal portion of a [REF:term:fndtn]foundation wall that supports masonry veneer and is insulated on the exterior.

A reduction in the effective thermal resistance of ceiling assemblies

Except for tubular daylighting devices, the minimum effective
thermal resistance values for walls stated in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect2.art6.table1:long]

content.text: Glass block assemblies separating [REF:term:cnd-sp]conditioned space from unconditioned space or the exterior shall have

clauses.text: an overall thermal transmittance of not more than 2.9 W/(m^{2}×K), and
a total aggregate area of not more than 1.85 m^{2}.

content.text: One door separating a [REF:term:cnd-sp]conditioned space from an unconditioned space or the exterior is permitted to have an overall thermal transmittance up to 2.6 W/(m^{2}×K).
Storm windows and doors need not comply with [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect2.art7.sent1:short].
Vehicular access doors separating a [REF:term:cnd-sp]conditioned space from an unconditioned space or the exterior shall have a nominal thermal resistance of not less than 1.1 (m^{2}×K)/W.
Access hatches separating a [REF:term:cnd-sp]conditioned space from an unconditioned space shall be insulated to a nominal thermal resistance of not less than 2.6 (m^{2}×K)/W.
A door separating a [REF:term:cnd-sp]conditioned space from an unconditional space or the exterior is not required to conform to [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect2.art7.sent1:short] if,

clauses.text: in the case of a [REF:term:bldng]building in a location with a heating degree-day value of less than or equal to 3999, the door is one of not more than three nonconforming doors, each of which has an overall thermal transmittance not greater than 2.10 W/m^{2}·K,

in the case of a [REF:term:bldng]building in a location with a heating degree-day value of at least 4000 and not greater than 5999, the door is one of not more than two nonconforming doors, each of which has an overall thermal transmittance not greater than 2.10 W/m^{2}·K,

in the case of a [REF:term:bldng]building in a location with a heating degree-day value of greater than or equal to 6000, the door is one of not more than two nonconforming doors, each of which has an overall thermal transmittance not greater than 2.00 W/m^{2}·K, or
in any case, the door is the only nonconforming door and has an overall thermal transmittance not greater than 2.60 W/m^{2}·K.

content.text: A [REF:term:bldng]building described in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect2.art7.sent9.clause1:long] or [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect2.art7.sent9.clause2:short] is permitted to have an additional nonconforming door with an overall thermal transmittance not greater than 2.10 W/m^{2}·K if the effective thermal resistance of the ceilings of the [REF:term:bldng]building is at least 0.88 m^{2}·K/W greater than the relevant value shown in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect2.art6.table1:long] or [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect2.art6.table2:long], as applicable.

For [REF:term:bldng]buildings described in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect1.art3.sent6:long], fenestration shall have an overall thermal transmittance (U-value) not greater than the values listed in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect2.art7.table4:long] for the applicable heating-degree day category.
