content.text:
Where an entire floor assembly falls into two of the categories listed in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect2.art8.table1:long]
                           [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect2.art8.table2:long]
                           [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect2.art8.table3:long], the more stringent value shall apply. (See [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.appnote239:short].)

Where the top of a section of [REF:term:fndtn]foundation wall is on average less than 600 mm (metric) above the adjoining ground level, the above-ground portion of that section of wall shall be insulated to the effective thermal resistance required in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect2.art8.table1:long]
                           [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect2.art8.table2:long]
                           [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect2.art8.table3:long].

Unheated floors-on-ground that are above the frost line and
have no embedded heating pipes, cables or ducts shall be insulated
to the effective thermal resistance required in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect2.art8.table1:long]
                           [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect2.art8.table2:long]

clauses.text: on the exterior of the [REF:term:fndtn]foundation wall down to the footing, or
on the interior of the [REF:term:fndtn]foundation wall and, as applicable,

subclauses.text:
beneath the slab for a distance not less than 1.2 m (metric) horizontally or vertically down from its perimeter with a thermal
break along the edge of the slab that meets at least 50% of the required
thermal resistance,
on top of the slab for a distance not less than 1.2 m (metric) horizontally from its perimeter, or

within the wooden sleepers below the floor for a distance not
less than 1.2 m (metric) horizontally from its perimeter.

content.text:
Except as provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect2.art8.sent6:short], floors-on-ground with embedded heating ducts, cables or pipes shall be insulated to the effective thermal resistance required in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect2.art8.table1:long]
                           [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect2.art8.table2:long]
                           [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect2.art8.table3:long] under their full bottom surface including the edges.

Where only a portion of a floor-on-ground has embedded heating ducts, cables or pipes, that heated portion shall be insulated to the effective thermal resistance required in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect2.art8.table1:long]
                           [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect2.art8.table2:long]
                           [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect2.art8.table3:long] under its full bottom surface to 1.2 m (metric) beyond its perimeter including exterior edges if applicable.

In addition to the requirements stated in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect2.art8.sent5:short]
                           [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect2.art8.sent6:short], heated floors-on-ground shall be insulated to the effective thermal resistance required in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect2.art8.table1:long]
                           [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect2.art8.table2:long]
                           [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect2.art8.table3:long] vertically

clauses.text: around their perimeter, or
on the outside of the [REF:term:fndtn]foundation wall, extending down to the level of the bottom of the floor.

content.text:
Floors on permafrost shall be insulated to the effective thermal resistance required in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect2.art8.table1:long]
                           [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect2.art8.table2:long]
                           [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect2.art8.table3:long] under the entire slab and around all edges, and under the integral perimeter footing.
Slabs-on-grade with an integral perimeter footing shall

clauses.text:
be insulated to the effective thermal resistance required in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect2.art8.table1:long]
                              [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect2.art8.table2:long]
                              [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect2.art8.table3:long] under the entire slab and around all edges, but not under the integral perimeter footing, and
be constructed with skirt insulation having the same effective thermal resistance as the insulation installed under the slab.

content.text:
Junctions between below-[REF:term:grade]grade assemblies
shall be protected from the ingress of [REF:term:l]soil gas in conformance with [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect25.subsect3:long]

The leakage of air into and out of [REF:term:cnd-sp]conditioned
spaces shall be controlled by constructing

clauses.text:
a continuous [REF:term:r-brrr]air barrier system in
accordance with [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect2.art9.sent2:short]
                              [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect2.art9.sent6:short], [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect25.subsect3:long] and [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect2.art10:long],

a continuous [REF:term:r-brrr]air barrier system in
accordance with [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect2.art9.sent2:short]
                              [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect2.art9.sent6:short] and [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect25.subsect3:long] and a [REF:term:bldng]building assembly having an air leakage rate not greater than 0.20 L/(s×m2) (metric) (Type A4) when tested in accordance
with [REF:standard:ulcs742] at a pressure
differential of 75 Pa (metric), or

a continuous [REF:term:r-brrr]air barrier system in
accordance with [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect2.art9.sent2:short]
                              [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect2.art9.sent6:short] and [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect25.subsect3:long] and a [REF:term:bldng]building assembly having an air leakage rate not greater than 0.20 L/(s·m2) (metric) when tested in accordance with [REF:standard:astme2357] where

subclauses.text:
the [REF:term:bldng]building will not be subjected
to sustained wind loads calculated based on a 1-in-50 hourly wind
pressure that exceed 0.65 kPa (metric), and

the air barrier assembly is installed on the warm side of the
thermal insulation of the opaque [REF:term:bldng]building assembly.

content.text:
An [REF:term:r-brrr]air barrier system installed
to meet the requirements of [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect2.art9.sent1:short] shall be continuous

clauses.text: across construction, control and expansion joints,
across junctions between different [REF:term:bldng]building materials and assemblies, and
around penetrations through all [REF:term:bldng]building assemblies.

content.text:
Windows, doors and skylights and their components shall comply
with the minimum air leakage requirements stated in

clauses.text: [REF:standard:csa101a440] (Harmonized Standard), and
[REF:standard:csaa440S1]

content.text:
Vehicular access doors that separate heated garages from unconditioned
spaces or the exterior shall be weatherstripped around their perimeter
to prevent air leakage.

Fireplaces shall be equipped with doors, enclosures or devices
to restrict air movement through the [REF:term:chmn]chimney when the fireplace is not in use. (See [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.appnote243:short].)

Where the airtight material used in the [REF:term:r-brrr]air barrier system is installed toward the exterior of the [REF:term:bldng]building envelope, its location and properties
shall conform to [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect25.subsect5:long] (See [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.appnote244:short].)

Materials intended to provide the principal resistance to air
leakage shall conform to [REF:standard:ulcs741]

see_also.content:
(See [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.appnote152:long] for air leakage characteristics
and water vapour permeance values for a number of common materials.)

content.text: Materials referred to in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect2.art10.sent1:short] shall be

clauses.text: compatible with adjoining materials, and
free of holes and cracks.

content.text:
Where the [REF:term:r-brrr]air barrier system consists
of rigid panel-type material, all joints shall be sealed. (See [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.appnote245:long].)

Where the [REF:term:r-brrr]air barrier system consists
of timber logs, all joints shall be sealed to resist airflow through
gaps between logs that have shifted due to in-service conditions such
as shrinkage and settling.

Where the [REF:term:r-brrr]air barrier system consists
of flexible sheet material, all joints shall be

clauses.text: lapped not less than 50 mm (metric),
sealed (see [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.appnote245:short]), and
structurally supported.

content.text: Sealant material used for the purpose of creating a continuous [REF:term:r-brrr]air barrier system shall

clauses.text: be a non-hardening type, or
conform to

subclauses.text: [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect27.subsect4:long],
[REF:standard:ulcs710.1] or
[REF:standard:ulcs711.1]

content.text:
Penetrations by electrical wiring, outlets, switches or recessed
light fixtures through the plane of airtightness shall be constructed
airtight

clauses.text:
where the component is designed to provide a seal against air
leakage, by sealing the component to the air barrier material (see [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.appnote246:short]), or

where the component is not designed to provide a seal against
air leakage, by covering the component with an air barrier material
and sealing it to the adjacent air barrier material.

content.text:
The joints between the [REF:term:fndtn]foundation wall and the sill plate, between the sill plate and [REF:term:rm-jst]rim joist, between the [REF:term:rm-jst]rim joist and the subfloor material, and between the subfloor
material and the bottom plate of the wall above shall be constructed
airtight by

clauses.text:
sealing all joints and junctions between the structural components,
or

covering the structural components with an air barrier material
and sealing it to the adjacent air barrier material.

content.text:
The interfaces between windows, doors and skylights and wall/ceiling
assemblies shall be constructed airtight by sealing all joints and
junctions between the air barrier material in the wall and the window,
door or skylight frame. (See [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.appnote247:short].) (See also [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect7.subsect6:long])

Cantilevered floors and floors over unheated spaces or over
the exterior shall be constructed airtight by one of the following
methods or a combination thereof:

clauses.text:
sealing all joints and junctions between the structural components,
or

covering the structural components with an air barrier material
and sealing it to the adjacent air barrier material.

content.text:
Interior walls that meet exterior walls or ceilings whose plane
of airtightness is on the interior of the [REF:term:bldng]building envelope and knee walls that separate [REF:term:cnd-sp]conditioned
space from unconditioned space shall be constructed airtight
by

clauses.text: sealing all junctions between the structural components,

covering the structural components with an air barrier material
and sealing it to the adjacent air barrier material, or

maintaining the continuity of the [REF:term:r-brrr]air barrier
system above or through the interior wall or below or through
the knee wall, as applicable.

content.text:
Steel-lined [REF:term:chmn]chimneys that penetrate
the [REF:term:bldng]building envelope shall be constructed
airtight by blocking the void between required clearances for metal [REF:term:chmn]chimneys and surrounding construction with sheet
metal and sealant capable of withstanding high temperatures.

[REF:term:mnr-r-cn]Masonry or concrete chimneys that
penetrate the [REF:term:bldng]building envelope shall be
constructed airtight by mechanically fastening a metal flange or steel
stud that extends not less than 75 mm (metric) out from the [REF:term:chmn]chimney and sealing the air barrier material to
it with a sealant capable of withstanding high temperatures.

Ducts that penetrate the [REF:term:bldng]building envelope shall be constructed airtight by sealing the penetration
through the [REF:term:bldng]building envelope. (See [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.appnote248:short].)
Plumbing vent stack pipes that penetrate the [REF:term:bldng]building envelope shall be constructed airtight by

clauses.text:
sealing the air barrier material to the vent stack pipe with
a compatible sealant or sheathing tape, or

installing a rubber gasket or prefabricated roof flashing at
the penetration of the plane of airtightness then sealing it and mechanically
fastening it to the top plate.

content.text:
Where a [REF:term:prt-wll]party wall meets the plane
of airtightness, that junction shall be constructed airtight by sealing
any voids within the [REF:term:prt-wll]party wall at the
perimeter to the adjacent air barrier material and by

clauses.text: sealing all junctions between the structural components, or

covering the structural components with an air barrier material
and sealing it to the adjacent air barrier material.

content.text:
Where the concrete in a flat insulating concrete form wall acts
as the air barrier, the continuity of the plane of airtightness shall
be maintained between the concrete and adjacent air barrier materials.

articles.title:
Trade-off Options for Above-ground Building Envelope Components
and Assemblies

content.text:
Subject to the limitations stated in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect2.art11.sent6:short]
                           [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect2.art11.sent8:short], the trade-off options described in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect2.art11.sent2:short]
                           [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect2.art11.sent4:short] apply only to above-ground [REF:term:bldng]building envelope components and assemblies,
or portions thereof, of a single [REF:term:bldng]building.

The effective thermal resistance of one or more above-ground
opaque [REF:term:bldng]building envelope assemblies is
permitted to be less than that required in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect2.art6:long], provided

clauses.text:
the total areas of all proposed and reference assemblies are
equal,

the effective thermal resistance of one or more other proposed
above-ground opaque [REF:term:bldng]building envelope assembly
areas is increased to more than that required by [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect2.art6:long], and

the sum of the areas of all traded above-ground opaque [REF:term:bldng]building envelope assemblies divided by their
respective effective thermal resistance is less than or equal to what
it would be if all assemblies complied with [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect2.art6:long]

content.text:
The effective thermal resistance of one or more windows, as
calculated in accordance with [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect2.art11.sent5:short], is permitted to be less than that required in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect2.art7:long], provided

clauses.text: the total areas of all traded windows are equal,
the traded windows are located in the same orientation,

the effective thermal resistance of one or more other windows
is increased to more than that required by [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect2.art7:long], and

the sum of the areas of all traded windows divided by their
respective effective thermal resistance is less than or equal to what
it would be if all windows complied with [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect2.art7:long]

content.text:
The effective thermal resistance of one or more portions of
floor insulation or ceiling insulation in attics under sloped roofs
in [REF:term:bldng]buildings that are one [REF:term:tr]storey in [REF:term:bldng-hg]building height is
permitted to be less than that required in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect2.art6:long], provided

clauses.text:
the total area of fenestration, excluding skylights, and doors
does not exceed 15% of the above-ground gross wall area as calculated
in accordance with [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect2.art3:long],

the floor-to-ceiling height measured from the top of the subfloor
to the underside of the finished ceiling of the [REF:term:tr]storey does not exceed 2.34 m (metric),

the distance measured from the top of the subfloor to the underside
of the bottom chord of the truss or joist of the roof is not more
than 2.39 m (metric), and

the difference between the sum of the proposed areas of ceilings
or floors divided by their respective proposed effective thermal resistance
and the sum of the reference areas of ceilings or floors divided by
their respective thermal resistance required in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect2.art6:long] is not more than the difference between 17% fenestration
and door area and the proposed fenestration and door areas divided
by the required effective thermal resistance values for windows and
doors in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect2.art7:long]

content.text: The effective thermal resistance of windows shall be determined as RSI = 1/U-value.

The reduction in effective thermal resistance of above-ground
opaque [REF:term:bldng]building envelope assemblies permitted
by [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect2.art11.sent2:short]
                           [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect2.art11.sent4:short] shall result in an RSI
value that is not less than

clauses.text:
55% of that required in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect2.art6:long] for above-ground
walls and joist-type roofs (see [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.appnote254:short]), and

60% of that required in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect2.art6:long] for other
opaque assemblies.

content.text:
The effective thermal resistances of above-ground opaque assemblies
with embedded heating cables, pipes or membranes are not permitted
to be traded.

The effective thermal resistances of doors and access hatches
described in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect2.art7.sent3:long]
                           [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect2.art7.sent7:short] are not permitted to
be traded.

This Subsection is concerned with the efficient use of energy
by systems and equipment used for heating, ventilating and air-conditioning
(HVAC).

Where HVAC systems, equipment or techniques other than those
described in this Subsection are used, the [REF:term:bldng]building shall be designed and constructed in accordance with the energy
efficiency requirements of the [REF:standard:nrcc-necb].

HVAC systems shall be sized in accordance with good practice
as described in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect32:long]
                           [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect33:long] (See [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.appnote255:short].)

Ducts shall be designed and installed in accordance with [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect32:long]
                           [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect33:long] (See [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.appnote256:short].)

Except for [REF:term:xht-dct]exhaust ducts leading
directly to the exterior, ducts and [REF:term:plnm]plenums carrying conditioned air and located outside the plane of insulation
shall

clauses.text:
except as provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect3.art2.sent4:short], have all joints sealed against air infiltration and exfiltration
with

subclauses.text:
sealants or gaskets made from liquids, mastics or heat-applied
materials,
mastic with embedded fabric, or
foil-faced butyl tape, and

clauses.text: except as provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect3.art2.sent5:short], be insulated to the same level as required in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect2:long] for exterior above-ground walls.

content.text:
Fabric-backed tape with rubber adhesives shall not be used as
a primary sealant to meet the requirements of [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect3.art2.sent3.clause1:medium].

The underside of rectangular ducts installed under an insulated
floor over an unconditioned space is permitted to be insulated to
a lower level than required in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect3.art2.sent3:short] but not to less than 2.11 (m2×K)/W (metric),
provided both sides of such ducts are insulated to a compensating
higher thermal resistance so that the resulting heat loss does not
exceed that of ducts complying with [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect3.art2.sent3:short]. (See [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.appnote257:short].)

Except as provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect3.art3.sent3:short]
                           [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect3.art3.sent4:short], every duct or opening intended to discharge air to
the outdoors shall be equipped with

clauses.text: a motorized damper, or
a gravity- or spring-operated backflow damper.

content.text:
Except as provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect3.art3.sent3:short]
                           [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect3.art3.sent4:short] and except in locations with fewer than 3500 heating
degree-days as listed in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.appendixC:long], every outdoor
air intake duct or opening shall be equipped with a motorized damper
that remains in the “open” position if the damper fails.

Where other regulations are in effect that do not permit dampers,
air intakes and outlets need not comply with [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect3.art3.sent1:short]
                           [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect3.art3.sent2:short].

Air intakes and outlets serving HVAC systems that are required
to operate continuously need not comply with [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect3.art3.sent1:short]
                           [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect3.art3.sent2:short]. (See [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.appnote258:short].)

articles.title: Piping for Heating and Cooling Systems

content.text:
Piping for heating and cooling systems shall be designed and
installed in accordance with [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect33.subsect8:long] (See [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.appnote245:long].)

Except for high-temperature refrigerant piping, all piping forming
part of a heating or air-conditioning system shall be located

clauses.text: inside the plane of insulation, or

within or outside the plane of insulation, provided the piping
is insulated to a thermal resistance not less than that required in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect2:long] for exterior above-ground walls.

articles.title: Equipment for Heating and Air-conditioning Systems

content.text:
Equipment for heating and air-conditioning systems shall be
located

clauses.text: inside the plane of insulation, or

outdoors or in an unconditioned space, provided the equipment
is designated by the manufacturer for such installation.

content.text:
Except for manually fuelled solid-fuel-fired [REF:term:pplnc]appliances, the supply of heating and cooling energy to each [REF:term:dwllng-n]dwelling unit, [REF:term:t]suite or common space shall be controlled by thermostatic controls that
activate the appropriate supply when the temperature in a [REF:term:cnd-sp]conditioned space fluctuates ±0.5°C (metric) from the set-point temperature for that space.

Where heating and cooling systems are controlled by separate
thermostatic controls, means shall be provided to prevent these controls
from simultaneously calling for heating and cooling.

Space temperature control devices used to control unitary electric
 resistance [REF:term:pc-htr]space heaters shall conform
to [REF:standard:csac828]

Controls required by [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect3.art6.sent1:short] shall be designed such that lowering the set-point temperature
on the thermostat for the heating system will not cause cooling energy
to be expended to reach the lowered setting, and raising the set-point
temperature on the thermostat for the cooling system will not cause
heating energy to be expended to reach the raised setting.

Automatic devices or manually operated dampers, valves or switches
shall be provided, as appropriate for the heating system used, to
allow the heating of each zone to be adjusted.

Heat pumps equipped with supplementary heaters shall incorporate
controls to prevent supplementary heater operation when the heating
load can be met by the heat pump alone, except during defrost cycles.

Heat pumps with a programmable thermostat shall be equipped
with setback controls that will temporarily suppress electrical back-up
or adaptive anticipation of the recovery point, in order to prevent
the activation of supplementary heat during the heat pump's recovery.
(See [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.appnote262:short].)

Where an HVAC system is equipped with a means for adding moisture
to maintain specific humidity levels, an automatic humidity control
device shall be provided.

articles.title:
Heat Recovery from Dehumidification in Spaces with an Indoor
Pool or Hot Tub

content.text:
Except as provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect3.art8.sent2:short]
                           [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect3.art8.sent3:short], spaces containing an indoor pool or hot tub shall
be equipped with air exhaust systems conforming to [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect3.art8.sent4:short] at design conditions. (See also [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect25.subsect4.art2:long])

Spaces containing an indoor pool need not comply with [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect3.art8.sent1:short], provided a stationary mechanical
or desiccant dehumidification system is installed that provides at
least 80% of the dehumidification that would result from compliance
with [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect3.art8.sent1:short].

Spaces containing an indoor pool or hot tub having a total water
surface area of less than 10 m2
                            (metric) need not
comply with [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect3.art8.sent1:short], provided they
are equipped with a cover having a nominal thermal resistance not
less than 2.1 (m2×K)/W (metric).
Heat-recovery systems used to meet the requirements of [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect3.art8.sent1:short] shall

clauses.text:
be capable of recovering at least 40% of the sensible heat from
exhausted air when tested in accordance with [REF:standard:ahri1060] (see [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.appnote264:short]), or
have a sensible-heat-recovery efficiency complying with [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect3.art9.sent3:long] when tested in accordance with [REF:standard:csac439]

The sensible heat, in kW, referred to in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect3.art8.sent4.clause1:medium], which is the sensible heat content

content.text:
This Article applies where a self-contained mechanical ventilation
system is installed whose principal exhaust component is equipped
with heat-recovery capability. (See [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.appnote265:short].)

Where an integrated mechanical system (IMS) with a heat-recovery
ventilator provides the principal exhaust ventilation, the IMS shall

clauses.text: be tested in accordance with [REF:standard:csap.10] and

have a minimum overall thermal performance factor conforming
to [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect3.art10.table1:long]

content.text:
When tested in conformance with the low-temperature thermal
and ventilation test methods described in [REF:standard:csac439] heat-recovery ventilators described in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect3.art9.sent1:short] shall have a sensible heat-recovery
efficiency of

clauses.text:
at least 60% at an outside air test temperature of 0°C for locations
with a 2.5% January design temperature greater than or equal to –10°C,
and

at least 60% at an outside air test temperature of 0°C and at
least 55% at an outside air test temperature of –25°C for locations
with a 2.5% January design temperature less than –10°C.

content.text:
The requirements of [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect3.art9.sent3:short] shall
be met using a principal ventilation rate not less than that required
in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect32:long] (See [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.appnote266:long].)

HVAC equipment and components shall comply with the performance
requirements stated in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect3.art10.table1:long] (See [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.appnote267:short].)

content.text: Natural gas and propane fireplaces shall be

clauses.text: direct-vent (sealed), and

pilot-on-demand, interrupted or intermittent ignition systems
without a standing pilot light.

content.text:
The heat source component of combined space- and service water
heating systems that are not within the scope of [REF:standard:csap.9] shall meet the performance requirements
stated in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect3.art10.table1:long] for the applicable equipment
type. (See [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.appnote268:short].)

Space-heating systems that use solar thermal technology shall
conform to the manufacturer's design requirements and installation
procedures.

Service water heating systems that use solar thermal technology
shall be installed in accordance with the [REF:standard:nrcc-npc].

Hot water storage tanks associated with the systems referred
to in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect3.art11.sent2:short] shall be installed
in a [REF:term:cnd-sp]conditioned space.

This Subsection is concerned with the efficient use of energy
by systems used to heat service water for household use as well as
for indoor pools and hot tubs.

Where service water heating equipment or techniques other than
those described in this Subsection are used, the [REF:term:bldng]building shall be designed and constructed in accordance with
the energy efficiency requirements of the [REF:standard:nrcc-necb].

[REF:term:rvc-wtr-]Service water heaters, [REF:term:blr]boilers, pool heaters and storage tanks shall comply
with the performance requirements stated in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect4.art2.table1:long] (See [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.appnote269:short].)

Hot service water storage tanks not listed in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect4.art2.table1:long] shall be covered with insulation having a minimum
thermal resistance of 1.8 (m2×K)/W (metric).

content.text:
Except for components that are required to be installed outdoors,
service water heating equipment shall be installed in a [REF:term:cnd-sp]conditioned space. (See [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.appnote270:short].)

Service water heating systems that use solar thermal technology
shall conform to the manufacturer's design requirements and installation
procedures.

Service water heating systems that use solar thermal technology
shall be installed in accordance with the Book II (Plumbing Systems) of this Code.

Hot water storage tanks associated with the systems referred
to in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect4.art3.sent2:short] shall be installed
in a [REF:term:cnd-sp]conditioned space.

The first 2 m (metric) of outlet piping downstream and of
inlet piping upstream leading from a storage tank or heating vessel
shall be covered with piping insulation that is at least 12
mm (metric) thick.

All piping forming part of a continuously operating recirculating
service water heating system shall be covered with piping insulation
that is at least 12 mm (metric) thick.

Where piping forming part of the service water heating system
is located outside the [REF:term:bldng]building envelope
or in an unconditioned space, it shall be insulated to a thermal resistance
not less than the effective thermal resistance required for the exterior
above-ground walls.

Service water heating systems with storage tanks shall be equipped
with automatic temperature controls capable of adjustment between
the minimum and maximum temperature settings permitted for the intended
use.
Heaters for indoor swimming pools shall be equipped with

clauses.text: a thermostat, and

a readily accessible and clearly labeled device that allows
the heater to be shut off without adjusting the thermostat setting.

content.text:
Pumps and heaters for indoor swimming pools shall be equipped
with time switches or other types of controls that can be set to automatically
turn off the pumps and heaters when their operation is not required.
(See [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.appnote271:short].)

This Subsection is concerned with modeling the energy performance
of components, systems and assemblies, including heat gains from internal
loads described in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect5.art4.sent4:long], that are addressed
in the scope of the prescriptive requirements in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect2:long]
                           [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect4:long] and that are installed in [REF:term:bldng]buildings described in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect1.art3.sent3:long].

Internal loads other than those described in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect5.art4.sent4:long] shall be excluded from the performance compliance
calculations as they relate to

clauses.text: the lighting of unconditioned spaces,
exterior lighting, and
the ventilation of unconditioned spaces.

content.text:
For the purpose of this Subsection, the term "reference house" shall mean a hypothetical replica of the proposed house design using the same energy sources for the same functions and having the same environmental requirements, [REF:term:ccpnc]occupancy, climatic data and operating schedules, but made to comply with all applicable prescriptive requirements of [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect2:long]
                           [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect4:long], not including [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect2.art6.table3:long]
                           [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect2.art7.table4:long]
                           [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect2.art8.table3:long]

For the purpose of this Subsection, the term “proposed house”
shall mean a modeled replica of the actual house under consideration,
in which some elements covered in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect2:long]
                           [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect4:long] are specific to the actual house, while other elements not covered
in those Subsections, but that are necessary for the calculation of
the annual energy consumption, are assigned default values.

The performance compliance calculations shall determine the annual energy consumption of the proposed house and the house energy target of a reference house in accordance with (See [REF:internal:en001475:short].)

clauses.text: this Subsection, or
the EnerGuide Rating System, version 15, and [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect5.art3.sent2:short].

content.text: Except as permitted by [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect5.art3.sent7:short], the annual energy consumption of the proposed house in comparison to the house energy target of the reference house shall demonstrate a percent improvement in accordance with Table 9.37.6.3.-G. (See [REF:internal:en001765:short].)

Except for Tables 9.37.2.6.-C, 9.37.2.7.-D, and 9.37.2.8.-C, in establishing the house energy target, [REF:term:bldng]building components, systems and assemblies shall be accounted for in accordance with the prescriptive requirements of Subsections 9.37.2. to 9.37.4. for the climate zone under consideration.

In establishing the annual energy consumption, [REF:term:bldng]building components, systems and assemblies that are addressed in the scope of the prescriptive requirements of Subsections 9.37.2. to 9.37.4. shall be accounted for for the climate zone under consideration.

Where the construction techniques or [REF:term:bldng]building components, systems or assemblies used are more energy-efficient than those prescribed by the prescriptive requirements, the performance compliance calculations are permitted to take this increased performance level into account in the determination of the annual energy consumption, provided it can be quantified and is not dependent on occupant interaction.

Both the proposed and reference houses shall be modeled using the same climatic data, [REF:term:l]soil conditions, operating schedules in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect5.art4:long] and temperature set-points.
For log homes, the annual energy consumption of the proposed house shall not exceed the house energy target of the reference house. (See [REF:internal:en001765:short].)

Except as provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect5.art4.sent2:short], the energy model calculations shall account for the annual energy
consumption of systems and equipment required for

clauses.text: space heating,
ventilation,
service water heating, and
where installed, space cooling.

content.text:
Redundant or back-up equipment for the systems and equipment
listed in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect5.art4.sent1:short] is permitted to
be excluded from the energy model, provided it is equipped with controls
and is not required to meet the space-conditioning load of the house.
(See [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.appnote278:short].)
The schedules used in the energy model shall

clauses.text:
be based on a time interval not greater than one hour, where
the energy model evaluates the  performance of the house over hourly
intervals, or

be applied in an hourly-bin model then averaged, where the energy
model does not evaluate the performance of the house over hourly intervals.

content.text:
The energy model calculations shall account for the loads due
to heat gains from occupants, lighting and miscellaneous equipment, which shall be fixed for
every day of the year, by

clauses.text: following the schedule provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect5.art4.table1:long], and

increasing the loads for each hour by 3.58 W (metric) per
square metre of [REF:term:flr-r]floor area in common spaces,
if applicable.

day the heat gains from the metabolic activity of the occupants and occupant-dependent appliance,
lighting and receptacle electrical loads are present; it does not
account for heat gains from exterior lighting, lighting of unconditioned
spaces, service water heating systems and HVAC equipment.

content.text:
The energy model calculations shall account for the following
space-heating temperature set-points:

clauses.text: 20°C in all living spaces above the [REF:term:bmnt]basement,

19°C in [REF:term:bmnt]basements and common spaces,
and

15°C in crawl spaces intended to be [REF:term:cnd-sp]conditioned
spaces.

content.text:
The energy model calculations shall account for a space-cooling
temperature set-point of 25°C in all [REF:term:cnd-sp]conditioned
spaces served by the cooling system.

The energy model calculations shall account for a thermostatic
control that responds to fluctuations of ±0.5°C from the temperature
set-point. (See [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.appnote279:short].)

If a computer program is used to carry out the compliance calculations,
the calculation methods employed in the energy model shall

clauses.text: be used for both the reference and proposed houses, and

be tested in accordance with [REF:standard:ashrae140] with variations in the computer program from the
range recommended therein reported in accordance with Division C.

content.text:
The proposed and reference houses shall both be modeled using
the same approach and assumptions, except where [REF:term:bldng]building components or energy efficiency features are permitted
by this Subsection to be different.

The energy model calculations shall account for the effect of
airtightness in accordance with [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect5.art10.sent10:long] or [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect7.art3:long], as applicable.

The energy model calculations shall account for heat transfer
through elements separating [REF:term:cnd-sp]conditioned space from unconditioned space, the exterior or the ground.

To calculate the effect of heating and cooling consumption,
the energy model calculations shall be performed using climatic data
measured at time intervals no greater than one hour for one year (8
760 hours) based on the average of at least 10 years of measured data
collected at the weather station nearest to the region in which the
proposed house is located. (See [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.appnote280:short].)

For urban regions with several climatic data sets and for locations
for which climatic data are not available, the energy model calculations
shall be performed using climatic data that best represent the climate
at the [REF:term:bldng]building site.

The energy model calculations shall account for ground reflectance
by

clauses.text:
increasing ground reflectance due to snow cover in a ratio of
30% without snow cover and 70% with snow cover, or

taking into account changes in ground reflectance throughout
the heating season.

content.text:
For each hour of the year, the energy model calculations shall
account for heat transfer through wall assemblies, roof-ceiling assemblies,
including attics where applicable, and exposed floor assemblies due
to the thermal characteristics of the particular assembly and thermal
bridging.
The following [REF:term:bldng]building envelope assemblies and components shall be addressed in the energy model calculations: (See [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect2:long].)

clauses.text: above-ground walls and roof-ceiling assemblies,
floors and walls in contact with the ground, and
doors, windows and skylights.

content.text:
For each wall assembly, fenestration component, roof-ceiling
assembly and exposed floor assembly, the energy model calculations
shall account for

clauses.text: the area of the interior side of the insulated surface,
emissivity, and

the effective thermal resistance or overall thermal transmittance,
as applicable.

content.text:
The energy model calculations shall account for the effect that
each assembly in contact with the ground has on below-[REF:term:grade]grade heat transfer due to

clauses.text: the geometry of the [REF:term:fndtn]foundation,
[REF:term:l]soil conditions (see [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part1.sect3.appnote2:long]), and
the configuration of the insulation.

content.text:
The energy model calculations shall account for heat transfer
through fenestration separating [REF:term:cnd-sp]conditioned spaces from the outdoors, including skylights, while accounting for both
temperature difference and transmission of solar radiation based on

clauses.text: orientation as a function of azimuth and tilt of the surface,
area of frame opening and glazed area,
overall thermal transmittance, and
solar heat gain coefficient.

content.text:
Where the energy model calculations account for the effect of
thermal mass, the contents of the house shall be excluded. (See [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.appnote281:short].)

The energy model calculations shall account for the presence
of thermally active walls, floors and ceilings with embedded conditioning
systems that form part of the [REF:term:bldng]building envelope.

Where skylights are installed in the roof, the gross roof area
shall be determined in accordance with [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect2.art3.sent1:long].
Skylights shall be considered to have no shading.

The energy model calculations shall account for the effects
of exterior permanent and fixed shading only on solar heat gain from
fenestration.

The ratio of fenestration area to opaque area of doors shall
be the same for the proposed and reference houses. (See [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.appnote282:short].)

Each heating system and, where installed, cooling system shall
be accounted for separately in the energy model calculations.

[REF:term:cnd-sp]Conditioned spaces in both the reference
and proposed houses shall be modeled as being

clauses.text:
heated, where only heating systems are provided in the proposed
house,

cooled, where only cooling systems are provided in the proposed
house, or

heated and cooled, where complete heating and cooling systems
are provided in the proposed house.

content.text: The performance requirements stated in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect3.art10.table1:long] shall be used in the energy model calculations.

Where duct and piping losses are accounted for in the energy
model calculations, they shall be included for both the proposed and
reference houses and calculated the same way for both houses. (See [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.appnote284:short].)

The same time periods shall be used in the simulation of the
operation of the ventilation system for both the proposed and reference
houses.

During the heating season, any solar and internal heat gains
that cause an increase in space temperature beyond 5.5°C above the
setpoint shall be

clauses.text: excluded from the energy model calculations, or
calculated as being vented from the house.

content.text:
The energy model calculations shall account for the part-load
performance of equipment, including electrical consumption.

The energy model calculations shall account for the heat-recovery
efficiency of heat-recovery ventilators using a minimum of 2
data (metric) test points derived from testing in accordance with [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect3.art9.sent3.clause1:long]
                           [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect3.art9.sent3.clause2:short], as applicable.

The energy model calculations shall account for the energy consumption
of all service water heating systems.
The performance requirements stated in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect4.art2.table1:long] shall be used in the energy model calculations.

Where piping or standby losses are accounted for in the energy
model calculations, they shall be included for both the proposed and
reference houses, including their effect on space heating and cooling,
and calculated the same way for both houses.

The energy model calculations shall use a supply cold water
temperature, in °C, that is

clauses.text:
equal to –0.002 (HDD) + 20.3 (metric), where HDD <
7 999 (metric),
equal to 4.3, where HDD ≥ 8 000 (metric), or

determined based on the ground and air temperatures in the climatic
data file.

content.text:
Except as provided
in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect5.art8.sent8:short], the energy
model calculations shall use a service water delivery temperature
of 55˚C. (See [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.appnote285:short].)

For hot service
water usage other than for showering, the energy model
calculations shall take into account the service water heating use
schedule presented in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect5.art8.table1:long] using a load of

clauses.text:
97 L/ day (metric) for houses without a [REF:term:scnd-t]secondary
suite, or
65 L/day (metric) for each [REF:term:dwllng-n]dwelling unit in residential [REF:term:bldng]buildings with two or more [REF:term:dwllng-n]dwelling units.

content.title: Default Schedule of Service Water Heating Use

header_rows.content: Distribution of Hourly Draws on Service Water Heating, L/h

body_rows.content:
Each [REF:term:dwllng-n]dwelling
unit in residential [REF:term:bldng]buildings with
two or more [REF:term:dwllng-n]dwelling units (65
L (metric)/day/[REF:term:dwllng-n]dwelling unit)

content.text:
The energy model calculations shall take into account daily
hot service water usage for showering

clauses.text:
at 7 a.m. (metric) for 15 mins (metric) for houses without
a [REF:term:scnd-t]secondary suite, or

at 7 a.m. (metric) for 10 mins (metric) for each [REF:term:dwllng-n]dwelling unit in residential [REF:term:bldng]buildings with two or more [REF:term:dwllng-n]dwelling
units.

content.text:
The energy model shall set the service water delivery temperature
for showering to 41°C at the shower head, with a flow rate of 7.6 L/min (metric).

articles.title: General Requirements for Modeling the Proposed House

content.text:
Except where permitted by [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect5.art10:long]
                           [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect5.art12:long], the energy
model calculations for the proposed house shall be consistent with
the proposed construction specifications for that house with regard
to

clauses.text:
fenestration and opaque [REF:term:bldng]building envelope
assembly type, effective thermal resistance and areas,
HVAC system types and capacities, and
service water heating system types and capacities.

articles.title: Modeling Building Envelope of Proposed House

content.text:
Except as provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect5.art10.sent2:short]
                           [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect5.art10.sent3:short], the energy model calculations for the proposed house
shall be consistent with the proposed construction specifications
for that house with regard to

clauses.text: the area of the above-ground portion of [REF:term:fndtn]foundation walls,

the effective thermal resistance of above-ground walls, ceilings
below attics, roof assemblies and [REF:term:rm-jst]rim joists,

the maximum overall thermal transmittance of doors, as calculated
in accordance with [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect2.art2.sent3:long],
the effective thermal resistance of below-ground walls and slabs-on-ground,

exterior walls, roof-ceiling assembly, doors, walls, exposed
floors, and floors in contact with the ground,

distribution, orientation and area of fenestration and doors,
as calculated in accordance with [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect2.art3:long],

solar heat gain coefficient and overall thermal transmittance
of fenestration, as calculated in accordance with [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect2.art2.sent3:long],

configuration of insulation in assemblies in contact with the
ground, and
effective thermal resistance of [REF:term:fndtn]foundation walls.

content.text:
Except for penetrations, slab-on-ground edge insulation and
assemblies with embedded heating pipes, where a [REF:term:bldng]building envelope component or assembly covers less than 2%
of the total area of the assembly type to which it belongs, its thermal
characteristics are not required to be calculated as belonging to
a distinct assembly, provided the area of the component or assembly
is included in an adjacent assembly having the same orientation (See [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.appnote287:short].)

[REF:term:bldng]Building envelope assemblies with
the same thermal characteristics and orientation are not required
to be calculated as distinct assemblies, provided their area is included
in an adjacent assembly.

[REF:term:bldng]Building envelope assemblies and
components separating [REF:term:cnd-sp]conditioned space from enclosed unconditioned space shall have a solar heat gain coefficient
equal to 0.

Except as stated in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect5.art6.sent9:long], the energy
model calculations for the proposed house shall account for the effects
of exterior permanent and fixed shading devices, including fins, overhangs,
and light shelves, on solar heat gain.

Where thermal mass is included in the energy model calculations
for the proposed house, it shall be set as

clauses.text:
the specified mass up to the inside edge of insulation in exterior
walls, the mass of interior walls, the mass up to the centre-line
of [REF:term:prt-wll]party walls, and the mass of floors,
as applicable,

the specified mass of the [REF:term:bldng]building envelope assembly, where the energy model calculations include a
transient analysis of thermal transfer of the entire [REF:term:bldng]building envelope assembly, or
a default value of 0.060 MJ/(m2×°C) (metric).

content.text:
Exterior walls, roofs and exposed floors shall have a solar
absorptance of 0.4.

The orientation of the [REF:term:fndtn]foundation of the proposed house as constructed shall be within 22.5° of the
orientation used in the energy model calculations.

The airtightness used in the energy model calculations for the
proposed house shall be

clauses.text: 3.2 air changes per hour at 50 Pa (metric) pressure differential with a pressure exponent of 0.67, where the construction complies with [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect25:long],

2.5 air changes per hour at 50 Pa (metric) pressure differential with a pressure exponent of 0.67, where it can be shown that the [REF:term:r-brrr]air barrier
system is constructed in accordance with [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect25.subsect3:long] and [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect2.art9:long]
                              [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect2.art10:long], or

the airtightness
determined in accordance with [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect7.art3.sent1:long] expressed as

subclauses.text:
the number of air changes per hour at 50 Pa (metric) pressure
differential with a pressure
exponent determined through a multi-point test, and
the equivalent leakage area.

content.text:
For compliance
with [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect5.art10.sent9.clause3:medium],
a design airtightness value shall be assigned for use in the energy
model until the actual airtightness has been measured.

articles.title: Modeling HVAC System of Proposed House

content.text:
Where multiple HVAC systems serve a single space, the energy
model calculations for the proposed house shall call each system in
the order of priority established by the system control in the proposed
house.

Where a heat pump is included in the proposed house, the energy
model calculations shall include

clauses.text:
the effect of the source temperature on the heat pump's efficiency,
and
the temperature at which the heat pump shuts down.

content.text:
Permanent supplementary heating systems that are operated by
a thermostat or automatic control shall be included in the energy
model calculations for the proposed house.

The performance characteristics of the heat-recovery ventilation
system of the proposed house shall be as specified at not less than
the principal ventilation rate required for a system designed in accordance
with [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect32:long]

The ventilation system shall be modeled as operating 8 hours
a day at the principal ventilation rate.

The energy model calculations shall determine the required principal
ventilation rate, in L/s, in accordance with [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect32.subsect3.art3:long] based on the number of bedrooms in the proposed house.

The energy model calculations may include duct and piping losses,
taking into account the properties of the specified duct and piping
insulation of the proposed house.

The energy model calculations shall include a heating system
and, where installed, a cooling system sized according to the specifications
for the proposed house.

The energy model calculations shall include the effect of part-load
performance of equipment using

clauses.text:
the same modeled part-load performance data used for the reference
house as per [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect5.art15.sent6.clause1:long],
the default part-load performance characteristics stated in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect5.art15.sent6.clause2:long], or
measured data for the specified equipment.

content.text:
Where a heat-recovery ventilator is installed in the proposed
house, the energy model calculations shall only account for the recovery
of sensible heat using the efficiency ratings in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect3.art9.sent3:long]. (See [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.appnote289:short].)

Except as provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect5.art11.sent12:short], where a forced-air system is installed in the proposed house,
the energy model calculations shall assume the circulation fan operates
when the heating, cooling or principal ventilation system is operating.
(See [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.appnote290:short].)

Where a forced-air system is installed in the proposed house
and where the principal ventilation system in the proposed house is
a separate, fully ducted ventilation system, the energy model calculations
shall assume the circulation fan operates only when the heating or
cooling system is operating.

Where the proposed house contains multiple HVAC systems, the
circulation fan power shall be the sum of the circulation fan power
capacity of each system.
The ventilation fan power consumption shall be modeled

clauses.text:
as being 2.32 W/L/s (metric) for each ventilation fan on
the exhaust side and, where applicable, on the supply side, or
as specified, where a heat-recovery ventilator is used.

content.text:
Where a forced-air system is installed in the proposed house,
the energy model calculations shall determine the flow rate, in L/s,
of the circulation fan in the reference house by multiplying the capacity,
in W, of the heating system in the proposed house by

clauses.text: 0.0604 for heat pumps, and
0.0251 for all other types of heating systems.

content.text:
Where a forced-air system is installed in the proposed house,
the energy model calculations shall determine the minimum electricity
requirement, in W, of the circulation fan by multiplying the flow
rate, in L/s, of the circulation fan in the reference house, determined
in accordance with [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect5.art11.sent15:short], by a
factor of 2.30.

Where a forced-air system is installed in the proposed house,
the flow rate of the circulation fan shall be modeled as being the
larger of

clauses.text:
the flow rate of the circulation fan of the reference house,
determined in accordance with [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect5.art11.sent15:short], or

the flow rate of the circulation fan for the forced-air system
specified in the design for the proposed house.

content.text:
Except as provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect5.art11.sent19:short], where a forced-air system is installed in the proposed house,
the  power capacity of the circulation fan shall be modeled as specified
in the design for the proposed house.

Where the design for the proposed house specifies a forced-air
system with a circulation fan flow rate that is lower than the flow
rate of the circulation fan in the reference house, as determined
in accordance with [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect5.art11.sent15:short], the electricity
capacity, in W, of the circulation fan shall be modeled as being the
larger of

clauses.text:
the electricity capacity specified for the circulation fan in
the proposed forced-air system, or

the minimum circulation fan electricity capacity determined
in accordance with [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect5.art11.sent16:short].

content.text:
For natural gas-, oil-, propane- and wood-burning heating systems,
the energy model calculations shall set the auxiliary electricity
requirements, including that of combustion fans, to those specified
for the proposed house.

articles.title: Modeling Service Water Heating System of Proposed House

content.text:
The service water heating system used in the energy model calculations
shall be sized as specified in the design for the proposed house.
The energy model calculations may include

clauses.text: piping losses, and
drain-water heat recovery, provided

subclauses.text:
the calculation
of the heat recovered is based on the performance of the drain-water
heat-recovery unit specified, as determined in accordance with [REF:standard:csab55.1] using a drain-water
inlet temperature of 35°C, and

where there are
one or two above-ground showers, all of them are served by the drain-water
heat-recovery unit, and where there are more than two above-ground
showers, at least two of them are served by the drain-water heat-recovery
unit.

articles.title: General Requirements for Modeling the Reference House

content.text:
Except as provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect5.art13.sent2:short] and [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect5.art14:long]
                           [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect5.art16:long], the energy model calculations for
the reference house shall be consistent with the prescriptive requirements
of [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect2:long]
                           [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect4:long] with regard to

clauses.text:
fenestration and opaque [REF:term:bldng]building envelope
assembly types and areas,
HVAC system types and capacities, and
service water heating system types and capacities.

content.text:
The energy model calculations for the reference house shall
include the same values as those used for the proposed house with
regard to

clauses.text: [REF:term:flr-r]floor area,
heated volume, and
number and types of rooms.

articles.title: Modeling Building Envelope of Reference House

content.text:
The energy model calculations for the reference house shall
include the same values as those used for the proposed house with
regard to

clauses.text: the gross area of above-ground portion of [REF:term:fndtn]foundation walls,
[REF:term:l]soil conditions,
the orientation of the [REF:term:fndtn]foundation, and
the ratio of fenestration area to opaque area of doors.

content.text: The energy model calculations for the reference house shall use the following values:

clauses.text: 0.060 MJ/(m2×°C) (metric) for thermal mass,
a solar absorptance of 0.4 for the exterior walls, roofs and exposed floors,
0.26 for the solar heat gain coefficient of fenestration,
an airtightness of
the pressure exponent used for the proposed house where this value is less than 0.67, otherwise, 0.67.

content.text:
The effective thermal resistance and overall thermal transmittance
values, as applicable, used in the energy model calculations for the
reference house shall be determined for the applicable heating degree-day
zone in accordance with

clauses.text:
[REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect2.art6.table1:long] for walls, ceilings below attics,
roof assemblies and [REF:term:rm-jst]rim joists,
[REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect2.art7.table1:long] for doors, and
[REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect2.art8.table1:long] for below-[REF:term:grade]grade walls and slabs-on-ground.

content.text:
Except as provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect5.art14.sent5:short]
                           [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect5.art14.sent6:short], the exterior walls, roof-ceiling assembly, doors,
walls, exposed floors, and floors of the reference house that are
in contact with the ground shall have the same area as those of the
proposed house.

The area and orientation of fenestration and doors of the reference
house shall be modeled as being equally distributed on all sides of
the house.

The gross wall area and the area of fenestration and doors of
the reference house shall be determined in accordance with [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect2.art3:long]

Windows and other glazed components in the reference house shall
have a maximum overall thermal transmittance as required in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect2.art7.table1:long] for the applicable heating degree-day category.

The configuration of insulation in assemblies of the reference
house that are in contact with the ground shall be modeled as conforming
to [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect2.art8:long]

[REF:term:fndtn]Foundation walls shall be modeled
using the applicable effective thermal resistance values in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect2.art8.table1:long] and as conforming to [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect2.art8.sent2:long].

The fenestration and door area to gross wall area ratio (FDWR)
of the reference house shall be

clauses.text:
for houses containing 1 or 2 two dwelling units
                               (metric),

subclauses.text:
as per the proposed house, where its FDWR is between 17% and
22%,

17%, where the FDWR of the proposed house is less than 17%,
or

22%, where the FDWR of the proposed house is greater than 22%,
and

clauses.text: for [REF:term:bldng]buildings of [REF:term:rdntl-cc]residential occupancy containing more than 2 [REF:term:dwllng-n]dwelling units,

subclauses.text:
the FDWR determined in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect5.art14.sent10.clause1:short] for the areas determined in accordance with [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect2.art3.sent2:long] and, where the FDWR determined in accordance with the calculation
in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect2.art3.sent3:long] only does not exceed 40%, or

40% of the gross wall area enclosing [REF:term:cnd-sp]conditioned
space where the area of fenestration and doors is greater than
40% of the gross wall area enclosing [REF:term:cnd-sp]conditioned
space determined in accordance with [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect2.art3.sent2:long].

articles.title: Modeling HVAC System of Reference House

content.text:
Where multiple HVAC systems serve a single space, the energy
model calculations for the reference house shall use the same order
of priority as that used for the proposed house. (See [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect5.art11.sent1:long].)

The energy model calculations for the reference house shall
include the same features as those used for the proposed house with
regard to

clauses.text:
the principal heating and cooling energy sources, which are
gas, electricity, oil, propane, wood or a heat pump,

the primary and secondary energy sources, which are gas, electricity,
oil, propane, wood or a heat pump, and
the ventilation rate (see [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect5.art11.sent6:long]).

content.text:
Except as required in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect3.art8.sent1:long], the reference
house shall be modeled without a heat-recovery ventilator.

The ventilation system shall be modeled as operating 8 hours
a day.

The heating system and, where installed, the cooling system
shall be sized in accordance with [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect33.subsect5.art1:long] with
regard to total heat output capacity and nominal cooling capacity.
(See [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.appnote293:short].)

The part-load performance of HVAC equipment in the reference
house shall be calculated using

clauses.text:
modeled part-load performance characteristics, where applicable,
or

the performance values for each type of system multiplied by
an adjustment factor from [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect5.art15.table1:long]
                              [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect5.art15.table2:long]
                              [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect5.art15.table3:long] as follows:

subclauses.text:
for [REF:term:frnc]furnaces, by multiplying the [REF:term:frnc]furnace steady-state efficiency by the adjustment
factor given in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect5.art15.table1:long],

for heat pumps and air conditioners, by multiplying the heat
pump steady-state coefficient of performance by the adjustment factor
given in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect5.art15.table2:long], and

for [REF:term:blr]boilers, combination space-heating
and service water heating systems, and integrated mechanical systems,
by multiplying the net-full-load heating efficiency by the adjustment
factor given in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect5.art15.table3:long].

content.text:
The performance of the HVAC equipment in the reference house
shall be modeled

clauses.text:
as conforming to [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect3.art10.table1:long] for the corresponding
type, fuel source and capacity of equipment in the proposed house,
or

utilization efficiency.

content.text:
Where a heat-recovery ventilator is installed in the reference
house, the energy model calculations shall only account for the recovery
of sensible heat using the efficiency ratings in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect3.art9.sent3:long]. (See [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.appnote295:short].)

The energy model calculations shall assume all ventilation and
circulation fans required to be modeled in the reference house are
equipped with permanent-split capacitor (PSC) motors.

Where a forced-air system is installed in the reference house,
the energy model calculations shall assume the circulation fan operates
when the heating, cooling or principal ventilation system is called
for.

Where the reference house contains multiple HVAC systems, the
circulation fan power shall be the sum of the circulation fan power
capacity of each system.

The principal ventilation flow rate, in L/s, prescribed in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect32:long] shall be multiplied  by 2.32 W/L/s (metric) to determine the ventilation fan power capacity, in W, to be used
in the energy model calculations for each fan on the exhaust side
and, where applicable, on the supply side.

Where a heat-recovery ventilator is required in the reference
house in accordance with [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect3.art8:long], the ventilation
flow rate, in L/s, in the zone served by the pool or hot tub shall
be multiplied by 4.18 W/L/s (metric) to determine the heat-recovery
ventilator power, in W, to be used in the energy model calculations.

Where a forced-air system is installed in the reference house,
the system's capacity, in W, shall be multiplied by one of the following
factors to determine the circulation fan flow rate, in L/s:

clauses.text: 0.0604 for heat pumps, and
0.0251 for all other types of heating systems.

content.text:
Where a forced-air system is installed in the reference house,
the circulation fan flow rate, in L/s, shall be multiplied by 2.30 W/L/s (metric) to determine the circulation fan power capacity,
in W.

the energy model calculations shall set the auxiliary electricity
capacity, including that of combustion fans, to 208 W (metric) during operation.

header_rows.content:
[REF:term:fr-rtnc-]Fire-Resistance Rating
                              
                                 [REF:term:fr-rtnc-]Fire-resistance
ratings and [REF:term:stc]STC ratings of wood-frame
construction were evaluated only for constructions with solid-sawn 38 mm × 89 mm (metric) lumber. However, the [REF:term:fr-rtnc-]fire-resistance ratings and [REF:term:stc]STC ratings
provided for 38 mm × 89 mm (metric) wood-frame construction may
be applied to wood-frame constructions with solid-sawn 38 mm
× 140 mm (metric) lumber; in some cases the ratings may be conservative.
Where 38 mm × 140 mm (metric) framing is used and absorptive material
is called for, the absorptive material must be 140 mm (metric) thick. (See [REF:internal:nbc.divB.appendixD.appsect1.subsect2.article1.para2:long] of Appendix D for the significance of [REF:term:fr-rtnc-]fire-resistance
ratings.) The [REF:term:stc]STC ratings may also
be applied to fingerjoined lumber. The [REF:term:fr-rtnc-]fire-resistance
ratings are applicable to constructions using fingerjoined
lumber that has been manufactured with a heat-resistant adhesive (HRA)
in accordance with NLGA special product standard [REF:standard:nlgasps-1] or [REF:standard:nlgasps-3] (See also [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.appnote125:long].)
                              For all [REF:term:fr-rtnc-]fire-resistance ratings, the
given spacing for framing is a maximum value.
                              [REF:table-note:nbc.divBV2.part9.spectables1.table1.note4]

Typical [REF:term:stc]Sound Transmission Class
                              [REF:table-note:nbc.divBV2.part9.spectables1.table1.note2]
                              Sound
ratings listed are based on the most reliable laboratory test data
available for specimens conforming to installation details required
by [REF:standard:csaa82.31] Results of specific
tests may differ slightly because of measurement precision and minor
variations in construction details. These results should only be used
where the actual construction details, including spacing of fasteners
and supporting framing, correspond exactly to the details of the test
specimens on which the ratings are based. For wood- and steel-framed assemblies, if the fasteners
are spaced less than 300 mm o.c. (metric), subtract 1 from the [REF:term:stc]sound transmission class value; if the fasteners
are spaced less than 200 mm o.c. (metric), subtract 2 from the [REF:term:stc]sound transmission class value. Narrower fastener
spacing is not detrimental to the [REF:term:fr-rtnc-]fire-resistance
rating. Assemblies with  [REF:term:stc]sound
transmission class ratings of 50 or more require methods to minimize airborne sound
transmission at electrical boxes and other openings,
and at the junction of intersecting walls and floors, except intersection
of walls constructed of concrete or [REF:term:sld-m-u]solid masonry
units where the masonry joints at the intersection are mortared.
                              Sound ratings are only valid
where there are no discernible cracks or voids in the visible surfaces.
For concrete blocks, surfaces must be sealed by at least 2 coats of
paint or other surface finish described in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect29:long] to prevent sound leakage.

tables.title: Fire and Sound Resistance of Floors, Ceilings and RoofsSee [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.appnote57:long]

header_rows.content:
DescriptionFor assemblies with a ceiling consisting of a single layer
of gypsum board on resilient metal channels to obtain the listed ratings,
the resilient metal channel arrangement at the gypsum board butt end
joints should be as shown in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.appnote57.figure1:long].
                              For assemblies with a ceiling
consisting of 2 layers of gypsum board on resilient metal channels
to obtain the listed ratings, the fastener and resilient metal channel
arrangement at the gypsum board butt end joints should be as shown
in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.appnote57.figure2:long].
                              The [REF:term:fr-rtnc-]fire-resistance
rating and [REF:term:stc]sound transmission class values given are for a minimum thickness of subfloor or deck as
shown. Minimum subfloor thickness required is determined by structural
member spacing (see [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect15.art5.table1:long]). Thicker subflooring
or decking is also acceptable.

[REF:term:fr-rtnc-]Fire-Resistance Rating
                               Sound absorptive material includes
                                     fibre processed from rock, slag, or glass, and
                                    loose-fill or spray-applied cellulose fibre.
                                 To obtain the listed [REF:term:stc]sound transmission class rating, the nominal insulation thickness
is 150 mm (metric) for rock, slag, or glass fibres or loose-fill
cellulose fibre, and 90 mm (metric) for spray-applied cellulose
fibre, unless otherwise specified. Absorptive material will affect
the [REF:term:stc]sound transmission class by approximately
adding or subtracting 1 per 50 mm (metric) change of thickness.
However, no additional [REF:term:stc]sound transmission class value is achieved by adding a greater thickness of insulation than
the depth of the assembly.
                              The [REF:term:fr-rtnc-]fire-resistance rating and [REF:term:stc]sound transmission class values are
based on the spacing of ceiling supports as noted. (See also [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.spectables1.table2.note10:long].) A narrower spacing will be detrimental to the [REF:term:stc]sound transmission class rating, but not to the [REF:term:fr-rtnc-]fire-resistance rating.
                              To obtain the listed rating, fastener type, spacing and penetration
depth for the attachment of gypsum board must conform to [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect29.subsect5:long], and
                                    fastener distance to board edges and butt ends should be
not less than 38 mm (metric), except for fasteners on the butt
ends of the base layer in ceilings with two layers (see [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.appnote57.figure2:long]), 
                                    fasteners are spaced not more than 300 mm o.c., (metric)
                                    
                                    fasteners must
consist of nails or screws when attaching gypsum board to wood members,
and
                                    fasteners must
consist of screws when attaching gypsum board to cold-formed steel
channels or resilient metal channels.
                                 For wood- and
steel-framed assemblies, if fasteners are spaced less than 300
mm o.c (metric)., subtract 1 from the [REF:term:stc]sound transmission
class value; if fasteners are spaced less than 200 mm
o.c. (metric), subtract 2 from the [REF:term:stc]sound transmission
class value. Narrower fastener spacing is not detrimental to
the [REF:term:fr-rtnc-]fire-resistance rating.
                              See [REF:internal:nbc.divB.appendixD.appsect1.subsect2.article1.para2:long] of Appendix D
for the significance of [REF:term:fr-rtnc-]fire-resistance ratings.
