paragraphs.content: The term "percent improvement" expresses the energy performance of the proposed house relative to the reference house in terms of the energy use of the house or building for space heating, hot water and ventilation.

Although the energy model calculation methods of the NECB are permitted to be used, the results of those calculations must reflect the definitions and the requirements related to mechanical energy use intensity and thermal energy demand intensity as set out in Articles 9.36.6.2. and 9.36.6.3., and not the Annual Energy Consumption as required by Part 8 of the NECB.

application_notes.title: Air Leakage Rate in Energy Model Calculations

paragraphs.content: For buildings that conform to the requirements of any of Steps 3 to 5, higher than expected air leakage may require the building design to be altered and the energy model calculations to be repeated. Alternatively, the air leakage rate could be retested after making alterations to the air barrier system to attain the desired air leakage rate.

The terms "reference house" and "proposed house" have the same meanings as in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect37.subsect5:long] and they apply to energy models for both houses and multi-unit residential buildings. The term "house" is used for consistency and is intended to be applied to both houses and buildings within the scope of [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect37.subsect6:long].

The annual gross space heat loss has been selected as a good proxy for heat loss due to building envelope performance. It is readily extracted from building simulation models and correlates well with the combined conductive (through both fenestration and opaque elements) and air leakage losses, while excluding solar and internal gains. The inclusion of ventilation losses is not strictly relevant to building envelope performance, but their contribution to the annual gross space heat loss is generally small and, given that unbalanced ventilation is permitted by the Code and thus may be modeled, disaggregating energy losses due to unintentional air leakage from those due to intentional ventilation can be difficult in most simulation models.

bc_amendments.content:
Encapsulation of Mass Timber Elements
                           
                              Except as provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect1.subsect6.art4.sent3:short]
                                 [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect1.subsect6.art4.sent6:short], [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect1.subsect6.art3.sent4:number]
                                 [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect1.subsect6.art16.sent2:long]
                                 [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect1.subsect6.art17.sent2:long], and [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect1.subsect6.art7:long]
                                 [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect1.subsect6.art12:long], the exposed surfaces of structural
mass timber elements conforming to [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect1.subsect6.art3:long] shall
be protected from adjacent spaces in the [REF:term:bldng]building, including adjacent concealed spaces within wall, floor and roof
assemblies, by a material or assembly of materials conforming to [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect1.subsect6.art4.sent2:short] that provides an [REF:term:ncps-rtng]encapsulation rating of not less than 50 min (metric).
(See [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect9.appnote21:short].)
                           
                           
                              Except as provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect1.subsect6.art11.sent1:long], the material
or assembly of materials referred to in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect1.subsect6.art4.sent1:short] shall consist of 
                              
                                 gypsum board,
                              
                              
                                 gypsum concrete,
                              
                              
                                 
                                    [REF:term:ncmbtbl]noncombustible materials,
                              
                              
                                 materials that conform to [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect1.subsect5.art1.sent2:long]
                                    [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect1.subsect5.art1.sent4:short], or
                              
                              
                                 any combination of the materials listed in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect1.subsect6.art4.sent2.clause1:short]
                                    [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect1.subsect6.art4.sent2.clause4:short].
                              
                           
                           
                              Except as provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect1.subsect6.art4.sent5:short], the exposed surfaces of mass timber beams, columns and arches
within a [REF:term:t]suite or [REF:term:fr-cmprt]fire
compartment need not be protected in accordance with [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect1.subsect6.art4.sent1:short], provided
                              
                                 their aggregate surface area does not exceed 10% of the total
wall area of the perimeter of the [REF:term:t]suite or [REF:term:fr-cmprt]fire compartment in which they are located,
and
                              
                              
                                 the [REF:term:flm-prd-]flame-spread rating on any
exposed surface is not more than 150.
                              
                              (See [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect9.appnote22:short].)
                           
                           
                              Except as provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect1.subsect6.art4.sent5:short]
                                 [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect1.subsect6.art4.sent6:short], the exposed surfaces of mass timber walls within a [REF:term:t]suite need not be protected in accordance with [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect1.subsect6.art4.sent1:short], provided
                              
                                 each exposed surface faces the same direction, and
                              
                              
                                 the [REF:term:flm-prd-]flame-spread rating on any
exposed surface is not more than 150.
                              
                              (See [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect9.appnote23:short]
                                 [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect9.appnote22:short].)
                           
                           
                              The aggregate exposed surface area of mass timber elements within
a [REF:term:t]suite permitted in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect1.subsect6.art4.sent3:short]
                                 [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect1.subsect6.art4.sent4:short] shall not exceed 35% of the total wall area of the
perimeter of the [REF:term:t]suite. (See [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect9.appnote22:short].) 
                           
                           
                              The exposed surfaces of mass timber ceilings within a [REF:term:t]suite need not be protected in accordance with [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect1.subsect6.art4.sent1:short], provided their aggregate area does
not exceed 
                              
                                 10% of the total ceiling area of the [REF:term:t]suite, where the exposed surfaces have a [REF:term:flm-prd-]flame-spread
rating not more than 150, or
                              
                              
                                 25% of the total ceiling area of the [REF:term:t]suite, where 
                                 
                                    the [REF:term:t]suite contains no mass timber walls
with exposed surfaces, and
                                 
                                 
                                    the exposed surfaces of the mass timber ceiling have a [REF:term:flm-prd-]flame-spread rating not more than 75.
                                 
                              
                              (See [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect9.appnote22:short].)

Except as provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect1.subsect6.art4.sent3:short]
                                    [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect1.subsect6.art4.sent9:short], [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect1.subsect6.art3.sent4:number]
                                    [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect1.subsect6.art16.sent2:long]
                                    [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect1.subsect6.art17.sent2:long], and [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect1.subsect6.art7:long]
                                    [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect1.subsect6.art12:long], the exposed surfaces of structural mass timber elements conforming to [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect1.subsect6.art3:long] shall be protected from adjacent spaces in the [REF:term:bldng]building, including adjacent concealed spaces within wall, floor and roof assemblies, by a material or assembly of materials conforming to [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect1.subsect6.art4.sent2:short] that provides an [REF:term:ncps-rtng]encapsulation rating that
                                 
                                    is not less than 50 min (metric) in a [REF:term:bldng]building or part of a [REF:term:bldng]building constructed in conformance with [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect2.subsect2.art48:long] or [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect2.subsect2.art57:number], or
                                 
                                 
                                    conforms to the minimum values stated in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect2.subsect2.art93.table1:long] for the applicable [REF:term:mjr-ccpn]major occupancy and [REF:term:bldng-hght]building height. (See [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect9.appnote21:short].)
                                 
                              
                              
                                 Except as provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect1.subsect6.art11.sent1:long], the material or assembly of materials referred to in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect1.subsect6.art4.sent1:short] shall consist of
                                 
                                    gypsum board,
                                 
                                 
                                    gypsum concrete,
                                 
                                 
                                    
                                       [REF:term:ncmbtbl]noncombustible materials,
                                 
                                 
                                    materials that conform to [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect1.subsect5.art1.sent2:long]
                                       [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect1.subsect5.art1.sent4:short], or
                                 
                                 
                                    any combination of the materials listed in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect1.subsect6.art4.sent2.clause1:short]
                                       [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect1.subsect6.art4.sent2.clause4:short].
                                 
                              
                              
                                 Except as provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect1.subsect6.art4.sent5:short]
                                    [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect1.subsect6.art4.sent7:short], the exposed surfaces of mass timber beams, columns and arches within a [REF:term:t]suite or [REF:term:fr-cmprt]fire compartment in a [REF:term:bldng]building or part of a [REF:term:bldng]building constructed in conformance with [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect2.subsect2.art48:long] or [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect2.subsect2.art57:number] or permitted by [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect2.subsect2.art93:long] to have a 50 min (metric)
                                    [REF:term:ncps-rtng]encapsulation rating need not be protected in accordance with [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect1.subsect6.art4.sent1:short], provided
                                 
                                    their aggregate exposed surface area does not exceed 35% of the total wall area of the perimeter of the [REF:term:t]suite or [REF:term:fr-cmprt]fire compartment in which they are located, and
                                 
                                 
                                    the [REF:term:flm-prd-]flame-spread rating on any exposed surface is not more than 150. (See [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect9.appnote22:short]
                                       [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect9.appnote28:short].)
                                 
                              
                              
                                 Except as provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect1.subsect6.art4.sent5:short]
                                    [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect1.subsect6.art4.sent7:short], the exposed surfaces of mass timber walls within a [REF:term:t]suite in a [REF:term:bldng]building or part of a [REF:term:bldng]building constructed in conformance with [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect2.subsect2.art48:long] or [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect2.subsect2.art57:number] or permitted by [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect2.subsect2.art93:long] to have a 50 min (metric)
                                    [REF:term:ncps-rtng]encapsulation rating need not be protected in accordance with [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect1.subsect6.art4.sent1:short], provided
                                 
                                    all portions of the exposed surfaces
                                    
                                       face the same direction, or
                                    
                                    
                                       are separated by a horizontal distance of not less than 4.5 m (metric), and
                                    
                                 
                                 
                                    the [REF:term:flm-prd-]flame-spread rating on any exposed surface is not more than 150. (See [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect9.appnote24:short]
                                       [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect9.appnote28:short].)
                                 
                              
                              
                                 Except as provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect1.subsect6.art4.sent7:short], the aggregate exposed surface area of mass timber elements within a [REF:term:t]suite permitted in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect1.subsect6.art4.sent3:short]
                                    [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect1.subsect6.art4.sent4:short] shall not exceed 35% of the total wall area of the perimeter of the [REF:term:t]suite. (See [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect9.appnote22:short]
                                    [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect9.appnote28:short].)

                                    [REF:term:ncps-rtng]encapsulation rating need not be protected in accordance with [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect1.subsect6.art4.sent1:short], provided their aggregate surface area does not exceed

bc_amendments.content:
Encapsulation Materials
                           
                              Gypsum‐concrete topping and concrete not less than 38
mm (metric) thick are deemed to have an [REF:term:ncps-rtng]encapsulation
rating of 50 min (metric) when installed on the upper side
of a mass timber floor or roof assembly.
                           
                           
                              Two layers of Type X gypsum board each not less than 12.7
mm (metric) thick are deemed to have an [REF:term:ncps-rtng]encapsulation
rating of 50 min (metric) when installed on a mass timber
element, provided they
                              
                                 are fastened with a minimum of two rows of screws in each layer
                                 
                                     directly to the mass timber element with screws of sufficient
length to penetrate not less than 20 mm (metric) into the mass
timber element that are spaced not more than 400 mm o.c. (metric) and 20 mm (metric) to 38 mm (metric) from the boards' edges,
or
                                 
                                 
                                    to wood furring or resilient metal or steel furring channels
not more than 25 mm (metric) thick spaced not more than 400 mm o.c. (metric) on the mass timber element,
                                 
                              
                              
                                 are installed with the joints in each layer staggered from those
in the adjacent layer, 
                              
                              
                                 are installed in conformance with [REF:standard:astmc840] except that their joints need not be taped
and finished, and
                              
                              
                                 conform to
                                 
                                    
                                       [REF:standard:astmc1396m] or
                                 
                                 
                                    
                                       [REF:standard:csaa82.27]
                                    
                                 
                              
                              (See [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect9.appnote25:short].)

Encapsulation Materials
                              
                                 Gypsum-concrete topping and concrete not less than 38 mm (metric) thick are deemed to have an [REF:term:ncps-rtng]encapsulation rating of 50 min (metric) when installed on the upper side of a mass timber floor or roof assembly.
                              
                              
                                 One layer of Type X gypsum board conforming to [REF:standard:astmc1396m], "Standard Specification for Gypsum Board," or [REF:standard:csaa82.27], "Gypsum Board," not less than 12.7 mm (metric) thick, is deemed to have an [REF:term:ncps-rtng]encapsulation rating of 25 min (metric) when installed on a mass timber element in accordance with [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect1.subsect6.art6.sent6:short].
                              
                              
                                 Two layers of Type X gypsum board conforming to [REF:standard:astmc1396m], "Standard Specification for Gypsum Board," or [REF:standard:csaa82.27], "Gypsum Board," each not less than 12.7 mm (metric) thick, are deemed to have an [REF:term:ncps-rtng]encapsulation rating of 50 min (metric) when installed on a mass timber element in accordance with [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect1.subsect6.art6.sent6:short].
                              
                              
                                 Two layers of Type X gypsum board conforming to [REF:standard:astmc1396m], "Standard Specification for Gypsum Board," or [REF:standard:csaa82.27], "Gypsum Board," each not less than 15.9 mm (metric) thick, are deemed to have an [REF:term:ncps-rtng]encapsulation rating of 70 min (metric) when installed on a mass timber element in accordance with [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect1.subsect6.art6.sent6:short].
                              
                              
                                 Three layers of Type X gypsum board conforming to [REF:standard:astmc1396m], "Standard Specification for Gypsum Board," or [REF:standard:csaa82.27], "Gypsum Board," each not less than 12.7 mm (metric) thick, are deemed to have an [REF:term:ncps-rtng]encapsulation rating of 80 min (metric) when installed on a mass timber element in accordance with [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect1.subsect6.art6.sent6:short].
                              
                              
                                 Installation of the gypsum board described in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect1.subsect6.art6.sent2:short]
                                    [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect1.subsect6.art6.sent5:short] shall be
                                 
                                    fastened with a minimum of two rows of screws in each layer
                                    
                                       directly to the mass timber element with screws of sufficient length to penetrate not less than 20 mm (metric) into the mass timber element that are spaced not more than 400 mm o.c. (metric) and 20 mm (metric) to 38 mm (metric) from the boards' edges, or
                                    
                                    
                                       to wood furring or resilient metal or steel furring channels not more than 25 mm (metric) thick spaced not more than 400 mm o.c. (metric) on the mass timber element,
                                    
                                 
                                 
                                    for multiple layer systems, installed with the joints in each layer staggered from those in the adjacent layer, and
                                 
                                 
                                    installed in conformance with [REF:standard:astmc840], "Standard Specification for Application and Finishing of Gypsum Board," except that, for multiple layer systems, their joints need not be taped and finished. (See [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect9.appnote24:short].)

                                 Group E [REF:term:mjr-occ]major occupancies and [REF:term:strg-grg]storage garages located in a [REF:term:bldng]building or part of a [REF:term:bldng]building classified as a Group A, Division 2, Group C, or Group D [REF:term:mjr-occ]major occupancy within the scope of this Article are permitted to be constructed in accordance with this Article and the corresponding Group A, Division 2, Group C, or Group D [REF:term:mjr-occ]major occupancy requirements contained in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect2.subsect2.art93.table1:long]Table 3.2.2.93., provided

(See Note A-3.2.2.48.(4), 3.2.2.57.(3) and 3.2.2.93.(5) to (7).)
                              
                              
                                 Group F, Division 2 and 3 [REF:term:mjr-occ]major occupancies located in a [REF:term:bldng]building or part of a [REF:term:bldng]building classified as a Group D [REF:term:mjr-occ]major occupancy within the scope of this Article are permitted to be constructed in accordance with this Article and the corresponding Group D [REF:term:mjr-occ]major occupancy requirements contained in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect2.subsect2.art93.table1:long]Table 3.2.2.93., provided they are located below the third [REF:term:tr]storey. bc_amendments.content:
Requirements for Residential Buildings with a Single Exit
                           (See [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect9.appnoteA-3.2.10:long].) (See also [REF:internal:nbc.divA.part1.sect5.appnoteA-3:long].)
                           
                              Application
                              
                                 Except as provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect2.subsect10.art1.sent2:short] to [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect2.subsect10.art1.sent4:short], this Subsection applies to [REF:term:bldng]buildings of only [REF:term:rdntl-cc]residential occupancy that
                                 
                                    are not more than six [REF:term:tr]storeys in [REF:term:bldng-hg]building height,
                                 
                                 
                                    have a height not more than 18 m (metric) measured between the floor of the [REF:term:frt-tr]first storey and the uppermost floor level, excluding any floor level within a rooftop [REF:term:ncls]enclosure that is not considered as a [REF:term:tr]storey in calculating [REF:term:bldng-hg]building height in accordance with [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect2.subsect1.art1.sent1:long],
                                 
                                 
                                    contain not more than four [REF:term:dwllng-n]dwelling units on each floor,
                                 
                                 
                                    does not exceed an [REF:term:ccpnt-ld]occupant load of 24 persons (metric) per floor, and
                                 
                                 
                                    have a [REF:term:trvl-dst]travel distance from
                                    
                                       any part of the [REF:term:flr-r]floor area to an [REF:term:xt]exit not more than 25 m (metric), and
                                    
                                    
                                       each [REF:term:dwllng-n]dwelling unit to an [REF:term:xt]exit of not more than 6 m (metric).
                                    
                                 
                              
                              
                                 This Subsection does not apply to [REF:term:flr-r]floor areas permitted by [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect4.subsect2.art1:long] to be served by one [REF:term:xt]exit.
                              
                              
                                 This Subsection does not apply to detached houses, semi-detached houses, houses with a [REF:term:bc-scnd-t]secondary suite, duplexes, triplexes, townhouses or row houses.
                              
                              
                                 
                                    [REF:term:rdntl-cc]Residential
                                    [REF:term:bldng]buildings with a single [REF:term:xt]exit are not permitted for
                                 
                                    hotels, motels, dormitories or lodging houses,
                                 
                                 
                                    
                                       [REF:term:rdntl-cc]residential clubs, colleges or schools,
                                 
                                 
                                    monasteries,
                                 
                                 
                                    seniors' residences, or
                                 
                                 
                                    care facilities accepted for residential use pursuant to provincial legislation.
                                 
                              
                              (See [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect9.appnoteA-3.2.10.1.4:long].)
                              
                                 This Subsection, in accordance with the application of this Article and in conformance with the provisions of this Subsection and all other applicable provisions of this Code, may be used as an alternate to the requirements for a second [REF:term:xt]exit in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect4.subsect2:long].
                              
                           
                           
                              Building Construction
                              
                                 Notwithstanding the permissions in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect2.subsect5.art12.sent2:short] to [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect2.subsect5.art12.sent4:short], a [REF:term:bldng]building to which this Subsection applies shall be [REF:term:prnklrd]sprinklered throughout with an automatic sprinkler system designed, constructed, installed and tested in conformance with [REF:standard:nfpa13], "Standard for the Installation of Sprinkler Systems." (See [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect9.appnoteA-3.2.10.2.1-2:long].) (See [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect2.subsect4.art1.sent7:long].)
                              
                              
                                 All balconies and decks shall be [REF:term:prnklrd]sprinklered in accordance with [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect2.subsect10.art2.sent1:short]. (See [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect9.appnoteA-3.2.10.2.1-2:long].)
                              
                              
                                 The [REF:term:xt]exit facility shall be constructed either of [REF:term:nncmbst]noncombustible construction or, notwithstanding the application of [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect1.subsect13.art7:long], with finishes that do not exceed the maximum [REF:term:flm-sprd]flame-spread rating and maximum smoke developed classification for [REF:term:xt]exit stairways in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect1.subsect13.art7.table1:long], and shall
                                 
                                    be separated from all other spaces in the [REF:term:bldng]building by a [REF:term:fr-prtn]fire separation having a [REF:term:fr-rtnc-]fire-resistance rating not less than 2 h (metric),
                                 
                                 
                                    be not less than 1 500 mm (metric) wide,
                                 
                                 
                                    discharge directly to the exterior of the [REF:term:bldng]building without passing through a lobby,
                                 
                                 
                                    be designed to limit the probability of storage or the accumulation of material, and
                                 
                                 
                                    have signs posted in conspicuous locations near each landing to indicate that storage is not permitted.
                                 
                              
                              (See [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect9.appnoteA-3.2.10.1.3:long].)
                              
                                 The discharge from the [REF:term:xt]exit stair described in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect2.subsect10.art2.sent3.clause3:long] shall be located not less than 3 m (metric) and not more than 15 m (metric) from the closest portion of the access route required for fire department use, measured horizontally from the face of the [REF:term:bldng]building. (See [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect9.appnoteA-3.2.10.2.4:long].)
                              
                           
                           
                              Limits to Smoke Movement
                              
                                 Except as permitted by [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect2.subsect10.art3.sent3:short] and notwithstanding the scope of [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect2.subsect6:long], a [REF:term:bldng]building to which this Subsection applies that is greater than four [REF:term:tr]storeys in [REF:term:bldng-hg]building height shall be designed in accordance with [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect2.subsect6.art2:long].
                              
                              
                                 Fans required to limit smoke movement by [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect2.subsect10.art3.sent1:short] shall be provided with an emergency power supply capable of operating under full load for not less than 2 h (metric) provided by an emergency generator. (See also [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect2.subsect7.art9:long].)
                              
                              
                                 Pressurization of the stair shaft described in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect2.subsect10.art3.sent1:short] is not required if each doorway from the [REF:term:pblc-crrd]public corridor serving the [REF:term:xt]exit facility is protected with a vestibule on the [REF:term:pblc-crrd]public corridor side of the doorway
                                 
                                    consisting of a [REF:term:cls]closure in the [REF:term:pblc-crrd]public corridor
                                    
                                    
                                       equipped with electromagnetic hold-open devices that release upon activation of the fire alarm system, and
                                    
                                    
                                       that has a [REF:term:fr-prtc-]fire-protection rating not less than a 45 min (metric), and
                                    
                                 
                                 
                                    that forms a space that is separated from the remainder of the [REF:term:bldng]building by a [REF:term:fr-prtn]fire separation with a [REF:term:fr-rtnc-]fire-resistance rating not less than 45 min (metric)
                                    
                                    
                                       that contains no [REF:term:t]suite entry doors, and
                                    
                                    
                                       with the distance from doorway to the [REF:term:xt]exit facility and the [REF:term:cls]closure not less than 1 800 mm (metric) long and a width of the path between doorways not less than 1 500 mm (metric).
                                    
                                 
                              
                              
                                 Elevator hoistways shall not be designed as a means of venting.
                              
                              
                                 The systems for control of smoke movement required by [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect2.subsect10.art3.sent1:short] shall be tested to ensure satisfactory operation. (See [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect2.subsect6.art9.sent1:long] and [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect9.appnoteA-3.2.6.9.1:long].)
                              
                           
                           
                              Doors in Public Corridors and Suite Entry Doors
                              
                                 All doors along [REF:term:pblc-crrd]public corridors and all [REF:term:t]suite entry doors shall be equipped with electromagnetic hold-open devices designed to release upon activation of the fire alarm system in accordance with [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect1.subsect8.art14:long].
                              
                              
                                 Hold-open devices on [REF:term:t]suite entry doors shall not require a force applied to the door or release device of more than 22 N (metric) to allow the occupant to manually release the door from the hold-open position to allow it to close.
                              
                              
                                 
                                    [REF:term:t]Suite entry doors shall have a [REF:term:fr-prtc-]fire-protection rating of not less than 45 min (metric).
                              
                              (See [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect9.appnoteA-3.2.10.4.3:long].)

Adaptable Dwelling Unit Bedrooms
                           
                              At least one bedroom or sleeping space in an [REF:term:dptbl-dwllng-nt]adaptable dwelling unit shall have
                              
                                 a floor area that permits a turning area of not less than 1 700 mm (metric) in diameter, or not less than 1 700 mm (metric) by 1 500 mm (metric), that could be adjacent a bed,
                              
                              
                                 a pathway clearance of not less than 850 mm (metric) wide, that could be unobstructed by a bed, to allow functional use of the bedroom, and
                              
                              
                                 at least one closet that provides
                                 
                                    a clear opening width of not less than 900 mm (metric), and
                                 
                                 
                                    a clear floor space, that need not be separate from the turning areas required in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect8.subsect5.art6.sent1.clause1:short], of not less than 1 700 mm (metric) in diameter or 1 700 mm (metric) by 1 500 mm (metric) on at least one side of the closet. (See Note A-3.8.5.6.(1).)

Adaptable Dwelling Unit Bedrooms
                              
                                 At least one bedroom or sleeping space in an [REF:term:dptbl-dwllng-nt]adaptable dwelling unit shall have
                                 
                                    a floor area that permits a turning area of not less than 1 700 mm (metric) in diameter, or not less than 1 700 mm (metric) by 1 500 mm (metric), that could be adjacent a bed,
                                 
                                 
                                    a pathway clearance of not less than 850 mm (metric) wide, that could be unobstructed by a bed, to allow functional use of the bedroom, and
                                 
                                 
                                    when provided, a [REF:term:clst]closet with
                                    
                                       a clear opening width of not less than 900 mm (metric), and
                                    
                                    
                                       a clear floor space, that need not be separate from the turning areas required in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect8.subsect5.art6.sent1.clause1:short], of not less than 1 700 mm (metric) in diameter or 1 700 mm (metric) by 1 500 mm (metric) on at least one side of the [REF:term:clst]closet. (See Note A-3.8.5.6.(1).)
                                    
                                 
                              
                              
                                 Though the Code doesn't regulate bed furniture or sizes or styles such as bunkbeds, designs should allow for a bed to be located to accommodate transfer from the turning area to either side of the bed, such as by flipping the orientation of the bed, as well as for functional maneuvering space in the room.
                              
                              
                                 A built-in closet is not required by this Code.

3.1.6.4.(1)
                           Encapsulation of Mass Timber Elements
                           The general intent of [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect1.subsect6.art4.sent1:long] is that all exposed surfaces of the mass timber elements be encapsulated,
including the upper surface of a mass timber floor assembly. However,
the exposed surfaces in certain concealed spaces formed by or contained
within mass timber elements are exempted from complying with this
Sentence (see [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect1.subsect6.art3.sent4:long]
                              [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect1.subsect6.art16.sent2:medium]
                              [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect1.subsect6.art17.sent2:medium]
                              [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect1.subsect6.art7:long]
                              [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect1.subsect6.art12:short]). Moreover, the upper
surface of a mass timber roof assembly need not be encapsulated where
there is no concealed space above it. As well, the exterior side of
a mass timber exterior wall assembly need not be encapsulated; however,
the provisions of [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect1.subsect6.art9:long]
                              [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect2.subsect3:long] for exterior walls
still need to be considered.

3.1.6.4.(1)
                              Encapsulation of Mass Timber Elements
                              The general intent of [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect1.subsect6.art4.sent1:long], which generally applies for any building where a 50- or 70-minute encapsulation rating is otherwise required, is that all exposed surfaces of the mass timber elements be encapsulated, including the upper surface of a mass timber floor assembly. However, for some buildings, depending on the building height and occupancy, portions of mass timber elements are permitted to be exposed to varying degrees in accordance with the permissions stated in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect1.subsect6.art4.sent3:long]
                                 [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect1.subsect6.art4.sent8:short]. Also, the exposed surfaces in certain concealed spaces formed by or contained within mass timber elements are exempted from complying with this Sentence (see [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect1.subsect6.art3.sent4:long]
                                 [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect1.subsect6.art16.sent2:medium]
                                 [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect1.subsect6.art17.sent2:medium]
                                 [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect1.subsect6.art7:long]
                                 [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect1.subsect6.art12:short]). Moreover, the upper surface of a mass timber roof assembly need not be encapsulated where there is no concealed space above it. As well, the exterior side of a mass timber exterior wall assembly need not be encapsulated; however, the provisions of [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect1.subsect6.art9:long] and [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect2.subsect3:long] for exterior walls still need to be considered.

bc_amendments.content:
3.1.6.4.(4)
                           Exposed Surfaces of Mass Timber
Walls
                           The primary objective of encapsulating mass timber
elements is to limit the probability that these elements will significantly
contribute to fire spread and fire duration in the event of a fire.
Since thick wood members require a source of imposed heat flux to
burn, the stipulation in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect1.subsect6.art4.sent4.clause1:long] that
the exposed surfaces of mass timber walls face the same direction
within a suite is intended to reduce the potential of re-radiation
between burning mass timber surfaces that face each other, which could
sustain flaming combustion into the decay phase of a fire if the sprinkler
system failed to operate or to control the fire. Additionally, the
maximum percentage of exposed surface area stated in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect1.subsect6.art4:long] is low so that it is not sufficient
to sustain a ventilation-controlled fire that might provide the radiation
required to sustain flaming combustion into the decay phase of a fire
if the sprinkler system failed to operate or to control the fire.

3.1.6.4.(4)
                              Exposed Surfaces of Mass Timber Walls
                              The primary objective of encapsulating mass timber elements is to limit the probability that these elements will significantly contribute to fire spread and fire duration in the event of a fire. Since thick wood members require a source of imposed heat flux to burn, the stipulation in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect1.subsect6.art4.sent4.clause1:long] that any portions of the exposed surfaces of different mass timber walls within a suite either face the same direction or have a minimum horizontal distance between one another. If the sprinkler system fails to operate or to control the fire, this directional orientation or minimum distance is intended to avoid or reduce the potential for re-radiation between portions of burning mass timber surfaces on different walls, and particularly those that either face or are in close proximity to one another, which could sustain flaming combustion into the decay phase of a fire. Additionally, if the sprinkler system fails to operate or to control the fire, the maximum percentages of exposed surface areas and maximum flame-spread ratings stated in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect1.subsect6.art4:long] are intended to be insufficient to sustain a ventilation-controlled fire that might provide the radiation required to sustain flaming combustion into the decay phase of a fire.
bc_amendments.change_summary: Updated to reference Clause 3.1.6.4.(4)(a) and expanded explanation about directional orientation and minimum distance requirements

bc_amendments.content:
3.1.6.6.
                           Encapsulation Materials
                           Research has been conducted on different types of encapsulation materials,
such as gypsum board, gypsum concrete and cement board. The results
of tests using an intermediate-scale furnace and of cone calorimeter
tests indicate that a combustible timber element protected with a 38 mm thick (metric) layer of gypsum-concrete topping or with two layers
of 12.7 mm (metric) Type X gypsum board will not ignite or contribute
significant heat to a fire until average temperatures of 325–380°C (metric) are attained at the interface between the encapsulation material
or assembly of materials and the combustible substrate. These temperatures
are consistent with the ignition temperatures of wood-based materials.

3.1.6.6.
                              Encapsulation Materials
                              Research has been conducted on different types of encapsulation materials, such as gypsum board, gypsum concrete and cement board. The results of tests using an intermediate-scale furnace and of cone calorimeter tests indicate that a combustible timber element protected with a 38 mm (metric) thick layer of gypsum-concrete topping or with one (25 min) (metric), two (50 min) (metric) or three (80 min) (metric) layers of 12.7 mm (metric) Type X gypsum board or two layers (70 min) (metric) of 15.9 mm (metric) Type X gypsum board will not ignite or contribute significant heat to a fire until the time at which average temperatures of 325°C to 380°C (metric) are attained at the interface between the encapsulation material or assembly of materials and the combustible substrate. These temperatures are consistent with the ignition temperatures of wood-based materials.
bc_amendments.change_summary: Updated layer specifications to include specific timing (25 min, 50 min, 80 min, 70 min) and board thickness details (12.7 mm and 15.9 mm Type X gypsum board)

bc_amendments.content:

bc_amendments.content:
3.2.10.
                              Fire Protection and Firefighting Assumptions for Residential Buildings with a Single Exit.
                              The firefighting assumptions discussed in Note A-3 raise circumstances where additional firefighting capabilities and additional building protection measures may be required. The provisions in Subsection 3.2.10. for residential buildings with a single exit were developed with the expectation of a high level of capacity of the local fire department for fire prevention activities, fire suppression activities, the ability of the fire department to assist in egress of occupants in the event of an emergency, as well as a secure water supply for the function of the automatic sprinkler system and the manual fire suppression activities of a responding fire department.
                              
                                 <bold>Fire Prevention</bold>
                              
                              Maintenance of fire safety systems is essential for all buildings but becomes increasingly important when redundancies, such as a second and separate exit, are reduced or eliminated. The provisions for residential buildings with single exit stairs were developed with the expectation that fire officials routinely enforce the British Columbia Fire Code to ensure that the inspection intervals specified within are carried out, and that follow up inspections resulting from observed non-compliances occur at expedited intervals. Building owners and managers are required to be actively involved in carrying out the maintenance and upkeep of the building's fire safety systems. Residential buildings with a single exit should not be located in jurisdictions where a high level of fire prevention oversight cannot be maintained.
                              
                                 <bold>Fire Suppression</bold>
                              
                              The provisions for residential buildings with single exit stairs were developed with the expectation that a permanent, paid fire department is available to respond to a fire event twenty-four hours a day, every day. Firefighting personnel are expected to have a high level of training and the fire department is expected to be suitably equipped to provide fire suppression activities appropriate to the buildings and developments in their jurisdiction within tight response times. Residential buildings with a single exit should not be located in jurisdictions where a high level of fire suppression activities cannot be maintained.
                              
                                 <bold>Egress and Safety of Occupants</bold>
                              
                              The premise of egress in the British Columbia Building Code is that occupants of residential buildings receive early notification of a fire event, and occupants are able to respond unassisted in such an event. Early notification however does not guarantee occupant self-evacuation and when redundancies, such as a second and separate exit, are reduced or eliminated, occupant response options are likewise reduced. The provisions for residential buildings with single exit stairs were developed with the expectation that the local fire department has a service level that can coordinate and assist occupants with moving to a safe place in a fire event. Building owners and managers must be actively involved in fire safety planning in conjunction with the local fire department. Residential buildings with a single exit should not be located in jurisdictions where a service level that includes search and rescue by firefighting personnel cannot be maintained.
                              
                                 <bold>Water Supply</bold>
                              
                              The British Columbia Building Code requires an adequate water supply for firefighting be readily available and of sufficient volume and pressure to enable emergency response personnel to control fire growth so as to enable the safe evacuation of occupants and the conduct of search and rescue operations, prevent the fire from spreading to adjacent buildings, and provide a limited measure of property protection. As for any water-based fire protection systems or suppression activities, the water supply serving the building needs to be dependable over the life of the building through seasonal droughts and other eventualities. The provisions for residential buildings with single exit stairs were developed with the expectation of a highly dependable water supply would be available during construction and throughout the lifecycle of the building. Redundancies such as secondary or back up water supplies should to be considered to limit the probability that the water supply may become insufficient for an extended or even temporary period.
bc_amendments.change_summary: Added Note A-3.2.10 explaining fire protection and firefighting assumptions for residential buildings with single exit stairs

3.2.10.1.(4)
                              Residential Buildings Not Permitted.
                              The residential uses described in Sentence 3.2.10.1.(4) include short term as well as long term accommodations where Subsection 3.2.10. is not permitted to apply. For example, longer-term hotels and rooming houses sometimes referred to as single room occupancy hotels or single room accommodations with or without private bathrooms or kitchens are not permitted to apply Subsection 3.2.10.

3.2.10.2.(1) and (2)
                              Automatic Sprinkler Systems.
                              Automatic sprinkler systems serving a building to which Subsection 3.2.10. applies must be sprinklered in accordance with NFPA 13, "Standard for the Installation of Sprinkler Systems," regardless of the permissions for other buildings to follow the NFPA 13R, "Standard for the Installation of Sprinkler Systems in low-Rise Residential Occupancies," or the NFPA 13D, "Standard for the Installation of Sprinkler Systems in One- and Two-Family Dwellings and Manufactured Homes," standards. All balconies and decks regardless of depth must be sprinklered.
                              The requirement for sprinklers conforming to NFPA 13, "Standard for the Installation of Sprinkler Systems," means that a fire alarm system described in Subsection 3.2.4. is also required.
bc_amendments.change_summary: Added Note A-3.2.10.2.(1) and (2) regarding automatic sprinkler system requirements for buildings under Subsection 3.2.10

bc_amendments.content:
3.2.10.2.(3)
                              Exit Facility.
                              The single exit facility serving a building to which Subsection 3.2.10. applies shall either be of noncombustible construction or shall be finished as an exit stair serving an unsprinklered high building described in Subsection 3.2.6. Should a fire event occur, protection of the exit stairs must not solely rely on the automatic sprinkler system.
                              A 1 500 mm wide exit facility facilitates the movement and passing of people for regular use as well as in an emergency. The design of intermediate handrails, such as for widths exceeding 1 700 mm, should consider the movement of emergency personnel including their equipment on each side. The design of the exit facility must also consider misuse and proactively deter the storage or collection of materials so as not to obstruct passage and to minimize fuel load. For example, excess landing areas and alcoves in all exits (not limited to residential buildings with single exit stairs) must be carefully designed to deter any activities other than exiting and accessing floor areas as per Sentence 3.4.4.4.(6). Void spaces underneath stairs should be avoided. Landings must have signage to remind occupants that storage is not permitted in exit facilities.
bc_amendments.change_summary: Added Note A-3.2.10.2.(3) regarding exit facility design and construction requirements

bc_amendments.content:
3.2.10.2.(4)
                              Exit Facility Discharge.
                              Fire department access to buildings to which Subsection 3.2.10. applies must be provided to the principal entrance as well as to the access point most directly connected to the exit facility. As such, the exit facility discharge must be located to coordinate with the fire department access route described in Subsection 3.2.5.
                              Designers should consider locating the exit facility discharge in close proximity to the principal entrance for the benefit of coordinating multiple access points with the fire department access route but also to avoid unintended use of the exit facility for package delivery or other material drop-off. There should be clear distinction between the principal building entrance (likely connecting to a lobby and elevator) and the exit facility discharge so that activities such as deliveries can be intuitively completed in the safe and intended manner. Locating the exit facility discharge in close proximity to the principal building entrance also reduces the potential that an access point is located in an isolated location of the building which could increase building and occupant security concerns.
bc_amendments.change_summary: Added Note A-3.2.10.2.(4) regarding exit facility discharge location and coordination with fire department access

bc_amendments.content:

                              Suite Entry Doors.
                              Sentence 3.2.10.4.(3) supersedes the permission in Article 3.1.8.12. to reduce the fire-protection rating of closures. Suite entry doors with less than a 45 min fire-protection rating are not permitted in buildings to which Subsection 3.2.10. applies, nor would these doors be permitted any undercuts such as described in Article 9.32.3.10.

As a result of the updating procedure for the 2010 edition of the Code, the 1-in-50 reference
wind velocity pressures remained unchanged for most of
the locations listed in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.appendixC.table2:long]; both increases
and decreases were noted for the remaining locations. Many of the
decreases resulted from the fact that anemometers at most of the stations
used in the previous analysis were installed on lighthouses, airport
hangers and other structures. Wind speeds on the tops of buildings
are often much higher compared to those registered by a standard 10
m tower. Eliminating anemometer data recorded on the tops of buildings
from the analysis resulted in lower values at several locations.

As a result of the updating procedure, the 1-in-50 reference
wind velocity pressures remained unchanged for most of
the locations listed in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.appendixC.table1:long]. However, the reference wind velocity pressures for some locations were
revised to reflect the availability of additional wind data. The reference wind velocity pressures for
locations in British Columbia were revised to reflect the availability of additional wind data and the
use of a different extreme value distribution.

Fire Separations and Smoke-tight Barriers between Rooms and
Spaces within Buildings
                        
                           Application
                           
                              This Subsection applies to
                              
                                 
                                    [REF:term:fr-prtn]fire separations required between rooms and spaces in [REF:term:bldng]buildings, except between rooms and spaces within a [REF:term:dwllng-n]dwelling unit, and
                              
                              
                                 reserved.
                              
                           
                        
                        
                           Continuous Barrier
                           
                              Except as permitted in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect10.subsect9.art3:long], a wall or
floor assembly required to be a [REF:term:fr-prtn]fire separation  shall be constructed as a continuous barrier against the spread
of fire and retard the passage of smoke.
                           
                           
                              Reserved.
                           
                           
                              Except as provided
in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect10.subsect9.art2.sent6:short], the continuity of a [REF:term:fr-prtn]fire separation where it abuts another [REF:term:fr-prtn]fire separation, a floor,
a ceiling, or a roof shall be maintained by a [REF:term:fr-tp]firestop that, when subjected to the fire test method in [REF:standard:ulcs115] has an FT rating
not less than the [REF:term:fr-rtnc-]fire-resistance rating for the abutting [REF:term:fr-prtn]fire separation. (See [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.appnote60:short].) (See also [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect9.appnote29:long].)
                           
                           
                              Except as provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect10.subsect9.art2.sent6:short], joints located in a horizontal plane between a floor and an exterior
wall shall be sealed by a [REF:term:fr-tp]firestop that,
when subjected to the fire test method in [REF:standard:astme2307] has an F rating not less than the [REF:term:fr-rtnc-]fire-resistance rating for the horizontal [REF:term:fr-prtn]fire separation.
                           
                           
                              Except as provided
in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect10.subsect9.art2.sent6:short], all gypsum
board joints in the assemblies described in Sentence (1) shall conform to [REF:standard:csaa82.31] to
maintain the integrity of the smoke-tight barrier over the entire
surface.
                           
                           
                              Joints between ceilings and walls, between floors and walls,
and between walls at corners need not comply with [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect10.subsect9.art2.sent3:short]
                                 [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect10.subsect9.art2.sent5:short] where such joints consist
of gypsum board that is attached to framing members and arranged so
as to restrict the passage of flame and smoke through the joints.
(See [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect9.appnote30:long].)

in required [REF:term:fr-prtn]fire separations shall be

                                 have a self-closing device.
                              
                               (See [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect10.subsect13:long] and Note A-9.10.9.3.(2).)

suite need not be constructed as [REF:term:fr-prtn]fire
separations.

penetration is sealed by a [REF:term:fr-tp]firestop conforming
to [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect10.subsect9.art6.sent1.clause1:long].
                              
                           
                           
                              
                                 [REF:term:cmbtbl]Combustible drain, waste and vent
piping is permitted on one side of a vertical [REF:term:fr-prtn]fire separation, provided it is not located in a vertical
shaft.
