                                 the piping is [REF:term:cmbtbl]combustible and is
not located in a vertical shaft, and the penetration is sealed by
a [REF:term:fr-tp]firestop conforming to [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect10.subsect9.art6.sent1.clause1:long].
                              
                           
                        
                        
                           Penetrations by Outlet Boxes or Service Equipment in Concealed
Spaces
                           
                              Except as provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect10.subsect9.art8.sent2:short]
                                 [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect10.subsect9.art8.sent5:short], outlet boxes are permitted to penetrate the membrane
of an assembly required to have a [REF:term:fr-rtnc-]fire-resistance
rating, provided they are sealed at the penetration by a [REF:term:fr-tp]firestop that, when subjected to the fire test
method in [REF:standard:ulcs115] has an FT rating not less than the [REF:term:fr-rtnc-]fire-resistance
rating of the [REF:term:fr-prtn]fire separation.
(See [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.appnote63:short].)
                           
                           
                              Except as provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect10.subsect9.art6.sent2:long], [REF:term:ncmbtbl]noncombustible outlet boxes that penetrate
a [REF:term:fr-prtn]fire separation or a membrane forming
part of an assembly required to have a [REF:term:fr-rtnc-]fire-resistance
rating need not conform to [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect10.subsect9.art8.sent1:short], provided
                              
                                 they do not exceed
                                 
                                    
                                       0.016 m (metric)
                                       ^{2} in area, and
                                 
                                 
                                    an aggregate area of 0.065 m (metric)
                                       ^{2} in
any 9.3 m (metric)
                                       ^{2} of surface area, and
                                 
                              
                              
                                 the annular space between the membrane and the [REF:term:ncmbtbl]noncombustible outlet boxes does not exceed 3 mm (metric).
                              
                           
                           
                              Except as provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect10.subsect9.art6.sent2:long], [REF:term:cmbtbl]combustible outlet boxes that penetrate a [REF:term:fr-prtn]fire separation or a membrane forming part
of an assembly required to have a [REF:term:fr-rtnc-]fire-resistance
rating need not conform to [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect10.subsect9.art8.sent1:short], provided
                              
                                 the outlet boxes are
                                 
                                    separated from the remainder of the space within the assembly
by an enclosure of not more than 0.3 m (metric)
                                       ^{2} in area made of [REF:term:fr-blk]fire block material
conforming to [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect10.subsect16.art3:long] (see [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.appnote64:short]), or
                                 
                                 
                                    located in a space within the assembly that is filled with preformed
fibre insulation processed from rock or slag conforming to [REF:standard:ulcs702] and having a mass
per unit area of not less than 1.22 kg/m (metric)
                                       ^{2} of wall surface such that the exposed sides and back of the outlet
box are encapsulated by the [REF:term:ncmbtbl]noncombustible insulation, and
                                 
                              
                              
                                 the outlet boxes do not exceed an aggregate area of 0.016
m (metric)
                                    ^{2} in any individual enclosure as described
in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect10.subsect9.art8.sent3.clause1.subclause1:short] or any individual insulated
space as described in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect10.subsect9.art8.sent3.clause1.subclause2:short].
                              
                           
                           
                              
                                 [REF:term:ncmbtbl]Noncombustible outlet boxes conforming
to [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect10.subsect9.art8.sent2:short] are permitted to be located
on opposite sides of a vertical [REF:term:fr-prtn]fire separation having a [REF:term:fr-rtnc-]fire-resistance rating and
need not conform to [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect10.subsect9.art8.sent1:short], provided
they are
                              
                                 separated from each other by a horizontal distance of not less
than 600 mm (metric),
                              
                              
                                 separated from each other and the remainder of the wall space
by an enclosure conforming to [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect10.subsect9.art8.sent3.clause1.subclause1:medium], or
                              
                              
                                 located in an insulated wall space in accordance with [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect10.subsect9.art8.sent3.clause1.subclause2:medium].
                              
                           
                           
                              
                                 [REF:term:cmbtbl]Combustible outlet boxes conforming
to [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect10.subsect9.art8.sent3:short] are permitted to be located
on opposite sides of a vertical [REF:term:fr-prtn]fire separation having a [REF:term:fr-rtnc-]fire-resistance rating and
need not conform to [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect10.subsect9.art8.sent1:short].
                           
                           
                              Service equipment is permitted to penetrate a horizontal [REF:term:fr-prtn]fire separation conforming to [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect10.subsect9.art12.sent2:long], provided the penetration is sealed by
                              
                                 a [REF:term:fr-tp]firestop that, when subjected to
the fire test method in [REF:standard:ulcs115] has an FT rating not less than the required [REF:term:fr-rtnc-]fire-resistance rating for the [REF:term:fr-prtn]fire separation,
                              
                              
                                 a [REF:term:fr-tp]firestop conforming to [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect10.subsect9.art6.sent1.clause1:long], where the service equipment is located entirely
within the cavity of a wall assembly above and below the horizontal [REF:term:fr-prtn]fire separation having a required [REF:term:fr-rtnc-]fire-resistance rating, or
                              
                              
                                 a [REF:term:fr-tp]firestop conforming to [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect10.subsect9.art6.sent1.clause1:long], where the penetration is
                                 
                                    contained within the concealed space of a floor or ceiling assembly
having a [REF:term:fr-rtnc-]fire-resistance rating,
                                 
                                 
                                    located above a ceiling membrane providing a horizontal [REF:term:fr-prtn]fire separation, or
                                 
                                 
                                    contained within a [REF:term:hrzntl-r]horizontal service
space conforming to [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect10.subsect9.art12.sent2:long] that is directly
above or below a floor or ceiling.
                                 
                              
                           
                        
                        
                           Penetrations by Raceways, Sprinklers and Fire Dampers
                           
                              
                                 [REF:term:cmbtbl]Combustible totally enclosed raceways
that are embedded in a concrete floor slab are permitted in an assembly
required to have a [REF:term:fr-rtnc-]fire-resistance rating, provided the concrete cover between the raceway and the bottom
of the slab is not less than 50 mm (metric).
                           
                           
                              Totally enclosed raceways are permitted to penetrate a [REF:term:fr-prtn]fire separation, provided they are sealed at
the penetration by a [REF:term:fr-tp]firestop conforming
to [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect10.subsect9.art6.sent1.clause1:long].
                           
                           
                              Sprinkler piping is permitted to penetrate a [REF:term:fr-prtn]fire separation, provided the [REF:term:fr-cmprt]fire
compartments on each side of the [REF:term:fr-prtn]fire
separation are [REF:term:prnklrd]sprinklered.
                           
                           
                              Sprinklers are permitted to penetrate a [REF:term:fr-prtn]fire separation or a membrane forming part of an assembly
required to have a [REF:term:fr-rtnc-]fire-resistance rating without having to meet the [REF:term:fr-tp]firestop requirements
of [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect10.subsect9.art6:long] and [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect10.subsect9.art8.sent6.clause1:long], provided
the annular space created by the penetration of a fire sprinkler is
covered by a metal escutcheon plate in accordance with [REF:standard:nfpa13]
                              
                           
                           
                              
                                 [REF:term:fr-dmpr]Fire dampers are permitted to penetrate
a [REF:term:fr-prtn]fire separation or a membrane forming
part of an assembly required to have a [REF:term:fr-rtnc-]fire-resistance
rating without having to meet the [REF:term:fr-tp]firestop requirements of [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect10.subsect9.art6.sent1:long], provided the [REF:term:fr-dmpr]fire damper is
                              
                                 installed in conformance with [REF:standard:nfpa80]
                                 
                              
                              
                                 specifically designed with a [REF:term:fr-tp]firestop, or 
                              
                              
                                 provided in conformance with [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect10.subsect5.art1.sent3:long].
                              
                              (See also [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect9.appnote37:long].)
                           
                           
                              In a house with a [REF:term:bc-scnd-t]secondary suite including their common spaces, ducts penetrating [REF:term:fr-prtn]fire separations need not be equipped with [REF:term:fr-dmpr]fire dampers in conformance with [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect1.subsect8.art10:long] provided they are [REF:term:ncmbtbl]noncombustible with all openings in the duct system serving only one [REF:term:fr-cmprt]fire compartment.
                           
                        
                        
                           Collapse of Combustible Construction
                           
                              
                                 [REF:term:cmbtbl-c]Combustible construction that
abuts on or is supported by a [REF:term:ncmbtbl]noncombustible
                                 [REF:term:fr-prtn]fire separation shall be constructed
so that its collapse under fire conditions will not cause collapse
of the [REF:term:fr-prtn]fire separation.
                           
                        
                        
                           Reduction in Thickness of Fire Separation by Beams and Joists
                           
                              Where pockets for the support of beams or joists are formed
in a masonry or concrete [REF:term:fr-prtn]fire separation, the remaining total thickness of masonry and/or grout and/or concrete
shall be not less than the required equivalent thickness shown for
Type S monolithic concrete in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.appendixD.appsect2.subsect1.article1.table1:long] of Appendix
D for the required [REF:term:fr-rtnc-]fire-resistance rating.
                           
                        
                        
                           Concealed Spaces above Fire Separations
                           
                              Except as provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect10.subsect9.art12.sent2:short], a [REF:term:hrzntl-r]horizontal service space or other
concealed space located above a required vertical [REF:term:fr-prtn]fire separation shall be divided at the [REF:term:fr-prtn]fire separation by an equivalent [REF:term:fr-prtn]fire
separation within the space. 
                           
                           
                              Where a [REF:term:hrzntl-r]horizontal service space or other concealed space is located above a required vertical [REF:term:fr-prtn]fire separation other than a vertical shaft,
such space need not be divided as required in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect10.subsect9.art12.sent1:short] provided the construction between such space and the
space below is constructed as a [REF:term:fr-prtn]fire separation having a [REF:term:fr-rtnc-]fire-resistance rating not
less than that required for the vertical [REF:term:fr-prtn]fire
separation, except that where the vertical [REF:term:fr-prtn]fire separation is not required to have a [REF:term:fr-rtnc-]fire-resistance rating greater than 45 min (metric), the [REF:term:fr-rtnc-]fire-resistance rating of the ceiling may
be reduced to 30 min (metric).
                           
                        
                        
                           Separation of Residential Occupancies
                           
                              Except as provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect10.subsect9.art13.sent2:short], [REF:term:rdntl-cc]residential occupancies shall be
separated from all other [REF:term:mjr-ccpn]major occupancies by a [REF:term:fr-prtn]fire separation having a [REF:term:fr-rtnc-]fire-resistance rating of not less than 1 h (metric).
                           
                           
                              Except as provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect10.subsect9.art13.sent3:short], a [REF:term:mjr-ccpn]major occupancy classified as
a [REF:term:rdntl-cc]residential occupancy shall be separated
from other [REF:term:mjr-ccpn]major occupancies classified
as [REF:term:mrcntl-c]mercantile or [REF:term:mdm-hzrd]medium-hazard industrial occupancies by a [REF:term:fr-prtn]fire separation having a [REF:term:fr-rtnc-]fire-resistance
rating of not less than 2 h (metric).
                           
                           
                              Where not more than two dwelling
units
                                  (metric) are located in a [REF:term:bldng]building containing a [REF:term:mrcntl-c]mercantile occupancy,
such [REF:term:mrcntl-c]mercantile occupancy shall be separated
from the [REF:term:dwllng-n]dwelling units by a [REF:term:fr-prtn]fire separation having not less than 1 h (metric)
                                 [REF:term:fr-rtnc-]fire-resistance rating.
                           
                        
                        
                           Residential Suites in Industrial Buildings
                           
                              Not more than one [REF:term:t]suite of [REF:term:rdntl-cc]residential occupancy shall be contained within
a [REF:term:bldng]building classified as a Group F, Division 2 major occupancy
                                  (metric).
                           
                        
                        
                           Separation of Suites
                           
                              Except as required in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect10.subsect9.art16:long] and as permitted
by [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect10.subsect9.art15.sent2:short], each [REF:term:t]suite in other than [REF:term:bn-nd-pr]business and personal
services occupancies shall be separated from adjoining [REF:term:t]suites by a [REF:term:fr-prtn]fire separation having a [REF:term:fr-rtnc-]fire-resistance rating of
not less than 45 min (metric).
                           
                           
                              In [REF:term:prnklrd] sprinklered
                                 [REF:term:bldng]buildings, [REF:term:t]suites of [REF:term:bn-nd-pr]business and personal services occupancy  and [REF:term:mrcntl-c]mercantile occupancy that are served by [REF:term:pblc-crr]public corridors conforming with [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect3.subsect1.art4.sent4.clause2:long] are not required to be separated from each other
by [REF:term:fr-prtn]fire separations.
                           
                        
                        
                           Separation of Residential Suites
                           
                              Except as provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect10.subsect9.art16.sent2:short]
                                 [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect10.subsect9.art16.sent4:short] and [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect10.subsect21.art2:long], [REF:term:t]suites in [REF:term:rdntl-cc] residential occupancies shall
be separated from adjacent rooms and [REF:term:t]suites by a [REF:term:fr-prtn]fire separation having a [REF:term:fr-rtnc-] fire-resistance rating of not less than 45 min (metric).
                           
                           
                              Sleeping rooms in boarding and lodging houses where sleeping
accommodation is provided for not more than 8 boarders or lodgers
need not be separated from the remainder of the [REF:term:flr-r]floor area as required in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect10.subsect9.art16.sent1:short] where the sleeping rooms form part of the proprietor's residence
and do not contain cooking facilities.
                           
                           
                              Except as provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect10.subsect9.art16.sent4:short], [REF:term:dwllng-n]dwelling units that contain 2 or
more [REF:term:tr]storeys including [REF:term:bmnt]basements as well as houses with a [REF:term:bc-scnd-t]secondary suite including their common spaces shall be separated from the remainder of the [REF:term:bldng]building by a [REF:term:fr-prtn]fire separation having a [REF:term:fr-rtnc-]fire-resistance rating of
not less than 1 h (metric). (See [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect9.appnote142:long].)
                           
                           
                              In a house with a [REF:term:bc-scnd-t]secondary suite, [REF:term:dwllng-n]dwelling units shall be separated from each other and from ancillary spaces and common spaces with a fire separation
                              
                                 having a fire-resistance rating not less than 15 min (metric) when all smoke alarms within the house are of photo-electric type and interconnected as described in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect10.subsect19.art5.sent2.clause1:long] (see also [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect10.subsect3.art1.sent2:short]),
                              
                              
                                 having a fire-resistance rating not less than 30 min (metric) when additional smoke alarms of photo-electric type are installed and interconnected as described in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect10.subsect19.art5.sent2.clause2:long] (see also [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect10.subsect3.art1.sent3:short]),
                              
                              
                                 having a fire-resistance rating not less than 45 min (metric) when smoke alarms are not installed and interconnected as described in Clauses (a) or (b), or
                              
                              
                                 that is not required to have a fire-resistance rating if the [REF:term:bldng]building is [REF:term:prnklrd]sprinklered.
                              
                           
                        
                        
                           Separation of Public Corridors
                           
                              Except as otherwise
required by this Part and as provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect10.subsect9.art17.sent2:short]
                                 [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect10.subsect9.art17.sent5:short], [REF:term:pblc-crr]public corridors shall be separated from the remainder of the [REF:term:bldng] building by a [REF:term:fr-prtn]fire separation having not less than a 45 min (metric)
                                 [REF:term:fr-rtnc-]fire-resistance rating.
                           
                           
                              In other than [REF:term:rdntl-cc]residential occupancies, no [REF:term:fr-rtnc-]fire-resistance rating is required
for [REF:term:fr-prtn]fire separations between a [REF:term:pblc-crr]public corridor and the remainder of the [REF:term:bldng]building if
                              
                                 the [REF:term:flr-r]floor area is [REF:term:prnklrd]sprinklered,
                              
                              
                                 the sprinkler system is electrically supervised in conformance
with [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect2.subsect4.art9.sent3:long], and
                              
                              
                                 the operation of the sprinkler system will cause a signal to
be transmitted to the fire department in conformance with [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect2.subsect4.art7.sent4:long].
                              
                           
                           
                              In other than [REF:term:rdntl-cc]residential occupancies, no [REF:term:fr-prtn]fire separation is required between
a [REF:term:pblc-crr]public corridor and the remainder
of the [REF:term:bldng]building if
                              
                                 the [REF:term:flr-r]floor area is [REF:term:prnklrd]sprinklered,
                              
                              
                                 the sprinkler system is electrically supervised in conformance
with [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect2.subsect4.art9.sent3:long],
                              
                              
                                 the operation of the sprinkler system will cause a signal to
be transmitted to the fire department in conformance with [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect2.subsect4.art7.sent4:long], and
                              
                              
                                 the corridor exceeds 5 m (metric) in width.
                              
                           
                           
                              A [REF:term:pblc-crr]public corridor located in a house with a [REF:term:bc-scnd-t]secondary suite shall be separated from the remainder of the spaces in the house with a fire separation
                              
                                 having a fire-resistance rating not less than 15 min (metric) when all smoke alarms within the house are of photo-electric type and interconnected as described in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect10.subsect19.art5.sent2.clause1:long] (see also [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect10.subsect3.art1.sent2:short]),
                              
                              
                                 having a fire-resistance rating not less than 30 min (metric) when additional smoke alarms of photo-electric type are installed and interconnected as described in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect10.subsect19.art5.sent2.clause2:long] (see also [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect10.subsect3.art1.sent3:short]),
                              
                              
                                 having a fire-resistance rating not less than 45 min (metric) when smoke alarms are not installed and interconnected as described in Clauses (a) or (b), or
                              
                              
                                 that is not required to have a fire-resistance rating if the [REF:term:bldng]building is [REF:term:prnklrd]sprinklered.
                              
                           
                           
                              No [REF:term:fr-prtn]fire separation is required
in a [REF:term:prnklrd]sprinklered
                                 [REF:term:flr-r]floor area between a [REF:term:pblc-crr]public corridor and a space containing plumbing fixtures required by [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect7.subsect2.art2:long] and [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect31:long], provided
                              
                                 the space and the [REF:term:pblc-crr]public corridor are separated from the remainder of the [REF:term:tr]storey by a [REF:term:fr-prtn]fire separation having a [REF:term:fr-rtnc-]fire-resistance rating not less than that
required between the [REF:term:pblc-crr]public corridor and the remainder of the [REF:term:tr]storey, and
                              
                              
                                 the plumbing fixtures are not located within a [REF:term:dwllng-n]dwelling unit or [REF:term:t]suite.
                              
                           
                        
                        
                           Separation of Storage Garages
                           
                              Except as provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect10.subsect9.art18.sent2:short]
                                 [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect10.subsect9.art18.sent3:short], a [REF:term:trg-grg]storage garage  shall
be separated from other [REF:term:ccpnc]occupancies by
a [REF:term:fr-prtn]fire separation having not less than
a  1.5 h (metric)
                                 [REF:term:fr-rtnc-]fire-resistance rating.
                           
                           
                              Except as permitted in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect10.subsect9.art18.sent3:short], [REF:term:trg-grg]storage garages containing 5 motor
vehicles or fewer shall be separated from other [REF:term:ccpnc]occupancies by a [REF:term:fr-prtn]fire separation of not less than 1 h (metric).
                           
                           
                              Where a [REF:term:trg-grg]storage garage  serves
only the [REF:term:dwllng-n]dwelling unit to which it is
attached or in which it is built, it shall be considered as part of
that [REF:term:dwllng-n] dwelling unit and the [REF:term:fr-prtn]fire separation required in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect10.subsect9.art18.sent2:short] need not be provided between the garage
and the [REF:term:dwllng-n]dwelling unit.
                           
                           
                              Except as provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect10.subsect9.art18.sent5:short], where a [REF:term:trg-grg]storage garage  is attached
to or built into a [REF:term:bldng]building of [REF:term:rdntl-cc]residential occupancy,(See [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.appnote65:short].)
                              
                                 an [REF:term:r-brrr]air barrier system conforming
to [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect25.subsect3:long] shall be installed between the
garage and the remainder of the [REF:term:bldng]building to provide an effective barrier to gas and exhaust fumes, and
                              
                              
                                 every door between the garage and the remainder of the [REF:term:bldng] building shall conform to [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect10.subsect13.art15:long]
                                 
                              
                           
                           
                              Where membrane materials are used to provide the required airtightness
in the [REF:term:r-brrr]air barrier system, all joints
shall be sealed and structurally supported.
                           
                        
                        
                           Separation of Repair Garages
                           
                              Except as provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect10.subsect9.art19.sent2:short]
                                 [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect10.subsect9.art19.sent3:short], a [REF:term:rpr-grg]repair garage shall
be separated from other [REF:term:ccpnc]occupancies by
a [REF:term:fr-prtn]fire separation having a [REF:term:fr-rtnc-]fire-resistance rating of not less than 2 h (metric).
                           
                           
                              Ancillary spaces directly serving a [REF:term:rpr-grg]repair
garage, including waiting rooms, reception rooms, tool and
parts storage areas and supervisory office space, need not be separated
from the [REF:term:rpr-grg]repair garage but shall be separated
from other [REF:term:ccpnc]occupancies as required in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect10.subsect9.art19.sent1:short].
                           
                           
                              The [REF:term:fr-prtn]fire separation referred to
in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect10.subsect9.art19.sent1:short] shall have a [REF:term:fr-rtnc-]fire-resistance rating of not less than 1 h (metric), where
                              
                                 the [REF:term:bldng]building is not more than one [REF:term:tr]storey in [REF:term:bldng-hg]building height,
                              
                              
                                 the [REF:term:bldng]building is operated as a single [REF:term:t]suite, and
                              
                              
                                 the only [REF:term:ccpnc]occupancy other than the [REF:term:rpr-grg]repair garage is a [REF:term:mrcntl-c]mercantile
occupancy.
                              
                           
                           
                              Except as provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect10.subsect9.art19.sent5:short], where a [REF:term:bldng]building containing a [REF:term:rpr-grg]repair garage  also contains a [REF:term:dwllng-n]dwelling unit, an [REF:term:r-brrr]air
barrier system conforming to [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect25.subsect3:long] shall be installed between the [REF:term:dwllng-n]dwelling
unit and the [REF:term:t]suite containing the garage

more than one [REF:term:fr-cmprt]fire compartment, the
duct shall have a fan located at or near the exhaust outlet to ensure
that the duct is under negative pressure.

to in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect10.subsect9.art20.sent1:short] shall not have fans
that exhaust directly into the duct in the [REF:term:vrtcl-rv]vertical service space.

Rough-in for a Subfloor Depressurization System
                           
                              Floors-on-ground shall accommodate the future installation of a subfloor depressurization system by installing a radon vent pipe, and a contiguous gas-permeable layer between the [REF:term:r-brrr]air barrier system and the ground consisting of
                              
                                 a material or materials that allow effective depressurization of that space (see [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect16.subsect2.art1.sent1:long]), or
                              
                              
                                 not less than 100 mm (metric) of coarse clean granular material containing not more than 10% of material that would pass a 4 mm (metric) sieve.
                              
                           
                           
                              The radon vent pipe required by [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect13.subsect4.art3.sent1:short] shall
                              
                                 be sealed to maintain the integrity of the [REF:term:r-brrr]air barrier system, with no perforations along the pipe above the [REF:term:r-brrr]air barrier system,
                              
                              
                                 have one or more inlets that allow for the effective depressurization of the gas-permeable layer (see Note A-9.13.4.3.(2)(b) and (3)(b)), and
                              
                              
                                 permit connection to depressurization equipment,
                              
                              
                                 where it passes through [REF:term:cnd-sp]conditioned space, be completely surrounded by [REF:term:cnd-sp]conditioned space,
                              
                              
                                 consist of pipe and fittings in accordance with 7.1.3 of CAN/CGSB-149.11, "Radon control options for new construction in low-rise residential buildings,"
                              
                              
                                 terminate outside the [REF:term:bldng]building in a manner that does not constitute a hazard,
                              
                              
                                 be installed to prevent the accumulation of moisture and away from locations where snow and ice accumulate, and
                              
                              
                                 be clearly labeled every 1.8 m (metric) and at every change in direction to indicate that it is intended only for the future removal of radon from below the floor-on-ground.
                              
                           
                           
                              A radon vent pipe shall be deemed to comply with
                              
                                 
                                    [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect13.subsect4.art3.sent2.clause2:medium] where its inlet or inlets below the [REF:term:r-brrr]air barrier system are located at or near the centre of the floor-on-ground with gas-permeable material extending not less than 100 mm (metric) beyond any inlet, and
                              
                              
                                 
                                    [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect13.subsect4.art3.sent2.clause6:medium] where it terminates outside the [REF:term:bldng]building, not less than 1.8 m (metric) from a property line, and located in accordance with either 7.2.4.6 or 7.3.4 of CAN/CGSB-149.11, "Radon control options for new construction in low-rise residential buildings," with the opening of the pipe fitted with a corrosion-resistant screen or grille with a mesh opening size of 10 mm (metric) to 12.5 mm (metric) or a product of equivalent air flow performance.
